[**freemytv.io**](https://freemytv.io) · [Install](#install) · [LG TVs](#lg-tvs-webos) · [Samsung TVs](#samsung-tvs-tizen) · [Any TV](#any-tv) · [Make it yours](#make-it-yours)

evidence.heading: What you get
evidence.text:
- **No ads.** No sponsored rows, banners or autoplaying promos. Not one.
- **Your apps, front and center.** The streaming apps you actually use, on a glass shelf. Pick them and their order right on the TV.
- **Trending, not sponsored.** Three fresh picks every hour from what's trending this week and the latest releases, only from apps you already have. Movies and Shows get their own tabs.
- **Weather and markets, one press away.** The hour-by-hour forecast, sunrise and sunset, and live crypto prices.
- **Light by day, dark by night.** It follows your city's real sunset, the way your phone does.
- **A screensaver to match.** Full-screen photos of the picks with a big glass clock.
- **Your own photos** (Google TV and Android TV). Send them from your computer (up to 100): the screensaver shows them, and without picks one is the home screen's background each hour.
- **Fast.** 60 fps, every frame in 16.6 ms, on the TV's own chip. The home screen uses 96 MB of memory instead of 242 MB (−60%).Measured on a 98″ TCL Google TV running Android 14.
- **Set up on the TV.** Language, your city, temperature, theme, the weather and prices cards, which coins, and the apps on the shelf, in Free My TV's own settings.
- **Safe.** No root. Nothing is uninstalled. One button brings back the factory home screen.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text: About ten minutes. You need a Google TV or Android TV (Android 8 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi.

evidence.heading: The easy way: an AI assistant
evidence.text:
1. **On the TV**, turn on developer mode: Settings → System → About → press *Android TV OS build* 7 times. Then Settings → System → Developer options → turn on **USB debugging**. Write down the TV's IP address (Settings → Network & Internet).
2. **On your computer**, open an AI coding assistant ([Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), Codex or Antigravity) and say:
   > Install Free My TV (github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv) on my TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon.

   It downloads the code, installs the tools it needs, builds the app and puts it on your TV, and asks before anything important. Swap in your TV's IP and your city.
3. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*. That's when the TV asks *Allow USB debugging?* for Free My TV: tick *Always allow* and accept.

evidence.heading: The manual way
evidence.text:
1. **On the TV**, do step 1 above.
2. **Tools:** a JDK (17+), the Android SDK command-line tools (build-tools 34, platform android-34) and adb. On a Mac:
   ```bash
   brew install --cask temurin android-commandlinetools android-platform-tools
   sdkmanager "build-tools;34.0.0" "platforms;android-34"
   ```
   On Linux, get OpenJDK 17, Android's command-line tools and adb from your package manager, then run the same `sdkmanager` line. On Windows, use Git Bash (which Claude Code uses there) or WSL.
3. **Build:**
   ```bash
   ./build.sh
   ```
   The first run creates `config.properties`. Set your city and your [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key) there, then run it again.
4. **Install:**
   ```bash
   adb connect 192.168.1.50:5555
   adb install -r FreeMyTV.apk
   ```
   If the install seems stuck, look at the TV: on Android 14, Google Play Protect may hold it with *Risky app blocked* ("built for an older version of Android"), since Free My TV targets Android 13. Choose *More details* → *Install anyway*. Updates don't ask again.

   Chromecast with Google TV on Android 14 keeps port 5555 closed even with USB debugging on: turn on *Wireless debugging* (Developer options), pair with `adb pair <address:port> <code>`, then run `adb tcpip 5555` over that connection. Port 5555 closes again at every restart, so after one, *Original*, the watchdog and the boot check can't reach ADB until you run `adb tcpip 5555` again (the pairing stays).

   On TCL TVs, also let it run in the background (TCL blocks it by default, and the switch never starts):
   ```bash
   adb shell "appops set io.freemytv AUTO_START allow || appops set io.freemytv APP_AUTO_START allow"
   ```
5. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*. The TV asks *Allow USB debugging?* once more, now for Free My

evidence.heading: What it changes
How it works
evidence.text:
- **A plain Android app, no Gradle, no libraries.** [`build.sh`](build.sh) runs aapt2 → javac → d8 → zipalign → apksigner and makes a 2 MB APK.
- **It uses the TV's own ADB, from inside the TV.** The app connects to `127.0.0.1:5555` with its own key (that's the *Allow USB debugging?* prompt) and runs the same commands you would: `cmd package set-home-activity`, `settings put secure screensaver_components`, `pm disable-user`. Nothing listens to the network.
- **Drawn by hand on one Canvas**, with Android 13 shaders for the frosted glass and the sky (plain fills on Android 8 to 12, with lighter shadows and no GPU layers on 8 to 11 for their older GPUs).
- **A safety net.** A watchdog in a separate process brings back the stock home screen after three crashes in five minutes, and a boot check keeps your choice after TV updates.
- **On LG and Samsung, the same design in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript** ([`web/`](web)), written for the Chromium of older TVs, with no frameworks. [`webos/build.py`](webos/build.py) packs it with `config.properties` into an `.ipk` without LG's tools, and [`webos/install.py`](webos/install.py) installs it through Developer Mode; on LG it lists and opens apps through the TV's own service bus (Luna), as LG's launcher does. [`tizen/build.py`](tizen/build.py) packs the same app into a Samsung `.wgt`, which uses Tizen's web APIs for the apps and the inputs. To preview it on a computer: `python3 webos/build.py --preview`, then open `out/webos/index.html` (a stand-in lists sample apps).
- **Data** from TMDB (trending titles, new releases and which app streams what in your country), Open-Meteo (forecast, sunrise and sunset), and optionally Binance (24-hour prices when `show_crypto=true`).

github_projects.description: A Claude Code / Codex plugin that helps you learn how to build while AI writes the code.
github_projects.description_zh: 一个 Claude Code / Codex 插件，帮助你在 AI 编写代码时学习如何构建。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: A Claude Code / Codex plugin that helps you learn how to build while AI writes the code.

evidence.heading: VibeWise
evidence.text:
**You build. AI writes.**

A plugin for **Claude Code** and **Codex** that puts learning first and keeps you in control while AI writes the code you designed. The AI **asks for your approach first**, helps you examine tradeoffs, and explains unfamiliar concepts. You shape the design and decide when it's ready to implement. The AI writes the code, then explains what it changed and why.

For anyone who wants to learn as they build—whether you're an aspiring engineer, a junior developer, or an experienced engineer exploring an unfamiliar stack. Practice planning how the pieces fit together, anticipating failures, and checking the result while keeping ownership of the decisions.

evidence.heading: Get started
evidence.text:
You need an up-to-date [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) or
[Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex), and
[Python 3](https://www.python.org/downloads/). In Claude Code, VibeWise uses Python
to restore learning context and reset learning notes. In Codex, only reset needs it.
No extra Python packages are needed.

evidence.heading: Claude Code
evidence.text:
Install from the built-in **Anthropic Directory**. In Claude Code, run:

```text
/plugin install vibe-wise@anthropic-plugin-directory
```

Choose an installation scope and confirm. No marketplace setup is needed.

Restart Claude Code in the project you want to work on, then run:

```text
/vibe-wise:learn
```

Setup asks one question at a time. Use the arrow keys and Enter for choices; pick **Use defaults** to skip preference setup. Then ask Claude to build something. Starting fresh or joining an unfamiliar repository both work. For an existing repository, Claude first inspects the code and sketches a small system map.


Alternative: install through GitHub

If Anthropic Directory isn't available in your Claude Code version, use the GitHub
marketplace. Choose one installation method; you don't need both.

Run these commands **one at a time** in Claude Code. First, add the marketplace:

```text
/plugin marketplace add nykooi1/vibe-wise
```

After it finishes, install the plugin:

```text
/plugin install vibe-wise@vibe-wise
```

Enable automatic updates through `/plugin` → **Marketplaces** → **vibe-wise** →
**Enable auto-update**. This is off by default for third-party marketplaces.
Restart Claude Code, then run `/vibe-wise:learn` in your project.

evidence.heading: Codex
evidence.text:
In a terminal, run these commands **one at a time**. First, add the marketplace:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add nykooi1/vibe-wise
```

After it finishes, install the plugin:

```sh
codex plugin add vibe-wise@vibe-wise
```

Start Codex in your project and run `$vibe-wise:learn`. Run it again at the start
of each Codex session, and whenever Codex seems to have lost track of learning
mode. It resumes from your saved notes without repeating setup. To reset, run
`$vibe-wise:reset`. Claude Code and Codex share the same `.vibe-wise/` notes.

In Codex, the commands in this guide use `$` instead of `/`: `/vibe-wise:learn`
becomes `$vibe-wise:learn`.

evidence.heading: What it feels like
evidence.text:
You're building a Notion-style notes app: users sign in, create and edit private
notes, and organize them into folders. Here, you're working through how notes and
folders relate—and what should happen when someone deletes a folder.

This condensed example is adapted from a real learning session. Later implementation
steps are illustrative; intervening design discussions are omitted.

**You:**

```text
A note can be in several folders. Deleting a folder should delete its notes.
```

**Claude / Codex:**

```text
✦ Build checkpoint: Deleting a shared note

"Trip ideas" is in both Travel and Summer. Deleting it removes it from both.

When someone deletes Travel, what should happen to that note in Summer?
```

**You:**

```text
Keep it in Summer. If it has no folders left, keep the note outside any folder.
```

**Claude / Codex:**

```text
That separates deleting a folder from deleting a note.

✦ Build checkpoint: Connecting notes and folders

How would you represent which folders a note belongs to, without copying the note?
```

**You:**

```text
A links table with note_id and folder_id. Deleting a folder removes its links,
not the notes.
```

**Claude / Codex:**

```text
Each link records one membership. Several links can point to the same note;
a note with no links is unfiled.

notes ← folder links → folders

✦ Design checkpoint: Folder membership

Proposed: store notes once and track folder membership in a links table.
Deleting a folder removes its links and keeps the notes. This supports multiple
folders per note; loading a folder's notes needs a lookup through those links.

Confirming records this design. We still need to work through access rules
and technology choices before writing code.

❯ 1. Confirm and continue
     This approach makes sense to me; move to the ne

evidence.heading: Make it yours
evidence.text:
Experience changes the support you get, not your ownership of decisions:

| Level | Teaching approach |
| --- | --- |
| Beginner | Explain unfamiliar pieces, use diagrams, ask smaller reasoning questions. |
| Intermediate | Less introductory context; explore interactions and tradeoffs. |
| Advanced | Probe difficult constraints, failure modes, and design assumptions. |

Everyone reasons first. The AI adapts to what you demonstrate and how familiar you
are with the stack. Checkpoint frequency—Light, Normal, or Frequent—is separate.

- “Use fewer checkpoints.”
- “Focus on backend architecture.”
- “Use multiple-choice questions.”
- “Just implement this one.”
- “Pause learning.” Resume with `/vibe-wise:learn`.

Preferences, learning notes, and a project map live in `.vibe-wise/` in your project. In a Git repository, that's the repository root, and VibeWise finds it from any subfolder. Without Git, it's the folder you start in, so always start from your project's top folder. Learning mode resumes in future sessions and after compaction. Add `.vibe-wise/` to your `.gitignore` to keep your notes out of Git; the plugin won't change it silently.

No extra account, backend, or telemetry. Saved notes are included in the AI's context, so your normal Claude Code or Codex data settings still apply.

To start learning this project from scratch, run `/vibe-wise:reset`. It shows the
project and asks **Cancel / Reset learning**. After confirmation, it backs up your
profile, progress, and project map inside the notes directory's `backups/` folder,
then restarts onboarding. Source code and other projects stay untouched. To change
your experience level or preferences, just tell the AI; no reset is needed.

evidence.heading: 快速开始（作者案例跟跑）
evidence.text:

evidence.heading: 硬件要求（参考）
evidence.text:
底模为 Qwen-Image 2.1 int8 套件，模型文件合计约 16GB（diffusion 6.8GB / text encoder 8.7GB / VAE 0.6GB），LoRA 各自 ≤608MB。

- **最低**：NVIDIA 12GB 显存 + 32GB 内存——能跑，ComfyUI 会自动把部分模型卸载到内存，出图慢一些
- **推荐**：24GB 显存（3090/4090 级）+ 32–64GB 内存——模型基本常驻，体验最顺
- **8GB 显存**：建议用 GGUF 量化版（社区实测 12–16GB 显存可跑 Q4；8GB 靠 offload 会明显更慢）
- 纯 CPU 不推荐（单张图耗时过长）
- 硬盘预留 ~40GB；CPU 无特殊要求（现代 x86_64/ARM 均可）；Linux 最省事；Windows 可原生运行基础脚本（doctor / `--list-poses` / 媒体锁回退，社区贡献），完整流程仍建议 WSL2；Mac（Apple Silicon）见下方单独小节
- 路线④额外需要一个可连接的桌面浏览器（Playwright/CDP，见 `install/setup.md`）

本仓库案例图与实测数据来自统一内存设备（DGX Spark）：1024×1024、40 步约 32 秒/张，峰值增量约 7–10GB。

evidence.heading: macOS（Apple Silicon）
evidence.text:
- 适用 M 系芯片（M1 及以上）；Intel Mac 不建议
- **模型选择看统一内存**：≥32GB 直接用本仓库原版 int8 套件（ComfyUI + MPS）；16–32GB 建议改用 GGUF 量化版（搭配 ComfyUI-GGUF；社区实测 Q8 更快、Q4 更省内存）
- **速度预期：分钟级/张**——社区报告：M5 Pro 48GB 跑 int8 约 144 秒/1024；M1 Max 64GB 约 7–10 分钟/张（加缓存优化节点如 Comfyui-Spectrum-Qwen2.1 可提速 2–3 倍）。对比本仓库 DGX Spark 实测 32 秒/张，仅供参考
- 已知坑：编辑模式在 MPS 上偶发 VAE 编码异常，可用 ComfyUI 的 `--cpu-vae` 绕过（ComfyUI issue #16433，已有修复讨论）；内存紧张时建议单张生成、关闭其他大内存应用
- 路线兼容：①②③ 脚本在 macOS 可直接运行（纯 Python 标准库、POSIX 兼容）；④ 需 `playwright install chromium`（macOS 版），`install/setup.md` 中的 AppArmor 提示不适用
- ⚠️ 以上 Mac 数据来自社区报告，维护者没有 Mac 硬件、未经实测；如果你在 Mac 上跑通或遇到问题，欢迎开 issue 反馈，我们会持续更新本说明

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
```
iPhone ──Screen Mirroring (Wi-Fi)──▶ ESP32-S3: AirPlay receiver ──BLE──▶ ESP32 Agent app (same iPhone)
   ▲                                    own hotspot, H.264 passthrough        decode → vision model → action
   └──────── USB HID mouse + keyboard ◀──────────── BLE commands ◀────────────────────┘
```

- **Eyes — AirPlay to the board.** The board opens its own Wi-Fi hotspot and appears in the phone's Screen Mirroring
  list as *ESP32 Agent*. It keeps the H.264 stream (no decoding on the board) and forwards it to the app over BLE.
  The phone keeps using cellular data for the model while it is on the board's hotspot.
- **Hands — USB HID.** The board is a standard USB mouse and keyboard. With AssistiveTouch on, the mouse moves an
  on-screen pointer, so a click is a tap and a drag is a swipe.
- **Brain — the app.** The app decodes the stream, sends screenshots to any OpenAI-compatible vision model, and runs
  a planner and an actor: tap, swipe, draw, type, press keys, go home, finish. It runs in the background while it
  works; the Dynamic Island shows what it is doing.
- **Closing the loop.** The pointer is relative, so the app tracks it and re-homes it in a corner; before precise taps
  it wiggles the pointer, finds it on screen and corrects the miss. After each action it waits for the screen to
  settle and tells the model whether anything changed. A lost board, hotspot or mirroring link pauses the run and
  resumes it from the same step.
- **Review.** Every run is kept on the phone: replay it step by step with the taps and swipes drawn on top.
  Export the screenshots, actions and saved annotations from **Runs → open a run → ⋯ → Export trace** for analysis
  by another agent. See [Export runs for agent review](docs/run-data-export.md) for batch export, USB copyin

evidence.heading: Hardware
evidence.text:
| Part | Notes |
|---|---|
| **ESP32-S3 board** | Tested with a [Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32s3_getting_started/) (plain version, 8 MB PSRAM; not Sense, not Plus). About $7. Any ESP32-S3 with native USB on its USB-C port and PSRAM should work. |
| **iPhone** | iOS 18 or later, with cellular data (the Wi-Fi is taken by the board's hotspot). USB-C models plug in directly; Lightning models need a Lightning to USB Camera Adapter. The phone powers the board. |
| **Vision model** | Any OpenAI-compatible chat API that accepts images: a cloud API or your own server. |
| **Mac with Xcode** | Only to flash the board and build the app once. Not needed at run time. |

evidence.heading: 2. Install the app
evidence.text:
```bash
cp ios/Config/Local.xcconfig.example ios/Config/Local.xcconfig   # set DEVELOPMENT_TEAM and IA_BUNDLE_ID
open ios/IPhoneAgent.xcodeproj                                    # run the IPhoneAgent scheme on your iPhone
```

The project is generated with [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) from `ios/project.yml`
(`cd ios && xcodegen`). A free Apple ID can sign it (re-sign every 7 days). The one-tap hotspot join needs the
Hotspot Configuration capability (a paid account); without it the app shows the hotspot password to join by hand.

evidence.heading: Limitations
evidence.text:
- BLE carries about 300-500 kbps, so the screen is mirrored small (480×1040, ≤5 fps); each step takes a few seconds,
  most of it the model.
- iOS does not mirror some screens (passcode entry, Apple Pay, DRM video); the agent cannot see them. Mirroring stops
  when the phone locks.
- While the agent runs, the phone's Wi-Fi is the board's hotspot (no internet over it); the model is reached over
  cellular data.
- The app leaves itself with a private iOS API (`suspend`); fine for a self-built app, to be replaced before the App Store.
- Keyboard input is ASCII only. Landscape apps are not supported yet.

evidence.heading: Responsible use
evidence.text:
Only automate devices and accounts you own or are allowed to use, and respect the terms of the apps involved. The
agent acts with your hands: watch it, and keep the stop button within reach.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
**Desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux)**

The desktop app brings its own DSH, so you don't need to install DSH first. Download it from [Releases](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot/releases):

- Windows (x64): `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>-win-x64.exe`. Run it; it installs for your user only, without administrator rights. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", select **More info** → **Run anyway**.
- macOS: `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>-mac-arm64.zip` for an Apple chip, `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>-mac-x64.zip` for Intel. Safari unzips it by itself; drag **DeepSeek Bot** into **Applications** and open it. When macOS says it cannot check the app, open **System Settings** → **Privacy & Security** and select **Open Anyway**.
- Linux (x64): `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage` runs on every distribution — make it executable and open it. It mounts through FUSE 2, which you may need to install first (`sudo apt install libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04+, `sudo dnf install fuse-libs` on Fedora, `sudo pacman -S fuse2` on Arch). On Ubuntu 24.04 and later an AppImage can refuse to start (Ubuntu restricts the sandbox it needs); the `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>-linux-amd64.deb` on Debian/Ubuntu does not have this problem and adds a menu entry.

At the first start the app asks where to keep its data and the Bots' files, and offers to copy a Bot team from your DSH (it only reads your DSH). Set up a model in its settings. The Windows app and the Linux AppImage update themselves; the macOS app and the Linux deb tell you when a new version is ready to download.

**As a plugin in DSH**

First install DSH and set up at least one model in it. DS Bot uses the models from DSH.

**DSH Desktop (Windows, macOS)**

1. In the sidebar, select **Plugins** → **Add plugin**.
2. In **Package name or address*

evidence.heading: Setup
evidence.text: I strongly recommend that you set up your other bots and group chats by just talking to a bot.

evidence.heading: Web search
evidence.text: DS Bot selects its `auto` search provider for the whole profile. If you disable `web-search-auto`, also select another registered search provider in that profile. See [Web search](ds-bot/README.md#web-search) and the [recovery steps](docs/known-issues.md#web-search-fails-everywhere-after-turning-off-web-search-auto).

evidence.heading: Bot
evidence.text:
You can do all your talking and work with one bot, in one window. You don't need to worry about the context behind it. The bot's details page shows its info, and there you can pick the model you want it to use. You can switch models at any time, but I still recommend that you keep one model for a bot for a long time, and switch only when you really need to.

Bots also have memory. A bot remembers what you like and uses it in later work. You can manage its memory on the bot's details page, or just tell the bot.

evidence.heading: Main bot
evidence.text:
The main bot is your chief. It has very high rights: it manages the other bots and the group chats. The first time you open DS Bot, there is already a main bot called Chief. Talk to it, and it walks you through the setup.

In short: have a question? Ask the main bot.

Omnara is an open-source managed agent platform. Use the API to run AI agents
on any model and any machine, with tools, secrets, permissions, and streaming
built in. Self-host it for free under Apache 2.0, or use
[Omnara Cloud](https://app.omnara.com).

evidence.heading: Omnara Cloud
evidence.text:
Sign in at [app.omnara.com](https://app.omnara.com). Your first project comes
with a model provider (`omnara-openrouter`) and a pool of managed sandboxes
(`default-pool`), so this config runs as is. Save it as `agent.yaml`:

```yaml
version: v1
instruction: |
  You are an engineering assistant. Use your machine to run commands.
model:
  provider_config: omnara-openrouter
  name: anthropic/claude-fable-5.1
machine_sources:
  - machine_pool_name: default-pool
```

Launch it with the CLI (Node.js 22 or newer). If you're not logged in, the
first command opens your browser to sign in.

```sh
npx omnara agents launch --file agent.yaml \
  --name "Machine assistant" \
  --message "Report this machine's operating system and free disk space."
```

Chat with the agent in your terminal with `npx omnara agents chat <agent-id>`,
or open it in the dashboard to watch its tool calls and reply.

evidence.heading: Self-host
evidence.text:
Requires Docker with Compose.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/omnara-ai/omnara.git
cd omnara
docker compose -f compose.yaml --profile app up -d
```

Open [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000) and sign up. Local
development prints the verification link in `docker compose logs api`, so no
email provider is needed. To build from source instead of using published
images, run `docker compose --profile app up -d --build`.

A new instance has no models or machines yet. In the console, add a model
provider and a model, connect this computer under **Machines**, and share both
with your project. Sandboxes also work once your instance has a
[public URL](https://docs.omnara.com/self-hosting/deployment#exposing-the-deployment-publicly).

Point the CLI at your instance and log in:

```sh
npx omnara config --api-url http://localhost:8000/api/v1 --issuer-url http://localhost:8000
npx omnara login
```

In `agent.yaml`, use your provider and model names, and replace the
`machine_pool_name` entry with `machine_name: <your machine>`. Then launch it
with the same command as above.

The local defaults are intentionally insecure. For a real deployment, follow
the [self-hosting guide](https://docs.omnara.com/self-hosting/deployment) and
the [configuration reference](https://docs.omnara.com/self-hosting/configuration).

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Your product talks to Omnara, and Omnara runs each agent with the model,
tools, and machines in its config.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph yours["Your side"]
        users(["Your users"]) --> app["Your appREST API · TypeScript SDK"]
        team["Your teamCLI · dashboardSlack · Discord · GitHub"]
    end
    subgraph omnara["Omnara"]
        api["APIlaunch · inputevent stream · approvals"] <--> pg[("Postgreseach agent's event log")] <--> worker["Workersrun the agent loop"]
    end
    subgraph plug[" "]
        models["ModelsOpenAI · AnthropicOpenRouter · self-hosted"]
        tools["Toolsbuilt-in · skillsMCP · custom"]
        machines["Machinessandboxes or your ownlaptop, VM, container"]
    end
    app --> api
    team --> api
    worker --> models
    worker --> tools
    worker --> machines

    classDef side fill:none,stroke:#8b949e,stroke-width:1px
    classDef core fill:#506FCF,stroke:#3D5BB5,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff
    classDef store fill:#3D5BB5,stroke:#2E4794,stroke-width:1px,color:#ffffff
    classDef plugin fill:none,stroke:#85A0E6,stroke-width:1.5px
    class users,app,team side
    class api,worker core
    class pg store
    class models,tools,machines plugin
    style yours fill:none,stroke:#8b949e,stroke-dasharray:4 3
    style omnara fill:#506FCF14,stroke:#506FCF,stroke-width:1.5px
    style plug fill:none,stroke:#85A0E6,stroke-dasharray:4 3
    linkStyle default stroke:#8b949e,stroke-width:1.5px
```

- **API.** Your app, the CLI, and the dashboard all use the same REST API to
  launch agents, send messages, and answer approvals. Events stream back as
  they happen.
- **Postgres.** Every step of every agent is saved here. That record is the
  agent's state, so any worker can pick an agent back up after a crash or
  restart.
- **Workers.*

evidence.heading: Build agents
evidence.text:
- **[Any model](https://docs.omnara.com/organization/model-providers).** Bring
  your own keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock, LiteLLM,
  Ollama, or any compatible endpoint, including models you host yourself.
- **[Tools](https://docs.omnara.com/tools/built-in).** Built-in tools for shell
  commands, files, web search and fetch, and asking a person a question, plus
  [MCP servers](https://docs.omnara.com/tools/mcp) and
  [custom tools](https://docs.omnara.com/tools/custom) that run in your own
  systems.
- **[Skills](https://docs.omnara.com/tools/skills).** Package instructions and
  files once, attach them to any agent, and the agent loads them when it needs
  them.
- **[Memory](https://docs.omnara.com/agents/configuration#memory-stores).**
  Memory stores give agents files that persist between conversations and can
  be shared with other agents, with read or read-write access per agent.
- **[Subagents](https://docs.omnara.com/agents/configuration#subagents).** An agent
  can start subagents with a fresh context, check their progress, and send them
  new instructions. Each subagent is a full agent you can inspect.

evidence.heading: Examples
evidence.text:
Each of these is an `agent.yaml` plus a `SKILL.md` in [`examples/`](examples),
and you can deploy any of them with one prompt to your coding agent.

- [Slack coding agent](examples/slack-coding-agent) fixes issues you mention in
  Slack, Discord, or a GitHub pull request and opens a PR.
- [PR review agent](examples/pr-review-agent) reviews your GitHub pull requests
  against a checkout of the repository and leaves inline findings.
- [SRE agent](examples/sre-agent) investigates production problems such as a
  5xx spike.
- [Browser agent](examples/browser-agent) works in a real browser on
  long-running tasks.
- [PostHog analytics agent](examples/posthog-analytics-agent) compares
  yesterday's product usage with the 7-day average and reports what changed.
- [Reddit](examples/reddit-signal-agent), [X](examples/x-signal-agent), and
  [LinkedIn](examples/linkedin-signal-agent) signal agents summarize the last
  24 hours of posts about a topic you pick.
- [Video generation agent](examples/video-generation-agent) makes short videos
  from a brief.

There are also code samples for a [CLI chat app](examples/cli-agent) built on
the TypeScript SDK, [custom tools over webhooks](examples/custom-tool-webhook),
and a [SharePoint filesystem mount](examples/sharepoint-mount).

evidence.heading: Use Omnara from your coding agent
evidence.text:
**MCP server.** Connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or any MCP client that
supports OAuth to `https://app.omnara.com/mcp` to launch and manage Omnara
agents. You sign in through the browser, so there are no tokens to paste. In
Claude, add it from the
[connectors directory](https://claude.ai/directory/app-omnara-com). Omnara is
also listed in the official MCP Registry as `com.omnara/omnara`.

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http omnara https://app.omnara.com/mcp
codex mcp add omnara --url https://app.omnara.com/mcp
```

Then sign in with `/mcp` in Claude Code or `codex mcp login omnara` in Codex.
See [Connecting MCP clients](https://docs.omnara.com/api/authentication#connecting-mcp-clients).

**CLI.** [`omnara`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/omnara) manages agents,
profiles, machines, model providers, secrets, skills, and cron triggers from
your terminal or your coding agent's shell. Run `npx omnara --help` to start.

**Setup skill.** [`skills/setup-omnara-agent`](skills/setup-omnara-agent/SKILL.md),
also served at [omnara.com/SKILL.md](https://www.omnara.com/SKILL.md), walks a
coding agent through setting up Omnara for your project.

**Docs for LLMs.** [docs.omnara.com/llms.txt](https://docs.omnara.com/llms.txt).

evidence.heading: The problem: motion that falls apart
evidence.text:
Most motion videos an AI makes today — and most template tools — come out **loose**. Title card, fade, UI shot, fade,
feature card, fade, logo. Each shot can look fine and the whole still reads like a slideshow, because nothing
connects one beat to the next: scenes *replace* each other.

evidence.heading: What onetake does differently: every beat is carried
Continuity is measured, not hoped for
evidence.text:
Every film is checked by an oracle before a human watches it. `probe.py` records what is on screen in every frame, finds
each boundary, and asks what carried across it. A film whose beats replace each other fails.

| film | verdict | continuity (carry score) |
|---|---|---|
| an earlier launch film, v1 — perfect rhythm, still a slideshow | rejected | **0.00** |
| the same film, v2 | rejected | **0.40** |
| the same film, v3 — every beat grows out of the last | accepted | **0.75** |
| onetake launch film | accepted | **0.83** |

The same oracle fails uniform cadence (shots all the same length), no stillness, clipped audio, fast moves without
motion blur, and a subject that leaves the frame.

evidence.heading: How a film is made
evidence.text:
1. **Deconstruct the reference in numbers:** how much of it is still, where it cuts, how its moves ease.
2. **Three concepts, pick one.** Each is one sentence about the *picture* — "one dot becomes everything", "one zoom through scale" — not three stories told with the same cards.
3. **A beat sheet for rhythm *and* carry.** Shot lengths vary by ≥ 4×, and every boundary names what survives it.
4. **Compose** one HTML file on the move library. **Render** with motion blur. **Score** the sound from the film's events.
5. **Verify**, then show a human.

evidence.heading: Folkbench Switch
evidence.text:
对新手友好的 AI 编程助手配置工具，Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI 等一键配好，简单易用。[下载 macOS / Windows 版](https://github.com/Folkbench/folkbench/releases)。

macOS：Apple Silicon / Intel（`.dmg`）；Windows：x64（`.exe`）。安装包与 SHA256 校验文件统一在 [Releases](https://github.com/Folkbench/folkbench/releases) 下载。


  
  


Switch 是 Folkbench 配套的开源桌面客户端（基于 Tauri + Rust 构建）。它的核心价值是：**让你在多个中转站和官方线路之间一键切换 Base URL 与 API Key，彻底告别人肉修改配置。**

evidence.heading: 🎯 核心功能
evidence.text:
- 🔄 **一键切换服务商**：保存多家服务的 Base URL 与 API Key，点击即可将配置应用到目标工具，支持随时切换与还原。
- 🛡️ **配置无损与状态保护**：修改前提供配置差异预览。切换 Codex 至第三方服务时，会自动安全暂存官方 ChatGPT OAuth 凭据，切回官方时无损恢复。
- 📈 **探针数据集成**：在客户端内直接查看各站点的公开实时可用率与延迟，切源前确认线路状态。
- 🔒 **本地存储与隐私**：所有 API Key 和配置仅存储在本地设备中，不上传云端，完全离线运行。
- 📊 **本地用量估算**：按会话统计 Token 消耗量，并根据公开参考单价提供调用成本估算。

evidence.heading: 🧰 支持的工具
evidence.text:
Switch 对各工具的配置路径与字段规范进行了适配，切换时仅覆盖连接参数，保留其余自定义设置：

| 工具 | 配置文件 / 路径 | 说明 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Claude Code** | `~/.claude/settings.json` | 自动写入 Base URL，智能处理 Token 与 API Key 凭据类型 |
| **Codex** | `~/.codex/config.toml` | 写入自定义 provider，暂存官方凭据，切回自动恢复 |
| **Gemini CLI** | `~/.gemini/.env` & `settings.json` | 同步写入环境变量与验证方式 |
| **Aider** | `~/.aider.conf.yml` | 写入模型与 API 端点参数 |
| **OpenCode** | `~/.config/opencode/` | 快速注入服务映射与认证 Key |
| **Kimi CLI** | `~/.kimi-code` / `~/.kimi` | 自动兼容新老版本目录 |
| **DeepSeek Harness** | `~/.dsh/` | 适配官方 CLI 环境 |
| **其他** | MiniMax Code、Qwen Code、Grok Build、Hermes、Pi 等 | 持续维护适配中 |

github_projects.name: jevgrep
github_projects.description: Find code by asking what it does. A CLI for coding agents that uses Jev to discover relevant files and source context.
github_projects.description_zh: 通过询问作用来查找代码。用于编码智能体的 CLI，使用 Jev 查找相关文件和源代码上下文。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Find code by asking what it does. A CLI for coding agents that uses Jev to discover relevant files and source context.

evidence.heading: jevgrep
evidence.text:
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dzhng/jevgrep)
[](LICENSE)
[](apps/cli/README.md)
[](https://github.com/dzhng/jevgrep/actions/workflows/publish.yml)

**Same intelligence. ~30% lower cost.**

Find code by asking what it does. In our ten-task SWE-bench comparison, Jevgrep
successfully completed the same 8 of 10 tasks as the baseline, at lower cost.

Coding agents spend part of every unfamiliar task finding the right files.
Jevgrep gives them a place to start: ask a repository question, and `jg` returns
relevant files, reading leads, and verbatim source excerpts in one stdout response.
It uses [Jev](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/jev) to judge relevance across
folders, files, and declarations. Your coding agent then implements and tests the change.

```sh
npm install -g @dzhng/jevgrep
jg auth
jg skill
jg "How are telemetry events recorded and sent?" ./my-project
```

Requires **Node.js 22+**, **macOS, Linux, or Windows**, and a key for **Vercel AI Gateway, TypeSafe, OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, or a custom TypeSafe-compatible endpoint**.
No separate Python, Bun, or ripgrep installation is required to use `jg`.

evidence.heading: Install the agent skill — required for agent setup
evidence.text:
Installing the CLI alone does not teach your coding agent to use it. **Install
the skill as well**, from the project where your agent works:

```sh
jg skill
```

The installer detects your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and
others) and asks where to install. Add `--global` for a user-wide install, or
`--yes` for unattended installation. The
[skill](skills/jevgrep/SKILL.md) explains installation, invocation and the meaning of returned context.
It leaves research and implementation decisions to the calling agent. The current repository skill
checks for `jg` and installs the CLI if it is missing; authentication still needs
your selected provider’s key. The skill installer itself does not configure credentials.

`jg skill` installs the `jevgrep` skill from the repository's `main` branch using
a pinned [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills), with npm lifecycle
scripts disabled. Skill installation needs Node 22.20+ and npm/npx plus network
access for the installer. Rerun `jg skill` to get the current skill without
waiting for a new npm release.

evidence.heading: Upgrade
evidence.text:
There is currently no `jg upgrade` command. Upgrade the CLI with npm:

```sh
npm install -g @dzhng/jevgrep@latest
jg --version
```

After updating the CLI, refresh the installed skill by rerunning `jg skill`.
Updating the npm package does not overwrite skill files in your projects. The
installer records the GitHub source and skill path in `skills-lock.json`; rerun
`jg skill` on another machine or after changing your Node installation. See the
[package guide](apps/cli/README.md) for authentication details.

evidence.heading: Start with a question, leave with source
evidence.text:
Use `jg` when you know the behavior you need to understand but not where it lives:

```sh
jg "Where is authentication checked before a request reaches a handler?" .
jg "How are database connections created, pooled, and closed?" ./src
jg "Which tests cover retry behavior when a request times out?" .
```

Jevgrep explores the repository hierarchy and follows qualifying branches. It
selects files using content previews, then identifies useful source units and
surrounding context. It keeps qualifying file locations even when it cannot
confidently return an excerpt; it does not force every search into a fixed top-two
list.

The summary and compact file list come first, followed by selected source with
line references, then detailed declaration and call locations. Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go and Rust support declaration
parsing, with extensionless Python and Node scripts recognised by their shebang;
other text uses a fallback. The output is evidence for the agent to use,
not a generated answer or a guarantee that every relevant file was found.
[See a recorded output example](specs/done/jevgrep/assets/stdout-example.txt).

When you already know an exact symbol or path, a direct read or `rg` search may be
all you need. Jevgrep is most useful for questions that span unfamiliar files.

evidence.heading: What we measured
evidence.text:
**Same intelligence, ~30% lower coding-agent cost.** Both
Jevgrep and the no-Jev baseline solved **8/10 tasks**. Full Sol cost fell from
**$7.62 to $5.44**—a measured **28.6% reduction**, rounded to ~30%—including failed
attempts and excluding Jev cost.



This comparison uses ten tuned Python SWE-bench tasks, one frozen installed
package and the exact public skill in this repository. It measures task success
and cost, not a speed improvement or guaranteed savings on every repository.
See the [results and methodology](evals/results/relevance-threshold-2026-09-27.md)
for per-task costs, artifact identities and limitations. A separate
[speed study](evals/results/speed-2026-09-28.md) measures the follow-up local
optimizations with Jev’s native TypeSafe endpoint.

The [0.4.3 total-cost rerun](evals/results/total-cost-2026-09-28.md), including
Jev, measured **25.8% lower total cost with the same 8/10 tasks solved**.
The older ~30% graphic above reports Sol-only cost. Future benchmark totals include Jev.

The [0.5.0 evaluation](evals/results/combined-cost-research-2026-09-28.md) retained
8/10 solves while reducing native Jev cost by about 59% versus that 0.4.3 run.
Combined Sol-plus-Jev cost was 2–3% higher, accepted as a small tradeoff for this
release. These single-run observations do not establish statistical equivalence
or a speed improvement.

Current protocols and subsequent experiments are in the
[evaluation records](evals/README.md).

evidence.heading: Source, credentials, and local state
evidence.text:
Searches send eligible source content to Jev through the provider selected during auth. Default
filesystem filtering respects ignore files and excludes hidden, dependency/build,
binary, and obvious credential files, including `.env` variants and any path
component whose name ends in `.env`.
It also excludes a whole file as `sensitive_content` when its text matches a
conservative credential heuristic: a known provider token prefix (such as `npm_`
or `glpat-`), a Slack webhook URL, or a credential-shaped assignment with a
long, high-entropy value. UUID-shaped identifiers are excluded from that entropy
signal. This is best-effort detection, not redaction or a guarantee that all
sensitive information has been removed; choose a search root you intend to send.
Use `--include-sensitive` when a search must include sensitive names, private-key
markers, and content-level matches.
`jg files [root]` counts the files a search under that root may read, grouped by
top-level directory, with no provider key or network request. It takes the same
filtering flags as search.
To skip paths inside that root for one search, pass `--exclude` with a gitignore pattern
relative to the root, for example `--exclude '**/*.test.ts' --exclude 'src/generated/'`.

`jg auth` asks for your provider, then saves its key in an owner-only config file.
Re-running auth replaces that setup; searches always use the saved provider.
`jg doctor` checks it with synthetic input. Existing saved keys without a provider
remain Vercel keys. Environment-based credentials and endpoint overrides are not
used; run `jg auth` if you previously relied on them.
Evaluation answers are cached locally by default. The CLI writes its output to
stdout and does not create report files. Use `jg --help` for cache controls,
search overrides

evidence.heading: Development
evidence.text:
The repository uses TypeScript, Bun workspaces, and Turborepo. From a checkout:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run dev --help
bun run verify
```

Verification includes Docker tests of the installed Node-only package. For the
reasoning behind retrieval, parsing, caching, and failure handling, start with the
[architecture](docs/architecture.md) and [implementation record](specs/done/jevgrep/README.md).
[Release guidance](scripts/RELEASING.md) covers tag-triggered npm publication and
verification of the exact public package.

See [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the pull-request review and maintenance
policy.

**nanoMuse is an open-source personal agent for every device you own.** One agent with a name and a look of its own, in the style of Meta's [Muse](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/): it does things instead of answering questions, keeps working while the app is closed, remembers you, and stops to ask before anything you could not undo.

*nano* means the whole set, small enough to run and deploy yourself: the phone app, the desktop app, the web console and the relay that joins them are all in this repository, under GPL-3.0-or-later. **[Free, open source, non-profit. Let's build it together.](CONTRIBUTING.md)** Sign in and you get a free allowance of model use on the community relay (the developer pays for it); when it is gone, [use your own key](docs/own-key.md). The same relay runs on a server of yours, so nothing has to leave your house. Latest: **1.0.6 Beacon**, [release notes](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/releases/tag/v1.0.6) · [try it in the browser](https://demo.nanomuse.dev/).

> [!NOTE]
> **nanoMuse keeps evolving**
>
> A personal agent should not live only in someone else's cloud, so nanoMuse is the open-source, low-cost alternative: on your own devices, with a model you choose and a relay you can host yourself. We want to build it with developers and users everywhere, so that each person truly owns a personal agent. Open an [issue](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/new/choose) or send a [pull request](CONTRIBUTING.md); either one helps nanoMuse get better.

evidence.heading: What it does
evidence.text: Does things.A Linux shell, a browser, MCP servers and skills, and, with Hands on, the apps on your phone and the windows on your computer through their screens, for everything that never had an API. Asks first.A stop before deleting, sending or paying, remembered for once, this chat or always; passwords and codes are yours to type. A login or a CAPTCHA is handed to you, Done resumes. Reaches your other devices.Say it on the phone, it runs on your PC; @Mac … at the start of a message sends the task there. Approvals come back to the device in your hand. Keeps going.Goals checked on a schedule, routines that run while the app is closed, a feed written for you each morning. Remembers you.What it is, what it knows about you and when it wakes are Markdown files you can read and edit. Lives in your chat apps.It answers in 飞书, 钉钉, 企业微信 and Telegram. A look of its own.Describe one, your image model draws it, a video model makes it move. A small dragon by default. Any model.The relay's allowance, your own key at one of twenty-two providers (Bailian, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek and more), or a plan you already pay for: ChatGPT, Claude, Kimi. A provider without picture or video models leaves those two off, and the app says so.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Each device runs its own agent: the phone inside the APK (Alpine Linux under proot, a shell, a browser, MCP), the computer inside nanoMuse Desktop (DeepSeek Harness with the Python runtime for the hands). Signed in, they meet on the relay and can ask each other for things; the text of the conversations travels through it, files and screenshots stay where they were made.


  


[docs/every-device.md](docs/every-device.md) explains the devices, [docs/hub.md](docs/hub.md) the frames, [docs/cloud.md](docs/cloud.md) the relay, [docs/privacy.md](docs/privacy.md) what it keeps.

evidence.heading: earshot
evidence.text:
**Ears for coding agents.**


[**Watch the 22 s launch film**](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot/releases/tag/v0.1.0) - every sound in it was made
in code by `earshot forge`; no recordings, no music track.



AI coding agents can now write the code that renders a film, a product demo or a game. They still cannot hear what
they made. They cannot tell a premium key press from a cheap one, notice that a hit lands 80 ms after the cut, or
hear that the music swells in the wrong place.

earshot turns sound into evidence an agent can reason about: what a file sounds like in words, how well it fits a
description, the best moment inside a long recording, whether it is a real recording or code-synthesized, a
second-by-second listening transcript of a whole film, an annotated picture of it, and a scorecard against
professional launch films. It runs locally on CPU, as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.

With ears, an agent can also **make its own sounds in code** and improve them by listening (`earshot forge`), and
**translate a recording into code** it can vary (`earshot fit`). Both below.

style those films use: rounded UI pops, wood and plastic knocks, short cut hits and sub hits with a kick, gated

short dark risers, bright swishes, burst glitches and mid dings (the bank now holds 252). A new `launch` kit preset
mixes every effect against the music bed instead of at a fixed level, says where each one sits against the cut (taps
lead it, whoosh peaks land after it) and how close a run may go. And `earshot fit` was re-made against professional

evidence.heading: Make sounds: earshot forge
evidence.text:
Listening makes iteration possible. The agent writes a sound as code: a **recipe** of physical synthesis (modal
resonators, contact excitations, filtered noise, a computed room and a microphone; no recorded audio inside). The
forge renders candidates from the recipe's parameters, and a **critic** built from earshot scores each one:
description match against named confusions, realness, closeness to real reference recordings and measured shape, then
model-free penalties against the references: 1/3-octave tonal balance, the spectro-temporal envelope (a tail that dies
too fast shows here), artifacts (clicks, aliasing, DC / infrasound, harsh resonances, comb ring, cut tails, clipping)
and polish (attack, onset snap, tail smoothness). A cheap model-free **pre-screen** ranks many renders with the same
measurements, so the models only hear the best; an evolutionary **search** keeps the best and mutates them. Then the
agent reads the critic's words ("sounds like: a cork pop, a glass ting", "decay +2.4 outside the refs", "bumpy tail"),
looks at spectrograms next to the references, rewrites the recipe, and runs it again.

```bash
earshot forge --list                             # the recipes (click, impact, keypress, pop, whoosh, ...) + refsets
earshot forge keypress --refs path/to/real/keypresses/ --budget 144 --variants 4 --dir made/keypress
earshot forge whoosh --refset whoosh_fast --budget 96 --dir made/whoosh      # a reference set's 'forge' split
earshot forge whoosh --target "a fast crisp air whoosh" --alts "a wind gust" "a sword swing" \
  --refs path/to/real/whooshes/ --mode real --dir made/whoosh
earshot forge --render keypress --params made/keypress/report.json --seeds 1 2 3 --dir made/again
```

Output (`--dir`): the best diverse sounds as WAVs; `report.md` (what was a

evidence.heading: earshot fit: audio to code
evidence.text:
`earshot fit` translates a recording into code by analysis by synthesis. It fits a small synthesis model with readable
parameters (ringing modes, tracked partials, a time-varying noise gesture, or a layered hybrid of them) until its
render matches the recording, then writes the model as a forge recipe module whose `render()` makes the sound. The
module stores the structure of the sound, not its samples, so it can make new takes, variations (size, damping,
pitch, brightness, decay, ...) and morphs between two recordings.

```bash
earshot fit click.wav -o made/click_fit.py --report    # recipe + its render + side-by-side spectrogram + metrics
python made/click_fit.py 3 take3.wav                   # the module renders on its own (seed 3)
earshot fit --morph a.wav b.wav --amount 0.5 -o made/ab_morph.py
earshot fit --forge made/click_fit.py --budget 96 --dir made/click_variations   # critic-searched variations
```

Measured with the earlier engine (0.2-0.3) on 12 real recordings (2 each of click, key press, pop, impact, fast
whoosh, notification): median CLAP cosine 0.945 between each recording and the render of its generated code (minimum
0.881), and the same top `earshot describe` tag in 10 of 12. In our 12-trial blind test of that engine (recording vs
render, loudness-matched, random order) the listener could not tell which clip was the recording. One listener is a
small test, not a proof. Neither was re-run on 0.4.0, whose choice changed (the gesture model, the CLAP margin rule,
the gate, the finish); its benchmark below is measurement only (CLAP and the mel gap are proxies; nobody listened).
The renders are close, not identical: onsets, tone balance and noise texture still differ measurably; the selection
weights were set on the same 12 recordings; zips, long glides and

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Python 3.10+ and ffmpeg / ffprobe on PATH. CPU only; no GPU is used.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot && cd earshot
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu   # Windows: .venv/Scripts/python
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e ".[mcp,llm,dev]"
.venv/bin/python -m earshot doctor --load
```

The first model use downloads two open models (~1.1 GB) into `.cache/hf` inside the repo (or `EARSHOT_HOME`), each at
a pinned revision with safetensors weights: CLAP `laion/larger_clap_general` @ `16c8cc3` (text-audio embeddings; the
Hub's safetensors conversion of its main revision) and the AudioSet tagger `MIT/ast-finetuned-audioset-10-10-0.4593`
@ `f826b80`. `earshot doctor --fetch` downloads them up front. After that earshot loads them from that cache only and
never contacts the Hub; a damaged cache is an error that names the folder, not a silent new download.

Offline: `EARSHOT_OFFLINE=1`, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1` all mean the same to earshot: it never
downloads, and a model missing from the cache is an error that says so. earshot never sets or clears these variables.

A cache made before 0.2.1 holds CLAP's main revision `ada0c23`, whose only weights are a pickle (`pytorch_model.bin`,
the same tensors). earshot still loads it from the cache (torch `weights_only`), never downloads it, and `earshot
doctor` says so; `earshot doctor --fetch` downloads the pinned safetensors (776 MB), used from then on.

Settings (environment variables): `EARSHOT_THREADS` (torch CPU threads, default min(4, cores/2)), `EARSHOT_HOME`
(cache root), `EARSHOT_PRECISION` (`bf16` by default, used only on CPUs with native bf16 such as AVX512-BF16 / AMX,
fp32 everywhere else; `fp32` forces fp32), `EA

evidence.heading: How good is it?
evidence.text:

earshot cannot judge is in [docs/LIMITS.md](docs/LIMITS.md).

  "strong" verdict is the right kind of sound 98% of the time and the exact variant 61% of the time.
- **Finding the moment**: on a recording of 17 single key presses the found trims land on real key presses; in a

- **Real vs code-synthesized**: held-out ROC-AUC 0.92 with whole sound families held out. Firm verdicts call 6.7% of
  real clips synthesized and 5.5% of synthesized clips real; a fifth of clips get "uncertain".

  of the quiet ones under music). A 60-90 s film takes about 1.5 minutes on a laptop CPU.

文章を生成するAIは日常的な道具となりました。
一方で、AIで生成された文章には独特のクセが残りやすく、そのままでは実務や技術発信に使いにくい場面が多くあります。

これまでに様々な文体調整プロンプトやスキルが試されてきましたが、依然として「AI特有の読みにくさ」が残るケースが見られます。

従来のアプローチが抱えていた限界は、主に次の4点でした。

1. 禁止語の置き換えにとどまる対処  
   「手触り」「解像度」「泥臭い」といった表層の単語を禁止しても、別の曖昧な語へ置き換わるだけで、不自然な文構造そのものは解消されませんでした。
2. 編集ルールの過剰適用  
   修辞の規範を与えすぎると、モデルが指示を過剰に解釈し、かえって不自然な造語や大げさな文体を招いていました。
3. 主述関係の曖昧さと非生物主語  
   誰が何をどうするのかが省略されたまま、概念や道具が比喩的な動詞（壊れる、倒す、効くなど）と結びつき、読み手が文脈を大きく補って読む必要がありました。
4. 形式の偏重と情報密度の低下  
   太字や箇条書きが増える一方で、手順やコードの仕組みといった核心の部分は抽象的に書かれ、文章の量に比べて実際の情報が少なくなっていました。

github_projects.name: openfilm
github_projects.description: The open source AI video agent: turns any coding agent into a video agent, with an editor to change anything it makes.
github_projects.description_zh: 开源 AI 视频智能体：将任何编码智能体转变为视频智能体，并提供一个编辑器，可修改它生成的任何内容。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: The open source AI video agent: turns any coding agent into a video agent, with an editor to change anything it makes.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
The open source AI video agent.

One HTML file, one function, one real editor.

English · 简体中文

evidence.heading: About
evidence.text:
OpenFilm lets your coding agent make videos, and lets you edit them.

Ask Codex, Claude Code or any coding agent to make a film. It writes the film as web pages, and Studio, a local
editor that runs in your browser, shows it taking shape. Then change anything you like, by hand or by asking.

- **One HTML file.** `film.html` cuts animated web pages, footage, pictures and sound together on tracks, styled
  with CSS. Nothing new to learn: your agent already knows the web.
- **One function.** Each shot is a web page that draws any moment with `frame(t)`, using anything a browser can
  draw: three.js, WebGL, canvas, SVG, CSS, GSAP, video and more. No framework (like Remotion or HyperFrames): one
  function is enough.
- **One real editor.** Move, scale and rotate any element inside a page, change its text, color and style; place,
  crop and restyle every clip, trim and cut them on the timeline.


▶ Watch the 1:42 launch video, made with OpenFilm from start to finish.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Requires Node 22.2+ and ffmpeg, on macOS, Windows or Linux (git too, for Studio's saved versions); the first run
downloads a headless Chromium (about 100 MB).

```sh
npx skills add openfilm/openfilm
```

Then ask your agent for a film:

> Make a 20-second launch video for my CLI, with music.

It opens the film in Studio and you watch it take shape. If your agent has no skills, tell it: "Run
`npx -y openfilm@latest` and follow the manual it prints."

Or download the desktop app for macOS or Windows from [openfilm.dev](https://openfilm.dev) or
[Releases](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/releases): Studio with a chat beside it for the agents you have. It
comes with ffmpeg and the headless browser, so there is nothing else to install.

Making, editing and rendering films needs no account. For generated voice, music, images and video, connect the
services you use (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google, fal and others) with your own keys in Studio's Settings → Providers.

To start from a finished film, open one of the [examples](https://github.com/openfilm/examples):

```sh
npx -y openfilm@latest open https://github.com/openfilm/examples/tree/main/one-prompt
```

evidence.heading: Commands
evidence.text:
Your agent runs them; so can you, with `npx -y openfilm@latest <command>` or `npm i -g openfilm`.

```sh
openfilm                          # the manual: all an agent needs to know
openfilm open   [folder | url]    # show a film in Studio: a new one, an existing one, one from GitHub, else this one or the last
openfilm look   [what] [t | a-b]  # check the film, a page or a media file: a contact sheet, one frame, or a range
openfilm render [a-b]             # the MP4; --4k, --blur (motion blur), --alpha (.webm / .mov)
openfilm get    [what]            # voice-over, music, sound effects, transcripts, images, video, from your services
openfilm doctor                   # what this computer has for OpenFilm, to paste into an issue
```

`openfilm <command> --help` lists a command's options; `openfilm get` alone lists what can be made and how to
connect a service in Studio with your own key.

evidence.heading: Studio
evidence.text:
Studio runs on your machine, in your browser: use one built on Chromium (Chrome, Edge), the engine films are drawn
and exported with, so the preview is what you export. Everything in the film can be changed: text and layers in the
picture, clips on the timeline, their place, look, volume and speed, and the subtitles. Your edits are saved to the
film's files, so the agent sees and keeps them, and you can save named versions to go back to. Export a video, a GIF,
the sound or its stems, subtitles, stills, slides, a transparent video, or the timeline itself for Final Cut Pro,
Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve.

The desktop app ([apps/desktop](apps/desktop)) is Studio with a chat beside it, for Claude Code, Codex and the other
agents, or its own agent with your own key.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
A film is a folder with a `film.html`: tracks of clips cut together.

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=1920, height=1080">

<section>
  <iframe src="title.html#t=0,4"></iframe>
</section>
<section>
  <video src="assets/footage.mp4#t=12,18" at="4" speed="0.5" class="card" style="left: 160px; top: 90px; width: 1600px; height: 700px"></video>
</section>
<section>
  <audio src="assets/music.mp3" volume="0.6"></audio>
</section>
```

Each `<section>` is a track, in the order the timeline shows them: the first on top. A clip is an element: a page,
a video, a still picture or a sound. Which part of its file plays is a media fragment (`#t=12,18`), where it starts
is `at`, where it sits is its style's `left`, `top`, `width` and `height`, and how it looks is CSS. Every sound is a
clip of its own. `overrides` hold your changes to elements of a page, and agents keep them when they edit.

A page is a web page that draws any moment of itself, and that is the whole contract:

```html

```

**The one rule:** the same `t` always draws the same picture, whatever was drawn before. Frames are asked for out of
order, in parallel and between frames (for motion blur), so a page that keeps the rule renders the same at any size,
on any machine. Anything else that makes pictures (Python, Blender, a video model) comes in as video or images.

OpenFilm spends its effort where models fail: checking the film. `look` draws every frame of its sheet twice, in two
shuffled orders, and names any that changed, along with page errors, fonts that failed to load, missing sound files,
and text cut off by the frame.

[MANUAL.md](packages/openfilm/MANUAL.md) is what `openfilm` tells your agent; [SPEC.md](packages/openfilm/SPEC.md)
is for anyone building a player, renderer or editor.

evidence.heading: From source
evidence.text:
You need Node 22.18 or later, pnpm 9 (`corepack enable` gives you the version this repository names), ffmpeg on the
PATH, and git.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm && cd openfilm
pnpm install
pnpm dev            # Studio from this checkout, with a sample film, beside an installed OpenFilm
pnpm test
```

Tell your coding agent to run `packages/openfilm/.dev/bin/openfilm` and it makes films with your checkout, in that
Studio. Every OpenFilm, installed or from source, keeps its projects in the same library.

`pnpm dev:desktop` runs the desktop app from source, and `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build` and `pnpm audit:public` do
what they say.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the details of each package.

github_projects.description: Your personal AI agent in your own Cloudflare account. Chat, memory, tasks, notes and scheduled reminders, deployed with one command: npx create-talorys@latest. Free-tier friendly, single-user, no telemetry.
github_projects.description_zh: 你在自己的 Cloudflare 账户中的个人 AI 智能体。聊天、记忆、任务、笔记和计划提醒，一条命令部署：npx create-talorys@latest。适合免费层，单用户，无遥测。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Your personal AI agent in your own Cloudflare account. Chat, memory, tasks, notes and scheduled reminders, deployed with one command: npx create-talorys@latest. Free-tier friendly, single-user, no telemetry.

evidence.heading: Talorys
evidence.text:
**Your personal AI agent. Your own cloud.**

Website: [rociiu.github.io/talorys](https://rociiu.github.io/talorys/)

Talorys is a free, open-source personal AI assistant that runs entirely inside
**your own Cloudflare account**. It chats with you, remembers what matters,
manages tasks, notes and projects, and runs reminders and routines on a
schedule — without any server, database or account operated by the Talorys
developers.

One person. One Cloudflare account. One command. One personal AI agent.

```bash
npx create-talorys@latest
```

Or install it with [Appflare](https://appflare.dev), which deploys it as a
[single Worker](docs/deployment.md#one-worker-without-pages):

[](https://appflare.dev/install/talorys/)

---

evidence.heading: 1. What Talorys is
evidence.text:
- **A private assistant** — chat with streaming responses, Markdown and tool activity indicators.
- **Memory** — durable personal facts and preferences you can view, edit and delete. Only the most relevant memories are sent to the model on each turn.
- **Semantic recall (optional)** — finds memories by meaning as well as keyword, lists them newest first with their saved date, and lets the agent find tasks, notes and automations by meaning. Off by default; turn it on with the **Semantic memory recall** switch near the bottom of Settings → AI (its other settings appear once it is on), or install with `--semantic`. See [docs/semantic-recall.md](docs/semantic-recall.md).
- **Memory history** — facts that change over time: when you say you sold your car, Talorys asks you whether the old one is now a past fact, and with the optional AI check a confident answer does it for you. Unclear conflicts also wait for your review. See [docs/memory-history.md](docs/memory-history.md).
- **Tasks, notes and projects** — full CRUD in the UI, and from chat ("Add a task to review my project tomorrow"). Chat task due dates reject impossible calendar dates, including timestamps with explicit UTC offsets.
- **AI task planning** — describe a goal ("Plan the tasks to launch my iOS app next month") and Talorys proposes a plan as an interactive card in chat. Review, edit or remove tasks, pick a project, then confirm: nothing is created until you do, and confirming creates everything at once, exactly once.
- **Automations** — one-time and recurring reminders, daily task digests and optional AI routines, delivered to an in-app notification center. They run on Durable Object alarms, so nothing has to stay online.
- **Push notifications** — reminders, digests and routines also arrive as system notifica

evidence.heading: Screenshots
evidence.text:
| Chat with tool activity | Tasks |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |
| **Memory (dark mode)** | **Automations** |
|  |  |

evidence.heading: 2. How it works
evidence.text:
```
Browser ──HTTPS──▶ Cloudflare Pages (React app + /api Pages Function)
                         │  service binding (no public URL)
                         ▼
                   Private Worker (Hono router)
                         │  getAgentByName("personal-agent")
                         ▼
                   TalorysAgent — Cloudflare Agents SDK Durable Object
                     ├─ SQLite: conversations, memories, tasks, notes, projects,
                     │          automations, sessions, settings, usage
                     ├─ Workers AI: @cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash (streaming + tool calling)
                     └─ Alarms: reminders and recurring schedules
```

- The browser only ever talks to your `*.pages.dev` site. `/api/*` requests run a
  Pages Function that forwards them over a **service binding** to the agent Worker.
- The agent Worker is deployed with `workers_dev: false` and `preview_urls: false`:
  it has **no public URL**.
- Authentication and authorization happen in the Worker, not the frontend.
- Chat responses stream as Server-Sent Events end-to-end.

More detail: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

evidence.heading: 3. Cloudflare services used
evidence.text:
| Service | Used for | Free plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloudflare Pages | Frontend + Pages Function | Yes |
| Cloudflare Workers | Private API Worker | Yes |
| Durable Objects (SQLite) | All data, scheduling alarms | Yes |
| Workers AI | Chat model (`@cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash`) | Yes, daily allocation |

Talorys does **not** provision R2, D1, KV, Vectorize, AI Search, Workflows or any
paid service.

evidence.heading: 4. Deploy
evidence.text:
```bash
npx create-talorys@latest
```

The installer:

1. Checks Node.js (22+) and uses its bundled Wrangler CLI (any globally installed `wrangler`/`cf` is detected but not required).
2. Verifies your Cloudflare login, or **opens Cloudflare's authorization page in your browser**.
3. Lets you choose an account (if you have several) and an agent name.
4. Asks for an owner password (hidden input, strength-checked). It is hashed locally with PBKDF2-SHA256 and stored only as a Cloudflare secret.
5. Generates a 256-bit session secret, a Web Push key pair, and unique resource names (`talorys-<id>-agent`, `talorys-<id>-web`).
6. Deploys the private Worker (creating its SQLite Durable Object), stores secrets, creates and deploys the Pages project with the service binding.
7. Verifies the live deployment (frontend, auth endpoint, unauthenticated rejection, storage health) **without** running any AI inference.
8. Prints the real `https://….pages.dev` URL reported by Cloudflare.

It writes a `talorys/` directory containing `talorys.json` (installation id,
account id, resource names, URL — **no secrets**) and the deployable artifacts.
Keep it for updates.

**Interrupted?** Run the same command again in the same place. It reconciles
what already exists: no duplicate resources, no password re-prompt if the
password is already configured, and **no data is ever deleted**.

Non-interactive installs: `TALORYS_OWNER_PASSWORD=... npx create-talorys@latest --yes --account-id <id>`
(with `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` set if you are not logged in).

evidence.heading: Permissions
evidence.text:
Browser login uses Wrangler's standard OAuth flow — no Global API Key. If you
use an API token instead, it needs:

- Account › Workers Scripts › Edit
- Account › Cloudflare Pages › Edit
- Account › Workers AI › Read
- Account › Account Settings › Read
- User › User Details › Read (optional; shows your email)

See [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md).

github_projects.description: A design system for AI applications. Material, physical, tactile, technical.
github_projects.description_zh: 面向 AI 应用的设计系统，强调材质感、空间厚度、触感与精密的技术视觉。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: A design system for AI applications. Material, physical, tactile, technical.

evidence.heading: Solid Glass
evidence.text:
[The style](#the-style) · [Install](#install) · [What is here](#what-is-here) · [Contributing](#contributing)

[](https://github.com/deeplethe/solid-glass/stargazers)
[](LICENSE)
[](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/docs/components/status-glyph)
[](https://ui.shadcn.com)

[](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass)
[](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/r/registry.json)
[](https://tailwindcss.com)
[](https://react.dev)
[](https://github.com/deeplethe)



A refined glass-inspired aesthetic that feels solid from afar and reveals its subtle materiality up
close. Delicate highlights, fine borders, and soft shadows create depth, while a restrained finish
emphasizes clarity, stability, and a sense of solidity over transparency, refraction, and fluidity.

[](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/blocks)

That is one of the [blocks](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/blocks): whole screens made of the
components, to look at, read and copy in. Below, the components themselves.





It stands between flat design and liquid glass. Flat is an opaque block with no finish to speak of;
liquid glass is nearly clear, and on a page with a lot of text the reader is always fighting the
background for the words. Solid Glass lets only an outline through: enough to know it is glass, not
enough to get in the way of reading.

evidence.heading: The style
evidence.text:
| | |
|---|---|
| **Tactility** | Interfaces that feel tangible. Every interaction carries a subtle sense of touch and response. |
| **Precision** | Clean geometry, refined details, and restrained lighting create a precise, technical aesthetic. |
| **Physicality** | Depth comes from thickness, shadow, and spatial hierarchy, giving every element a sense of physical presence. |
| **Materiality** | Subtle edge highlights, fine borders, and soft shadows define the character of each surface. |

evidence.heading: Why it is built this way
evidence.text:
AI applications are built around information that is constantly changing — responses streaming in,
agents performing tasks, and decisions waiting for human input.

Solid Glass keeps the interface calm and readable. Neutral surfaces reduce visual distractions,
depth establishes hierarchy, and color and motion are reserved for meaningful feedback.

The entire system is built with lightweight CSS and works with existing shadcn/ui components in both
light and dark modes.

The [Material](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/docs/material) page shows how a pane is made,
and the [Create](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/create) page lets you turn the dials.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Solid Glass is one stylesheet. It finds each part of a shadcn/ui component by the `data-slot` and
the classes it already carries, so the components you have need no changes.

Start from a shadcn/ui project (React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, the Base UI components):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest init
```

Add the stylesheet, straight from this repository:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add deeplethe/solid-glass/solid-glass
```

Import it after Tailwind and shadcn's stylesheet, and delete the `:root` and `.dark` colour
variables that `shadcn init` wrote (Solid Glass defines the same names):

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "tw-animate-css";
@import "shadcn/tailwind.css";
@import "./solid-glass.css";
```

Dark is the material as designed; light is there too. The
[installation page](https://deeplethe.github.io/solid-glass/docs/installation) has the rest.

Solid Glass's own components install the same way:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add deeplethe/solid-glass/status-glyph
```

| Component | What it is |
|---|---|
| `status-glyph` | Three points of light that say a turn is going, and what it is doing. |
| `panel`, `tag`, `dot-loader` | The thinnest pane, a small label, and a row of dots that waits. |
| `turn-status`, `composer`, `tool-steps`, `diff-view`, `ask-card`, `context-ring`, `task-notice`, `reasoning` | For interfaces where an agent works: its status line, the box you write to it in, the steps it took, a diff, a question it asks, how full its context is, a notice from a task, and its thinking. |

evidence.heading: What is here
evidence.text:
| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/solid-glass.css` | The theme. The whole material in one file: colours, the three thicknesses of glass, the one state, motion. It defines shadcn/ui's own variable names. |
| `registry.json` | The registry: what `shadcn add` installs from. Written by `scripts/build-registry.mjs`, which also builds `public/r/` for the site. |
| `src/components/ui/` | The components the site shows. shadcn/ui's (Base UI, `base-nova`), installed with its command line, and Solid Glass's own. A few of shadcn/ui's (`button`, `input`, `tabs`, `dialog`, `dropdown-menu`, `sheet`, `sidebar` and some form controls) differ from stock in small ways; the stylesheet does not depend on those differences. |
| `src/create/`, `src/pages/create.tsx` | The Create page: the material with its dials out (thickness, tint, chart colour, type, radius, rim, blur), a preview that takes each choice as it is made, and the few lines of CSS that come of it. `options.ts` says what each choice does to the stylesheet's variables; the preview cards are shadcn/ui's. |
| `src/blocks/`, `src/pages/blocks.tsx` | Blocks: whole screens made of the components, shown on the Blocks page in a frame of their own (`/view/<name>`). The single files at the top of the folder are Solid Glass's own (`agent-workspace`) and are in its registry; the folders are shadcn/ui's blocks in the material, installed from shadcn/ui. |
| `src/examples/` | One small file per example, as on ui.shadcn.com: shadcn/ui's own examples, and Solid Glass's for its own components. |
| `content/` | The documentation. `components/` is shadcn/ui's page for each component; `solid/` and `docs/` are Solid Glass's. |
| `src/site/`, `src/pages/`, `src/home/` | The site: header, sidebar, component preview, and the wall of cards on the hom

evidence.heading: Run
evidence.text:
```bash
npm install
npm run dev         # http://localhost:5191
npm run build       # into dist/
npm run typecheck
```

`/dev/banner` (development only) is the banner above, drawn with the theme: `docs/banner-5.webp` is a
screenshot of it in an 820 by 200 window at twice the size, saved as WebP like the other pictures
here (a quarter of the size of the same picture as PNG). When the picture changes, save it under
the next number and point the README at that: GitHub serves a README's pictures from one address
per file, whatever is added to the link, and a browser keeps what it fetched from it.

`/dev/examples` (development only) mounts every example at once and lists any that fail. It takes
`?q=button,card` to show some of them, `?theme=light`, `?hover=<selector>` to show what matches as
if the pointer were on it, and `?click=<selector>` to press something and look at what it opens.

`SOLID_GLASS_ORIGIN` is the address the site is served from (Solid Glass's own components name one
another by it) and `SOLID_GLASS_BASE` the path it lives under there; the defaults are this
repository's GitHub Pages.

evidence.heading: Add a component of Solid Glass's own
evidence.text:
1. `src/components/ui/<name>.tsx`, written like a shadcn/ui component: function components, a
   `data-slot` on every part, `cn()` from `@/lib/utils`.
2. `src/examples/<name>-demo.tsx`, and one file per further example.
3. `content/solid/<name>.mdx`: front matter (`title`, `description`), then
   `<ComponentPreview name="<name>-demo" />`, Installation, Usage, and a heading per example.

Keep to the four rules (the Material page shows them): the finish is at the edge; heavy, not airy;
depth is thickness; one state.
