evidence.heading: ⚠️ Read first — authorized use and legal notice
evidence.text:
ARTEX may be used **only against targets you own or for which you have explicit written authorization.** Any scanning, probing, or exploitation beyond the authorized scope may itself be illegal.

- In the Republic of Korea, intruding into or disrupting another party's information and communications network without authorization violates the **Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection** (정보통신망법).
- Personal data collected or exposed during a penetration test is subject to the Korean **Personal Information Protection Act** (개인정보보호법). Even with authorization, handle the access, retention, and deletion of personal data with care.
- Wherever you are, comply with your own jurisdiction's laws on network security, data protection, and computer crime.
- Use this for **learning, research, and verification in locally isolated environments.** Before targeting any live external system, secure written authorization and an agreed scope and time window.

Full license terms, usage restrictions, and the disclaimer are in the [License and disclaimer](#license-and-disclaimer) section below. Using this tool constitutes your agreement to those terms.

---

evidence.heading: Why a global edition
evidence.text:
Upstream ARTEX has its prompts, UI, and documentation entirely in Chinese, which made it cumbersome for anyone who does not read Chinese to read the results and share them with a team. This edition aims to:

- **Localize the output** — the findings, fact summaries, final reports, and chat replies that agents surface to a human are forced into the selected language (English by default; Korean, Chinese, Spanish, and Japanese selectable). Commands, payloads, code, URLs, and raw logs are needed for analysis and are left in their original form.
- **Preserve performance** — the internal reasoning prompts (the behavioral instruction body) that drive the agents' judgment are **not** translated. Behavior benchmarked in the original language is kept intact, and only the output language is changed, avoiding the quality drift that translation introduces.
- **State the legal boundaries** — the "authorized scope only" warning is stated clearly, together with Korea-specific notices on network and privacy law (the maintainers are based in Korea); the law of wherever you operate applies as well.
- **Support diverse LLM stacks** — the LLM provider can be swapped from a frontier model to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (domestic or open models). See [Configuration](#configuration).

> The boundaries and design policy of this multilingual edition are documented in more detail in the repository's working notes. To make it easy to diff against the upstream repository, the original Chinese document is preserved as [`README.zh.md`](README.zh.md).

---

evidence.heading: Quick start (Docker Compose)
evidence.text:
> **Prerequisites:** Docker and Docker Compose. The database is **PostgreSQL**, brought up by compose. Exploration requires an **LLM** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`; can also be set in the UI).

> **Image:** the `artex` service in `docker-compose.yml` pulls `ghcr.io/jiwoochris/artex-global`, the global-edition image this repository publishes to GitHub Container Registry on every release tag (`v*`). The default tag is `latest` (the most recent release); set `ARTEX_TAG` in `.env` to pin a specific release. Upstream's original image `autumn27/artex` has been taken down from Docker Hub and is no longer used.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jiwoochris/artex-global.git
cd artex-global
cp .env.example .env          # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is optional
docker compose up -d          # brings up the artex image + postgres together
# → open http://localhost:8787 (on first visit, set the admin password at /setup)
#   /setup asks for the setup token printed in the startup log: docker compose logs artex | grep -F '[auth]'
```

The image bundles common tools (ripgrep, curl, vim, npm, nmap, and more), and when brought up with compose, `./skills` and `./data` are bind-mounted to the host and survive container recreation.

evidence.heading: Other installation methods
evidence.text:
Upstream provides several methods: an install script (`./install.sh`), precompiled binaries (Releases), and a single-binary build from source. The commands and full procedure are collected in the "安装" (Installation) section of [`README.zh.md`](README.zh.md#安装) (in Chinese); the essentials are reproduced below.

- **Install script:** running `./install.sh` detects/installs Docker and then lets you choose "① all-in-Docker" or "② local compile and run." "① all-in-Docker" pulls and starts the same image as the quick start above (`ghcr.io/jiwoochris/artex-global`), while "② local compile and run" builds it yourself the same way as the **single-binary build from source** below.
- **Single-binary build from source:**

  ```bash
  cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd ..   # 1) static frontend build
  rm -rf server/webui/dist && mkdir -p server/webui/dist && cp -a web/out/. server/webui/dist/   # 2) sync into the embed directory (avoids nesting on rebuild)
  CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex   # 3) compile with the frontend embedded
  ./start.sh                                          # → http://localhost:8787
  ```

> The `npm ci` in step 1) installs the devDependencies the build needs (e.g. `@tailwindcss/postcss`). If your shell has `NODE_ENV=production` set, `npm ci` skips devDependencies and the build fails with `Error: Cannot find module '@tailwindcss/postcss'`; in that case install with `npm ci --include=dev`.

> Launch with `start.sh` (`start.bat` on Windows) rather than running `./artex` directly. That script is a supervisor that restarts the program based on its exit code, and it also handles the UI's "one-click update."

---

evidence.heading: System architecture
evidence.text: ARTEX is an **autonomous penetration system driven by LLM multi-agents.** It uses a single Go backend (with the Next.js frontend embedded) over PostgreSQL, and the agent capabilities are provided by the [`norma`](https://github.com/Autumn-27/norma) (currently unreachable, checked 2026-10) SDK. At its core is a **dual-graph structure** and the two autonomy mechanisms around it: process-level information exchange between workers, and the planner's multi-round shared todolist.

evidence.heading: Usage restrictions
evidence.text:
- Use this tool to **read and study the source code**, and to **verify its technical principles in a locally isolated environment.**
- Unless the target is one you own or for which you have **explicit written authorization**, do not scan, probe, exploit, or attack any website, online service, or connected system.
- Using it for illegal intrusion, data theft, denial of service (DoS), or any other destructive or criminal activity is strictly prohibited.
- You must comply with all laws on network security, data protection, and computer crime in your country and region (in Korea, the 정보통신망법, 개인정보보호법, and others).

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text: Blazingly fast 3D animation engine for agents, compatible with Manim CE's API. Powered by Rust and wgpu. Install with a prompt or pip. Run in the browser. Documentation · Quickstart · Examples · API Reference **36.2 seconds of video, rendered in 3.08 seconds.** Across five scenes at 1080p60 on an Apple M4 Pro, ManimGX is **90.6× faster than ManimCE**, **11.5× faster than ManimGL**, and **18.7× faster than Blender Workbench**, from launch to finished MP4. [How it was measured](https://github.com/academa-labs/manimgx/tree/main/benchmarks): the scenes, the settings and every run. **Compare the same scene.** Linked rings at 2.5 seconds, rendered by each engine. | ManimGX | ManimCE | ManimGL | Blender Workbench | Blender EEVEE | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | | | | | |

evidence.heading: Get started
evidence.text:
**With a prompt.** Paste into Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor. Your agent handles setup:

```text
Follow https://manimgx.academa.ai/llms.txt.
Install ManimGX, make a 3D animation of the solar system, and open it.
```

**With pip.** Install on macOS, Linux or Windows with Python 3.13+:

```sh
pip install manimgx
```

Fonts, typesetting and video encoding are included.
For editor setup and a guided first animation, follow the
[Quickstart](https://manimgx.academa.ai/user-guide/quickstart/).

evidence.heading: From Python to MP4
evidence.text:
Save this as `scene.py`:

```python
import manimgx as m


class Hello3D(m.ThreeDScene):
    def construct(self) -> None:
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=65 * m.DEGREES, theta=-45 * m.DEGREES)
        self.begin_ambient_camera_rotation(rate=0.5)
        cube = m.Cube(side_length=3, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        self.play(m.Create(cube), run_time=2)
        self.wait(4)
```

Render it:

```sh
manimgx render scene.py
```

You get `Hello3D.mp4`, a 1080p60 video:

evidence.heading: Why ManimGX?
evidence.text:
**An API for 3D video in the age of agents.** Your agent writes Python using
[Manim CE's API](https://www.manim.community).
ManimGX's Rust + wgpu engine renders the MP4, blazingly fast.

- **Fully statically typed.** Keyword arguments and `.animate` chains included.
- **2D and 3D together.** Surfaces, meshes and moving cameras alongside text, equations
  and plots.
- **Runs in the browser.** `npm install manimgx`. [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) runs
  Python in a Web Worker; WebGPU renders the scene.
  [Embed a scene](https://manimgx.academa.ai/user-guide/rendering/#embed-in-a-web-page) with no render server.
- **Agent feedback.** [`manimgx inspect`](https://manimgx.academa.ai/user-guide/rendering/#inspect): storyboards and 2D layout checks, at play endings or times you choose.
- **Text and math.** Write LaTeX or Typst. No LaTeX installation needed.
- **Speech in sync.** [Match animations to spoken words](https://manimgx.academa.ai/user-guide/sound-and-voice/)
  with `self.say()`.

evidence.heading: Documentation
evidence.text:
**[manimgx.academa.ai](https://manimgx.academa.ai)** has the guides, rendered examples
with source code, and API reference:

- [Quickstart](https://manimgx.academa.ai/user-guide/quickstart/): install, set up your
  editor, and render your first scene.
- [User Guide](https://manimgx.academa.ai/user-guide/the-basics/): learn scenes,
  animations, 3D, text and sound, one idea at a time.
- [Examples](https://manimgx.academa.ai/gallery/): watch complete films and read the
  Python that makes them.
- [API Reference](https://manimgx.academa.ai/reference/): look up classes, methods
  and their typed parameters.
- [Coming from Manim CE](https://manimgx.academa.ai/user-guide/coming-from-manim-ce/):
  adapt existing scenes and check where behavior differs.

For agents, [llms.txt](https://manimgx.academa.ai/llms.txt) provides setup instructions
and links to the documentation as Markdown.

evidence.heading: On the shoulders of giants
evidence.text:
[Grant Sanderson](https://www.3blue1brown.com) created
[Manim](https://github.com/3b1b/manim). ManimGX targets the API of
[Manim Community Edition](https://www.manim.community), the widely used
community-maintained fork.

The Rust renderer uses [wgpu](https://wgpu.rs) for native GPU rendering and WebGPU in
the browser. Its 3D lighting is adapted from Google's
[Filament](https://github.com/google/filament): physically based materials,
image-based lighting, ambient occlusion, bloom and AgX tone mapping.
[Typst](https://typst.app) typesets text and math, with
[mitex](https://github.com/mitex-rs/mitex) translating LaTeX input to Typst.
[x264](https://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html) encodes native video exports as
H.264; [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) decodes imported audio, using
[libopus](https://opus-codec.org) for Opus.

[Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) runs Python scenes in a browser worker. Linux wheels
bundle [Mesa](https://mesa3d.org)'s lavapipe for Vulkan rendering on the CPU when no
suitable GPU is available.

evidence.heading: Community
evidence.text:
ManimGX is an open-source project by [Academa](https://academa.ai), created by [Abdullah Geduk](https://geduk.io) and [Sina Atalay](https://sinaatalay.com). We welcome contributions from the community.

Questions, bug reports and feature requests start with an
[issue](https://github.com/academa-labs/manimgx/issues/new/choose).
To contribute, read [Contributing](https://github.com/academa-labs/manimgx/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)
and the [Developer Guide](https://manimgx.academa.ai/developer-guide/).

[Changelog](https://manimgx.academa.ai/changelog/) ·
[Citing ManimGX](https://github.com/academa-labs/manimgx/blob/main/CITATION.cff)

Everyone participating follows the
[Code of Conduct](https://github.com/academa-labs/manimgx/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
Report vulnerabilities privately through the
[security policy](https://github.com/academa-labs/manimgx/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md).

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: UI design skill for Claude Code, Codex and other AI agents: explore distinct directions, compare them side by side, refine against real screenshots. 给 AI Agent 用的 UI 设计 Skill。

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
English · [中文](README.zh-CN.md)


  



  


Oil UI is an interface design skill for AI agents. It explores a few genuinely different design directions side by side, lets you choose one, then refines it against real screenshots. It works for websites, apps, dashboards, and components. See more designs at [ui.oiloil.org](https://ui.oiloil.org/en/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=readme-en).

evidence.heading: How it designs
evidence.text:
1. **Understand what the product is.** Before drawing anything, it names the product category, finds two or three peers with the most distinctive styles, and looks at what they do and why. Then it decides what to keep and what to change.
2. **Turn “premium” and “clean” into real decisions.** Everyone uses these words, but they don't tell you what to put on the screen. It first sets the tone from the subject, audience, and brand voice, such as lively or calm, polished or raw, dense or airy. Then it turns that tone into visible choices: which typefaces, how much white space, and how much of the page uses color.
3. **Start each direction from something concrete.** That could be a material in its setting, a scene, a character, or the visual language of another field. Ideas come from the product itself, not from adjectives like “minimal” or “bold.”
4. **Decide who the first screen is for.** On pages where people browse, shop, or get work done, the first screen should be the content itself. Only pages meant to persuade need a designed opening layout, settled before the copy is written.
5. **Make the directions truly different.** Of layout, typography, color, and key imagery, any two directions may share at most one. Once the previews exist, it puts them side by side and squints at the light and dark shapes of each first screen. If two look alike, it changes the layout instead of just swapping colors.

The composer **Undo once** and **Undo last round** follow official DSH `session.fork({ atSeq })`: the withdrawn turn is cut off, a new session keeps the earlier context, the old session is archived, and the line returns to the input so **send again** re-injects. `/rewind` does the same.

evidence.heading: Handwired
evidence.text: Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net; no training, exact, yet also fully differentiable!

evidence.heading: How It Works
evidence.text:
A program's made of if-else, loops, and state. Handwired transforms them into matrix multiplication + reglu over floats. For example:

```ts
const a = 5
const result = (a > 4) ? 10 : 12
```

The above can be expressed as basic arithmetic:

```ts
const a = 5
// Math.max(0, x) is ReLU. For an integer a, above4 is 1 if a > 4, and 0 otherwise
const above4 = Math.max(0, a - 4) - Math.max(0, a - 5)
// Both branches compute, and above4 picks one
const result = above4 * 10 + (1 - above4) * 12
```

You can calculate that by hand and see that both arrive at the same result.

We then collect the + and * and relu into a giant matmul, and either run it on JS or WebGPU, for fun.

Because we basically only use these 2 primitives:
- the full program stays differentiable
- the weights don't need training since they're written manually
- existing gpu techniques, such as fusion, sparsity, reordering, have a great time optimizing such minimal primitives

This unlocks lots of funny use-cases, like:
- unfreezing the weights and train them (what does that even do? Let's find out!)
- attaching a specific frozen program to a generic neural net and train end-to-end (now a nanoGPT can do both Shakespeare and your particular UI?)
- achieving GPU-level of parallelism with JS code that was written in a traditional single-threaded way (see the JSON search demo that runs in milliseconds over 100k documents)

evidence.heading: ts-rust (aka tsc-rs)
evidence.text:
I wanted to see if LLMs could port the TypeScript compiler, checker and lsp to Rust. Turns out they can.

It [cost over $420,000](#how-did-this-go) in tokens to do it, but you could probably have done it for ~$20k (see below).

evidence.heading: Benchmark: T3 Code with Effect diagnostics
evidence.text:
Full type check of [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code) with Effect diagnostics on.\*
Time is the sum of the medians for its five checked projects. Lower is faster. Bar length is
in proportion to time. See [Benchmark: T3 Code](#benchmark-t3-code) for the method and the run
without Effect diagnostics.

| Checker | Time | Relative time | Speed vs tsc 7 |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| `tsc-rs --fast` | 9.77s | █ | 4.35× |
| `tsc-rs` | 14.30s | ██ | 2.98× |
| `tsc` 7 | 42.55s | █████ | baseline |
| `bun check` | 59.24s | ███████ | 0.72× |
| `tsc` 6 | 191.00s | ████████████████████████ | 0.22× |

\* `tsc-rs` is 0.6.0 with Effect diagnostics built in. `tsc` 7 is from `@effect/tsgo`. The
`bun check` time adds a separate `effect-tsgo diagnostics` run. `tsc` 6 uses the JavaScript
Effect plugin.

evidence.heading: Motivations
evidence.text:
- Test model capabilities
- Make a fast TypeScript type checker
- Make a ts checker that can work in WASM with high performance
- Memes

evidence.heading: Warnings
evidence.text:
**This is an early release.** It has 100% compatibility in every real world project we have
tested. It should work as a drop in
replacement for the vast majority of apps. See [Known problems](#known-problems).

Also worth mentioning: I've never read a line of this code.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Be warned, I have no idea if this will actually work.

```sh
npm install -D tsc-rs
npx tsc-rs -p tsconfig.json
```

evidence.heading: How did this go?
evidence.text:
I used a lot of OpenAI models to try and complete this port. In total I did **over $400,000 in API priced tokens with GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT 6 Astra**. They wrote over 1.3m lines of Rust over multiple months of /goal loops and never got past like 84% compat.

When I saw how little my Claude Code limits were burning, I figured it'd be fun to throw Opus 5.5 at this. It had a working v0 in 10 hours.

I assumed it kept using the code the Codex models wrote. I was wrong. **Opus 5.5 started from scratch. It got further than Astra in 1/10th the time.**

I let it keep going, and it definitely did. Total token spend was **~$24,047 of API spend over 2 weeks**. I was using my Claude accounts, and it worked out to somewhere between **925% and 983% of my $200 plan weekly limits**.

Expensive, for sure, but not that bad considering how much work has gone into typescript-go.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
```sh
npm install -D tsc-rs
npx tsc-rs -p tsconfig.json
```

`tsc-rs` takes the same options as `tsc`. The npm package is `tsc-rs` so that it does not clash
with the `typescript` package. To use tsc-rs as the `typescript` package (its `tsc` bin, its JS API
and the TypeScript 7 VS Code extension), install
[@tsc-rs/typescript](npm/typescript-readme.md) under that name (from the first release after
0.7.0):

```json
{ "devDependencies": { "typescript": "npm:@tsc-rs/typescript@<version>" } }
```

Each [release](https://github.com/pingdotgg/ts-rust/releases) also has a standalone archive per
platform: the `tsc` binary with the lib files next to it.

Platforms: Linux x64 and arm64 (static, any distribution), macOS arm64, and (from the first
release after 0.2.0) macOS x64, Windows x64 and Windows arm64.

To use it in VS Code, see [@tsc-rs/typescript](npm/typescript-readme.md#vs-code).

evidence.heading: What it is

Claude Opus 5.5 made every film by writing code from a prompt: the picture, the animation, the music and the sound effects. - **No image or video generation.** The picture is code: SVG, Canvas, WebGL and Three.js, with Blender for the 3D film. A few films use CC0 or public-domain photos.
- **The sound is code too.** Each film's `audio.py` synthesises its music and sound effects; the 15 soundtracks draw on 103 recorded instrument samples.
- **Everything is published.** The film, the style notes, the full prompt and the complete source, for all 15 styles.

evidence.heading: How a film is made
evidence.text: Every film is a web page that draws the frame for any time you give it (`window.renderAt(t)`). The renderer captures each frame in headless Chrome, then ffmpeg joins the frames and the soundtrack. The 3D film is the one exception: Blender renders its picture, and a web page adds the type and grain. Each film went through two rounds of review and revision. Final scores from the AI jury run from 7.57 to 8.21 out of 10.

evidence.heading: Make a film from a prompt
evidence.text:
1. Open an AI assistant that can write code and run commands (for example Claude Code) in an empty folder. The machine needs Node, Chrome and ffmpeg; the suggested route for the 3D style uses Blender.
2. Open any file in `prompts/` and send the whole prompt block.
3. To make it your own: only `Creative seed` is a specific story. Replace its story, brand name, copy and colours with yours, or change `Output` to vertical 1080×1920 or another length. Keep `Signature features`: it is what makes the style recognisable at a glance.
4. To push it further: once the film is done, have a second AI review it with [rubric.md](rubric.md) and paste the review back for another round. The original films went through make → review → revise twice.
5. To write a new style: fill in the four sections of [template.md](template.md) (output spec, technical route, creative seed, signature features) and copy the shared parts as they are.

To save effort, you can also point the AI at this repository's `harness/render.mjs` for rendering and `lib/audio` for the soundtrack, instead of building both from scratch.

evidence.heading: SPACE
evidence.text:
[](LICENSE)

[Guide](https://space.docs.perplexity.ai/guide/index.html) · [API Reference](https://space.docs.perplexity.ai/api/index.html)

SPACE (Sandboxed Platform for Agentic Code Execution) is a sandbox platform for running code in isolated Firecracker microVMs. Applications use its HTTP API to create Linux environments, execute commands, collect output, and manage sandbox lifecycles.

Use SPACE when your application needs a separate execution environment for an agent, a user workspace, or a code-running job. Your application decides what to run and what results to keep; SPACE manages the sandbox, its processes, and the connection carrying command output.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
A **template** supplies the starting environment. A **sandbox** is an instance of that environment with its own VM and writable filesystem; multiple commands can run in the same sandbox.

```text
Your application
    |
    +-- Create sandbox from template --> Wait for readiness
    |
    +-- Create command session --------> Attach to start the process
    |                                    Read output and exit result
    |
    +-- Keep, pause, or suspend --------> Wake when needed
    |
    +-- Delete sandbox
```

Sandbox lifecycle changes are asynchronous: the API returns an operation ID that you poll for completion. Command output uses a separate data-plane connection and a session-scoped attachment token.

evidence.heading: Get started
evidence.text: Follow [Installation and configuration](docs/installation.md) to deploy SPACE in a local Kind cluster and authenticate. Then follow [Your first sandbox](docs/first-sandbox.md) to run a command and collect its output. The setup guide covers Kubernetes; the [architecture guide](docs/architecture.md#request-and-execution-flow) also explains how SPACE can run without it.

evidence.text:
Read the hosted [Guide](https://space.docs.perplexity.ai/guide/index.html) and [API Reference](https://space.docs.perplexity.ai/api/index.html) online. Both update automatically after changes merge. The links below point to source documentation in this checkout.

| [Installation and configuration](docs/installation.md) | Host prerequisites, local Kind deployment, configuration defaults, authentication, verification, and teardown. |
| [Operator CLI](crates/apps/admin/cli/README.md) | API access, port forwarding, `space-admin-cli login`, nodes, warm pools, and system-template builds. |

| [E2B Compatibility Wrapper](docs/ecw.md) | Configure ECW, create a compatibility API key, use the tested E2B Python SDK, and understand supported behavior and limitations. |
| [API reference](docs/api/index.md) | Endpoints, request and response fields, and examples. |
| [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | Local setup, authentication, lifecycle operations, command streams, and safe retries. |

| [Warm pools](docs/warm-pools.m

evidence.heading: Build documentation locally
evidence.text:
To browse the guide and API together locally, install [mdBook 0.4.52](https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook/releases/tag/v0.4.52) and the [API build prerequisites](docs/api/index.md#browse-locally). From a clean checkout, run:

```bash
bash scripts/build-docs.sh
python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory target/docs/site
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>. The build also requires Git and Python 3.11+. The standalone commands remain `bash scripts/build-guide-docs.sh` and `bash scripts/build-api-docs.sh`; they also support local uncommitted edits.

The API serves its generated reference at `/openapi-m1.json`, with request fields, response schemas, and errors. `/openapi.json` adds the incubating operations that are not hidden. Some incubating operations, including snapshots, checkpoint, and rollback, are hidden: unless the deployment enables them for your organization, they answer as if they did not exist. Neither document lists them for any caller; `/openapi-full.json` documents every operation and requires API credentials.

evidence.heading: SPACE API
evidence.text:
The SPACE API manages sandbox lifecycles, runs and controls processes, and streams their output. Fields marked `incubating` in the schema are outside the supported contract.

SPACE is implemented in Rust, but applications interact with it over HTTP and server-sent events. You do not need to embed a Rust library to use it; the first-sandbox walkthrough runs a standard-library-only Python example. Installation and cluster diagnostics use Bash.

evidence.heading: Development
evidence.text:
See [DEPENDENCIES.md](DEPENDENCIES.md) when adding or updating third-party code.

After [local installation](docs/installation.md), the Tilt watcher that `up.sh` started keeps running: it rebuilds affected images and rolls their workloads as files change. Rerun `up.sh` to wait for the stack to settle again; do not start a second `tilt up`. The [Kind runbook](infra/space/kind/README.md) covers this development loop, local topology, and template builds.

Use focused unit tests for component logic and the [Kind smoke suites](infra/space/kind/README.md#smoke-test) for runtime behavior. For setup-specific diagnostics, see [host-path troubleshooting](infra/space/kind/README.md#host-paths-and-running-as-a-user-other-than-dev) and [template-build debugging](infra/space/kind/README.md#debugging-a-template-build).

evidence.heading: Let your AI agents paint big arrows, boxes and text on your screen
evidence.text:
**big-arrow-on-the-screen** (`bigarrow`) is a macOS command-line tool, plus a skill for Claude Code and Codex, that draws an arrow and a sign on top of every window. Clicks go through, your keyboard focus stays put, and the arrow removes itself. MIT licensed.

[](https://github.com/franzenzenhofer/big-arrow-on-the-screen/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](LICENSE)



[Real apps](#real-apps-real-use-cases) · [Copy & paste](#copy--paste) · [What is it for?](#what-is-this-actually-for) · [Install](#install) · [Commands](#the-three-commands-an-agent-needs) · [Looks](#looks) · [Creative arrows](#creative-arrows) · [Starred by](#starred-by) · [FAQ](#faq) · [How we know it works](#how-we-know-it-works) · [For agents](#for-agents-and-the-humans-who-configure-them) · [Plan](#plan-decisions-research) · [Prior art](#prior-art-and-thanks) · [License](#license)

> Your AI agent can refactor a monorepo, write a migration and explain monads, but when it needs you to click one button it prints *"please click Allow in the dialog"* into a terminal you are not looking at. `bigarrow` gives it a finger.



```bash
bigarrow point --element "Allow" --app "System Settings" --text "Franz, click Allow: Ghostty may control your Mac"
```

One transparent window above everything, on every display and every Space. Drawing needs **no macOS permission at all**. One Swift binary: no daemon, no menu-bar icon, no account, no telemetry, and, we checked twice, no AI inside. It is an arrow.

evidence.heading: Real apps, real use cases
evidence.text: Real apps on a real Mac (macOS 27), the real `bigarrow`, staged by `scripts/real-scenes.sh`.

evidence.heading: macOS Desktop & Dock: stop "click wallpaper to show desktop"
evidence.text: ["The most annoying change in Mac update history"](https://www.imore.com/mac/macos/macos-sonoma-click-to-reveal-desktop-turn-off), fixed in six arrows ([MP4](docs/videos/wallpaper.mp4)).

evidence.heading: Keynote: a three-step how-to
evidence.text:
```bash
bigarrow start --element Animate --app Keynote --role radiobutton --text "1. Click Animate" --from right \
  --style ring --color purple
bigarrow start --element "Add an Effect" --app Keynote --text "2. Add an Effect" --from right \
  --style box --corners sharp --color "#FF9F0A" --shape straight
bigarrow start --element Play --app Keynote --role button --text "3. Press play. Bask in the applause." \
  --from top --color teal --shape zigzag --size S
```

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
```bash
brew install franzenzenhofer/tap/bigarrow
bigarrow install-skill          # teaches Claude Code (~/.claude/skills) and Codex (~/.agents/skills)
```

From source: `swift build -c release` (Xcode 16+, macOS 14+), binary at `.build/release/bigarrow`. The binary is pure Swift; `scripts/` only records screenshots and runs tests.

evidence.heading: It never takes the focus. How is it in front?
evidence.text: **On top and focused are two different things on macOS.** The arrow sits at screen-saver level, above windows, dialogs and full-screen apps, but never becomes the active window.

evidence.heading: How much CPU does a pulsing arrow cost?
evidence.text: **1.4 % on a CI runner.** Core Animation does the work in the render server.

⭐ **700+ stars on its first day, 1,000 in just over three** · on PyPI, the official MCP Registry, Cursor Directory, LobeHub, Tessl, ClawHub and skills.sh

[Quick start](#quick-start) · [What it reads](#what-it-reads) · [The keyword table](#the-keyword-table) · [Agents and MCP](#use-it-from-an-agent-skills-and-an-mcp-server) · [config.json](#configjson) · [中文说明](README.zh-CN.md)



A daily report of the names that are starting to surge in AI: new models, products, tools and repos, caught where they are said first, before they show up in keyword tools.

Built for people who make pages, posts or products around new terms: SEO for AI tool sites, newsletters, directories, anyone who wants to know about "Strata" or "Seedance" the day it appears and not two weeks later.

evidence.heading: Why
evidence.text:
A new name leaves a trail, in this order:

1. A lab or a well-followed account says it on X; a model enters Hugging Face's trending list.
2. One GitHub repo takes off on its own.
3. Directories and competitors add pages for it; someone registers a domain for it and the site starts to rank.
4. Your own site gets its first search impressions for it.
5. Google Trends shows the curve, days or weeks later.

Keyword tools read step 5. This radar reads steps 1 to 4 every day and uses step 5 only to check itself.

One example it was built around: [Niko1221/Strata](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata) was created on 2026-09-24 and had 7,700 stars nine days later. People were searching "niko strata" from 9/26, while no second repo carried the name and no keyword tool listed it. A single repo gaining 800 stars a day is the whole signal, and it is public.

evidence.heading: What it reads
evidence.text:
Purple, tagged NEW: what 0.3 to 0.5 added (⑥ revenue, ⑦ Reddit asks, ⑧ sellers, the page-one check, the format and ⚡ marks, the `pains` command).

| Signal | What it catches | Needs | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| ① X | Names the accounts in your list used for the first time in 60 days | AIsa key | $0.003 per account per run |
| ① Hugging Face | Models and Spaces (the demos people try) new to the trending top 50; quantised copies and a model's own demo grouped under the base name | nothing | free |
| ② GitHub breakout | A repo under 14 days old averaging 200+ stars a day, or +400 since yesterday; adds the search variants people use ("niko strata") | nothing (a GitHub token raises the rate limit) | free |
| ③ Sitemaps | Words that several new URLs on a site share and its older URLs rarely carried. The example config watches eight AI tool directories (toolify, aixploria, ai-bot.cn, opentools, dang.ai, clipfly, aitoptools, futurepedia) and four MCP and skill directories | the sitemaps you list | free |
| ③ New sites | Domains registered and first indexed in the last 90 days that already rank for 20+ keywords | AIsa key | about $0.13 per query, weekly |
| ⑦ Asks | What people ask for on Reddit ("is there an AI tool that…", twelve phrasings): a model keeps the requests and complaints an AI tool could answer and writes each job as people would search it; jobs with searches get the page-one check | AIsa key | about $0.12 a week |
| ⑧ Sellers | Sites that just put up their first payment link (Stripe Payment Links, Polar, Lemon Squeezy, Gumroad, Creem), from the public link graph with the day each site first linked; new pages of old sellers, platform pages and forum threads left out; the site's own description goes to the keyword table | AIsa key; GoAnyAPI optional, for visits | ab

evidence.heading: The keyword table
evidence.text:
A name is half of what you need. "SynthID Detector" has a short life as a keyword and belongs to Google; the job it does, "ai image detector", is what people keep searching, and nobody owns it. Each day the radar reads the new names once more and writes one table with both:

```
| Keyword | Type | Behind | New? | Est. searches/day | Started rising | Peak vs gpts | Peak day | Last 7 days vs the 7 before | Now | Page one | Decision |
| **photocraft** 🖼 | name | — | yes | 12747 | 2026-10-05 | 97 vs 3.1 | 2026-10-09 | — | still rising | — | **prioritize** |
| **claude haiku 5.5** | name | — | yes | 1863 | 2026-10-07 | 100 vs 23.7 | 2026-10-08 | ×6.0 | still rising | — | **prioritize** |
| **ai image detector** 🖼 | generic | synthid detector | no | 2537 | — | 87 vs 31.6 | 2026-10-04 | ×1.2 | flat | — | watch |
| **photoshop alternative** ⚠ | generic | photocraft | no | 244 | — | 61 vs 61.7 | 2026-10-08 | ×1.8 | flat | — | skip |
```

(a real run, 2026-10-12, shortened; the Page one column came later, see below)

How it is made (`radar/usecases.py`):

1. **Evidence**: the most-liked posts that mention the name (X advanced search) and, for a repository, its README.
2. **Phrases**: a model reads the evidence and writes the keyword an ordinary person would type for each job it sees people doing, with a quote that backs it. A phrase built on another product's name ("photoshop alternative") is kept and marked ⚠: demand often hangs on the incumbent, and whether to use someone's brand is your call.
   With a GoAnyAPI key (optional, below) the radar also takes **Google Trends' related queries** for the name: what people really searched together with it. For SynthID Detector that gave "ai photo detector", "google ai detector" and "ai detector"; these rows carry 🔎. Queries that hold th

evidence.heading: When a source is missing or down
evidence.text:
The table is still written, but it gets thinner, and it says which part is missing:

| What happens | What the table loses | The line it prints |
|---|---|---|
| No `GOANYAPI_API_KEY` (the default) | The 🔎 rows, each name's long-tails, the other names searched alongside, and the `(US)` readings. Phrases come from the model alone and every curve from the worldwide series, where a real move can read flat | "Related queries are off: set GOANYAPI_API_KEY…" |
| GoAnyAPI's Trends is down (seen on its first day in use, 2026-10-12) | The same as having no key, for that run | "Related queries failed for: …" and "Country series failed, worldwide data used instead: …" |
| AIsa's post search fails for a name (timeouts seen twice on 2026-10-13) | That name's posts. A repository still has its README; a model or product without one is left with the related queries only, and with no GoAnyAPI key it gets no generic terms that day | "The post search failed; this run used READMEs and related queries only: …" |
| Neither posts nor a README for a name | Its generic terms; the name's own row stays | "No posts or README found for: …" |
| No lead that day is a thing with a name score of 0.8 or more | The whole table | "Nothing to read today…" |
| AIsa's search-volume or Trends lookup fails | The whole table: these two are not replaceable | the error, in place of the table |

A thin table is not a quiet day. Read the lines under it before you conclude that nothing moved.

Set `"usecases": {"per_day": 0}` or pass `--skip usecases` to turn it off.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
Python 3.10 or newer. The radar uses only the standard library.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zhuyansen/new-term-radar
cd new-term-radar
cp config.example.json config.json      # then edit: your X accounts, sitemaps, topics
export AISA_API_KEY=...                 # from https://go.aisa.one/yansen-zhu; or `aisa login` with the AIsa CLI
python -m radar daily --out report.md
```

The first run builds its snapshots: yesterday's X vocabulary, star counts and sitemap URLs do not exist yet, so only GitHub breakouts (which need no yesterday) are reported. From the second run on, every signal reports what changed.

Two commands:

```bash
python -m radar sources --out sources.md           # ① only: X and Hugging Face. Run every few hours.
python -m radar daily --skip x,hf --out report.md  # everything else, once a day
```

`sources` writes a report only when there is a new name. `daily` with `--skip x,hf` lists what `sources` kept in the last 24 hours. If you run only once a day, use `python -m radar daily` and skip nothing.

Other flags: `--skip` takes any of `x,hf,breakout,sitemaps,newsites,gsc,review,judge,usecases`; `--new-sites` runs the weekly signal today; `--mail` sends the report (below); `--state DIR` moves the database and snapshots.

evidence.heading: How the pieces decide
evidence.text:
- **Names in posts** (`radar/terms.py`): capitalised words, words with a digit (`Qwen3.8`) or inner capitals (`HyperFrames`); a number after a name joins it (`Opus 5.5`). A name two accounts used counts; a name one account used needs 100 likes and must be unmistakably a name, since a capitalised word is often just the start of a sentence.
- **Surges in sitemaps**: counted per distinct URL against the site's own baseline, so one page with a long slug cannot fake a wave.
- **The judge** (`radar/judge.py`): one chat call per 25 terms, each with up to three places it appeared. If the call fails the report still goes out, unsorted.
- **The review** (`radar/review.py`): a variant "rose" when its peak after the day we reported it clears its own earlier baseline by 2x and by 10 points. A word with an older meaning ("strata": rock layers, property law) has a high baseline and does not count; "niko1221 strata" going from 0 to something does. Trends' unsettled last two days are left out.

evidence.text:
Project Maya

GLM-5.3-Flash (321 B) and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (748 B) on your own GPU
private and fast · one NVIDIA GPU or up to 16 · AMD and Windows (experimental) · chat, pictures, OpenAI- and
Anthropic-compatible API · several requests at once







Created and led by Peasant Smith (@mw00), co-maintained
with @needmorevram


Project Maya is free. If it runs well on your PC, a coffee keeps the work on it going.

Models this size usually need a datacenter. Maya runs **[GLM-5.3-Flash](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash)**
(zai-org, MIT license; 321 B parameters, about 18 B active per token, a context of up to 1 M tokens) and
**[DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017)** (DeepSeek, MIT license;
748 B parameters) on the hardware you already have. Each model has an engine built for it. It keeps the experts your
conversation uses most on the GPU, the next ones in RAM and the rest on your NVMe SSD, and moves them as you chat. It
measures your GPUs, CPU, RAM and SSD and tunes itself to them. Nothing leaves your machine.

- **Fast:** up to 124 tokens/s on two H100s, 118 on four RTX 4090s, 81 on one RTX PRO 6000, 30+ on a single RTX 5090. Real numbers from
  real users below.
- **Close to the original:** Maya's own quants of GLM-5.3-Flash keep 97.7-99.2% of the FP8 model's zero-shot
  accuracy; Maya-S of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 picks the same next token as the original 92.6% of the time.
- **Plugs into your tools:** OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API with tool calls, ready for coding agents.
- **Several requests at once:** up to 8 answered together - for agents that run several sessions, or several people
  on one PC.
- **Everything in the box:** a chat and a live monitor in the browser, pictures, thinking levels, a

evidence.heading: The models
evidence.text:
Project Maya's own quants of GLM-5.3-Flash, made from Z.ai's FP8 release with statistics from the FP8 model. Each keeps
the model's MTP block, which drafts tokens ahead.

| Model | Size | Made for | Against the FP8 model |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| **Maya-S** (default) | 96.5 GB | PCs with a smaller memory pool (RAM and VRAM together) | 97.9% of its zero-shot accuracy; the same next token 83% of the time |
| **Maya-S24** | 94.7 GB | cards of 24 GB or less: 4-bit attention leaves ~1.5 GB more of the card for experts, decode +14% | 97.7%; 83% |
| **Maya-M** | 116 GB | a bigger memory pool; more bits where they count, calibrated toward tool calls and front-end code | 97.9%; 86% |
| **Maya-M-Derisked** | 116 GB | Maya-M with a weight edit by [Blackfrost_AI](https://x.com/Blackfrost_AI) that reduces blanket refusals ([its repo](https://huggingface.co/peasantsmith/GLM-5.3-Flash-Maya-M-Derisked-IQ2_S-GGUF)); experimental | not measured yet |
| **Maya-L** | 156.3 GB | the biggest memory pools | **99.2%**; 90% |

The setup asks which one to download and recommends one for your PC. How they're made and measured: [MAYA-S](bench/results/MAYA-S.md),
[MAYA-S24](bench/results/MAYA-S24.md), [MAYA-M](bench/results/MAYA-M.md), [MAYA-L](bench/results/MAYA-L.md). On
[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/peasantsmith/GLM-5.3-Flash-Maya-GGUF).

The server uses the pinned official prompt encoder, with numeric reasoning budgets and ID-matched parallel tool

evidence.heading: What you need
evidence.text:
| | |
| --- | --- |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA, compute capability 7.0 or newer (V100, RTX 20 and newer): one, or up to 16 that share the model. More VRAM is faster. Pascal (Tesla P40 / P100, GTX 10) is experimental, not validated yet. **AMD (experimental):** RX 7900 XT / XTX, Radeon AI PRO R9700 / RX 9070, Strix Halo and Gorgon Halo (Radeon 8060S / 8065S); RX 6800 / 6900 and Radeon PRO V620 / W6800 not validated yet; GLM-5.3-Flash reads text only there, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 pictures too - [docs/AMD_MAYA.md](docs/AMD_MAYA.md) |
| **RAM** | 32 GB runs it. More RAM keeps more experts close and is faster |
| **Disk** | **A fast NVMe SSD** with room for the model (~100 GB for Maya-S, ~160 GB for Maya-L, ~350 GB for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017's Maya-S, ~520 GB for unsloth's GGUF) and its picture encoder (1.1 GB). Not a hard disk |
| **System** | Linux (x86-64; a CPU with AVX2 is best), the NVIDIA driver, CUDA 12.x (CUDA 13 works for RTX 20 and newer, not for the V100 or Pascal), g++, Python 3.10+. Windows 10/11 (experimental): [docs/WINDOWS.md](docs/WINDOWS.md). Not WSL2. AMD: ROCm 7 |

The setup checks all of this, prints the exact command for anything missing, and installs nothing system-wide.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/mw00/project-maya.git && cd project-maya
./setup.sh
```

Answer a few questions (Enter takes the recommended choice). The setup shows every download before it starts it,
builds everything once (20-40 minutes plus the download) and **starts the model**. Then open
`http://127.0.0.1:8080`. Ctrl+C stops it, and `./setup.sh` starts it again right away.

- **Windows:** `START-MAYA.bat` instead of `./setup.sh` - see [docs/WINDOWS.md](docs/WINDOWS.md).
- **AMD:** [docs/AMD_MAYA.md](docs/AMD_MAYA.md).
- **Updating:** the dashboard's **About > Update**, or `git pull` then `./setup.sh`. The model isn't downloaded again.
- **Every option** (GPUs, context, a model folder you already have, remote access, ...): [docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md).

> **The start takes a few minutes:** the engine pins most of the free RAM (all but about 6 GB) for its expert tier,
> so other programs get little RAM while Maya runs.

evidence.heading: Using it
evidence.text:
- **In the browser:** chat (kept in your browser, per-chat instructions, edit and regenerate, HTML previews), a live
  **Monitor** of the model and your hardware (down to what fills each GPU's memory), and a context size and port you
  can change in Settings.
- **Your apps and coding agents:** an OpenAI-compatible API at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`, and Anthropic's at
  `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/messages` (Claude Code: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080`). Tool calls are
  streamed as the model writes them, and a long prompt's reading progress too when a request asks for it
  (`"return_progress": true`). A web page served from another address can call it too once you allow its
  address (`"cors_origins"`, [docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md#web-pages-on-another-address)).
- **Responses API:** `/v1/responses` supports text/image conversations, streaming,
  function tool calls, schema-validated output, background tasks with cancellation/replay,
  and optional shared in-memory history (`store:true`, `previous_response_id`).
  Responses are not stored by default. Options and limits: [docs/RESPONSE

kind_reason.text: Provides private, high-performance local inference of large language models on consumer-grade hardware.

summary.text: A framework for running GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 locally on a single GPU or up to 16 GPUs, supporting OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs with quantized models.

value.text: Up to 124 tokens/s on two H100s, 118 on four RTX 4090s, 81 on one RTX PRO 6000, and 30+ on a single RTX 5090.

audience.text: Developers building local AI applications, researchers requiring privacy, and teams needing flexible deployment across hardware configurations.

outcome.text: Enables efficient local inference of large language models with variable speed profiles depending on hardware configuration.

mechanism.text: Manages resource allocation across multiple GPUs, selects optimal expert tiers for each request, and serves through a RESTful API supporting text/image interactions and tool calling.

inspiration.text: An application designed to bring enterprise-grade large language model capabilities to private, on-device environments.

limitations.text: Requires significant GPU memory (minimum 32GB), limited to models fitting within available VRAM, and some features depend on specific OS and CUDA versions.

how_to.text: Clone the repository and navigate to the project root.
Edit config.json to specify X accounts, sitemaps, and topic filters.
Export the AISA_API_KEY from the provided credentials page.
Execute 'python -m radar daily --out report.md' to generate the analysis report.

input.text: Install the project and run the daily scan.

output.text: A running local LLM instance accessible via HTTP API with chat and tool-calling capabilities.

evidence.heading: Community projects
evidence.text:
- [DiffSynth-Studio](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio) now supports full fine-tuning and LoRA training for **MOSS-Image-Base** and **MOSS-Image-SFT**. See the [training documentation](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio/blob/main/docs/en/Model_Details/MOSS-Image.md#model-training) and [example scripts](https://github.com/modelscope/DiffSynth-Studio/tree/main/examples/moss_image/model_training).

- [MOSS-Image-SFT-DeBand](https://huggingface.co/MATLOWAI/MOSS-Image-SFT-DeBand) by **MATLOWAI** provides community LoRAs to reduce vertical color banding in **MOSS-Image-SFT**, together with ComfyUI preset workflows. See the model card for examples, settings, and the trade-offs between stripe reduction and changes to image details.

- [MOSS-Image-SFT-8-steps-dmd](https://huggingface.co/lodestones/MOSS-Image-SFT-8-steps-dmd) by **lodestones** is a community 8-step DMD distillation of **MOSS-Image-SFT**, with LoRA adapters for ComfyUI. See the model card for the latest checkpoints and usage recommendations.

- [MOSS-Image-FP16-fixed](https://huggingface.co/KBlueLeaf/MOSS-Image-FP16-fixed) by **KBlueLeaf** provides FP16-compatible transformer weights for **MOSS-Image-Base** and **MOSS-Image-SFT**, using residual-stream rescaling to improve overflow headroom. - [ComfyUI-Spectrum-MOSS](https://github.com/Rkkss/ComfyUI-Spectrum-MOSS) by **Rkkss** adds Spectrum-style hidden-state forecasting to accelerate MOSS-Image sampling in ComfyUI, with manual and experimental adaptive nodes. See the repository for recommended sampling settings and examples.

evidence.text:
MOSS-Image is supported natively in [ComfyUI](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/17095). No MOSS-Image plugin is required for this workflow.

The repository plugin remains available for loading a local Hugging Face / Diffusers directory and for existing plugin workflows.

evidence.heading: Prompt enhancer skill
evidence.text:
The [MOSS-Image Prompt Enhancer](skills/moss-image-prompt-enhancer/SKILL.md) turns
image ideas into detailed captions or spatial Layout prompts. It is designed for
GPT-6-family agents with local file and Python tools. The bundled script converts
pixel-coordinate drafts into compact JSON with integer centered coordinates;
it does not call an image-generation service.

Install the [skill folder](skills/moss-image-prompt-enhancer) in your agent's skills
directory, then invoke `$moss-image-prompt-enhancer` with your image idea, desired
caption or Layout output, and any canvas dimensions. Paste the compiled result
into MOSS-Image's positive prompt; for Layout, use the same generation dimensions.

evidence.heading: The Founder skill
evidence.text:
Eleven Claude skills that test a business before you launch it. Free, MIT, no
signup, no API key, nothing to connect.

`skills/founder-board` `skills/founder-marketing` `skills/founder-cfo`
`skills/founder-consumer` `skills/founder-launch` `skills/founder-pricing`
`skills/founder-offer` `skills/founder-competitors` `skills/founder-brand`
`skills/founder-ops` `skills/founder-plan`

One of them is your board of directors, trained on the frameworks of Alex
Hormozi, Peter Thiel and Steve Jobs. One is your marketing director. One is your
CFO and finds your real profit margins. And one is the consumer panel: it spins
up 100 buyer agents trained on your target customer and runs your business
through 100 buyer scenarios.

So you know how to launch, how to market and how to actually make money, before
you spend thousands of dollars finding out the hard way.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Paste this repo link into Claude and say `install skill`:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/founder-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/founder-skill
/plugin install founder-skill@founder-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/founder-skill:founder-board` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/founder-board`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/founder-skill.git
cp -r founder-skill/skills/founder-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the top
of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the sub-agents and the Python tools,
but the method works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install.

evidence.heading: How to use it
evidence.text:
Run them in this order. Each one reads what the others wrote, in a `founder/`
folder in your project.

```
board -> competitors -> consumer -> pricing -> offer -> cfo -> marketing -> brand -> ops -> launch -> plan
```

An example: a matcha café in Toronto, iced matcha lattes at $6.50 a cup. (Every
input is in the example files in this repo, so you can run the tools on it.)

1. **`/founder-board`** writes `founder/idea.md` from what you told it and puts it
   in front of three board members. Each scores it, lists the risks and votes:
   fund, fund if, or pass. The conditions become a checklist for the rest.
2. **`/founder-competitors`** maps the matcha bars and coffee shops within walking
   distance, what they charge for a latte and what their reviews complain about.
3. **`/founder-consumer`** builds the target customer (urban professionals, 24 to
   38, who buy coffee most days), deals 100 buyer cards across income, habits and
   objections, and runs one sub-agent per buyer. Back comes who buys, who passes,
   the reasons in their words ("my coffee place is closer", "$6.50 is steep for a
   drink") and what would flip a no.
4. **`/founder-pricing`** reads the panel's four price answers per buyer into a
   price range and checks $6.50 against it and against the competitors.
5. **`/founder-offer`** answers the top objections with the offer (a launch-week
   price, a loyalty card) and re-runs a quick panel to see if the buy rate moves.
6. **`/founder-cfo`** runs the unit economics. With the example numbers: each cup
   leaves $4.76 after its own costs, break-even is 186 cups a day, the profit
   margin at the planned 383 cups a day is 38%, year 1 makes $93,926 on operations
   after a slow ramp, the $25,280 startup spend is earned back in month 8, and the
   founder needs

evidence.heading: The tools
evidence.text:
Four of them, all standard-library Python. None touch the network.

```bash
python3 skills/founder-cfo/unit_economics.py founder/numbers.json --out founder/cfo.md   # margins, break-even, year 1
python3 skills/founder-consumer/panel.py init --customer founder/customer.json --pitch founder/pitch.md
python3 skills/founder-pricing/van_westendorp.py founder/panel/answers --price 6.50       # the acceptable price range
python3 skills/founder-plan/compile.py --dir founder                                     # the plan and its verdict
```

**`unit_economics.py`** reads one JSON (example: `skills/founder-cfo/example.json`)
and reports contribution, break-even, the margin at plan, year 1 by month, cash
needed, payback and three what-ifs. Every number traces to an input; a missing
field is an error, never a guess.

**`panel.py`** deals persona cards from your target customer (same seed, same
cards), writes one brief per buyer, checks the answers and tallies them. It never
answers for a buyer.

**`van_westendorp.py`** reads four price answers per buyer (from the panel, or a
CSV from a real survey) and finds the points of marginal cheapness and
expensiveness, the optimal and the indifference price.

**`compile.py`** assembles the plan and computes the verdict.

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

evidence.heading: Fine print
evidence.text:
**The board applies published frameworks. It is not those people.** The three
lenses are short summaries, in our words, of ideas from *$100M Offers* by Alex
Hormozi, *Zero to One* by Peter Thiel with Blake Masters, and Walter Isaacson's
biography of Steve Jobs. The board never speaks as them, quotes them or claims
they endorse anything. This project is not affiliated with any of them.

**The consumer panel is simulated buyers, not customers.** It is a fast, cheap way
to find objections, segments and wording before you spend. It is not a forecast:
language models lean agreeable, so read the buy rate as an upper bound, and
confirm the big calls with real people. `/founder-launch` starts with exactly that
test. Panel answers are research; never use them as testimonials.

**The numbers are only as good as the inputs.** The CFO marks every estimate as an
estimate and asks for real quotes. Check costs with suppliers and the structure,
payroll and tax with an accountant.

**Research uses public sources, with links.** No invented competitors, prices,
reviews or quotes. No scraping against a site's terms.

**Not financial, legal or tax advice.** Permits, trademarks and claims depend on
where you are. The skills tell you what to check and where; a professional
confirms it.

**让你的agent做动画、作曲，指着画面改。**

跟Claude Code、Codex这些agent说一句「给我的产品做个30秒的发布片」，
它会先读你的产品，给你三个方向挑，写出整支片子，自己写谱配乐，
然后在浏览器里打开一个编辑器等你。哪里不满意，在画面上点一下，写下要改什么，它就只改那一处。


[看效果](#看效果) · [安装](#安装) · [能做什么](#能做什么) · [怎么做到的](#怎么做到的) · [背后的故事](#背后的故事)



---

evidence.heading: 看效果
evidence.text: 这篇README里的每一段动画都是huashu-motion做的。上面那段取自它给自己做的53秒发布片，👉 [下载完整发布片（MP4，带声音）](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-motion/releases/latest)，下面Grok Bot（非官方）、huashu-design、DeepSeek、Claude Duet（非官方）这几支的完整版也在同一个页面。

evidence.heading: 指着画面改
evidence.text:
按C，在画面上点一下，写下要改什么。评论发过去的时候带着时间点、场景、点中的元素和它在源码里的位置，agent先把那一帧和你点的那一小块截图放大看一眼，再只改那一处，改完回一句人话，预览停在原来的位置刷新。每一版都留着，⌘Z随时撤回；标题、数字、颜色、停留时长这些会变成编辑器右边的输入框，自己改，不用等agent。

（这段里的编辑器和终端是照真实界面重建的，代码细节是示意；评论是真实提过的意见。）

evidence.heading: 先写谱，再拍片
evidence.text: 做发布片用的是作曲家模式：agent按节奏单先写一份谱（ABC记谱法，纯文本的乐谱），谱里的标记对齐每个场景，再由三角钢琴、弦乐和鼓组的采样演奏出来（真乐器采样要先跑一次`om samples build`，不跑就用合成音色）；画面上每个东西落地的那一帧，再配一个音效。配乐全部在本机现场生成，不调用任何收费接口。

evidence.heading: 一天，二十支
evidence.text:
16个镜头，来自同一天做的七支片子，按拍子切。



Grok Bot（粉丝自制，非官方）· 30秒：傍晚交代任务，夜里几个agent各干各的，早上7点手机上收到汇报。这段是汇报一张张送往Chief of Staff的那几拍。


huashu-design 3.0 · 一句提示词钉住不动，背后的风格按拍子换
小猫补光灯Pro · 八种补光色，一拍换一种

evidence.heading: 不依赖Opus：DeepSeek V4.1 Flash也能做
evidence.text: 这支22秒的动效片，是把Claude Code背后的模型换成DeepSeek V4.1 Flash（1017版）做的。中间我给了三轮意见（比如加上DeepSeek的鲸鱼logo、删掉几个镜头），带配乐和音效，前后不到半小时，按当时的价格花了1块9毛5（缓存命中率99.4%）。统一的配色、贯穿全片的那颗圆点、卡在124BPM上的配乐，是skill带出来的，我一句都没提过。方法写进了skill，便宜的模型也能拍出像样的片子。

evidence.heading: 诚实边界
evidence.text:
- 它听不见。agent靠谱面、能量曲线和频谱图检查配乐，最后一耳朵还得是你的。
- 它不会凭空生成真人和实拍。画面全是代码画的；要真人、实拍，用你自己的素材，它负责合成和包装。
- 效果跟模型有关。我主要在Claude Code里用Opus 5.5；DeepSeek V4.1 Flash也能做得不错，但不同模型的品味差别是真实存在的。
- 要能跑命令的环境。预览和导出在本机跑，需要Node、Chrome和FFmpeg。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Open decision models from 0.8B to 27B: a calibrated probability for every option in one pass, and a short thought only when unsure. Engine for vLLM, llama.cpp and MLX.

evidence.heading: README
Demos
evidence.text:
Helicopter rescue: calls each stage of a Coast Guard hoist rescue in Hurricane Harvey, one frame a second
    Chess: with White, checkmates Jev 1.13 on move 19 of a Scotch Game, and neither side searches
  
  
    Super Mario Bros.: clears World 1-1
    StarCraft II: makes the strategic calls for a Terran bot and beats the built-in Hard AI
  
  
    Rocket launch: follows the Artemis I night launch one frame a second, calls liftoff and tells the camera when to tilt up
    JevBall: makes the decisions for a football team in real time
  


In the chess and game runs, every step is one request with typed questions, answered by StartLux-Decision-v1-27B, the
first release, in one pass. The rescue and launch videos send one frame a second with nine questions to the 27B
AutoThink model on [bamboonode.dev](https://bamboonode.dev/), which thinks only when its top probability is below the
0.6 gate. Their footage is from the U.S. Coast Guard and NASA (public domain, no endorsement implied), and the faces of
the people being rescued are blurred. Click a preview for the video. [v1/README.md](v1/README.md#demos) describes each
harness, and the harnesses for computer use and chess are in [v1/demos](v1/demos).

evidence.heading: Release notes
evidence.text:
- 2026-10-16: StartLux-Decision v1.1 27B Instant ranks first of 174 entries on the
  [Decision Index 0.3.2](https://huggingface.co/spaces/multimodalart/jev-decision-index) leaderboard on Hugging Face,
  with a Full score of 69.12. It is also first on each of the three parts: the public benchmarks (72.88), the private
  tests of the same skills (64.82) and the private tasks from new domains (61.41).

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
To try a model without a GPU, use [bamboonode.dev](https://bamboonode.dev/). It hosts the 27B AutoThink model with the
same request format (`POST /v1/decisions`), free and without usage limits, and needs only a Bamboo API key.

On NVIDIA GPUs, [StartLux-Prism](https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/StartLux-Prism) is our inference engine written for
these models. It serves v1 and v1.1 AutoThink (4B, 9B and 27B) straight from the released GGUF files, behind the same
`/v1/systemone` API; v1.1 Instant models are not supported yet. Install it on Linux with Python 3.12 and a CUDA 13
driver:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/StartLux-Prism.git
cd StartLux-Prism
python3.12 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt     # PyTorch 2.14.1 for CUDA 13, Triton, nvcc 13.0
source scripts/cuda_env.sh          # nvcc from pip as CUDA_HOME (in every new shell)
```

Download a GGUF file with its release's tokenizer and config, and start the server:

```bash
M=~/models/StartLux-Decision-v1.1-27B-AutoThink-GGUF
hf download startlux-models/StartLux-Decision-v1.1-27B-AutoThink-GGUF \
  StartLux-Decision-v1.1-27B-AutoThink-Q8_0.gguf --local-dir $M
hf download startlux-models/StartLux-Decision-v1.1-27B-AutoThink --exclude "*.safetensors" --local-dir $M
python -m startlux_prism.server --gguf $M/StartLux-Decision-v1.1-27B-AutoThink-Q8_0.gguf --model-dir $M --port 8090
```

The server is ready when it prints `Ready`; the first start compiles its CUDA kernels and measures the int8 activation
ranges once. It answers the request below as it is. `allow_none` is on by default for v1.1 models (`--allow-none off`
matches this package), and the server has no API keys or TLS, so keep it behind your own access control.
[StartLux-Prism's README](https://github.com/S

evidence.heading: Controls
evidence.text:
A request can steer the reasoning of AutoThink models and ask for more detail. All fields are optional.

| Field | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `think_mode` | `auto` | `auto` reasons when the first read-out's top probability is below `gate`; `never` answers in one pass; `always` reasons first |
| `gate` | 0.6 | the confidence below which `auto` reasons (the published results use 0.9) |
| `think_budget` | 4096 | the longest thought, in tokens |
| `none_check` | true | every choice answer reports `none_probability`, the chance that no listed option fits; `choice` stays a listed option |
| `allow_none` | false (`serve --allow-none`: true) | lets `choice` be null when "None of the above" is the most likely answer |
| `return_details`, `return_thought` | false | per-answer read-outs and timings, and the thought text |
| `images` | none | base64 strings or data URIs used as evidence |

The default gate of 0.6 answers more requests in one pass. A gate of 0.9 thinks more often and is more accurate on
decisions that need rules or arithmetic. For the 27B AutoThink model on this engine, moving the gate from 0.9 to 0.6
lowers Decision Index 0.3 from 73.22 to 72.85 and DecisionPivot pair accuracy from 88.1% to 68.4%. Instant models
always answer in one pass.

We suggest treating a `none_probability` of 0.2 or more as "no listed option fits". At 0.2 it catches two thirds
(66.3%) of the questions whose listed options are all wrong, and flags 2.2% of the questions that do have a right
answer. Lower thresholds flag many more good questions, higher ones miss more of the bad ones
([why 0.2](docs/none_probability.md#why-02)). [docs/api.md](docs/api.md) describes the full request and response
format, the confidence definitions, the details fields and the errors.

evidence.heading: Engines
evidence.text:
| Engine | Instant | AutoThink | Images | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM (default) | yes, with the plugin in this package | yes | vLLM 0.31 | serving, and the published numbers |
| [StartLux-Prism](https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/StartLux-Prism) | not yet | yes, 4B, 9B and 27B | with the `mmproj` file | the GGUF files on NVIDIA GPUs, lowest latency |
| llama.cpp | yes, GGUF builds marked non-causal | yes | with the `mmproj` file | machines without vLLM |
| MLX | yes, mlx-vlm builds | yes | yes | Apple Silicon |
| transformers | yes | yes | yes | reference checks |

FP8 and GGUF Q8_0 largely preserve BF16 decision performance, while Q4_K_M can lose up to 4.3 points (27B AutoThink
on DecisionPivot). [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md)
lists the engine settings to switch on and off and why, and [docs/quantization.md](docs/quantization.md) covers the
quantized builds.

github_projects.description: Turn any website into an API your agent can call. Learns from the site's own frontend, heals itself when the site changes.
github_projects.description_zh: 将任何网站变为你的智能体可以调用的 API。学习网站自身前端，当网站变化时自动修复。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Turn any website into an API your agent can call. Learns from the site's own frontend, heals itself when the site changes.

evidence.heading: API Anything
evidence.text:
[](https://github.com/goodnight000/api-anything/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

**Teach your agent a website once. After that, it calls the site like an API instead of driving a browser.**

API Anything watches a site's own page make a request and learns which parts of it are your
inputs. It saves the result as an operation. Your agent calls that operation with new inputs
over MCP, the CLI or TypeScript, and gets JSON back over plain HTTP.

[](docs/media/agent-race.mp4)

Same agent (Claude Opus 5.5), same prompt, started together. Left: it drives headless Chrome
through Playwright MCP. Right: it calls API Anything's Google Flights operation. Shown at 3× speed with no cuts;
the timers show real elapsed time. Recorded 2026-09-28. [MP4](docs/media/agent-race.mp4) · [how it was recorded](bench/README.md#the-recorded-race)


  
  


Across 5 runs of each task, the agent using API Anything answered 1.5 to 2× sooner, read about
half as many tokens, and cost the same or less. All 20 answers were correct.
[Method, raw numbers and limits](bench/README.md).

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Paste this into Claude Code, Codex or another coding agent:

```text
Set up API Anything for me: https://github.com/goodnight000/api-anything/blob/main/INSTALL.md
```

The agent checks Node 22.13+, builds and installs the `api-anything` command, confirms that a
call works, then connects the MCP server and the skill to itself. Restart the agent, then ask it
something like "What does Goodreads rate Piranesi?"


Install by hand

The package isn't on npm yet. Don't use `npm install -g github:...`, because it fails under npm 11.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/goodnight000/api-anything.git && cd api-anything
npm ci && npm install -g "$(npm pack --silent)"
api-anything call hacker-news search query=sqlite
```

```json
{"ok":true,"class":"ok","tier":1,"data":[{"title":"Hosting SQLite databases on GitHub Pages or any static file hoster","url":"https://phiresky.github.io/blog/2021/hosting-sqlite-databases-on-github-pages/", ...}, ...],"ms":111}
```

`tier: 1` means plain HTTP with no browser. A failure returns `ok: false` with a `class`, a
`reason` and a `next` step. Connect an agent with `codex mcp add api-anything -- api-anything mcp`,
`claude mcp add --scope user api-anything -- api-anything mcp`, or this MCP entry:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "api-anything": { "command": "api-anything", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```



Over MCP an agent **calls** operations, using four tools: `list_sites`, `list_operations`,
`call_operation` and `login`. To **create** operations, an agent needs a shell and the
[skill](skills/api-anything/SKILL.md). A Chromium browser is needed only for creating operations
and for the browser tier — Google Chrome by default, or Brave, Edge, Chromium, Vivaldi, Arc; any
Chromium executable works via `API_ANYTHING_BROWSER`. [Setup details](docs/QUICKSTART.md).

evidence.heading: Teach it a new site
evidence.text:
Give it the page URL with a placeholder, and two example inputs:

```sh
api-anything add hn-demo links \
  --trigger 'https://news.ycombinator.com/from?site={domain}' \
  --example domain=github.com --example2 domain=github.io --match path=/from \
  --html '{"items":"tr.athing","fields":{"title":".titleline > a","url":".titleline > a@href"}}'

api-anything call hn-demo links domain=arxiv.org      # 30 arxiv.org stories, tier 1
```

The headless browser loads the page once for each example. The part of the request that changed with
the input becomes a parameter, and the rest is stored as a template. The agent (or you) picks the
request and the fields. API Anything builds the template without an LLM.
[Recorded demos](docs/demos/README.md).

evidence.heading: Use and share specs
evidence.text:
Someone may have learned the site already. `pull` fetches a spec others published to the registry
(this repository's `sites/`), checked against the shared rules first:

```sh
api-anything pull goodreads
api-anything call goodreads searchBooks q=piranesi
```

To share one you learned, `publish` previews exactly what would become public: the files, every
host the spec sends to, and anything that may be yours, such as an email or an account id. Nothing
is sent until you add `--yes`. Then it opens a pull request from your fork with the GitHub CLI,
committed under your account's noreply address. A maintainer reviews it, CI runs the same rules,
and once it merges anyone can pull it.

```sh
api-anything publish hn-demo            # preview only
api-anything publish hn-demo --yes      # open the pull request
```

evidence.heading: Map a site from an intent
evidence.text:
Tell an agent what you need from a site. The [skill](skills/api-anything/SKILL.md) makes it do
this, in order:

1. Ask about whatever the request leaves unclear.
2. Propose operations and wait for your approval.
3. Scout each page with `capture --outline`. This is a summary of what each request returns, so
   the agent doesn't have to read full responses.
4. Build each operation and check it with an input that wasn't an example.

Goodreads has had no public API since 2020. One run took 6.3 minutes and $1.19. It produced
search, book details, an author's books and reviews:

```sh
api-anything call goodreads searchBooks q=piranesi
api-anything call goodreads getBook bookId=50202953
```


  
  


- **Tested on unseen books.** The test used 30 books that nobody used while building the
  operations. For the 29 books the search found, every checked field matched the page Chrome
  rendered: title, rating, ratings count and pages. All 146 calls went over plain HTTP.
- **Agent comparison.** An agent using the operations answered 5 books in 30.5 s; the browser
  agent took 182.5 s. For one book, it cost a third as much.
- **No agent needed.** A plain script ([`examples/reading-list.mjs`](examples/reading-list.mjs))
  builds the same five-book table in 16 s with no model.

[How it was explored, tested and compared](bench/explore/README.md).

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
- **Learn.** The headless browser records the page's requests for two example inputs. The request that
  followed the inputs becomes a template with slots, and cookies and tokens become references to
  a local store.
- **Call.** Fill the slots and send the request with Node's `fetch`. If the site blocks that,
  fetch from inside a browser page. As a last resort for reads, run the page itself and read its
  own response.
- **Repair.** If the request stops working (a rotated id, a moved field), re-learn it and save
  the new version only after a replay succeeds. Otherwise the call returns an error, not
  someone else's data.

[Details](docs/REFERENCE.md#replay-fallback-and-repair) · [design](docs/DESIGN.md)

evidence.heading: Limits
evidence.text:
- It is a local tool, not a hosted API. It uses your machine, your network and your sessions.
- It knows only the operations it was taught. It doesn't support every feature of every site.
- Repair can fail. There is no CAPTCHA solving, and if a site challenges real Chrome, you have
  to clear the challenge by hand.
- No write operations are bundled. LinkedIn messaging isn't bundled and hasn't been tested
  against LinkedIn. Writes are tested only against a local fixture, and they need
  `--allow-writes`. An HTTP 2xx doesn't prove a message was delivered.
- Credentials stay in `~/.api-anything`, and specs hold references, never values. Read each
  site's terms: you are responsible for how you use it.

[All limits](docs/REFERENCE.md#status-and-known-limits)
