evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Newsletters where you pay for the emails you send, not for dormant subscribers, at a fraction of the price of beehiiv and the like. Open source: self-host it, or use mailcheap.ai.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
MailCheap


  Newsletters where you pay for the emails you send, not for dormant subscribers.
  A fraction of the price of beehiiv and the like.



  Website ·
  API docs ·
  Sign up for MailCheap Cloud



  
  
  




MailCheap is a newsletter app: write an issue, send it to your list, publish it on the web, from the dashboard or from your AI agent. This repository is the whole app. Self-host it with your own Amazon SES or PostShiba account, or use [MailCheap Cloud](https://mailcheap.ai), which runs this same code.

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **AI agents and the dashboard.** Everything the dashboard does also works from an AI agent through the MCP server, and from code through the REST API, with the same checks and limits. ChatGPT, Claude and Grok Bot connect with OAuth; Claude Code, Codex and Cursor with an API key. MCP marks sending as an action that can't be undone, so agents ask you first.
- **Write, review, send.** Write in an editor with slash commands, images and boxes, or send Markdown or a complete HTML email through the API and MCP. Review shows what to fix before sending: subject, preview text, unsubscribe link, Gmail's 100 KB clip, postal address, sender. Then send it, schedule it, or start with your most engaged readers and send to more later.
- **Imports from beehiiv, Substack and Mailchimp.** Their CSV exports import as they are, with each reader's status and signup date, and so do Kit's, MailerLite's, Buttondown's, Ghost's and EmailOctopus's.
- **A website for each newsletter**, on a free subdomain on MailCheap Cloud (`<slug>.mailcheap.ai`), or on your server: every issue gets a page search engines can find, with a signup form, an author page, share images and a sitemap.
- **Sending from your own domain**, with the DKIM, return path and DMARC records to add and a check for each. On MailCheap Cloud, a newsletter without a domain sends from its own shared address, `hello@<slug>.mailcheap.ai`.
- **Deliverability protections**, built in:
  - warm-up: contacts the account never emailed go out as a 5% slice first, and the rest 3 hours later if the slice's bounces and complaints stay low. On MailCheap Cloud, an account's sends also speed up as it proves clean volume;
  - list cleanup, on by default: readers who ignored several issues get one "do you still want this?" email, then stop getting issue

evidence.heading: MailCheap Cloud or self-hosted
evidence.text:
| | [MailCheap Cloud](https://mailcheap.ai) | Self-hosted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Price | From $19 a month for 20,000 emails | Free, plus what your provider charges per email: $0.10 to $0.16 per 1,000 on Amazon SES |
| Sending | Set up for you, from `hello@<slug>.mailcheap.ai` or your domain | Your Amazon SES or PostShiba account, from your domain |
| Website | `<slug>.mailcheap.ai` | `/archive/<slug>` on your server's domain |
| Who signs in | Anyone who signs up | The emails you allow |
| Limits | Emails a month and active subscribers, by plan | None |
| Setup | A few minutes | About an hour, most of it waiting for DNS and production access |
| Support | A chat in the dashboard | None: issues are off |

MailCheap Cloud is this repository with `MAILCHEAP_CLOUD=true`, which adds open sign-up, plans and Stripe billing. Only active subscribers count toward a plan, not the ones list cleanup marked dormant. Its marketing site (the landing, pricing and legal pages) isn't part of the open source. Every change to the app ships to both.

With your own sending account, you pay your provider for the emails you send: 10,000 readers and 4 issues a month is 40,000 emails, about $4 to $6 on Amazon SES.

evidence.heading: Self-hosting
evidence.text:
[](https://vercel.com/new/clone?repository-url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmarclou%2Fmailcheap&project-name=mailcheap&repository-name=mailcheap&env=MONGODB_URI,BETTER_AUTH_SECRET,SUPPRESSION_HASH_KEY,ADMIN_EMAILS,EMAIL_FROM&envDescription=Database%2C%20a%20signing%20secret%20and%20a%20hash%20key%20%2832%2B%20characters%20each%3A%20openssl%20rand%20-base64%2048%29%2C%20your%20email%20to%20sign%20in%20with%2C%20and%20the%20from%20address%20of%20sign-in%20codes.%20Add%20RESEND_API_KEY%2C%20or%20set%20up%20SES%20or%20PostShiba%2C%20so%20the%20codes%20can%20reach%20you.&envLink=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmarclou%2Fmailcheap%23environment-variables)

Plan for about an hour, most of it waiting for DNS and for your provider to approve production sending. Self-hosting comes without support: issues are off and setup questions go unanswered.

evidence.heading: What you need
evidence.text:
| Service | For | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [MongoDB](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas) | Contacts, campaigns, stats | Free tier works |
| [Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/) or [PostShiba](https://postshiba.com) | Sending | SES: $0.10 to $0.16 per 1,000 emails, depending on its pricing plan. PostShiba: a fixed price per cluster, invite only for now |
| [Upstash QStash](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash) | Background sending and scheduling | Free tier to start, then pay per message. One message sends 50 emails |
| [Vercel](https://vercel.com) or any Node.js 22+ host | Hosting | Free tier works |
| [Resend](https://resend.com) (optional) | Sign-in codes and alerts. Without it, they go through SES or PostShiba | Free plan works |
| [Upstash Redis](https://upstash.com/docs/redis) (optional) | Rate limits shared by every server instance | Free tier |
| [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/) with [CloudFront](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/), or [Vercel Blob](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob) (optional) | Image uploads in the editor, the newsletter settings and the API | S3 and CloudFront: pay per use. Blob: free tier |

Without Redis, MailCheap counts the same rate limits in each server instance's memory. That still stops a script hammering a form, but on serverless hosts the limits aren't shared between instances and reset on each deploy. Add Redis before you put a signup form on a busy site. Without S3 or Blob, image uploads are off; HTML and Markdown campaigns can still use images hosted anywhere.

evidence.heading: Environment variables
evidence.text:
| Variable | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `MONGODB_URI` | MongoDB connection string with a database name |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | Signs sessions and every link in sent emails. 32+ random characters (`openssl rand -base64 48`), or the server refuses to start. Rotating it signs everyone out and breaks links in emails already sent |
| `SUPPRESSION_HASH_KEY` | Keys the hashes of the never-email list every account shares. 32+ random characters of its own, never `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, or the server refuses to start, after an upgrade too. Changing it empties the list |
| `ADMIN_EMAILS` | Comma-separated emails that can sign in and open `/admin` |
| `ALLOWED_EMAILS` | Who else can sign in: addresses and `@domain` entries, comma-separated |
| `EMAIL_FROM` | From address of sign-in codes and alerts, on a domain your Resend account or email provider verified |
| `APP_URL` | Public URL of the app, for email links and sign-in. On Vercel it defaults to the production domain |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | Optional: sign-in codes and alerts through Resend. Without it, they go through the email provider |
| `SENDING_ENABLED` | Nothing goes to readers unless it's `true`. Sign-in codes and alerts don't wait for it |
| `SES_*` or `POSTSHIBA_*` | The email provider, in step 4 |
| `QSTASH_*` | Background sending and scheduling, in step 5 |

[`.env.example`](.env.example) lists every variable with what it does, the optional ones included: Google sign-in and Postmaster Tools, image uploads, Redis, Telegram alerts, the shared domain, and MailCheap Cloud's own.

evidence.heading: 1. Database
evidence.text:
1. Create a free cluster on [MongoDB Atlas](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas).
2. **Database Access**: add a user with a password and the "Read and write to any database" role.
3. **Network Access**: allow `0.0.0.0/0`. Vercel doesn't have fixed IP addresses.

evidence.heading: Learning
evidence.text:
- [Azeria Labs](https://azeria-labs.com/writing-arm-assembly-part-1/) - ARM assembly tutorials with exercises for learning registers, memory, and calling conventions.
- [Compiler Explorer](https://godbolt.org/) - Compiles code in the browser with many compilers and shows the generated assembly, for seeing how source constructs and optimization levels translate to machine code.
- [Corkami](https://github.com/corkami/pics) - Visual references and posters explaining binary formats and file structures, including executable-format layouts.
- [Nightmare](https://guyinatuxedo.github.io/) - Course built from annotated CTF challenges, progressing from assembly and reversing basics to binary exploitation.
- [OpenSecurityTraining2](https://ost2.fyi/) - Structured courses in assembly, architecture, debugging, and reverse engineering.
- [pwn.college](https://pwn.college/) - Free courses with hands-on challenges in Linux, assembly, reverse engineering, and binary exploitation, run in a browser-accessible environment.
- [Reverse Engineering for Beginners](https://beginners.re/) - Free book connecting compiled C and C++ examples to assembly across several architectures.
- [RPISEC Modern Binary Exploitation](https://github.com/RPISEC/MBE) - Course materials and labs covering reverse engineering, memory corruption, and exploitation; no commits since December 2021, so labs may need older toolchains.

evidence.heading: Books
evidence.text:
- [Hacking the Xbox](https://www.bunniestudios.com/blog/2013/releasing-free-pdf-of-hacking-the-xbox-in-honor-of-aaron-swartz/) - Introduction to hardware reverse engineering through the original Xbox's security design; free PDF edition released by the author.
- [Practical Binary Analysis](https://nostarch.com/binaryanalysis) - Covers ELF and PE internals, disassembly, binary instrumentation, taint analysis, and symbolic execution, with tools built in the exercises.
- [Practical Malware Analysis](https://nostarch.com/malware) - Hands-on introduction to static and dynamic Windows malware analysis with lab exercises; published in 2012, so some tooling chapters are dated.
- [The Ghidra Book](https://nostarch.com/ghidra-book-2e) - Guide to Ghidra's disassembler, decompiler, scripting, and extension APIs; the 2026 second edition covers BSim and PyGhidra.

evidence.heading: File identification and triage
evidence.text:
- [capa](https://github.com/mandiant/capa) - Identifies capabilities in executable files using rules over static or dynamic analysis results.
- [checksec](https://github.com/slimm609/checksec) - Checks ELF security properties such as PIE, RELRO, stack canaries, and non-executable stacks; mitigation flags are not a vulnerability verdict.
- [Detect It Easy](https://github.com/horsicq/Detect-It-Easy) - Identifies executable formats, compilers, packers, and other file characteristics.
- [FLOSS](https://github.com/mandiant/flare-floss) - Recovers obfuscated strings, including strings constructed on the stack.
- [hexvero](https://github.com/maximilianfeix/hexvero) - Statically triages Electron archives and JavaScript bundles for IPC channels, preload bridges, and window settings, plus ELF/Mach-O/PE imports and hardening; its CLI, MCP server, and local web UI require Node.js 22.12+, and pattern-based JavaScript analysis can miss indirect code.
- [LIEF](https://github.com/lief-project/LIEF) - Parses and modifies executable formats such as PE, ELF, and Mach-O from code.
- [Malcat](https://malcat.fr/) - Hex editor and disassembler for triaging unknown files, with 50+ format parsers, embedded-file extraction, YARA scanning, and Python scripting. **Commercial**, with a free Lite edition for non-professional use.
- [PE-bear](https://github.com/hasherezade/pe-bear) - Graphical PE viewer and editor for a quick first look at headers, sections, imports, and resources, including malformed files.
- [pestudio](https://www.winitor.com/) - Flags suspicious imports, strings, resources, and other indicators in Windows executables for initial assessment. **Commercial**, with a free basic edition for private use.

evidence.heading: Native analysis
evidence.text:
- [Binary Ninja](https://binary.ninja/) - Interactive disassembler and decompiler with intermediate representations and scripting APIs. **Commercial**, with a free edition.
- [Cutter](https://github.com/rizinorg/cutter) - Graphical reverse-engineering interface built on Rizin.
- [Decompiler Explorer](https://dogbolt.org/) - Web service that runs an uploaded binary through several decompilers and shows their output side by side.
- [Ghidra](https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra) - Disassembly, decompilation, scripting, and headless analysis for native binaries.
- [IDA](https://hex-rays.com/ida-pro) - Interactive disassembler and decompiler with processor modules and a plugin ecosystem. **Commercial**, with a free edition.
- [radare2](https://github.com/radareorg/radare2) - Command-line toolkit for disassembly, binary inspection, debugging, and scripting.
- [RetDec](https://github.com/avast/retdec) - Retargetable LLVM-based decompiler for ELF, PE, Mach-O, and other formats; in limited maintenance mode, with little new development.
- [Rizin](https://github.com/rizinorg/rizin) - Reverse-engineering framework with command-line analysis and reusable libraries.
- [Rubber Room](https://binarybacktrace.com/tools/rubber_room) - Browser PE workbench with x86-64 disassembly, partial Win32 API emulation and experimental C-like pseudocode that may omit program logic; alpha.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Trace-native CI/CD for AI agents: grade production traces, cluster failures, freeze them into replayable regression tests, and block PRs that regress. Self-hostable.

evidence.heading: Production failures become regression tests.
evidence.text: **Trace-native CI/CD for AI agents.** Tracely grades every agent trace as it lands, clusters the failures into issues, freezes the bad runs into hermetic replayable cases, blocks the pull request that would ship them again — and tells you the moment any of it happens. production trace → failure detection → regression test → CI gate → alert [**Website**](https://tracely-ai.com) · [**Docs**](https://doc.tracely-ai.com) · [**Product guide**](https://doc.tracely-ai.com/product) · [**Agent skill**](#teach-your-coding-agent-tracely) · [**Guided tour**](guides/OVERVIEW.md) · [**2-min demo**](guides/DEMO.md) · [**Design dossier**](design/README.md) [](https://github.com/jwuthri-cloud/Tracely-ai/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [](https://pypi.org/project/tracelyai-sdk/) [](https://pypi.org/project/tracelyai-sdk/) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/jwuthri-cloud/Tracely-ai/stargazers) [](https://mcpvault.io/servers/tracely/health?utm_source=external_badge&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=mcp_health_report) **Self-host the whole stack in one click** — API, worker, UI, Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis and MinIO: [](https://railway.com/deploy/n5n_LE?referralCode=WCq5Cn&utm_medium=integration&utm_source=template&utm_campaign=generic) [](https://app.railyard.run/deploy?repo=https://github.com/jwuthri-cloud/Tracely-ai) One workspace: what ran, what broke, what is already pinned as a test. ---

evidence.heading: Why another agent-observability tool?
evidence.text:
Because observability stops at the dashboard. You can see that your agent broke — then what?

Every eval tool asks you to **hand-author a dataset**: sit down, invent questions, write ideal
answers, keep them current as the product changes. That dataset is a guess about what might break.

Production already handed you the real thing: a trace of the exact run that failed, with the exact
input, the exact tool calls, the exact model responses.

> **The recorded run _is_ the test.** Tracely freezes that trace into a hermetic regression case and
> replays it on every PR. Everything else — quality scores, failure clusters, suggested fixes, CI
> verdicts, trends, alerts — is **derived from the trace**. There are no hand-authored datasets.

|  | Dataset-first tools | Tracely |
|---|---|---|
| Where tests come from | You write them | Promoted from real failing traces |
| Fidelity to production | A guess | The exact failing run, byte for byte |
| Cost to replay in CI | Live model calls | **$0** — recorded tool/LLM fixtures |
| What happens on regression | A dashboard number moves | **The PR is blocked** |
| How you find out | You go and look | **It comes to you** — Slack, email, your own webhook |

---

evidence.heading: 1 · Observe — every run, hierarchically
evidence.text:
Traces arrive over plain OTLP. Agent semantics (`agent.id`, `conversation.id`, `turn`, `step`) are
promoted to first-class indexed columns, so runs group into conversation threads instead of a flat
span soup. The waterfall shows agent → thinking → skill → generation → hand-off, with the failing
span in red and its I/O beside it.



Evaluators are **columns on the trace table**, not a separate tab — each one grades at conversation,
run or span level and writes its verdict into the grid. Scores stream in live over SSE as judges
finish, so you watch a run get graded in place. Tokens, cost, latency, metadata and the rolling
per-turn summary are columns too.




Two extra ways to read one conversation — a step-by-step replay, and a pixel-art office



**Replay** walks the conversation event by event on a timeline. **Fleet** renders the same
conversation as a room: each agent is a character, hand-offs are walks across the floor, tools are
objects on the wall — which turns out to be the fastest way to explain a multi-agent system to
someone who doesn't read waterfalls.

evidence.heading: 2 · Detect & triage — failures group into issues
evidence.text:
Online evaluators grade every run as it lands (LLM-as-judge at conversation / run / span level, plus
structural checks that need no model at all). Failures then cluster — structurally and semantically —
so 31 broken runs become **one issue with a count**, not 31 rows to read. Each cluster can suggest
the evaluator that would have caught it.

evidence.heading: 3 · Test — freeze the failure
evidence.text:
One click promotes a failing trace into a hermetic case: recorded input, tool and LLM outputs bundled
as fixtures, and a **fail-to-pass contract** attached — the case must fail on the old code and pass on
the fix, or the promotion isn't trusted. Multi-turn behaviour gets **scenarios** instead: a scripted
conversation, or an adversarial goal a red-team model improvises against.

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text: **Prerequisites:** Docker + Docker Compose. (For local dev also [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node 20+ / pnpm.)

evidence.heading: Architecture
evidence.text:
The write path deliberately mirrors Langfuse's proven design — reimplemented in Python, with agent
semantics promoted to **first-class indexed columns** (Langfuse keeps them as read-time strings):

```
SDK/OTLP → POST /v1/traces → S3 blob (durable FIRST) → Redis/Celery
  → worker: otel mapping → registry upsert → ClickHouse events
  → evaluate_run_task → scores + structural clustering → alert flows
```

| Layer | Tech | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Backend (API + domain) | **FastAPI** + Pydantic v2 | [`backend/`](backend/README.md) |
| Workers | **Celery + Redis** | [`workers/`](workers/README.md) |
| Traces + scores (OLAP) | **ClickHouse** (`ReplacingMergeTree`) | `backend/tracely/infrastructure/clickhouse/ddl` |
| Registry (OLTP) | **Postgres + pgvector** + SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Alembic | `backend/migrations` |
| Queue / Blobs | **Redis** / **MinIO·S3** (blob-first, source of truth) | — |
| Frontend | **Next.js 15** (App Router) + Tailwind + React Flow | [`frontend/`](frontend/README.md) |
| SDK + CI gate CLI | **`tracelyai-sdk`** (OTel wrapper + `tracely` CLI) | [`sdk/`](sdk/README.md) |
| Tooling | **uv** workspace (Python) · **pnpm** (web) | — |

One deliberate adaptation: ClickHouse server-side `async_insert` instead of an in-process write buffer
(Celery tasks don't share memory). [Why](design/part2-tracely/01-steal-and-do-not-copy.md)

github_projects.description: Reason Network: your team's coding agents, talking to each other. The engine behind `reason network`.
github_projects.description_zh: Reason Network：你的团队编码智能体，相互交流。‘reason network’ 背后的引擎。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Reason Network: your team's coding agents, talking to each other. The engine behind `reason network`.

evidence.heading: Reason Network
evidence.text:
Your agents, talking to your **teammates'** agents. End-to-end encrypted, peer to peer.

> **AI agent asked to join the Reason Network?** Follow https://reasonmachines.com/network

One small daemon per computer. Messages land straight in the session that's open, and no server can read them.

Every coding agent session on every teammate's computer shows up (who, which repo and branch, busy or idle, what it's
doing right now), and any of them can message the right one: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI,
Grok CLI, opencode, pi, DeepSeek Harness and Reason.

evidence.heading: Get started
evidence.text:
Paste this line to your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, …):

```
Join the Reason Network: https://reasonmachines.com/network
```

Or run it yourself, in a terminal:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://reasonmachines.com/install.sh | bash -s -- network
```

How it works:

1. **Sign in, and you have a network.** Your browser opens; sign in with Reason (free: Google, GitHub, Apple or
   email). The coding agents on this computer are set up.
2. **Your other computers join by signing in with the same account.** Run the same line there; it lands on your network.
3. **Friends join with your invite line.** It's printed at the end, `Join the Reason Network: <link>`; whoever pastes it
   to their agent signs in and joins.

With an invite link, in a terminal:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://reasonmachines.com/install.sh | bash -s -- network join '<link>'
```

- **Hosted assistants** (Grok Bot, Muse, ChatGPT, …): add the MCP server `https://mcp.reasonmachines.com/mcp`.
- **Windows**, in PowerShell: `irm https://reasonmachines.com/network/install.ps1 | iex`

That's it. Ask any agent "who's on the network?", tell it to ask someone's agent something, or to send them a file.

evidence.heading: What you get
evidence.text:
- **Every agent on the team.** Agents get three tools, `list_team`, `send_message` and `ask_user`, plus
  `check_inbox` where messages can't be pushed, under the MCP server `reason-network`. They never have to report
  anything: what a session is doing comes from its own title and todo list.
- **Messages land right away.** Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi and Reason get them mid-session, and idle ones wake
  up; Cursor, Gemini, Copilot and Grok at their next step; DeepSeek Harness when it checks its inbox (every tool
  result says if mail is waiting). Claude sessions you already had open join without a restart.
- **ZCode Desktop too.** `setup` adds the MCP server to `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` (or `~/.agents/mcp.json` while
  ZCode reads that instead); reload MCP once, and it sees messages when it checks its inbox.
- **Small text files go along.** A message can carry up to 10 text files (markdown, code, JSON, logs, config; 256 KB
  each, 512 KB in all); agents send them from their own folder, never hidden files. The recipient's engine saves copies
  under `~/.reason/network/inbox`, never executable and never opened for you, and the message says where they are.
- **Your sign-off, even when you're away from your agent.** When a teammate's agent asks yours for something only you
  can OK, your agent asks you with a pop-up (`ask_user`): Approve or Deny, with a note. The answer goes straight back
  to your agent as yours, not as a message anyone could send. With `notify`, a message also pops up on the person's
  screen as a heads-up. (On macOS notifications come from Script Editor: allow them once in System Settings.)
- **A menu bar icon** on macOS shows who's online and what they're doing.
- **No setup to maintain.** It runs in the background and stays up to date (on its own

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Each computer runs a small daemon. Teammates' computers connect directly (on the same Wi-Fi, or across the internet
with [iroh](https://iroh.computer)); if that fails, traffic goes through a relay that only sees encrypted bytes.
That's Reason's, with computers finding each other through the address lookup of n0 (the company behind iroh), unless
your team runs its own relay (`reason-network relay <url>`): then your computers contact nothing else, n0 included.
Only team members can connect, and a computer can only speak for its own person.
Messages to someone offline wait and go out when they're back.
An agent session's name stays with its conversation, for a session the agent identifies: resumed after a restart, it
gets the same name back with the messages that waited for it, and for a day no new session takes the name.

Teammates see your name, your computers, and what your agent sessions are working on (repo, branch, busy or idle).
Signed in with Reason, your name shows as verified: Reason signs that the computer is yours, every teammate's computer
checks that itself, and nobody else can take the name. State lives in `~/.reason/network`. Details: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

Direct connections use a random UDP port each time the daemon starts. To open or forward one port in a firewall or
router instead, set it in `~/.reason/network/config.toml` (per computer; the daemon reads it when it starts):

```toml
port = 41641
```

Put `port` at the top of the file, above any `[table]` section such as `[inbound]`. The daemon ignores it under a table.

It is bound on IPv4 and IPv6 (IPv4 alone on a computer without IPv6). If another program holds it on either, the
daemon logs that and uses a random port, as without it; `port = 0` is the same as leaving it out.
`reason-network doctor`

evidence.heading: Uninstall
evidence.text:
```sh
reason-network leave && reason-network setup --remove && rm -rf ~/.reason/network ~/.local/bin/reason-network
rm -f ~/.local/bin/tincan   # if you came from tincan
```

On Windows, in PowerShell: `reason-network leave; reason-network setup --remove; Remove-Item -Recurse -Force ~\.reason\network, ~\.local\bin\reason-network*`

With the Reason CLI: `reason network leave`, then `reason network setup --remove`.

evidence.heading: Build
evidence.text:
```sh
cargo fmt && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test
cargo build && python3 tests/e2e/two_machines.py   # two machines over iroh (needs internet)
python3 tests/e2e/hooks.py && python3 tests/e2e/codex_busy.py && python3 tests/e2e/guided.py
```

A `v*` tag builds the macOS, Linux and Windows archives and the install scripts; the Reason CLI pins the macOS and
Linux ones.

evidence.heading: 项目介绍
evidence.text:
**用户说"我想吃巨无霸套餐，怎么最便宜"，它拉取门店菜单和所有可用优惠券，
用算法穷举出总价最低的合规组合，并帮你下单。**

示例：巨无霸 + 中薯条 + 可乐，直选 **¥47.00**；
用「1+1 随心配」组合后 **¥21.90**，省 **¥25.10（53%）**。

它不止会算"最便宜"，还能回答四个衍生问题：

| 问题 | 能力 |
|---|---|
| 这顿饭我想省钱 / 吃全 / 低卡 / 少排队 | **多目标优化**：4 种点餐目标，同一约束给不同最优解 |
| 手里这堆券，哪张优惠更实在？ | **券体检**：名义面额 vs 实际节省 vs 机会成本 |
| 差几块钱到下一档满减，加购划不划算？ | **凑单建议**：最小代价补位，算出净变化（可能为负） |
| 便宜和低卡不可兼得，边界在哪？ | **帕累托前沿**：价格 × 热量的不可支配解集 |
| 一家人 / 一桌同事怎么点？ | **多人拼单**：按份数计价、人均分摊，优惠只计一次（保守） |

🎮 **在线试算（无需登录）**：<https://hujjun.github.io/mcd-saver-strategist/> ——
优化算法的前端完整复刻，选好想吃的、切换目标、拖动预算和热量上限，实时算出最优组合；
页面里还有券体检和帕累托前沿图，打开即玩。

🔎 静态示例：[`docs/demo.html`](docs/demo.html) ·
🖼️ 原理图：[`images/how-it-works.png`](images/how-it-works.png) ·
🎬 宣传动画：[`images/promo.mp4`](images/promo.mp4)





---

evidence.heading: 它解决什么问题
evidence.text:
麦当劳的优惠是典型的**组合爆炸**问题：

- 菜单几十项、优惠券动辄十几张、叠加规则各不相同；
- 用券还要考虑「为凑满减而加购是否划算」；
- 用户懒得算，大模型**也容易算错**（价格、折扣、叠加口算不可靠）。

本 Skill 的核心洞察是：**取数交给 MCP，算术交给代码，表达交给 Agent。**

| 角色 | 职责 |
|---|---|
| 麦当劳 MCP | 实时菜单、价格、优惠券、营养、门店、下单 |
| `scripts/optimizer.py` | 确定性组合优化，输出总价最低的 Top-N 方案 |
| WorkBuddy Agent | 理解需求、归一化数据、讲解方案、确认后下单 |

---

evidence.text:

flowchart TD

```

evidence.heading: 使用示例
evidence.text:
**示例 1 · 单人到店**
> 用户：我想吃巨无霸 + 薯条 + 可乐，怎么最便宜？

精算师：拉菜单 + 四路券池 → 优化 → 「1+1 随心配 ¥12.9 覆盖巨无霸和中薯条，另外单点可乐 ¥9，
合计 ¥21.90，比直选省 ¥25.10」。

**示例 2 · 预算硬约束**
> 用户：30 块钱在麦当劳能吃到什么？

精算师：以 `budget=30` 求解，返回在预算内的最优搭配，并列出各方案到手价与热量。

**示例 3 · 热量约束**
> 用户：减脂期，想吃麦当劳，800 大卡以内还要便宜。

精算师：引入 `list-nutrition-foods`，以 `max_calories=800` 求解，
给出低卡又省钱的组合（如板烧鸡腿堡 + 麦咖啡 + 圆筒）。

**示例 4 · 外送**
> 用户：帮我在麦乐送点一份午餐，别超过 40。

精算师：`delivery-query-addresses` → `delivery-query-stores` → 后续流程同上，
下单前用 `calculate-price` 核价（含配送费）。

**示例 5 · 券太多不会用**
> 用户：我有 8 张券，帮我看看哪张值得用。

精算师：四路券池归一化 → `audit_coupons()` 逐张体检 →
「1+1 随心配值得用；这张'满 35 减 7'名义省 7 元，但用了它就吃不到 1+1，反而多花 18 元」。

**示例 6 · 凑单**
> 用户：还差多少能到满减？加个什么划算？

精算师：`suggest_gap()` 用子集和 DP 找最小代价补位 →
「还差 7 元，加个香芋派 7.5 元，多减 12 元，净省 4.5 元」。

**示例 7 · 多人拼单**
> 用户：我们 3 个人各要一份，一共多少钱？

精算师：`party_size=3` 求解 → 总价 + 人均，优惠只计一次（保守计价，不报假低价）。

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Co-op Anything

Any single-player game. Your friends. Your agent does the work.








Quick start ·
How it works ·
What you can co-op ·
Games so far ·
Contribute ·
FAQ ·
Docs


Want to play a single-player game with your friends? Point your AI coding agent at this
repo. It researches what exists, reverse engineers the game and its engine if it has to,
builds or fixes the co-op, **tests it with bots inside the game**, and packages it so your
friends install it in one click and join over Steam without port forwarding.

The sky is the limit. Every game that runs on your PC is a candidate.

Games being made co-op right now: **[Deus Ex](https://github.com/cranebeaker/deus-ex-coop)** (released) ·
**[Fallout: New Vegas](https://github.com/cranebeaker/fnv-coop)** · **[Zelda: Ocarina of Time](https://github.com/cranebeaker/ocarina-coop)** (fully synced) ·
**[Dungeon Keeper](https://github.com/cranebeaker/dungeon-keeper-coop)** · **[S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Shadow of Chernobyl](https://github.com/cranebeaker/stalker-soc-coop-fixes)**

From the community: **[Mega Man X](https://github.com/mstan/MegaManXSNESRecomp)** and
**[Mega Man X4](https://github.com/mstan/MegaManX4Recomp)** (native PC with co-op netplay) ·
**[Pilotwings 64](https://github.com/NoahVl/Birdman64)** (split-screen) ·
**[Crab Champions](https://github.com/Dudiebug/CrabMods/blob/main/crabsync/README.md)** · **[Stacklands](https://github.com/Dudiebug/stacklands-coop)** ·
**[Half Sword](https://github.com/Dudiebug/halfsword-multiplayer-mod)** · **[Enter the Gungeon](https://thunderstore.io/c/enter-the-gungeon/p/GoTeamAlex/Gungeon_Online/)** ·
**[Clive Barker's Jericho](https://github.com/dolbaras/jericho-coop)** · **[Poppy Playtime](https://github.com/romannazarov057-spec/PoppyCoop)** ·
**[Divinity II](games/divinity-2-develo

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
Tell your agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, ...):

```
Read https://github.com/cranebeaker/coop-anything and follow AGENTS.md.
I want to play <game> in co-op with my friends.
```

The agent follows [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the skills in [`.agents/skills`](.agents/skills)
(also in `.claude/skills` for Claude Code).

evidence.heading: Add the MCP server
evidence.text:
The **Co-op Anything MCP** lets any agent search the co-op directory, detect a game's engine
from its install folder, read the playbook and skills, and validate contributions.
Claude Code picks it up from this repo's `.mcp.json`; for other agents:

```
claude mcp add coop-anything -- python <clone>/tools/mcp/coop_mcp.py
```

Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor setup: [playbook/mcp.md](playbook/mcp.md). For the binary work,
pair it with a reverse-engineering MCP such as [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea)
(`npx rea-agents setup`): Co-op Anything knows what to do, REA looks inside the game.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Your agent takes one of two paths.

| | Path 1: finish what exists | Path 2: build it from zero |
|---|---|---|
| When | A co-op mod exists but is buggy, stalled or abandoned. Most loved games are here. | Nothing usable exists. |
| How | Find the last build, mine its bug reports (issues, forums, Discord), audit the code, fix it as a separate package, test, ship. | Reverse engineer the game and engine, hook in, show the second player, sync enemies, world and story, handle level changes and saves, test, ship. |
| Skills | `coop-research`, `coop-revive`, `coop-qa` | `coop-reverse-engineer`, `coop-build-from-zero`, `coop-networking`, `coop-sync-testing`, `coop-qa` |
| Guide | [Reviving abandoned mods](playbook/reviving-abandoned-mods.md) | [How co-op mods work](playbook/how-coop-mods-work.md) |

Both paths end the same way: automated tests with real game clients
([QA](playbook/automated-qa.md)), easy install, Steam relay networking
([networking](playbook/networking.md)), and a pull request back here.

evidence.heading: Sync test tools
evidence.text:
Ready-made, game-agnostic tools for building and testing co-op sync, in [`tools/`](tools/README.md).
Each has tests, mutation twins and one command that prints `ALL OK`
(`python -I tools/test_all.py` runs them all).

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| [chaos](tools/chaos) | UDP relay that adds lag, loss, reorder, duplicates and one-way cuts between real clients, with live control |
| [flight](tools/flight) | Flight recorder for your mod plus an analyzer: lines up 2 to 4 machines, finds the first desync, shrinks it and writes a regression test |
| [fuzz](tools/fuzz) | Seeded N-player co-op fuzzer with invariant oracles (converge, no double apply, one owner, no dupes, nothing stale) |
| [ownership](tools/ownership) | Small C++ library: one owner per NPC with epochs, handoff, and stale echo rejection |
| [fakeworld](tools/fakeworld) | Example in-memory game world for testing sync without launching the game |
| [gameslot](tools/gameslot), [gamepool](tools/gamepool) | Lock and warm pool for running several game copies on one PC safely |
| [scenarios](tools/scenarios), [bots](tools/bots) | JSON start states plus multi-bot co-op playbooks with a state diff after each step |
| [animcheck](tools/animcheck) | Compares animation and pose across machines and flags sliding, T-poses, floating and rubber-banding |
| [bridge](tools/bridge), [inspect](tools/inspect) | An RPC server template for inside your game (console line, state dump, save, load, screenshot) with a Python client, plus a live side-by-side view of every copy |
| [hotreload](tools/hotreload) | Split your mod into a loader and a core, and swap the core inside the running games instead of restarting them |
| [mutants](tools/mutants), [buildlock](tools/buildlock) | Runtime mutation twins for every fix, and a shared build

evidence.heading: What you can co-op
evidence.text:
| Your game is... | Typical approach | Tools your agent uses |
|---|---|---|
| On an engine with multiplayer already (Unreal 1/2, Source, id Tech, X-Ray) | Make the single-player logic run on the existing netcode with script mods | Script source, SDK compilers, mod packages |
| Bethesda (Gamebryo, Creation) | Script extender plugin, host-authority sync, reuse Tilted Online style designs | SKSE / F4SE / xNVSE, Ghidra, REA |
| Unity | Harmony patches through a mod loader, a networking library in C# | BepInEx, MelonLoader, dnSpyEx, Il2CppDumper |
| Unreal Engine 4/5 | Lua or C++ mods with an SDK dump of the game's classes | UE4SS, Dumper-7 |
| RE Engine, FromSoftware, other proprietary | DLL hooks; extend the game's own online features where they exist | REFramework, MinHook, Ghidra, REA, x64dbg |
| Decompiled or open source (N64 decomps, KeeperFX, OpenMW, source ports) | Add networking directly in the code | A compiler, the decomp, Docker cross builds |
| Console only (PS1, PS2, N64, Dreamcast, GameCube, Wii, GBA, ...) | Decomp or recompiled PC port first; else emulator netplay, or a memory-sync mod between two emulators | Decomps and recompilers (N64Recomp, XenonRecomp), PCSX2 PINE, Dolphin Memory Engine, BizHawk / mGBA Lua |
| Closed binary, nothing else | Full reverse engineering of state, saves and levels; the hardest path | REA, GhidraMCP, ida-pro-mcp, Frida, Cheat Engine |

Console games: [emulator co-op](playbook/console-emulators.md) and
[decompiled or recompiled PC ports](playbook/decomp-and-recomp.md), the route Ocarina of Time co-op took.

Couch co-op on one PC? [Split screen](playbook/split-screen.md) builds on Nucleus Co-op
(Windows) and PartyDeck (Linux and Steam Deck), both open source.

Full tool list with install notes: [playbook/tools.md](playbook/tools.

[English](./README.en.md) | 简体中文

CodeAgent 是一个跑在终端里的 AI 编程助手：你用自然语言下指令，它读代码、改文件、跑命令、查资料，把活干完。它有自己的一套「长本事」机制——从对话轨迹里沉淀可复用的技能，越用越顺手。

evidence.heading: 🧭 这是一份手写的「中文版 claude code」
evidence.text:
不是套壳，也不是翻译——是从交互界面到 Agent 主循环一行行手写出来的完整实现，**注释全是中文**：

- 📚 **想学 Agent 开发？这就是活教材。** 工具自注册、上下文分级压缩、权限审批、子代理团队、工作流引擎、记忆系统——一个真实可跑的 Agent 全链路都在这儿，每个模块都是「大白话流程 → 参数 → 返回」的保姆级中文注释，读代码像读教程。
- 🛠 **欢迎上手改。** 觉得哪里不顺手？fork 了直接改——代码结构清晰、注释到位，改起来不费劲。欢迎 PR：修 bug、加功能、优化界面都行。
- 💬 **有问题社区问。** 卡住了、看不懂了、想讨论设计，直接去 [Issues](https://github.com/Harvil1/codeAgent/issues) 或 [Discussions](https://github.com/Harvil1/codeAgent/discussions) 发帖，有问必答。

evidence.heading: ✨ 特性
evidence.text:
**终端体验（对标 claude code）**
- 流式回答圆角框、思考流暗色框、工具事件行（`● Bash(...)` + `⎿ 结果`）
- 危险命令 / 白名单外写文件的**审批面板**：允许一次 / 总是允许 / 拒绝三选，面板答完自擦不污染上下文
- Ctrl+C 语义分明：回合中一键中断、双击强退；审批面板上 Ctrl+C 一击取消并中断整轮
- 皮肤系统、页脚状态栏、命令补全、输入历史、粘贴大段文本自动落盘引用

**模型与工具**
- 多模型接入：OpenAI 兼容协议（默认 DeepSeek）与 Anthropic 协议均可配；主模型 + 辅助小模型（压缩/检索/记忆提取等杂活走便宜模型）
- 工具自注册体系：`tools/` 下模块 import 即登记，按「套餐」（toolset）控制发给模型的工具集
- MCP 外部工具：项目级 `.mcp.json` 声明即接入，首次连接需审批
- 内置工具覆盖文件读写、终端执行、搜索、代码检索、Web 抓取、后台任务、子代理派发等

**安全防线**
- 破坏性命令审批 + 跨会话白名单（按命令 / 按前缀规则记忆）
- 注入面检测（`$()`、进程替换等「所见非所执行」形态升审批）、删除路径红线、自我保护
- 秘钥扫描（防 API key 写入文件/记忆）、SSRF 防护、Web 内容注入隔离
- Linux 下可选 bwrap 沙箱执行

**记忆与自学习**
- 长期记忆：`MEMORY.md` 索引 + JSONL 存储 + 检索结果临时注入（不污染正式历史）
- 技能系统：用户技能 + 插件市场技能（`/plugin` 管理），支持按触碰文件路径条件激活
- 自学习管线：观察对话轨迹 → 沉淀新技能（启发式 / 辅助模型两种观察方式）

**协作与自动化**
- 子代理：同步 / 后台派发，worktree 隔离，后台代理无人审批时自动 fail-closed
- 团队模式：coordinator / worker / 消息总线 / 邮箱
- 工作流引擎：确定性编排、日志断点续跑、花费封顶
- 定时任务（cron）、声明式 hooks、任务清单、会话 checkpoint 回溯（`/rewind`）

**上下文工程**
- 分级压缩（L1 轻裁剪 → L4 深度摘要）、批间工具摘要、时间基线旧结果清理
- 前缀缓存友好：临时消息注入与剥离时机讲究，不破坏缓存前缀

evidence.heading: 🚀 快速开始
evidence.text:
前提：[Python 3.11+](https://www.python.org/) 和 [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)（Python 包管理器）。

```bash
# 1) 安装 uv（已有可跳过）
#    Windows (PowerShell):  powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
#    macOS / Linux:         curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# 2) 拉代码 + 装依赖
git clone https://github.com/Harvil1/codeAgent.git
cd codeAgent
uv sync

# 3) 配置 API key（二选一）
#    a) 环境变量——按所用厂商设置其一即可，程序会自动识别：
#       DEEPSEEK_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY /
#       OPENROUTER_API_KEY / ZHIPUAI_API_KEY（BIGMODEL_API_KEY 亦可）
#    b) 写入 ~/.codeAgent/settings.json 的 models.<名字>.api_key
#       （首次运行会自动生成默认配置文件，默认模型为 DeepSeek）

# 4) 跑起来
uv run python main.py              # 交互模式
uv run python main.py -c           # 自动恢复最近一次会话
```

> 提示：换模型 / 换厂商在会话里输 `/model` 按引导配置，或直接编辑 `~/.codeAgent/settings.json`。

evidence.heading: ⌨️ 常用操作
evidence.text:
会话内 40+ 个 slash 命令，常用如下：

| 命令 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `/help` | 命令帮助 |
| `/model` | 切换 / 配置模型（按引导填厂商、key、端点） |
| `/new` `/resume` `/sessions` | 新会话 / 恢复 / 会话列表 |
| `/rewind` | 回溯到某个 checkpoint 重来 |
| `/skills` `/plugin` | 管理技能 / 插件市场 |
| `/memory` | 查看维护长期记忆 |
| `/permission` `/sandbox` `/approved` | 权限模式 / 沙箱开关 / 已批准命令白名单 |
| `/doctor` | 自诊断（配置、网络、组件健康检查） |
| `/plan` | 计划模式：先出方案批准再动手 |
| `/stats` `/usage` `/trace` | 花费统计 / 用量 / 调用链追踪 |

evidence.heading: ⚙️ 配置与数据
evidence.text:
运行时数据统一放在 `~/.codeAgent/`（环境变量 `CODEAGENT_HOME` 可覆盖，测试 / 多配置隔离用）：

| 路径 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `settings.json` | 全部配置（默认值单一源头在代码里，落盘深合并，手改安全） |
| `sessions.db/` | 会话持久化（JSONL） |
| `MEMORY.md` + 记忆库 | 长期记忆索引与正文 |
| `skills/` | 用户技能 |
| `plugins/` | 插件（含官方市场 `claude-plugins-official`） |
| `logs/` | 运行日志（滚动，5MB × 3） |

evidence.heading: 🏗 架构一览
evidence.text:
调用链一句话：`main.py`（点火：控制台编码、终端自举）→ `cli.main` → `run_interactive`（REPL + slash 命令 + RuntimeContext 装配）→ `AIAgent.run_conversation`（主循环心脏）。

主循环每轮：组装消息（注入后台 / 定时 / 团队 / 计划等临时消息）→ 上下文压缩 → 刷新工具集 → 调 LLM → 分发工具调用，模型不再要工具即收尾。

| 子系统 | 模块 |
|---|---|
| LLM | `llm_client.py`（OpenAI 兼容 / Anthropic 协议）、`aux_llm.py`（辅助小模型路由） |
| 记忆 | `memory_store.py`、`memory_retriever.py` |
| 上下文 | `context_compressor.py`（分级压缩）、`context_pipeline.py` |
| 子代理 / 团队 | `tools/delegate_tool.py`、`agent/team/` |
| 工作流 | `workflow_engine.py` + `workflow_journal.py` |
| 技能 | `~/.codeAgent/skills/` + `agent/skill_learning/`（自学习） |
| 安全 | `bash_injection.py`、`ssrf_guard.py`、`secret_scanner.py`、`sandbox_runner.py`、`permission.py` |
| 持久化 | `session_store.py`、`task_store.py`、`hooks.py` |

kind_reason.text: 可扩展终端编程智能体及工具循环实现。

summary.text: CodeAgent 是以 Windows 体验为优先的终端编程助手，支持读写代码、命令执行、MCP、记忆与子智能体，提供中文注释便于学习实现。

value.text: 将可运行的智能体链路与解释性源码放在一起，兼顾使用和二次开发。

mechanism.text: 主循环组装消息、压缩上下文、刷新工具集、调用模型并分发工具；辅助模型处理压缩、检索等任务，模块导入即可注册工具。

inspiration.text: 可尝试将复杂模块用“流程、参数、返回”注释解释，同时把配置、网络和组件诊断集中到 doctor。

limitations.text: 需要外部模型配置；MCP 首次连接和特定命令或文件写入存在审批，长期数据默认放在 ~/.codeAgent。自学习效果未由摘录证明。

how_to.text: 准备 Python 3.11+ 和 uv，克隆后 uv sync，配置模型密钥；用 /model、/doctor、/skills 等命令管理。

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
EasyRead
让你更舒服地读论文
导入 PDF，后台逐页翻译；公式、表格照原文排好，随时对照原文，边读边划线、记笔记、提问。
本地运行，文献库默认保存在电脑上，也可以放进你自己的网盘同步文件夹

简体中文 · English

▶ 在线试读一篇 · 项目主页 · 下载

evidence.heading: 它和“把 PDF 丢给翻译软件”有什么不一样
evidence.text:
- **像读一本排好版的中文书。** 宋体正文、舒服的行宽和行距，公式用 KaTeX 按原文重排，表格是三线表，参考文献保留原文。顶栏一键切深色。
- **随时核对原文。** 一键切“对照”，每段下面附英文；右侧可以开原页，跟着阅读位置翻页，还会框出当前段落在原页的位置。
- **在论文里找内容。** 按 Ctrl / ⌘ + F 同时搜索原文和译文，显示匹配数、高亮结果，用 Enter / Shift + Enter 跳到下一处 / 上一处
- **翻译和解释分开。** 正文只放忠实的译文；AI 的解释、回答放在页边，一眼就能分清哪句是论文说的。
- **边读边问 AI。** 右侧“问 AI”面板实时对话，回答逐字流出来；可以一次引用好几段（选中文字拖进输入框就行）。问“我标红的那些公式有什么联系”，它会按颜色找出你的划线。可以开多个对话，模型单独选：Claude、GPT（Codex）、DeepSeek、通义、本机 Ollama……好的回答一键放到页边。
- **ASD-STE100 问答。** 在“问 AI”的“回答方式”里选择这个模式，用简明中文回答问题或总结论文，保留专业术语、公式和数值。模式按对话保存，支持复制、放到页边和导出 Markdown。[ASD-STE100](https://www.asd-ste100.org/STE_faq.html) 是英文标准；这个模式借鉴其短句、主动表达和术语一致等原则，提供中文写作辅助，不将中文答案标为符合英文标准或已认证。正文过长时只提供节选，回答需说明依据范围。
  中文提示词另参考 [asd-ste100-skill](https://github.com/danyuchn/asd-ste100-skill) 的语义保留原则：保留条件、范围和“可能／建议／必须”等语气强度，不为简短而丢失精度。
- **精读问答。** “回答方式”里的第三档，适合想弄明白“作者为什么这么做、这个结论能撑多远”的时候：先还原作者要解决的问题，分清哪些设计拿掉就塌、哪些是顺手加的，把关键公式代进具体数字算一遍，再核对正文数字和图表、基线对照条件是否对齐。论文没报告的就直说没报告，不替作者补数字。和简明回答一样会把全文发给模型，用量更多。
- **边读边批注。** 选中文字四色荧光笔或下划线、写笔记、提问；问题一键让 AI 回答，笔记可以让 AI 点评。笔记面板按正文顺序汇总批注，可以筛选、滚动回看；点击卡片定位正文，点“编辑”才改笔记。通过缩略图选择或从正文拖拽，把图表关联到笔记，展开查看或修改图表名称；正文里的图表引用可以悬停预览。可以勾选导出成 Markdown（放进 Obsidian、Notion）
- **译文可以改。** 双击一段直接改；术语表里改一个译法，全文替换。
- **不只是 arXiv。** 拖进任何 PDF；或者填 arXiv 编号、DOI、论文标题、论文网页（OpenReview、ACL、NeurIPS、bioRxiv、PMC、期刊页面），自动找到公开的 PDF 并补全作者、年份、出处。
- **从 Zotero 搬过来。** 导入对话框里点“从 Zotero 迁移整个文献库”，自动找到 Zotero 的数据文件夹，把有 PDF 的论文连同分类（多级照样分层）、标题、作者、年份、期刊、DOI、摘要一起搬进来；只读 Zotero 的数据库副本，不改动 Zotero，可以重复迁移。也能“导入整个文件夹”：选一个放论文的文件夹，子文件夹的层级就是分类的层级。两种都在后台导入、可以中途停止，导入后不翻译，想读哪篇再译哪篇。
- **链接本地 PDF。** Zotero 和文件夹批量导入可勾选“链接本地 PDF，不复制原文件”，命令行可用 `--link`。原 PDF 留在原位，缓存、笔记和进度留在 EasyRead；删除论文不会删除原 PDF。链接需要原路径一直可访问，已有论文不会因重复导入而改变存储方式。[用法](docs/linked-local-pdfs.md)
- **文献库。** 侧栏像聊天软件：论文和分类都能置顶；自己建分类（右键改名、删除，把论文拖进去），分类可以分层（右键“新建子分类”“移到…”，点父分类列出所有子分类的论文），内置分类可以隐藏；最近阅读、搜索、未读 /

evidence.heading: 翻译用什么模型：你来选
evidence.text:
| 引擎 | 要什么 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code**（推荐） | 装好并登录 [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/setup) | 不用 Key，用你订阅的额度；会自己看原页图核对公式，译文最好 |
| **Codex CLI** | 装好并登录 [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) | 不用 Key，用 ChatGPT 账号 |
| **CodeBuddy CLI** | 按[官方 CLI 文档](https://www.codebuddy.cn/docs/cli/headless)安装并登录，账号需有 CLI 使用权益 | 不用 Key；模型名自己填，留空用 CLI 默认模型。[当前免费体验版不含 CLI](https://www.codebuddy.cn/docs/workbuddy/Pricing)，与 WorkBuddy 同账号共享积分 |
| **Grok Build / Antigravity CLI / Cursor CLI** | 装好并登录 [Grok Build](https://x.ai/cli)、[Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli) 或 [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/installation) | 不用 Key，用各自的订阅；模型名自己填，留空用它的默认 |
| **API 接口 · 国内直连**：DeepSeek / 智谱 / 阿里云百炼 / Kimi / 硅基流动 / 魔搭 | API Key | 智谱 GLM-4.7-Flash、硅基流动小模型免费；DeepSeek 一篇 20 页论文几毛钱 |
| **API 接口 · 海外（要梯子）**：OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / OpenRouter / Groq / Cerebras | API Key | Gemini、OpenRouter、Groq、Cerebras 有免费额度 |
| **API 接口 · 本机**：Ollama / LM Studio | 本机装 [Ollama](https://ollama.com) 或 [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai) | 完全离线、免费，推荐 qwen3.5:9b（显卡小用 4b） |
| **API 接口 · 自定义地址**：任意 OpenAI 兼容接口、中转站 | 地址 + Key | Chat Completions 和 Responses 两种格式都支持；接口名称和地址可保存复用，Key 按地址分别保存；点“获取模型列表”从接口拉模型名 |

不想让它导入后马上翻译，在设置里关掉“导入后自动开始翻译”就行，之后可以让对话里的 agent 来译。

设置里会自动检测本机装了什么，点“试译一句”马上知道能不能用。某一页翻译失败（限流、网络、额度）会自动重试，还不行就先跳过、接着译后面的页，最后一键“重试失败的页”。

默认逐篇翻译，单篇内部仍可分段并发。在“设置 → 模型 → 翻译”中可将“同时翻译几篇”设为 1–4 篇，重启后生效。多篇并行会叠加分段并发，增加内存和模型限流风险，建议保持默认 1 篇；详见[配置说明](docs/paper-concurrency.md)

evidence.heading: 安装
evidence.text:
**最省事：下载安装包**（不用装 Python）。在 [Releases](https://github.com/Edwardxlai/easyread/releases/latest) 下载：

- **Windows**：`EasyRead-Setup-x.x.x.exe`，双击安装。没有代码签名，如果弹出“Windows 已保护你的电脑”，点“更多信息 → 仍要运行”。
- **macOS**（Apple 芯片）：`EasyRead-x.x.x-arm64.dmg`，把 EasyRead 拖进“应用程序”；第一次打开被系统拦截时，按下面对应的提示处理
- **Linux**：`EasyRead-x.x.x.AppImage`，`chmod +x` 后运行。
- 如果 Linux 提示缺少 `libfuse.so.2`，可按 [AppImage 官方说明](https://docs.appimage.org/user-guide/troubleshooting/fuse.html)配置 FUSE，或在独立目录运行 `./EasyRead-x.x.x.AppImage --appimage-extract`，再运行 `./squashfs-root/AppRun`；无需关闭沙箱

论文和设置存在哪：Windows 安装版在安装目录下的 `data` 文件夹（装在 D 盘就在 D 盘，更新和卸载都会保留）；macOS、Linux 在用户目录下的 `EasyRead` 文件夹（和 pip 安装版同一个位置）。卸载重装不会丢。

以后升级：Windows、macOS 安装版和直接打开的 Linux AppImage 都可以在程序里更新，有新版本时顶栏会提示（也可以在右上角问号里手动检查），点“更新”，可以放到后台下载，下好后点“更新并重启”。解压运行的 AppImage 和从源码运行的照旧从 Releases 下载新版。macOS 和 Linux 从 1.3.2 及以前升级时，要先手动下载 1.3.3 一次；macOS 要把 EasyRead 放在“应用程序”里才能在程序里更新。

evidence.heading: macOS 首次打开
evidence.text:
1. **提示“无法验证开发者”或“Apple 无法验证是否包含恶意软件”**：先点“完成”（不要点“移到废纸篓”），打开“系统设置 → 隐私与安全性”，向下找到安全性提示，点“仍要打开”；在确认窗口点“打开”，按提示输入登录密码或使用 Touch ID
2. **提示“已损坏，无法打开”**：先从 [EasyRead 官方 Releases](https://github.com/Edwardxlai/easyread/releases/latest) 重新下载，并把应用拖进“应用程序”；文件也可能确实损坏或被改动，不能只凭这条提示判断原因。只有确认文件来自这个官方仓库、并信任该文件后，才在“终端”执行下面的命令，再重新打开 EasyRead；这条命令移除隔离属性，不会修复损坏的文件

   ```bash
   xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/EasyRead.app
   ```

3. **为什么会出现验证提示**：目前的 macOS 安装包用的是项目自己的自签名证书（为了应用内更新），不是 Apple 开发者证书，也没有经过公证，因此可能被系统拦截；代码完全开源，也可以[从源码运行](#run-from-source)

如果系统提示“将损坏你的电脑”，或明确检测出恶意软件并要求移到废纸篓，请停止安装，不要用上面的步骤绕过；按 [Apple 官方说明](https://support.apple.com/zh-cn/102445) 处理



**或者从源码运行**：需要 [Python 3.10+](https://www.python.org/downloads/)。

先从 [Releases](https://github.com/Edwardxlai/easyread/releases/latest) 下载最新版的 zip 解压（或者 `git clone` 本仓库）。

**Windows**：双击 `start.cmd`。第一次会自动装好环境（一分钟左右），之后双击直接打开。

**macOS / Linux**：在解压出来的目录里运行

```bash
./start.sh
```

这样启动的，浏览器里的 EasyRead 页面全部关掉后，后台服务过十几秒会自己退出；还有翻译在跑的话，等译完再退。

每次推送都会在 Windows、macOS、Linux 上自动装一遍、跑测试、启动一次（见上面的“测试”徽章）。

**或者用 pip**（数据放在 `~/EasyRead`）：

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/Edwardxlai/easyread
easyread
```

浏览器会打开 `http://127.0.0.1:8765`。服务只监听本机。

evidence.heading: 桌面版（Electron）
evidence.text:
桌面版复用同一套本地 Python 服务和 Web 界面，由 Electron 负责启动服务并显示窗口。开发环境需要 Node.js 22+、Python 3.10+ 和 PyInstaller：

```bash
npm install
python -m pip install pyinstaller
npm run dev
```

生成可分发安装包：

```bash
npm run dist
```

输出在 `dist/electron/`：Windows 为 NSIS 安装程序，macOS 为 DMG（另有一个给应用内更新用的 zip），Linux 为 AppImage。macOS 包由 `scripts/mac_sign.cjs` 用固定的自签名证书签名，证书从环境变量 `MAC_SIGN_P12`、`MAC_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD` 读（发版时来自仓库 Secrets）；本机没设时退回临时签名，这样打出的包不能应用内更新。推送 `v*` 标签后，GitHub Actions 会在三个系统上构建，并把这些安装包自动附加到 GitHub Release；源码 zip 仍会由 GitHub 保留。打包后的文献库和设置：Windows 存在安装目录下的 `data`（安装目录写不进去时退回 `~/EasyRead`），macOS、Linux 存在 `~/EasyRead`。

evidence.heading: 怎么用
evidence.text:
1. 右上角“设置” → “模型”：添加要用的模型，点卡片选“设为翻译”。翻译和“问 AI”用的模型都在这一页管理。
2. 把 PDF 拖进窗口；或者粘贴 arXiv 编号、arXiv / OpenReview 链接、PDF 直链（在文献库页面直接 `Ctrl+V` 也行）。长论文可以选“只译正文”，或者“指定页”只译第几页到第几页。导入时还能选这次用哪个模型；“导入后”选“读英文原文”就只排版、不翻译，想看中文了随时点“翻译成中文”。
   整篇翻译默认超过 60 页时会先确认，可以选择全部翻译、只译前 60 页或先不译；上限在“设置 → 模型”里修改，填 0 表示不询问
3. 翻译在后台一页页进行，已译的部分马上能读，没译到的页先显示原页。一次导入超过 5 篇时会先问要不要全部翻译（默认只导入）；想停下来，点列表顶部的“停止翻译”，已译的部分保留。
4. 读的时候点一下段落出现操作条；选中文字可以划线、写笔记、提问。快捷键在“设置 → 快捷键”里查看和修改；遇到问题点右上角的问号。
5. 论文默认译成中文，也可以在导入时选择繁体中文、英语、日语、韩语、西班牙语、法语、德语或意大利语，或在“设置 → 阅读 → 论文译成”里修改默认语言；界面语言独立设置，支持中文和英文，也可以跟随系统

evidence.text:
Three before / after comparisons. In each, the same brand is filmed twice: once without the skill (mid) and once with it (maxxed). The brands belong to their owners and are used only to show the difference (see [Ethics and credits](#ethics-and-credits)).

**Cluely, mid to maxxed. Same model, same brief: both films were generated with GPT-6.1.** Left: without the skill. Right: with it. You don't need the most expensive model to get motion that looks designed. The difference is the skill, not the price tag. [Watch the MP4](docs/media/cluely-comparison.mp4) (30 s with sound, 1920x600).

[](docs/media/cluely-comparison.mp4)

The left film is a slide deck: a brand label top-left, a "REAL-TIME ASSISTANCE" tag top-right, a held left headline in two colours, two cards, and a "02 / 05" counter. The right film is the product: the real assist overlay on a lit desktop, the ⌘ + ↵ shortcut as physical keys, then the overlay sitting on a live call.

evidence.heading: Why your AI video is mid
evidence.text:
Most AI motion graphics fail in the same recognisable way: everything is a slide. A slop autopsy of rejected AI films ranked 25 default patterns. These are the loudest tells, and what catches each one.

| The tell | What it looks like | Caught by |
|---|---|---|
| **Page chrome** | A brand name in a corner, a "02 / SPEAK" counter, a timecode, corner brackets, a progress bar | `lint.mjs` (G5), rules C1-C6, P1 |
| **Deck layouts** | A held left-aligned headline, a kicker above it, "headline left, device right" | `lint.mjs` (G5), rules C7, D1 |
| **Letter-typed headlines** | A headline typed out character by character with a caret | `lint.mjs` (G5), rule T1 |
| **Vibe-coded UI cards** | A rounded card with a status dot and "label . value", a "Good morning" header, zinc greys | `lint.mjs` (G5), rules V1-V5 |
| **Flat swatches** | A different flat colour per scene, or a small card floating on a void | Your eyes on the contact sheet ([`references/world.md`](references/world.md)) |
| **Dead frames** | Runs of frames where nothing on screen moves | `look.py` (G2): more than 3 flat frames in a row fails |
| **Fades everywhere** | Every element arrives by opacity and every beat ends in a dissolve | Measured instead: pros use 3,392 transform entries against 584 opacity fades, and cut on motion |

Several of these were prescribed by earlier wording of the skill itself ("alternate flat grounds", "a recurring carrier"), so the fix was an edit to the skill, not a scolding for the agent. The lint is a lead, not a verdict: it cannot see text inside an image or a canvas.

evidence.heading: The numbers a designer can use
evidence.text:
| Finding | Measured |
|---|---|
| The median move | **10 frames** (0.33 s). Entries 11-12 f, opacity 6 f, blur 7-8 f |
| Landing vs leaving | **Landing decelerates** (58% ease out); **leaving accelerates** (37% ease in, against 16% of landings) |
| Overshoot | **Under 9%** of moves (8.8%), and late: a slow lean past the mark, not a fast spring |
| Arrival | Decelerates **from oversize**. Logos crash in from about 3.5x. **Nothing grows from zero** |
| Fades | Elements arrive by moving: **3,392 transform entries against 584 opacity fades** |
| Cuts | Pros **cut on motion**, not on rest. 96% of moments use hard cuts, about 20 per moment |
| Dead frames | In the 3-7 s pro moments, motion on **about 99% of frames** (median still run: 1 frame). Whole films breathe more; the skill treats that as a question, not a target |
| The ending | A resolved end hold of 0.6-1.4 s; the ending usually gets smaller |

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
**Requirements:** Node 22+, Python 3, ffmpeg, Google Chrome. Optional: an ElevenLabs key for voice, sound effects and music (`ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`); the Codex CLI with image generation for surface plates.

**Claude Code**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Tejashmakwana/motionmaxxing ~/.claude/skills/motionmaxxing
bash ~/.claude/skills/motionmaxxing/install.sh        # checks the requirements; installs nothing system-wide
```

Or, from a checkout somewhere else: `./install.sh` links it into `~/.claude/skills/motionmaxxing`. Flags: `--dir PATH` for another skills folder, `--copy` to copy instead of symlink, `--force` to replace an existing install.

**Other agents.** The skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` at its root. Point any agent that reads `SKILL.md` at the folder (or copy it into that agent's skills directory) and give it shell access. The scripts only need `node`, `python3` and `ffmpeg` on the path.

**Check your machine**

```bash
bash scripts/providers.sh        # JSON: chrome, ffmpeg, key, codex, disk. Never installs anything.
```

evidence.heading: Status and known limits
evidence.text: Early release, so a glow-up in progress. It works end to end on the author's machine and has been used on a handful of real briefs, but it has not had a wide test. Known limits, said plainly in [docs/KNOWN-LIMITS.md](docs/KNOWN-LIMITS.md): the lint cannot see text inside a canvas or an image; G1 and G4 are judged by eye; ElevenLabs music does not always hit tempo or length; WebGL renders run at about 7-11 fps; the sound-effect normaliser can corrupt very short clips; `look.py` treats show and hide events as cuts; and `fetch_logo.mjs` can return a header ribbon instead of the mark.

**市面上的省钱工具都在回答「这一单怎么点最省」。**
**我们多回答一个问题：「你正在白扔多少钱？」**

[快速体验](#快速体验30-秒) · [真实例子](#一个真实例子) · [核心亮点](#我们做对了什么别人没做的) · [架构](#架构) · [设计原则](#设计原则)



---



基于麦当劳中国 MCP 打造的点餐成本助手，做两件事：

**短期 —— 这一单怎么点最省**
- 拉取**当前门店**的实时菜单与价格
- 拉取你**账户里当前门店可用**的优惠券
- 枚举「单品 / 套餐 / 券组合 / 加购凑单」的候选方案
- 用 MCP 的 `calculate-price` 逐方案**真实计价**（而不是猜）
- 输出最省钱的方案，以及**为什么不推荐更便宜但吃不饱的选项**

**长期 —— 你白扔了多少钱**
- **券的沉默成本**：你手里有几张券即将过期？那就是正在流失的钱
- **消费习惯画像**：近 N 个月花了多少、客单价是否偏高、哪些单品该改成套餐
- 数据来自 `order-list` 历史订单 + `query-my-coupons` 券存量



| 🍟 一次点餐平均省 | 💸 沉默成本发现 | 🧮 价格来源 | 🔑 使用门槛 |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **3 ~ 13 元** | **一次几十元** | MCP 真实计价 | 无需 Token 即可跑测试 |



---

evidence.heading: 一个真实例子
evidence.text:
同一个账号，同一个门店，两种问法：

**问「今天怎么点最省」** →

```
推荐方案
  组合：套餐：麦辣鸡腿汉堡三件套
  实付 33.5 元

超预算（仅供对照）
  · 单点：麦辣鸡腿汉堡 + 薯条 + 可乐 —— 实付 46.5 元，比推荐方案贵 13.0 元
```

> 同样吃到「汉堡 + 薯条 + 可乐」：套餐 33.5 元，单点 46.5 元，**差 13 元**
> —— 而单点那条已经超出 40 元预算，所以它是对照，不是备选。

**问「我最近在麦当劳花了多少」** →

```
【一】券的沉默成本
  你的券有风险：9 张将在 7 天内陆续过期（面值 21.1 元）；
  另有 7 张的券面价值无法从菜单推算，未计入面值。
  优先处理这几张：
    · 大脆鸡扒堡早餐两件套  价值未知  还剩 1 天
      仅 周四 05:00-10:29 可用 · 到店专用
    · 中薯条买一送一  省 14.5 元  还剩 2 天
      周一至周五 可用
    · 王牌小食拼  省 6.6 元  还剩 2 天
      周一至周五 可用

【二】消费习惯
  订单数：8 单（其中 2 笔 0 元）
  总支出：103.5 元
  客单价：17.25 元（按 6 笔有支出的订单计算）
  洞察：
    · 近 3 个月你在麦当劳共消费 103.5 元，其中 6 笔有实际支出，平均每单 17.25 元。
    · 另有 2 笔 0 元订单（多为券核销或积分兑换）—— 不计入客单价，但算作一次点单机会。
    · 还有 2 笔「部分退款」订单 —— 接口不返回退款金额，无法确认 realTotalAmount 是退款前还是退款后的口径，上面的支出可能略偏高。
```

> **本月最该做的事：先把 21.1 元的券用掉，这笔钱不用就是纯损失。**

第二个问题的价值不在这一次的数字大小，而在于**它是持续性的**：
第一个问题每单只影响一次；第二个问题每次都会告诉你又有什么在悄悄过期 ——
**而这是一次性工具永远给不出的答案。**

注意「王牌小食拼」那个 6.6 元：这张券的标题里没有数字，菜单里也没有对应商品，
**靠反查原价这条路根本走不通**。它的价值是把券的商品码传给 `calculate-price`
**实测**出来的 —— 而不是估一个「差不多」的数。

> 这两段输出与 `python demo.py` 的结果**逐字一致** —— 你可以自己跑一遍验证。

---

evidence.heading: 我们做对了什么别人没做的
evidence.text:
省钱类工具已经很多了，多到这次比赛报名里就有好几支在做同一件事。所以先说清楚**我们的不同点到底在哪**：

| 常见做法 | 我们的做法 | 差别 |
|---|---|---|
| 让模型估算价格 | 所有金额由 MCP `calculate-price` 回填 | 模型给不出真实价格，只能猜 |
| 只说「推荐买这个」 | 说清**省在哪**：哪张券、哪个套餐、加了什么 | 用户才能学会，而不是依赖工具 |
| 为用券鼓励凑单 | 主动检测**凑单陷阱**并劝退 | 凑单常常反而更贵 |
| 只看这一单 | 同时看**历史订单 + 券存量** | 一次性工具看不到长期结构 |
| 券是「可用资源」 | 券是**有保质期的钱** | 过期即损失，这是本项目独有的视角 |
| 积分是「攒够就换」 | 积分也是**有保质期的钱**，且**`status` 不等于可兑换** | 实测 24 个兑换品里 15 个已过兑换期，接口状态却仍标「上架」 |
| 「有券就建议用」 | 算**净价值**，该劝退就劝退 | 名义 ¥150 的券包，可实现的可能只有 ¥60 |
| 教你「怎么用券」 | 还提醒你**「还有券没领」** | 未领取的券是唯一一种零成本的省钱来源 |
| 用「平均客单价」一刀切 | 分清**消费口径 / 点单口径**、**全时段 / 分时段** | 口径错，后面所有券的判定都会跟着偏 |
| 券 = 「门店里能用的」 | 券分两种口径：**门店可用的** vs **卡包里持有的** | 实测差 2 张 vs 9 张 —— 拿门店券算沉默成本，会把 7 张即将过期的早餐券整个漏掉 |
| 拿活动文案里的价格当依据 | 只取活动的**日期与标题**，文案价格一概不用 | 营销文案无法核实，拿它算钱等于编 |
| —— | **券的沉默成本** | 别处见不到这个指标 |



> **差异化内核：别处都在帮用户花钱，我们在帮用户止损。**
> 下单前省的那几块钱是「收益」，快过期的券是「损失」——
> 人对损失的敏感度是对收益的两倍，而这个数字从来没人给他算过。

evidence.heading: 关键实现：怎么知道一张券真值多少钱
evidence.text:
「券的沉默成本」要成立，前提是得知道**每张券真实值多少钱**。而 MCP 返回的券通常只有名字，没有面值：

```
「中薯条买一送一」  →  值多少钱？
「9.9元中杯冰美式」 →  值多少钱？
「王牌小食拼」      →  值多少钱？
```

**首选：直接问收银台。** 把券自带的商品码连同 `couponId` 传给 `calculate-price`，
返回的 `discount` 就是这张券的**精确价值**，`price` 就是用券实付：

| 券 | 实测结果 |
|---|---:|
| 中薯条买一送一 | 14.5 元 |
| 王牌小食拼 | **6.6 元** |

**兜底：从菜单反查原价**（拿不到券的商品码时用）：

| 券形态 | 价值推算 | 本例结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 满减券 `满50减12` | 直接取减免额 | 12.0 元 |
| 买一送一 `中薯条买一送一` | 取该商品菜单单价 | 14.5 元 |
| 免费券 `免费脆薯饼` | 取该商品菜单单价（券面即免费） | 脆薯饼单价 |
| 固定价券 `9.9元中杯冰美式` | 菜单原价 − 固定价 | 23.0 − 9.9 = 13.1 元 |

**为什么首选实测**：「王牌小食拼」标题里没有数字、菜单里也没有对应商品 ——
反查只能返回 0（价值未知），而它实际值 6.6 元。
反查不只是可能低估，**还会把真实存在的价值报成 0**。

**两条路都走不通时，一律取 0 并在报告中标注「价值未知」**，
绝不估一个「看起来合理」的数。宁可少报，不可编造。

evidence.heading: 4. 开始使用
evidence.text:
直接对话即可，例如：

```
我在麦当劳点外卖，门店选好之后帮我算一下：
我手里有券，想吃一个汉堡 + 一份薯条 + 一杯饮料，预算 40 元，
怎么点最省钱？给我两个方案对比。
```

---

evidence.heading: 使用示例
evidence.text:
**示例一：预算内吃饱**

> **你**：预算 35 元，想吃鸡类主食 + 一个配餐，帮我选。
>
> **助手**：已查询当前门店菜单与你名下可用券，为你计价了 3 个候选方案：
>
> | 方案 | 组合 | 实付 | 预算 35 元 |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | ✅ 推荐 | 麦辣鸡腿汉堡三件套（汉堡 + 薯条 + 可乐） | **33.5** | 预算内 |
> | 超预算 | 单点：麦辣鸡腿汉堡 + 薯条 | 37.0 | 超 2 元 |
> | 超预算 | 单点：麦辣鸡腿汉堡 + 薯条 + 可乐 | 46.5 | 超 11.5 元 |
>
> 只推荐三件套：**33.5 元拿到三样**，比只买两样的单点组合（37 元，已超预算）还便宜 3.5 元，
> 比同内容的单点组合省 13 元。这是套餐结构本身带来的价差，不必再叠加优惠券。

**示例二：凑单陷阱提醒**

> **你**：我有一张「满 50 减 12」的券，是不是该凑单？
>
> **助手**：不建议。你当前想买的商品合计 46.5 元，为触发门槛需要再加 3.5 元商品，
> 实付变为 46.5 + 3.5 - 12 = 38 元；而直接买三件套只要 33.5 元。
> 也就是说，**凑单用券后反而比直接买套餐贵 4.5 元**。
> 除非你本来就想吃那个凑单品，否则不划算。

> 这是一个**演示场景**（该账户当前没有满减券），用于说明凑单陷阱的判定逻辑。
> 逻辑本身由 [`src/test_saver.py`](./src/test_saver.py) 覆盖。

> 以上金额均来自 MCP `calculate-price` 的真实返回，非估算值。

---

github_projects.description_zh: 将一幅插图变成带编码智能体和本地编辑器的 2D 动态网格头像。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Turn one illustration into an animated 2D mesh avatar with a coding agent and a local editor

evidence.heading: Mesh Avatar Studio
evidence.text:
[日本語](README.ja.md)

Turn a single illustration into an animated 2D mesh avatar: it blinks, talks, turns its head,
breathes and sways its hair. A coding agent prepares the avatar from your image; you fine-tune
it in a local editor with a live preview.

See it move on the [landing page](https://shinshin86.github.io/mesh-avatar-studio/).
To move it with your own face and voice without installing anything, open the
[Player](https://shinshin86.github.io/mesh-avatar-studio/play/) in Chrome or Edge.

evidence.heading: Try the sample
evidence.text:
Requires Node.js 22.17+ and Git.

```sh
npx create-mesh-avatar-studio
cd mesh-avatar-studio
npm run dev
```

The first command downloads the repository, installs its packages and checks the tools
Studio needs. If you cloned the repository yourself, run `npm install`, then
`npm run doctor` for the same check. Only Node.js is needed for the editor and the Live
page. uv and Python rebuild layers, and Playwright Chromium renders the motion review when
an agent creates an avatar; the check warns about each one that is missing.

Open the URL printed in the terminal (for example `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`). The editor opens
the bundled sample, Miko in a qipao. Pick a part on the left, drag its dots on the image and
watch the preview on the right. The sample is read-only; when you change it, choose
**Copy and keep editing** to continue in your own copy.

evidence.heading: Using Windows
evidence.text:
Use `git clone` to download the repository when possible. If you use a ZIP, open its
Properties in File Explorer and select **Unblock**, if shown, before extracting it.

Create `projects/` yourself under your Windows account before asking an agent to work in it
(`npx create-mesh-avatar-studio` creates it for you).
Folders created by another account or an agent running in a sandbox can have permissions
that prevent the editor from reading them. If a project cannot be read, use the folder's
**Properties → Security** settings to grant your account access to the whole project,
including its files and subfolders through permission inheritance.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Making an avatar from your own illustration takes four steps. Steps 1 and 4 are done by a
coding agent (Claude Code or Codex) working in this repository; steps 2 and 3 happen in the
editor.

evidence.heading: 1. Ask your agent to create the avatar
evidence.text:
Open Claude Code or Codex in this repository folder and give it your illustration:

> Create an avatar from this image following docs/agent-guide.md: `/path/to/your-image.png`

The agent follows [the agent guide](docs/agent-guide.md): it checks how accurately it reads
coordinates, places the rig on zoomed grids, cuts the image into layers and reviews the
avatar in fixed poses. The project is saved in `projects/<name>/`, which is never committed.
Best results come from a front-facing, head-and-shoulders PNG with a transparent background.
When no project is open, the editor shows this request ready to copy.



Recommended setups:

| Agent | Model |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | Claude Opus 5.5 |
| Codex | GPT-6.1 Sol |

evidence.heading: 2. Open the project and check it
evidence.text:
Start the editor (`npm run dev`), choose **Open project** and pick your project from the list.
In the preview, use **Pose test** to turn and tilt the head and close the eyes, and
**Lip sync** to check the vowel mouth shapes.

evidence.heading: Without installing anything
evidence.text:
The [Player](https://shinshin86.github.io/mesh-avatar-studio/play/) runs face tracking,
microphone lip sync, expressions and lighting entirely in the browser. Open the sample or
your own `.mavatar` file; nothing is uploaded. It has no stream URL: choose **Open avatar
window** (Chrome or Edge) and add that window to OBS with **Window Capture** on a green
background and a Chroma Key filter. Transparency, the OBS Browser Source and switching
expressions from other apps need Studio's Live page.

github_projects.name: git-ai
github_projects.description: Git designed for AI agents.
github_projects.description_zh: 为 AI 智能体设计的 Git。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Git designed for AI agents.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Git designed for AI agents.


Anthropic built **Scion**, a faster version control system for coding agents,
and described it in
[Redesigning source control](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control):
a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land
code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to
the public.

So I built **gitai**: an open-source version of that design that anyone can
run, and that the community can improve and maintain together.

MIT licensed. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every
AI feature works with any provider, or none.

gitai is an independent implementation of the publicly described design. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.

---

evidence.heading: Why
evidence.text:
Classic Git hosting was built for humans who clone a repository, work for hours
and push once. Coding agents work differently: thousands of short-lived tasks,
each touching a few files, each wanting to land in seconds, all on the same
branches. Full clones, merge queues and client-side history walks become the
bottleneck.

Scion's answer is to move the work to the server: clients stay online and fetch
only what they need, history questions are answered (and cached) by the server,
changes land through a compare-and-swap instead of a queue, every update is an
entry in a changeset log, and the repository state lives in a consistent
database plus object storage so servers scale out. gitai implements these
ideas, with normal Git repositories underneath.

evidence.heading: The Scion ideas, implemented
evidence.text:
| Scion idea | In gitai |
|---|---|
| **Always-online clients** that fetch exactly what they need | `ObjectService` serves single objects and sparse trees; `graft clone` and `graft sparse` materialize only the paths you ask for. |
| **Source control as an API**: history runs on the server | Blame, path history, ancestry and code search run server-side and are memoized as derived data, computed once per commit. |
| **Landing without a merge queue** | `UserLand` rebases a change onto the current tip and lands it with a compare-and-swap; concurrent lands on one branch are batched into a single reference update. |
| **Automatic conflict resolution** | A conflicting land is resolved by a resolver you choose (any LLM provider, a deterministic tool, or none) through a versioned, vendor-neutral protocol. A model's resolution is only a proposal: it lands by itself only if the `verify.command` you configure passes on the exact tree that would land, and otherwise the agent gets the conflict package with the proposal. The deterministic rules you configure need no such condition of their own, and are verified on the exact tree as well when you turn the verification on (`verify.enabled`). |
| **Changeset log** | Every accepted reference update is recorded with its operation and actor in a dense, ordered log that clients list or watch live. |
| **Storage core: a database and object storage, stateless servers** | Each change is a changeset in a write-ahead log in SQLite or PostgreSQL, with a compare-and-swap per reference; packs live in object storage (file, S3, GCS, Azure). Server nodes are caches that any node can rebuild, so you add nodes to scale. |
| **Test after landing, revert the culprit** | `graft-verify` tests the tip, bisects a failure and reverts the change that broke it. |

evidence.heading: Architecture
evidence.text:
```
        agents, CI jobs, sparse workspaces          graft CLI / Go SDK
                            |
                            v   gRPC
        +-------------------------------------------------+
        |  graft-cache (optional daemon and cache tiers)  |
        +------------------------+------------------------+
                                 v
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
   |  gitai server (any number of nodes)                           |
   |  land - objects - changesets - derived data - search - review |
   |  write path: changeset + compare-and-swap per reference       |
   +-----------+--------------------------------+------------------+
               |                                |
               v                                v
   +-----------------------+       +-----------------------------+
   |  SQLite / PostgreSQL  |       |  object storage             |
   |  changeset WAL, refs, |       |  content-addressed packs    |
   |  changelog, reviews   |       |  (file, S3, GCS, Azure)     |
   +-----------------------+       +-----------------------------+
               \                              /
                local Git repositories = caches any node can rebuild
```

Details: [ARCHITECTURE.md](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md).

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
Requirements: Linux or macOS, Go 1.26, a C toolchain, Meson and Ninja (the
build compiles a bundled Git).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/feder-cr/git-ai.git
cd git-ai
make build                         # server, CLI and tools into _build/bin
examples/graft/quickstart.sh       # a server, a cache daemon, two agents and a land, in a temporary directory
./_build/bin/graft                 # the CLI and its commands
```

To run your own server, adapt [`examples/graft/config.toml`](examples/graft/config.toml)
and start it with `_build/bin/gitaly serve config.toml`. To put the repository
state in a database and object storage, add a `[graft.storage]` section: start in
`shadow` mode, import your repositories, then switch to `authoritative`
([STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md)).

Inside the code the extensions are called **Graft**: the `[graft]`
configuration section, the `graft` CLI, `internal/graft` and `doc/graft`.

evidence.heading: Documentation
evidence.text:
- [Quickstart](doc/graft/QUICKSTART.md) and [configuration reference](doc/graft/CONFIGURATION.md)
- [Architecture](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and the [storage core](doc/graft/STORAGE.md)
- [Landing and batching](doc/graft/LAND-BATCHING.md), [conflict resolution](doc/graft/RESOLVE.md), [derived data](doc/graft/DERIVED.md)
- [Review](doc/graft/REVIEW.md), [search](doc/graft/SEARCH.md), [verification](doc/graft/VERIFY.md), [superfans](doc/graft/SUPERFAN.md) and [Slack chat](doc/graft/SUPERFAN-CHAT.md)
- [Agent security](doc/graft/AGENT-SECURITY.md), [benchmarks](doc/graft/BENCH.md), [fuzzing](doc/graft/FUZZING.md)
- [Limitations and roadmap](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md)
- Design documents of each phase: [PLAN.md](doc/graft/PLAN.md) to [PLAN6.md](doc/graft/PLAN6.md), and [PLAN8.md](doc/graft/PLAN8.md) (faster landing)

evidence.heading: Benchmark
evidence.text:
50 agents land 5 changes each on one branch; 20% of the changes conflict on
purpose. "Classic" is the same server with batching off: every agent rebases
and retries its own compare-and-swap, up to 20 attempts. Measured with
[`acceptance-phase4.sh`](examples/graft/demo/acceptance-phase4.sh) on one
16-core machine, two runs:

| 50 agents, 250 changes, no conflict resolver | classic | gitai |
|---|---|---|
| changes landed | 100-106 | 200 |
| attempts per landed change | 26.5-28.7 | 1.0 |
| lands per minute | 264-385 | 1,487-1,944 |
| p99 latency | 4.4-5.2 s | 1.9-2.7 s |

The 50 changes gitai does not land are the planned conflicts, returned to their
agents: these runs use no conflict resolver. With the deterministic resolver of
[`resolve.toml`](examples/graft/demo/resolve.toml) every conflict is resolved
and all 250 changes land (1,245-1,806 lands per minute, p99 2.0-3.4 s). Details and more sizes in [BENCH.md](doc/graft/BENCH.md).

kind_reason.text: 为并行智能体开发提供版本控制服务、CLI 与 SDK。

summary.text: gitai 借鉴作者对 Scion 的理解，实现面向大量并行编程智能体的服务端版本控制：按需取文件、服务端查询历史和集中落地变更。

value.text: 针对短任务只修改少量文件的工作方式，减少完整克隆和反复争抢分支的成本。

mechanism.text: ObjectService 提供单对象及稀疏树，历史与搜索在服务端缓存，UserLand 将变更变基到当前分支顶端后落地。

inspiration.text: 可尝试让版本控制接口匹配智能体的小任务颗粒度，优先请求所需路径并缓存派生查询。

limitations.text: 是作者实现的开源设计版本，与 Anthropic 内部 Scion 并非同一产品；基准来自作者指定的冲突场景和单机测试。

how_to.text: 按要求安装 Go 与构建工具，运行 make build，再执行 examples/graft/quickstart.sh 查看双智能体演示。

evidence.heading: One MCP for reverse engineering across binaries, applications, and runtime behavior.
evidence.text: **See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level.** [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rea-agents) [](https://github.com/morluto/rea/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [](docs/mcp-contracts.md#generated-catalog) [](https://nodejs.org/) [](https://skills.sh/morluto/rea/reverse-engineer-anything) [](LICENSE) [](https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM) **[Website](https://rea.tools/) · [Guides](https://rea.tools/guides/) · [Showcases](https://rea.tools/showcase/)** [Quick start](#quick-start) · [How REA works](#how-rea-works) · [What you can analyze](#what-you-can-analyze) · [Showcases](#showcases) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Documentation](#documentation) npx rea-agents setup Join the Reverse Engineering Community Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell --- See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper or Ghidra installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs neither engine. > **[Visit the REA website](https://rea.tools/)** for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies.

evidence.heading: Set up your agent
evidence.text:
With Node.js and npm installed, run:

```bash
npx rea-agents setup
```

Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds
REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing
configuration. Restart your agent afterward.

Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and
[other agents](docs/installation.md#supported-agents). See
[installation and setup](docs/installation.md) for provider configuration and
manual MCP registration.

evidence.heading: Ask your agent
evidence.text:
```text
Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a
similar feature for my project.
```

Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand.

evidence.heading: Use the terminal
evidence.text:
Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR:

```bash
npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json
```

The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence.
Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows.

To install the `rea` command for regular use:

```bash
npm install --global rea-agents
rea --help
```

For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the
[CLI and Evidence guide](docs/cli.md) for native commands, provider selection,
snapshots and scripting.

evidence.heading: Update REA
evidence.text:
REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your
installation up to date.

For an npm-installed CLI:

```bash
rea update
```

To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed
by the update.

If you use `npx`, update your agent setup with:

```bash
npx rea-agents@latest setup
```

Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands,
use `npx rea-agents@latest` followed by the command.

evidence.heading: How REA works
evidence.text:
Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code.
REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up
questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation.
CLI commands use the same workflows.



[Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg).

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Scout: the open-source browser agent, by Outcrawl. Mirrored automatically from Outcrawl's own repository.

evidence.heading: README
Tell it the task. It opens a browser and gets it done.
evidence.text:
Scout is an open-source agent that uses a real browser to finish a task for you. Describe what you need in plain words. Scout reads the page, clicks, types and scrolls until the job is done, then hands back the answer. If it cannot finish, it tells you what is missing and returns what it found.

**Scout runs best on Outcrawl's cloud.** One line gives it a browser that sites treat like anyone at home, with captcha solving and a replay of every run. It also runs on your own machine.



  
  
  


A recorded run on Outcrawl's cloud, 13 October 2026, shown at 6x speed with nothing cut.

evidence.heading: Start in three steps
What you can ask it to do
evidence.text:
Tasks you would do in a browser yourself, written the way you would ask a colleague. Each of these is a working example you can run:

- **Research.** "Go to Hacker News and report the three stories with the most comments: title, link and comment count." [`research.ts`](packages/scout/examples/research.ts)
- **Fill in a form.** "Order a pizza on this form, then tell me exactly what the shop received." [`form-fill.ts`](packages/scout/examples/form-fill.ts)
- **Compare.** "Find these two books and compare their price and stock, then tell me which is cheaper." [`compare.ts`](packages/scout/examples/compare.ts)
- **Sign in.** "Sign in with these details and read the welcome message." [`login.ts`](packages/scout/examples/login.ts)
- **On the cloud.** The research task on Outcrawl's cloud, with a link to watch the replay. [`outcrawl.ts`](packages/scout/examples/outcrawl.ts)

Want the answer in a fixed shape, such as a list of names and prices? Pass a JSON Schema with the task and the answer comes back in exactly that shape.

evidence.heading: Bring your own models
evidence.text:
Scout has no built-in model and no default. You choose a model for each job, on any service that speaks the chat completions API: a hosted provider, a gateway, or a server on your own machine. Each job can use a different model and a different key.

| Job | Needed | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hands` | Yes | Reads the page and takes each step: click, type, scroll, read. It runs on every step, so a fast model pays off here. |
| `brain` | No | Plans the run and decides each step. Helps long tasks that cross many pages. |
| `eyes` | No | Looks at a screenshot when the page has to be seen. Needs a model that accepts images. |
| `extract` | No | Reads a page into your answer or your schema. Without it, `hands` does this. |

```ts
models: {
  hands: { model: 'your-fast-model', baseURL: urlA, apiKey: keyA },
  brain: { model: 'your-strong-model', baseURL: urlB, apiKey: keyB },
  eyes: { model: 'your-vision-model', baseURL: urlA, apiKey: keyA },
  extract: { model: 'your-local-model', baseURL: localUrl, apiKey: '' },
}
```

If a service refuses Scout's request for a structured reply, the run's error says which job it was and what to change: set `structuredOutput` on that job to `'json_object'` or `'strict'`.

evidence.heading: The best way to run it: Outcrawl's cloud
evidence.text:
Many sites stop a browser that runs from a data center or behaves like a script, and a task that stops halfway is no answer at all. On Outcrawl's cloud, Scout gets a browser built to get through:

- **Residential connections.** Traffic leaves through ordinary home connections, so sites load the way they do for anyone at home.
- **Captcha solving.** Challenges are answered inside the browser, and the run carries on.
- **Natural input.** The browser plans every pointer move, scroll and keystroke itself, so Scout sends it plain actions.
- **Recordings.** Runs are recorded by default, and `result.replayUrl` opens a step-by-step replay.
- **Nothing to install.** No browser to download, update or keep running on your machine.

**Measured:** runs on Outcrawl's cloud reached **92.5%** of pages on Browser Use's 80-site benchmark, scored with their own code; the next best reached 81.4%. Three full runs, 7 October 2026. [Method and every run](https://outcrawl.ai/resources/benchmarks).

A cloud run is billed as an ordinary Outcrawl browser session, and your model calls still go to your own services. Every account gets 1,000 free credits a month, no card needed. [Get a key at outcrawl.ai](https://outcrawl.ai).
