github_projects.description: A durable, multiplayer, mobile-first web app for Pi agents, built on Pi Durable
github_projects.description_zh: 基于 Pi Durable 构建的耐用、多用户、移动优先的 Pi 智能体 Web 应用

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: A durable, multiplayer, mobile-first web app for Pi agents, built on Pi Durable

evidence.heading: Pi Pocket
evidence.text:
**Your Pi coding agent, in your pocket.**

A durable, multiplayer, mobile-first web app for Pi agents, built on [Pi Durable](https://earendil.com/posts/pi-durable/).
Runs on your own machine or directly on your phone. No cloud VM.

[](https://github.com/TannerMidd/pi-pocket/releases)
[](https://nodejs.org)
[](LICENSE)

[Website](https://tannermidd.github.io/pi-pocket/) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Feature tour](docs/features.md) · [Docs](https://tannermidd.github.io/pi-pocket/docs/)

evidence.heading: Highlights
evidence.text:
- **Durable.** Every model call, tool call, and subagent is stored as it happens. Restart the server mid-run, and the work continues.
- **Multiplayer.** Share a live session with presence, a side chat Pi does not see, invites, and roles.
- **Made for phones.** Push notifications, dictation, sharing into Pi from other apps, and a home-screen app.
- **PiP.** An assistant that starts, follows, and reports on your other sessions, and watches GitHub for you.
- **Your models.** Pi's own providers, sign-ins, skills, and prompt templates, with the model chosen per session.
- **Live-editable.** No build step. Pi can change Pi Pocket while it runs, and you can add your own extensions.

The [feature tour](docs/features.md) covers everything else, from plan mode and peek tiles to the built-in browser.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
Requires Node.js 22.19 or newer. Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, and Android (Termux); Linux is the most tested. Sign in to a provider with Pi first (`pi`, then `/login`), or later from the app's Providers sheet.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/TannerMidd/pi-pocket.git
cd pi-pocket
npm install
npm start
```

The launcher asks how your devices should connect, then prints a sign-in link and a QR code. The link is the owner's key: keep it private. `--rotate-token` replaces it and signs out every device that used it.

While it runs: **q** quit · **r** restart server · **a** change access · **o** open in browser · **s** show QR code.

**Updating:** stop the server, back up `~/.pi-pocket`, pull, run `npm install`, and start again. Read the [release notes](https://github.com/TannerMidd/pi-pocket/releases) first: 0.21.0 upgrades the database one way, so going back needs the backup.

evidence.heading: Other ways to run it
evidence.text:
- **Docker or Podman:** `docker compose up -d --build`. See [docs/docker.md](docs/docker.md).
- **Nix:** `nix run github:TannerMidd/pi-pocket`, or the NixOS module `services.pi-pocket.enable = true;` ([nix/module.nix](nix/module.nix)).
- **Android (Termux):**

    ```bash
    pkg update && pkg upgrade && pkg install nodejs git
    npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
    pi    # /login, then quit
    git clone https://github.com/TannerMidd/pi-pocket.git
    cd pi-pocket && npm install --ignore-scripts && termux-wake-lock && npm start
    ```

    Lancet Guard may not load on Android. If it is on but fails, start with `PI_POCKET_GUARD=off`.

evidence.heading: Remote access
evidence.text:
Choose a mode in the launcher, or pass `--access`:

| Mode         | Who can connect      | Notes                                                    |
| ------------ | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `local`      | This machine         | `127.0.0.1`; bring your own tunnel to port 8787          |
| `lan`        | Your local network   | Plain http                                               |
| `cloudflare` | Anyone with the link | Free https quick tunnel, no account; needs `cloudflared` |
| `tailscale`  | Your tailnet         | Tailscale address only                                   |

Other options: `--port` (8787), `--cwd`, `--data` (`~/.pi-pocket`), `--host`, and `-y` to reuse the last access choice. `npm start -- --help` lists them all. `PI_POCKET_BROWSER` and `PI_POCKET_BROWSER_ARGS` pick the built-in browser and its flags when Chromium or Chrome is not found by itself.

> [!WARNING]
> Anyone who can steer a session can make Pi run commands on this machine, as you. That reaches your files, Pi Pocket's own settings and tokens, and its code. Invite only people you would trust at your keyboard. View-only users cannot make Pi act. [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says what is protected and what is not.

evidence.heading: Documentation
evidence.text:
- [Feature tour](docs/features.md): every feature, in full.
- [Docs site](https://tannermidd.github.io/pi-pocket/docs/): customizing Pi without code, and writing extensions.
- [Engineering](https://tannermidd.github.io/pi-pocket/engineering.html) and [code map](docs/map.md): how Pi Pocket is built.

evidence.heading: Limitations
evidence.text:
- Pi Durable is experimental, and its API can change between releases. Versions are pinned in `package.json`.
- Only one server process can use the database at a time.
- Pi's own extensions are not supported. Pi Pocket runs its own, on Pi Durable.
- A git worktree keeps a session's files apart; it is not a sandbox.
- The built-in browser needs Chromium, Chrome, Brave, or Edge on the server. It is tested on Linux and macOS.

The [full list](docs/features.md#limitations) has the details.

**AI 跨境电商运营智能体工具箱** · *Turn cross-border ecommerce SOPs into reusable AI Agent workflows.*

[](./LICENSE)
[](./CHANGELOG.md)
[](#-agent-全景)

---

evidence.heading: 这是什么
evidence.text:
把**跨境运营 SOP 里沉淀的经验**，翻译成**可复制的 AI Agent 工作流**：一个标准 Prompt + 一份输入模板 + 一个真实案例，任何人都能拿去直接跑出可发布的商品素材。

不是软件，不是 SaaS，只做四件事：

| 交付物 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 📘 运营方法论 | SOP 章节 → Agent 模块的完整拆解表 |
| 🧠 AI Prompt | 角色 / 任务 / 输入契约 / 输出契约 / 自检 |
| 🔁 工作流程 | 什么顺序跑、什么条件进入下一步、什么条件回流重改 |
| 📄 模板 + 案例 | 标准输入格式 + 真实产品的完整跑通记录（含复测数据） |

**为什么做这个**：跨境运营的难点不是"不知道要做什么"，而是"知道但做不出稳定下限的产出"。同一个类目，老手写标题一次到位，新人写十遍还是堆词。这套工具箱的目标是把老手的**判断规则**结构化，让 AI 的产出稳定在老手水平线上。

---

evidence.heading: 📎 原始资料来源
evidence.text:
本仓库的方法论拆解自一份 38 页的内部运营手册，原文已随仓库提供：

📄 **[《Shopee 巴西站运营 SOP 总框架》（PDF · 38 页 · 29.7 MB）](./docs/电商运营SOP总框架.pdf)**

SOP 章节与 Agent 模块的逐条对应关系见 [`docs/00_Architecture_SOP_to_Agent.md`](./docs/00_Architecture_SOP_to_Agent.md)。

> ⚠️ **请注意**：这份 PDF 是**未经删改的原始内部手册**，其中包含平台明确禁止的做法（如刷单、诱导评价、虚假举报、参数虚标等）。
>
> **本仓库的 7 个 Agent 模块均未实现这些做法**：已识别项及其合规替代方案见 [`docs/03_Compliance_Guard.md`](./docs/03_Compliance_Guard.md)，未实现项逐条登记见 [`docs/05_SOP_Gap_Register.md`](./docs/05_SOP_Gap_Register.md)。
>
> 换句话说 —— **这份 PDF 是「原料」，不是「产品」。** 本仓库的产出物只包含合规路径。

---

evidence.heading: 🗂 Agent 全景
evidence.text:
7 个模块，**全部已完成**。

| # | Agent | 中文 | 一句话职责 | 版本 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **01** | [Market Research Agent](./Agents/01_Market_Research_Agent/) | 市场分析 | 前置判断 / 容量 / 集中度 / 价格带（波谷检测）/ 配置组合 · **带计算脚本** | ✅ v0.4 |
| **02** | [Product Strategy Agent](./Agents/02_Product_Strategy_Agent/) | 产品策略 | 定位 / 配置 / 主推卖点收敛 / 定价模型 / SKU 四角色 · **净利率/盈亏价/券余量矩阵** · Skill 化 | ✅ v0.4 |
| 03 | [Listing Creative Agent](./Agents/03_Listing_Creative_Agent/) | 商品内容生成 | 关键词分类 → 标题 → 详情页 → 卖点/参数 · **字符实测/参数溯源校验** · Skill 化 | ✅ v0.4 |
| 04 | [Product Image Agent](./Agents/04_Product_Image_Agent/) | 主图与详情图 | 9 图规划 → 出图 Prompt → **像素级合规校验** · Skill 化 | ✅ v0.4 |
| 05 | [Product Video Agent](./Agents/05_Product_Video_Agent/) | 短视频生成 | 脚本 → 分镜 → AI 视频 Prompt → 配音字幕 | ✅ v0.4 |
| 06 | [Advertising Optimization Agent](./Agents/06_Advertising_Optimization_Agent/) | 广告优化 | 四类漏斗诊断 + 盈亏线核算 + **P0/P1/P2 分级动作** · Skill 化 | ✅ v0.4 |
| 07 | [Review Analysis Agent](./Agents/07_Review_Analysis_Agent/) | 评论分析 | 八类归因 + 误解型识别 → 详情页修补建议 | ✅ v0.4 |

> **这七个模块构成一条完整链路，而且是闭环的**：
>
> ```text
> 01 市场分析 ──► 02 产品策略 ──► 03/04/05 素材产出 ──► 上架
> （做什么）      （做成什么样）    （怎么表达）
>                                                      │
>                          ┌───────────────────────────┘
>                          ▼
>              06 广告诊断 ─┐
>              07 评论诊断 ─┴──► 回流 03/04 修正 ──► 复测 ──► 达标放量 / 未达标回诊断
> ```
>
> **为什么按这个顺序编号**：`01-02` 分析簇（前置链路）→ `03-04-05` 创意簇（素材产出）→ `06-07` 运营簇（数据回流）。
>
> ✅ 编号方案已确认。原始规划为 `03` Listing / `04` Advertising / `05` Review / `06` Video（且无 Market Research 与 Product Strategy 的独立编号），本仓库按工作簇重排，变更记录见 [CHANGELOG](./CHANGELOG.md)。

---

evidence.heading: 🚀 快速开始
evidence.text:
不需要 API key，不需要装环境。**三个文件就能跑。**

```text
Step 1  复制 Agents/<模块>/templates/ 下的输入模板
Step 2  填上你的产品信息（10 分钟）
Step 3  把「系统 Prompt」+「任务 Prompt」+「填好的模板」丢给任意 LLM
Step 4  用 docs/04_Result_Checklist.md 逐条自检，通过即发布
```

**第一次跑，建议按这个顺序**（以 Patinete Elétrico 为例，见 [`Examples/`](./Examples/)）：

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["类目导出数据"] --> B["01 市场分析+ 脚本算指标"]
    B -->|价格带/配置/机会点| C["02 产品策略定价+SKU"]
    C -->|主卖点+盈亏线| D["03 ListingCreative"]
    D -->|标题/卖点/参数| E["04 ProductImage"]
    D -->|核心卖点| F["05 ProductVideo"]
    E --> G["上架"]
    F --> G
    G -->|广告数据| H["06 广告漏斗诊断"]
    G -->|评论数据| I["07 评论八类归因"]
    H -.->|回改·iterate| D
    H -.->|换主图| E
    I -.->|补注意事项段| D
    I -.->|补包装清单图| E
```

三个关键点：

1. **01 带脚本**。指标（集中度、价格带、配置交叉表）由 `scripts/` 计算，**Agent 只负责解读**——能算的别让模型猜。
2. **02 决定卖点，03/04/05 才能开工**。主卖点必须收敛成**唯一一句**，否则主图打两行字、视频开头讲两件事，两个都记不住。
3. **06 和 07 会把结论回流到 03/04**。这一步是整套工具箱和"一次性生成工具"的分界线——产出的 Listing 会随着真实数据变准。见 [`Examples/03_Closed_Loop/`](./Examples/03_Closed_Loop/)。

evidence.heading: PandaCode
evidence.text:
A small, native desktop workspace for coding agents. PandaCode runs the coding
CLIs you already use — **Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code, OpenCode, GLM Coding
Plan and Xiaomi MiMo** (through Claude Code), **GitHub Copilot CLI, Antigravity,
xAI's Grok Build, DeepSeek, Command Code, Cline and Kilo Code** (through ACP), **Pi** and its
fork **omp** (through Pi's RPC mode), and Meta's **Muse Code** (through its MSP
protocol) — side by side, with your projects, Git, a
terminal and a browser in one window.

PandaCode is free and open source under the [PandaCode License](LICENSE), the MIT
License with one addition: forks that are used commercially or released publicly
must say "This is a fork of PandaCode" and link to this repository. There is no
account, no license key and no telemetry.

Built with Tauri 2, Rust, SQLite and plain TypeScript. It uses the operating
system's webview: no bundled Chromium, resident Node server, React runtime or
embedded editor engine.


  Download:
  macOS (Apple silicon) ·
  macOS (Intel) ·
  Windows x64 ·
  Windows arm64 ·
  Linux x64 ·
  Linux arm64 ·
  All releases

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Every harness in one place.** Pick the harness, model and reasoning effort
  per task; switch between them from the composer. See [providers](docs/providers.md).
- **Tasks and a task board.** Parallel tasks across projects, a Pending → In
  progress → Review → Completed [board](docs/task-board.md), message queueing
  and steering while an agent runs.
- **Agent teams.** An [architect and up to three workers](docs/architect-workers.md),
  mixing harnesses and models, or named team profiles. Each spawned worker is one
  line in the turn that started it; click it to open the worker.
- **Bots.** Put an agent behind Telegram, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp or a local web
  chat; each conversation is an ordinary task. The sidebar's **Bots** view lists
  every bot with its latest message. See [bots](docs/bots.md).
- **Local VMs and cloud sandboxes.** Headless macOS/Linux VMs on Apple silicon
  (Tart), and Daytona, Cloudflare and AWS sandboxes that agents can drive.
- **Cloud agents.** Pick a cloud provider in a New task's **Run on** menu and the
  agent runs on a machine in your own account (Daytona, Cloudflare, AWS, Google Cloud,
  E2B, Modal, Vercel Sandbox, CodeSandbox, Runloop, Blaxel, Tensorlake, Freestyle,
  boat). PandaCode installs the harness there, copies your login, and keeps the run
  going while your laptop sleeps; changes come back to a local worktree. See
  [cloud agents](docs/cloud-agents.md).
- **Simulators.** iOS Simulator and Android emulator tools for agents.
- **Deploys.** Start a deploy task for Vercel, Cloudflare, Railway, AWS or Google
  Cloud from the header, with approval-gated CLI runs (AWS and Google Cloud use
  your installed CLI and its login).
- **GitHub view.** Your repositories with their threads, pull requests and issues;
  review, fix checks, me

evidence.heading: Screenshots
evidence.text:
**A board for everything in flight.** Tasks from every project move from Pending to
Review, each with its harness, model and linked issue.




  
    Live replies. Responses stream in as Markdown, with tool activity folded above.
    Any harness, any model. Switch per task, with context size and reasoning effort.
  


**Agent teams.** An architect plans the work, runs workers in parallel across
harnesses, and reviews what they bring back.



**Your app beside the chat.** The iOS Simulator and Android emulator run in the
inspector on a lifelike device, so you can tap through what an agent just built.



**Bots that keep working.** A bot's conversation is an ordinary task thread, with
the same streaming, composer and model picker; reach it from Telegram, Slack,
Discord, WhatsApp or a browser too.




  
    Review every turn. Each turn saves its changes, with unified and split diffs.
    Bot settings. Memory, schedules, channels and rules, in one place.
  


Screenshots come from the browser preview with sample data. Regenerate them with
`npm run screenshots` (see [`scripts/screenshots`](scripts/screenshots/capture.spec.ts)).

evidence.heading: Privacy
evidence.text:
- **No telemetry, no analytics, no accounts.** PandaCode does not phone home.
- **Your code stays on your machine.** Projects, conversations and settings are
  stored locally in SQLite. Prompts go only to the coding CLI or service you
  pick, under that provider's own terms.
- **It only talks to services you choose.** Provider keys (GLM, MiMo, DeepSeek, Command Code, cloud
  sandboxes, bot channels, connection secrets) are sent only to that provider.
  On macOS they live in `secrets.json` in PandaCode's app data folder, readable
  only by your user (0600), never the Keychain, so updates never ask for your
  login password; keys saved in the Keychain by older versions move there on
  first use. Linux keeps them in the Secret Service and Windows in Credential
  Manager.

A few automatic checks send no personal data — just plain requests for public
information:

| What | Where | How often |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latest versions of installed coding CLIs | `formulae.brew.sh`, `downloads.claude.ai`, `api.github.com`, `cdn.kimi.com` | About every 6 hours |
| Plan usage checks for your signed-in agents | That agent's provider | When you open the menu bar item or the Usage dialog |
| Public model price list (for cost estimates) | `raw.githubusercontent.com` | Daily |
| PandaCode's own updates (`latest.json` on this repository's latest release) | `github.com` | At launch and about every 6 hours; turn off in Settings → About |
| Cloud agents (optional): the task's checkout, prompt and harness login go to the machine you chose; PandaCode checks on its active runs | The cloud provider you connected | Only for tasks you start on a cloud provider; while a run is active and at launch to re-attach |
| PandaCode Connect (optional): GitHub sign-in, then the relay that forwards your device

evidence.heading: Use
evidence.text:
Open a project folder, then click **New task** or press `⌘/Ctrl N`. A centered
"What should we build in …?" page opens in the last active project with the
message box focused. Choose the harness and model from the searchable picker in
the message box; new tasks remember your last choice. The **+** button attaches
images, documents, folders, project files or a mockup. Open **Changes** to
inspect and stage diffs, or the terminal to run shell commands. Conversations
and provider session IDs persist across restarts; agents start only for active
turns.

In **Files**, click an HTML, SVG, image or PDF to open it in the sidebar browser.
Filenames mentioned in responses become clickable and resolve against the task's
own project or worktree.

The bar above the prompt shows the project, checkout and branch. Its branch chip
is the one place for [worktrees](docs/worktrees.md): an unstarted task moves into
a new worktree in place, a started one spawns a sibling task, and archiving a
clean worktree task offers to remove its checkout and merged branch.

Choose **Board** in the header to manage tasks by status. Choose **Team** in the
composer for an automatic team, or set up an architect and workers. Each turn's
tool calls sit inside a compact **Worked for …** row; final answers and errors
stay visible, and approval requests wait in the bar above the prompt.

The branch chip also switches the project checkout to `main` or another local
branch, and in a worktree task offers **Merge into main**: it merges the
worktree's committed work locally, refuses uncommitted changes or conflicts
without touching anything, then offers to remove the worktree.

**Standard** permissions keep each provider's native checks. Claude's **Accept
edits** allows its editing tools; Codex uses its workspace sandb

evidence.heading: Resource limits
evidence.text:

each turn and resume by provider session ID. After a Claude Code turn, the next
turn's process starts in the background so a follow-up skips the CLI's startup;
at most two wait at a time, each for up to 10 minutes. PandaCode's fixed
instructions go to Claude-family harnesses once as a cached system prompt rather
than in every message. The interface has no transitions: everything appears at
once, and a thread you return to is drawn in a single frame. Terminal and Markdown c

github_projects.description: Run many Claude Code and Codex agents side by side, in one sidebar that tells you which one needs you. An unofficial fork of Warp.
github_projects.description_zh: 在一个侧栏中并排运行多个 Claude Code 和 Codex 智能体，该侧栏会告诉你哪个需要你。Warp 的非官方分支。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Run many Claude Code and Codex agents side by side, in one sidebar that tells you which one needs you. An unofficial fork of Warp.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Run many Claude Code and Codex agents side by side, in one calm sidebar that tells you which one needs you.



  
  


Harp is an unofficial fork of the open-source [Warp](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp) terminal.
It replaces the tab bar with a sidebar built for long-running coding agents and keeps the rest of
Warp as it is.

evidence.heading: What it adds
evidence.text: Agent states at a glance Each row shows whether its Claude Code or Codex session is working, waiting for you or done, with an unread mark until you look. A dot means background work is still running; a moon marks a tab you set aside. Cmd+R renames a tab. Groups that stay put Put tabs into named groups. With the tmux integration on, the group and the order are stored on the tmux sessions, so they survive a restart and other tmux clients see the same layout. Limit rings Two rings per provider in the footer: the 5 hour window and the weekly limit. Hover one for the numbers and reset times. Codex's come from its own session logs, Claude's from Claude Code's status line (see below). Harp fetches nothing and reads no credentials. Phone-friendly tmux Tabs attached to tmux follow their session: name, group, read and inactive flags. A session started elsewhere, for example from your phone over ssh, can ask for a tab with tmux set-option @warp_adopt 1. Everything else is upstream Warp, including its AI and cloud features (agents, Warp Drive, session sharing, login). They talk to Warp's servers exactly as upstream does; Harp adds no servers of its own. Logging in through Harp is untested.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
**Download:** grab the latest `Harp-<version>.dmg` from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and drag
Harp into Applications. Harp has its own bundle id (`com.dominikmartn.Harp`), URL scheme (`harp://`)
and settings folder (`~/.harp`), so it runs next to Warp without sharing anything.

**Updates:** Harp checks the latest GitHub release every 10 minutes, the same way Warp checks its
own server. When the release's version is newer than `version` in `app/Cargo.toml` of the running
build, Harp downloads its DMG in the background, checks that it is signed by Harp's Developer ID
team, and offers to restart into it. To try this on an installed build, launch it with an older
version: `open --env HARP_UPDATE_PRETEND_VERSION=0.0.1 /Applications/Harp.app`.

**Build from source** (macOS, Rust toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml`):

```sh
./script/bootstrap   # one-time: toolchain and build dependencies
./script/run         # builds target/debug/bundle/osx/Harp.app and launches it
```

`script/macos/run` signs with the first "Apple Development" identity in your keychain and falls
back to an ad-hoc signature. A signed, notarizable release DMG comes from `script/release_macos`
(see `--help`).

evidence.heading: Limit rings
evidence.text:
The rings are on by default and show the agents you use:

- **Codex:** read from the `rate_limits` Codex logs into `~/.codex/sessions` (or `$CODEX_HOME`).
  They appear once Codex has answered at least once.
- **Claude Code:** Claude Code hands its plan limits only to its status line. On first start, if
  `~/.claude/settings.json` has no `statusLine` yet, Harp adds one that saves the status line's
  input to `~/.harp/claude-statusline.json` and prints nothing. A status line you already have is
  left alone; to keep yours and get the rings, save the input first, for example
  `"command": "tee ~/.harp/claude-statusline.json | your-command"`. The rings appear after Claude
  Code's next answer, for Claude.ai plans (not API keys).

More providers can come from a JSON file another tool keeps current
([format](docs/limit-rings.md)); its entries replace Harp's own readings of the same name.

evidence.heading: Other extras
evidence.text:
The other extras are off by default. Turn them on in `~/.harp/settings.toml`; the app reloads the
file when it changes.

```toml
[integrations.limit_rings]
enabled = true
file = "~/.cache/limit-rings.json"

[integrations.tmux]
enabled = true
```

| Setting | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `integrations.limit_rings.enabled` | `true` | Shows the limit rings in the sidebar footer. |
| `integrations.limit_rings.file` | `""` | Optional JSON file with more providers; `~` is your home folder. |
| `integrations.tmux.enabled` | `false` | Tmux sync (names, groups, order, flags, adopting sessions) and agent detection inside tmux. Polls every 10 s. |
| `integrations.tmux.session_script` | `""` | Optional script that renames and regroups instead of the built-in tmux commands: `<script> rename <shell_pid> <group> <title>`, `<script> group <session_id> <old_group> <new_group>`. |
| `appearance.vertical_tabs.full_tab_menu` | `true` | `false` shrinks the tab and group menus to the essentials. Also in Settings > Appearance > Tabs. |
| `agents.third_party.should_render_cli_agent_toolbar` | `false` | `true` brings back upstream's toolbar under CLI agent sessions. With it off, update the Warp plugin for Claude Code through Claude Code's plugin marketplace. |

A Claude Code hook that reports background tasks to the sidebar lives in
[integrations/claude-code](integrations/claude-code/README.md).


Details for contributors

**Removed on purpose:** the tab bar's search field, view options and tab-config buttons in the
sidebar layout (new tabs come from Cmd+T, a double-click or the right-click menu on empty sidebar
space), the sidebar divider option and the title-strip panel toggles.

**Development switches** (environment, at launch): `WARPOSS_STATUS_TRACE=1` logs every change of a
row's sho

evidence.heading: Based on Warp
evidence.text:
Harp is an unofficial fork of [warpdotdev/warp](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp) and is not
made, endorsed or supported by Warp (Denver Technologies, Inc.) or affiliated with them. "Warp" is
their name. Please report issues with Harp here, not to Warp.

evidence.heading: Credits
evidence.text:

- Sidebar icons from the [Hugeicons](https://hugeicons.com) free set (MIT) and
  [Phosphor](https://phosphoricons.com) (MIT); the licenses are in
  `app/assets/bundled/svg/hugeicons/` and `app/assets/bundled/svg/phosphor/`.

evidence.heading: ESP32s3-LLM-Cluster
evidence.text: A distributed pipeline inference engine on multiple ESP32S3 running 1.58-bit (BitNet) Language model.

evidence.heading: Architecture
evidence.text:
This project runs a sliced 0.5B LLM across a cluster of 7 ESP32s3. One act as master and others are node. The master node runs the tokenizer and embeding and the other attention layer and MLP ran on the nodes. The master and node communicate through high speed SPI Daisy-Chain.

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     MASTER NODE                         │
│                                                         │
│  [ Prompt ] ---> BPE Tokenizer                          │
│                       │                                 │
│                 Token Embedding                         │
│             (INT4, ~14MB in Flash)                      │
│                       │                                 │
│             (SPI CH A - TX to Node 1)                   │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                        │ Hidden State Vector (FP32)
                        ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    COMPUTE NODE 1                       │
│             (SPI CH B - RX from Master)                 │
│                                                         │
│  ► Layer 0 to 3 (4x Transformer Blocks)                 │
│    • RMSNorm (FP16 scaled to FP32)                      │
│    • 1.58-bit Attention (Q, K, V, O proj) + RoPE        │
│    • KV Cache (PSRAM)                                   │
│    • 1.58-bit MLP (Gate, Up, Down proj)                 │
│                                                         │
│             (SPI CH A - TX to Node 2)                   │
└───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                       ... (Nodes 2 to 5)
                        │

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Herald OS


  An agent-native operating system, with Hermes Agent as the interface.



  
  
  
  




Herald OS is an operating system built around an AI agent. Instead of working through menus and
folders yourself, you talk or type to Hermes, and it works across the whole machine: it opens apps,
finds and organises files, watches what is running, remembers what matters to you, runs routines on
a schedule, and builds software while you watch. Every action that changes something goes through a
permission system you control.

> [!NOTE]
> **Herald OS is an independent project by [Luke The Dev](https://github.com/iamlukethedev).** It is
> not an official Hermes or Nous Research product, and it is not affiliated with, sponsored by or
> endorsed by Nous Research. Herald OS runs on [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent),
> the open-source agent Nous Research publishes, which is installed alongside it.

> **Status: alpha (0.1).** Expect rough edges, and keep backups of anything you let an agent
> touch.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Every download is on the [releases page](https://github.com/iamlukethedev/Herald-OS/releases).
Pick the way that matches your machine:

| Your machine | What to install |
| --- | --- |
| A Mac, Apple Silicon or Intel | [Herald OS for macOS](#macos) |
| A PC you can give to Herald OS | [The Herald OS Linux installer](#herald-os-linux-on-a-pc) |
| Arch Linux | [The Arch package](#arch-linux) |
| Omarchy | [The Arch package, then one command](#omarchy) |
| Another Linux | [The tarball](#another-linux) |
| An Apple Silicon Mac, to try the whole OS | [The virtual machine in UTM](#on-a-mac-with-utm) |
| An Intel Mac, to try the whole OS | [The x86_64 virtual machine](#on-linux-or-an-intel-mac) |
| A Windows 11 PC, to try the whole OS | [The virtual machine in Hyper-V](#on-windows-with-hyper-v) |

Hermes needs a model provider whichever you pick: a [Nous Portal](https://portal.nousresearch.com)
account, or an API key for a provider Hermes supports (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, a local model,
and others). Herald OS shows a sign-in card the first time Hermes needs one, and Settings > Hermes &
agents > Model provider switches to another provider or takes its API key, a custom endpoint's
included.

evidence.heading: macOS
evidence.text:
You need macOS 13 (Ventura) or later, on Apple Silicon or Intel ([On an Intel Mac](#on-an-intel-mac)).

**1. Install Hermes Agent** and choose a model, if you don't have it yet:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
source ~/.zshrc
hermes setup
```

**2. Install Herald OS.** Download `HeraldOS-<version>-mac-arm64.dmg` (Apple Silicon) or
`HeraldOS-<version>-mac-x64.dmg` (Intel) from the
[releases page](https://github.com/iamlukethedev/Herald-OS/releases), open it and drag Herald OS to
Applications. Apple menu > About This Mac says which you have: "Chip: Apple M…" is Apple Silicon,
"Processor: … Intel …" is Intel.

**3. Let it open.** This build is not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS stops it the first time.
Run this once, then open Herald OS from Applications:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Herald OS.app"
```

Or, without Terminal: open Herald OS once and close the warning, then go to System Settings >
Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, click Open Anyway next to "Herald OS was blocked", and
confirm with your password. Since macOS Sequoia, right-click > Open no longer skips the warning.

Herald OS takes over the screen: `Cmd+Ctrl+F` leaves or re-enters fullscreen and `Cmd+Q` quits. On
its first start it adds its system tools to Hermes (`~/.hermes/plugins/herald-os-bridge`). macOS asks
for each of these the first time a feature needs it:

- **Microphone**: talking to Hermes, dictation, and screen recordings with sound.
- **Camera**: the camera bubble on a screen recording, when you turn it on.
- **Screen Recording**: asking Hermes about the screen, copying text or a QR code from it,
  screenshots and screen recordings. Without it, Herald OS captures nothing and says where to turn
  it on (System Settings >

evidence.heading: On an Intel Mac
evidence.text:
Download `HeraldOS-<version>-mac-x64.dmg` and follow the steps above. The Intel build is the same
app built for x86_64, with node-pty's Intel binaries for the Terminal, but it is new and has not
been tried on an Intel Mac yet: please [open an issue](https://github.com/iamlukethedev/Herald-OS/issues)
if something does not work.

To try the whole OS instead, open the ready-made x86_64 disk in [UTM](https://mac.getutm.app), as in
[On Linux or an Intel Mac](#on-linux-or-an-intel-mac), or install the x86_64 installer ISO from
[Herald OS Linux on a PC](#herald-os-linux-on-a-pc) in a VM that boots with UEFI. CI installs it in
QEMU with UEFI, 4 cores, 6 GB of memory and a 40 GB disk
([installer-test.yml](.github/workflows/installer-test.yml)).

evidence.heading: Herald OS Linux on a PC
evidence.text:
The whole operating system, for a 64-bit Intel or AMD PC: Fedora underneath, everything you see is
Herald.

1. Download both parts of the installer from the
   [releases page](https://github.com/iamlukethedev/Herald-OS/releases),
   `herald-os-<version>-x86_64.iso.part0` and `.part1` (GitHub takes files of up to 2 GB), and join
   them. On macOS or Linux:

   ```bash
   shasum -a 256 -c herald-os-<version>-x86_64.iso.sha256sums   # each part; sha256sum -c on Linux
   cat herald-os-<version>-x86_64.iso.part* > herald-os-<version>-x86_64.iso
   shasum -a 256 -c herald-os-<version>-x86_64.iso.sha256         # the joined file
   ```

   On Windows: `copy /b herald-os-<version>-x86_64.iso.part0 + herald-os-<version>-x86_64.iso.part1 herald-os-<version>-x86_64.iso`.
2. Write the ISO to a USB stick of 8 GB or more with
   [Fedora Media Writer](https://fedoraproject.org/workstation/download) or
   [balenaEtcher](https://etcher.balena.io).
3. Start the PC from the stick and follow the installer. Its disk screen lets you erase the disk or
   install next to Windows, and encrypts it unless you untick "Encrypt my data". The disk password
   is typed at every start, before Bluetooth is up, so use a wired keyboard or one with a 2.4 GHz
   receiver for it; `herald-os password --disk` changes it later. Secure Boot can stay on.
4. The first start sets up Hermes Agent, then Herald OS asks for your name, a password and Wi-Fi.

Updates come as a whole new version of the system: `herald-os update` installs one, and
`herald-os rollback` goes back to the one before. Already on Fedora Silverblue or another bootc
system? It can switch to the Herald OS image in place, which replaces the system you run: try it on
a spare machine or in a virtual machine. Afterwards a login screen asks who signs in

evidence.heading: Arch Linux
evidence.text:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/iamlukethedev/Herald-OS.git
cd Herald-OS/packaging/arch/herald-os-bin
makepkg -si
herald-os setup        # once per user: Hermes Agent and Herald's system tools
```

The package downloads the release build for your architecture (x86_64 or aarch64). Then choose
Herald OS on your login screen for the full session (it needs `niri`; the package's optional
dependencies list what each panel uses), or run `herald-os-app` to use Herald OS as an app inside
your current desktop. The session applies Herald's theme to GTK apps, foot and GNOME's colour
scheme for the account that runs it, so on a desktop you already use, try it from a second account.
The package is not on the AUR yet.

evidence.heading: How Herald OS fits together
evidence.text:
**Herald OS Linux is the operating system.** Fedora supplies the kernel, drivers and packages, and
everything you see is Herald. The machine boots to the Herald splash screen and signs you straight
in. The niri compositor arranges the windows, Herald draws the menu bar, dock, notifications, app
launcher and system menus, and its theme styles the lock screen. Hermes starts with the session,
with tools to see and operate the machine. Linux apps such as Firefox, LibreOffice and VS Code run
as windows inside it, and a curated set comes preinstalled. It installs on a PC from the installer
image or runs in a virtual machine, and it updates as a whole system you can roll back.

**On Arch Linux and Omarchy,** Herald OS is a package: the full session from the login screen, or
Herald as an app inside Hyprland and Omarchy, following Omarchy's theme and keys.

**Herald OS also runs on a Mac,** fullscreen over macOS: the same interface, agent and tools, with
macOS underneath handling the hardware and your Mac apps. It is the quickest way to try Herald OS,
and where most of it is built.

Herald OS does not fork Hermes. It runs a standard Hermes Agent install and adds its system
abilities as a regular Hermes plugin, `herald-os-bridge`.

evidence.heading: English
evidence.text:
**Snitch** is an open-source application firewall and real-time network monitor.
See every connection your computer makes — who it talks to, where they are, and which app is responsible.

The entire interface is available in **English, Français, Español, Deutsch, Русский, 日本語, Português (BR) and 简体中文**: use the language picker in the top-right toolbar.

evidence.heading: Why Snitch?
evidence.text:
- **vs Little Snitch / Lulu** — same idea (per-app outbound visibility + blocking rules), but Snitch is cross-platform, free and open-source. Blocking is orchestrated through the OS-native firewall (`netsh` / `iptables` / `pf`) — Snitch never filters in user-space.
- **vs GlassWire** — Snitch is free, open-source (AGPL), requires no account and makes **no outbound calls without opt-in**; even geolocation is offline.
- **vs Wireshark** — Snitch gives a live, high-level overview anyone can read, instead of raw packet dissection.
- **vs cloud-based monitors** — everything runs on `127.0.0.1` behind a token; your traffic data never leaves the machine.

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Force Graph | Live node graph — your machine at the center, every connection as a node |
| World Map | Geolocated IPs with animated arcs on an interactive globe |
| 15/30/60-min Timeline | Sliding history stored locally in SQLite (24 h retention) |
| Anomaly Detection | Flags port scans, beaconing (regular-interval C2), potential exfiltration |
| Advanced Detection | DNS-tunnelling heuristic, cleartext-port spotting, per-app country baseline deviation |
| Passive TLS Inspection | Leaf-certificate metadata read off the wire (issuer, self-signed, SAN/SNI mismatch) — TLS 1.3 honestly unobservable |
| ICMP Tunnel Heuristic | Repeated fat echo payloads flagged — the ptunnel/icmpsh exfiltration signature |
| ML Anomaly Scoring | Pure-Python isolation forest over your own flows (zero deps) — outlier flows flagged after ~400 samples |
| Entropy Watch | Encrypted-looking payloads on cleartext channels (covert crypto/stego hint) |

evidence.heading: This project is discontinued
evidence.text:
I've decided to stop working on decomp.wtf and archive it.

Over the last few days I noticed that a lot of the decompilation community, the people who made the tools and projects all of this is built on, is against AI decompiling like this. I didn't make decomp.wtf to do any harm, but I respect their opinion, and that's why I'm stopping it here.

The code stays up as it is, under the MIT license. If you want to fork it and keep going with it, you can. I won't fix issues, review pull requests or make new releases anymore. If you already have it installed it keeps working, it just won't get any updates. You can still install the last version (0.10.6) with the commands under [Install](#install).

If you do use it or build on it, please only use it on games you own, don't share the game code it produces, and respect the rules of the projects you work with, because many of them don't want AI-made contributions.

Thanks to everyone who tried it, reported bugs and sent fixes.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
decomp.wtf runs on **Linux**, and on **Windows** (supported, still unstable). The compilers it runs are Linux
programs, so on Windows it runs in its own small Linux (a WSL 2 distribution called `decomp-wtf`), set up by the
same script as on Linux. macOS isn't supported.

**Linux**

```
curl -fsSL https://decomp.wtf/install.sh | bash
```

Can't reach decomp.wtf from your network? The same installer from GitHub (it then installs the release from GitHub
too):

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i12bp8/decomp.wtf/main/site/public/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows** (PowerShell; new and still unstable: problems are worth an [issue](https://github.com/i12bp8/decomp.wtf/issues))

```
irm https://decomp.wtf/install.ps1 | iex
```

It turns on WSL 2 if it isn't yet (Windows asks for permission once, and may want a restart), makes decomp.wtf's
Linux from Debian's official WSL image and installs everything in it. You get a `decomp` command, a Start menu entry
and a desktop shortcut. Your projects are at `\\wsl.localhost\decomp-wtf\home\decomp\Decomp`.

One line sets up everything: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), the app, the period compilers (pinned and
checksum-verified) and the m2c draft decompiler. It then opens decomp.wtf in your browser. After that, start it any
time from your apps menu (the Start menu on Windows) or by typing `decomp` in a terminal.

**Updates** come by themselves: when there's a new version, decomp.wtf asks once, and one click installs it and
restarts the app in the same tab (helper agents carry on). Settings has "check now", "install updates by itself" and
"don't look for updates".

> [!TIP]
> No ROM at hand? The app ships with **Demo Quest 64**, a real N64 ROM built from public-domain code and zlib.
> Open it from the home screen and watch y

evidence.heading: Or just ask your agent
evidence.text:
Already living in Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI or opencode? Give it decomp.wtf's tools once:

```
decomp connect
```

Then ask it, in your own terminal:

> decompile my game at ~/roms/game.z64

It confirms the game is your own copy, imports it, opens the live view so you can watch, and gets to work with every
tool decomp.wtf has: the original compiler, the byte-for-byte judge, the autopilot, helper agents running in
parallel (`start_agents`) and the rebuildable export. Behind it is `decomp mcp`, an MCP server that starts the app
when needed; you can also add it yourself (`claude mcp add decomp -- decomp mcp`).

| Agent | Install it as a package instead |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Claude Code** | `/plugin marketplace add i12bp8/decomp.wtf`, then `/plugin install decomp-wtf@decomp-wtf` (adds a "decompile" skill) |
| **Codex, Antigravity CLI, opencode** | `decomp connect codex`, `decomp connect antigravity`, `decomp connect opencode` |

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
1. **Open a ROM.** splat and spimdisasm find every function and data symbol, and decomp.wtf recognises the
   compiler that built the game.
2. **Add agents.** Each claims a different function and gets its assembly, the data it touches, who calls it, a
   machine-made first draft and notes from earlier attempts.
3. **Watch them match.** Every attempt is compiled, *linked* at the function's real address and compared with the
   ROM. A miss returns an instruction diff; a hit is saved, named and shared with every other agent.


What a match looks like


The assembly decomp.wtf takes from the ROM:

```asm
800007D0  slt     $v0, $a0, $a1
800007D4  bnez    $v0, .L800007EC
800007D8   addu   $v0, $a1, $zero
800007DC  addu    $v0, $a2, $zero
800007E0  slt     $v1, $v0, $a0
800007E4  beql    $v1, $zero, .L800007EC
800007E8   addu   $v0, $a0, $zero
.L800007EC:
800007EC  jr      $ra
800007F0   nop
```

The C an agent wrote, which compiles to exactly those bytes with KMC GCC 2.7.2 at `-O2`:

```c
s32 clamp_s32(s32 v, s32 lo, s32 hi) {
    if (v < lo) {
        return lo;
    }
    if (v > hi) {
        return hi;
    }
    return v;
}
```

evidence.heading: Continue a public decomp
evidence.text:
Most games people decompile already have a community project with its build set up and part of the code done.
decomp.wtf plugs your agents into them as they are:

1. **Browse** the decomp.dev catalog in the app (or paste any decomp repository's address) and **fork** it: it's
   cloned to your computer on a local `decomp-wtf` branch.
2. **Add your copy of the game.** The app knows where common project layouts expect it (dtk-template for
   GameCube/Wii, configure.py + ninja, splat + make) and runs the project's own setup. Anything else you set up
   by its README, and decomp.wtf picks it up once it builds.
3. **Add agents.** Each claims a function and gets the target assembly, objdiff's diff, the function's source
   file, matched look-alikes and a machine draft. Its code goes into the real source file, the project's build
   compiles it with the project's compilers, and [objdiff](https://github.com/encounter/objdiff) judges it.
4. **Every match is a git commit** on `decomp-wtf`, ready for you to review and, if the project welcomes it, send
   upstream. Nothing is sent anywhere by itself.

Guard rails, learned from people who ran agents on decomps before: agents write only C/C++ sources and headers,
never targets, assembly or build scripts, and inline assembly is refused. A change that breaks any function that
already matched is undone. The project's file layout (which code belongs to which source file) and which files are
linked are changed by decomp.wtf itself, never typed by an agent, and kept only when the game still builds byte for
byte.

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
| Feature | What you get |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Live view** | A map of every function in the game, each agent's tool calls, scores falling to zero, all in real time. |
| **Autopilot** | Free matches before agents spend a token: code the game has more than once is matched from its matched twin (names swapped, judged like any attempt: in Mario Party 6, 762 functions in 12 minutes, and 678 copies of hand-written assembly set aside), then every function's machine draft goes through the judge. |
| **Permuter** | Near misses agents leave (95% and up) get rewritten in the background, the way decomp-permuter does it: statement and declaration order, casts, temporaries. Improvements become the function's best attempt; a match is a match. |
| **Fast agents** | Small functions come in batches (one turn writes several, one call judges them all), identical code is shown in the brief, agents are told to move on after four tries without progress, and functions whose code repeats are handed out first (one match, many free). |
| **Your agent, your terminal** | `decomp connect`, then ask Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity CLI to decompile your game: it imports, opens the live view and works. |
| **Edit it yourself** | Every function has an editor: write C, press Ctrl+Enter, see the judge's diff. You count as an agent. |
| **Byte-for-byte check** | Candidates are linked at the real address, so calls, globals, strings and jump tables are verified too. |
| **Any agent** | Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, opencode, or any model with an API key, several at once: save one endpoint per machine or provider (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, DeepSeek...) and spread sessions across them. |
| **Lean context** | Compact assembly, diffs that say what's wrong before showing where, close look-alikes' C up

evidence.heading: Use it responsibly
evidence.text:
decomp.wtf contains no game code and doesn't provide ROMs. Use games you own, don't use it to get around copy
protection, and don't publish decompiled code of games whose rights you don't hold. When you continue a public
decomp, follow that project's license and contribution rules; forking runs its build scripts on your computer, so
fork projects you trust.

Many community decomps don't accept AI-written contributions, and the ones that do expect a person to stand behind
every line. decomp.wtf never sends anything upstream: your agents' work stays on your local branch. Before you open a
pull request, read the project's CONTRIBUTING (or ask its maintainers), review the code yourself, and say how it
was made.

evidence.heading: Dioramas
evidence.text:
**A free, open-source framework for cinematic, interactive 3D websites — with AI-generated hero assets.**

Dioramas is a way of building landing pages where the 3D scene *is* the page: a hyper-detailed object, real lighting,
a choreographed camera, and one interaction you can touch. It ships with **20 complete example sites** built with it.

Everything is free. No paid tier, no account, no CLI to install.

evidence.heading: The framework
evidence.text: Dioramas is three layers that work together:

evidence.heading: 1. Asset pipeline — prompt → image → 3D model
evidence.text:
Hero objects are generated, not modelled:

1. **Nano Banana 2** (on [fal](https://fal.ai)) renders a clean product plate of the object on white.
2. **Meshy 7.1 image-to-3D** (on fal) turns it into a 60k–250k-triangle PBR model at 4K geometry (optionally rigged + animated).
3. **`scripts/optimize.mjs`** welds, compresses (meshopt) and converts textures to WebP — a 25 MB raw model becomes 3–8 MB.

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # add your FAL_KEY
node scripts/gen.mjs all assets/jobs/<your-job>.json   # images + meshes (resumable)
node scripts/optimize-all.mjs                          # → public/models/<example>/
```
Every prompt used for the 20 examples is in `assets/jobs/` and `assets/manifest.json`. A textured model costs about $1.20; the
whole collection (65 models, 111 images) cost roughly $90.

evidence.heading: 2. Engine — `src/core/`
evidence.text:
A small three.js layer that makes generated models look expensive:
HDR post stack (N8AO ambient occlusion, mip-chain bloom, AgX tone mapping, grain, vignette), raymarched **volumetric
spotlights**, **planar reflections** with roughness blur, GPU-baked procedural textures, Lenis + GSAP scroll choreography,
custom cursor, preloader and cross-site navigation. See [`docs/ENGINE.md`](docs/ENGINE.md).

evidence.heading: 3. Method — brief → build → review → revise
evidence.text:
Each example started as a one-page brief (`docs/briefs/`) and was built by an AI coding agent against the engine, then
iterated with a headless-GPU screenshot battery (`scripts/review.mjs`) and a brutal art-direction review until every scroll
stop was a composed frame. Hand a brief plus `docs/ENGINE.md` to your agent to build your own world, or re-theme an example.

   Ollama starts with `ollama serve`; LM Studio uses `lms server start --port 1234`; llama.cpp uses `llama-server -m /path/to/model.gguf`; vLLM uses `vllm serve <model>`.
2. Open setup → **Change provider** → **Custom server**, or Settings → Intelligence → **Custom server**. If a server is on a default port, Atticus offers **Use Ollama**, **Use LM Studio**, **Use llama.cpp**, or **Use vLLM**.
3. Leave Key empty for an unauthenticated local server. Pick a model from the list Atticus reads from `GET /v1/models`, then ask normally.

Small local models are usually weaker at reliable tool use and following long screen context. Screen reading also needs a vision-capable model; text-only models can still use accessible window and page text.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
You need:
- **macOS 26** or later (Atticus uses Apple's new on-device speech)
- **An AI client:** a paid Claude plan (Pro or Max) and [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), the [Devin CLI](https://docs.devin.ai/cli) signed in to a Devin plan, [Pi](https://pi.dev) with your chosen provider/model, or a custom server through Claude Code with no Claude account. Pick one in setup (“Change provider”) or Settings → Intelligence.
- Apple's command line tools: `xcode-select --install`
- Accessibility permission enables native clicks, scrolling, menus, keys, dragging and field typing.

Paste this in Terminal:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SaarthurR/atticus-mac/main/install.sh | bash
```

It checks your Mac, downloads Atticus to `~/.atticus`, builds `~/Applications/Atticus.app`, and opens it. Atticus starts at login and updates itself from there (turn that off in Settings → About & Updates).

evidence.heading: Anonymous usage
evidence.text:
Atticus sends a random ID (made on your Mac, not tied to you) with daily use, ask outcomes, feature names, timings, dictation outcomes, and code locations for errors. It never sends task text, dictated words, file contents, paths, or screen content. Turn it off in Settings → Account & Access → Count me as a user.

If you say yes to **Help improve Atticus** (asked once, off until you do), a task that fails sends what you asked, the steps Atticus took and why it failed, under the same random ID. Emails, numbers, file paths, link details and anything typed for you are removed on your Mac first. Turn it off in Settings → Account & Access → Help improve Atticus.

evidence.heading: ff-tracking
evidence.text:
**A virtual camera films an AI agent's screen while a tracker locks onto every glyph it types.**

Six seconds, two [fframes](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes) passes, one SkSL shader.
No footage, no stock audio: every pixel and every sound comes from code.

[](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes)
[](https://www.rust-lang.org)
[](https://skia.org)
[](LICENSE)


  


**[▶ Full 1080p with sound](https://github.com/mrsarac/ff-tracking/releases/download/v1.0.0/tracking.mp4)** ·
[On X](https://x.com/0xsarac/status/2108515856544317489) ·
[How it works](#how-it-works) ·
[Quick start](#quick-start)

**Part 2 → [ff-unmute](https://github.com/mrsarac/ff-unmute): the one you can unmute. Music written in code, every number on screen measured from the sound.**

fframes studies · #1 ff-tracking · #2 ff-unmute, the one you can unmute



---

evidence.heading: What you are looking at
evidence.text:
An agent thinks out loud in a terminal: `thinking…` → `reading 14 files` →
`tool_call: render_frame()` → … → `✓ 0 problems` → `Done`. A computer-vision style tracker
follows the newest characters. A camera that never sits still films the screen up close.

- **Real coordinates.** Every `x: 1403 y: 559` label is the box's actual pixel position in
  that frame of the output. None of them are random numbers.
- **Focus that follows the tracker.** The focal plane is set by the box being tracked, so
  the depth of field racks along the line as the agent types.
- **Chain of thought, drawn.** Links run from box to box in reading order, and a dot runs
  along every link.
- **The lock.** Every shot ends with the newest word locking on: red for two frames, a
  scanline tear, a beep panned to where the box is.
- **Twelve shots, twelve looks.** A cut every 0.5 s through paper white, thermal, black
  and white, phosphor, amber, navy and neon.
- **A collapse and a landing.** Fourteen boxes fall into one, and that box becomes a
  `Done` pill before the fade to black.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
```text
hud ──► flat    pass 1: SVG, 3840×2160 ─────────► out/pass/flat.mp4 ──┐ iChannel0
 │                                                                      ▼
 ├────► lens    pass 2: SkSL on Skia Metal + camera tracker ──► out/tracking.mp4
 │                                                                      ▲ audio
 └────► tracks ──► out/tracks.json ──► sfx.py ──► out/pass/sfx.wav ─────┘
```

**Pass 1, `flat`**, draws the screen the way a terminal would: black, white, monospace, one
`<text>` per glyph, so the position of every character is known exactly. The tracker boxes
are on the screen itself. Some are hatched with an SVG pattern in `mix-blend-mode:
difference`, so the stripes turn dark where they cross a glyph. The only color is pure red,
and it marks a locked box. The pass renders at 2× because the lens magnifies it up to 3×.

**Pass 2, `lens`**, binds each frame of pass 1 as a shader input and films it. One SkSL
shader does everything physical:



1. **Perspective.** Every pixel shoots a ray at a tilted plane: real perspective, not an SVG skew.
2. **Depth of field.** The circle of confusion comes from the depth difference to the tracked
   target, with 36 golden-angle taps and highlights weighted like bokeh.
3. **Palette and aberration.** Brightness maps through five color stops per shot. R, G and B
   sample at radially shifted points, and the shift grows on a lock.
4. **Bloom and LED grid.** A wide ring of taps lifts everything around bright glyphs. The
   grid uses equal-area RGB stripes, so it adds no tint, and it fades out of focus.
5. **Tear, grain, camera tracker.** Rows slide on a lock and right after a cut. On top, the
   lens draws its own tracker sharp: links, labels and target brackets, projected with
   `hud::project`, the CPU copy of the sha

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
macOS uses Metal; Linux and Windows use Vulkan. For Windows requirements and the
PowerShell render pipeline, see [Windows setup](docs/WINDOWS.md).

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
- Rust (2024 edition), ffmpeg and ffprobe on `PATH`.
- Python 3 with `numpy` and `scipy`, or [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)
  (`render.sh` uses `uv run --with numpy --with scipy` if the packages are missing).
- macOS: Apple silicon, Skia on Metal (the existing path).
- Linux: a Vulkan loader and GPU driver, plus a C/C++ toolchain, pkg-config,
  libclang, fontconfig and OpenGL development libraries for Skia. On Debian/Ubuntu:
  `sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config libclang-dev libfontconfig1-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libvulkan1 ffmpeg`.
  For NVIDIA, install your distribution's proprietary Vulkan-capable driver.
  Rust Skia normally downloads a prebuilt; a source build also needs Python and Ninja.
- README images additionally need Pillow and `img2webp`.

Linux uses Vulkan, not Metal. The default `FF_BACKEND=auto` tries the platform GPU
and reports a CPU fallback if context creation fails. To choose explicitly:

```bash
FF_BACKEND=gpu tools/render.sh  # Vulkan on Linux/Windows, Metal on macOS; no silent fallback
FF_BACKEND=cpu tools/render.sh  # no GPU context is created (also works with GPUs hidden)
```

The CPU flat pass uses fframes' tiny-skia SVG renderer. The CPU lens pass uses
fframes' `SkiaCpuCtx` raster compatibility backend, **not** tiny-skia, because
tiny-skia cannot run SkSL. The original lens shader still runs: perspective,
depth of field, palette, aberration, bloom, LED grid, tear and grain are retained.
This is slower, and SVG antialiasing/filter kernels can differ from the GPU pass.
Backend selection is printed to stderr; invalid values fail rather than choosing
a different backend. `FF_BACKEND` also works when invoking either binary directly.
`preview` still needs a GPU/window; the fallback is for offline rendering.

evidence.heading: Render
evidence.text:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/mrsarac/ff-tracking && cd ff-tracking
tools/render.sh            # → out/tracking.mp4
```

`render.sh` builds the workspace, exports the tracks, renders pass 1, synthesizes the sound
and renders pass 2. It takes about 40 s on an M3 Pro, plus the first build.

Every pass is an fframes CLI, so the usual tools work on each of them:

```bash
target/release/lens strip all -n 12        # contact sheet of the final video
target/release/lens frame 81 -o frames     # one full-size frame
target/release/lens preview                # real-time window with sound
target/release/lens audio analyze          # loudness, true peak
LENS_STAGE=1 target/release/lens frame 81  # stop the shader after a step (0-3), as in the image above
python3 -I tools/readme_media.py           # rebuild the images in this README
```

evidence.heading: Slab score
evidence.text:
`tools/score.sh` is `render.sh` with the Slab score in place of `sfx.py`:

```bash
tools/score.sh                          # uses the committed render, score/score.wav
SLAB=/path/to/slab tools/score.sh       # renders the score again from Rust
SLAB=/path/to/slab SCORE_IMPL=python tools/score.sh  # original Python reference
```

Rendering needs a [Slab](https://github.com/nooga/slab) checkout built with
`zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`. The Rust `score` crate uses the MIT-licensed
[slabkit-rs](https://github.com/nooga/slabkit-rs) library to write the project
`score/ff_tracking.slab`, which opens in Slab's arrangement and mixer, and renders it headless.
The render runs past the picture for the reverb tail, so `score.sh` cuts it at 6 s and fades
it with the fade to black. It comes out around -10.7 LUFS with a -1 dBTP true peak.

Generate just the editable project, or render it separately:

```bash
SLAB=/path/to/slab cargo run -p score
SLAB=/path/to/slab cargo run -p score -- --render --stems
cargo run -p score -- --help
```

The Rust port reproduces the committed Python project's complete JSON values,
including Python's seeded random notes, note rounding, colors, clip names and
automation ordering. `cargo test -p score` checks every field against the existing
project using fixed resource fixtures; it needs neither Slab nor Python. For a
live comparison against your Slab resources, including changed camera/event
inputs and identical float32 renders, run:

```bash
SLAB=/path/to/slab python3 tools/check_score.py --render
```

Python is used only by the optional reference/comparison path; the Rust score
and `tools/score.sh` need no Python packages when `SLAB` is set. Python remains
part of the default `tools/render.sh` sound pipeline.

summary.text: 一个虚拟相机拍摄 AI agent 的屏幕，追踪器锁定它键入的每个字符；6 秒视频，两遍 fframes 渲染，一个 SkSL shader，所有像素与声音均由代码生成。

value.text: 展示了如何用 shader 编程实现复杂的电影级视觉效果（透视、景深、色差、Bloom、撕裂），将枯燥的终端 AI 思考流转化为具有视觉冲击力的叙事；对创意编码者而言，它是学习 SkSL 与 fframes 管线的高质量参考实现。

audience.text: 对创意编码、实时渲染、AI 可视化感兴趣的开发者与数字艺术家；希望了解 fframes + SkSL 渲染管线的研究者；适合有一定 Rust/Python 与图形学基础的人群。

outcome.text: 生成一段 6 秒的 1080p 视频，以电影化手法将 AI agent 的终端思考过程转化为具有 12 种不同视觉风格的追踪镜头，最终所有追踪框汇聚为 Done 状态。

mechanism.text: 两遍渲染管线：第一遍用 SVG 生成精确的 4K 平面终端画面，每个字符坐标已知，追踪框以 difference 混合模式叠加；第二遍将第一遍每帧作为 shader 输入，用单一 SkSL shader 在 GPU 上模拟真实光学效果——光线投射倾斜平面实现透视，圆弥散圆根据追踪目标距离计算景深，五段色 stops 映射亮度，R/G/B 径向偏移产生色差，宽环 Bloom 提亮，等面积 RGB LED 网格添加无染色网格，锁定时行偏移产生撕裂，CPU 端 hud::project 投影追踪器标签。

inspiration.text: 可尝试将类似的「虚拟相机追踪 AI 思考流」思路应用到其他场景，例如实时转录会议中发言人的唇动追踪、代码编辑器中光标轨迹的电影化可视化，或为终端工具（如 htop、htop-like）制作具有景深与色差的「赛博朋克」监控风格界面。

limitations.text: 依赖特定 GPU 后端（macOS Metal / Linux+Windows Vulkan），CPU 回退模式下 SkSL 无法运行且效果有差异；需要较新的 Rust 工具链与系统库；渲染时间较长（40 秒+），不适合实时交互；仅提供预渲染视频，无交互式部署。

how_to.text: 入口：克隆仓库 https://github.com/mrsarac/ff-tracking 并进入目录。
前提：Rust (2024 edition)、ffmpeg/ffprobe 在 PATH 中；Python 3 与 numpy/scipy（或 uv）；macOS 需 Apple Silicon + Metal，Linux 需 Vulkan 加载器与 GPU 驱动及 C/C++ 工具链、pkg-config、libclang、fontconfig、OpenGL 开发库。
操作：运行 tools/render.sh，自动构建工作区、导出 tracks.json、渲染 Pass 1、合成音效、渲染 Pass 2，最终输出 out/tracking.mp4（M3 Pro 上约 40 秒 + 首次构建时间）。
操作：如需单独调试，可用 target/release/lens frame 81 -o frames 导出单帧，或 target/release/lens preview 实时预览带声音的窗口。

input.text: 一段模拟 AI agent 在终端中「思考」的文本流（thinking… → reading 14 files → tool_call: render_frame() → ✓ 0 problems → Done），每帧中每个字符的精确像素坐标。

output.text: 一段 6 秒的 1080p 视频（tracking.mp4），包含 12 个不同外观的镜头（纸白/热成像/黑白/磷光/琥珀/海军蓝/霓虹等），呈现透视、景深、色差、Bloom、LED 网格、撕裂与颗粒效果，最终所有追踪框汇聚为一个 Done 药丸。

steps.text: Pass 1 (flat)：用 SVG 绘制 3840×2160 的平面终端画面，每个 <text> 对应一个字符，精确已知坐标；追踪框以 difference 混合模式绘制条纹，红色表示锁定。
Pass 2 (lens)：将 Pass 1 每帧作为 shader 输入，用一个 SkSL shader 在 Skia Metal/Vulkan 上模拟真实相机：光线投射到倾斜平面实现透视，景深根据追踪目标距离计算，R/G/B 采样点径向偏移产生色差，Bloom 环提升亮字，LED 网格以等面积 RGB 条纹添加不染
音频：tracks.json 导出追踪数据到 sfx.py，合成与追踪框位置同步的音效（锁定时的蜂鸣声）。
合成：Pass 1、Pass 2 与音频合成为最终 tracking.mp4。

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Whirl


  The AI chat app that sweats the details. Every top model, real memory,
  living documents, and your own tools, in one fast and friendly place.



  whirl.chat ·
  Self-hosting ·
  Architecture ·
  Contributing


---

Whirl is a full-stack AI chat app built on Next.js and Convex. It's the code
behind [whirl.chat](https://whirl.chat), published in full under the MIT
license. Read it, run your own, or help make it better.

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Every top model** in one conversation, routed through
  [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai), with adjustable thinking levels.
- **Living artifacts:** documents, charts, and full interactive pages that
  stay editable in a side panel and can be shared by link.
- **Integrations** with your own tools over MCP (OAuth included), plus
  installable skills that teach Whirl new tricks.
- **Long-term memory** that carries preferences and projects across chats.
- **Live web search** and page reading for answers grounded in today's web.
- **Locked chats**, encrypted on your device with a password the server never
  sees, answered only by zero-retention models.
- **Incognito mode**, message queueing, voice input, image generation, file
  attachments, folders, sharing, and a lot of care around motion and polish.
- **Light and dark mode**, accent colors, and an installable mobile web app.

evidence.heading: Tech stack
evidence.text:
| Layer     | What it uses                                                         |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Web app   | [Next.js 16](https://nextjs.org), React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, Motion  |
| Backend   | [Convex](https://convex.dev): database, functions, streaming, crons  |
| Auth      | [Clerk](https://clerk.com)                                           |
| Models    | [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai) via the [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev) |
| Tooling   | [Bun](https://bun.sh) workspaces, TypeScript                         |

Everything beyond Convex, Clerk, and OpenRouter is **optional** and switches
on with its own keys: billing (Autumn), web search (Exa), memory
(Supermemory), analytics (PostHog, Axiom), tracing (Braintrust), email
(Resend), and the support agent (Median). Leave them out and Whirl hides the
features they power. See [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md).

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
You'll need [Bun](https://bun.sh), a free [Convex](https://convex.dev)
account, a [Clerk](https://clerk.com) application, and an
[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai) API key.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/whirlchat/whirl.git
cd whirl
bun install

# 1. Create a Convex dev deployment and push the backend.
cd packages/backend
bunx convex dev            # first run walks you through creating a project

# 2. In another terminal, give the backend its secrets.
bunx convex env set CLERK_JWT_ISSUER_DOMAIN https://your-instance.clerk.accounts.dev
bunx convex env set OPENROUTER_API_KEY sk-or-v1-...

# 3. Point the web app at Convex and Clerk.
cd ../../apps/v2
cp .env.example .env.local  # then fill in the four required values

# 4. Run everything from the repo root.
cd ../..
bun run dev
```

Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) and say hi. The
[self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md) covers each step in detail,
including the Clerk JWT template Convex needs and how to deploy to
production.

brand/        Logo, colors, banners, and app icons

evidence.heading: ✨ catbus 是什么
evidence.text:
catbus（猫巴士）是一个命令行工具，用**统一的语法**调用 11 个中外主流平台的 web 端能力：搜索、详情、评论、用户、推荐流、下载、发布、私信、直播弹幕、列车余票票价……

```bash
catbus xhs      item search 露营 --sort latest
catbus douyin   item search 露营 --sort latest
catbus bilibili item search 露营 --sort latest
catbus x        item search camping --sort latest
```

四个平台，四条几乎一样的命令，输出**同一种结构**的 JSON。笔记、作品、稿件、推文一律叫 `item`，搜索一律叫 `search`，点赞一律叫 `like`。学一次，十个平台都会用。

evidence.heading: 🧭 同义同名
evidence.text: 含义相同的能力，在所有平台上用**同一个命令、同一组参数、同一种输出**。用了平台原生叫法（`note`、`aweme`、`tweet`……）也没关系，catbus 会告诉你该用哪个词。

evidence.heading: 📦 只需要 Node
evidence.text: 不需要 Python、编译器或任何系统依赖。原生依赖全部带预编译包，覆盖 Windows、macOS、Linux 的 x64 / arm64（含 musl），**8 个目标系统**在 CI 上逐一冒烟。

evidence.heading: 🤖 为 AI Agent 而生
evidence.text: stdout 只有 JSON，退出码稳定，错误里带着下一步该执行的命令；`catbus platforms` 输出完整的能力清单。自带 [Agent 技能](.claude/skills/catbus/SKILL.md) 与 [llms.txt](llms.txt)。

evidence.heading: 🔐 登录态只在你的电脑上
evidence.text: 扫码、短信、cookie 导入都支持，凭证按 **平台 × 端 × 账号** 隔离在 `~/.catbus/`（0700 / 0600），多账号随时切换。不收集、不上传任何数据，没有遥测。

github_projects.description: Official implementation of LittleBit (NeurIPS 2025) and its follow-up LittleBit-2 (ICML 2026)
github_projects.description_zh: LittleBit（NeurIPS 2025）的官方实现及其后续版本LittleBit-2（ICML 2026）

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Official implementation of LittleBit (NeurIPS 2025) and its follow-up LittleBit-2 (ICML 2026)

evidence.heading: Sub-1-Bit LLM Compression via Latent Factorization
evidence.text:
Official implementation of **LittleBit** (NeurIPS 2025) and **LittleBit-2** (ICML 2026).



---

evidence.heading: Papers
evidence.text:
**LittleBit-2: Maximizing the Spectral Energy Gain in Sub-1-Bit LLMs via Latent Geometry Alignment** *(ICML 2026)*
Banseok Lee, Youngmin Kim
[](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00042)
[](https://icml.cc/)

**LittleBit: Ultra Low-Bit Quantization via Latent Factorization** *(NeurIPS 2025)*
Banseok Lee*, Dongkyu Kim*, Youngcheon You, Youngmin Kim
[](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13771)
[](https://neurips.cc/)

---

evidence.heading: Abstract
evidence.text:
**LittleBit** compresses large language models into the sub-1-bit regime by factorizing each dense weight matrix into low-rank latent factors, binarizing those factors, and restoring magnitude information through lightweight learned scales. This enables extreme compression, including the 0.1 bits-per-weight setting, while preserving the original model architecture at inference time.

**LittleBit-2** improves this recipe by addressing latent geometry misalignment in the initialization stage. It applies Internal Latent Rotation with Joint Iterative Quantization (Joint-ITQ), aligning the SVD-derived latent factors with the binary hypercube before QAT. LittleBit-2 initialization is available as an opt-in (`--use_itq`) and produces no additional inference overhead.

---

evidence.heading: Highlights
evidence.text:
- **Sub-1-bit compression:** Designed for 1.0 to 0.1 bits per weight.
- **LittleBit-2 opt-in:** Enable Joint-ITQ initialization with `--use_itq` for improved latent geometry alignment.
- **No inference-time change:** LittleBit-2 modifies initialization only; the deployed factorized layer remains the same.
- **QAT-friendly:** Supports Quantization-Aware Training with SmoothSign and optional residual factorization.

evidence.heading: Supported Models
evidence.text:
The codebase currently supports:

- OPT
- Llama and Llama 2/3
- Phi-4
- Qwen2.5 and QwQ
- Gemma 2 and Gemma 3
- Qwen3

---

evidence.heading: Installation
evidence.text:
We recommend Python 3.12.

```bash
conda create -n littlebit python=3.12
conda activate littlebit

# Install CUDA toolkit. Adjust the CUDA version if needed.
conda install nvidia/label/cuda-12.4.1::cuda-toolkit -c nvidia/label/cuda-12.4.1

# Install PyTorch.
pip install torch==2.8.0+cu124 torchvision==0.23.0+cu124 torchaudio==2.8.0+cu124 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124

# Install dependencies.
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> For reproducing the paper results, use `transformers` 4.51.x. Newer `transformers` releases may change model internals or evaluation behavior.

```bash
pip install "transformers==4.51.*"
```

---

evidence.heading: Training
evidence.text:
Train a model with Quantization-Aware Training. By default, `LittleBitLinear` uses the original SVD-only initialization. To enable LittleBit-2 (Joint-ITQ), pass `--use_itq True`.

**Single GPU**

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m main \
    --model_id meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf \
    --dataset c4_wiki \
    --save_dir ./outputs/Llama-2-7b-LittleBit-2 \
    --num_train_epochs 5.0 \
    --per_device_train_batch_size 4 \
    --lr 4e-05 \
    --warmup_ratio 0.02 \
    --report wandb \
    --quant_func SmoothSign \
    --quant_mod LittleBitLinear \
    --residual True \
    --eff_bit 1.0 \
    --kv_factor 1.0 \
    --min_split_dim 8 \
    --l2l_loss_scale 10.0

# Opt-in to LittleBit-2 initialization
# --use_itq True
```

**Multi-GPU with DeepSpeed**

```bash
deepspeed --num_gpus=4 main.py \
    --model_id meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf \
    --dataset c4_wiki \
    --save_dir ./outputs/Llama-2-7b-LittleBit-2 \
    --ds_config_path configs/zero3.json \
    --num_train_epochs 5.0 \
    --per_device_train_batch_size 4 \
    --lr 4e-05 \
    --report wandb \
    --quant_func SmoothSign \
    --quant_mod LittleBitLinear \
    --residual True \
    --eff_bit 1.0 \
    --kv_factor 1.0 \
    --min_split_dim 8
```

github_projects.name: plain-backtest
github_projects.description: Say It Simply, Test It Properly. Agent-powered strategy research with independent ledger checks and reproducible reports.
github_projects.description_zh: 简单表达，正确测试。基于智能体的策略研究，带有独立账本检查和可复现报告。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Say It Simply, Test It Properly. Agent-powered strategy research with independent ledger checks and reproducible reports.

evidence.heading: PlainBacktest
evidence.text:
**English** | [中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**Say It Simply, Test It Properly.**

Describe your trading strategy in everyday language. PlainBacktest works with your coding agent to turn it into explicit rules, run the backtest, and reconcile orders and daily account balances against an independent ledger. Explicit execution timing, recorded data and code hashes, and reproducible reports make the calculation open to inspection.

Source code and bundled data: [Sixian-Li/plainbacktest](https://github.com/Sixian-Li/plainbacktest).

```text
Strategy in natural language → Agent + Skill clarify the rules → Freeze the experiment
→ Data checks → PyBroker execution + independent ledger → Report and research record
```

Your agent interprets the strategy and implements its rules; the Python framework handles reproducible calculation and validation. The repository includes three Skills, curated local data, research code, and 83 experiment definitions. Start with an offline example, then use your agent to continue the research.

evidence.heading: Run your first example
evidence.text:
Clone the repository and run the following commands. The verified environment is macOS with Python 3.13. Installing dependencies requires an internet connection; running the example needs no market-data API, credentials, or live data.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Sixian-Li/plainbacktest.git
cd plainbacktest
python3.13 -m venv backtest/.venv
backtest/.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r backtest/requirements.lock
backtest/.venv/bin/python backtest/scripts/release_data.py check
backtest/.venv/bin/python backtest/scripts/quickstart.py
```

Open the `outputs/example_…/report.html` path printed at the end. Each execution creates a new directory containing the input data, frozen rules, daily account state, orders, metrics, code and data hashes, and reconciliation results.

The default example uses QQQ from 2016-01-01 through 2026-08-04. It holds QQQ when SMA20 is above SMA100 and stays in cash otherwise. Signals are confirmed at the close and executed at the next session's open, with a cost of 5 bps per side. Initial capital is $100,000; fractional shares are allowed, with no leverage. The example uses the framework's PyBroker execution engine, independent ledger, and v5 report template.

Change the parameters or choose another approved symbol:

```bash
backtest/.venv/bin/python backtest/scripts/quickstart.py --symbol SPY --fast 50 --slow 200
```

This exploratory example checks installation, execution, and reconciliation. It does not mark existing experiments as validated or replace parameter robustness and out-of-sample analysis. Moving averages use earlier history for warmup. Adjusted OHLC prices approximate total returns without modeling individual cash dividend payments.

evidence.heading: Research with natural language
evidence.text:
Open this directory with an agent that supports project Skills. Have it read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), then describe a strategy. For example:

> Use quant-backtest to study QQQ with an SMA20/SMA100 rule. If the fast SMA is above the slow SMA at the close, hold a fully invested position from the next session's open; otherwise, exit to cash. Define the data range, costs, warmup, and benchmark before implementing the strategy, reconciling the ledgers, and explaining the results.

The project overview and quickstart are available in English and Chinese. Detailed research documents and report text are currently mainly in Chinese.

All three Skills are versioned with the repository, each with a `SKILL.md` entry point:

| Skill | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [quant-backtest](.agents/skills/quant-backtest/SKILL.md) | Turn a strategy description into an experiment, execution, independent reconciliation, report, and research record |
| [data-update](.agents/skills/data-update/SKILL.md) | Inspect data snapshots and manage isolated updates and candidate review when needed |
| [quant-tidy](.agents/skills/quant-tidy/SKILL.md) | Maintain directories, experiment lineage, and workspace structure |

These Skills are part of the project. Agents that support `.agents/skills` can discover them directly; other agents can read the relevant `SKILL.md` and its references. They do not depend on the author's global Skill installation. See the [research architecture](backtest/docs/architecture.md) for Git provenance, run lifecycles, validation gates, and worktree conventions used in formal research. The example also works from a downloaded source ZIP.

evidence.heading: What's included
evidence.text:
- `backtest/quantkit/`, `scripts/`, and `tests/`: execution, ledgers, strategies, metrics, data handling, and validation.
- `backtest/report_templates/`: self-contained Plotly reports. The default v5 template explains the strategy before presenting results.
- `backtest/experiments/`: 83 definitions and their lineage across three research programs: DER, ROT, and TIM.
- `data/`: 1,303 canonical daily-price CSVs, trading calendars, membership tables, quality evidence, and two original Nasdaq-100 ZIP archives. See the [data documentation](data/README.md).
- `research/`: indicator and market-observation tools without strategy account ledgers.

This is an independent distribution snapshot. Historical runs and large collections of old reports are not bundled, and the active/latest run pointers have been cleared. Historical findings from the source workspace have not been revalidated here. Some experiments require earlier training artifacts or original archives that are not included; see the [distribution scope](backtest/docs/release/scope.md). The source revision and data hashes at the time of copying are recorded in [source_snapshot.json](backtest/docs/release/source_snapshot.json).

This version uses the bundled data by default. `yfinance` is a transitive dependency of PyBroker, but it has not been integrated as this project's default data provider. The quickstart does not call Yahoo. The existing shadow-update tools are optional advanced features.

evidence.heading: Validation and optional labs
evidence.text:
```bash
backtest/.venv/bin/python -m pip check
backtest/.venv/bin/python backtest/scripts/release_data.py check
cd backtest
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v
.venv/bin/python -m scripts.build_research_catalog --check
.venv/bin/python -m scripts.audit_workspace --workspace ..
```

Tests that require original archives absent from this distribution report an explicit skip, not a pass. See the [verification record](backtest/docs/release/verification.md) for results. The distributed test suite does not implicitly rebuild the bundled canonical data.

Two optional Streamlit labs are included. Launch either from the project root:

```bash
backtest/.venv/bin/python -m streamlit run backtest/dual_sma_lab/app.py
backtest/.venv/bin/python -m streamlit run research/indicator_lab/app.py
```

Browser interaction checks and PDF export also require Node.js and Chrome/Chromium. Set `QUANT_CHROME_PATH` to use a specific browser executable. The standard example and Python tests do not require them. Other operating systems have not yet been fully verified.

evidence.heading: 默认工作节奏
evidence.text:

2. 修改完成后统一检查、构建、测试和游戏验收，汇总失败；实现期间不逐文件或逐补丁启动测试。
3. 按根因集中修复，定向复测失败项和受影响项，再用最终构建确认受影响的游戏路径。

只有缺失关键事实、后续实现无法可靠继续时，才提前执行最小探针。全量修改以当前任务为边界，最终仍需真实运行证据，不将代码完成或构建成功等同于可玩。

evidence.heading: 致谢与参考
evidence.text:
本 Skill 将本地游戏移植实践整理为通用工作方法。感谢以下项目公开原生执行、兼容层和平台适配的设计与实现；其中经验来源与相关工程参考分别说明如下：

- **[c22dev/mush8](https://github.com/c22dev/mush8)**：本 Skill 的 Rust/Cargo 模块划分提炼自基于 mush8 的本地 BOTW 移植实践。mush8 的 ARM64 离线改写、Horizon 宿主、NVN → Metal，以及 macOS 运行时装载与 iOS 构建期链接的分工，是相关架构经验的来源。
- **[jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile)**：本 Skill 所总结的早期 iPad 移植实践曾参考其原游戏 ARM64 代码改写、宿主服务、离线 shader 转换与 iOS 壳层路线；跨游戏复用的是方法与边界，游戏专用地址、补丁和逻辑仍需独立核实。
- **[ly05010419/MacNativeGames](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames)**：作为相关工程参考，展示了用户自备资源、按版本核验模块、原生执行与 Metal 图形适配、独立缓存/存档，以及区分构建检查和真实游戏验收的实践。它与本 Skill 的路线相呼应；当前未确认它是本 Skill 原始编写时的直接来源。

以上致谢说明思路与实践的关联，不表示这些项目为本 Skill 背书，也不表示本仓库包含其运行时代码。
