**Add to your agent**

Teach Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Hermes, and 70+ others how to author, animate, and render compositions:

```bash
npx skills add gatewai-dev/framefields
```

---

Framefields is built for coding agents. It packs the capabilities usually split across three desktop creative suites—Photoshop-style compositing & VFX, After Effects-style typography & motion graphics, and Blender-style 3D scenes & cameras—into a single lightweight npm package.

- **Zero Headless-Browser Overhead** — No Chromium, no Puppeteer, no DOM reflows, and no screenshot pipeline. Renders directly on native GPU hardware via Dawn / WebGPU / Metal / Vulkan.
- **Deterministic & Frame-Accurate** — Discrete sample points, absolute frame clocks, and frame-accurate audio BeatGrids. No floating timers, no drift.
- **Agent-First Workflow** — Your coding agent writes TypeScript, inspects rendered frame grids, and exports hardware-encoded MP4s headlessly.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: ⚡ Pi, the coding agent, compiled ahead of time to one native executable. 10× faster to start, 7× less CPU and 4.5× less memory than Pi on Node. Linux, macOS, Windows, ARM64 and Android (Termux).

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Pi-Bolt


  The Pi coding agent, compiled ahead of time to native code.
  One executable for Linux x86-64 and ARM64, macOS on Apple silicon and Windows x64.
  No JIT, no Node.js or Bun required.



  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  



  Install ·
  Benchmarks ·
  Docs ·
  Website


Pi-Bolt is the Pi you already use, with the same commands, sessions, settings, providers and extensions, but every function is
compiled to machine code when the executable is built, so nothing is parsed or JIT-compiled at launch. Against Pi as released on
Node 24, it writes a 400 KB file 120 times faster, uses 8 times less CPU while a long answer streams, 7 times less over a session
and a quarter of the memory; against Pi on stock Bun, much the same.





https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d043eb7d-ecb2-4837-a3ee-cbd98079adf9

evidence.heading: Why Pi-Bolt
evidence.text:
| | Pi on Node 24 | Pi‑Bolt |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ready to type | 423 ms | **41 ms**10× sooner |
| Writing a 400 KB file through a tool call | 143.7 s | **1.2 s**120× faster |
| CPU while a long answer streams | 18.6 s | **2.3 s**8× less |
| CPU per prompt, 40 prompts into a session | 352 ms | **46 ms**7.7× less |
| Memory after 40 prompts | 521 MB | **117 MB**4.5× less |

Pi-Bolt 1.0.0 against Pi 1.4.0 as released, Linux x86-64, one CPU. Every platform: [Benchmarks](#benchmarks).

- **Nothing to install first:** one executable; no Node.js, Bun or npm to run it.
- **The same Pi:** same commands, sessions, settings and providers; every Pi extension works unchanged.
- **Long sessions stay fast:** a frame costs about the same with 4,000 messages as with none, and typing stays responsive.
- **Everywhere:** Linux x86-64 and ARM64 (Android too, in Termux), macOS on Apple silicon, Windows x64.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
**Linux, macOS, Android (Termux)**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://pi-bolt.opensec.in/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows** (PowerShell)

```powershell
irm https://pi-bolt.opensec.in/install.ps1 | iex
```

Or:

- Command Prompt: `powershell -c "irm https://pi-bolt.opensec.in/install.ps1 | iex"`
- npm: `npm install -g --allow-scripts=pi-bolt pi-bolt`
- Bun: `bun add -g --trust pi-bolt`
- Arch Linux: the community AUR package
  [`pi-bolt-avx2-bin-release-git`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/pi-bolt-avx2-bin-release-git) (the x86-64 AVX2 build,
  signature checked), `paru -S pi-bolt-avx2-bin-release-git`

Then, in your project:

```bash
pi-bolt                         # start
pi-bolt update                  # install the latest release
pi-bolt update --rollback       # put back the build it replaced
pi-bolt update --channel beta   # take pre-releases too
```

New to Pi? Run `/login` to connect a provider. Your Pi configuration in `~/.pi/agent` is used as is. Pi-Bolt installs next to Pi as `pi-bolt`, so both can stay installed;
running the installer again updates, reinstalls or uninstalls it.


Optional extensions the installer offers

The installer verifies the release signature and offers three optional extensions by OpenSec:

- [`opensec-pi-subagents`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opensec-pi-subagents): specialized agents in separate sessions,
  parallel workflows and scheduled jobs.
- [`opensec-pi-todo`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opensec-pi-todo): a todo list for the model, shown as a live panel above the
  editor.
- [`opensec-pi-fff`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opensec-pi-fff): pi-fff's fast fuzzy find, grep and `@`-mentions, at full
  speed on the default build.




JIT build, for heavy plugins

The default build has no JIT: Pi's own code is compiled machine code,

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Editors:** `pi-bolt --acp` runs Pi-Bolt in the agent panel of Zed, JetBrains IDEs, VS Code, Neovim and other
  [ACP](https://agentclientprotocol.com) editors, with your Pi settings, extensions, skills and sessions. [Setup](docs/ACP.md)
- **Other agents:** `pi-bolt --mcp` is an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server; other agents give Pi-Bolt a task with
  its `prompt` tool and continue the session in later calls. [Setup](docs/MCP.md)
- **Built-in search:** the `grep` and `find` tools are on by default and search in-process, following `.gitignore`, with
  nothing to install. With [`opensec-pi-fff`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opensec-pi-fff) or `@ff-labs/pi-fff` loaded,
  FFF's search tools are used instead.
- **Compiled plugins:** `pi-bolt compile` compiles the extensions installed on this machine into your Pi-Bolt (Linux and macOS)
  with the release's own compiler, where they run as machine code; `pi-bolt update` compiles them into each new release.
  [Plugins](docs/PLUGINS.md)
- **Doctor:** `pi-bolt doctor` prints a plain-text report of your installation to paste into an issue. [Details](#pi-bolt-doctor)
- **Updates:** `pi-bolt update` installs the latest release, and `--rollback` puts back the build it replaced.
- **Herdr:** Pi-Bolt shows its state in a [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane, and a Herdr restart reopens the conversation.
  [Details](#herdr)
- **ARM64 and Android:** Linux ARM64 builds, and the same installer in Termux. [Android](#android-termux)

Pi extensions work unchanged. The default build has no JIT, so an extension loaded at run time is interpreted; compile the ones
you use every day into Pi-Bolt with `pi-bolt compile`, or use the [JIT build](#jit-build-for-heavy-plugins).

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
1. **Bun bundles Pi** and compiles it to JavaScriptCore bytecode.
2. **An ahead-of-time compiler** turns every function into optimized x86-64 or ARM64 machine code, through B3, the back end of
   JavaScriptCore's top-tier JIT.
3. **A prebuilt heap** holds Pi's modules already loaded, and is mapped from the executable at launch.
4. **A training profile** orders the code so that startup touches as few pages as possible.


Diagram and sources



  
  


The compiler builds on [oven-sh/WebKit#743](https://github.com/oven-sh/WebKit/pull/743). Pi-Bolt ports it to x86-64 and macOS
and adds its own code generation and runtime work ([docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)). `packages/` is the Pi release
named in [`sources.json`](sources.json) with Pi-Bolt's changes on top; the engine changes are in `patches/`.

github_projects.name: AI-Scientist-v3
github_projects.description: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
github_projects.description_zh: 智能体科学家：编排编码智能体进行自动化科学（共）发现

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
The Agentic Scientist
  Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery



  Turn a task description into experiments, ablations, and a paper, driven by coding agents.



  
  
  


Agentic Scientist treats coding agents as AI scientists. Starting from a
`task.md`, the agents propose ideas, run experiments, evaluate outcomes against
the task rubric, and iterate toward stronger programs. The pipeline then runs
baselines and ablations, a sealed final evaluation, post-hoc analyses, and
writes the paper, with every stage kept under one run directory.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
The recommended setup runs every agent phase inside Docker, which is the
default for `agsci run`. Install [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/),
then build the agent image:

```bash
docker build -t agentic-scientist/agent-cli:latest -f src/docker/agent-cli/Dockerfile .
```

If the build cannot reach package mirrors, add `--network=host` to the
`docker build` command.

> **Security note** — Agentic Scientist launches coding agents with full tool
> permissions (Headless `--allow yolo`). They can run arbitrary commands and
> inherit the API keys you give them, and the task files and papers they read
> steer what they do. Keep runs inside the Docker image rather than on your
> workstation, only run tasks and sources you trust, and review run directories
> before sharing them: agent logs can echo document contents and paths.

evidence.heading: Prerequisites
evidence.text:
- **Python ≥ 3.11 with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)**. `uv sync` creates
  `.venv` and installs the `agsci` command:

  ```bash
  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  uv sync
  source .venv/bin/activate
  ```

- **API keys** in a `.env` file at the repo root (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
  `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, ... whichever your agent
  needs). The pipeline mounts it into the agent containers. Never commit it.
- **Agent CLIs** are already inside the image. For native (non-containerized)
  runs, install the CLI of the agent you use plus Git and Node.js; versions and
  commands are in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).
- **GPUs** are required only by the GPU task presets. The pipeline discovers
  them through `nvidia-smi` and refuses to start compute phases unless the
  visible GPUs match the preset.
- **Autoillustrate** (optional) is built into the image for concept figures.
  To use it directly on the host, follow the single-command install in the
  [Autoillustrate README](https://github.com/SakanaAI/Autoillustrate#readme).

Run `agsci doctor` to check the host, or `agsci doctor examples/<task> preset=<task>`
to check everything one specific run needs (CLI, credentials, image, GPUs, task
scaffold).

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
Point `agsci run` at a task directory. This runs the default six phases
(task drafting → investigation → ablations → final evaluation → post-hoc analysis
→ paper) on the CPU-only circle-packing example:

```bash
agsci run examples/circpack
```

Add `--dry-run` to validate the configuration and preview the exact commands
without running anything. Every option is a Hydra `key=value` override; `agsci
run --help` lists them all.

> **Note** — Agentic Scientist drives `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `opencode`,
> `gemini`, and `pi` through
> [Headless CLI](https://github.com/RobertTLange/headless-cli), so the same
> experiment can be repeated across agents and models: pick one with
> `agent.name=<agent> agent.model=<model>`.

Task drafting only writes a scaffold when the task directory has none; every
shipped example already includes its evaluator, so the drafting phase only
snapshots it and the investigation phase builds and validates the task runtime.
Drafting a task from a bare research brief is experimental (see
[example 8](#8-draft-a-task-from-a-research-brief-experimental)).

evidence.heading: What you get
evidence.text:
Each run writes one predictable envelope under `results/`:

```text
results/<task>/<agent>/<run_id>/
├── task_drafting/ # drafting logs and validation audit
├── task/          # immutable run-local task snapshot
├── investigation/  # ideas, attempts, winner, and optimizer memory
├── ablations/     # baselines and ablations
├── final_evaluation/         # sealed final evaluation
├── posthoc/       # post-hoc analyses
└── paper/         # manuscript, PDF, manifest, and optional AI reviews
```

Investigation plus the task snapshot is enough to write a paper; the other
phases add evidence when available and are reported as degraded when they fail.
Browse any run in the browser with `agsci inspect start`
(`http://127.0.0.1:8765`).

evidence.heading: Recommended starting setup
evidence.text:
The default configuration is the one to start with: the `claude` agent, every
phase in Docker, and the CPU-only `examples/circpack` task. It needs a Claude
login, no GPUs, and exercises every phase through to a compiled paper.

1. **Build the image and the Python environment** as described in
   [Install](#install).

2. **Create `.env` at the repo root.** Only the selected agent's keys are
   forwarded into its containers:

   ```bash
   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=...   # claude, billed to your Claude subscription (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for pay-per-token)
   OPENAI_API_KEY=...            # recommended: concept figures in the paper and the `review` phase
   ```

   Other agents: `codex` reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY`, `gemini`
   reads `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `cursor` reads `CURSOR_API_KEY`, and Bedrock-backed
   Claude reads the `AWS_*` variables. Concept figures use `OPENAI_API_KEY`,
   fall back to `GEMINI_API_KEY`, and otherwise ship a plain export.

3. **Export host variables only if you need them.** Everything else (host
   networking, the image, the `.env` mount) is already the `agsci run` default:

   ```bash
   export AGENTIC_TEMP_ROOT=/path/to/scratch       # existing writable dir on a large disk; default: $TMPDIR, /mnt/localssd, or /tmp
   export AGENT_CONTAINER_GPUS=device=<UUID,...>   # GPU presets only: which GPUs to use; default: the first `container.gpu_count` (x investigation workers) from nvidia-smi
   ```

4. **Check, preview, then run.** Shrinking the ablation and post-hoc budgets
   makes the first end-to-end run finish faster without skipping a phase:

   ```bash
   agsci doctor examples/circpack          # host, image, credentials, task scaffold
   agsci run examples/circpack --dry-run   # print every phase command, run nothing
   agsci run examples/

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Six phases run in sequence: **Task drafting → Investigation → Ablations →
Final evaluation → Post-hoc analysis → Paper**, with optional **Review** and
**Revision** phases afterwards. Task drafting (experimental for tasks without a
shipped scaffold) turns `task.md` into a sealed evaluator and rubric;
investigation is the agentic idea → experiment → evaluate loop; ablations
compare the winning program against baselines and ablated variants; the final
evaluation re-scores it in a sealed environment; post-hoc analysis mines the artifacts for extra evidence; and the paper phase writes,
compiles, and audits the manuscript against that evidence. Each phase runs in its own container and only ever reads
the run-local snapshot, so results stay reproducible and `examples/` is never
modified. See [docs/pipeline.md](docs/pipeline.md) for the details.

github_projects.description: Fold papers, web pages, files, and AI replies into five levels of detail. Zoom from an overview to the original text.
github_projects.description_zh: 将论文、网页、文件和 AI 回复折叠为五个细节层级。从概览缩放到原文。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Fold papers, web pages, files, and AI replies into five levels of detail. Zoom from an overview to the original text.

evidence.heading: TextFold
evidence.text:
**Fold any text, from a one-screen map to every word**

Formerly PaperFold





**English** · [简体中文](https://github.com/chenxiachan/textfold/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md)


  
  


**Paste a link:** any web page · arXiv · PubMed Central · bioRxiv · medRxiv · Wikipedia · GitHub
**Drop files, one or several:** PDF · Word · PowerPoint · Excel · EPUB · HTML · CSV · pictures · Markdown · text
**Works with:** [Claude Code](#in-claude-code-and-pi) · [Pi](#in-claude-code-and-pi) · [Zotero](#works-on-your-zotero) · [Obsidian](#works-with-your-obsidian)

**[Try the demo →](https://chenxiachan.github.io/textfold/gallery/)** or **[download the app ↓](#get-started)** · [What's new ↓](#whats-new)

evidence.heading: Read with less in your head
evidence.text:
Choose the level of detail you need, and lower your cognitive load.

| | Level | Each paragraph becomes | In whose words |
|:-:|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Full** | the paragraph as written | the author's |
| **2** | **Brief** | its one to three key sentences, verbatim | the author's |
| **3** | **Key** | its point and the reason for it | AI, resting on the Brief sentences |
| **4** | **Takeaway** | one line on the spine of its section | AI |
| **5** | **Topic** | a few words; the text becomes a map of section cards | AI |

evidence.heading: Also for agent output
evidence.text: Your agent writes more than you have time to read. A [Claude Code mod](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview) folds every reply the same way, one key per level, and an extension does the same in Pi. [More ↓](#in-claude-code-and-pi)

evidence.heading: One fold, three places
evidence.text:
- **Read.** Paste a link or drop a file; it opens as a map of its sections that you zoom into. [Get started ↓](#get-started)
- **Fold your agent's replies.** One key per level in Claude Code and in Pi, with no second model. [In Claude Code and Pi ↓](#in-claude-code-and-pi)
- **Plug it into your workflow.** `python3 -m textfold get` hands your agent or script a document one level at a time, and an open format lets any program read and write folded text. [For agents ↓](#for-agents-and-scripts)

evidence.heading: What you get
evidence.text:
- **Words that travel.** As you zoom, every word that stays slides to its new place and the rest fade around it.
- **Zoom under your fingers.** Stop halfway, turn back, or open one paragraph alone.

- **Beside the original.** Open a paper's or a PDF's own pages next to the text, each paragraph shown where it stands on its page.
- **Ask AI about exactly what you read.** Select a passage, or ask about the whole text. The answer comes structured: the short answer first, then the evidence, each point citing the paragraph it rests on, one click away.
- **Notes that zoom with the text.** Highlight and write in the margin; what you marked stays as you zoom out, and is saved with the page.

- **Your language.** Read in many languages, translated sentence by sentence, with every formula as typeset.

[News](#news) · [Results](#results) · [Demos](#demos) · **[Quick start](#quick-start)** · [SDK](#sdk) · [Open stack](#open-stack) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Contributing](#contributing) · [Contact](#contact)





**Computer use has reached a turning point.** GPT-6 Astra's demos offered an exciting vision of what
computer-use agents could make possible, and the focus is expanding from GUI-only interaction to both visual
and programmatic interfaces. The question has changed, from how well a model operates a GUI to how well a
system completes work on a real computer by whatever means works.

**We call such a system a generalist computer-use agent (GCUA).** It uses a computer in more ways than you do.
It reads the accessibility tree and calls app APIs, runs shell commands, and operates the GUI when it needs to.
With **code execution**, it writes GUI operations as code and combines them with all of these in one program,
with loops and conditions. It can also share the computer with you, working in background windows without
interrupting what you are doing.

**Yet frontier systems remain largely closed.** We therefore introduce **Open Generalist CUA (OpenGCUA)**, an
ongoing project to develop and open the full stack for GCUAs with the community, including model, system,
trajectories, efficiency optimization, and evaluation.

**What we open in this version:**

- 🧠 **[OSWorld integration example](packages/harness/examples/osworld/)** with reference screenshot-action
  and code-action agents for integrating the OpenGCUA design.
- 📜 **Evaluation trajectories** of the 8 fronti

evidence.heading: 🔥 News
evidence.text:
- **[2026-10]** 🚀 The OpenGCUA research preview is out, with the [tech report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200), the
  [OSWorld integration example](packages/harness/examples/osworld/), the [macOS real-device harness](packages/harness/), the
  [Cross-Device SDK](packages/sdk/), and evaluation trajectories of 8 frontier models.

evidence.heading: 📊 Results
evidence.text:
We test the design on two fronts: OSWorld-v2 with eight frontier models, and real Macs with our real-device
harness.



- **Every model improves, including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5, and Gemini 3.8 Flash.** Over a GUI-only
  baseline with batched actions, the mean partial score rises from 45.3 to 64.9 (+19.6 points), and steps per
  task fall by 53% on average. GPT-6 Astra goes from 102 to 34 steps per task.
- **Weaker models gain the most.** GLM-5.3-Flash gains 35.2 points and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 29.8. The gap
  between the strongest and the weakest model shrinks from 39.1 to 18.0 points.
- **Code execution adds value beyond shell access.** With the same GUI and shell access, writing operations as
  code adds 6.1 points and cuts steps by 14.8% over a GUI+CLI agent (mean of three models).



With our real-device harness held fixed, on four macOS tasks Qwen3.8-Max used 19.4 times the reasoning tokens
of GPT-6 Astra and still completed fewer tasks. The case studies trace this gap to model behavior, which is what
our next release, the GCUA model, works on. The [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200) has the full setup, ablations, and case
studies.

evidence.text:
This is the shortest path from a clean clone to an interactive agent. It requires macOS 14+,
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), Python 3.11–3.14, Rust/Cargo 1.89+, and Xcode Command Line Tools.
Python 3.12 is recommended. Prebuilt SDK wheels do not require Rust.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA.git
cd OpenGCUA

uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ./packages/sdk -e ./packages/harness/runtime

.venv/bin/mu setup macos
.venv/bin/mu doctor macos

.venv/bin/mu setup browser --engine chromium
.venv/bin/mu doctor browser --engine chromium 

# Create a private local configuration from the shipped defaults.
cp packages/harness/configs/macos_demo.json packages/harness/configs/local.json
```

Edit the following fields in `packages/harness/configs/local.json`:

```json
{
  "api_key": "YOUR_API_KEY",
  "model_name": "qwen3.8-flash",
  "llm_base_url": "https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1",
  "llm_protocol": "openai"
}
```

Keep the other fields copied from `macos_demo.json`; the object above shows only the values
normally changed. Chat Completions-compatible gateways use `"llm_protocol": "openai"`;

encrypted reasoning across turns. Native Anthropic Messages endpoints use `"anthropic"`;

that support adaptive thinking. The Anthropic path preserves signed thinking blocks
in subsequent requests; `reasoning_effort` is not an Anthropic thinking switch.
Provider examples and every advanced setting are documented
in [Setup, configuration, and troubleshooting](QUICKSTART.md).

evidence.heading: Agent Skills
evidence.text:
The macOS harness can use local `SKILL.md` workflows on demand. It advertises each Skill's name
and short description first; the full instructions enter the model context only after you select
one or the agent calls `skills.load("name")`. The source checkout includes a
[PDF-form workflow](packages/harness/skills/pdf-form/SKILL.md) and a
[DingTalk workflow](packages/harness/skills/dingtalk-workflow/SKILL.md); the macOS app bundles the
same built-ins. The DingTalk Skill can guide an already available MCP tool, authenticated `dws`
CLI, or GUI session; it does not connect a server or log you in. Skills do not grant computer
permissions or automatically run scripts.

In the visual TUI, `/skills` lists available workflows, `/skill pdf-form` selects one for your
next message, `/skill new my-workflow` creates a personal starter, and `/skills reload` picks up
edits. You can also put an exact `$pdf-form` marker in a task message (including plain CLI or demo
hub input). Personal Skills live in `~/Library/Application Support/Generalist/skills/`; additional
absolute directories can be listed in `skills_dirs` in `local.json`. See the
[Skill authoring and troubleshooting guide](QUICKSTART.md#agent-skills) for the format and limits.

evidence.heading: 🧩 How it works
evidence.text:
Formally, a GCUA is an agent system that completes diverse computer tasks through visual interaction and
programmatic access, choosing **how to observe, act, and organize its work** as each task requires. These are
three decisions made at every step. A GUI agent leaves all three to fixed rules in its harness. OpenGCUA lets
the model make them.

| Decision | GUI agent | OpenGCUA |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 👁️ **What to observe** | a screenshot after every action | `screenshot()`, only when the model needs one |
| ✋ **How to act** | one click or keystroke at a time | a Python program that combines the accessibility tree and app APIs, shell commands, and GUI actions, with loops, branches, and checks |
| 🗂️ **How to organize work** | fixed by the harness | the model keeps a `todo` list and states its `<intent>` before each program |

Two designs make this work. **Code execution** lets a model bring the programming skill it already has, and
lets intermediate results decide the next operation without another model call. **Harness-to-model decision
transfer** moves choices such as when to look and what to track out of harness rules and into the model.
GUI agents, CLI agents, and GUI+CLI hybrids such as our earlier Qwen-UI-Agent are special cases that fix some
of these decisions in advance.

Here is one real step by GPT-6 Astra on a CRM task in OSWorld-v2. Lines marked `...` are cut, and long lines

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Strands Box

  An open source sandbox engine for AI agents.

  
    
    
    
    
  



<hr>

evidence.heading: Overview
evidence.text:
Strands Box is an open source sandbox for AI agents.
It combines operating-system isolation with semantic policies
written in [Dogwood](https://dogwood-policy.github.io/dogwood/), so you can control
what agents can access and the conditions under which they can act.

Box is harness-agnostic. You choose the agent program or binary to run, configure
its access in `box.toml`, and write its policies in `policy.dw`.

The host OS enforces the direct access restrictions in `box.toml`. Strands Shell,
Monty for Python, the egress gateway, and the MCP broker send the operations
they handle to the embedded Dogwood Local Engine, which evaluates the rules in
`policy.dw`. Box enforces its allow or deny decisions outside the agent process.

Dogwood uses `permit` and `forbid` rules. Operations checked by the engine are
denied by default: a matching `permit` must allow the operation, and a matching
`forbid` overrides that permission.

Box's interpreters and gateways share an event history, so rules can use earlier
actions and elapsed time to decide what is allowed next. For example, a file read
through Shell or Python can cause the gateway to deny a later outbound HTTP request.

**Preview:** Box currently supports local execution on macOS with Apple silicon.
We welcome feedback through [GitHub issues](https://github.com/strands-agents/box/issues).
Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a change.

evidence.heading: Key capabilities
evidence.text:
- **File, program, and network restrictions.** The agent's sandbox limits its
  direct access. Box reports the configured grants at startup.
- **Semantic and temporal policies.** Dogwood rules can depend on the requested
  operation, its arguments, earlier actions, and elapsed time. Operations checked
  by the policy engine are denied unless a rule permits them.
- **Policy across code and tools.** Strands Shell, Monty for Python, the egress
  gateway, and the MCP broker use one policy engine and event history. A file read
  through one interpreter can affect whether a later network request is allowed.
- **Request and tool-call checks.** The egress gateway checks connections and
  HTTP requests, including their method and path. The MCP integration checks
  configured tool calls and their arguments.
- **Credential injection.** The gateway authenticates permitted requests with
  configured API credentials or AWS SigV4 signing. The agent does not receive the
  underlying secrets.
- **Decision records.** Box records policy decisions in OTLP JSON. By default,
  records go to `<box_dir>/private/telemetry/records.jsonl`.

Direct filesystem grants in `box.toml` are enforced by the OS and do not produce
individual Dogwood decisions. To apply a policy to file operations, use the
interpreters and keep those files out of the agent's direct grants. See
[filesystem access](docs/user/security.md) and [policy](docs/user/policy.md).

evidence.heading: Use Box as a Rust library
evidence.text:
Link the `strands-box` package in `crates/box`, then call:

```rust,no_run
let exit_code = strands_box::run("/absolute/box.toml".into(), Vec::new(), Default::default());
```

This runs the existing Box command in the calling process and waits until it finishes.
By default, it uses the process's terminal and returns its exit
code. The second argument appends arguments to `[agent] command`.
Use `RunOptions::terminal` to supply the workload's terminal and `RunOptions::on_ready`
to start host threads after hardening and signal registration, before workload setup.
Call it before starting application threads or loading secrets, and use one Box workload
per host process. Later `run` calls fail, even if the first call failed.
Ship the matching Box helper binaries beside the host application.

To generate policy schemas:

```rust,no_run
let exit_code = strands_box::generate_policy_schema(
    "/absolute/box.toml".into(),
    "/absolute/schemas".into(),
);
```

evidence.heading: Architecture
evidence.text:
Box runs the Dogwood Local Engine and its enforcement components outside the
agent's sandbox, in either the Box command's process or the calling Rust
application's process. Strands Shell, Monty, the egress gateway, and the MCP broker
check operations with the engine before allowing them.
They also record events that later policy decisions can use.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph sandbox["Agent OS sandbox"]
        agent["Agent application"]
    end

    net["network requests"]:::label
    py["Python code"]:::label
    sh["shell commands"]:::label
    mc["local MCP calls"]:::label

    subgraph trusted["The box's trusted process (outside the agent sandbox)"]
        proxy["Egress gateway"]
        monty["Monty for Python"]
        shell["Strands Shell"]
        mcp["MCP broker"]
        policy[["Dogwood Local Engine and event history"]]
    end

    agent --- net --> proxy
    agent --- py --> monty
    agent --- sh --> shell
    agent --- mc --> mcp
    proxy -->|"policy checks"| policy
    monty -->|"policy checks"| policy
    shell -->|"policy checks"| policy
    mcp -->|"policy checks"| policy

    classDef label fill:none,stroke:none;
```

When the agent uses a program such as `git` or `cargo`, or a local MCP server,
Box checks the launch against policy and runs the program in its own sandbox.
You configure which files each program can read or change. The agent can send
requests to Box's interpreters, but external programs and local MCP servers
cannot. Box receives their output and exit status, and their
network traffic goes through Box's gateway by default. See the
[security model](docs/user/security.md) for details.

For each part, where it runs, what it decides, and how one request moves through them, read
[Box architecture](docs/design/architecture.md).

The download script checks the release checksum and unpacks the binaries into

Keep the downloaded binaries together in `./box-core`.

**Ontology-Augmented Generation for AI agents.**

Carrel is a self-hosted knowledge base for AI agents. It automates document
parsing, indexing, and retrieval, with optional knowledge graphs. Agents use
its API to retrieve source passages, images, and related facts, then generate
their own answers.

Use it to give an agent access to a collection of product documents, research,
contracts, meeting notes, or other files that change over time. A web console
manages knowledge bases, models, and processing tasks. A bundled
[search skill](skills/carrel-search/SKILL.md) connects agents such as Claude
Code and Codex to the retrieval service.

[Features](#features) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Agent integration](#agent-integration) · [Documentation](#documentation)

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Document parsing:** PDF, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheets, images, HTML,
  Markdown, and source code, with processing suited to each format.
- **Automatic updates:** scan for file changes, update indexes, and maintain
  enabled knowledge graphs through scheduled tasks.
- **Hybrid retrieval:** combine vector, keyword, graph, and visual search,
  with automatic knowledge-base selection and optional reranking.
- **Knowledge graphs:** extract entity types, relationships, and facts from
  your documents; retain sources, time information, and conflict indicators.
- **Agent access:** search through an API, fetch surrounding text or original
  images, and follow graph relationships when more evidence is needed.
- **Web console:** configure processing, inspect chunks and graphs, track
  tasks, and manage services. Available in English and Chinese.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D[Document folders] --> P[Parse and chunk]
    P --> I[Vector and keyword indexes]
    P --> G[Optional knowledge graphs]
    I --> R[Retrieval API]
    G --> R
    R --> A[AI agent]
    A -->|Follow-up queries| R
```

Carrel uses MinerU and native parsers for ingestion, Qdrant for vectors,
OpenSearch for keywords, and Neo4j for graph queries. SQLite tracks files and
tasks. Model services can run locally or through compatible hosted endpoints.
See [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) for the pipeline and retrieval design.

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
- Python 3.12+ and Docker 25+ with Compose v2.
- A text embedding endpoint; a vision-language endpoint for image descriptions;
  and a chat model for knowledge graph construction, if enabled.
- An NVIDIA GPU and NVIDIA Container Toolkit to run the optional local model
  stack. CPU parsing is also supported. Resource needs depend on the models
  and collection size.

| Platform | Deployment |
|---|---|
| Linux with NVIDIA GPU | GPU parsing and optional local model services; systemd scheduling |
| Linux without GPU | CPU parsing; connect to model services on another host or a provider |
| macOS with Docker Desktop | CPU containers and native Python services; arrange scheduling separately |
| Windows | Use WSL2; native Windows deployment is not supported |

[Example setup](docs/example-setup.md) describes the author's installation
on an NVIDIA DGX Spark and some lighter alternatives.

evidence.heading: 1. Deploy the services
evidence.text:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/FengZhenfei/carrel.git
cd carrel
./deploy.sh
```

The script detects the host, starts the infrastructure, installs the Python
app, and creates configuration files. On Linux with user systemd available,
it also enables services and scheduled tasks. Other hosts receive manual
startup commands. First startup downloads the parser models.

evidence.heading: 2. Configure model endpoints
evidence.text:
Edit `config/knowledge-base.env` to set the embedding and vision model URLs,
model names, and API keys. The initial URLs point to local model servers;
starting those servers requires the optional local model setup below.

To use the bundled local models, prepare their weights and deploy with
`./deploy.sh --with-local-models`. See [Model configuration](docs/configuration.md#model-endpoints)
and the [local model setup](deployment/compose/README.md#local-model-servers-profile-local-models).
Restart running application services after changing their environment settings.

evidence.heading: 3. Add documents
evidence.text:
Open the console at **http://127.0.0.1:9800**. Put documents in
`runtime/mirror/<folder>/`, then enable that folder in the console. Each
enabled folder becomes a knowledge base; scheduled tasks process its files.

For a knowledge graph, register a chat model in the console, select it in the
knowledge-base settings, and enable graph building. Check service health and
task progress in the console before making your first query.

system under proot, without root, and is its Wayland compositor: every Linux
window opens as its own Android task, with its own card in Recents.

  Copilot, opencode and others, which open in a terminal
- No account, no ads, no tracking

Needs an arm64 phone with Android 10 or newer. Without Linux, the launcher still
has the themes, wallpapers, Android apps and the widgets that don't run commands.

installed one; the choice is saved in `~/.config/omalauncher/agent`. Hold the mic to talk and release to send, or tap it to dictate

supports it), so only text reaches Linux.

editing. Right goes into a widget's own buttons, Left back out to its tile.

evidence.heading: Harnesses
evidence.text:
GPT with Taste compiles from a single behavioral recipe into native instructions and event steering for each supported host:

| Harness | Integration | Setup Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **OpenAI Codex** | Native model instructions & hooks overlay | [docs/install.md](docs/install.md) (or quick start below) |
| **Claude Code** | Main instructions append & native plugin (Sub + 3 Steer) | [docs/harnesses/claude.md](docs/harnesses/claude.md) |
| **Kiki** | Native Recipe (general bundle & Sol/Astra compat) | [docs/harnesses/kiki.md](docs/harnesses/kiki.md) |

| **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)** | Native Cordis plugin with request-local steer | [docs/harnesses/dsh.md](docs/harnesses/dsh.md) |

Running in another host? See [docs/harnesses/porting.md](docs/harnesses/porting.md). Maintainers edit the single English authoring source in `recipe/` and compile across targets: see [docs/authoring.md](docs/authoring.md).

---

evidence.heading: Install · Codex
evidence.text:
With Node.js 22 or newer installed:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/NB-Corp/gpt-with-taste.git
cd gpt-with-taste
node scripts/install.mjs --hooks
```

We recommend Hooks for multi-turn work in Codex Desktop: user submissions, child startup and supported wait results receive scoped reminders. Later child-input coverage depends on the [client entry point](docs/install.md#runtime-coverage). For a prompt-only installation, run `node scripts/install.mjs` instead. Neither route needs npm packages.

Both routes install into the active `CODEX_HOME` (otherwise `~/.codex`), write the two managed prompt files, and point `model_instructions_file` at the main one. Your model, provider, effort, authentication, permissions, MCP servers, roles, and `AGENTS.md` remain unchanged. To target another home, add `--home` with a quoted absolute path, for example `--home "C:/Users/you/.codex"`.

With `--hooks`, review and trust the three installed definitions in Codex Desktop under **Settings → Hooks**, or in the interactive terminal with `/hooks`. Enable only the events you want. Open a **new Codex session** after installation.

Check updates with `node scripts/check-updates.mjs`. Installation also checks official metadata before writing; add `--skip-update-check` for offline installation. [Update instructions](docs/install.md#update-or-resolve-a-conflict) cover the installed components and customized checkouts.

Prefer to delegate? Give your coding assistant this repository and [docs/install-for-ai.md](docs/install-for-ai.md). To recover the managed state, use [docs/recovery.md](docs/recovery.md). The complete installation contract is in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

---

evidence.heading: What changes
evidence.text:
GPT with Taste puts judgment into the outcome: choose sensible defaults, preserve supported claims, synthesize useful collaborator results, and finish work with care.


  
  
  


The recipe combines judgment, continuous execution, collaboration, and engineering and visual craft. Explore the principles in [Research](docs/research.md), or inspect complete runs, task inputs, and side-by-side outputs in the [Case Archive](docs/cases.md) and [Web Comparison](https://nb-corp.github.io/gpt-with-taste/).

---

evidence.heading: Comparison · From installation logs to a first task
evidence.text:
> **Task request**: Use `notes.md` to write a Chinese getting-started guide for a colleague who has just finished installing. Save it as `START_HERE.md`.

The visible improvement is straightforward: get the reader started first, while installation audits and process disclaimers step out of the way.

[](https://nb-corp.github.io/gpt-with-taste/)

Inspect full inputs, generated documents, and run conditions: [Task & run conditions](docs/cases/codex-first-use/input.md) · [Web comparison page](https://nb-corp.github.io/gpt-with-taste/) · [Case index](docs/cases.md).

---

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
1. **The system prompt sets standing priorities.** It covers judgment, execution, collaboration, and craft across hosts. The instructions are English; replies follow your latest language.
2. **Steer refreshes priorities at supported events.** Using local hooks, extensions, or native recipe events, reminders route user context to main, scoped reminders to delegated agents, and input-consumption guidance to main upon receiving collaborator results.

Standalone prompt definitions provide the complete behavior for each agent role; supported harnesses connect the matching reminder paths.

---

evidence.heading: Research
evidence.text:
[docs/research.md](docs/research.md) details the findings, prompt architecture, and iteration loop behind the recipe: how defensive writing affects the reader's experience, why models need room for ordinary judgment, and how collaborator findings are turned into direct action.

---

用户级 systemd 服务，以及 SL 本地托管和 Docker 托管。没有桌面时可用浏览器中的 noVNC 扫码。
多实例各有独立端口、账号数据、SL 容器和 MCP 授权；新增私聊、图片导入、SL 扩展工具及授权编辑。

安装与限制见 [Linux 教程](README.linux.md)、[使用说明](doc/LINUX_TERMINAL.md)；
开发分工见 [模型贡献记录](doc/LINUX_CONTRIBUTORS.md)。下方桌面下载和启动教程继续适用于 Windows。

evidence.heading: 使用场景
evidence.text: 下面是可以交给 Agent 的请求示例，实际能力取决于资料、授权、模型和客户端。

evidence.heading: 让小鲸鱼来水群
evidence.text:
> 先列出可用人格和允许的 QQ 群，核对“我的测试群”后，用小鲸鱼持续聊天，直到我停止。接得上话再说，不必每条都回复。

随包提供小鲸鱼（`little_whale`）、小鲸鱼2号（`little_whale_v2`）和龙娘（`dragon_girl`，测试版），也能用 Markdown 写自己的角色。支持按语境接话、原生 @ 与引用；授权后可看图、发送和收藏表情、给消息贴表情回应，保留理解笔记供后续会话选用。

持续聊天会在当前已授权的机器人账号和群里积累群友表达与黑话，潜水时也能学习；同账号同群重开可接续积累。人物卡与学习参考分开，模型可以选择本轮不用。[聊天节奏](doc/MCP_CHAT_TURNS.md) · [实时学习](doc/MCP_LANGUAGE_LEARNING.md)

人格卡只改变表达，不会替换底层模型；发言和表情使用由 Agent 决定。详见 [人格教程](doc/MCP_CHAT.md)与[表情链路](doc/MCP_STICKERS.md)。

evidence.heading: 找回聊过的资料和文件
evidence.text:
> 帮我找我的群里的一些我需要的附件，核对时间，并标出消息来源。

按关键词、人物、会话和日期检索，再展开上下文。图片、语音和文件按需读取；轻量版可经 OneBot 下载 QQ 群原文件，交给同机 Agent 自己的文件工具阅读。

evidence.heading: 把消息整理成有出处的总结
evidence.text:
> 总结项目群这周确定的分工和待确认事项，把每项对应的原话列出来。

从消息和文件中整理结论，保留可回查的来源。完整版还提供回复草稿、会话记忆、关注卡和持续调查工作区；完整能力见[功能清单](doc/FEATURES.md)。

evidence.heading: 为什么用 Tulpa
evidence.text:
- **复用熟悉的 Agent**：Tulpa 负责资料读取、检索和授权，外部 Agent 负责理解与任务执行；只用 MCP 无需在 Tulpa 另配模型 API Key。
- **范围由你决定**：按平台、会话、日期开放资料，写操作另行授权，每个客户端的连接可单独撤销。
- **查得到，也能回头核对**：从结论展开上下文、查看原文，按需取图片和文件，不必反复复制聊天。

已接入以下客户端：

 [Codex](doc/AGENT_SETUP.md#codex) ·
 [Claude Code](doc/AGENT_SETUP.md#claude-code) ·
 [DeepSeek Harness](doc/AGENT_SETUP.md#deepseek-harness) ·
 [Antigravity](doc/AGENT_SETUP.md#google-antigravity) ·
 [WorkBuddy](doc/AGENT_SETUP.md#workbuddy)


客户端实测范围

- **Codex / DeepSeek Harness**：已验证聊天查询、图片和文件读取，以及授权测试群发言、修改群名并恢复。
- **Claude Code**：已接入并由用户在本机确认功能正常，使用原生 HTTP MCP 与 Bearer Token。
- **Antigravity**：已验证消息查询和图片理解；验收仅开放只读权限，尚未实测持续群聊、发送与群管理。
- **WorkBuddy**：已接入并由用户确认跑通；调用记录覆盖消息、图片、文件、群资料及人格发现。

客户端的识图、工具审批与持续运行机制不同。详见 [Agent 教程](doc/AGENT_SETUP.md)和[验证记录](doc/VALIDATION.md)。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: A self-hosted job search app that writes tailored resumes and cover letters from your profile.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Dossier


  Your job search, on your own server: one profile, a tailored resume and cover letter for every job, and every application tracked from draft to offer.



  
  
  
  
  
  


Dossier keeps your career history in one profile and turns it into a clean resume. For every job you apply to, it reads the posting, shows how you match, and drafts a tailored resume and cover letter that only use facts from your profile. You refine them in a chat, download them as PDFs and track each application from draft to offer.

It's for one person on a small server: one password, your data in your own PostgreSQL database, and an AI model of your choice. That can be a local model through Ollama or LM Studio, so your profile and documents stay on your own hardware, or a hosted one (any OpenAI-compatible API, Anthropic or Mistral), which then receives what it writes from. [Privacy](https://github.com/AienTech/dossier/wiki/Privacy) says what goes where.

**Get started:** [run it on your computer](#run-it-on-your-computer) in a few minutes, or [self-host it](#self-hosting) on a server. The [installation guide](https://github.com/AienTech/dossier/wiki) covers every way: Docker with or without Compose, Node.js, a plain Ubuntu server, CapRover, Coolify and Dokploy.

evidence.heading: Demo
evidence.text: Recorded with the demo data (Jane Doe is made up) and a stand-in AI server that answers at once, played at 1.2× speed. With a real model, reading a posting and writing the documents takes from a few seconds to a few minutes.

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Profile:** basics, skills and languages, experience, projects, education, publications and references, in the order you choose, with a strength meter that counts only what a profile needs. Projects (side, open-source, course or thesis work) show what you can do where your job titles don't yet. Publications are cited in your own style, with bold and italics, and go on resumes word for word. Start it from an existing resume (PDF, Word or Markdown) if you like.
- **Base resume:** twelve themes and a theme builder, previewed live and printed to PDF on the server. Duplicate themes, or share them as files.
- **Find jobs:** search postings near your city, or anywhere you choose, through JSearch (LinkedIn, Indeed and more) or Adzuna. Save the good ones, dismiss the rest, score any of them against your profile, and start an application from a posting with one click.
- **Startups:** startups that are hiring, from YC startups' job posts and Hacker News' monthly “Who is hiring?” thread, kept to the ones that hire where you live or remotely from your country and ranked against your profile, with the address each one publishes for applications. Dossier reads their sites politely and follows their robots.txt. Start an application to one with a click; you decide whom to write to.
- **Job agent (optional):** once a day it runs one search for you, skips what you've seen, scores the new postings against your profile and keeps the best on the Agent screen, with its reasons. It can prepare tailored drafts too, which wait for your review. It never sends or applies.
- **New application:** paste a posting; Dossier pulls out the details and requirements, matches them against your profile, and writes a tailored resume and cover letter in the tone you pick.
- **Never invents experience:** dra

evidence.heading: Run it on your computer
evidence.text:
All you need is [Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/) on macOS or Windows, or Docker Engine with its Compose plugin on Linux, and about 2 GB of free memory. Run the commands in a terminal: macOS's Terminal, Linux, or WSL on Windows.

**1. Fetch the Compose file** into a folder of its own, and make the secrets Dossier needs:

```bash
mkdir ~/dossier && cd ~/dossier
curl -fsSL -o compose.yml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AienTech/dossier/main/compose.production.yml
echo "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24)" > .env
echo "DOSSIER_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)" >> .env
```

On an Apple Silicon Mac, also run `printf 'services:\n  app:\n    platform: linux/amd64\n' > compose.override.yml`: the image is built for Intel and AMD processors, and Docker Desktop runs it under emulation.

**2. Choose your password.** This asks for it twice and prints a hash of it, one line that starts with `argon2id:`:

```bash
docker run --rm -it --platform linux/amd64 ghcr.io/aientech/dossier hash-password
```

Add that line to `.env` as `DOSSIER_PASSWORD=argon2id:…`, with any text editor. Dossier only keeps the hash, never the password.

**3. Start it:**

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

The first start downloads the image (about 1.7 GB) and sets up the database. Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000), sign in with your password, and pick an AI model in **Settings → AI provider** (see [Choosing an AI provider](https://github.com/AienTech/dossier/wiki/Choosing-an-AI-provider)).

`docker compose stop` stops it and `docker compose start` starts it again, with your data kept. It's only reachable from your own computer. The [installation guide's Docker Compose page](https://github.com/AienTech/dossier/wiki/Run-locally-with-Docker-Compose) has more: another port,

evidence.heading: Self-hosting
evidence.text: To put Dossier on a server, on your own domain with HTTPS, follow the [installation guide](https://github.com/AienTech/dossier/wiki#self-host-on-a-server): a plain Ubuntu server with Docker Compose and Caddy (or Node.js, without Docker), CapRover, Coolify or Dokploy. Give the server at least 2 vCPUs and 2 GB of memory (see [Performance and sizing](#performance-and-sizing)).

evidence.heading: Known limitations
evidence.text:
- **Desktop only:** made for a laptop or desktop browser, not for phones.
- **Single user:** one password and one profile; there are no accounts.
- **English interface:** the app itself is in English. Documents can be written in other languages; in the 21 built-in ones, their headings, dates and language levels are in that language too, and in one added with **Other language…** those stay in English.
- **One instance:** run a single copy of the app per database. The nightly backups, the AI job queue and the PDF browser live inside the app's process.

evidence.heading: Let your AI set it up
evidence.text:
Do you use an AI coding assistant (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, ...)? Paste this into it:

```text
Set up PolyStrata on this PC for me: https://github.com/VecSzn/PolyStrata - follow docs/AI_SETUP.md in that repository.
```

It checks your graphics card, RAM and disk and picks the model that fits. Then it installs and starts it and tells
you how to connect your apps. AI tools can also install, start and stop PolyStrata through its
[MCP server](docs/MCP_SERVER.md).

evidence.heading: Or do it yourself
evidence.text:
[Download PolyStrata](https://github.com/VecSzn/PolyStrata/archive/refs/heads/main.zip) and unzip it (or `git clone` it).
**Windows:** double-click **`START-HERE.bat`**. **Linux:** run **`./setup.sh`** in the PolyStrata folder.

**Mac (Apple Silicon, M1 to M5, macOS 15 or newer):** install Apple's Command Line Tools once
(`xcode-select --install` in Terminal; Xcode itself is not needed). Then open Terminal in the PolyStrata folder and run
**`./setup.sh`**. It builds the Mac engine on your Mac (about 7 minutes), asks the same questions, downloads the model
and starts it. Next time, `./setup.sh` starts it right away. Which size fits your Mac and how fast it is:
[docs/MAC.md](docs/MAC.md). The Mac engine runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next only; the other nine models need an NVIDIA or AMD
card.

The installer finds your card and sets up the right engine for it. It asks you a few questions:

- which model and which size,
- how much context (how much text the model keeps in mind),
- whether it should read pictures (GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Flash, LFM2.5 and Flint read none).

Press Enter each time for the recommended answer. Then it downloads the model (about 70 GB for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next,
79 to 114 GB for GLM 5.3 Flash, 91 GB for DeepSeek V4 Flash, 11 to 42 GB for the other seven) and starts it. If the download stops, run it again:
it continues where it left off. Your browser opens the PolyStrata app at `http://127.0.0.1:8080`.

All ten are in the installer's list of models. `./setup.sh --family glm`, `deepseek`, `lfm25`, `flint`, `qwen36`, `ornith`,
`gemma4`, `tiel` or `minicpmv` goes straight to one ([what it asks and writes](docs/GLM.md#install)).

> **While the model starts, your PC can be slow or stop responding for 1-3 minutes** (longest the first time).
> PolyStrata loads 35-55

| [Flint 40B-A2.5B](docs/models/flint.md) | UD-Q4_K_XL from about 40 GB of RAM | UD-Q3_K_XL | UD-Q6_K_XL, Q8_0 |

What each size is, its download, the RAM it needs beside other cards and how close it comes to the largest: each model's page, linked from the table under "How fast is it?".

evidence.heading: How does it work?
evidence.text:
Models like these usually run on servers with hundreds of gigabytes of graphics memory. Your graphics card has
8-32 GB. PolyStrata makes the model fit by **sharing the work across your whole PC**. Think of a kitchen: the things
you use all the time stay on the counter, and the rest waits in the pantry.

Each model's diagram and how it works: [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS_MODELS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS_MODELS.md).

evidence.heading: 安全边界
evidence.text:
**控制台**：Docker 是硬依赖。每个项目一个 Kali 容器（`sentinel:latest`），Agent 的 bash 命令**在容器内执行**（`docker exec`），项目目录 bind mount 进 `/work`，容器**以 root 运行**。容器网络默认 **host**（容器直接用宿主机网络栈，反向 shell、payload 服务、本地靶场、内网与 VPN 才是真实的），可在「设置 → 环境 → 容器网络」切到 **bridge**；两种模式都保留 `NET_RAW`，`NET_ADMIN` 只在 bridge 模式授予。Docker 检查有阻断项时控制台拒绝 `prompt`、`compact` 与持续目标。

**但容器只约束命令，不是整体沙箱**：控制台与 Agent 进程本身以启动者的用户身份跑在宿主机上，只有命令进容器。

- 审批链只覆盖 bash、安卓 shell（`droid_shell`）与 iOS shell（`ios_shell`），子代理的 bash 走同一条链；**read/edit/write、文件面板、MCP 工具、codemode，以及 frida、抓包、APK 分析等直接调用容器的工具都不过门**。工程任务的 bash 另有一套正则黑名单、20 秒超时与 40 条预算，同样不走审批门。
- `read/edit/write` 直接读写宿主机文件系统，项目目录只是相对路径的基准，绝对路径不受限制；MCP 的 stdio 服务器是宿主机子进程。
- AI 审批（守门模型）只判六类破坏性操作，判定失败、超时或无法解析一律放行（fail-open），**不是沙箱、也不做数据防泄漏**。
- 容器以 root 运行，没有资源上限，也没有 cap-drop / seccomp / read-only；同一项目的所有会话与并发任务共用一个容器。
- 控制台会加载项目目录下的 `settings.json`、`.pi/extensions`、`AGENTS.md`，且没有项目信任确认步骤——不要把来源不可信的工作目录设为项目。MCP 服务器不在此列：它们只来自「设置 → MCP」，项目目录里的 `.pi/mcp.json` 与配置目录里的 `mcp.json` 都不读。
- **自定义 MCP 的 stdio 服务器在控制台宿主机上直接执行**：不在容器内，也不经过 bash 审批与守门模型，因此必须逐条勾选风险确认才能保存。需要 OAuth 登录的 HTTP 服务器请在终端执行 `sentinel mcp login`。
- **Web 搜索会把搜索关键词与 API Key 发送给 Tavily**：请求在控制台进程里直接 HTTPS 发出，不过审批门、也不经过容器；搜索内容对 Tavily 可见。多 Key 明文存本机 `websearch.json`（权限 0600），前端不回显；流水与原始响应留在本机（`websearch.db` 与项目 `evidence/search/`）。
- **资产测绘会把查询内容与 API Key 发送给第三方平台**（FOFA / 360 Quake / 奇安信 Hunter）：查询在控制台进程里直接 HTTPS 发出，不过审批门、也不经过容器，但目标域名、IP 等查询内容对这些平台可见。密钥明文存在本机配置目录的 `assets.json`（权限 0600），前端不回显；查询流水与原始响应留在本机（`assets.db` 与项目 `evidence/asset/`）。若配置了自定义 BaseURL，API Key 与查询内容会发送到该地址，只应填写可信的反向代理。

完整边界与配置见 [packages/web/README.md](packages/web/README.md#安全提示)。

- **发包重放（replayd）在容器内运行，控制台用 `docker exec` 调用它**：服务只监听容器内回环 `127.0.0.1`（端口按容器名推导，被占用时自动换），控制台通过容器内 `curl` 调它的 REST，因此不发布端口、不改容器创建参数，host 与 bridge 两种网络模式都可用；访问 token 由 replayd 自

github_projects.name: pgx
github_projects.description: PGX — Lightweight Postgres for AI agents. Written in Rust. Thousands of isolated databases in one runtime. 🐘
github_projects.description_zh: PGX — 轻量级人工智能智能体Postgre。用Rust编写。数千个孤立数据库，运行于一个运行时。🐘

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: PGX — Lightweight Postgres for AI agents. Written in Rust. Thousands of isolated databases in one runtime. 🐘

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
PGX


  PGX. Postgres for agents. 🐘
  One runtime. Thousands of Postgres databases.



  
  
  
  


```bash
npx pgxdb@latest
```


  One command: PGX installed, database running, connection URL printed.
  No Docker required · Native Mac & Linux · Automatic cleanup



  Open source · Free · v0.1.0 · For disposable databases, not production data


PGX is a database runtime for short-lived Postgres databases: agent
sandboxes, CI and per-PR databases, test and preview environments. One PGX
process holds many isolated databases. Each costs tens of kilobytes of
memory while idle, is created in milliseconds from a sealed template, and
is backed, on a copy-on-write storage backend such as ZFS, by a clone
that starts at a few megabytes whatever the template's size (on a
filesystem without block cloning a branch is a full copy).

PGX speaks the Postgres wire protocol and SQL dialect. Rails, Django,
Prisma, SQLAlchemy and node-postgres run their full migrate → test →
schema-change lifecycles on it unchanged.

PGX is the database engine behind PGRun branches.

> A database should be cheap enough to allocate like an object, not
> provision like a server.

evidence.heading: Why PGX
evidence.text:
Agent workflows, test suites, CI jobs and preview environments create
databases constantly and throw them away minutes or hours later. Giving
each one its own PostgreSQL server costs a process, tens of megabytes and
a cold start every time. Traditional PostgreSQL is built to keep one
database running for years; PGX is built to create one in milliseconds,
use it briefly and delete it.

Instead of

```text
1 database → 1 PostgreSQL server
```

PGX runs

```text
1 PGX runtime → hundreds or thousands of isolated databases
```

Immutable state is shared. Each database pays mainly for what makes it
different.

evidence.heading: At a glance
evidence.text:
```text
~6.2 ms      warm database mint, p50
~70 KB       memory per untouched idle database
~128 KB      memory per idle database that has been queried
1,000        isolated databases on a 4 vCPU / 8 GB VM
128–155 MB   total runtime memory with 1,000 untouched databases
~213 MB      after all 1,000 have been used

10 GB        template
~674 ms      copy-on-write branch ready
~13.6 MB     initial additional physical storage

219 / 231    PostgreSQL src/test/regress byte-exact against PG 18.6 expected output
0            result differences (the other 12 differ in EXPLAIN plan text only)
```

These describe measured configurations and workloads, not a claim that
PGX is faster than PostgreSQL in general. The regression figure is
PostgreSQL's own test suite on one platform under the regress profile
(see Benchmarks), not a compatibility percentage for arbitrary SQL. The detail and the scripts are
under Benchmarks.

evidence.heading: Disposable Postgres
evidence.text:
PGX is built around a different database lifecycle:

```text
sealed template
      ↓
   mint database        milliseconds, copy-on-write
      ↓
agent / CI / test       minutes or hours
      ↓
    discard             dropped a grace period after the last session
```

A database is created from a sealed template without copying it. On
Linux, ZFS block cloning lets a branch share every unchanged block with
its template, so a branch of a 10 GB database is ready in under a second
and starts at about 14 MB of its own storage.

evidence.heading: Built for agents
evidence.text:
A coding agent's database workload looks like this, and many agents do it
at once:

```text
create database → run migrations → change schema → load fixtures
→ run tests → inspect results → throw the database away
```

PGX optimizes for that lifecycle rather than for a long-running
production primary. Every agent, every pull request and every test run
can have its own real Postgres-compatible database.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
The central idea: **share everything immutable, pay for divergence.** It
applies to memory and to storage alike.

- **Shared runtime.** Databases are isolated by name, roles and limits
  inside one process with a thread per connection. A database costs its
  catalog caches, not a server.
- **Shared catalog state.** Databases cloned from the same template share
  identical relation-cache entries. Idle databases are skipped by
  autovacuum.
- **Mint-on-connect.** Connecting to `<prefix><template>__<token>` creates
  that database from a sealed template and connects you to it. A warm pool
  of pre-created spares serves bursts. A janitor drops databases a grace
  period after their last session.
- **Copy-on-write storage.** `file_copy_method = clone` turns database
  creation into ZFS block clones, so a branch shares every unchanged block
  with its template and its cost grows with divergence:

  ```text
  template
  ├── branch A → only changed blocks
  ├── branch B → only changed blocks
  └── branch C → only changed blocks
  ```
- **Limits at every level.** Session, database and runtime memory limits
  inside the engine, connection limits per database, and a Linux cgroup
  around the runtime. Memory-heavy work fails with a PostgreSQL-style
  error instead of taking the host down:

  ```text
  session → database / runtime → Linux cgroup
  ```
- **Machine-readable status.** `pgrust_runtime_status()` returns JSON with
  databases, sessions, memory against limits, and warm-pool and mint
  counters.

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
One command installs PGX, starts it, creates an `app` database and prints its
connection URL. No Docker, Rust or system PostgreSQL; the native distribution
is self-contained and relocatable.

```bash
npx pgxdb@latest
```

```console
PGX is ready.

  postgres://postgres:…@127.0.0.1:5432/app
```

Point `DATABASE_URL` at that URL. `npx pgxdb` with no arguments is `pgx run`;
every other `pgx` command works the same way through npx:

```bash
npx pgxdb url app                      # its connection URL
npx pgxdb ls                           # databases, TTL, expiry, size
npx pgxdb clone app agent-001 --ttl 5m # a 5-minute copy-on-write branch
npx pgxdb --json ls                    # machine-readable output for agents
npx pgxdb stop
```

The binary is downloaded once (SHA-256 verified) into `~/.pgx/dist/<version>`
and reused. `npm install -g pgxdb` puts `pgx` on your PATH for good. Supported:
Apple silicon Macs and Linux (arm64, x86-64). Intel Macs are not supported yet.

Without Node, the shell installer does the same install:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://pgx.dev/install | sh
pgx run
```

Any PostgreSQL client or ORM works against `pgx url <db>`. The full CLI,
install options, integrations (Rails, Node, Python, Go, psql), storage model
and troubleshooting are under [`docs/pgx/local-dev/`](docs/pgx/local-dev/); the
test matrix and release decision are in
[`docs/pgx/local-dev/validation-report.md`](docs/pgx/local-dev/validation-report.md).

evidence.heading: 1. 展示与功能

| 顶部内容（Top Shelf） | 展开全部 App |

|  |  |

evidence.heading: 核心功能
evidence.text:
- **主屏幕**：5 列 16:9 圆角图标，选中时弹性放大、倾斜并带高光和投影。右上角显示时间、网络与可选头像；时间支持 12 / 24 小时制，也可改成左上角大时钟或隐藏。
- **Liquid Glass Dock**：第一排应用放在液态玻璃 Dock 中，下一排露出上沿。玻璃模糊、边缘折射和高光会按当前背景预先生成，低配电视可改用更省性能的样式。
- **顶部内容**：选中 Dock 中的云视听小电视或斗鱼时，上半屏轮播对应的热门内容。数据来自服务公开的网页接口，使用前需要安装对应的 TV 版 App。
- **主屏幕设置**：仿 tvOS 的分组布局，可分别调整时钟、聚焦动画、控制中心样式、背景、相框、开机动画、头像和桌面守护。
- **最近打开自动置顶（可开启）**：首次安装及升级后默认关闭；开启后成功打开一个 App，它会移到第一位，其他图标保持相对顺序。可在「主屏幕设置 → App」关闭，之后固定使用当前排序，长按「编辑主屏幕」可自行调整。
- **编辑、文件夹与删除**：长按图标可移动、放入文件夹或删除。电视预装 App 也可用 `pm uninstall --user 0` 从当前用户空间移除，并可在设置中恢复；系统运行必需组件受到保护。
- **控制中心**：遥控器返回键或右上角按钮打开，提供网络、待机、关机、重启、释放内存、相框、设置、亮度、音量和 HDMI 输入源。低配机型可切换成深色面板。
- **背景与手机上传**：支持必应每日风景、360 壁纸、Wallhaven 全年龄二次元、公有领域名画、纯色渐变、手机相册照片和自定义图片链接。手机扫码页面还支持上传头像、开机视频和设置页背景。
- **相框与航拍屏保**：照片全屏轮播，画面缓慢平移缩放，时间文字定时移动以减少 OLED 烙印；也可在线播放 Apple TV 航拍视频，支持左右键切换，断网时回到照片。
- **HDMI 输入源上屏**：在控制中心把常用 HDMI 口固定到主屏幕，按一下即可切换。
- **软件更新与投屏**：每 6 小时检查 Tigris 和 [MiracastReceiver](https://github.com/weekdayjast/MiracastReceiver) 的正式版。更新前验证包名、系统版本、递增版本号和签名；不会自动卸载、不清数据、不接受降级。电视系统仍可能要求一次安装来源授权或每次确认。
- **内存清理**：支持定时清理和待机清理，保留名单可在设置中修改。

evidence.heading: 2. 安装指南
evidence.text:
> [!CAUTION]
> **不要停用或卸载电视原厂桌面。** 尤其是小米 / Redmi 的 `com.mitv.tvhome`（PatchWall）；强行停用后，部分电视会开机黑屏，只能通过 ADB 恢复。正确做法是保留原桌面，使用 Tigris 的默认 HOME 或桌面守护。
>
> **手动修改前先记录原配置。** 至少保存默认 HOME、屏保、无障碍服务和通知监听的原值。`install.sh` 会自动保存快照；手动安装请自行记录，缺少记录时不要猜包名。
>
> **只在自己的局域网开启 ADB。** 不要把电视调试端口暴露到公网。
>
> **签名不一致时不要直接卸载。** `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` 表示新 APK 与原包签名不同；直接卸载会丢失设置和授权。应先找到原签名密钥重新签名。

Tigris 官方包要求 **Android 9 / API 28 或更高**，不支持 LG webOS、三星 Tizen、华为鸿蒙智慧屏等非 Android 系统。

evidence.heading: 2.2 让 AI Agent 安装（推荐）
evidence.text:
适合 Codex、Claude Code，以及能在电脑上执行命令的 WorkBuddy、豆包电脑版 / 工作版、千问电脑版、Trae 等。把下面整段发给 Agent，并替换电视 IP：

```text
请帮我把开源电视桌面 Tigris 装到我的电视上，并设置为默认桌面或启用桌面守护。
电视 IP：<电视IP>
保持 ADB 常开：要

安装说明：
https://github.com/lesnolie/Tigris/blob/main/AGENTS.md
打不开时：
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lesnolie/Tigris/main/AGENTS.md

请先完整阅读安装说明，再在我的电脑上亲自运行命令，不要只把步骤告诉我。
需要我在电视上操作时请提醒我。
不要未经确认重启、待机、关机、卸载旧版、清空配置或停用原厂桌面。
签名不匹配时先寻找原签名密钥，不要自动卸载。
请先记录默认 HOME、屏保、无障碍服务和通知监听，安装后分别验证安装、主页键、待机唤醒和开机。
没有实际测过的项目不要写成通过。

最后把下面命令的原始输出贴给我，每条 adb 都加 -s <电视IP>:5555：
- adb shell cmd package resolve-activity --brief -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME
- adb shell settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services
- 按主页键并等待两秒后：adb shell "dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus"
```

Agent 必须能在这台电脑上实际运行命令。手机聊天或网页版如果只能回复步骤，就不能完成安装。

验收时看按主页键后的 `mCurrentFocus` 是否包含 `com.leslie.tvhome`。守护版可能仍把原厂桌面保留为 HOME resolver，因此不能只看 `resolve-activity`；应以前台窗口和主页键结果为准。

evidence.heading: 2.4 手动安装
evidence.text: 这里的 **Windows** 指电脑系统，**PowerShell** 是 Windows 自带的命令行工具，两者不是互斥选项。PowerShell 中的 `curl` 可能是 `Invoke-WebRequest` 的别名，所以下载文件时写 `curl.exe`；Python 通常写 `python`，不是 `python3`。macOS / Linux 则使用 `curl` 和 `python3`。后面的 `adb` 命令在两个系统上相同。

evidence.heading: 第二步：下载并安装
evidence.text:
索尼、小米、原生 Android TV 等一般使用标准版。发布的 APK 均带版本号（如 `Tigris-v2.0.6.apk`），可在 [最新 Release](https://github.com/lesnolie/Tigris/releases/latest) 手动下载，也可使用校验 SHA-256 的下载助手：

Windows PowerShell：

```powershell
curl.exe -fsSL -o download-release.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lesnolie/Tigris/main/tools/download-release.py
$apk = python .\download-release.py standard
adb -s 192.168.1.20:5555 install -r $apk
```

macOS / Linux：

```bash
curl -fsSL -o download-release.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lesnolie/Tigris/main/tools/download-release.py
apk=$(python3 download-release.py standard)
adb -s 192.168.1.20:5555 install -r "$apk"
```

TCL / 雷鸟国行固件通常拒绝直接安装，也拒绝声明 HOME 的标准包，需要使用守护版和电视自带的「多屏互动」：

```powershell
curl.exe -fsSL -o download-release.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lesnolie/Tigris/main/tools/download-release.py
$apk = python .\download-release.py guard
curl.exe -fsSL -o tcast-push.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lesnolie/Tigris/main/tools/tcast-push.py
python .\tcast-push.py 192.168.1.20 $apk
```

macOS / Linux：

```bash
curl -fsSL -o download-release.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lesnolie/Tigris/main/tools/download-release.py
apk=$(python3 download-release.py guard)
curl -fsSL -o tcast-push.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lesnolie/Tigris/main/tools/tcast-push.py
python3 tcast-push.py 192.168.1.20 "$apk"
```

运行推送脚本时，电视角落会出现「多屏互动：正在发起应用推送」，用遥控器选择 **同意**。如果电脑防火墙询问，允许脚本访问局域网。

遇到安装失败先停止，处理错误后再继续授权。`INSTALL_FAILED_OLDER_SDK` 表示系统低于最低要求；`INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` 表示签名不一致，不要直接卸载。

evidence.heading: What is Hermes Agent?
evidence.text:
[Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) is the self-improving AI agent from Nous Research. It writes skills from experience and keeps improving them as it works, remembers what matters across sessions, and runs where you are: the terminal, the Hermes Desktop app, Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal and more, all through one gateway. You can bring any model (Nous Portal, OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, your own endpoint) and run it on a laptop, a $5 VPS or serverless infrastructure.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

evidence.heading: A lean core, with plugins at the edges
evidence.text:
The Hermes core keeps the parts every user needs: the agent loop, memory, skills, the gateway, model routing and the tool runtime. Everything specific to one product, one vendor or one hobby belongs in a **plugin**, which you install when you want it and which ships on its own schedule.

That gives you:

- **Smaller, faster installs.** You don't download a Spotify client to run a coding agent.
- **Fixes without waiting for a release.** A plugin ships a fix as soon as it's reviewed. It doesn't wait for the next Hermes version.
- **A clear owner for each integration.** Vendor plugins live with the vendors who build them, community plugins with their authors, and Nous's own plugins live here.

evidence.heading: The plugin catalog
evidence.text:
The [**Hermes plugin catalog**](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins) is the reviewed index of everything you can install: model providers, memory providers, messaging platforms, Desktop extensions, voice, web and automation tools. It has hundreds of entries from Nous, vendors and the community. Each entry is **pinned to a reviewed commit**, so what you install is exactly what was reviewed, and an update moves you only when a new pin passes review.

```bash
hermes plugins search            # browse the catalog
hermes plugins info spotify      # what it does, what it needs, which commit
hermes plugins install spotify   # install at the reviewed pin
hermes plugins update spotify    # follow the catalog to the next reviewed pin
```

Hermes Desktop has the same catalog under **Capabilities → Plugins**.

Catalog entries come in two tiers:

| Tier | Who maintains it | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **official** | Nous Research | **This repo**, one directory per plugin |
| **community** | Vendors and independent authors | Their own repos, reviewed when they enter the catalog |

evidence.heading: The plugins
evidence.text: Home Assistant hermes plugins install homeassistant A gateway platform plus four tools. Hermes watches your Home Assistant event bus, reacts to the state changes you care about, controls devices over the REST API, and replies as Home Assistant notifications. Cron jobs can deliver straight to your phone with deliver=homeassistant. ha_list_entities · ha_get_state · ha_list_services · ha_call_service Spotify hermes plugins install spotify Seven tools over the Spotify Web API: playback, Spotify Connect devices, the queue, search, playlists, albums and your library, plus hermes spotify login for a loopback PKCE login with your own Spotify developer app. Playback control needs Premium. spotify_playback · spotify_devices · spotify_queue · spotify_search · spotify_playlists · spotify_albums · spotify_library Claude Subscription DirectSDK experimental hermes plugins install claude-subscription-directsdk A model provider that runs Hermes turns on your Claude Pro or Max subscription through the official Claude Code CLI, with no separate API key or per-token bill. Hermes keeps its own agent loop, tools, approvals and compaction; the plugin drives the logged-in claude binary as a request-scoped model client, and refuses cleanly with an install hint when Claude Code is missing. Pick it in hermes model → Claude Subscription DirectSDK (Experimental) Memory Wiki hermes plugins install hermes-memory-wiki A dashboard and Desktop tab that turns your local session history into browsable subject pages and daily logs, plus a read-only audi

evidence.heading: Already used one of these?
evidence.text:
Most plugins here used to live somewhere else: Home Assistant and Spotify were built into Hermes core and then briefly had their own repos, Langfuse shipped bundled with core as `observability/langfuse`, the Singularity/Apptainer terminal backend and the Camofox browser backend were built into core, MCP Serve was core's `hermes mcp serve`, and the rest each had a standalone `NousResearch/hermes-*` repo. **Except for MCP Serve, you don't need to do anything.**

- **You used the built-in Home Assistant, Spotify, Langfuse, Singularity or Camofox backend:** `hermes update`, or the first start after updating, installs the plugin from the catalog with your existing config, env vars and login.
- **You installed it from the catalog:** the catalog now points here, so `hermes plugins update <name>` moves your install to this repo and keeps your files.
- **You used the built-in `hermes import-agent`:** profiles that registered an import for `--sync` get the `agent-importers` plugin on update; anywhere else, running `hermes import-agent` prints the one-line install (`hermes plugins install agent-importers`).
- **You used `hermes claw migrate` (OpenClaw):** it now comes with the same plugin. After `hermes plugins install agent-importers`, both `hermes import-agent openclaw` and the old `hermes claw migrate` / `hermes claw cleanup` work with the same flags.
- **You ran `hermes mcp serve`:** install with `hermes plugins install mcp-serve` and change your MCP client's args from `["mcp", "serve"]` to `["mcp-serve"]`. MCP clients are configured outside Hermes, so this one is not installed for you.
- **You installed it by URL** (for example `hermes plugins install NousResearch/hermes-homeassistant`): reinstall once from the catalog with `hermes plugins install <name> --force` to follow fu

evidence.heading: Repository layout
evidence.text:
```
hermes-official-plugins/
├── assets/                         # README and catalog art
├── homeassistant/                  # one self-contained plugin per directory
│   ├── plugin.yaml                 #   manifest: name, tools, env vars, Hermes version
│   ├── __init__.py                 #   register(ctx)
│   ├── pyproject.toml              #   plugin dependencies
│   └── tests/                      #   the plugin's own suite
├── blender/                        # portable plugins: plugin.json + mcp.json + skills/
├── accent-picker/                  # Desktop plugins: plugin.yaml + desktop/plugin.js
└── ...
```

Each directory is a complete Hermes plugin. The catalog installs one by `repo` + `subdir` at a pinned commit, and Hermes fetches only that directory (a blobless sparse clone), so installing Spotify never downloads Home Assistant.

evidence.heading: Try it in 30 seconds
evidence.text:
```sh
# 1. Point Hycli at any website and describe your goal (prepares reads & writes; zero live mutations)
hycli prepare https://your-website.example --intent "Search posts, save drafts, and publish articles"

# 2. See every prepared read, write, and multi-step workflow
hycli describe your-website

# 3. Run read actions immediately
hycli your-website search-posts --query "release notes"

# 4. Enable writes once for this CLI when you're ready to create, edit, or delete
hycli writes your-website allow
hycli your-website create-draft --title "Hello from Hycli" --body "Automated from my terminal."
