evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: All your machines, one app. For you and your AI agents: agent sessions, desktops, files, logs and GitHub across your Macs, Linux and Windows machines, with an MCP server.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Muxin

One app for all your machines, run by you or by your AI agents.
muxin.dev · free and open source (Apache-2.0)


  
  


Point it at the machines you own (a Mac Studio under the desk, a NUC, a Linux box, a few MacBooks, a Windows laptop) and Muxin becomes the hub for all of them:

- **Agent sessions:** Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Amp, Pi or a shell on any machine, in a real terminal, still running after you close the app.
- **Boxes:** hand a task to an agent that works on it by itself, in a container of its own on one of your machines. A box pauses when it's quiet and picks up where it left off when you ask it more.
- **Desktops:** see a Linux machine's screen live and use it, beside an agent's terminal or in its own window.
- **Files and clipboard:** copy files and folders between any two machines, and copy on your Mac to paste on a machine (and back).
- **GitHub:** your inbox, repositories, issues and pull requests, with one click to hand an issue to an agent on the machine you pick.
- **Self-hosted runners:** which runners are working, idle or offline, which jobs no runner can take, and installing, starting, stopping or removing runners.
- **Health:** CPU, memory, disk and uptime, and a plain answer when a machine is offline or unreachable.

Agents can also **borrow a machine as a work environment**: an [agent workspace](#agent-workspaces) is a persistent folder (optionally a git checkout) on one of your machines where an agent runs commands, edits files and syncs code.

- **Native and fast.** The window is built with [GPUI](https://www.gpui.rs), the GPU-accelerated UI framework behind the Zed editor. It runs on macOS, Linux and Windows.
- **Agent-first.** Every capability is available as an MCP server (`muxin mcp`) and as scriptable commands with

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Download the app from the [latest release](https://github.com/LumaryLabsLLC/muxin/releases/latest):

- **macOS** 12 or later, Apple silicon and Intel: `Muxin-<version>-macos.dmg`. Open it and drag Muxin to Applications. It's signed and notarized.
- **Linux** with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36, openSUSE Tumbleweed, RHEL 10 and later), for Intel and AMD (`x86_64`) or Arm (`aarch64`):
  - Debian and Ubuntu: `Muxin-<version>-linux-x86_64.deb`, then `sudo apt install ./Muxin-<version>-linux-x86_64.deb`.
  - Fedora, openSUSE and RHEL: `Muxin-<version>-linux-x86_64.rpm`, then `sudo dnf install ./Muxin-<version>-linux-x86_64.rpm` (or `zypper install`).
  - Arch: `yay -S muxin-bin` from the [AUR](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/muxin-bin), or `Muxin-<version>-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` with `sudo pacman -U`.
  - Any distribution: `Muxin-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage`. Make it executable and run it; it needs no FUSE 2.
  - Or `Muxin-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`: unpack it and run `./Muxin/install.sh`, which installs it for you, no root needed.
- **Windows 11**: `Muxin-<version>-windows-x64-setup.exe`, or `windows-arm64` on Windows on Arm. The installer isn't signed yet, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC": click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

Or with [Homebrew](https://brew.sh), on macOS and Linux:

```sh
brew install --cask lumarylabsllc/tap/muxin
```

`SHA256SUMS.txt` in each release has the files' checksums.

Muxin tells you when a new version is out: the sidebar says so, and About shows how to update the copy you have (with Homebrew or the AUR, or the new file to download). It asks GitHub for the latest release when it opens and twice a day; turn that off in **Settings › General › Updates**. `muxin updates` checks from a termin

evidence.heading: Build from source
evidence.text:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/LumaryLabsLLC/muxin && cd muxin
cargo build --release --workspace
./target/release/muxin            # opens the window
```

`--workspace` also builds Muxin's agent for this computer, which the app sets up on it. For your other machines' platforms, `./scripts/build-agents.sh` builds every agent into `dist/agents` (it needs zig and cargo-zigbuild).

Requirements:

- A recent stable Rust (edition 2024).
- On macOS, Xcode (GPUI compiles Metal shaders).
- On Linux, GPUI's system libraries. On Ubuntu/Debian:
  `sudo apt install libxkbcommon-dev libxkbcommon-x11-dev libwayland-dev libvulkan-dev libfontconfig-dev libx11-xcb-dev libxcb1-dev`.

For servers, CI boxes and agent machines there's a headless build with no GUI libraries: just the CLI and the MCP server.

```sh
cargo build --release --no-default-features
```

There's nothing else to set up. Fonts and icons are compiled into the binary.

To run `muxin` from a terminal, use **Settings › General › Command line › Install**, or `muxin shell-command install`. On macOS it links `/usr/local/bin/muxin` to the app (macOS asks for your password when that folder needs it), on Linux `~/.local/bin/muxin`, and on Windows it adds Muxin's folder to your user PATH. `muxen`, its name from before, runs it too. `muxin shell-command remove` takes it out again.

To get a real app with the Muxin icon:

- **macOS:** `./scripts/bundle-macos.sh` builds `dist/Muxin.app`, signed with the Developer ID when it's in your keychain. Drag it to Applications. Agents can still use the binary inside it: `Muxin.app/Contents/MacOS/muxin mcp`.
- **Linux:** `./scripts/package-linux.sh` makes a tarball; its `install.sh` puts Muxin in `~/.local` with an entry in your app menu.
- **Windows:** `scripts\package-windows.ps1` makes t

evidence.heading: Use it from AI agents
evidence.text:
Muxin ships an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Print setup snippets that point at your binary:

```sh
muxin mcp --print-config
```

**Claude Code**

```sh
claude mcp add muxin -- /path/to/muxin mcp
```

**Codex** (`~/.codex/config.toml`)

```toml
[mcp_servers.muxin]
command = "/path/to/muxin"
args = ["mcp"]
```

**Other MCP clients** (Claude Desktop, Cursor, …)

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "muxin": { "command": "/path/to/muxin", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

Add `"--demo"` after `"mcp"` to let an agent practice on the simulated machines.

The MCP server has these tools:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | Counts, GitHub state, every machine, and the `attention` list. Start here. |
| `get_machine` | One machine's resources, runners and diagnostics, with hints. |
| `list_runners` | Runners, optionally filtered by machine or state. |
| `list_jobs` | Queued and running jobs, including which ones no runner can take. |
| `check_machines` | Runs the read-only machine check over ssh now. |
| `add_machine`, `remove_machine`, `rename_machine` | Edit `config.toml`. Nothing on the machine changes, except that `remove_machine` turns off a direct connection from this app. |
| `connect_machine` | Disconnect from a machine (`connected: false`) or connect again. Its sessions keep running there. |
| `machine_ports` | What's listening on a machine: ports, programs or containers, and web servers' page titles. |
| `machine_processes`, `process_signal` | A machine's busiest processes and its GPUs; stop or kill one. |
| `run_on_machines` | Runs one shell command on several machines at once, with each one's output and exit status. |
| `wake_machine` | Wakes a machine that's asleep or off (Wake on LAN). |

evidence.heading: How checks and installs work
evidence.text:

evidence.heading: 🤖 Grok Bot 是什么
evidence.text:
Grok Bot 是 xAI 和 Cursor 在 2026-08-11 联合推出的 AI 队友（beta）。每个 bot 有名字、有岗位，共用一台一直开着的云电脑（浏览器、文件、终端都有）。你可以派活、让它定时跑 **Routine**、教它 **Skill**，也可以从 [模板市场](https://x.ai/bot/marketplace) 一键导入别人做好的 bot。

它和聊天助手 Grok、编码命令行 Grok Build 是三个不同的产品。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: A 2007 Nokia can't search Google anymore, so I gave it Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok. J2ME app for Nokia S40/S60 + tiny Go server.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
> **Formerly Claude S40.** The project was called *Claude S40* up to phone
> app 0.10.x / server 0.7.x, while it only talked to Claude. Since it also
> speaks to OpenAI, Gemini and Grok it is called **AIKON** (Nokia spelled
> backwards). The repository moved from `emir/claude-s40` to `emir/AIKON`
> (GitHub redirects the old address); the Java package and server names
> keep the old name.



**Today's AI on a 2007 Nokia.** AIKON is an AI chat client for
Nokia Series 40 and Symbian S60 phones (Java ME, CLDC 1.1 / MIDP 2.0), plus
the small Go server it talks to. Pick a model per chat (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini or Grok),
type on the keypad, get the answer on a 240x320 screen: with today's news,
weather and exchange rates from web search, long answers you can page
through, and a UI in Turkish, English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Russian or
Indonesian. Tested on the Nokia 6300 (S40) and
the Nokia E63 (S60 QWERTY).

**Video** (still as Claude S40): [on a Nokia 6300, on X](https://x.com/EmirKarsiyakali/status/2104183718483018026)

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
**On the phone**

- **Pick the model per chat**: first the provider (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini,
  Grok), then one of the models the server offers; switch in the middle of
  a chat with Options > Model. Every reply is labelled with its model.
- **Chat**: your messages in bubbles, replies full width, day headings
  ("Today", "Yesterday"), and a typing indicator that counts the seconds.
  Replies keep their paragraphs and lists (dots, numbers, hanging indent);
  an unsent draft waits in the input bar.
- **Web search** for news, weather, rates: the model searches on the server
  with its provider's search tool; the phone's 2007 browser is not involved. Sources are listed under the
  reply.
- **Reading mode** (key 7): one reply full width, page by page, whole lines
  only, page number and progress line. It keeps its place when you change
  the text size (key 9) or load the rest.
- **Long replies in parts**: "0 · Show the rest" fetches the next part
  from the server for free; the model is not asked again.
- **Message actions**: select a message with 1/3, press the centre key:
  shorten, explain more simply, translate, ask about it, open it in the
  editor. They only fill in the editor; nothing is sent until you press
  Send.
- **Earlier chats** from the server, continue any of them; **pin** the ones
  you want to keep at the top (kept until unpinned), **delete** or **search**
  all chats (no Turkish letters needed: "sise" finds "şişe"); optional
  offline copy of the last chat.
- **Save to phone**: a reply as a .txt file (memory card if there is one),
  readable later without the network under "Saved".
- **Calendar and to-do**: ask "add to my calendar: dentist tomorrow at 3"
  and the reply carries a ready entry; the centre key opens a prefilled
  form, and only your "Save" wri

|---|---|---|---|

Start-up animation: [docs/images/splash.gif](docs/images/splash.gif).

> Independent side project. Not made, endorsed or supported by Anthropic,
> OpenAI, Google, xAI or Nokia. See [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md).

Tested on a **Nokia 6300 (RM-217, firmware V06.60)**, and on a **Nokia E63**
(Symbian S60 3rd Edition FP1, 320x240, QWERTY, over WLAN; see
[docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md#5-install-the-app-on-the-phone)). Other Series 40
phones (CLDC 1.1 / MIDP 2.0, 240x320) may work but are untested.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
```
Nokia (Java ME app) --HTTPS: TLS 1.0, RSA, no SNI, cert from YOUR private CA--> claude-s40-server --HTTPS--> Claude / OpenAI / Gemini / Grok APIs
                                                                                     |
                                                                              SQLite (Docker volume)
```

A 2007 phone cannot speak modern HTTPS: the Nokia 6300 offers only TLS 1.0
with RSA key exchange, sends no SNI, and its root store stops around 2008.
Public clouds (including Cloudflare) refuse that handshake. So the server
terminates TLS itself with a certificate from a private root CA that you
put on the phone once. Details and measurements: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

evidence.heading: What's inside
evidence.text:
| Path | What |
|---|---|
| [`app/`](app/) | The phone app: CLDC 1.1 / MIDP 2.0 MIDlet, ~220 KB JAR, UI in eight languages (see Features). Reproducible build with package checks. |
| [`server/`](server/) | One Go binary / Docker image (~7 MB): phone-facing TLS, chat backend (Claude via the official `anthropic-sdk-go`; OpenAI, Gemini, Grok over plain HTTPS), SQLite, pairing, admin API bound to localhost. |
| [`docs/`](docs/) | [SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md) (step by step), [ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) (protocol, TLS, design). |

evidence.heading: Get it
evidence.text:
```
git clone https://github.com/emir/AIKON.git
cd aikon
```

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
Full guide: **[docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md)**. In short:

1. A Docker host with a public IPv4 and TCP 443 (a $4-6/month VPS is enough).
2. `server/scripts/pki.sh ca ~/.config/claude-s40/pki` and
   `server/scripts/pki.sh server ~/.config/claude-s40/pki <server-ip>`.
3. `server/deploy/push.sh root@<server-ip> --execute` (starts in test mode, no API cost).
4. `echo GATEWAY_URL=https://<server-ip> > app/app.local.properties && make -C app`,
   then install `app/dist/AIKON.jad/.jar` on the phone.
5. Put the root CA on the phone (`server/deploy/serve-ca.sh`, compare the fingerprint).
6. On the phone the setup wizard walks through the connection test and
   pairing; approve the code with
   `server/deploy/admin.sh root@<server-ip> pair <code>`.
7. `server/deploy/set-key.sh root@<server-ip>` (Claude; add `openai`, `gemini`
   or `xai` for the others), then
   `S40_MOCK=0 S40_MODELS=... server/deploy/push.sh root@<server-ip> --execute` to go live.

evidence.heading: axuse — browser & computer use, done right
evidence.text:
**Accessibility-first browser and computer use for agent harnesses.** One MCP
server plugs into Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Antigravity, or any
MCP-capable host. Zero dependencies (Node ≥ 22). Windows desktop driver is
verified; macOS desktop control is available as an explicit opt-in with
native TCC permission checks; Linux desktop control runs over X11/XWayland
(XTEST input + capture + EWMH windows, zero extra packages).

The design is distilled from the two best implementations of this problem —
OpenAI's Codex Chrome extension and the ZCode harness — and exists to prove a
point: **a screenshot loop is not the right interface for a machine**. The
DOM tree, the accessibility tree, and CDP are. axuse instruments the target
instead of photographing it.

**Not a developer?** You don't need anything below. In the Claude desktop
app, download `axuse.mcpb` from [ax-use.com](https://ax-use.com) and
double-click it. In ChatGPT's Codex app, Claude Code, Cursor or any other
agent, paste the [install prompt](https://ax-use.com/install.md) and the
agent sets axuse up for you. See the
[non-developer guide](docs/non-developer-onboarding.md).

evidence.heading: Proven in production
evidence.text:
axuse is maintained by **CTOL Digital Solutions**
([ctol.digital](https://ctol.digital)), a leading AI, Strategy and IT
consultancy. This work has been tested and used at large scale across many
client engagements. CTOL Digital Solutions holds the copyright of all the
code.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
You need **Node.js 22+** and a Chromium-family browser (Chrome, Edge,
Chromium, or Chrome for Testing; found automatically, or set
`AXUSE_BROWSER=/path/to/chrome`). On a bare server with no browser and no
sudo: `node src/cli.js install-browser` provisions a pinned Chrome for
Testing under `~/.cache/axuse` — nothing else: axuse has no npm dependencies.

**1. Get it and check the environment**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ctoldigital/axuse.git
cd axuse
node src/cli.js doctor        # finds a browser, launches it, takes a snapshot
```

For a daily Chrome/Edge session, use the guided bridge setup. It registers the
native host, opens the extensions page, prints the exact folder to load, and
can print your harness configuration in the same command:

```bash
node src/cli.js setup --browser chrome --harness codex
```

After clicking **Load unpacked** once, verify the connection with:

```bash
node src/cli.js bridge verify
```

**2. Add it to your harness** (use your absolute path to `src/cli.js`)

```bash
# Codex
codex mcp add axuse -- node /abs/path/axuse/src/cli.js mcp

# Claude Code
claude mcp add --scope user axuse -- node /abs/path/axuse/src/cli.js mcp

# OpenCode, Antigravity, any other MCP host: print the config block to paste
node src/cli.js print-config --harness opencode   # or agy | generic
```

**3. Ask for something in the browser**

> Open https://example.com, find the "More information" link and tell me
> where it goes.

The agent calls `ax_open`, reads the accessibility snapshot, and acts on
element refs like `[ref=e7]`. Each action returns only what changed.

**Optional settings** (environment variables for the MCP server)

| variable | effect |
|---|---|
| `AXUSE_SERVER_MODE` | `auto` (default): on a display-less Linux server, boot a private Xvfb and

evidence.heading: Servers, no desktop (Ubuntu server lane)
evidence.text:
axuse runs under agent CLIs (codex, claude code, opencode) on headless
Ubuntu servers. Challenge/anti-bot pages check *is this a headless browser?*
first, so server mode never uses `--headless`: it boots a private Xvfb and
runs Chrome **fully headed** on it — real headed build, no headless
fingerprint (verified live against Turnstile: `ax_solve_captcha` solves on a
server with no desktop, and the slider engine's human-curve drags land
10/10). Beyond headed-vs-headless, server mode covers **persona
coherence** (`AXUSE_TIMEZONE`/`AXUSE_LANG` matching the egress persona,
`AXUSE_DISPLAY_SIZE=random` fleet diversity, `--disable-blink-features=
AutomationControlled` so `navigator.webdriver` stays `false` at the source)
and fleet hygiene (zombie-Xvfb sweep). Solver plugins that need vision call
a multimodal model through any OpenAI-compatible API; keys come from env
vars or an owner-only secrets file. One-time setup, systemd wiring, env
reference and scale notes: [`docs/server-mode.md`](docs/server-mode.md) —
and `node src/cli.js doctor` verifies the whole lane (it prints the measured
anti-bot posture and persona).

evidence.heading: Benchmark
evidence.text:
On 16 server-scored browser tasks, run in the same harness (Codex CLI) with
the same model against Codex's own Chrome extension and
[browser-use](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) 0.13:

| | axuse | Codex + Chrome extension | browser-use |
|---|---|---|---|
| tasks passed | 28/28 | 27/27 | 27/27 |
| median time per task | **17 s** | 26 s | 56 s |
| tokens, all runs | **4.7M** | 9.8M | 8.8M |
| median tool calls | **5** | 7 | 12 |

Accuracy tied on those tasks. A harder 7-task extension (checkout flow,
virtualized grid, date pickers, signup errors, nested iframes, file upload,
local dev app) has been run once so far: axuse 7/7; Codex + Chrome failed 2
by stopping to ask for confirmation; browser-use failed 1. Method, anti-cheat
rules and how to reproduce: [`bench/suite/README.md`](bench/suite/README.md).
Install footprint and setup comparison: [`bench/suite/EASE.md`](bench/suite/EASE.md).

evidence.heading: Install into a harness
evidence.text:
```bash
node src/cli.js print-config --harness codex       # or claude-code | opencode | agy | generic
```

- **Codex** — append the printed `[mcp_servers.axuse]` block to `~/.codex/config.toml`
- **Claude Code** — `claude mcp add --scope user axuse -- node <path>/src/cli.js mcp`
- **OpenCode** — merge the printed `mcp` block into `opencode.json`
- **Antigravity / any MCP host** — the printed `mcpServers` block

Verify the environment: `node src/cli.js doctor`.

The model-facing usage contract lives in [`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md) — point your
harness's skill system (or system prompt) at it.

evidence.heading: Architecture
evidence.text:
```
harness (Codex / Claude Code / OpenCode / Antigravity / …)
        │  MCP over stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0) — the universal integration layer
        ▼
src/mcp/ — thin, stateless-per-call adapter (hand-rolled, zero deps)
        │  one frozen command contract (src/core/commands.js)

evidence.text:
Code graph and memory for your coding agents, in one Rust program.


  
  
  
  



  Graphicle maps your repository into a code graph, remembers your project's docs, decisions and past agent sessions,
  and gives your coding agent cited excerpts from both: the exact files and lines. It runs on your machine: no API key needed, no account, no telemetry.
  Works with Claude Code · Cursor · Codex · VS Code · Claude Desktop · any MCP client



  Quick start · How it works · Benchmarks · Docs · Coming from Graphify? · Discussions

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text: ```sh brew install graphicle-ai/tap/graphicle cd your-repo graphicle setup ``` No Homebrew? curl -fsSL https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh · [Release archives](https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases) · [Other ways to install](docs/install.md) Windows: a preview build for x86-64, not yet code-signed ([Windows (preview)](docs/install.md#windows-preview)). `graphicle setup` indexes the repository, builds its code graph and connects the coding agents it finds. It also turns on session capture, adds a two-line section to `AGENTS.md` (unless Claude Code is the only agent) and installs Git hooks that keep the project current. It lists every file it changes and backs each one up first; `graphicle disconnect` undoes it all. Then ask your agent to *"use graphicle to find where failed requests are retried"*, or ask from the terminal: ```console $ graphicle ask "where is tax added to prices?" With no model configured, ask shows the evidence; graphicle config set model anthropic (or openai, ollama) adds written answers. evidence.heading: Start here
evidence.text:
| You want to | Run |
|---|---|
| Give your coding agent the code graph and your project's memory | `graphicle setup` in the repository |
| Ask a question from the terminal | `graphicle ask "how are failed requests retried?"` |
| Browse the graph, the sources and the memory | `graphicle open` |
| See what a change to a symbol touches | `graphicle graph extract . --code-only`, then `graphicle graph affected "retry()"` |
| Check that everything works | `graphicle doctor` |
| Undo everything setup did | `graphicle disconnect` |
| Move from Graphify, or run a server for a team | [Moving from Graphify](docs/migrate-from-graphify.md) · [Team server](docs/team.md) |

evidence.heading: Why Graphicle
evidence.text:
- **Native and fast.** One Rust program. On 13 codebases, Graphicle's 0.1.1 memory engine (a pre-release build) took 3.0 to 22.7 times less time than Graphify 0.9.91 in all 39 measurements (code-only extract, priming update and update with no change, on the same machine with 3 CPUs and 8 workers each). The graphs differ slightly: node counts within 4.7%, edge counts within 2.0% ([speed table](docs/benchmarks.md#speed-on-13-codebases-against-graphify-0991)). A later pre-release build with 0.1.1's memory changes, whose graphs also differ from Graphify's, used less peak memory than Graphify 0.9.91 in all 39 measurements, from 0.29 to 0.97 times Graphify's figure ([memory table](docs/benchmarks.md#peak-memory-against-graphify-0991)).
- **Cited context, within a budget you set.** Your agent asks Graphicle and gets the relevant code, docs and decisions as cited excerpts, within a token budget you set. In our tests it tied grep on finding code, and we do not claim it saves tokens ([what we measured](#benchmarks)).
- **Answers you can check.** Every excerpt names its file and lines. Memories an agent proposes wait for your approval.
- **One program, not a stack.** The code graph, the memory, one MCP server, the web app and the command line come in one install, with one SQLite file. No Python, Docker or database server.
- **Local and private.** No account and no telemetry. Your code and data leave your machine only when you ask. The only automatic request is a daily check for a new release, which `GRAPHICLE_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` turns off.

evidence.heading: What it does
evidence.text:
- **Code graph.** Files, functions, classes, calls and imports, parsed with tree-sitter and no model. `graphicle graph` searches it, explains a symbol,
  traces a path and exports an interactive HTML graph. After `graphicle graph extract . --code-only`, `graphicle graph affected "retry()"` lists what depends on a symbol.
- **Project memory.** Docs (Markdown, PDF, Office, HTML), reviewed decisions and procedures, and past Claude Code and Codex sessions, searchable alongside the code.
- **Cited context on a budget.** `graphicle context` and the MCP tools return excerpts with their sources, within a token budget, without calling a model.
- **One MCP server.** `graphicle mcp` serves the code-graph tools, under Graphify's tool names such as `query_graph`, `get_neighbors` and `shortest_path`, next to the memory tools. With `--pull-requests` it also serves the pull-request tools `list_prs`, `get_pr_impact` and `triage_prs`, which use the GitHub CLI ([MCP](docs/mcp.md)).
- **Memory tied to your code.** Reviewed memories are tied to the functions they are about: a memory goes stale when that code changes, and edits elsewhere in the file usually leave it current ([the exact rule](crates/graphicle/README.md#memory-anchored-to-code-symbols)). Mentions of code in your docs are linked to the definitions they name (`graphicle call graph.doc_links` lists them).
- **Across repositories.** Recall can span the repositories of a workspace: `graphicle context --workspace`, or [the workspace MCP endpoint](docs/mcp.md#several-projects-in-one-connection).
- **Always current.** Before each answer Graphicle syncs the few files you changed; Git hooks sync after each commit, merge and checkout.
- **Sessions carry over.** Session capture keeps each finished turn, and once you have reviewed memories

evidence.heading: Works with your agents
evidence.text:
`graphicle setup` connects every client it finds over MCP. Each file is backed up once as `<file>.graphicle-bak`, and `graphicle disconnect` removes what it added.

| Client | Where setup connects it | Session capture |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `.mcp.json` in the repository | hooks in `.claude/settings.local.json` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` | hooks in `~/.codex/hooks.json` (Codex asks you to trust them) |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | |
| VS Code | `.vscode/mcp.json` in the repository | |
| Claude Desktop | `claude_desktop_config.json` in Claude's settings folder | |
| Any other MCP client | a short JSON entry ([MCP](docs/mcp.md)) | |

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
1. **Sync.** Graphicle reads the folder (it respects `.gitignore` and skips secrets), keeps a versioned copy of each source and builds the code graph.
2. **Recall.** When your agent calls a tool, Graphicle syncs what changed, ranks excerpts from code, documents, sessions and reviewed memory, and returns them with citations. The tools call no model; your agent's own model reads the excerpts.
3. **Remember.** Captured sessions become sources. Memories that agents propose wait for your approval in the app.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Agent skill: 按 ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English) 原则用中文向用户汇报结果

evidence.heading: ste-zh：简化技术中文规范
evidence.text:
**语言 / Language：** 简体中文 | [繁體中文](https://github.com/dualface/ste-zht)

一个面向 AI Agent 的任务汇报规范 skill。借鉴航空与工业界严谨的 **ASD-STE100**（Simplified Technical English，简化技术英语）原则，约束 Agent 用清晰、严密且无歧义的中文汇报工作结果。

Agent 的日常汇报常常过程冗长、推测含糊，或者漏掉关键的验证证据。开启 `ste-zh` 后，Agent 将遵循受控中文规范进行汇报：**关键信息先行、实证说话、状态固定、一目了然**。

> 💡 本 skill 仅规范 Agent 向用户汇报与讨论时的表达方式，绝不影响项目代码、注释、Commit 信息及生成的文件内容。

---

evidence.heading: 为什么需要 ste-zh？
evidence.text:
同一个 Bug 修复任务，常见汇报与规范化汇报的差异如下。以下摘录以 [结果汇报示例](examples/result-report.md) 为准，示例中的来源事实见该文件。

**常见 AI 汇报（冗长、推测、不报实证）：**

> 「好的，我先看了一下登录相关的代码，发现问题应该是出在 token 刷新的逻辑上，大概是并发的时候两个请求同时去刷新导致的。然后我对 `auth/refresh.ts` 进行了修改，加了一个锁来实现串行化处理，另外顺手把一些日志之类的也优化了一下。测试基本都跑过了，应该没什么问题，不过 iOS 那边因为没有环境暂时没法验证。你看要不要我再把重试逻辑也一起改了？」

**`ste-zh` 规范化汇报（结论先行、实证可查、便于决策）：**

> 已完成：登录刷新逻辑的代码修改。iOS 端未验证。
>
> **原因**：两个请求同时刷新 token。后完成的刷新使先拿到的 token 失效。
>
> **证据**：
>
> - `auth/refresh.ts:42` — 刷新前不检查是否已有刷新在进行。
>
> **改动**
>
> - `auth/refresh.ts`：同一时间只发一个刷新请求。其他请求等待这次刷新的结果。
> - `auth/logger.ts`：删除 3 处重复日志。这项改动不在原范围内。
>
> **验证**
>
> - 已验证：`npm test auth` — 48 项通过，0 项失败。包含新增并发刷新测试 `auth/refresh.test.ts:88`。
> - 未验证：iOS 端 — 本机没有 iOS 构建环境。
>
> **待确认**
>
> - 是否保留 `auth/logger.ts` 的改动：
>   1. 撤回（推荐）— 本次提交只含登录修复。
>   2. 保留 — 日志清理和登录修复一起提交。

---

evidence.heading: 核心特性
evidence.text:
- **关键信息先行**：首句按回复类型写。结果写状态与完成范围，进度写当前动作，需求总结写总结范围。普通解释或建议不强套模板。
- **状态固定**：工作状态与验证状态分别表述，且各自限定范围。「已完成」不自动表示「已验证」。完整定义见 [术语表第 4 节](references/terminology.md#4-状态词)。
- **如实写验证**：修复效果、运行行为和检查结果写明检查方法、结果与覆盖范围。进度、建议、需求摘要和待决事项不强加验证状态；其中的实际效果断言仍须写验证。资料内容证据不能代替运行验证。
- **一词一义与主动语态**：规范专用词汇，消除虚化动词与歧义长句，降低阅读心智负担。
- **选项化决策**：遇到需要人工定夺的决策点，自动整理为带推荐倾向的编号选项，用户输入数字即可快速推进。

---

evidence.heading: 推荐：使用 `skills` CLI 安装
evidence.text:
[`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) 是 Vercel Labs 推出的 Agent Skill 管理工具，支持 Claude Code、Cursor、Codex 等主流环境。工具会自动按配置将本技能安装至 `ste` 目录。

全局安装（所有项目通用）：

```bash
npx skills add dualface/ste-zh -g
```

安装到当前项目：

```bash
npx skills add dualface/ste-zh
```

仅为指定 Agent 安装（例如 Claude Code）：

```bash
npx skills add dualface/ste-zh -g -a claude-code
```

更新与卸载：

```bash
npx skills update ste -g
npx skills remove --global ste
```

evidence.heading: 手动安装
evidence.text:
将本仓库克隆至 Agent 的 skills 目录下即可。由于本 skill 的标准名称为 `ste`，克隆时请确保目标目录命名为 `ste`：

**Claude Code（全局）：**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/dualface/ste-zh.git ~/.claude/skills/ste
```

其他支持 `SKILL.md` 规范的 Agent，参考各自文档将文件放置在对应的 skills 路径下。

---

evidence.heading: 使用方式
evidence.text:
在对话中输入以下任意指令，即可启用本 skill：

- `/ste`
- 「用 STE 规范输出」
- 「按 ASD-STE100 汇报」

启用后，当前会话中的所有汇报都将严格按照本规范组织。如需退出，发送「停止 ste」或「stop ste」即可。

> 更高优先级指令和用户明确指定的输出格式优先。同级风格规则冲突且用户未明确指定风格时，按本 skill 写。

evidence.heading: 注意事项
evidence.text:
- **运行机制**：本 skill 靠 Agent 遵守上下文中的指令生效，没有程序强制执行。
- **上下文衰减**：在极长会话或发生上下文压缩（compaction）后，Agent 可能会遗忘指令规范。若发现输出风格退化，随时重新发送 `/ste` 即可恢复。
- **全局常驻**：如希望每个会话默认开启，可将「每个会话开始时加载 ste skill」写入 Agent 的全局规则中（例如 Claude Code 的 `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` 或 `~/.claude/rules/` 规则文件）。

---

github_projects.description: 把 OpenCode 的免费模型摆渡给 WorkBuddy —— 隔离运行时、并发检测、判定缓存、一键导入、本机 OpenAI 兼容转发口
github_projects.description_zh: 把 OpenCode 的免费模型摆渡给 WorkBuddy —— 隔离运行时、并发检测、判定缓存、一键导入、本机 OpenAI 兼容转发口

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: 把 OpenCode 的免费模型摆渡给 WorkBuddy —— 隔离运行时、并发检测、判定缓存、一键导入、本机 OpenAI 兼容转发口

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
OC Ferry
  把 OpenCode 的免费模型摆渡给 WorkBuddy
  跨平台托盘应用 · 无需登录注册、无需 API Key · 隔离运行时 · 并发检测 · 判定缓存 · 一键导入 · 本机 OpenAI 兼容转发口

  
  
  
  


---

WorkBuddy 支持在它的 `models.json` 里填自定义模型。OpenCode 的免费模型池是现成的免费额度，但它不是一个能直接填进去的 OpenAI 端点：目录里带 `free` 的模型不一定免费，能聊天不等于能按 WorkBuddy 的方式产生工具调用，而且免费池随时上下线。

**OC Ferry 就是中间这一层**：在数据目录里放一份**隔离的** OpenCode，按**价格**筛出免费模型，逐个探测它们能不能按 WorkBuddy 的工具协议干活，把通过的写进你的 `models.json`，再起一个只监听本机的转发口供 WorkBuddy 调用。

evidence.heading: 界面
evidence.text:
浅色与深色两套主题，四档状态一眼可读；检测是并发的，多个模型同时跑。





深色主题并发检测：多路同时跑，底部实时显示还剩几个

行内展开详情，可「只重测这一个」判定来自缓存时如实标注

evidence.heading: 工作流程
evidence.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["托盘 / 控制面板"] -->|读取模型目录| B["隔离 OpenCode运行时"]
  B --> C{"逐个检测能否按协议产生动作"}
  C -->|产生正确动作| D["判定缓存成功 6 小时"]
  C -->|只回文本| E["可用 · 仅对话工具关闭"]
  C -->|超时 / 限流| F["记录原因10 分钟后自动重试"]
  C -->|已下线 / 无权限| G["记录原因1 小时后重试"]
  D --> H["写入 WorkBuddymodels.json"]
  E --> H
  H --> I["WorkBuddy"]
  I -->|"OpenAI 兼容请求"| J["本机转发口127.0.0.1:41980"]
  J --> K["适配器：JSON 信封协议审批围栏 · 动作转交"]
  K --> B
  A -->|退出| L["摘掉自己导入的条目保留你手写的"]
```

**五条核心链路**

1. **发现**：只看价格字段（输入/输出/缓存读写全为 0）才算免费，名字里带 `free` 不算数；已声明 `deprecated` 的直接排除。
2. **体检**：给 5 个工具、自由选择，让它读一个带随机 token 的文件。**只回文本不算失败**——按「可用 · 仅对话」发布并关掉工具；动作不符重试一次；超时与格式失败不重试。
3. **提速**：检测 3 路并发（一轮约 60 秒）；判定按模型缓存，成功保留 6 小时、当时的负载只保留 10 分钟——**重启基本是秒开，不会每次都全量重测**。
4. **导入**：只增删自己标记过的条目，你手写的一条都不动；写前备份、加锁、原子替换，内容没变就不写；退出时把自己的条目摘干净。
5. **转发**：模型只能回一个 JSON 信封表达动作，**执行权始终在 WorkBuddy 手里**——任何本机动作一律被拒绝或转交成外部工具调用，模型永远不会自己动手。

evidence.heading: 用法
evidence.text:
先安装 WorkBuddy。**不需要另外装 Node.js**（打包后的应用用 Electron 自带的 Node 跑后台服务）。

- **macOS（Apple 芯片）**：下载 `OC-Ferry-<版本>-mac-arm64.dmg`（仓库右侧 Releases 里），双击打开，把 `OC Ferry` 拖进「应用程序」，再双击打开。未做 Apple 公证，首次打开可能要右键 →「打开」；若提示「已损坏」，先核对 Release 说明里的 sha256，再移除下载隔离标记：`xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/OC Ferry.app"`。也可以下载 zip，解压后把 `OC Ferry.app` 拖进「应用程序」。
- **Windows**：运行 `OC-Ferry-Setup-<版本>-win-x64.exe`，装完桌面就有了图标，双击即开。
  安装包会同时做两件事：把**开机自启**写进当前用户的 Run 项（启动参数 `--hidden`，开机后只常驻托盘、不弹窗）、并保证卸载时把这一条摘干净。
  因此装完就等于「一直连着」——不用每次先开一次应用，WorkBuddy 里的免费模型才在。
  （只想要绿色版的话用 `npm run build:win:portable`；portable 包必须完整解压，不要只复制 exe。）

首次启动会自动准备 OpenCode、扫描免费模型并逐个检测，**检测完自动导入一次**。之后重新检测或读取**不会**自动改 WorkBuddy，需要点「导入 WorkBuddy」。

几个日常操作：

- **关窗口 ≠ 退出**：关掉窗口它继续在托盘跑；从托盘退出时会把自己导入的条目摘掉（保留你手写的），所以这些模型可用期间请让它常驻。
- **想重新验证**：点「检测全部」强制重测一轮；只想重测某一个，在它的详情里点「只重测这一个」。
- **主题**：工具栏右上角可在**系统 / 浅色 / 深色**之间切换，选择会记住。

evidence.heading: 数据目录
evidence.text:
| 系统 | 应用数据 | WorkBuddy 配置 |

| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/OC Ferry` | `~/.workbuddy/models.json` |

数据目录里：`api-key`（本机转发口的密钥）、`status.json`、`settings.json`、`probe-cache.json`（判定缓存）、`runtime/`（托管运行时）、`opencode/`（隔离 OpenCode 自己的目录）。

**环境变量**（调试用）：`FERRY_DATA_DIR`、`FERRY_PORT`（默认 41980）、`FERRY_MODELS_FILE`、`FERRY_NO_SYNC=1`（完全不写 WorkBuddy）、`FERRY_OPENCODE_PATH`、`FERRY_PROBE_CONCURRENCY`（并发度，默认 3，上限 6）、`FERRY_PROBE_TTL_MINUTES`（成功判定有效期，默认 360 分钟）、`WORKBUDDY_CONFIG_DIR` / `WORKBUDDY_DATA_FOLDER_NAME`。

evidence.heading: 本机接口
evidence.text:
所有路由都要 `Authorization: Bearer <数据目录>/api-key`，带 `Origin` 头的请求一律 403（这个端口不给浏览器用）。

```
GET  /health                 # 完整状态
GET  /v1/models              # 已判定可用的模型（id 为 "OC · 名字"）
POST /v1/chat/completions    # 转发，支持 stream；并发上限 4
POST /admin/refresh | /admin/probe | /admin/import | /admin/selection
POST /admin/system-proxy | /admin/find-config
```

github_projects.name: whatsapp-mcp
github_projects.description: A read-only MCP server that lets your AI agent search and read your own WhatsApp messages. Runs on Cloudflare Workers.
github_projects.description_zh: 一个只读 MCP 服务器，让您的 AI 智能体可以搜索并阅读您自己的 WhatsApp 消息。在 Cloudflare Workers 上运行。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: A read-only MCP server that lets your AI agent search and read your own WhatsApp messages. Runs on Cloudflare Workers.

evidence.heading: whatsapp-mcp
evidence.text:
Let your AI agent read your WhatsApp messages.

This is a small server that runs in your own Cloudflare account. You link your phone to it once, the way you'd link WhatsApp Web, and from then on any MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, anything that speaks MCP) can search and read your chats. It can read and search your messages, and remember names you give it for phone numbers. It can't send anything.

Ask your agent things like:

- "What did Dana say about the flights?"
- "Find every message where someone mentioned the lease, across all my chats."
- "Summarize what I missed in the family group this week."

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Your phone stays the source of truth. The server is a linked device that your agent talks to.

It doesn't stay connected to WhatsApp. When your agent asks for something, and once a day, it connects, collects whatever WhatsApp queued for it since last time, writes that to its own database, and hangs up. Your phone keeps working normally and keeps getting notifications.

Your messages live in a SQLite database inside a Durable Object in your Cloudflare account. Nothing goes anywhere else.

evidence.heading: Set it up
evidence.text:
You need a Cloudflare account on the Workers Paid plan (see the note below), Node 20 or later, and your phone.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/finereli/whatsapp-mcp
cd whatsapp-mcp
npm install

# 1. A place for the sign-in tokens. Paste the id it prints into wrangler.jsonc.
npx wrangler kv namespace create OAUTH_KV

# 2. A password for the page that links your phone. 12+ characters.
npx wrangler secret put OWNER_PASSWORD

# 3. Deploy.
npm run deploy
```

Wrangler prints your URL, something like `https://whatsapp-mcp.your-name.workers.dev`. Open it. The front page has the two remaining steps:

1. **Link WhatsApp.** Scan the QR code with WhatsApp (Settings, Linked Devices, Link a Device). If you're on the phone itself and can't scan a screen, use the phone number option instead. The first link imports your history. The page shows progress, and you can close it.
2. **Connect your agent.** In Claude Code:

   ```sh
   claude mcp add --transport http whatsapp https://your-url/mcp
   ```

   Then type `/mcp` and sign in with the password. Other clients: point them at the same `/mcp` URL.

If you want your own domain, see the comments at the bottom of `wrangler.jsonc`.

evidence.heading: The Workers Paid note
evidence.text: Importing a large history decodes a lot of data in one go, and the default CPU limit on Workers is too small for it. `wrangler.jsonc` raises it, and raising it needs the paid plan, which is a few dollars a month. I haven't tried the free plan. If you're on it, remove the `limits` block and expect the first import to be fragile.

evidence.heading: Things to know
evidence.text:
**This isn't official.** WhatsApp has no API for reading your own personal messages. This uses the same protocol WhatsApp Web uses, through an open source library (Baileys). That's against WhatsApp's terms. For a linked device that only reads, the practical risk is low, but it isn't zero. Use it on your own account, and don't use it to send messages.

**You get what WhatsApp sends.** The first link imports whatever history WhatsApp decides to hand a new device. It may not be everything. It only does this once per link. To import again, relink (your stored messages are kept, and a re-import fills in anything missing).

**Some chats show up as phone numbers.** WhatsApp doesn't give a linked device every contact name, and most of these are one-off messages from people you never saved. For the ones that matter, your agent can fix it: it lists the unnamed chats, looks the numbers up in your contacts with whatever contacts tool it already has (a Google Contacts or Gmail connector, for example), and saves the names. The server never connects to a contacts service itself. See "Naming chats" below.

**Media isn't downloaded.** Photos, voice notes and documents appear as labels like `[image]` or `[voice note 12s]`, with the caption if there was one. Nothing is transcribed.

**It's for one person.** One deployment is one WhatsApp account and one owner. That's deliberate: each deployment holds a full message history and a live login to the account, so everyone should run their own.

**Relinking.** If your phone says the device was removed, or you want to start over, ask your agent to run `relink`, or open `/setup` and choose "Unlink and scan again". You scan a new QR code. Stored messages are kept.

evidence.heading: What your agent can do
evidence.text:
| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_chats` | Chats, most recent first. Filter by name or number. |
| `get_messages` | Read one chat. Page back or forward by date. |
| `search_messages` | Full-text search across everything, or within one chat. |
| `unnamed_chats` | Chats known only by phone number, busiest first, with the last thing the other person said. |
| `set_contact_names` | Save names for phone numbers, in any format. Names stick to the number, so they also show up in groups. |
| `sync_now` | Pull new messages right now. |
| `link_status` | Is it linked, when did it last pull, how much is stored. |
| `relink` | Unlink and start over. A human has to scan the new QR code. |

Every read tool first tops up from WhatsApp if the stored copy is more than ten minutes old.

evidence.heading: How sessions work
evidence.text:
All WhatsApp traffic happens inside `runSession()` in `whatsapp-do.ts`. There are two kinds:

- **Pairing** (`startPairing`). No credentials yet. Baileys emits QR strings, kept in memory and rendered to SVG by `pairStatus()`. After a scan WhatsApp closes the socket with code 515 (restart required), and the session reconnects with the new credentials. History arrives as `messaging-history.set` chunks with a `progress` percentage. The session ends when WhatsApp reports 100 percent and the stream has been quiet for a few seconds.
- **Pull** (`pull`). Reconnects with stored credentials. WhatsApp delivers whatever it queued while we were away, then signals `receivedPendingNotifications`. The session ends after a few quiet seconds.

Callers share one session: a second `pull()` while one is running gets the same promise.

A pairing session outlives the HTTP request that started it. `startPairing` sets a Durable Object alarm, and `alarm()` awaits the session promise. An in-flight alarm handler is what keeps the object alive. The pairing page only watches; closing it doesn't stop the import.

Idle detection counts only data events (`messaging-history.set`, `messages.upsert`), not connection chatter. Counting everything keeps a session open forever, because presence and contact updates never stop.

github_projects.name: sessiondeck
github_projects.description: SessionDeck — every coding-agent session in one tree, in VS Code and Cursor. Source-available.
github_projects.description_zh: SessionDeck —— 每个编程智能体会话都在一棵树上显示，支持 VS Code 和 Cursor。源代码可用。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: SessionDeck — every coding-agent session in one tree, in VS Code and Cursor. Source-available.

evidence.heading: SessionDeck
evidence.text:
SessionDeck tracks the Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and Cursor agent sessions running on your machine in one sidebar tree, grouped by project, with a status icon on each row. A red bell shows which Claude Code session is waiting on you. Click the row and you land in its tab or terminal; for a Claude Code session that works from another window too.

If you searched for a way to track Claude Code or Codex agent sessions across VS Code or Cursor windows, this is that.



Status is inferred from transcripts and process state on disk, not reported by the agents themselves, so it can lag or misread an edge case. The rest of this page says where.

It's for people who run many agents at once and lose track of which one stopped to ask.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
**VS Code** (Visual Studio Marketplace):

```sh
code --install-extension len5ky.sessiondeck
```

Or search **SessionDeck** in the Extensions view.

**Cursor** (Open VSX): search **SessionDeck** in the Extensions panel, or run `cursor --install-extension len5ky.sessiondeck`. If Cursor can't find it, download `sessiondeck-<version>.vsix` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/len5ky/sessiondeck/releases) and run **Extensions: Install from VSIX...**.

**Remote windows** (WSL, Remote-SSH, dev containers): SessionDeck runs on the workspace side, so it goes into the remote, next to your sessions. The optional bridge for seeing several hosts in one tree goes on your **local desktop** instead, and installing SessionDeck from the Extensions view puts it there for you; see [Other hosts](#other-hosts-the-bridge).

evidence.heading: Platform support
evidence.text:
- **Linux and WSL**: full support; this is what it's built and tested on.
- **macOS**: works, minus the `/proc` features. Auto-detected config homes degrade, and discovery is limited to config homes it already knows about. Terminal matching, the ↗ badge and Move into Editor read the process table with `ps`.
- **Native Windows**: the tree works on the 3-second poll, without hooks or approval alerts. Install Hooks isn't offered there, and running it from the palette writes a POSIX shell script SessionDeck doesn't support on Windows. Terminal matching, the ↗ badge and Move into Editor read the process table through PowerShell, so a new session can take a few seconds to get its badge.

**Run Diagnostics** reports what works on your machine. Trust it over this list.

evidence.heading: First run
evidence.text:
1. Click the compass icon in the activity bar. That's the SessionDeck view; your sessions appear under **Sessions**, grouped by project.
2. Run **SessionDeck: Install Hooks (instant updates + approval alerts)** from the command palette. Without hooks the tree still updates on a 3-second poll, but it can't see a session stuck on a permission prompt: that session just looks like it's working. Hooks are written into each Claude config home on the machine where SessionDeck runs, so do this once per machine (once per remote host, too). They apply to sessions started afterwards.
3. If the tree is emptier than you expect, run **SessionDeck: Run Diagnostics**. It prints one line per subsystem and the fix for each problem, and changes nothing.

evidence.heading: What a row tells you
evidence.text:
| Icon | Meaning |
|---|---|
| spinning sync, green | working |
| spinning sync, purple | working, with subagents running |
| bell, red | waiting for your approval or an answer |
| bell-dot, yellow | finished, you haven't looked yet |
| check, blue | finished and read |
| circle outline | idle |

A working row carries a short caption of what it's doing (`2m · ⚙3 · Migrating schema`, or just the tool, `2m · Bash`). A finished row you haven't opened shows the start of its last message. If a working session goes quiet far longer than its current tool usually takes (5 minutes for `Read` or `Edit`, 15 for `Bash`), the row keeps spinning but adds `· quiet 12m`. It may be wedged; the status itself never changes on a guess.

The activity-bar icon and a status-bar chip both show how many sessions need you. `Ctrl+Alt+]` (`Cmd+Alt+]` on macOS) jumps to the next one, oldest blocked first; `Ctrl+Alt+[` goes back.



Clicking a row opens the session: its Claude tab, even in another editor window, or the integrated terminal it runs in. If there's nothing to focus (a session in tmux, say), you get a rendered copy of its last message instead.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
SessionDeck reads files. Every few seconds it scans each Claude Code config home (`~/.claude`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, any you list in `sessionDeck.extraConfigDirs`, and on Linux any home a running `claude` process points at), reads the tail of each transcript, and checks the process in `/proc` to confirm it's still alive. The turn boundary comes from the transcript's `stop_reason`: `end_turn` means done, an interrupt marker means idle. So sessions started in a terminal, tmux or cron show up too.

Hooks make it faster. **Install Hooks** adds Stop, Notification and UserPromptSubmit entries to `settings.json` in every config home (backed up, safe to run twice) plus a small forwarder script at `~/.local/state/claude-overview/hook.sh` (`claude-overview` is SessionDeck's former name; the folder keeps it so existing installs carry over). Each event appends a line to a spool file SessionDeck watches, so the row flips the moment a session finishes or hits a permission prompt. **Remove Hooks** takes them out.

When a session blocks, you get a VS Code notification naming what it wants ("needs your permission to use Bash", or the question text) with an **Open** button. One notification per incident. Three or more blocks within 45 seconds collapse into one notice with a **Triage** button. Notifications live inside the editor window, which is exactly where you aren't when they fire, so two settings (both off by default) reach you when it's unfocused: `sessionDeck.unfocusedSound` and `sessionDeck.unfocusedOsNotification`. They fire at most once per 30 seconds.

The extension makes no network calls, licensing included.

evidence.heading: Splinter Cell: Double Agent - XBE Recomp
evidence.text:
An unofficial native PC port of the original Xbox version of Splinter Cell: Double Agent via static recompilation, built into a 64 bit Windows executable. The game's x86 code is translated to C++ ahead of time, the Xbox kernel, Direct3D and DirectSound calls are implemented on Windows, and everything is drawn with Direct3D 12 and played through XAudio2. Made with the [Xbox XBE Recomp](https://github.com/TGP482/XboxXBE-Recomp) tool, created for this game originally.

> [!NOTE]
> This project does not include any game assets. You must provide the files from your own legally acquired copy of the game to install or build.

evidence.heading: Installation
evidence.text:
The latest version of [SCDA-XBERecomp](https://github.com/TGP482/SCDA-XBERecomp/releases) can be found in the Releases page.

- Place your game files in the `assets` folder. This can be an ISO, or the extracted data files.
- Run `SCDA.exe`. The first start compiles the game's code for your PC, this only happens once.
- Recomp Settings can be adjusted in the in-game options menu while the game is running, or through the Settings overlay, which is opened with <kbd>F10</kbd> by default.

evidence.heading: Display
evidence.text:
- **Monitor** - Picks the monitor the game shows on, for Fullscreen and Borderless (and where Windowed opens). Lists every connected monitor by its Windows number and desktop resolution.
- **Display Mode** - Switch between Fullscreen, Borderless and Windowed.
- **Resolution** - Lists every mode your monitor reports and defaults to your desktop resolution, replacing the original 640x480 resolution.
- **Render Resolution** - Renders the game at 20% to 200% of the output resolution, allowing supersampling or downscaling independent of the window size.
- **Field of View** - Sets the horizontal field of view during gameplay from 45 to 140 degrees, with 75 being the game's default. Cutscenes, scopes, gadget views and lock picking keep the original.
- **Max Frame Rate** - Caps the frame rate to your monitor's refresh rate or a custom value, or removes the cap entirely, replacing the Xbox's 30 FPS limiter.
- **V-Sync** - Reduces screen tearing.
- **HDR Output** - Enables HDR10 output on displays with Windows HDR turned on, detected automatically. Highlights extend up to the display's peak brightness.
- **FPS Counter** - Displays the frame rate on screen.
- **FMV Scale** - Choose between Fill, which makes the FMVs fill widescreen displays, and 4:3, which shows them in a 4:3 frame as on the original Xbox.

evidence.heading: The sessionless, relentless personal agent.
evidence.text:
[](https://comma.surf/download)

Comma is an open-source personal agent built to be sessionless. Your work, memory, and context stay continuous across your computer, phone, cloud environment, applications, and connected devices.

It breaks down your goals into Tasks and keeps working through agentic loops until the job is done.

Built by AFK Inc., Comma is our attempt to create an open agentic system that keeps you away from software and away from the keyboard.

You can use the hosted service at [comma.surf](https://comma.surf), or run your own instance from this repository.

evidence.heading: Philosophy
evidence.text:
- **Sessionless**
  - Conversations are just interfaces. **Tasks are the persistent execution state.**
  - Your memory, context, and ongoing Tasks continue across devices, conversations, and interfaces.

- **Relentless**
  - Comma is always on and works 24/7.
  - Tasks are automatically turned into independent agent loops that plan, execute, review, and verify until the goal is completed.
  - The goal stays alive until it's done.

- **Swarm Intelligence**
  - Comma automatically distributes work across agents and models with different strengths.
  - Smaller independent contexts reduce compression, drift, and context corruption.
  - You manage the goal, not the swarm.

- **Works with your existing agents**
  - Codex, Claude Code, and other agents can be invoked like applications or registered as Workers and Sub-agents.
  - Keep your existing tools and workflows. Comma orchestrates and automates them.

- **Cloud for work. Your device for identity.**
  - Comma uses its own environment for long-running work, while sensitive identity, sessions, payments, and private data can stay on your devices.
  - When needed, Comma hands the Task to your computer or phone and continues from where it left off.

evidence.heading: What Comma does
evidence.text:
- **Turns requests into Tasks.** A quick question gets an answer in chat.
  Bigger work becomes a Task. Comma checks its own work and decides when the
  Task is done.
- **Waits for your decisions.** When a decision is yours, the Task waits in
  Needs Review. Comma does the rest on its own, or only drafts if you prefer.
- **Shows all work on one board.** Tasks move through In progress, Needs
  Review, and Done.
- **Writes first.** When something needs you, Comma tells you in chat and
  suggests the next step. Routines give you a briefing at the time you set.
- **Keeps watch with Loops.** A Loop is a small program that your agent writes.
  It watches an inbox, a repository, or a feed, and wakes the agent only when
  something needs it. A quiet hour uses no large-model tokens.
- **Works on your computers.** Salix connects your Mac. Comma can read files
  there. When you turn on Allow operations, it can also change files, run
  commands, and hand work to Codex, Claude Code, Pi, or Kimi.
- **Records your calls.** The Mac app can record a call, save it to Drive, and
  start a summary Task.
- **Uses your models.** Bring your own API key, or a ChatGPT or Claude plan.

evidence.heading: Built with Elixir and Lean. Verified with Lean and TLA+.
evidence.text:
Comma is built for long-running, fault-tolerant agent workloads. Its runtime is primarily built with **Elixir/OTP**, with **Lean** used for critical systems components. Important runtime properties are specified and machine-checked in Lean, and we use **TLA+** to model-check core distributed protocols.

Each agent runs as its own process on the Erlang VM. When one part fails, it restarts, and the other agents keep running. Messages that Salix has accepted survive the restart. An interrupted action that changes something does not run again on its own.

The formal models check properties such as:

- Accepted work is not silently lost across failures and restarts.
- A failed reply does not count as completed work.
- Side-effecting actions are recorded before they start.
- An interrupted mutating action does not run twice by accident.
- Stale workers cannot overwrite newer agent state.
- Data only crosses boundaries where policy allows it.

Formal verification does not prove model judgment or task success. It verifies that **the runtime follows its rules, even when things fail.**

See [Verification](docs/verification.md) and the [TLA+ models](tla/).

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
- Docker Engine with Compose v2.24 or later.
- Enough disk space for the build layers. The first build downloads public
  toolchains, including Lean, Elixir, Go, and Node.
- A model provider account for real model calls. The default stack does not
  include a mock model.

evidence.heading: How it works

- **The app** (`desktop/`, Electron) starts the **Bops server** (Next.js: `app/` and `lib/server/`) on your Mac, on port 3210. The server runs the team: chats, threads, routines, watches and the bots' tasks.
- **The bots' computers** are Orgo cloud computers, launched from a template built from this repo (`orgo/`, with what runs on them in `vm/`).
- **Tasks on the bots' computers** run on OpenAI's computer tool (Responses API). **Tasks on your Mac** run on OpenAI's Agents API, with the Codex CLI (`codex exec-server`) and a Chrome of the bots' own.
- **Signed in with Orgo**, the app works through Bops Cloud (`cloud/`), the server Orgo runs for hosted Bops. Orgo's provider keys stay there, and your Mac gets only narrow ones: a key for your own mailboxes and a spend-capped key for tasks. Bops Cloud also takes the webhooks for texts, calls and Slack, and keeps your chats in your account.
- **Self-hosted** (`BOPS_SELF_HOSTED=1`), the app calls each provider directly with the keys in `.env.local` and keeps its state in `.data/` on your Mac. A small relay (`edge/`) can give the webhooks a public HTTPS address.

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
- A Mac with Apple silicon, and Node 22 or newer.
- **Required:** an [Orgo](https://orgo.ai) account and an OpenAI API key, plus a second, restricted OpenAI key with a spend limit for tasks (`OPENAI_EXECUTOR_API_KEY`).
- **Recommended:** TypeSafe (small judgment calls), Honcho (memory), Composio (apps), treg (business data), AgentMail (email), Tailscale (a direct live view of the bots' screens).
- **Optional:** AgentPhone and a public URL, for texts and calls.
- **For tasks on your Mac:** Google Chrome. Bops uses your Codex CLI if you have one, or installs it, and never runs it on your ChatGPT account.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: FOREST is a research agent for long-horizon science, where evidence gets lost, errors compound, and goals drift. It explores ideas, reads literature, forms hypotheses, runs real experiments, analyzes results, revises paths, and builds a full paper—all in an editable graph you can inspect, branch, redirect, with claims and figures linked to evidence

evidence.heading: FOREST
evidence.text:
**Give it a research question. Turn it into ideas, real experiments, evidence, and a complete paper.**

FOREST is an end-to-end research agent framework for carrying a scientific project from an early question to a finished manuscript.

It can explore and compare research directions, search the literature, turn promising ideas into testable hypotheses, design experiments, run real code on your compute, analyze the results, and decide what to try next. As the project develops, FOREST can revise its plan, abandon weak directions, branch into alternatives, and build the figures, tables, and manuscript around the evidence that survives.

Instead of keeping the research process inside a long chat history, FOREST represents it as an editable research graph. Ideas, hypotheses, experiments, results, decisions, and paper sections remain connected. You can inspect the graph, change a plan, replace a hypothesis, branch from an earlier point, or redirect the research without starting over.

**Idea discovery → literature review → hypothesis formation → experiment design → real execution → result analysis → research-path revision → baselines & ablations → figures & tables → full-paper generation**

evidence.heading: What FOREST does
evidence.text:
**Finds research directions.**  
Start with a broad question or an unfinished idea. FOREST explores possible directions, compares them, checks the surrounding literature, and turns the strongest candidates into concrete research paths.

**Turns ideas into experiments.**  
Hypotheses are converted into executable plans with baselines, controls, metrics, ablations, and explicit conditions for success or failure.

**Runs real experiments.**  
FOREST writes and executes research code, launches training and evaluation jobs, collects logs and metrics, and keeps experimental artifacts attached to the research path that produced them.

**Analyzes the evidence and changes course.**  
Results are not treated as the end of a task. FOREST interprets them, compares competing explanations, identifies what failed, and decides whether to extend, revise, or drop a direction.

**Keeps the research path editable.**  
Researchers can intervene at any point: edit a node, change an experiment, revisit an earlier assumption, or branch the graph to investigate an alternative approach without losing the existing work.

**Continues across execution rounds.**
Agents save durable checkpoints at bounded work-round boundaries and automatically continue the same research run. Cumulative turns and planning cycles do not determine scientific lifetime. Recovery uses the retained goal, graph, evidence and action receipts; all rounds and branches share resource accounting. Actual spending, compute limits, permissions and unresolved blockers still govern execution. See [research execution and recovery](docs/RUNTIME.md).

**Builds scientific figures and tables.**  
Experimental results can be turned into publication-ready visualizations and tables while remaining tied to their underlying runs and observatio

evidence.heading: Quick Start
evidence.text:
Requires **Python 3.11+**. The Web workspace also requires **Node.js 22+**.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mikamikasuki/FOREST.git
cd FOREST
```

evidence.heading: Web Workspace — macOS / Linux
evidence.text:
Install dependencies and start FOREST:

```bash
python3.11 scripts/install.py
.venv/bin/forest serve
```

Open [localhost:8000](http://127.0.0.1:8000/), configure a model provider in **Settings**, and create a project with a research goal and an explicit spending budget.

evidence.heading: CLI / Headless
evidence.text:
Run the API and worker without Node.js or the Web build:

```bash
python3.11 scripts/install.py --headless
.venv/bin/forest serve --headless --data-dir ./var
```

Keep the service running and use another terminal for client commands. Run these commands from the repository root:

```bash
.venv/bin/forest --help
.venv/bin/forest init --name "My research" --goal "Your research question"
.venv/bin/forest status
```

The CLI supports project and node management, experiment execution, logs, run control, evidence inspection, budgets, and manuscript tasks. It shares the same research state as the Web workspace.

See the [CLI guide](https://github.com/mikamikasuki/FOREST/blob/main/docs/CLI.md) or try the [numerical experiment example](https://github.com/mikamikasuki/FOREST/blob/main/examples/cli/README.md) without model calls.

evidence.heading: Submission Workflow
evidence.text:
Scientific projects default to a complete submission and `full_paper`, with real experiments, accepted-paper comparison, and a review-and-repair loop.

The workflow connects literature, experimental design, baseline reproduction, execution, independent analysis, visual selection, manuscript authoring, and submission review. Delivery checks retain missing evidence and outstanding work when a pilot finishes or a budget is exhausted.

Figures and manuscript values bind to completed runs and recorded observations. Visuals attach to argumentative paragraphs, and compilation checks their actual placement in the document.

See the [submission workflow](docs/PUBLICATION_DELIVERY.md) and [16-paper reference corpus](docs/PUBLICATION_REFERENCE_CORPUS.md). The reference corpus informs framework design; each research project selects topic-matched papers.

[Paper authoring](docs/PAPER_AUTHORING.md) explains independent visual selection, manuscript placement, and manual insertion from Figure Studio.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text: Automate real Android phones from your code. Test your apps, script the tasks you repeat, run a shelf of phones, or let an AI agent use one. Python, Node.js, the shell or HTTP. No ADB, no USB cable, no root. Website · Docs · Download · Sponsor · Quick start · Languages · Guides English · 한국어 · 简体中文 No ADB, no cableInstall one app on the phone, turn on its permissions and pair it with a QR code. No developer options, no USB debugging, no root. The same command everywheretouch is touch in Python, Node.js, the CLI, HTTP and as an MCP tool, all generated from one spec. Phones anywhereThe phone connects out to your PC, so it works on the same Wi-Fi or on mobile data through a tunnel or a relay you run. Every line is encrypted end to end.

evidence.heading: What people use it for
evidence.text:
* **Testing your own app** on real phones, including flows that cross into other apps, such as a login with a code from a text message.
* **A shelf of phones** running the same routine every day, each through its own network or proxy.
* **Giving an AI agent hands**: through MCP, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other agents can look at a phone screen and act on it.
* **Small personal automations**, such as turning Wi-Fi off at night or collecting a value from an app every hour.

Droidline uses only permissions an ordinary app can get, so a few things are out of reach: see [What it cannot do](#what-it-cannot-do).

evidence.heading: See it in action
evidence.text: Try the same demo in your browser, and pick elements on a simulated screen, on droidline.dev

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
You need a PC (Windows, macOS or Linux) and an Android phone with Android 9 or later, on the same Wi-Fi for a first try. The [installation guide](https://droidline.dev/docs/install/) walks through each step with screenshots.

1. **Run the server on your PC.** Download the `droidline` archive for your system from [Releases](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Droidline/releases/latest), put `droidline` on your `PATH`, and start it. Leave it running.

   ```bash
   droidline serve
   ```

2. **Install the app on the phone.** Download `droidline-agent.apk` from the same release page and open it. On the app's **Setup** tab, turn on the accessibility service, the Droidline keyboard, notifications and unrestricted battery use. On Android 13 and later, allow **restricted settings** for the app first; the app shows where.

3. **Pair them.** Run this on the PC and scan the QR code with the app's **Pair** tab:

   ```bash
   droidline pair
   ```

   No camera? Tap **Pair on this Wi-Fi** in the app and type the 6-digit code it shows: `droidline pair 482913`.

4. **Send a command.**

   ```bash
   droidline launch com.android.settings
   droidline touch text "Network & internet"
   ```

No phone at hand? `droidline-fakephone`, included in every release, simulates one with a small demo app. The [first-script tutorial](https://droidline.dev/docs/tutorial/) builds a complete login script against it.

evidence.heading: Use it from your language
evidence.text:
Every interface talks to `droidline serve` on `localhost:8780` and uses the same command names.

**Python** (`pip install droidline`, Python 3.9+)

```python
from droidline import connect

d = connect()                                  # the phone paired with this PC
d.launch("dev.droidline.demo")
if d.exists("text", "Close ad"):               # conditions never wait and never fail
    d.touch("text", "Close ad")
d.input("id", "email", "knife")                # waits up to 10 s for the element
d.touch("text", "Log in")
print(d.get_text("id", "greeting"))
```

**Node.js and TypeScript** (`npm install droidline`, Node.js 18+)

```js
import { connect } from "droidline";

const d = await connect();
await d.launch("dev.droidline.demo");
await d.input("id", "email", "knife");
await d.touch("text", "Log in", { timeout: 15 });
console.log(await d.getText("id", "greeting"));
```

**C# and .NET** (`dotnet add package Droidline`, .NET 8+ or .NET Framework 4.6.2+)

```csharp
using Droidline;

await using var d = await DroidlineClient.ConnectAsync();
await d.LaunchAsync("dev.droidline.demo");
await d.InputAsync("id", "email", "knife");
await d.TouchAsync("text", "Log in", timeout: 15);
Console.WriteLine(await d.GetTextAsync("id", "greeting"));
```

**Command line** (comes with the server)

```bash
droidline touch text "Log in"
droidline which text="Log in" id=main_tab --timeout 15
droidline screenshot shot.png
```

**HTTP** (any language, any tool)

```bash
curl -s -X POST localhost:8780/devices/_/touch \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"by":"text","value":"Log in"}'
```

**AI agents over MCP** (Claude, Cursor, VS Code and others)

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "droidline": { "command": "droidline", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

With Claude Code: `claude mcp add droidline -- dro

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Pick the element, not the pixel.** `dump()` returns the screen as a tree with `text`, `id` and `desc` for every element. Commands take the field and the value: `touch("id", "login")`. When an element refuses a click, Droidline taps its parent or the center of its bounds by itself.
- **Waiting is built in.** `touch`, `input` and `wait` wait for their element, 10 seconds by default. Conditions such as `exists`, `checked` and `which` answer at once and never throw for a missing element.
- **Clear errors.** Every failure has a code, a message in English, Korean or Chinese, and a flag that says whether retrying helps: `NOT_FOUND: Could not find text 'Log in' within 10s. Current screen: com.example / .MainActivity`.
- **A shelf of phones.** One PC drives many phones. Commands to one phone run in order, different phones run in parallel, and each phone has a name you choose.
- **Per-app proxy.** Send chosen apps through a socks5 or http upstream with a local VPN, one upstream per phone, without root.
- **Notifications on the PC.** Wait for one, react to every one, reply, open or dismiss it, or forward it to a signed webhook.
- **New mobile IPs.** A `batch` sent with `cuts_network` keeps running on the phone while it is offline, so airplane mode on, wait, off works as one call. `intent` opens the Settings page first; the [recipes](https://droidline.dev/docs/recipes/#settings-force-stop-clear-data-network-switches) show it step by step.
- **Nothing runs twice.** A phone that drops off mobile data resumes where it left off; a command that was in flight is answered from the phone's cache, not run again.
- **Selectors that hold up.** Combine conditions or name an element by its neighbors: `touch({"class": "android.widget.Switch", "row": {"text": "Wi-Fi"}})`. `find` hands back el

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text: Four ways in — pick one (details in [Works with your tools](#works-with-your-tools)): the **VS Code extension** (below), the **`agent-standup` command** (`npx @double_geste/agent-standup@latest --open`), the **desktop app** (macOS, from the release page), or the **[Claude Code plugin](#claude-code-plugin)**. Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium get the same extension from Open VSX: search **Agent Standup** in their Extensions panel.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Claude Code writes every session to `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl`, and each sub-agent to `<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl` (with a `.meta.json` linking it to the tool call that created it). Agent Standup merges these into one timeline: orders (the prompt a lead sends to a sub-agent), spoken text, tool calls (with their inputs), the **results** of those calls (matched by tool-call id, with real durations) and final reports. Each file is parsed once and then only the new lines are read, so even a very large session refreshes in a few milliseconds; responses are compressed. The page asks the server every 0.4 s (every 2.5 s when the call is hidden and nobody hears it) and plays new events.

The website at agent-standup.com counts its visits, and the clicks on its buttons, with Vercel Web Analytics, the counter of its host: no cookie, nothing loaded from another service, and no count for a browser that sends Do Not Track. The earlier landing page on GitHub Pages counts visits anonymously (a 1-pixel file hosted on GitHub per channel: no cookies, no third-party tracker) and asks GitHub which release is the latest. The app sends nothing by default. Every form of it can count usage if you say yes (the VS Code extension through `agentStandup.shareUsage`; the desktop app, the command line and the Claude Code plugin through a question asked once), and the last three can also tell you when a new version is out, if you say yes (see below). Details in the [privacy policy](PRIVACY.md).

evidence.heading: Limits
evidence.text:
- Tool outputs are trimmed (about 1–2 KB each); the shared screen shows the beginning of long outputs.
- Output only exists once a tool call has finished: a running command shows a spinner and its live timer, not partial output.
- The natural voices need about 750 MB and npm; without them the agents babble.
- Very large sessions (10 MB+ of transcript) take a second or two to load the first time (about 1.9 s for a 12 MB, 168-sub-agent session on a recent Mac); after that updates take milliseconds.
- Video export and the clip record in real time and need a Chromium-based browser/VS Code. MP4 recording was checked in Chrome; it has not been tested inside VS Code's own panel, which may still produce a `.webm`.
- "Hide code & file names in videos" does not mask what the agents say (speech bubbles, subtitles, voices).

evidence.heading: Security and what it reads
evidence.text:
The full [privacy policy](PRIVACY.md) says what is read, what is kept on your computer and what can leave it.

- **It reads local files and sends nothing by default.** Agent Standup reads the output Claude Code writes for a command running in the background (in its temporary folder, while the shared screen shows that command), and the session files Claude Code already writes (`~/.claude/projects`, or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; the status it keeps for each open session in `~/.claude/sessions`, and the plan files a session names in `~/.claude/plans`) and the ones Codex, Mistral Vibe and Cowork write (`~/.codex/sessions`, or `CODEX_HOME`; `~/.vibe/logs/session`, or `VIBE_HOME`; the `local-agent-mode-sessions` folder of the Claude desktop app; each can be turned off) and draws them in a page. It never writes to your sessions; a click on a session that needs you opens it in the app it runs in (a local link, or that app brought to the front, found in the list of running programs); it starts Claude Code only for translation and the optional jokes, described below.
- **Local only.** The server listens on `127.0.0.1` (never on the network), refuses requests whose Host or Origin is not local, and refuses cross-site requests on every endpoint that does something (translation, jokes, sound, settings).
- **What calls out:** translation, which is on when the interface is in French, Spanish or Brazilian Portuguese (for the last two it can be switched off), and three things that are optional and off by default: jokes, the FIP radio stream, and the usage counter (only if you say yes: in VS Code, one empty request a day and at most one a week; in the desktop app, the command line and the Claude Code plugin, at most one a week; each to a 1-pixel file on GitHub), and, in those three, the new-ver

evidence.heading: Privacy and usage counting
evidence.text: Agent Standup reads local session files. With the interface in French, Spanish or Brazilian Portuguese it translates the call through your own Claude login (for the last two this can be switched off); in any other language it sends nothing anywhere by default. The other network uses are optional: jokes (your own Claude login, off unless you turn them on), the FIP radio stream (if you turn it on), and the **optional usage counter**: if you set `agentStandup.shareUsage` to `true` (off by default, and ignored when VS Code telemetry is off), the extension makes one empty request a day (when the editor starts) and at most one a week (when you open the call) to 1-pixel files in this repository's releases. There is no identifier and no content; GitHub sees your IP like for any download. The desktop app, the command line and the Claude Code plugin ask once, in the page, and then make at most one such request a week (when you open the call), each to a file of its own; never when the `DO_NOT_TRACK` environment variable is set, and ⚙ › All settings turns it off. They also ask once whether to tell you when a new version is out; with a yes they ask the npm registry for the latest version number at most once a day (nothing about you or your sessions; never with `DO_NOT_TRACK` or `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER` set). The usage counter lets the maintainer count active installs and weekly users (`npm run stats`).

evidence.heading: Windows：下载后启动桌宠
evidence.text:
1. 下载 [McPet-v0.1.0-windows-x64.zip](https://github.com/songconmaisaix31-design/mcpet/releases/download/v0.1.0/McPet-v0.1.0-windows-x64.zip)。
2. 解压完整文件夹，双击 **`Start-Pet.vbs`**。
3. 右键宠物，试试「角色与动作 → 麦麦套装」，或「设置 → 查看设置」。

便携包内置运行环境。保留 `McPet.exe`、`_internal` 和启动脚本的相对位置；直接双击 `McPet.exe` 会进入 MCP 服务模式。启动脚本不可用时，在解压目录运行：

```powershell
.\McPet.exe --desktop
```

首次使用不需要填写模型 Key。v0.1.0 下载包仍需自行填写餐饮凭证；最新源码已支持免 Token 在线试用。长期使用请在「设置 → 账号凭证」中填写自己的麦当劳、瑞幸 Token，余额查询按需配置，详见[账号设置](docs/USER-GUIDE.md#账号与本机配置)。

evidence.heading: Agent：接入正在使用的会话
evidence.text:
宿主需要支持 **MCP stdio**。下载 [通用 Agent 包](https://github.com/songconmaisaix31-design/mcpet/releases/download/v0.1.0/McPet-v0.1.0-agent.zip)，解压后在其目录运行；已有源码也可使用同样命令：

```powershell
python -m pip install -r requirements-agent.txt
python -m src.agent_install
```

需要 Python 3.10+。将输出的 `server.command` 和 `server.args` 填入宿主的 MCP 设置，服务名填 `mcpet`，传输方式选择 stdio；重新加载会话并完成宿主的信任流程。然后说：

> 用 McPet 查看当前角色和设置。切到 DeepSeek 娘，穿麦麦套装。

Windows 便携包用户可运行 `.\McPet.exe --install` 导出同样的连接设置。MCP 服务由宿主启动；桌宠通过 `Start-Pet.vbs` 单独启动。两者使用相同的数据目录时，Agent 的动作和皮肤指令会传给已运行的桌宠。

技能安装、通用配置示例及 OpenCode / Claude Code 的可选原生适配见[Agent 接入步骤](docs/USER-GUIDE.md#在-agent-中使用)。

| 看工作状态 | 会话与额度 → 会话进度 | 「用 McPet 看当前会话状态」 |
| 查优惠 | 麦当劳 → 查优惠券 | 「今天有什么麦当劳优惠？先查一下」 |

| 记录午餐 | 营养台账 → 选择餐品 / 记账 | 「查询巨无霸营养，我吃了 1.5 份」 |

领券、下单、撤单和营养记账都会先展示具体摘要，再取得明确确认。默认订单护栏为单笔 100 元、每日 3 单；确认时还会复核金额。遇到 `delivery_unknown`，先到官方 App 核对订单，停止重复提交。

evidence.heading: 当前版本与使用边界
evidence.text:
- **现行发行是 v0.1.0 Python/Qt 版。** Tauri 2、原创默认形象和系统密钥链的参赛版本处于 M0 阶段，进度见 [M0 报告](docs/contest/M0-REPORT.md)。个人凭证保存在本机 `.env`；公开试用凭证位于源码 `.env.trial`。
- 早期鲸鲸九姿态和全动作 GIF 相册属于后续源码功能，需要[本机导入或录制](docs/USER-GUIDE.md#可选动作与-gif-相册)，v0.1.0 发行包不附带这些本机文件。
- 本机用量只反映读取到的日志；厂商额度、余额和币种按各来源分别显示。未知数据保持未知，idle / Stop 表示会话状态，任务成功需要明确完成证据。
- 桌面定时提醒依赖桌宠运行；Agent 自动提醒依赖宿主活动。终端内 GIF 播放取决于宿主的图像资源能力。
- 真实账号订单、付款及完整宿主对话仍待人工验收；旧桌面心跳、前台性能和部分素材测试仍有历史 RED。各项范围见[验证记录](docs/README.md#当前交付记录)。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
