evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Xiryn


  The open-source personal agent. It does everything Muse, Grok Bot and Dots do — on your own computer.
  Each agent gets its own Linux desktop in Docker, so it works in the background and never interrupts what you're doing on your laptop.
  Your data stays on your disk. Bring any model. Control it from anywhere through Telegram.



  
  
  
  
  



  xiryn.com ·
  Quick start ·
  Why Xiryn ·
  Compare ·
  Telegram ·
  Architecture ·
  Contribute



  


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9769ff2-b9ae-426c-a47e-629910b11155

---

This year every major lab shipped a personal agent that works on a cloud machine for you — **Muse** from Meta, **Grok Bot** from xAI, **Dots** from OpenAI. They're impressive. They're also closed, gated behind subscriptions, and they run on someone else's servers with your conversations, your logins and — when they shop for you — your payment details.

**Xiryn is the same idea as an open-source personal agent you run yourself.** Clone it, add your API keys, and you have a team of agents that each own a Linux desktop in Docker — working in the background while you keep using your laptop — remember what matters, browse and research the web, write and run code, and hand work to one another. Nothing is stored anywhere but your computer, and you can message them from your phone.

**One command sets everything up** — Git, Node.js, Docker, the agents' desktop — and starts Xiryn:

```bash
# macOS / Linux
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SouravBeraAkaSpeed/xiryn/main/setup.sh | bash
```

```powershell
# Windows (PowerShell)
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SouravBeraAkaSpeed/xiryn/main/setup.ps1 | iex
```

**No API key? Run it free.** Add `--local` and the same command also installs [Ollama](https://ollama.com), downlo

evidence.heading: Why Xiryn
evidence.text:
**🔒 Private by design.** No account, no sign-up. Conversations, memory, settings and keys live in a single SQLite file on your disk; logins and cards, if you choose to save them, live in an encrypted vault whose key your operating system holds — and agents never see them. Even the agents' machines run on your computer. The only things that leave it are the calls you configure (your model provider, plus Firecrawl or Telegram if you turn them on). Run a local model through Ollama and not even your prompts leave.

**🖥️ It never touches your computer.** Every agent works on its **own** sandboxed Linux desktop — a Docker container with a shell, files and a real Chromium — completely separate from your system. It doesn't move your mouse, take over your screen or read your files. Watch a movie, play a game or keep coding while it works. Or watch it work, live, and take the wheel whenever you want.

**📱 Control it from anywhere.** Pair Telegram in two minutes — scan a QR code and you're done. No public URL, no tunnel, no port forwarding: Xiryn polls Telegram from your machine. Your agents answer from wherever you are, with live progress and screenshots.

**🧠 Any model, your keys.** OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Pick a model per agent. No subscription — you pay providers directly for what you use.

**🗑️ Disposable machines.** Reset an agent and its container is destroyed. Delete it and it's gone. Turn on auto-delete and workstations vanish after every session — while the agent's memory stays safe on your disk.

**👥 Agents that work as a team.** Put several agents in a squad. Ask any of them; they delegate to whoever fits the job — each on its own model and its own machine.

evidence.heading: How it compares
evidence.text:
|  | **Xiryn** | Hosted agentsMuse · Grok Bot · Dots | Local computer-use agentse.g. OpenClaw |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Source | ✅ Open source (MIT) | ❌ Closed | ✅ Open source (MIT) |
| Where the agent works | Its own sandboxed desktop (Docker, on your machine) | Vendor's cloud computer | Your computer |
| Uses your mouse, screen or files | **Never** | No — vendor cloud | Yes — shell, files and apps on your machine |
| Browses from | **Your own connection** | Vendor data centers | Your own connection |
| Where your data lives | **Your disk** | Vendor's servers | Your disk |
| Account required | **No** | Yes | No |
| Card on file to shop for you | **Your choice** — encrypted on your machine, used only after you approve each payment | Stored with the vendor | Depends on setup |
| Models | **Any — 11 providers, incl. local** | The vendor's own | Many |
| Remote control | Telegram | Vendor apps & integrations | Chat apps |
| Price | **Free** + pay-as-you-go APIs | Paid plans / subscriptions | Free + APIs |

Based on public launch coverage as of October 2026. These products move fast — corrections welcome.

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
**Agents with a job**
Name, role, standing orders, and a model of their own. Start from [16 ready-made agents and 4 squads](#ready-made-agents) or write your own.

**Routines — tasks on a schedule**
"Every morning at 8, brief me on…" — say it in the chat or set it up on the Routines page. Daily, weekdays, weekly, every few hours, or once. It runs on its own, even with the browser closed, and tells you when it's done.

**A workstation per agent**
A Docker container with a shell, a persistent home folder and a 1280×800 desktop with Chromium — created on first use, stopped when idle, never touching your own files.

**Live desktop, take over any time**
Watch the agent click and type in real time. Hit **Take over** and it pauses; hand it back with a note and it picks up from what you did.




**Long-term memory**
Agents save what matters about you and your work; every thread sees it. Inspect, add or delete notes any time.

**Web research**
Search and clean page reading through Firecrawl, with cited sources.

**Durable turns**
Close the tab mid-task — the agent keeps going. Reopen and you're re-attached to the live stream. Stop it any time.

**It tells you when it's done**
A chime and a desktop notification when an agent finishes, fails or needs you — and a Telegram message when you're away from the computer.

**Talk instead of typing**
Hit the mic and speak your request. It uses your browser's speech recognition — on the device itself where the browser supports it, so your voice never leaves your computer.

**Free local models in one click**
Settings → Local models shows Ollama, downloads models with a progress bar and makes one the default. Replies on local models are marked *free*.

**Know what every reply costs**
Each reply shows its price; the Usage page adds it up by da

evidence.heading: What can it do?
evidence.text:
Anything that can be done with a terminal, a browser and a desktop — while you get on with your day:

- **Build and debug** — clone a repo, install, run the tests, fix what fails, show you the diff.
- **Research** — search, read primary sources, and come back with a cited summary.
- **Write** — launch posts, docs, reports, saved as files on its workstation.
- **Work the web** — fill forms, compare options, prepare a booking or an order. When a site needs your login, a payment or a CAPTCHA, the agent **stops and hands you the screen**; your card never touches Xiryn.
- **Run as a team** — ask a squad, and the right specialist takes it.

Agents ask when they need a decision, confirm before anything irreversible, and remember what you tell them.

evidence.heading: Quick start

evidence.heading: Architecture
evidence.text:
```mermaid
graph LR
    you([You · browser]) -->|localhost| app
    phone([You · Telegram]) -.->|Bot API| tg[Telegram]
    tg -.->|long-poll from your machine| app

    subgraph machine [Your computer]
        app[Xiryn · Next.js server]
        app --> runtime[Agent runtime]
        app --> db[(SQLite · data/xiryn.db)]
        runtime --> db
        runtime -->|docker| ws[Workstations · one container per agent]

    runtime -.->|your key, optional| firecrawl[Firecrawl]

One process, one file. The Next.js server serves the UI, runs agent turns in-process through the [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev), and owns the SQLite database — no queue, no worker, no backend of ours. Details in **[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)**.

| `lib/workstation.ts`, `lib/docker.ts`, `workstation/` | Agents' machines: containers, desktop control and the image they run |
| `lib/web.ts` | Firecrawl |
| `db/` | Drizzle schema and migrations |

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Replay your coding agent sessions as a map and a timeline

evidence.heading: agentplay
evidence.text:
**See what your coding agent actually did. Replay every session as a map and a timeline: what it read, what it edited, what failed, and what it shipped. Local, open source, works across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, Kiro, Gemini CLI and Antigravity CLI.**

```bash
uvx agentplay
```

That one command finds the agent sessions already on your machine, builds a redacted replay of each one, and opens a local viewer. No account and no API key are required, and your session data never leaves your machine. The only network call is an optional email signup in the viewer, described under [Privacy](#privacy); set `AGENTPLAY_NO_NETWORK=1` to switch it off.



Screenshot of the bundled demo session (synthetic data). Dark mode: [docs/images/explorer-dark.png](docs/images/explorer-dark.png).

If agentplay shows you something about your agent you didn't know, a ⭐ helps other people find it.

evidence.heading: Why this exists
evidence.text:
Your agent's transcripts already record what it did: which files it read before editing, which commands it retried, which MCP servers failed, where the context window filled up, and which subagents came back empty. That data sits in `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor` and similar folders, and almost nobody looks at it.

agentplay makes that data readable. Every session becomes a map of everything it touched and a timeline you can play back, so you can answer questions like:

- What did the agent read before it edited this file, and what did it never open?
- Which commands failed, and how many times did it retry the same one?
- Where did the context window fill up, and what did the subagents bring back?
- Which PRs, commits and tickets did the session produce?

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
You need Python 3.11 or newer. agentplay has **no runtime dependencies** beyond the standard library.

```bash
uvx agentplay                 # run without installing (uv: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)
pipx run agentplay            # same, with pipx
pip install agentplay         # or install it into an environment
```

**Setting up with a coding agent?** Point it at [`install.md`](install.md): step-by-step instructions written for an agent, covering every option above and how to check the viewer is up.


From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Entelligence-AI/agentplay
cd agentplay
make setup        # python venv + viewer node_modules
make viewer       # build the web viewer and copy it into the Python package
make run          # agentplay view, from the checkout
```




Windows

The default session folders (`C:\Users\<you>\.claude`, `.codex`, and so on) are found automatically; no path configuration is needed.

`make` works under Git Bash or MSYS2 (it uses `python\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` on Windows) and in WSL. Without `make`, run the equivalent steps in PowerShell:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Entelligence-AI/agentplay
cd agentplay
uv venv python\.venv
uv pip install --python python\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -e "python[dev]" jsonschema
cd viewer
corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
corepack pnpm run build
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force ..\python\src\agentplay\viewer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Copy-Item -Recurse dist ..\python\src\agentplay\viewer
cd ..\python
.venv\Scripts\agentplay view
```

The viewer needs the pnpm version pinned in `viewer/package.json` (10.x). An older pnpm, such as 8, rejects the lockfile. `corepack pnpm ...` (as above) runs the pinned version without changing your global pnpm.



To try the viewer on its own, run `pnpm

evidence.heading: Using the viewer
evidence.text:
```bash
agentplay            # same as `agentplay view`
```

```
Found 412 sessions  claude-code 301 · codex 88 · cursor 23
Built 412 new, 0 unchanged, 0 skipped in 9.4s. Nothing left this machine.
Viewer → http://127.0.0.1:7317/   (Ctrl+C to stop)
```

Illustrative counts. Builds are incremental, so later runs only rebuild sessions whose transcript changed.

In the viewer:

- **The map** is a radial tree of everything the session touched: repos, directories and files (seen, read or edited), shell verbs, MCP servers and tools, skills, subagents, web hosts, error classes, models, and the outputs it produced (commits, PRs, tickets).
- **The timeline** plays the session back at 1x, 4x or 16x. Scrub it, or switch between step axis and wall-clock time. Its lanes show prompts, errors, delays, outputs, edits, exploration, MCP, skills, tools, model, cost, tokens, subagents and context size, with compactions marked.
- **Keyboard:** Space plays and pauses. Arrow keys step, Shift steps by 10. `E`, `X`, `D`, `O` and `R` jump to the next edit, error, delay, output or retry.
- **Scopes:** pick a task, a model, or a single subagent ("agent lens"). The whole explorer re-scopes to it.
- **Tasks:** a session is split into tasks, usually one per prompt you gave it, each labelled with the start of that prompt. Labels live only in your local index, are added when the viewer loads a session, and are never written into a map (see [Privacy](#privacy)).
- **Errors:** the Errors tab lists every error in the session, grouped by class and ranked by the longest run of the same failing command. Click a row to seek the replay to it. The error, PR and subagent badges on the session header narrow the timeline the same way.

Every view is a URL, so a link to a moment in a session reopens it for anyone w

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
```
 ~/.claude  ~/.codex  ~/.cursor  ~/.copilot  VS Code  opencode.db  ~/.kiro
      │         │         │          │          │          │          │
      │         │   materialize.py (decode SQLite / dir stores → NDJSON cache, read-only)
      ▼         ▼         ▼          ▼          ▼          ▼          ▼
 _core parsers (one per agent) ──► spans ──► builder.py ──► agentplay/v1 documents
 (Claude Code is read straight from JSONL by builder.py for subagents + per-request tokens)
                                               │
                                               ▼
                               ~/.agentplay/maps/*.json + index.json   (store.py)
                                               │
                                     server.py + viewer (127.0.0.1 only)
```

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `python/src/agentplay/_core/` | Transcript parsers and pure metrics: spans, tool taxonomy, pricing |
| `python/src/agentplay/builder.py` | Spans or JSONL → `agentplay/v1`, including redaction, path modes, outcomes, retries, delays, PR detection |
| `python/src/agentplay/materialize.py` | Decoders for database-backed agents (OpenCode, Cursor, Kiro) |
| `python/src/agentplay/discover.py` | Where each agent keeps its sessions; builds the parser over them |
| `python/src/agentplay/{store,pipeline}.py` | Incremental build into `~/.agentplay` |
| `python/src/agentplay/server.py` | Local read-only API and static viewer |
| `viewer/src/core/` | Pure TypeScript model: tree, radial layout, playback, signals, scopes, canvas painters. No React |
| `viewer/src/explorer/` | The React explorer |
| `viewer/src/data/` | `SessionMapSource` implementations: local server, dropped files, demo |
| `schema/` | JSON Schema for the format |

evidence.heading: Known limitations
evidence.text:
- **Cursor sessions have no token or cost figures.** Cursor does not write billed usage to disk, and agentplay will not call Cursor's API to fetch it.
- **Whole-file writes and "created vs modified".** A map is built after the session, so the builder cannot always tell whether a `Write` created a file or overwrote one. The map records such a write as an edit only when the session had already seen the file.
- **Costs are estimates** from public list prices in `_core/pricing.py`. Plan, enterprise and batch pricing are not modelled.
- **Large sessions** are capped at 20,000 events per map (flagged `truncated`). Transcripts over 512 MB are skipped.
- **Windows** is supported by the parsers but less tested than macOS and Linux. CI runs the Python tests on Windows for every supported Python version. Building, the viewer, `list`, `export` and `import` have been run end to end from a source install on Windows 11 with Python 3.12 (see the Windows notes under [Install](#install)). Paths outside the user's home, such as `%APPDATA%` for Copilot in VS Code, are exercised less.

[Entelligence](https://entelligence.ai), which maintains agentplay, offers a hosted team edition. It adds review comments traced back to the session edit that caused them, cross-engineer views, team-level recommendations, and measured adoption. The open-source tool does not depend on it and will not be degraded to sell it.

evidence.heading: 🤔 为什么要做这个项目？
evidence.text:
写一个"能跑"的 Agent 只要 20 行代码。但把它放进公司、让成千上万人用，你马上会遇到这些问题：

> 模型 429 了怎么办？Agent 陷入死循环一晚上烧了 2000 美元怎么办？用户在文档里藏一句"忽略之前的指令"就能让 Agent 重置管理员密码怎么办？A 公司的数据出现在 B 公司的回答里怎么办？改了一行 prompt，怎么知道有没有把别的场景改坏？进程在 Agent 执行到一半时重启了怎么办？

**这些问题决定了一个 Agent 能不能上线，而绝大多数教程只教那 20 行。**

| | 常见 Agent 教程 | 本项目 |
|---|---|---|
| 目标 | 让 Agent 跑起来 | 让 Agent **在生产中可靠、安全、可控地**跑起来 |
| 方式 | 调用框架 API（黑盒） | **从零手写每一层**（核心约 3800 行 + 多进程模块约 2000 行，每行都能看懂） |
| 覆盖 | 循环 + 工具 | LLM 必备知识、循环、工具、上下文、常见架构、编排、**工程考量全景**；重试熔断降级、检查点恢复、提示词注入防御、RBAC、人工审批、审计、追踪、评估；高并发与分布式执行、成本优化、权限感知 RAG、灰度发布与事故响应；检索质量、记忆系统、MCP 与沙箱、主流框架对照、Agent 数据、评估方法论、提示词优化与测试时计算、编码 Agent、主动式 Agent；**asyncio 并发、真实多进程执行（租约、fencing、kill -9 接手、网络分区）、Postgres/Redis/Temporal/OpenTelemetry/LiteLLM/Cedar 生产落地、多 worker 参考服务与压测** |
| 讲法 | 一种做法 | 企业问题卡片：**每个问题 2–4 种方案对比**，讲清怎么选 |
| 验证 | 看起来能用 | 每课都有**带自动化测试的练习**，离线、确定性、零成本；说"并发"就用在途峰值证明，说"多进程 / 崩溃接手"就起真实进程、发真实信号 |
| 模型 | 绑定某家厂商 | 任何 OpenAI 兼容接口（OpenAI / DeepSeek / Qwen / vLLM / 各类模型网关） |
| 语言 | 单语 | **中英双语**：每份讲义和文档都有等价的英文版（`*.en.md`） |

evidence.heading: ⚖️ 先说清楚：每一层做到了什么
evidence.text:
整个项目只有**一套** async 实现，从第 02 课用到第 31 课；往上每一层只是把"状态存在哪里"换成更强的组件，接口不变：

| 层 | 是什么 | 做到了什么（都有测试证明） | 局限（实话） |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agentkit/` 核心 | async Agent 运行时：主循环、工具、上下文、编排、可靠性、安全、追踪、评估 | 一个进程里同时推进成百上千个会话；只读工具并行；真取消（断开即停）、超时、舱壁、流式；子进程硬超时 | 状态默认在内存或本地文件；注入检测和 PII 脱敏是正则 |
| [`agentkit/distributed/`](agentkit/distributed/) | 多进程执行：租约队列、fence 检查点、跨进程幂等 / 限流 / 并发槽位 / 熔断器、worker 进程、`WorkerPool` | 真实进程上的 kill -9 接手（副作用不重复）、SIGSTOP 僵尸醒来后写不进去、SIGTERM 优雅停机、多进程抢任务不重复（第 12–13 课） | 基于 SQLite，只能在一台机器上；同一时刻一个写者 |
| [`agentkit/contrib/`](agentkit/contrib/) | 成熟组件适配器：Postgres、Redis、Temporal、OpenTelemetry、LiteLLM、Cedar、护栏分类器 | 同一套队列 / 检查点接口换成 Postgres 就能多机共享；真实 TCP 网络分区下旧 worker 被 fence 拒绝（第 26–29 课） | 用嵌入式 Postgres、fakeredis、Temporal 开发服务器测试；Redis 主从切换、集群分片、多区域没有实测 |
| [`production/`](production/) | 把上面串起来的参考服务：API、worker、压测、故障注入、docker-compose、Kubernetes | 压测与故障注入数字见第 31 课 | 参考实现，不是托管产品；本机没有 Docker，部署配置没有实际启动过 |

逐模块"做到了什么 → 还差什么 → 换成什么 → 怎么迁移"，见 [📋 生产就绪指南](docs/production-readiness.md)。

evidence.heading: 🗺 你将亲手造出的系统
evidence.text:
```mermaid
flowchart TB
    U["用户请求 + 可信身份tenant / user / roles"] --> API["API 进程入队 → 202（第 12 课）"]
    API --> Q[("持久化任务队列租约 / fencing / 死信")]
    Q --> W["worker 进程 × N崩溃接手 · 优雅停机（第 13 课）"]
    W --> IG
    subgraph Hooks["🛡 钩子层：横切关注点（第 08-11 课）"]
        IG["InputGuard注入检测"]
        PP["PermissionPolicyRBAC + 人工审批"]
        TG["ToolOutputGuard不可信数据隔离"]
        OG["OutputGuardPII 脱敏"]
        BG["BudgetHooktoken/金额/步数"]
        AU["AuditLog审计"]
    end
    IG --> LOOP
    subgraph Core["⚙️ Agent 核心（第 01-07 课）"]
        LOOP["Agent 主循环LLM ⇄ 工具"] --> CTX["上下文策略窗口 / 摘要"]
        LOOP --> REG["工具注册表Schema 校验 / 超时 / 幂等"]
        LOOP --> WF["编排模式路由 / 并行 / 多 Agent"]
    end
    LOOP --> RL["ResilientLLM重试 → 熔断 → 降级"]
    RL --> GW["模型网关 / 任意 OpenAI 兼容接口"]
    LOOP --> CP[("检查点崩溃恢复 / 暂停审批")]
    LOOP --> TR["Tracer链路追踪 → HTML 查看器"]
    TR --> EV["Evals评估集 + CI 门禁"]
    PP -.拦截.-> REG
    TG -.包裹.-> REG
```

用 `agentkit` 组装一个企业级 Agent 只需要这样（每一个参数背后都是一节课）：

```python
import asyncio
from agentkit import *

agent = Agent(
    llm=ResilientLLM(default_llm(), fallbacks=[default_llm("gpt-5.6-luna")]),   # 第 08 课：重试/熔断/降级
    tools=[search_kb, create_ticket, reset_password],                            # 第 03 课：工具设计
    system_prompt="你是 IT 服务台助手。" + UNTRUSTED_DATA_RULE,                    # 第 09 课：不可信数据规则
    hooks=[
        InputGuard(),                                                            # 第 09 课：输入检测
        PermissionPolicy(role_tools={"employee": {"search_kb", "create_ticket"},
                                     "it_admin": {"*"}}),                        # 第 09 课：RBAC + 高危审批
        ToolOutputGuard(), OutputGuard(),                                        # 第 09 课：隔离 + 脱敏
        BudgetHook(max_cost_usd=0.10, max_tool_calls=20),                        # 第 08 课：预算

evidence.heading: 🚀 快速开始
evidence.text:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/heaven999b/hello-agent-system.git
cd hello-agent-system
make setup          # 创建 .venv 并安装（核心依赖只有 openai + pydantic）
```

编辑 `.env`，填入任意 OpenAI 兼容接口：

```bash
LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1     # 或 DeepSeek / 通义 / 本地 vLLM / 模型网关
LLM_API_KEY=sk-xxx
LLM_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini                       # 需要支持 function calling
```

```bash
make check-env                                  # 检查模型连通性与工具调用能力
.venv/bin/python lessons/00_overview/demo.py    # 看一眼你将要造出的东西
```

> 💡 **没有 API key？** 所有 demo 都支持 `--offline`（用剧本模型 `ScriptedLLM` 运行），所有练习和测试都是离线的。你可以零成本学完整个课程。

evidence.heading: 📚 学习路线
evidence.text:
课程分四部分：**第一部分学会"怎么造"，第二部分学会"企业里出了问题怎么选方案"，第三部分学会"怎么让 Agent 持续变好"，第四部分学会"怎么用成熟组件真正上生产"**。前两部分加综合实战约 6 小时（主线）；第三部分约 3.5 小时、第四部分约 3 小时，是进阶路线。赶时间可以走 [4 小时速通路线](lessons/00_overview/README.md)（每课只读开头的"核心路径"）。

- **第一部分**：概念 → 从零实现 → 练习。以第 07 课"工程考量全景"收尾：20 个工程维度，每个维度都分成**通用必查点**（任何项目都要做）和**情境触发点**（"当……时，要考虑……"），作为进入第二部分的地图。
- **第二部分**：每节课由若干张**企业问题卡片**组成：真实场景（带具体数字）→ 为什么直觉方案会翻车 → 2–5 种方案对比（优点 / 缺点 / 适用规模）→ 怎么选 → 代码实现。
- **第三部分**：进阶的构建块（检索、记忆、MCP、框架），以及让 Agent 持续变好的 ML 闭环（数据 → 评估 → 优化），最后是编码 Agent 与主动式 Agent 等应用前沿。
- **第四部分**：把 SQLite 和进程内的状态换成成熟组件，**接口不变**。每课都讲"单机版为什么不够 → 组件选型对比 → 适配器怎么接 → 运维要点与坑"，并用真实进程、真实并发、故障注入证明它扛得住。

每节课的流程都一样：**读讲义 → 跑 demo → 写练习 → `make lesson N=xx` 让测试变绿 → 过自测清单**。每课开头都标注了一篇 📖 必读论文或文章。

evidence.text:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | [企业级 Agent 全景图](lessons/00_overview/README.md) | 10m | 什么时候该用、不该用 Agent；企业级比 Demo 多了哪些层 | — |
| 01 | [**LLM 与 Agent 开发必备知识**](lessons/01_llm_essentials/README.md) | 20m | token 与计费、非确定性、function calling 的真实机制、结构化输出、**流式工具调用参数的拼接**、推理模型、提示词工程 | [llm.py](agentkit/llm.py) |
| 02 | [Agent 循环的本质](lessons/02_agent_loop/README.md) | 30m | **asyncio 从零讲起**（事件循环、await、gather、取消、阻塞陷阱）；手写 async Agent 主循环、消息协议、停止条件、Hook 中间件 | [agent.py](agentkit/agent.py) |

| 04 | [上下文工程与记忆](lessons/04_context_memory/README.md) | 15m | 安全截断、摘要压缩、工具结果清理、长期记忆隔离 | [context.py](agentkit/context.py) · [memory.py](agentkit/memory.py) |
| 05 | [**常见 Agent 架构**](lessons/05_agent_architectures/README.md) | 20m | ReAct / Plan-and-Execute / ReWOO / Reflection / CodeAct、5 种多 Agent 拓扑、Deep Research / 编码 Agent 等产品架构拆解 | [workflows.py](agentkit/workflows.py) |
| 06 | [编排模式：Workflow 与多 Agent](lessons/06_orchestration/README.md) | 15m | 路由、并行、编排者-执行者、评估-优化、Agent 即工具 | [workflows.py](agentkit/workflows.py) |

kind_reason.text: 按课程与练习讲解企业智能体系统设计。

summary.text: 从零构建企业 Agent 系统的中英双语课程，覆盖异步运行、可靠性、安全、评估、多进程执行与生产组件适配。

value.text: 把能调用模型的演示逐层扩展到可恢复、可控成本和权限隔离的系统。

mechanism.text: 课程共用 async 运行时，先用本地状态与 SQLite 验证执行机制，再保持接口接入成熟基础设施。

inspiration.text: 可把生产问题写成场景卡，先比较适用规模与代价，再给对应实现。

limitations.text: SQLite 多进程版限制在单机且单写者；核心注入检测和个人信息脱敏为正则实现。

how_to.text: make setup 后配置兼容模型接口；无 API key 时可用 ScriptedLLM 离线运行演示与练习。

github_projects.description: Walk through a diff the way a senior engineer reads it. A read-only TUI that turns a git change into a guided tour.
github_projects.description_zh: 按高级工程师的方式浏览差异。一个只读 TUI，将 git 改动转化为导览式阅读。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Walk through a diff the way a senior engineer reads it. A read-only TUI that turns a git change into a guided tour.

evidence.heading: diff-tour
evidence.text:
Walk through a diff the way a senior engineer reads it.

**English** | [日本語](README.ja.md)

[](https://github.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/releases)
[](https://github.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](LICENSE)



A tour of a branch that adds coupons: what the change is for, how the usage limit is enforced, a question to think about, and the answer: applying a coupon twice to one order uses it up twice.

> [!NOTE]
> diff-tour is an early release. The tour format and the screens may still change.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
You need git and one of [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex), [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli), [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) 2 or [Copilot CLI](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli), signed in.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/main/install.sh | sh
cd your-repo
tour
```

Then it goes like this:

1. **Setup** (first time only): choose the display language and the LLM that writes the tour. Both have a recommended choice selected, so press Enter twice.
2. **Pick a change**: the changes you can tour are listed, with your current branch selected. Press Enter.
3. **Writing**: the LLM writes the tour. This takes 2 to 5 minutes.
4. **The tour**: **→** goes forward, **←** goes back, **q** quits.

If `tour` is not found, add the line the install script printed to your shell profile.

Other ways to install are in [Install](#install), and an example repository to try is in [First run](#first-run).

evidence.heading: What it is
evidence.text:
AI can write code that works. It does not teach you *why* the code is written that way, or what a reviewer would worry about.

`tour` turns a git change into a guided tour you step through with two keys, **→** and **←**. The tour shows what a senior engineer looks at when they read the change:

- **How they read it.** What the change is for, where to spend time, and which files to jump to next, including files that did not change.
- **What they ask.** Does it keep the promises the old code kept? What happens when something fails, or runs twice? Can it be rolled out and rolled back safely? Who can call it, and with what input? What happens at 100 times the data? Is the next change easier or harder? Would the tests fail if the code broke?
- **How they judge.** Which findings must be fixed and which are only suggestions or nits, what looks risky but is fine and why, what is done well, and whether the change makes the codebase better overall.
- **Where they stop and say "wait".** These come as questions, so you can predict the answer before you see it.

This view comes from what experienced engineers have written down about reading and reviewing code, collected in [`internal/generate/lessons`](internal/generate/lessons) (in Japanese). The LLM reads it before every tour.

The tour is written by an LLM you already use: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode or Copilot CLI. `tour` is read-only. It never changes your files or your repository.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
```text
 your repository                          cache directory (deleted after writing)
 ───────────────                          ──────────────────────────────────────
 git archive <base>  ──────────────────▶  base/          files before the change
 git archive <head>  ──────────────────▶  head/          files after the change
 git diff            ──────────────────▶  change.diff
 git log             ──────────────────▶  commits.txt
 (built into tour)   ──────────────────▶  lessons/       what senior engineers have learned
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
                      Claude Code / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode / Copilot, started in that directory
                      with read-only permissions. It reads, then writes the
                      tour as JSON.
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
 tour checks every file and line the JSON points to. If something is wrong,
 it asks the LLM to fix only that (up to 2 times). The tour is saved.
                                                 │
                                                 ▼
 tour shows the tour. The code on screen is read from git at the right commit,
 never copied from the LLM's reply.
```

1. **Export.** `tour` reads your repository with `git archive`, `git diff` and `git log`, and writes the files into a new directory in your cache. Only files that git tracks are exported. When you tour uncommitted changes, untracked files that are not ignored are exported too. Files in `.gitignore`, such as `.env`, are never exported.
2. **Write.** `tour` starts the LLM's command-line tool in that directory with a fixed prompt and read-only permissions (see below). This takes 2 to

evidence.heading: What the LLM can and cannot do
evidence.text:
Sending your code to an LLM is a real decision, so here is exactly what happens.

**Sent to the LLM you chose:**

- the files of your repository at the two commits being compared, the diff, and the commit messages. Only tracked files, plus untracked files that are not ignored when you tour uncommitted changes
- the prompt in [`internal/generate/prompts`](internal/generate/prompts)
- when you press <kbd>?</kbd>: your question and the whole tour, with the same files

They go to the provider of that tool (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google or GitHub; with OpenCode, the provider of the model you use), under the terms of your account with them. `tour` itself makes no network requests, has no server, and collects no telemetry.

**Not possible for the LLM:**

- reading files outside the export directory, including your real working tree, `.git` and your home directory
- reading files ignored by `.gitignore`, because they are never exported
- writing, editing or deleting any file
- running commands that change anything, or reaching the network
- using MCP servers, plugins, extensions or web search

This is enforced by the flags `tour` passes to each tool, not only by the prompt.


Claude Code: tools limited to Read, Grep and Glob

```text
claude -p --restricted --strict-mcp-config --tools Read,Grep,Glob
       --permission-mode dontAsk --permission-prompts none --no-session-persistence
```

- `--restricted` removes the command and web tools, and keeps file tools inside the working directory
- `--strict-mcp-config` loads no MCP servers
- `--tools Read,Grep,Glob` leaves only the three read-only tools
- `--permission-mode dontAsk` refuses anything that would need permission, without asking
- `--no-session-persistence` saves no session

Source: [`internal/generate/claude.go`](internal/gener

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
**macOS and Linux**

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/main/install.sh | sh
```

This downloads the latest release for your OS and CPU, checks it against `checksums.txt`, and puts `tour` in `~/.local/bin`. If that directory is not on your `PATH`, it prints the line to add. To choose the place or the version:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/main/install.sh | TOUR_INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local/bin TOUR_VERSION=v0.1.0 sh
```

**With Go 1.27 or later** (any OS)

```sh
go install github.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/cmd/tour@latest
```

This puts `tour` in `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`, usually `~/go/bin`.

**Windows** (PowerShell; not tested on Windows yet)

```powershell
$tag = (Invoke-RestMethod https://api.github.com/repos/init-co-jp/diff-tour/releases/latest).tag_name
$zip = "diff-tour_$($tag.TrimStart('v'))_windows_amd64.zip"
$dir = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\tour"
Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/init-co-jp/diff-tour/releases/download/$tag/$zip" -OutFile "$env:TEMP\$zip"
Expand-Archive "$env:TEMP\$zip" -DestinationPath $dir -Force
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User") + ";$dir", "User")
```

Open a new terminal afterwards. On ARM, use `windows_arm64`.

Check the install with `tour --version`.

evidence.heading: What a step can show
evidence.text:
- code and diffs, read from git at the right commit, with syntax highlighting
- code that is **not** in the repository, such as a naive version or a possible fix, labeled **Example**
- flow and timeline diagrams
- database schemas before and after the change, computed by applying the migrations to an in-memory SQLite database (SQLite migrations only for now)
- tables of example data
- questions to think about before the answer appears on the next step
- answers to your own questions about a step, saved with the tour (when you play a tour file, they last only until you quit)

Every explanation is labeled with how it is known:

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Verified** | backed by code, tests or commit messages in this repository |
| **From the code** | inferred from how the code is structured |
| **Senior view** | general design judgment, not checked against this repository |

github_projects.name: SOMA
github_projects.description: Desktop app for designing parametric 3D models in CadQuery together with the coding agent of your choice
github_projects.description_zh: 桌面应用，可在 CadQuery 中设计参数化 3D 模型，并可结合你选择的编码智能体使用。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Desktop app for designing parametric 3D models in CadQuery together with the coding agent of your choice

evidence.heading: SOMA
evidence.text:
**Solid Object Modeling with Agents.** A desktop app for designing parametric 3D models together with a coding agent.

**[somacad.app](https://somacad.app)** · [Download](https://somacad.app/download/) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3294d1e4-1f06-477d-9770-c91f3470330d


You tell the agent what you need. It writes the model as Python code with [CadQuery](https://github.com/CadQuery/cadquery), SOMA builds it and shows the result. You look at it, measure it, point at what is wrong, and the agent changes the code.

evidence.heading: What is SOMA?
evidence.text:
A CAD program where the AI does the CAD and you are the designer. SOMA brings together the three parts this needs: a code workspace with a terminal for your agent, an editor and Git for every version; a 3D viewer that rebuilds the model on every change; and instructions for the agent, with rules, skills and a command line tool.

It's vibe coding, but for CAD. Made for makers and tinkerers who need a case, a bracket or a mount for their project and don't want to spend hours in a CAD program to get it. Describe or sketch the part, check the result, export it, print it. You don't have to know CadQuery. The code is there if you want to change a dimension yourself.

SOMA is not an agent of its own. Any CLI agent that can read files and run commands works: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI or whatever comes next. It runs in a normal terminal inside the model folder, SOMA detects the common ones and can start them. You install and log in to them yourself, so your subscription, your model choice and your permission settings stay yours. SOMA gives the agent a command line tool (`soma build`, `soma analyze`, `soma render` …) and an `AGENTS.md` with the rules of the project.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Download SOMA from [somacad.app/download](https://somacad.app/download/), which offers the right package for your system, or from the [releases](https://github.com/Kai-Jungsthoefel/SOMA/releases): an installer or a portable ZIP for Windows, an AppImage or tar.gz for Linux, a dmg for macOS (Apple Silicon). Python, CadQuery, Git and CalculiX are included.

- You need a CLI agent installed and logged in, for example Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI or Gemini CLI. SOMA does not bring one
- The installed app takes over 1 GB of disk space, most of it for Python, CadQuery and OpenCascade
- The packages are not signed yet. On Windows, SmartScreen warns on the first start ("More info" > "Run anyway"). For the portable ZIP, tick "Unblock" in its Properties before extracting to avoid the warning, and extract it to a local folder. On macOS, open the app the first time with right-click > Open
- Linux needs glibc 2.31 or newer
- SOMA shows on its start page when a new version is out. Download it from the website or the releases page

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
1. Start SOMA and click **New model** on the start page. It starts from a small example, a box with a lid.
2. Start your agent with the **+** above the terminal on the right. SOMA lists the agents it found on your computer.
3. Tell the agent what you need, for example *"A case for a Raspberry Pi 5 with vents in the lid, printed in PETG"*. SOMA builds the model on every change and shows it.
4. Click parts, measure, or draw on the view and send it to the agent until it fits. Then export it from the menu, for example as STL or 3MF.

Press F1 in the app for a short guide with numbered screenshots. The agent knows the same guide, so you can also just ask it how something works.

evidence.heading: Agent apps (Codex app, Claude Desktop)
evidence.text:
Instead of an agent in SOMA's terminal you can use a desktop agent app that works on a local folder and can run commands, for example the Codex app or Claude Code in Claude Desktop.

1. Open the model in SOMA and keep SOMA open.
2. Click the **+** above the terminal and choose **Copy path for agent app**. For a model you opened with **Open folder**, the path is simply that folder.
3. In the agent app, open this path as the project folder and tell the agent what you need.

**Send to agent** also copies its note to the clipboard: paste it into the agent app. A markup note names its picture in `.soma/feedback/`, which the agent opens itself. A chat without file access and commands does not work.

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Models as code:** Python with CadQuery, rebuilt on every change
- **One file per model:** a `.soma` file holds code, result and history, like a CAD file
- **Point, measure, draw:** click a part, measure exactly or sketch on the view, and send it to the agent
- **Section and explode:** cut the model open, take an assembly apart
- **Parameters:** change the values the agent made adjustable, without touching the code
- **History:** every step of the agent on a timeline, preview and restore old states
- **Standard parts and STEP import:** screws, nuts, washers and heat-set inserts from dimension tables, purchased parts as STEP
- **Skills:** rule sets for the agent, such as 3D printing, CNC, laser cutting, sheet metal and tolerances, switched on per model. Edit them or add your own
- **Analysis:** overhangs, wall thickness, and strength with FEM (CalculiX)
- **Animation:** motion described in Python, played in the viewer or rendered to video
- **Export:** STEP, STL, 3MF, DXF and more, technical drawings as PDF
- **Plain CadQuery in and out:** start from an existing CadQuery script, export the model as a script for CQ-editor or VS Code
- **Your own folder:** open an existing folder, for example a Git repository, and use SOMA there. Agent apps such as Claude Desktop or the Codex app can work on a model too

evidence.heading: Screenshots
evidence.text:
**Explode:** take your assembly apart. SOMA works out in which direction each part comes off.



**Animate:** bring your models to life. Animations are created by your agent and rendered to video.



**Draw:** technical drawings from the model. The agent writes them in Python, with views, sections and dimensions measured on the model, as PDF and DXF.



Look at more examples in 3D on [somacad.app](https://somacad.app/#models): a CNC router, a parametric organizer, a walking robot dog and a shelf with FEM.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
🎯 Autumn-Recruit Algo Notes


  面向大模型时代的算法、工程与 AI 学习共建仓库
  从数学基础、数据结构，到机器学习、深度学习、LLM、Agent、AI-Infra、语音与数据科学，
  通过「理解 → 推导 → 手写 → 运行 → 验证 → 复盘」构建可持续迭代的知识体系。



  
  
  
  
  
  


---

evidence.heading: 🌱 为什么做这个项目
evidence.text:
学习算法和 AI，往往会遇到三个问题：

1. **资料很多，但知识之间缺少连接**：公式、代码、论文、工程实践和面试题分散在不同地方；
2. **看懂不等于会做**：读过推导，未必能独立写出实现；跑过代码，也未必真正理解为什么这样设计；
3. **技术变化太快**：大模型、Agent、推理优化、具身智能等方向不断演进，静态的学习清单很快会过时。

这个仓库尝试把学习过程整理成一条可执行、可验证、可复盘的路径：

> **把知识讲清楚，把公式写出来，把代码跑起来，把结果验证掉，再把自己的理解沉淀下来。**

它不是一份“标准答案”，也不是一个已经完成的教材，而是一个持续建设中的公开学习基地。内容中难免存在不准确、不完整或可以改进的地方，欢迎大家指出问题、补充案例、分享经验，一起把它变得更好。

---

evidence.heading: 🚀 项目愿景
evidence.text:
我们希望把这个仓库逐步建设成一个：

- **对初学者友好**：尽量用直觉、生活类比和小例子解释抽象概念；
- **对进阶者有用**：保留公式、边界条件、实现细节、复杂度和工程权衡；
- **对面试准备有效**：能够从一个知识点延伸到手撕代码、系统设计和追问；
- **对实践者可验证**：代码尽量自包含、可运行、有断言、有数值对照；
- **对社区开放共建**：欢迎不同背景的学习者贡献内容、勘误、图示和实践经验；
- **能够持续迭代**：随着模型、工具和工程范式变化，持续更新目录、案例和学习方法。

如果这个项目对你有帮助，欢迎：

- 点一个 Star，帮助更多同学发现它；
- 提交 Issue，指出错误、过时内容或难以理解的地方；
- 提交 Pull Request，补充推导、代码、图示、习题或工程经验；
- 分享你的学习路线和面试复盘，让体系获得更多真实反馈。

每一条认真反馈，都会帮助这个项目更接近“真正可学、可用、可复现”的目标。

---

evidence.heading: 🧭 大模型时代下，学习正在发生什么变化
evidence.text:
传统学习往往是：找资料 → 阅读 → 做笔记 → 背诵。

在大模型时代，我们可以把学习升级为一个**人机协作、代码驱动、持续验证的闭环**：

```text
提出问题
   ↓
让模型帮助检索资料、解释概念、比较方案
   ↓
自己追问假设、边界和反例
   ↓
把公式翻译成最小可运行代码
   ↓
用实验、断言、可视化验证理解
   ↓
与框架实现、论文结论或真实数据对照
   ↓
整理成自己的笔记、模板和面试表达
   ↓
分享给他人，接受反馈，再次修订
```

evidence.heading: 1. 不只问“答案是什么”，还要问“为什么”
evidence.text:
大模型可以快速给出解释，但解释不一定正确，也不一定适合你的背景。建议继续追问：

- 这个结论依赖哪些假设？
- 如果输入规模、分布或硬件变化，会不会失效？
- 有没有反例？
- 公式中的每一个符号分别代表什么？
- 能否用一个最小例子验证？

evidence.heading: 2. 不只阅读代码，还要让代码接受测试
evidence.text:
一个算法是否真正理解，至少可以尝试：

- 用 NumPy 从零实现核心步骤；
- 与 sklearn、PyTorch 或参考实现对照；
- 固定随机种子，验证输出形状和数值；
- 构造边界样例，检查空输入、极端值和异常情况；
- 用图把中间过程展示出来。

evidence.heading: 3. 不把大模型当作替代思考，而把它当作学习伙伴
evidence.text:
大模型适合帮助我们：

- 解释难点、生成反例、模拟面试官；
- 检查代码、补充测试、比较实现；
- 把同一个概念换成不同层次的表达；
- 帮助整理知识图谱和复习计划。

但关键的判断、实验设计、结果核验和最终表达，仍然应该由学习者自己完成。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Let your AI agents use your Chrome, signed in as you, in background tabs. By Alexey Indeev · blog: read.aindeev.com · X: @AlexeyIndeev

evidence.heading: Chrome Relay
evidence.text:
Lets your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Paseo, pi) use **your everyday Chrome**, with your real
logins, from the command line, **in background tabs**: nothing takes focus, nothing on your screen moves.

- **Whole goals in one command.** `chrome-relay do "Invite the new teammate as an admin" --data "Email=ada@example.com"
  --until "text:Invitation sent"` fills, clicks and checks every step, in about the time an agent spends on one
  click. [More](#whole-goals-in-one-command-chrome-relay-do)
- **Or step by step**, with checked commands that answer in tens of milliseconds (`open`, `snapshot`, `click`,
  `fill`). [More](#step-by-step-chrome-relays-own-commands)
- **Sign-ins without you.** Google account hops are clicked through; other logins come from the 1Password vaults
  you share with it (passwords, 2-step codes, passkeys), typed by Chrome Relay so the agent never sees them.
  [More](#signing-in-with-1password-optional)
- **Approvals on your iPhone** when you're away from the Mac, with Face ID. [More](#approving-from-your-iphone)
- **An audit trail** of everything every agent did. [More](#audit-trail)



**Status**
- **Mac service:** built from source on your Mac ([Setup](#setup-once-per-mac-2-minutes), about 2 minutes).
- **Chrome extension:** [in the Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/mdglmmedlbkjphgolcejpphnbclkfnom)
  (unlisted: only at that link).
- **iPhone app**, Chrome Relay Approve: [on TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/zhpm8gND) (install
  TestFlight on the iPhone, then open the link there); in App Store review.
- **Password managers:** 1Password only, for now.

**The core** is background tabs with your logins, `chrome-relay do`, Google sign-in hops and an audit trail.
**Everything else is optional** and off un

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
```
chrome-relay open/click/fill/... ──unix socket /driver──┐
chrome-relay do ──────────────────unix socket /driver───┼──▶ relay (127.0.0.1:9333, LaunchAgent) ──ws──▶ Chrome Relay extension ──chrome.debugger──▶ agent tab
agent-browser (optional) ─────────ws (DevTools)─────────┘         ▲
   │                                                               └── reads the page and acts, in that agent's own tabs only
   └── do decides: saved flows → the agent's data → Jev or Haiku (Claude Code) → hand back to the agent
```

- **Extension** (`extension/`, MV3, one per Chrome profile you load it in): opens each agent tab **inactive**
  in a collapsed "Agents" tab group and runs DevTools commands in it via `chrome.debugger`. No remote-debugging
  port, so Chrome never shows "Allow remote debugging?". Chrome does show "Chrome Relay started debugging this
  browser" while agents work.
- **`chrome-relay`**: one Go program, **built and signed on your own Mac** (`./build`). As a background service
  (`chrome-relay serve`) it is the relay: a DevTools endpoint per agent, where each agent sees and controls only
  the tabs it opened and commands that could raise or focus the browser are swallowed. It is also the CLI
  (setup, the connection URL, `do`, diagnostics, audit trail), and the optional 1Password vault and passkeys, whose
  Secure Enclave and Touch ID code (`internal/macos`, Swift) is linked into the same signed binary when Xcode's
  command line tools are installed.

evidence.heading: Setup (once per Mac, ~2 minutes)
evidence.text:
Fastest: paste [this prompt](https://agent-chrome-relay.aindeev.com/setup-prompt.txt) into Claude Code, Codex or
Cursor in its auto mode (Claude Code: Shift+Tab, or `claude --permission-mode auto`; Codex:
`--full-auto`) and let your agent do it. You only load the extension and approve in 1Password. By hand:

Needs macOS, Google Chrome and [Go](https://go.dev/dl/) 1.25+ (`brew install go`).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aindeev/agent-chrome-relay
cd agent-chrome-relay
./build                    # compiles chrome-relay and signs it on this Mac (see below)
./chrome-relay setup       # secret, background service, identities, `chrome-relay` on PATH, Claude Code skill
```

**Why you build it yourself**: the binary is signed on your Mac, and macOS ties Chrome Relay's Keychain item to
that signature, so only your own build can read it (see the 1Password section). The build uses the hardened
runtime, so other programs can't attach a debugger to the relay or inject code into it. Two things make the
build fuller, and neither is required:

| You have | `./build` makes | |
|---|---|---|
| Go only | the **core**: tabs, Google sign-in hops, audit trail | passkeys you keep in 1Password still work (1Password's prompt) |
| + Xcode's command line tools (`xcode-select --install`) | the core **plus 1Password and Secure Enclave passkeys** | |
| + a code signing identity | the same, **signed by you** | without one it signs ad-hoc: macOS may ask once after each rebuild before Chrome Relay reads its own Keychain item |

Any Apple Development or Developer ID certificate is an identity (`security find-identity -v -p codesigning`
lists yours; a free one comes with an Apple ID in Xcode → Settings → Accounts → Manage Certificates). With
several, pick one with `./build --identity "<name>"`; i

evidence.heading: Telling your agents
evidence.text:
Claude Code: `setup` links the skill (`skill/SKILL.md`) into `~/.claude/skills/chrome-relay`, so every
repo gets it. Codex, Cursor and others: point them at the same file, e.g. a line in your global
`~/.codex/AGENTS.md`: *"For any browser step that needs my logins, follow
`<path>/agent-chrome-relay/skill/SKILL.md`."* A repo's `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` only needs a
one-line pointer to the skill.

evidence.heading: Whole goals in one command: `chrome-relay do`
evidence.text:
Driving a page one command at a time costs the agent a model round trip per click: the relay
answers in ~15 ms, the agent thinks for seconds. `chrome-relay do` lets the agent state the goal once, with the
values it already knows and how to tell it's done, and Chrome Relay carries it out in the agent's own tab:

```bash
chrome-relay do "Invite the new teammate as an admin" --url https://app.example.com/team/invite \
  --profile you@company.com --data "Email=ada@example.com" --data "Role=Admin" --until "text:Invitation sent"
```

Without `--url` it works in the tab the agent used last. Each step is the cheapest thing that works:

1. **A flow that worked before.** A run that ends with its `--until` checks met is saved per site
   (`~/.chrome-relay/flows/`, steps and data keys, never values); the same kind of goal there replays at browser
   speed, with the new data. `chrome-relay flows` lists them.
2. **The agent's data.** A `--data` key that names a field (`Email` → "E-mail address") fills it, picks the
   dropdown option or ticks the box, no model involved. Values can be `op://` references: the relay types them
   from 1Password as it does for a `fill`.
3. **A fast decision model** for the rest: TypeSafe's Jev (~0.15 s a step) if you saved a key
   (`pbpaste | chrome-relay decider jev`), else Claude Haiku through your own Claude Code (~1–1.5 s a step, on your
   Claude plan). It picks from a shortlist of the page's controls and from the agent's data only: it never invents
   text. The decider sees the shortlist, up to 1,500 characters of the page's visible text and the `--data` values
   (never `op://` references or what they hold).
4. **Back to the agent** (exit code 2), with what it did, the page it's on and the elements it was choosing
   between, whenever it isn't su

evidence.heading: Step by step: Chrome Relay's own commands
evidence.text:
For the steps `do` hands back, or when an agent wants to look as it goes, `chrome-relay` drives the page one
command at a time. Each agent has its own session (`CHROME_RELAY_SESSION=<name>`; Claude Code, Codex and Paseo
sessions are told apart on their own), and only sees the tabs it opened.

```bash
chrome-relay open <url> [--profile <email>] [--new]   # the first open starts the session; --new: another tab
chrome-relay snapshot [--text] [--json]               # controls with refs (@e5), and with --text the page's text
chrome-relay click | dblclick | hover <target>        # <target>: @e5, a whole label ("Save", button:Save), or CSS
chrome-relay fill <target> <text>                     # replace a field's text; op:// references from 1Password
chrome-relay type | select | check | uncheck | upload | drag | press | scroll | back | reload
chrome-relay get text|value|html|attr|count|url|title  # and: is visible|enabled|checked, eval, wait, screenshot, pdf
chrome-relay console | errors | cookies | dialog accept|dismiss | tabs | tab <id> | cdp <Domain.method>
chrome-relay click <target> --download [--into <dir>]  # and wait for the file it brings
chrome-relay downloads [--into <dir>] | save <url>... [--into <dir>]   # files; addresses loaded as the tab would
chrome-relay close [--all]
```

- **Every action is checked.** Before it: the control is still the one the agent saw, enabled, on screen and not
  covered (or about to hit another control inside it). After it: what changed, at once; the wait for the page to
  finish comes before the next step, usually while the agent is thinking.
- **It never guesses.** A label that matches two controls is refused with their refs; clicking needs the whole
  label ("Cancel" never clicks "Cancel subscription"); a ref from a page that's gone

evidence.heading: Who can drive it
evidence.text:
Two checks on every agent connection:

1. **This Mac's secret**: generated at setup in `~/.chrome-relay/token` (mode 600) and embedded in the URL
   that `chrome-relay url` prints.
2. **An allowed agent app**: the connecting process must come from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Paseo. The
   relay looks the process up (`lsof`, `ps`) and checks the markers those apps set in their child processes
   (`CLAUDECODE`, `CODEX_*`, `CURSOR_*`, `PASEO_AGENT_ID`), then its parent processes.

Connections that carry a browser `Origin` header (a web page) are refused even with the secret. Only **Chrome
Relay's extension** may connect as the extension: the Web Store's copy (its ID is the store's, which no other
extension can have) or **this checkout's** unpacked copy (for the unpacked one, Chrome derives the ID from its
folder; `setup` records it in `~/.chrome-relay/config.json`). The relay checks the connection's `Origin:
chr

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
New here? [Make your first video](docs/guides/first-video.md): a 5-second test that checks the install and shows
every step a bigger video goes through.

**1. Install the two prerequisites** (details in [Requirements](#requirements)):
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 24 or 22 LTS (20 or newer works).
Restart your coding agent afterwards so it sees them.

**2. Add showtime to your agent.** In Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add FavioVazquez/showtime
/plugin install showtime@showtime
```

Using Codex, Cursor, Devin, OpenCode or another agent? [Works with](#works-with) has the exact
install for each, and `npx skills add FavioVazquez/showtime` covers any agent that supports Agent Skills.

**3. Ask for a video:**

```text
Make a 20-second launch video for this repo, with a voice-over and upbeat music.
```

The first time, your agent checks what is missing, tells you the download size and time (about
0.5 to 0.75 GB to download and 1.4 to 1.8 GB in `~/.showtime` once installed, depending on your system,
usually 2 to 6 minutes; outside that folder only uv's and npm's download caches change) and runs setup once
you say yes. If your agent's sandbox blocks the download, run setup once in a terminal
([Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md#setup-never-ran-or-the-sandbox-blocked-it)). Bigger pieces (the
transcription model, Manim, music tracks) come the first time a video needs them, announced with their size. After
that, a request in Claude Code looks like this:

Your agent states its assumptions in one line (it asks only when a request is ge

evidence.heading: X-ray
evidence.text:
Film a real thing doing its thing, a typewriter typing or a music box playing, and showtime draws its inside moving
on the exact frames the clip's own sound says: on the object as the camera moves, or beside it, as a dark radiograph
or a light blueprint. Instruments get their music written out from the sound too (a score, a guitar tab, a drum
sheet), and every film ends with a receipt that proves it.


An Underwood 315 typing, seen through. Clip: Erik Pålsson / Sounds of Changes, CC BY 3.0.

Say "X-ray this clip of my typewriter" to your agent, or run the three steps yourself:

```text
showtime xray analyze clip.mp4 --job xray-typewriter        # every event in the sound, with its frame
showtime new xray xray-typewriter/project --mechanism typewriter --theme dark
showtime xray verify xray-typewriter                        # after the render: reads the film back
```

```text
19 of 19 events on their frame · audio 0.0 ms from the original
```

The mechanisms come from a library that grows with every verified X-ray, and anyone can add one. The
**[X-ray gallery](https://faviovazquez.github.io/showtime/xray/)** plays every verified film with its receipt and the
commands that made it, and shows how to post yours; the [X-ray guide](docs/guides/xray.md) walks through filming,
mechanisms, music and drums, and what the receipt checks.

evidence.heading: Works with
evidence.text:
showtime is a skill, a command line and an MCP server, so it runs in any coding agent that reads
[Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) and can run shell commands. MCP adds typed tools on top, and
the ten [crew](#meet-the-crew) agents are an optional speed-up for hosts that have custom sub-agents.

**Tested with.** A real run passed: the agent installed showtime from this repository and made a
5-second test video ("make a 5-second test video that says hello", empty folder), ending in a `final.mp4`
whose `showtime qa` verdict had no FAIL.

| Agent | Install route | Crew agents | Tested with |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Claude Code](#claude-code) | plugin | yes | the primary host |
| [OpenAI Codex](#other-agents) | plugin | with `showtime install` | CLI 0.158.0, plugin route |
| [Cursor](#other-agents) | plugin (reads `.claude-plugin/`) | yes | CLI 2026.09.28 |
| [Devin](#other-agents) | plugin (reads `.claude-plugin/`) | yes (local only) | CLI 3000.11.3 |
| [OpenCode](#other-agents) | `showtime install` | yes | 1.18.33, a free model |

**Should work with** any agent that supports [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io): GitHub Copilot
(CLI and VS Code), Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cline, Kilo Code, Kiro, Zed, Goose, Amp, Factory Droid and Qwen
Code. The files each one reads are packaged and were checked with the agent's own tools where possible, but
no real video has been made in them yet. If you try one, an [issue](https://github.com/FavioVazquez/showtime/issues)
with what happened helps everyone. Exact steps for every agent, and what the tests covered:
[docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md).

evidence.heading: Now showing
evidence.text:
▶ Watch the 0.2.0 launch film (40 s, MP4; made with showtime, every frame from a real example, about the film). Every example plays in the gallery on the showtime site.Music: “With These Hands” by Scott Buckley, CC BY 4.0 (credits).

Every example was made by an agent acting as a user, and ships with its project sources and a README
that tells the story: the request, the assumptions, the commands, what the critic found and what
changed. Click a preview to open the example. Each one has a card with its prompt and links in
[`examples/`](https://github.com/FavioVazquez/showtime-examples/blob/main/examples/README.md). Previews are silent; the videos have sound.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Motion graphics are written as HTML, CSS and canvas and rendered frame-exactly in headless Chrome: every
frame is a pure function of time, so a render, its preview and its HTML video show the same picture.
Math scenes use Manim, and real footage is cut by transcript with ffmpeg.

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
**No GPU needed.** Without one, the browser draws every frame on the CPU, WebGL included; how long that takes, and
other common questions, are in the [FAQ](docs/faq.md).

showtime is built for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows 10/11 and Linux (x86_64 and arm64). What has
actually been run, and where ("end to end" means setup, doctor, a voiced render with qa, HTML export,
transcription, captions and the MCP server):

- **Intel Mac** (a physical machine): end to end, plus the fast test suite.
- **Apple Silicon**: end to end on GitHub's `macos-14` (M1) runners, plus the fast suite. A run on a physical
  Apple Silicon Mac is still welcome.
- **Linux x86_64**: end to end on Ubuntu 24.04 (AWS), plus the fast suite.
- **Linux arm64**: end to end on GitHub's `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners.
- **Windows Server 2025 x64**: end to end as a standard user (AWS) and on GitHub's `windows-2025` runners.
- **Windows 11 on Arm**: end to end on GitHub's `windows-11-arm` runners, plus the fast suite. showtime's
  Python and ffmpeg run as x64 under Windows' emulation there (some packages have no Windows arm64 build, and the
  native arm64 ffmpeg build did not start on the runner), so it is slower than on x64.
- **Windows 10/11 x64 desktop as a standard user**: not yet run on a real machine. If you have one,
  `scripts/e2e-windows.ps1` runs everything and zips the result to attach to an
  [issue](https://github.com/FavioVazquez/showtime/issues).

CI runs the fast test suite on Linux, Windows and Apple Silicon for every change, and on an Intel Mac
nightly. Expect rough edges on anything marked not yet run, and please open an issue when something breaks.

github_projects.description_zh: 开源桌面 AI 智能体，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux，从零开始编写：拥有自己的智能体引擎、自己的浏览器工具以及展示解释内容的绘图引擎。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Open desktop AI agent for Windows, macOS and Linux, written from scratch: its own agent engine, its own browser tooling and its own drawing engine that shows what it explains.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text: **Visualize, explore and learn in a new way, with OpenGhost.**

evidence.heading: OpenGhost
evidence.text:
[](https://discord.gg/6cKd2UND5) [](https://andretripol.github.io/OpenGhost/)

**v1.5.1 beta**

[Windows version 1.5.1](https://github.com/ANDRETRIPOL/OpenGhost/releases/download/v1.5.1/OpenGhost-1.5.1-Setup.exe)

[Linux version 1.5.1](https://github.com/ANDRETRIPOL/OpenGhost/releases/download/v1.5.1/OpenGhost-1.5.1-linux.tar.gz)

[macOS version 1.5.1](https://github.com/ANDRETRIPOL/OpenGhost/releases/download/v1.5.1/OpenGhost-1.5.1-mac.dmg)

What's new:
- The app checks the agent's work itself before a step of its plan closes: tests after the last change, documents read back and weighed against the request, removed files named, pages opened at phone and desktop width, links and quotes checked against what was really opened.
- After every reply the facts of the talk are kept in the chat's record and the shared memory, so even small models remember.
- Welcome cards on the first start, and the app starts in your computer's language.

Older versions are on the [Releases](https://github.com/ANDRETRIPOL/OpenGhost/releases) page.

Try the app in your browser, with no install, on [the website](https://andretripol.github.io/OpenGhost/).

OpenGhost is an open desktop agent for Windows, macOS and Linux. It runs commands, edits files, keeps git and works on the web in a browser of its own. And it shows what it explains: charts, schemes, photos and videos stand next to the text.

evidence.heading: An agent built for visualization
evidence.text: OpenGhost is an agent built for visualization. When something is better shown than told, the answer comes with a drawing beside it, and the whole app is made so that reading and working with documents feels comfortable. A new chat needs no folder: type, and it goes to Chats at the top of the list, with a folder of its own for the files the agent makes. A chat about a project still lives in that project's folder.

evidence.heading: Written from scratch
evidence.text:
Nothing in OpenGhost is assembled from ready parts. There is no UI framework inside, no Markdown library, no Mermaid, no chart library and no agent framework. Every part is our own code:

- **The agent.** The loop, the tools (commands, files, git, web search, pages, PDFs, video frames), the approval cards and the three permission modes.
- **The drawing engine.** It reads what a model writes, lays it out and draws it: 43 kinds of drawings, from flowcharts and loss curves to a day of meals and the route of a trip. A drawing is live: it answers the pointer and can be edited where it stands.
- **The browser.** The agent sees a page as text with numbered elements, moves its own cursor, clicks, types and reads, in a browser panel it shares with you.
- **The text.** The Markdown renderer that draws a reply while it is still being written, the code highlighter and the math.
- **The interface.** Every control, its motion and its glass, in plain JavaScript and CSS.

The app stands on two things only: Electron, which gives it a window, and Anthropic's official SDK, which talks to Claude.

evidence.heading: It shows what it explains
evidence.text: Ask how something works, and the answer comes with drawings: the whole as a scheme, the curves the topic is known for as charts, the key numbers as tiles. The engine knows more than forty kinds of drawings, from a day of meals and the route of a trip to the heavy charts of physics and any other science. Here one series of games stands as a mindmap of its universes and as a ring of what each universe holds.

evidence.heading: A scheme with the detail in it
evidence.text: A block carries its name and a line about what happens in it. Stages stand in groups, and a process that repeats closes into a ring.

evidence.heading: Show it a photo, a video, a PDF
evidence.text: Photos, videos and files attach from the plus menu or by a drop. A video comes in like a photo, and the agent watches it frame by frame. A PDF is read as text, and its pages with photos, charts, formulas or scans are looked at as pictures.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:shuyu-labs/transwork.git
cd transwork
docker compose up -d
```

首次启动会自动拉取四个镜像（Web、WebAgent、文档解析、PostgreSQL），完成 pgvector 扩展初始化、数据库建表与演示数据导入，等待约 1 分钟后访问：

```bash

OpenChart brings AI agents into every step of your investment journey: statistical
and technical analysis with code and charts, real-time responses to market events
with alerts, opportunity discovery through agentic research, and more.

OpenChart is not built to monetize software, but to explore a future where humans
and agents manage assets together. If you believe in this future and want to join
forces, [we want to talk to you](https://discord.gg/PR4gfbMKUD).

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
[Download Desktop for macOS (Apple Silicon)](https://downloads.longsurf.ai/openchart/darwin/arm64/OpenChart.dmg),
open the disk image, and install OpenChart.

To run Desktop from source, install [Node.js 24](https://nodejs.org/en/download),
[npm 11.11.1](https://docs.npmjs.com/downloading-and-installing-node-js-and-npm/),
[Bun 1.4.2](https://bun.sh/docs/installation), and [Just](https://just.systems/man/en/),
then run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/longsurf-ai/openchart.git
cd openchart
just install --frozen-lockfile
just desktop
```

`just install` also initializes and builds Tea, a programming language built for analyzing market, by the same team.
Follow the [setup guide](https://openchart.co/docs/getting-started/)
for your first chart and alert, or the [development guide](docs/development.md)
for building and packaging the app.

Desktop is free. AI usage follows your agent provider's plan; optional Cloud
market data is priced separately.

evidence.heading: Key features
evidence.text:
Charts without software quotas
      Add indicators and Volume Profile, then expand to a 4×4 grid. No software plan limits on charts, indicators, or price and indicator alerts.
    
    
      
      Use your own agents
      Use your Claude, Codex, and Gemini models to research markets, build indicators, and set up alerts with the accounts you already have.
    
  
  
    
      
      Describe what to watch
      Tell your agent what matters. It builds Tea monitors that evaluate incoming data and investigate when a condition fires.
    
    
      
      Explain what moved the chart
      Select a range and let your agent research the move, with source-linked annotations pinned to the bars.
    
  
  
    
      
      Draw it, get alerted
      Draw a line or zone on the chart. When price crosses it, an alert can ask your agent to research the move.
    
    
      
      Write your own market logic in Tea
      Build custom indicators and conditions with functions, loops, state, and collections that evaluate as data flows in. Explore Tea →

Help improve OpenChart through code, indicators, documentation, and feedback.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
claude-show-your-work

See, review and iterate on your agent's work without leaving the terminal.Images, videos and visual QA for Claude Code.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Run these two commands in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/iamumeransari/claude-show-your-work.git#releases
/plugin install show-your-work@iamumeransari
```

It works on macOS, Linux and Windows. You need a terminal that supports the kitty graphics protocol, like Ghostty or Warp, and Claude Code 2.1.286 or later. Videos also need ffmpeg: install it with your package manager (`brew install ffmpeg` on macOS), or ask Claude to install it.

When the install finishes, a short onboarding shows you around. Run `/show-your-work` at any time to change your settings.

evidence.heading: Usage
evidence.text:
Claude shows you its work in the chat whenever it builds or changes something visual. You can also ask for it directly:

- "Give me four directions for the homepage hero and show them side by side."
- "Build the sign-up form, test it, and show me the recording."
- "Fix the billing toggle and show me before and after."

evidence.heading: Visual QA with before-and-after recordings
evidence.text:
When Claude builds a feature or fixes a bug, it tests the change with Playwright, records the run and plays the recording in the chat, with everything you need to review the work in one place:

- **Before and After:** For any change, from a new feature to a bug fix, Claude records the same steps on the old version and the new one. Compare then plays both side by side, in sync.
- **Change Markers:** Every change Claude made is listed beside the video with its timestamp, and clicking one jumps straight to the moment it shows up.
- **Live Checks:** Each test check turns green or red as the video reaches it, so you can see exactly where the fix works and where something still fails.
- **One Place to Review:** You don't need to open a browser, rerun the tests or read through logs, because the recording and its results are right there in the chat.

evidence.heading: Images
evidence.text:
Whatever Claude designs, you see it right in the chat: landing pages, app screens, components, design concepts, slides, charts and generated images. Ask for a few directions and they appear side by side, then keep iterating on the one you like.

- **Compare Directions:** Several concepts show together, so you can pick one at a glance instead of opening files one by one.
- **Every Version Kept:** Each new version lands in the same player, and History lets you step back through every earlier draft.
- **Before and After:** Switch between the old and new design, or put them side by side, to see exactly what changed.

evidence.heading: Video
evidence.text:
Beyond product QA, Claude can show you a video of almost anything it works on. Building a website and want to see how it feels as you scroll from top to bottom? Just ask, and the recording plays in the chat, animations and all.

Making an ad, an animation or a launch video? Each cut plays right in the chat, in a full-featured video player:

- **Video Controls:** Play, pause, scrub through the timeline, and skip forward or back to the moment you want.
- **Timestamps:** The sidebar walks you through what happens in the video, step by step. Each step is timestamped, so one click takes you right to that moment.
- **Compare Versions:** When Claude makes a new version of a video, it opens in the same player. You can flip between drafts in History or play the old and new versions side by side, in sync.
- **Quick Functions:** Open the video in QuickTime Player for a bigger view, or save it straight to your Downloads folder in one click.

evidence.heading: Terminals
evidence.text:
show-your-work works in any terminal that supports the kitty graphics protocol, on macOS, Linux and Windows.

- **Ghostty and kitty:** pictures work straight away.
- **Warp, WezTerm and Konsole:** Claude Code leaves pictures off in these until you turn them on. The first time a picture can't show, press **Turn on pictures**, then restart Claude Code. You can turn it off again in `/show-your-work`.

Turn on pictures adds one line to your shell profile (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.bash_profile` or `~/.bashrc`, or fish's `config.fish`) that sets `CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_TERMINAL_IMAGES=1` only inside that terminal. Turning it off removes the line.

evidence.heading: Change the requirement. Watch the plan change.
evidence.text:
A real DeepSeek run proposed **gallery → noodles → reading room**. It satisfied the original constraints. We then made **coffee mandatory** in the structured requirements and resubmitted that actual plan:

| Step | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| Recheck the old plan | **Rejected:** a required activity was missing. No facts committed. |
| Give the feedback to DeepSeek | **One new model call** chose gallery → reading room → cafe. |
| Independently check the revision | **Accepted:** ¥73, 35 minutes walking, return at 13:04; all supplied hard constraints passed. |

The model chooses among possible plans; the verifier enforces the requirements. The cafe covers both a meal and coffee in the fictional catalog. This recorded experiment uses synthetic venue and transport data; the check establishes feasibility under those inputs.

[**Inspect both proposals, the rejection, and the checked revision →**](docs/evidence/open-planning/README.md)

[**Full planning rules and all three offline scenarios**](docs/open-planning.md) · [**Runnable example**](examples/open_planning.py) · [**Real DeepSeek audits**](docs/evidence/open-planning/README.md)

evidence.heading: Use the standalone Agent
evidence.text:
ResiMind owns the reasoning loop: collect evidence, propose, verify, commit facts, and rebuild remaining obligations. Run it directly:

```python
from resimind import Task
from resimind.domains.planning import DOMAIN, build_agent, demo_problem, verified_plan

agent = build_agent(demo_problem())  # Offline; inject complete=your_model for neural proposals.
result = agent.run(Task("day-out", "Plan a relaxed day with art and a meal.", DOMAIN))
run = result.run_result
if run.status == "solved" and run.residual.solved:
    print(verified_plan(result))
else:
    print("Still unresolved:", run.residual.pending)
```

Model SDKs and external workflow connectors are [optional integrations](#optional-integrations). No LangGraph installation is needed for this Agent or the built-in domain demos.

evidence.heading: The architecture
evidence.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T[Task] --> A[Agent]
    A --> E[Evidence tools]
    A --> P[Model / rule proposer]
    E --> P
    M[Reviewed route memory] --> P
    R[Residual obligations] --> P
    P --> C[Candidate + references]
    C --> V[Independent verifier]
    E --> V
    V -->|accept + binding checks| F[Commit verified facts]
    V -->|reject / defer + feedback| P
    V -->|interrupt| H[Stop and hand off]
    F --> D[Rebuild residual]
    D --> R
    F --> O[Facts + JSON audit trail]
    D -->|task complete| X[Extract derivation certificate]
    X --> K[Independent knowledge admission]
    K -->|verified| L[Persistent knowledge library]
    L -->|retrieve; application rechecked| P
```

- **Evidence before claims:** registered tools collect typed inputs for each task.
- **Verification before state changes:** verdicts bind to candidate, state, and evidence; commits check references and conflicts atomically.
- **Explicit unfinished work:** goals, unknowns, and hard constraints remain visible until discharged by the domain adapter.
- **Knowledge that carries forward:** completed derivations face independent admission, re-verification on reload, and checks on every new application.
- **Reusable routes:** in-memory routes require review and matching applicability; reused steps still need verification on current inputs.
- **Inspectable execution:** every attempt records its decision, reason, state, and residual; attempt and stall budgets bound the loop.
