evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: How many bugs can LMs find & fix in large codebases?

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
SWE-sweep

How many bugs can LMs find & fix in large codebases?


Given a real repository, an agent must discover & repair as many bugs as they can.
Agents are not given any hint about the type of bug or its location.

evidence.heading: Links
evidence.text:
- Website: https://swesweep.com
- Paper: https://swesweep.com/paper

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
> [!note]
> The code in this repo is only a thin wrapper around harbor, however see the warning below regarding harbor version

> [!warning]
> * **Harbor version**: Harbor 0.23 does not yet support the separate verifier environments and collect hooks
>   used by these tasks. The project therefore pins a compatible revision from Harbor's source
>   repository until Harbor 0.24 is released.
> * **Final score**: We build a micro-average of the bugs resolved (equivalent to a weighted average of the
>   individual task scores). See evaluation notes.

We recommend [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) for managing
Python environments.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/facebookresearch/swe-sweep.git
cd swe-sweep
uv sync   # or pip install .
```

Verify your setup:

```bash
sweep infra doctor
```


  Development setup

  Clone the repository and install the editable package with its dev dependencies:

  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/facebookresearch/swe-sweep.git
  cd swe-sweep
  uv sync --extra test
  ```

  Run the test suite (matches CI, which tests on Python 3.12 and 3.13):

  ```bash
  uv run pytest
  ```

  Run the linting/formatting hooks:

  ```bash
  uvx pre-commit run --all-files
  ```

evidence.heading: Evaluate a single task
evidence.text:
Pass a task name and a unified diff against that task's base commit:

```bash
sweep eval <task> <path/to/submission.diff>  # see raw harbor command below
```


  Raw harbor command

  ```bash
  uv run harbor run \
  --path tasks/pandora-bench__dateutil \
  --agent swesweep.patch_agent:PatchAgent \
  --agent-kwarg "patch_path=$(realpath /path/to/model.patch)" \
  --jobs-dir jobs \
  --n-concurrent 1 \
  --yes

  ```




The command runs the corresponding Harbor task with a small patch-applying agent. Harbor
then evaluates the resulting checkout in the task's separate verifier environment. Results
are written under `jobs/` by default.


How evaluation works

Evaluation follows the following pseudo-code:

```python
reset_to_base_commit()
apply(agent_patch)
reset(test_files)
build_if_needed()
base_commit_results = run_visible_suite()  # test -> pass/fail

subtask_results = {}   # subtask -> {test -> pass/fail}
for subtask in subtasks:
  apply(subtask.test_patch)
  subtask_results[subtask.id] = run(subtask.hidden_tests)
  revert(subtask.test_patch)

if any_new_failures(base_commit_results):
  task_score = 0
else:
  task_score = sum(passed_subtasks) / len(subtasks)
```

evidence.heading: Calculate the final score
evidence.text:
The benchmark score is calculated as

```
total number of bugs solved across tasks / total number of bugs =
    = mean(number of bugs in task * task score)
```

Summarize one or more directories containing graded Harbor trials:

```bash
sweep info path/to/graded-solutions --per-task
sweep info path/to/graded-solutions --json
```

github_projects.name: seiso
github_projects.description: A Markdown convention and linter for project docs written by AI and read by humans and agents
github_projects.description_zh: 一个用于 AI 编写、供人类和智能体阅读的项目文档的 Markdown 约定和代码检查工具。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: A Markdown convention and linter for project docs written by AI and read by humans and agents

evidence.heading: seiso
evidence.text:
**A Markdown convention and linter for project docs written by AI and read by humans and agents.**

[](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](https://crates.io/crates/seiso)
[](https://pypi.org/project/seiso/)
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@scarletkc/seiso)
[](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/LICENSE)
[](https://coderabbit.ai)
[](https://deepwiki.com/scarletkc/seiso)



AI writes project docs faster than anyone can review them, and coding agents
read those docs back as context for the next change. People and agents alike
take the page at its word, so a stale version number or a field list updated
in only one of its three copies misleads all of them. And AI makes the same
few mistakes over and over.

seiso defines one convention for how Markdown in a repository is organized,
the way rustfmt settled formatting for Rust code. Projects share the rules
instead of negotiating their own; each project mainly maps its documents to
kinds, and `seiso init` suggests a starting point.

evidence.heading: The convention
evidence.text:
- Every document declares one kind, such as `howto`, `reference`, or `adr`,
  and holds only what that kind is for. A how-to gives the steps. Why the
  design looks this way belongs in an ADR.
- Each fact has one home. Other pages link to it instead of retelling it.
- Long-lived pages don't record values that change faster than the page,
  such as versions, deployment status, or counts.
- A pointer names a file or symbol, so the reader doesn't have to search for
  what the sentence promised.
- The finished page doesn't address whoever asked for it or narrate how it,
  or the work it describes, was made.
- Judgment calls a tool can't make are written down with a reason. An
  exception without one is itself a violation.

The convention is written up as a standalone
[specification](https://seiso.fog.moe/latest/convention),
with [worked examples](https://seiso.fog.moe/latest/examples)
and an [adoption guide](https://seiso.fog.moe/latest/adopting),
so a project can follow it without installing anything. The specification is
provisional before 1.0.0 and versioned separately from seiso; its direction is
open for discussion in [#37](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/issues/37).

seiso is the reference implementation. Its rules check documents against the
specification; stable rules run by default, and the rest are opt-in previews.
Each diagnostic says where the problem is and how to fix it, so an agent can
repair most findings from seiso's output alone. When a fix needs a judgment,
such as which of two pages owns a fact, the diagnostic names the decision.
seiso doesn't guess whether prose sounds machine-written, and it leaves
formatting and spelling to other tools.
[How seiso checks the convention](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/docs/reference/convention.md)
maps

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
```sh
cargo install seiso
uv tool install seiso    # or: pipx install seiso
npm install -g @scarletkc/seiso
```

The PyPI and npm packages include prebuilt binaries for macOS on Apple silicon
and Intel, Linux x64 and arm64 with glibc or musl (such as Alpine), and
Windows x64 and arm64. On other platforms, use cargo; the PyPI package also
works there but builds from source, which requires a Rust toolchain. From a
source checkout, run `cargo run -- <command>`.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
From the repository root:

```sh
seiso init
seiso check
```

`seiso init` writes a `seiso.toml` at the repository root with suggested
exclusions, kind mappings, and documentation site entries; review them before
relying on the results.

`seiso check` runs only stable rules, which have met the
[promotion criteria](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/docs/evaluation/policy.md).
The other rules are in preview: they are experimental, can report false
positives, and run only with `--preview`. Try them locally before relying on
them, and keep them out of CI gates. `seiso rule --all` lists every rule with
its status, `seiso rule <CODE>` explains a rule with examples, and `seiso parse`
inspects the document model without running rules.

evidence.heading: Documentation
evidence.text:
- [Checking documents](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/docs/guides/checking.md): configuration, rule selection, and output formats
- [Integrations](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/docs/guides/integrations.md): Claude Code hooks, pre-commit, and CI
- [Development](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/docs/guides/development.md): building, testing, and validation commands
- [Architecture](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/docs/reference/architecture.md): command execution
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/docs/design/roadmap.md): proposed features and milestone evidence
- [Documentation index](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/docs/README.md): guides, references, and evaluation records
- [Contributing](https://github.com/scarletkc/seiso/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): issues, branches, commits, and pull requests

evidence.heading: 孙宇晨的观点，用 AI 落地
evidence.text:
[English](README.en.md)

孙宇晨最近上了两期访谈。邵艾伦那期 4 小时 22 分钟，聊年轻人怎么用 AI 抓住机会。金明那期 47 分钟，聊 AI 时代钱往哪放。邵艾伦那期 YouTube 上没有字幕，没法直接丢给 AI，我们就把两期都转成了带时间戳的全文。

访谈里不少观点能直接上手，我们给每个配了一篇教程，写清楚用什么工具、一步步怎么做。这些做法是我们按自己的理解配的，孙宇晨在访谈里没讲这么细。

evidence.heading: 从哪看起
evidence.text:
| 你想 | 看这个 |
| --- | --- |
| 让 AI 出主意 | 把 [AGENT.md](AGENT.md) 复制给你的 AI，再说说你的情况 |
| 看原话 | [邵艾伦那期全文](邵艾伦/全文.md)、[金明那期全文](金明/全文.md)，带时间戳，可以直接丢给 AI |
| 自己动手 | 先看 [00 准备](邵艾伦/guides/00-准备.md) 装好 AI，再挑一篇，比如[让 AI 每天替你写日报](邵艾伦/guides/01-生活AI化.md) |
| 只看重点 | [邵艾伦那期精华](邵艾伦/精华.md)、[金明那期精华](金明/精华.md) |
| 装成 skill | 一行命令装进 Claude Code、Codex，见[下面](#装进你的-ai) |
| 一张图看完 | [思维导图](思维导图.md) |

evidence.heading: 装进你的 AI
evidence.text:
用 Claude Code、Codex 这类 Agent 的话，可以把 AGENT.md 装成 skill。以后你提到孙宇晨、孙学，或者想按这两期访谈的思路给自己出主意，它会自己调出来。电脑上要先装好 Node.js。

```bash
npx skills add wousp112/awesome-justin-sun-ideas-to-ai-howto
```

能上网的 AI，也可以直接让它读这个链接：`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wousp112/awesome-justin-sun-ideas-to-ai-howto/main/AGENT.md`


AI 会怎么回你，看一次真实测试

把 AGENT.md 发给一个全新的 Codex 会话，接着问：「我自由职业接设计单，收入不稳定，想试试接海外客户，英语一般。」下面是它的回答，只改了标点和加粗。

建议先用你最熟悉的一类设计服务，试接一个范围小的海外项目。你要决定的是从哪里找到第一位海外客户，同时控制试错成本。现在最卡你的是收入不稳定、英语一般，还不适合投入太多钱。

| 路径 | 要做什么 | 能得到什么 | 最大的不确定 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 请熟人介绍海外客户 | 找合作过的客户或同行，询问有没有海外项目需要设计 | 有人介绍，沟通更容易建立信任 | 现有人脉有没有这类需求 |
| 给海外设计师或小工作室做协作 | 用一项明确的设计服务承接部分工作 | 可以先验证交付能力，减少独立获客的负担 | 对方的报价和修改要求是否合适 |
| 直接找海外终端客户 | 围绕一种客户需求整理案例，再针对性联系 | 能直接了解客户需求，积累自己的客户 | 获客和英语沟通都需要自己承担 |

我优先推荐第二条：给海外设计师或小工作室做协作。这是根据你当前情况做的判断。你已有接单经验，可以先测试这些经验能否迁移。如果你已经有能介绍海外客户的熟人，第一条更值得先做。

英语先围绕具体工作准备：能确认需求、解释方案、谈清修改范围。让 AI 帮你写邮件和检查表达，每次发出前确认自己理解其中的交付承诺。

可以先做一个小实验，联系数量按你能投入的时间来定，暂时不买广告或订阅新工具：

- 做什么：选你做得最熟、修改最容易控制的一项服务。整理一份简短英文案例，写清客户的问题、你负责的工作，以及最后交付了什么。随后找业务匹配的海外工作室，逐个联系。
- 产出什么：一份英文案例、一段介绍服务的话，以及真实的客户回复记录。目标是争取一个付费小单，提前写清交付内容和修改次数。
- 什么结果值得继续：对方愿意提供具体需求、讨论报价。实际交付后，扣掉沟通和修改时间，报酬仍达到你愿意接受的水平。
- 什么结果需要调整：有人回复却始终不谈项目，就检查服务是否足够具体。拿到项目却修改失控，就收窄范围或调整报价。没有回复时，先检查联系对象和案例匹配度，单凭沉默还不能判断海外接单不适合你。

这里用了邵艾伦那期的「商机全球找」和「先探路，再下注」。观点来自你提供的访谈摘要。选择工作室协作和付费小单，是我根据你的情况设计的方案。

现在第一步：挑出一个你最想再做一次、也最有把握交付的过往项目。你主要接哪类设计？每周能拿出多少时间，最多愿意投入多少钱试海外接单？





教程表里的「推荐」是我们觉得最好用的工具，「国内」是不用海外手机号和信用卡就能开的替代品，价格和国内能不能直接用统一记在[工具总表](工具总表.md)。每篇教程开头是孙宇晨的原话和视频时间点，后面是按先后顺序写的做法，每一步花多久看你自己。最后一段是写给 AI 的话，整段复制给你的 Agent，它会照着帮你装软件、建文件夹。要记的东西，[模板](模板/README.md)里有现成的格式。

evidence.heading: 邵艾伦那期：年轻人如何抓住 AI 时代的机会？
evidence.text:
原视频：[YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Z-vhBvBmUY) · 主持人：[邵艾伦 @AlanShao111](https://x.com/AlanShao111) · 4 小时 22 分钟

| | 观点 | 从哪下手 | 推荐 | 国内 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01 | [把生活 AI 化](邵艾伦/guides/01-生活AI化.md) | 建一个文件夹，让 AI 每天替你写日报 | Claude Code / Codex、Obsidian、Oura | Kimi Code、思源笔记、Zepp |
| 02 | [没钱也能开始](邵艾伦/guides/02-没钱也能开始.md) | 挑一件经常重复的事，用免费额度交给 AI | Gemini CLI | Kimi Code、Qwen Code |
| 03 | [先升级操作系统](邵艾伦/guides/03-升级操作系统.md) | 写下一个看法，找资料来验证它 | Obsidian、NotebookLM | 思源笔记、Kimi |
| 04 | [百分之百相信 AI](邵艾伦/guides/04-百分之百相信AI.md) | 同一个问题问三个模型，取中间那个去做 | ChatHub、Arena | Kimi、通义、智谱各问一遍 |
| 05 | [商机全球找](邵艾伦/guides/05-商机全球找.md) | 去海外论坛看看你这行的人在抱怨什么 | Google Trends、Shopify、Wise | 店匠、空中云汇、万里汇 |
| 06 | [先探路，再下注](邵艾伦/guides/06-先探路再下注.md) | 多找几个候选，挑出最好的先试一下 | Perplexity、Airtable | 秘塔搜索、飞书多维表格 |
| 07 | [身体是本钱](邵艾伦/guides/07-身体是本钱.md) | 把手环数据交给 AI，让它盯着趋势 | Oura / WHOOP、Apple 健康 | Zepp / 华为、Keep |
| 08 | [逐水草而居](邵艾伦/guides/08-逐水草而居.md) | 搞清楚你要的机会大多在哪个城市 | Nomads.com、Levels.fyi | 脉脉、电鸭社区 |
| 09 | [机器读得懂才值钱](邵艾伦/guides/09-机器读得懂.md) | 把常用资料转成 AI 能读的 Markdown | MarkItDown、OCRmyPDF | MinerU |
| 10 | [内容和投资不用二选一](邵艾伦/guides/10-内容和投资.md) | 内容和投资分两个文件夹，各记各的 | Ghost / beehiiv、Portfolio Performance | 公众号、本地记账 |
| 11 | [Small ego](邵艾伦/guides/11-small-ego.md) | 让 AI 站在反对者那边反驳你 | Decision Journal 方法 | 同左，任何笔记工具 |
| 12 | [先自由，后财富](邵艾伦/guides/12-先自由后财富.md) | 翻一遍账单，算出你的缓冲金 | YNAB / Actual Budget | 钱迹、随手记 |
| 13 | [游戏版本会更新](邵艾伦/guides/13-游戏版本更新.md) | 订阅几个一手信息源，让 AI 帮你看变化 | Folo、GitHub Trending、Awesome 列表 | Folo |
| 14 | [缺啥补啥](邵艾伦/guides/14-缺啥补啥.md) | 给自己出一道目标岗位的模拟题 | Forage、ADPList | 牛客、即刻 / 脉脉找人聊 |
| 15 | [多创造，少消费](邵艾伦/guides/15-多创造少消费.md) | 把刚搞懂的东西写成教程发出去 | GitHub Pages、Quartz | 公众号、B 站 |

evidence.heading: 金明那期：AI 黄金时代，普通人如何下注？
evidence.text:
原视频：[YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o9Jn__LGGI4) · 主持人：金明（William Joy，圈内叫他仙道） · 47 分钟

这期一半在聊仓位和市场，里面的判断都是孙宇晨自己的。下面的教程用 AI 帮你记录、研究和复盘，买卖要你自己拿主意。

| | 观点 | 从哪下手 | 推荐 | 国内 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01 | [从不关注到密切关注](金明/guides/01-密切关注.md) | 给一件长期风险找几个信号，订阅一手来源 | arXiv、BIP-360、Folo | Folo |
| 02 | [把币放进没签过名的地址](金明/guides/02-币进掩体.md) | 查一遍自己的地址有没有提前暴露公钥 | mempool.space、Sparrow、Trezor | OneKey |
| 03 | [看空也不急着做空](金明/guides/03-判断日志.md) | 判断和仓位分开记，隔一段时间对答案 | Obsidian、Portfolio Performance | 思源笔记、飞书多维表格 |
| 04 | [健康管理先埋点](金明/guides/04-健康先埋点.md) | 把体检报告整理成一张表，带着问题去见医生 | MinerU、Oura、Apple 健康 | MinerU、华为运动健康 |
| 05 | [零成本安装](金明/guides/05-零成本安装.md) | 把一套方法蒸馏成 AI 能装的 skill | Claude Code skill、AGENTS.md | Kimi Code、Qwen Code |
| 06 | [让机器来验证](金明/guides/06-让机器验证.md) | 让 AI 写一个 Lean 证明，交给机器验 | Lean 4 Web、自然数游戏、Mathlib | 同左 |
| 07 | [从数据里找 AI 应用](金明/guides/07-从数据找应用.md) | 在熟悉的场景里找采了没人用的数据 | Product Hunt、Google Trends | 少数派、百度指数 |
| 08 | [盘点你的老登和新登](金明/guides/08-老登和新登.md) | 把你的钱、技能和信息源盘一遍 | Obsidian | 思源笔记、飞书文档 |

evidence.heading: 全文是怎么做出来的
evidence.text:
两期都用 Gemini 3.8 Flash 转录。Gemini 系列在 [Artificial Analysis 语音转文字榜单](https://artificialanalysis.ai/speech-to-text)上排在前十，同系列的 Gemini 3.5 Transcribe 词错误率是 2.6%。

邵艾伦那期，原视频 4 小时 22 分 29 秒，YouTube 上没有字幕。我们把音轨切成 57 段，每段 5 分钟，相邻两段重叠 20 秒，防止句子在切口处被截断。第一轮有 5 段没有通过格式检查，我们把它们切成 30 个更短的片段重新转。有一段出现了一长串重复文字，也单独重转了一遍。最后得到约 12 万字，1,743 条发言。机器把「薄肌」听成了「搏击」「脖肌」「博弈」，把「孙学」听成了「孙诩」，一共改回来 200 多处，改了哪些都列在全文开头的勘误里。最后 5 分钟两个人的名字整段标反了，也已经对调。

金明那期，原视频 47 分 08 秒，切成 11 段，同样每段 5 分钟、重叠 20 秒。转录那晚网络不稳，7 段没转完，我们把这 7 段切成 40 个 1 分钟的小段重新转，相邻两段重叠 10 秒，再按文字把重叠的地方接上，去掉重复的句子。最后得到约 1.2 万字，316 条发言。机器把「孙学」听成了「孙选」，把「孙宇晨奖」听成了「孙正义奖」，把「薄肌」听成了「搏击」，这些都按上下文改了回来。

两期都从开头、中间、结尾各截 30 秒音频，单独再识别一次，拿去和主稿对照，内容和顺序都对得上。每条发言都标了时间，全文开头还有按话题分的目录，点时间看视频，点话题跳到原文。

还有几处要留意。全文没有逐句人工听校，个别人名和同音词可能有误，引用原话前最好回看视频。邵艾伦那期相邻两段重叠的地方，开头可能有几句重复，文中都标了出来。00:32:40 那段两个人的话被识别成了一整段，没能分开。金明那期开头 1 分 46 秒是正片片段剪成的预告，内容和后面重复。

evidence.heading: 一起改
evidence.text: 哪里写错了，或者想推荐工具，看 [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md)。每次改了什么，记在 [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)。

evidence.heading: Part 1 · Use TOMC Memory
evidence.text:
**TOMC Memory** is an open-source tool built on Task-Oriented Memory Compilation (TOMC). It compresses and compiles context for AI assistants and provides task memory through explicitly saved notes. It is available through an MCP server and a Python API. Give it a history, the next task and a memory budget. It selects source text and computes supported state, relation or count records, so your application can send the prepared context in place of the full history. Preparation runs on CPU, with no training or extra model service.

Use task memory while making videos, organizing materials, handling files or developing code: save the brief, decisions, constraints, completed steps and remaining work with `remember_memory`, then use `recall_memory` to prepare those notes for the next task. These are examples of how to use saved notes. The recorded measurements below cover synthetic project histories and the paper benchmarks, with their own tasks and protocols; they do not establish performance for every task in these workflows.

Add the Python API to your own application, install the plugin in Codex or Claude Code, or connect Cursor, TRAE, Tencent WorkBuddy and Claude Desktop through local MCP. Savings depend on the history and task; short histories can stay intact. The default keeps about 80% of a long history. Compare 40% or 60% budgets on your own tasks when you need smaller requests; see the separate [Codex and Claude results](#measured-savings).

Reuse saved task notes in a new chat with the same assistant or another assistant. With both clients using the same TOMC database on one computer, you can reuse saved decisions, constraints and next steps. [Try the Codex → Claude Code → Codex handoff](#switch-assistants).


  


This is a preview, version **0.1.0**. Download th

evidence.text:
[](launch/media/v13/videos/TOMC_Overview_EN.mp4)

[Full video (1:37, with sound)](launch/media/v13/videos/TOMC_Overview_EN.mp4) · [Chinese video](launch/media/v13/videos/TOMC_Overview_ZH.mp4) · [Media and test scope](launch/media/v13/README.md)

The [measured results](#measured-savings) give the Codex and Claude Code protocols and their source records.

[First-run guide](#first-run-tomc) · [Python API](#use-before-your-api-call) · [Full results and limitations](#measured-savings).

TOMC is a research preview. Feedback, issues, pull requests and research collaboration are welcome. Device choice and assistant choice are independent; cross-device notebook transfer uses manual Git.

evidence.heading: Install in your assistant
evidence.text:
Choose the setup for your client. TOMC prepares context locally on CPU; your assistant generates the answer. The plugin itself needs no additional model API key or GPU.

**The host manages the active chat.** When Codex, Claude Code or another host owns conversation compaction, TOMC does not proactively recompact that chat. Unknown host state also defaults to host ownership. Use TOMC for separately supplied external history or explicitly saved notes. This is a tool-use policy, not an automatic compaction detector. [Context ownership](docs/context_ownership.md). Plugin packages 0.1.1 include this policy; the compiler core remains 0.1.0.

evidence.heading: Use before your API call
evidence.text:
Install the core package from this checkout with `python -m pip install -e .`. Prepare the history, inspect `prepared.prompt`, then send `prepared.messages` with your existing chat-completions client:

```python
from tomc import prepare_context

prepared = prepare_context(history, task)
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=model,
    messages=prepared.messages,
)
```

Here `history`, `task`, `client` and `model` are your application's existing inputs and client. **Replace the original history for this request; appending the prepared context to it adds input.** Keep any instructions your application needs. For other text APIs, map the messages to your provider's format. TOMC changes the request text without changing model weights. [API guide and token counting](docs/api_reference.md).

evidence.heading: String matching and input limits
evidence.text:
The reference parser recognizes forms such as `key = value`, `B copies A`, and `x -[rel]-> y`. Evidence selection and routing also use fixed lexical rules. Paraphrases, ambiguous names, implicit updates, and unfamiliar formats can lead to missed evidence or an unsuitable route.

For structured state, use the documented syntax and inspect the source links. For ordinary prose, use retrieval or a route that retains source text. These options preserve useful evidence but do not guarantee that every relevant detail fits the budget. [Supported operations](docs/method.md) · [Known limitations](docs/claims_and_limitations.md).

evidence.heading: Use from Python
evidence.text:
For a Python application, call `prepare_context(history, task)` before your existing reader call.

**Your reader model stays the same.** TOMC returns text you can use with any text-based LLM API, or copy into a chat interface. The built-in connector supports chat-completions-compatible APIs; other providers use your own client and message format. No model weights or API key are needed to construct memory. Answer generation uses your chosen model as usual.

```text
History + current task → TOMC on CPU → prepared context → your existing LLM API
```

The core package requires Python 3.10+ and has no runtime dependencies. From an activated environment in the checkout, install `python -m pip install -e .`:

```python
from tomc import prepare_context

context = prepare_context(
    "The workshop now has 28 attendees. Room B is available but not booked.",
    "What should we do next?",
)
print(context.prompt)  # paste into a chat interface
# Or pass context.messages to your existing chat-completions client.
# For other APIs, use context.prompt or map the messages to their input format.
```

github_projects.name: cida
github_projects.description: 辞达：用你选择的大模型，在 Mac 的任何地方翻译和润色文字。Translate and polish text anywhere on your Mac.
github_projects.description_zh: 辞达：用你选择的大模型，在 Mac 的任何地方翻译和润色文字。Translate and polish text anywhere on your Mac.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: 辞达：用你选择的大模型，在 Mac 的任何地方翻译和润色文字。Translate and polish text anywhere on your Mac.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
辞达


  用你选择的大模型，在 Mac 的任何地方翻译和润色文字。
  官网 · 下载 · English

evidence.heading: 怎么用
evidence.text:
- **选中文字，按 <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd>。** 面板带着选中的文字出现，并执行动作栏的第一项，默认是翻译。翻译时，其他语言都译成你的语言，默认简体中文，可以在设置里写成任何语言、方言或文体，比如粤语；你的语言译成「翻译成」后面写着的外语，默认英文，要换就在那里直接写，比如日本語、英式英语。

  

- **选中文字，按 <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>F</kbd>，直接改进并替换。** 润色后的文字保持原来的语言，在原应用按 <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>Z</kbd> 可以撤销。生成时再按一次取消；如果你已经编辑文字、改变选区或切换应用，辞达保留结果，供你查看和手动复制。

  

- **在设置的「动作」页，添加自己的文字处理方式。** 比如精简、提取待办或改成邮件：写好名字和提示词，点「完成」，就能用当前模型预览固定样例。拖动排序，第一项成为面板的默认动作；截图翻译和原处翻译仍执行翻译。

  

- **屏幕上的文字，按 <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd>。** 框出要翻译的部分，辞达在本机识别后翻译。

  

- **在原处读外文，指着一段按 <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd>。** 这一段就地换成译文，前后的消息还是原文，带着上下文读；再按一次换回。

  

- **要连续读一门看不懂的语言，按 <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>⇧</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> 翻译整个窗口。** 比如 Slack 的频道或一篇长文：新内容出现就翻译，再按一次停止；想看某一段的原文，指着它按 <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd>。译文写在辞达的纸上，代码保持原样；点击和滚动照常落到原来的应用。

  

按 <kbd>Esc</kbd> 回到原来的应用。面板隐藏后请求会继续完成，下次唤出时结果还在。

evidence.heading: 安装
evidence.text:
需要 macOS 15 或更新版本，以及一个大模型服务。

1. 下载 [Cida.dmg](https://cida-releases.xuanwo.io/latest/Cida.dmg)。安装包经过 Developer ID 签名和 Apple 公证。
2. 打开 DMG，把辞达拖进「应用程序」，再从启动台或聚焦搜索打开。辞达只在菜单栏显示图标，不占用 Dock。
3. 按 <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>,</kbd> 打开设置，点「复制配置提示词」，交给 Claude Code、Codex 等 AI 助手。它会问你用哪家服务，通过辞达的[命令行](#命令行)写好配置，再用 `check` 确认能用。

API Key 不经过助手：它会请你复制 Key 后运行一条命令，Key 直接存进钥匙串。支持 OpenAI Chat Completions、Responses 与 Anthropic Messages 三种接口，在本机运行的模型（例如 `http://127.0.0.1:8080`）不需要 Key。辞达本身免费，模型调用按服务商的价格计费。

两个权限都是可选的，在设置的「快捷键」页点「去授权」即可开启：

| 权限 | 开启后 | 不开启时 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 辅助功能 | 按 <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> 带入选区；<kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> 原处翻译；<kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>F</kbd> 改进并替换 | 先 <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>C</kbd>，再在面板里 <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>V</kbd>；原处翻译和改进并替换不可用 |
| 屏幕录制 | 用 <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> 截图翻译；原处译文可跟随纵向滚动 | 截图翻译不可用；原处译文在滚动停止后重新定位 |

evidence.heading: 隐私
evidence.text:
- API Key 只存在 macOS 的钥匙串里。
- 不保存历史记录，不收集任何数据，文字处理和动作预览的请求只发往你选择的服务商。
- 截图在本机用 Apple 的 Vision 识别，图片不会离开你的 Mac。原处翻译通过辅助功能读取文字；已有屏幕录制权限时，还会在本机内存中处理源窗口的画面，让译文跟随滚动，画面不保存、不上传。未授权时，滚动中的译文暂时隐去，停下后重新定位。

evidence.heading: 快捷键
evidence.text:
| 按键 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> | 显示或隐藏面板 |
| <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> | 截图翻译 |
| <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> | 原处翻译：指针下这一段换成译文，再按换回；加 <kbd>⇧</kbd> 翻译整个窗口 |
| <kbd>⌥</kbd> <kbd>F</kbd> | 改进并替换选中文字；生成时再按一次取消 |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | 按顺序切换动作 |
| <kbd>Return</kbd> | 执行（<kbd>⇧</kbd> <kbd>Return</kbd> 换行） |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | 隐藏面板 |

四个全局快捷键都可以在设置里重新录制或清除。

evidence.heading: 命令行
evidence.text:
应用里的可执行文件就是辞达的命令行，不需要另外安装。它与正在运行的辞达共用同一份配置，改完立即生效：

```sh
cida=/Applications/Cida.app/Contents/MacOS/Cida
$cida config schema                        # 全部字段、取值与说明
$cida config show
$cida config set model=deepseek-chat       # 一次可写多项，也有 unset 与 reset
pbpaste | $cida config set api-key --stdin
$cida check --verbose                      # 真的请求一次，失败时给出请求与响应
```

每个命令都可以加 `--json`。API Key 只从 `--stdin`、`--file` 或 `--env` 读取，写在命令行参数里会被拒绝。字段的完整说明见 [`Design/spec/configuration.md`](Design/spec/configuration.md)。

evidence.heading: Why Antirion
evidence.text:
- **The fastest gateway we have measured.** Sub-millisecond overhead at thousands of requests per
  second on 4 vCPUs, and several times the throughput of the next fastest gateway on the same
  machine ([Performance](#performance)). Rust, no garbage collector, no interpreter, one data
  thread per CPU.
- **One binary, console included.** The gateway, the Admin API and the web console ship as a
  single Rust binary (or a distroless image). No sidecars, no separate UI deployment, no runtime
  to install.
- **Every major provider behind one API.** OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock,
  Google Vertex AI, Gemini, Mistral, Cohere, Groq, Together, Fireworks, DeepSeek, xAI, Cerebras,
  DeepInfra, Perplexity, and any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible server such as vLLM. Clients
  speak OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or Bedrock; Antirion translates between them.
- **Routing that keeps you up.** Fallback chains, weighted splits, least cost, least latency,
  least busy, tiers, content classifiers, retries, hedging and circuit breakers, decided per
  request and recorded in the request log.
- **Spend under control.** Rate limits and budgets in dollars or tokens on the organization,
  team, project and key, with prices per Model, a cost ledger and alerts before a budget runs
  out.
- **Safety at the edge.** Guardrails for PII, secrets, keywords, regexes, JSON schemas, tool
  permissions, topics, moderation, model-based judges and partner services that catch prompt
  injection, on requests, responses and streams, with redaction that keeps the format.
- **Ready for production.** Exact and semantic caching, MCP and agent gateways, SSO with OIDC,
  SAML and SCIM, an audit log with change requests, and a standalone node or a cluster on
  PostgreSQL and Valkey.

evidence.heading: Getting started
evidence.text:
You need Docker and an API key from OpenAI or Anthropic.

**1. Start the gateway.**

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 8081:8081 -v antirion-data:/var/lib/antirion eliasbiondo/antirion
```

No config file is needed. The first start prints the console's address and an admin token, shown
that once:

```text
  Console      http://localhost:8081/ui/
  Admin token  ak-antirion-…
               Shown on this first start only; it is kept in
               /var/lib/antirion/data/bootstrap-token
  Data plane   http://localhost:8080/v1
```

The data plane (the `/v1` API your apps call) is on port 8080, the admin plane (the Admin API and
the console) on 8081. The gateway keeps its data in the `antirion-data` volume, so a new container
finds the same providers, keys and history. `docker run --rm eliasbiondo/antirion serve --help`
lists the ports, the data directory and the other settings.

**2. Sign in.** Open <http://localhost:8081/ui/> and paste the admin token into **Admin token**.
Lost it? It is kept in the volume:
`docker cp <container>:/var/lib/antirion/data/bootstrap-token - | tar -xO`. From the console you
can invite your team, so everyone signs in with their own account.

**3. Add a provider.** **Providers → Add provider**, choose **OpenAI** or **Anthropic** and paste its
API key. **Test** the connection: the gateway asks the provider for its models, and the provider is
saved only once the test passes, so a wrong key shows here. Then **Add provider**.

**4. Add a Model.** **Models → Add model**, pick the provider, then a model from the list the
provider returned, such as `gpt-4.1-mini` or `claude-haiku-4-5`. The list shows each model's list
price, which applies when you leave the price fields blank. Name it `chat`, the name your apps will
send, and **Add model**.

github_projects.description: One endpoint for every LLM vendor. Any SDK, any model, any tool. One Rust binary.
github_projects.description_zh: 每个 LLM 供应商只有一个端点。任何 SDK、任何模型、任何工具。一个 Rust 二进制文件。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: One endpoint for every LLM vendor. Any SDK, any model, any tool. One Rust binary.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
The universal adapter for AI.
  
    
    
    
    
    
    
  



**Respan Gateway** is a single Rust binary that sits between your code and
every AI API. Point the SDK you already use at it, and it connects you to
everything: chat models, images, video and voice from every major provider;
tools for any model, from web search and memory to code sandboxes and any MCP
server; and traffic control (format translation, fallback, retries and hedged
requests), with a live log of every call. **[▶ Watch the demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVv2ibXiTXM)**

evidence.heading: Key features
evidence.text:
- **Any client, any model**
  OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages and Gemini API
  clients can all call any model, with streaming, tools,
  images and reasoning translated.

- **Multimodal**
  Realtime voice across vendors (an OpenAI Realtime client talks to Gemini
  Live, and back), plus images, speech, transcription, embeddings and video
  through OpenAI's or Gemini's APIs, to any vendor that has them.

- **MCP tools for every model**
  Put MCP servers or built-in tool vendors behind the gateway, from web search
  to code sandboxes. It runs their tools inside chat requests, so a plain chat
  call can use them, whatever the client or model.

- **Traffic control**
  Named routes, globs and `provider/model`; fallback, retries, cheapest or
  fastest; and hedged requests that race a slow call against a second
  provider.

- **Observability**
  A live request log with cost, latency and tokens for every call, and traces
  in [Respan](https://respan.ai), where span-02 analyzes how your agents
  behave.

- **Best-in-class performance**
  0.07 ms of added latency, 56,000 requests per second and 31 MB of memory in
  our benchmarks: about 3× the throughput of the next
  fastest gateway we tested.

- **Write your own plugin in minutes**
  Every feature above is a plugin, built on the same public Rust API you can
  use: one trait with four hooks. Start from the [plugin guide](docs/plugins.md)
  or an [example](examples/README.md) such as guardrails, PII masking or
  billing.

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
**1. Install**

```bash
pip install respan-gateway
```

Or `cargo install respan-gateway`, or a
[GitHub release](https://github.com/respanai/respan-gateway/releases).

**2. Run it with your keys**

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
respan-gateway
```

No config file needed: every vendor whose key is set becomes a provider.

**3. Call any model from any SDK**

```python
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(base_url="http://localhost:8080", api_key="unused")
reply = client.messages.create(
    model="gpt-6-luna", max_tokens=256,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello from the Anthropic SDK"}])
print(reply.content[0].text)
```

The web UI is at [localhost:8080/ui/](http://localhost:8080/ui/). Next:
[configuration](docs/configuration.md) and [MCP tools](docs/mcp.md).

evidence.heading: Other ways to run it
evidence.text:
- [Python, in-process](python/README.md) — Run the gateway inside your Python app, with no server.
- [Embed in Rust](docs/plugins.md#in-a-gateway-of-your-own) — Mount the gateway in your own Rust service.
- [Docker](Dockerfile) — Run the image `ghcr.io/respanai/respan-gateway` on any container host.

evidence.heading: Performance
evidence.text:
| | Respan Gateway | Bifrost | Portkey | LiteLLM (1 worker) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Added latency (p50) | **0.07 ms** | 0.16 ms | 0.17 ms | 4.34 ms |
| Throughput | **56,734/s** | 18,182/s | 4,187/s | 268/s |
| Memory | **31 MB** | 488 MB | 350 MB | 418 MB |
| 1k streams, success | **100%** | 92–100% | — | 79% |
| 1k streams, memory | **128 MB** | 688 MB | — | 493 MB |
| p99, 5% slow calls | **105 ms** | 2,002 ms | 2,003 ms | 2,024 ms |

evidence.heading: Configuration
evidence.text:
You don't need a config file to start. When you want more, run
`respan-gateway init` for a commented `gateway.toml`. One file sets up keys,
providers, traffic control, tools and tracing:

```toml
client_keys = [{ name = "app", key = "env:APP_KEY" }]   # who may call the gateway

[providers.openai]                      # a built-in vendor: just add a key
vendor = "openai"
key = "env:OPENAI_API_KEY"

[providers.anthropic]
vendor = "anthropic"
key = "env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"

[providers.local]                       # any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
formats = ["openai-chat"]
base_url = "http://localhost:8000/v1"

[routes.smart]                          # clients ask for "model": "smart"
to = ["anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5", "openai/gpt-6-luna"]
hedge = "800ms"                         # race the second if the first is slow

[tools.search]                          # web search as MCP tools
vendor = "linkup"
key = "env:LINKUP_API_KEY"

[plugins.tool_loop]                     # every model can use them
servers = ["search"]

[plugins.respan]                        # trace every call in Respan
key = "env:RESPAN_API_KEY"
```

`respan-gateway check` validates it, and `--watch` or `SIGHUP` reloads it
without a restart. Without client keys, the gateway answers only on loopback
and refuses to start on a public address.

**Reference:** [configuration](docs/configuration.md) ·
[vendors](docs/vendors.md) · [tool vendors](docs/tool-vendors.md) ·
[MCP and tools](docs/mcp.md) · [`gateway.example.toml`](gateway.example.toml)

evidence.heading: Supported API formats
evidence.text:
Call the gateway in any format on the left, and it reaches every provider on
the right, translating between them.

| | Your code calls | It can reach |
|---|---|---|
| **Chat** | OpenAI Chat CompletionsOpenAI ResponsesAnthropic MessagesGemini API |           any chat model, whichever of the four formats it speaks |
| **Realtime voice** | OpenAI RealtimeGemini Live |   OpenAI ⇄ Gemini voice; Mistral for transcription |
| **Images** | OpenAI ImagesGemini Images |      |
| **Speech, transcription** | OpenAI SpeechOpenAI Transcriptions |    |
| **Embeddings** | OpenAI Embeddings |         |
| **Video** | OpenAI VideosGemini Veo |  Google Veo |
| **Decisions** | Respan DecisionsTypeSafe System One |   |
| **Tools** | MCP |  your MCP servers and tool vendors |
| **Anything else** | A vendor's own API | Relayed to that vendor untouched |

Each vendor's formats are in [vendors](docs/vendors.md), and the translation
details in each format's README: [chat](crates/formats/conversation-http/README.md),
[media](crates/formats/media-http/README.md),
[realtime](crates/formats/realtime-ws/README.md) and
[decisions](crates/formats/decision-http/README.md).

github_projects.description: A lightweight Python SDK and CLI for evaluating recursive self-improvement (RSI) methods across agent benchmarks.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: A lightweight Python SDK and CLI for evaluating recursive self-improvement (RSI) methods across agent benchmarks.

evidence.heading: RSI Eval
evidence.text:
A lightweight Python SDK and CLI for evaluating recursive self-improvement (RSI)
methods across agent benchmarks. Bring your own improvement loop, choose your
tasks, and evaluate each candidate through one interface.

`candidate -> evaluate() -> task feedback -> your next candidate`

[Quick Start](#quick-start) · [Installation](#installation) ·
[Usage Examples](#usage-examples) · [Custom RSI Integration](#custom-rsi-integration) ·
[Custom Benchmark Integration](#custom-benchmark-integration)

evidence.heading: Why rsi-eval?
evidence.text:
An RSI method needs to run candidates, collect feedback, and decide what to
change next. RSI Eval supplies the evaluation boundary so that your method can
use existing benchmarks without implementing their execution and result
handling from scratch.

- **Keep control of your method.** You choose candidate generation, memory,
  selection, stopping rules, and evolve/test tasks. Call `evaluate()` from your
  own loop; no optimizer base class is required.
- **Reuse benchmark protocols.** Select pinned tasks and run their graders.
  Raw rewards, task budgets, and benchmark-specific metrics retain their meaning.
- **Get usable feedback.** Read per-task scores, execution status, token usage,
  verifier output, and trajectory paths through a common result format.
- **Record and resume experiments.** Each evaluation snapshots the candidate,
  records task and source identities, and preserves results for explicit recovery.

The catalog contains **24 evaluation configurations and two labeled legacy
subsets**. It covers coding, reasoning, engineering, and domain workflows:

| Area | Bundled benchmark families | Guides |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Terminal and software engineering | Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1, SWE-bench Verified, Multilingual and Pro, Aider Polyglot | [Additional coding benchmarks](docs/harbor-expansion.md) |
| Code generation | LiveCodeBench | [LiveCodeBench](docs/livecodebench.md) |
| Reasoning and mathematics | MMLU, GPQA, ARC-AGI, MGSM | [Reasoning](docs/reasoning-and-mce.md), [MGSM](docs/mgsm.md) |
| Reading comprehension | DROP | [DROP](docs/drop.md) |
| MCE tasks | FiNER, USPTO, Symptom2Disease, LawBench, AEGIS | [MCE](docs/reasoning-and-mce.md) |
| Engineering | EngDesign-Open, Frontier-Eng | [EngDesign](docs/engdesign.md), [Frontier-Eng](docs/frontier-eng.md) |
| Do

evidence.heading: Quick Start
evidence.text:
Preview a one-task evaluation with Python 3.12 or newer:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Danielxu0208/rsi_eval.git
cd rsi_eval
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e .

rsi-eval list
rsi-eval preview --config examples/evaluate.json
```

The example selects Terminal-Bench 2.0's `extract-elf` task and the bundled Codex
candidate. `preview` resolves the task references, candidate hash, and run
settings without Docker, Harbor, a login, or model calls.

For an actual evaluation, complete the execution setup below, then follow
[Run an evaluation](#run-an-evaluation).

evidence.heading: Core and execution backend
evidence.text:
The Quick Start installs the SDK and CLI from the checkout. To run benchmark
evaluations, install the Harbor extra in the same environment:

```sh
python -m pip install -e '.[harbor]'
```

This pins **Harbor 0.18.0**. Its executable must be on `PATH`, or specified through
`options.harbor_executable` in your run configuration. For a non-editable
installation, use `python -m pip install '.[harbor]'` instead.

The wheel includes the SDK, CLI, Codex candidate template, and four method
integrations. Upstream method repositories and benchmark assets are obtained
separately during preparation.

evidence.heading: Docker and task requirements
evidence.text:
The default execution backend runs tasks in Docker. On Linux, install Docker
Engine with Compose and Buildx. On macOS, use Docker Desktop or a Colima Linux
VM. Verify access from the account that will run evaluations:

```sh
docker info
docker compose version
docker buildx version
```

For a dedicated Colima profile on Apple Silicon:

```sh
brew install colima docker docker-compose docker-buildx
colima start rsi-eval --cpus 6 --memory 12 --disk 120 \
  --vm-type vz --vz-rosetta --runtime docker --activate=false \
  --ssh-config=false --mount "$PWD:w"
source scripts/mac-env.sh
```

Adjust resources for your machine. Rosetta is required for this Colima command;
x86-only images need emulation on Apple Silicon. Set
`DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64` when required by a task, and clear it for
configurations that select platforms per task.

Some tasks require an NVIDIA GPU, native Linux amd64, or external assets. See
[Frontier-Eng GPU setup](docs/frontier-eng.md#nvidia-gpu-setup) and
[EngDesign requirements](docs/engdesign.md). JobBench, Harvey LAB, and APEX require
separate native judge credentials, described in their guides. Check publisher
usage terms when choosing data for evolution; APEX is released for evaluation,
not training or parameter fitting.

evidence.heading: Usage Examples
evidence.text: Run these examples from the repository root with the virtual environment active.

evidence.heading: Use the Python SDK
evidence.text:
The SDK uses the same target, selection, and options as the CLI:

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from rsi_eval import BenchmarkSelection, RunOptions, TargetSpec, evaluate

profile = json.loads(Path("profile.json").read_text())["codex"]
target = TargetSpec(
    artifact_dir=Path("templates/codex_agent"),
    entrypoint="rsi_eval.harbor_codex:Agent",
    model=profile["model"],
    config={
        "codex_auth_dir": profile["auth_dir"],
        "codex_version": profile["expected_version"],
        "reasoning_effort": profile["reasoning_effort"],
    },
)
result = evaluate(
    target=target,
    benchmark=BenchmarkSelection(
        "terminal-bench", "2.0", task_ids=("extract-elf",)
    ),
    options=RunOptions(repetitions=1, concurrency=1),
    output_dir=Path("runs/sdk-candidate"),
)
print(result.status)
for trial in result.trials:
    print(trial.task_id, trial.status, trial.reward)
print(result.report_path)
```

The bundled subscription Codex target requires `concurrency=1`. Custom Harbor
agents can implement other execution and model protocols.

**宣传片**：一份产品简报 → 竖版宣传片（9:16）
**口播配画面**：一段口播 `talk.mp4` → 配好画面的口播（动效卡片 / AI 画面）
**讲课视频**：一份讲稿或 brief → 16:9 讲解课（可切竖版）
原名 promo-video-skill / 蒸馏视频，旧地址自动跳转。

evidence.heading: 为什么是精酿
evidence.text:
**便宜模型只填表，不写代码。** 宣传片填 `storyboard.json`，口播填 `broll.json`，讲课填 `lesson.json`：挑版式、填文字。所以 DeepSeek 这类模型也能出合格片。

**合规和质检先拦一遍。** 广告法、行业规则、数字出处、版式、动效有没有停死，有一项不过就不出片。

**开源，可以商用。** Apache-2.0。分发时注明出处。渲染出的视频不要求署名。

evidence.heading: 快速开始
evidence.text:
**装依赖。**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Finderchangchang/brewreel.git
cd brewreel/template && npm install && npx remotion browser ensure
cd .. && pip install numpy scipy imageio-ffmpeg
```

**宣传片**（`examples/ledger.json`）

```bash
node scripts/validate.mjs examples/ledger.json
node scripts/make.mjs examples/ledger.json --out ../brewreel-out/ledger
```

校验通过后出片，要几分钟，最后一行是「交付：<mp4 路径>」。`--out` 不能指向仓库里面。

**口播配画面**

```bash
node scripts/talk.mjs path/to/project --out ../brewreel-out/talk
```

项目目录里放好 `talk.mp4`。本机转写，动效画面直接画；AI 画面先占位，不花钱。

**讲课视频**（`examples/lesson/mascot-demo.json`，mock 配音）

```bash
node scripts/lesson/make-lesson.mjs examples/lesson/mascot-demo.json --out ../brewreel-out/first-lesson --voice-provider mock --no-bgm
```

用占位配音看版式和节奏，不花配音费。成功时最后一行是「交付：」。

需要 Node.js 18+、Python 3.10+；Windows 只支持 x64。平台、环境变量和完整说明见 [安装与上手](docs/quickstart.md)。

evidence.heading: 宣传片
evidence.text:
**你给什么**：一份产品简报。

**你得到什么**：竖版宣传片（9:16；`journey` 默认 4:5）。

**一条命令**：`node scripts/make.mjs examples/ledger.json --out ../brewreel-out/ledger`

实验写法 `scene.json`：模型写语义，引擎算样子。`node scripts/scene/make-scene.mjs examples/scene/c-techbrief.json --out ../brewreel-out/scene --voice-provider mock`。说明见 [场景](docs/scene.md)。

- 3 种配方：`cards` 卡片信息流（默认，9:16）、`quiz` 答题互动（9:16）、`journey` 角色漫游（默认 4:5，也可 9:16）。
- 6 个行业：软件、餐饮、电商实物、成人职业培训、生活美容、文旅住宿。各带广告法和行业规则。不做医疗美容、处方药 / 药品、K12 学科培训、保健品功效宣称、烟草。
- 配音可选 MiniMax、阿里云、火山引擎。镜头时长跟着旁白，字幕逐字点亮，配乐在人声处压低。
- 数据图表有条形、折线、点图、堆叠、环形。图上的数必须能在引用的事实原文里找到。见 [dataChart](docs/shots/dataChart.md)。
- 校验自查有 ✗ 不出片。配乐现场合成，卡着镜头切点；字幕可选中文或英文。cards 默认 6 套主题，另有 12 套可选，见 [配色](styles/cards/THEMES.md)。

详细说明 → [功能](docs/features.md)

evidence.heading: 口播配画面
evidence.text:
看演示视频

**你给什么**：一段口播 `talk.mp4`。

**你得到什么**：配好画面的口播。动效卡片不花钱；AI 画面要先估价、人审。

**一条命令**：`node scripts/talk.mjs path/to/project --out ../brewreel-out/talk`

- 本机用 SenseVoice（FunAudioLLM / 阿里通义实验室，由 sherpa-onnx 运行）转写。已有 `talk.srt` 不会被覆盖。
- 动效画面五种：关键词、清单、步骤、数字、对比。字只能照抄原话，脚本逐字核对，不花钱。
- 动效卡片默认跟着主风格配色。加 `--motion-look cutpaper-meadow` 或 `cutpaper-dusk` 换成剪纸拼贴：纸纹底、手剪卡片，说到重点词卡片抛起再落下。也不花钱。见 [动效外观](docs/motion-looks.md)。
- AI 画面用 MiniMax H3，全片共用 `broll/character.json` 里的一个机器人：积木风（`wood-blocks`，默认）、黏土定格（`clay-stopmotion`）、分层纸艺（`paper-layers`）。手绘线稿（`ink-sketch`）只能占位预览。默认最多 2 段。

**风格工厂。** 用一句话描述一种 AI 画面风格。脚本写配置、出参考图、看图打分、做一张静态试拍。看图会看错，最后要人看。人自己跑 `node scripts/broll/approve-style.mjs <id>`，AI 助手不许替人运行。欢迎把批准后的风格用 Pull Request 贡献回来。见 [风格工厂](docs/style-factory.md)。

**花钱和人审**：AI 画面先加 `--provider minimax-h3 --dry-run` 估价，加上 `--yes` 才生成。正式片要人自己跑 `node scripts/broll/approve.mjs <项目目录> --out <仓库外目录>`。`talk.mjs` 不会替你跑，批准命令只能人跑。

详细说明 → [口播配画面](docs/broll.md)

evidence.heading: 讲课视频
evidence.text:
**你给什么**：一份讲稿 `lesson.json`，或一份 brief。

**你得到什么**：16:9 讲解课。可以另出竖版切片和封面。

**一条命令**：`node scripts/lesson/make-lesson.mjs examples/lesson/mascot-demo.json --out ../brewreel-out/first-lesson --voice-provider mock --no-bgm`

- 20 种版式，4 套主题：`paper` 卷宗（普法默认）、`lecture` 讲台（其余默认）、`product` 产品、`editorial` 杂志（只能手选，不能用于普法）。
- 可以带讲解员和品牌包装。预设卡通不花钱。不写品牌也能出片。
- 改完一页后用同一个输出目录再跑，没改的页会复用。
- 普法没有有效审稿记录就不出片。技术课不强制。AI 助手不能替人签字。
- 领域包：`tech` 技术讲解，`legal` 普法。普法的法条只从已核对的《民法典》语料回填。

**花钱和人审**：照片建角色要本人同意，照片会发给 MiniMax 做识别，会花钱。没有当次明确要求不要跑。未确认的角色不能正式出片，确认只能人跑。

详细说明 → [讲课视频](docs/lesson.md)

evidence.heading: 已知限制
evidence.text:
- **还是预览版。** 不建议把成片不经人工修改直接对外发布。当成初稿，看完再改再发。
- **有的接入还没真实跑过。** 阿里云和火山引擎配音还没用真实 key。DeepSeek Harness 插件还没接真实 DeepSeek 模型。MiniMax 配音用真实 key 出过片。
- **没有实拍就只能插画。** 不做医疗美容、处方药 / 药品、K12 学科培训、保健品功效宣称、烟草。

测试方法和仍存在的问题见 [已知限制](docs/limitations.md)。

github_projects.name: wx-bot
github_projects.description: 把微信接入你的 AI Agent（Grok / Muse / Claude 等）· Connect WeChat to your personal AI agent via official iLink
github_projects.description_zh: 把微信接入你的 AI Agent（Grok / Muse / Claude 等）· Connect WeChat to your personal AI agent via official iLink

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: 把微信接入你的 AI Agent（Grok / Muse / Claude 等）· Connect WeChat to your personal AI agent via official iLink

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text: wx-bot 把微信接入到 Personal Agent（Grok、Muse 等）。 微信消息经腾讯官方 ClawBot / iLink 进入本机 wx-bot， 落盘后推送给你的 Agent（webhook）或由 Agent 拉取（pull）；Agent 再用 wx-bot send 发回微信。 --- > [!IMPORTANT] > **🤖 如果你是 Agent：先读 [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/lawrencewzen/wx-bot/blob/main/AGENTS.md)，找到你对应的文件，按步骤执行。** > Grok Bot：创建 routine 后，**必须在聊天回复里直接发出「Webhook URL」和「Webhook key」两个字段链接**，用户自己找不到。

evidence.heading: 特点
evidence.text:
- **不丢消息**：先落盘到本地 SQLite 收件箱，再确认；投递失败自动重投。
- **只出站**：不对外开端口，本地 API 只监听 loopback。
- **只能本人使用**：只理会扫码登录的那个微信号，不支持好友。
- **两种投递**：`webhook` 推给 Agent，`pull` 由 Agent 来取。
- 收发文本、图片、语音（带转写）、文件、视频。支持 Linux / macOS。

```
WeChat ──iLink──▶ wx-bot (inbox) ──webhook / pull──▶ Agent
       ◀─────────────────────────── wx-bot send ────┘
```

evidence.heading: 快速开始
evidence.text:
把这句话发给你的 Grok Bot 或 Muse：

```
帮我用 wx-bot 把微信接入你：https://github.com/lawrencewzen/wx-bot
```

它会自己装好，你只需要**用微信扫码**（Grok 还要你点两个链接，把 URL 贴回聊天、把 key 填进加密框）。

> [!NOTE]
> 装好后**先用微信给 ClawBot 发一条消息**，Agent 才能回复你。

> [!WARNING]
> Grok Bot 等 Agent 的云电脑会自动休眠，也会被自动重置；休眠或重置时 wx-bot 可能被直接停掉，安装的程序、服务、登录态都可能丢失。请按 [Grok 安装第 8 步](docs/agents/grok.md#安装步骤) 配好每 10 分钟的保活。登录态丢了需要重新扫码，期间收不到微信消息。

其他接法：[Pi Durable（Docker）](docs/integrations/pi-durable.md) · [Cloudflare Workers](docs/integrations/cloudflare.md) · 手动安装 ↓

evidence.heading: 手动安装
evidence.text:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lawrencewzen/wx-bot/main/install.sh | bash
# 源码安装：git clone 后运行 ./install.sh --service（--service 同时装开机自启）
```

编辑 `~/.config/wx-bot/config.json`，参考 [webhook 示例](examples/config.example.json) 或 [pull 示例](examples/config.pull.example.json)；密钥写进 `~/.config/wx-bot/env`，配置里用 `env:VAR` 引用。

```bash
wx-bot login xiaox          # 微信扫码
wx-bot run                  # 启动
wx-bot health --grace 0     # 退出码 0 才算装好
```

evidence.heading: 对接
evidence.text:
**收**：每条消息是一个 JSON 事件，含 `event_id`、`from_wxid`、`text`、`voice_text`、`media[]`（本机文件路径）。**同一事件可能送达多次，按 `event_id` 去重。**

- webhook：POST 到你的地址，返回 2xx 即送达。
- pull：`wx-bot inbox pull --lease 5m` 领取，处理完 `wx-bot inbox ack <event_id>`。

**回**：

```bash
wx-bot send --binding xiaox --to <wxid> --text - <<'EOF'
回复内容（引号、$ 都不用转义）
EOF
wx-bot send --binding xiaox --to <wxid> --image ./a.jpg   # 还有 --file / --video
```

**只发纯文本**，微信不渲染 Markdown。事件格式、签名、本地 HTTP API、`alert` 异常通知等细节见 [`docs/protocol.md`](docs/protocol.md)。

evidence.heading: 运维
evidence.text:
| 做什么 | 命令 |
| --- | --- |
| 看状态 | `wx-bot status` |
| 查微信聊天记录 | `wx-bot chatlog [--since 24h] [--with wxid]` |
| 排查收不到消息 | `wx-bot health --grace 0` |
| 重放已放弃（dead）的消息 | `wx-bot inbox requeue [--binding B] [event_id...]` |
| 升级（不用重新扫码） | `wx-bot update` |
| 回滚 | `wx-bot update --version <版本>` |
| 卸载 | `wx-bot uninstall --yes`（加 `--keep-data` 保留登录） |

配置项 `chatlog_days`（整数，默认 `0` 关闭）开启后，收发原文按天追加到 `<state_dir>/chatlog/<binding>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl`，并保留最近 N 天；改回 `0` 只停止写入，不删已有文件。聊天记录是隐私数据，默认不写。查询用 `wx-bot chatlog --since 24h`（可加 `--with <wxid>`、`--binding`、`--limit`、`--json`）；未开启且没有历史文件时退出码 1，并提示如何打开。

v0.4.0 之前的版本，重跑一遍 `install.sh` 即可升级。也可以直接让 Agent「把 wx-bot 升级到最新版」。

evidence.heading: 常见问题
evidence.text:
| 现象 | 处理 |
| --- | --- |
| Agent 收不到消息 | 先跑 `wx-bot health --grace 0`，按提示处理；详见[断线排查](docs/agents/troubleshoot.md) |
| 好友发的消息收不到 | 预期行为，wx-bot 只能本人使用 |
| `send` 报 `no context_token` | 对方还没给 ClawBot 发过消息，先发一条 |
| 日志出现 `-14` / `expired` | 登录过期，重新 `wx-bot login <binding>` |
| 只能走代理出网 | 把 `https_proxy` 写进 `~/.config/wx-bot/env`，重启服务 |
| `status` 里有 `dead` 消息 | 被 Agent 拒绝（400/413/422；响应体含 rate limit 的 400 会按 1/2/5/10 分钟重投，不记 dead）或超过 7 天，看日志 |
| 二维码要发给别人扫 | `wx-bot login <binding> --qr-png ./qr.png` |

github_projects.description: Build AI phone agents on your own computer and test every change with an AI caller. Open source, runs free with no API keys, cents per call with your own keys. Imports Dialogflow CX.
github_projects.description_zh: 在你自己的电脑上构建 AI 电话智能体，并用 AI 拨号员测试每次更改。开源，无需 API 密钥即可免费运行，自用密钥每次通话几美分。导入 Dialogflow CX。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Build AI phone agents on your own computer and test every change with an AI caller. Open source, runs free with no API keys, cents per call with your own keys. Imports Dialogflow CX.

evidence.heading: README
📋 Test any phone agent for free
evidence.text:
Lampline's **Evals** tab phones a voice agent over a real phone line, plays the
caller with an AI **Test Caller**, and grades the call against what should
happen. It works on any agent with a phone number: one built in Lampline,
Dialogflow CX, CX Agent Studio, Vapi, Retell, or your IVR.


  
    

  
  

    
    

- **Free calls through Google Voice.** The Lampline Phone Bridge extension (Chrome or Edge) connects the call's audio to the Test Caller inside the browser: no cables, Windows or Mac. Or use any phone on speaker.
- **Graded, with reasons.** You write who is calling, what they want and what must happen; your model grades the transcript, check by check. A call that heard nothing shows *Didn't run*, never *Failed*.
- **Tough callers.** Background noise, accents, interruptions, long pauses, hesitant or rambling speech.
- **The agent's speed, as callers hear it.** Typical and p95 response time, phone line included.
- **Bring your test scripts.** Paste Hammer, Cyara or spreadsheet tests and they become runnable cases. Replay any failed call.

[How to run evals →](docs/EVALS.md)
    
  


Only call agents you own or are allowed to test. You press Call yourself:
Google Voice doesn't allow automated dialing.

evidence.heading: 🔁 Bring your Dialogflow CX and CX Agent Studio agents
evidence.text:
Export an agent from Google's console, drop the .zip on **New agent → Import**, and
it opens in the builder: flows, pages, forms, routes, playbooks and tools carried
over, with a report of anything to check before it takes calls. It works the
other way too: **Export** writes any agent back as a Dialogflow CX package or a
CX Agent Studio app.


  
    

  
  

      📥 Import. A Dialogflow CX package or a CX Agent Studio app (JSON or YAML). The conversion runs on your computer and never runs code from the export.
    
    

  
  

      ✏️ Ready to edit. Pages become scripted pages, playbooks become LLM steps, flows group them, and webhooks and OpenAPI tools become tools.
    
  


| From Dialogflow CX | Becomes |
|---|---|
| Flows and pages | Flows of [scripted pages](engine/README.md#scripted-pages-and-flows): entry messages said word for word |
| Form parameters, entity types | Form fields with their types, choices and synonyms, patterns and keypad input |
| Intent and condition routes, no-match handlers | Transfers the model decides, rules, and "no match" transfers |
| Playbooks | LLM steps with their goal, guidelines and steps |
| Webhooks, OpenAPI tools, data store tools | Tools (webhooks answer with a mock until connected) and local knowledge search |

| From CX Agent Studio | Becomes |
|---|---|
| Root agent and child agents | A root agent with sub-agents and transfers both ways |
| Global instruction, variables | Global instructions and context variables |
| OpenAPI toolsets, Python tools, data stores | HTTP tools, tools with example answers, and local knowledge search |

From the terminal: `vk import auto export.zip` and `vk export dfcx|ces agents/<name>`.
The full mapping, both ways, and what doesn't carry over yet:
[cli/README.md](cli/README.md#import).

evidence.heading: 👀 A quick tour
evidence.text:
Sample data only.



  
    

  
  

      🧪 Test calls. Chat or talk through your microphone. The steps light up as the call moves, and every collected detail shows on the right.
    
    

  
  

      🧠 20 model providers. Pick one, paste a key, press Test connection. Speech runs in the cloud or free on your own computer.
    
  
  
    

  
  

      📞 Phone calls and SIP. Twilio, Telnyx, or your own SIP trunk, PBX or SBC through jambonz. Genesys, Avaya, Cisco and more are coming.
    
    

  
  

      🗄️ Data of its own. Collections agents look up and save during calls, and document search over your FAQs, all on your machine.
    
  


Screenshots use the bundled sample agents and made-up data.

evidence.heading: 🏠 Where it runs
evidence.text:
| | Status | |
|---|---|---|
| **Local and on-prem** | ✅ Available | One Docker container, or the engine natively, on any machine you control |
| **Google Cloud** | 🔜 Coming soon | A one-command deployment to your own Google Cloud project |

evidence.heading: 🚀 Quick start
evidence.text:
Needs Docker with Compose v2 (Docker Desktop is fine). **No API keys or accounts:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/C4rohan/lampline && cd lampline
scripts/docker-up.sh --free          # everything on this computer: Ollama, Moonshine and Kokoro
```

`--free` runs the model (Qwen3 4B in Ollama) and speech (Moonshine listening,
Kokoro speaking) on your own computer. The first start downloads about 3 GB and
shows progress; after that it starts in seconds. Replies are slower and simpler
than a cloud model's, and you can switch to any provider on the Integrations
page whenever you like. On a Mac, the native route is faster, because Ollama
uses the GPU outside Docker: install [Ollama](https://ollama.com), then
`scripts/engine-up.sh --free`.

Have API keys? Run `scripts/docker-up.sh` without `--free`. Either way it prints
a link like `http://localhost:7860/#/?key=…`: open it once and the page
remembers the key. Pick your model and voice on the Integrations page (or put keys like `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` in
`.env`; see `.env.example`). Your agents are in `./agents` (edit them, keep them
in git) and everything else the engine keeps, settings with your keys, records,
knowledge and downloaded models, is in `./.vpe-data`.
`scripts/docker-up.sh --down` stops it; `--logs` follows its log. Plain
`docker compose up -d --build` works too once `.env` has `VPE_DOCKER_API_KEY`.
Details: [engine/README.md](engine/README.md#docker).

Prefer no Docker? `scripts/engine-up.sh` runs the engine natively (Python 3.11+)
at http://localhost:7860, which also lets browser calls reach it directly.
Free, private speech: Integrations → Whisper and Kokoro → **Download models**,
or Moonshine for listening, which transcribes while the caller talks.

evidence.heading: ⚙️ How it works
evidence.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  you((You)) --> app[Lampline appbuilder, tests, integrations :7860]
  app --> engine[EnginePipecat pipelines]
  phone((Callers)) --> carriers[Twilio · Telnyx ·SIP via jambonz]
  carriers --> engine
  engine --> agents[(agents/YAML + Markdown)]
  engine --> data[(Records andknowledge, SQLite)]
  engine --> models{{Model and speechcloud APIs or localWhisper · Moonshine · Parakeet · Kokoro · Qwen3-TTS · Ollama}}
  engine -- tools --> hooks[Your APIs andMCP servers]
```

The engine reads the agent folders on every call, so a change is live on the
next call. Settings and keys live in a `chmod 600` file outside the repo.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: A Codex plugin for a better mobile development experience for android and iOS

evidence.heading: Mobile Dev for Codex
evidence.text:
Keep iOS and Android devices beside your Codex desktop chat while building,
running, and debugging mobile apps. Mobile Dev works with Expo, React Native,
SwiftUI, and other native mobile projects.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
Install the prebuilt plugin from the release marketplace:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/callstackincubator/codex-mobile-dev-plugin.git --ref release/latest
codex plugin add mobile-dev@mobile-dev
```

Open a new chat after installing. The package includes the built plugin and
bundled runtimes; no plugin build or `npm install` is needed.

Mobile Dev shows a banner when a newer release is ready to install. Click
**Update**, then fully quit and reopen Codex after it finishes.

You can also update an existing installation from the terminal:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace upgrade mobile-dev
```

Fully quit and reopen Codex after updating.

evidence.heading: Live devices beside your chat
evidence.text: Stream iOS simulators, Android emulators, and connected iPhones, iPads, and Android devices. Show iOS and Android together or use the fullscreen workspace.

evidence.heading: Device control, inspection and annotations
evidence.text: Select and boot simulators or emulators, interact with taps and drags, type on supported devices, and let Codex inspect accessibility elements and control your app through MCP tools. Select an element or screen region and leave instructions for Codex, with React Native component and source details when available.

evidence.heading: Native and JavaScript logs
evidence.text: Read iOS unified logs, Android logcat, and Metro console messages together. Follow the foreground app, search and filter logs, and send an error and its stack trace to chat.

evidence.heading: Live performance monitoring and improvements
evidence.text: Track app CPU and memory, expand individual thread charts, and view device-wide Display FPS on supported devices. Ask Codex to record an interaction, inspect interactive charts in chat, compare runs, and analyze selected ranges. Android recordings include display frame pacing and jank statistics.

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
The prebuilt plugin targets Codex desktop on an Apple Silicon Mac and uses
Codex's bundled Node runtime from its workspace dependency cache. Install the
tools for the platforms you use:

| Platform or feature | Requirements |
| --- | --- |
| iOS simulators | Xcode 26 or later with an installed simulator runtime. |
| Physical iPhones and iPads | Xcode 27 or later, a paired device with Developer Mode enabled, and USB or Wi-Fi connectivity. Screen mirroring requires HEVC WebCodecs support in the host. |
| Android | Android SDK platform-tools and emulator, and an AVD or a physical device with authorized USB or wireless debugging. Screen streaming requires H.264 WebCodecs support in the host. |
| Metro logs and React Native inspection | An existing local Metro server with a compatible app inspector target. |
| Physical iOS CPU and memory | iOS 17.4 or later, a running development-signed app with `get-task-allow`, a mounted developer disk image, and Xcode/LLDB detached. |
| Display FPS | Android 12 or later with FrameTimeline support, or a physical iOS device running iOS 17.4 or later. iOS simulators do not support Display FPS. |

Simulator tools use the full Xcode installation selected by `xcode-select` (or
`DEVELOPER_DIR`), including its Swift compatibility libraries. Custom Xcode names
and locations are supported. If Command Line Tools or an older Xcode is selected,
choose Xcode 26 or later in Xcode Settings > Locations > Command Line Tools.

The app project's own tools build, install, and launch your app. Mobile Dev supplies
its device panel, inspection, logs, and performance tools.

github_projects.name: modelsphere
github_projects.description: ModelSphere is an open-source LLM inference infrastructure designed to make production-grade model serving simple, efficient, and continuously optimized.
github_projects.description_zh: ModelSphere 是一个开源的 LLM 推理基础设施，旨在让生产级模型服务变得简单、高效且持续优化。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: ModelSphere is an open-source LLM inference infrastructure designed to make production-grade model serving simple, efficient, and continuously optimized.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Production-Grade Infrastructure for LLM Inference


  
  
  



  English | 简体中文

evidence.heading: Overview
evidence.text: ModelSphere is an open-source LLM inference platform designed to make production-grade model serving simple, efficient, and continuously optimized. It provides instant deployment across heterogeneous accelerators, stays ready for the latest models through a flexible inference architecture, and continuously improves serving performance based on real-world workloads.

evidence.heading: Highlights
evidence.text:
- **Intelligent Auto Scaling.** Dynamically adjusts inference replicas and compute resources based on real-time service demand, while prioritizing resources for high-priority models to improve overall GPU utilization.
- **Quality-Aware Dynamic Throttling.** Goes beyond traditional RPM/TPM limits by dynamically controlling traffic based on real-time service metrics such as TTFT and output speed, maintaining service quality under changing workloads.
- **Advanced Serving Architecture.** Supports advanced inference architectures such as Prefill/Decode disaggregation and a unified L3 KV cache pool, enabling efficient cache sharing and higher resource utilization across serving instances.
- **Performance-Tuned Day-0 Deployment.** Rapidly supports newly released models with production-ready, performance-tuned deployment configurations optimized for real-world serving workloads. Please refer to our [model catalog](https://modelsphere.github.io/model-catalog/) for more information.
- **Broad Heterogeneous Accelerator Support.** Provides a unified serving stack across NVIDIA GPUs, Huawei Ascend, Iluvatar CoreX, and dozens of other AI accelerators, together with mainstream inference frameworks such as SGLang and vLLM.
- **Seamless In-Flight Generation Recovery.** When a serving pod fails mid-generation, ModelSphere transfers the in-flight request to a healthy pod and resumes generation from the interruption point, without restarting the request or disrupting the client stream ([read more](https://github.com/modelsphere/continuation_gateway)).
- **Workload-Driven AutoTune (preview version).** Uses real production workloads to automatically explore better serving configurations during idle compute periods ([read more](https://github.com/modelsphere/llm-autotune)).

evidence.heading: **Prerequisites**
evidence.text:
1. a Kubernetes cluster, and `kubectl` pointing at it;
2. `helm`, `helmfile` and the `helm-diff` plugin.

evidence.heading: **Step 1: install the stack**
evidence.text:
```bash
# 1. the stack itself, one pass
cp environments/private.yaml.example environments/mycluster.yaml   # edit it,
#    then add it under `environments:` in helmfile.yaml.gotmpl -- a values file
#    nothing registers is a file helmfile never reads:
#      mycluster:
#        values:
#          - environments/default.yaml
#          - environments/mycluster.yaml
make helm-apply ENV=mycluster
```

evidence.heading: **Step 2: deploy a model**
evidence.text:
**Method 1: Using the command line**

```bash
helm repo add modelsphere https://modelsphere.github.io/helm-charts
helm upgrade --install qwen modelsphere/sglang -n llm-demo --create-namespace \
  -f <your values.yaml>       # models/examples/sglang-qwen.yaml is a worked example
```

The model is served through the routing layer, at `http://openresty.llm-route.svc:8080/<release>/v1/chat/completions` -- the release name from step 2 is the path prefix (`qwen` above), and it is how the router picks the model.

**Method 2: Using the GUI platform**

Alternatively, you can use the GUI console to deploy a model ([read more](https://github.com/modelsphere/console)).

evidence.heading: **Step 3: test the service**
evidence.text:
```bash
kubectl -n llm-route port-forward svc/openresty 8080:8080 &
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/qwen/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
       "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"max_tokens":32}'
```

Exposing that outside the cluster is a Gateway, an Ingress or a Service of your choosing -- [the walkthrough](docs/install.md#7-gateway-objects) ships Gateway API objects for it.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Agent skills and design systems from design.how. Build a design system from your app, use agents to ship UI, enforce it in CI.

evidence.heading: design.how
evidence.text: Skills and design systems for coding agents, from [design.how](https://design.how).

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
```bash
npx skills@latest add https://design.how
```

Or from GitHub, which installs the same six skills:

```bash
npx skills@latest add arla6ka/design.how
```

One skill, with `build-design-system` beside it for the shared glossary, taste file and scripts: `npx skills@latest add arla6ka/design.how --skill build-design-system --skill ui-review`. A design system's skill without its code: `npx skills@latest add arla6ka/design.how/systems/quartz`.

It works with any coding agent that reads skills. In Claude Code you can also run `/plugin marketplace add arla6ka/design.how`, then `/plugin install design-system-skills@design-how`. To install by hand, copy the folders in `skills/` into your agent's skills folder, such as `.agents/skills/`.

evidence.heading: Design systems
evidence.text: Each one installs with shadcn and brings its own skill, so your agent builds with its components and follows its rules.

evidence.heading: Glaze
evidence.text:
Glassy and compact, for AI products, with glass only on what you press.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://design.how/r/glaze/theme.json
```

[Components and source](systems/glaze) and [docs](https://design.how/systems/glaze).

evidence.heading: Lime
evidence.text:

```bash

```

[Components and source](systems/lime) and [docs](https://design.how/systems/lime).

evidence.heading: Quartz

[Components and source](systems/quartz) and [docs](https://design.how/systems/quartz).

evidence.heading: Skills
evidence.text:
These turn the UI your app already ships into a design system your agent can use, add a check that catches new drift, and move every screen onto it when you ask.

- [design-system-boss](skills/design-system-boss/SKILL.md). Start here. Say what's wrong in plain words, and it reads the repo, picks a playbook and runs the other skills in order. It ends with the system, one flow moved onto it and a CI check, then offers the full migration with its size.
- [build-design-system](skills/build-design-system/SKILL.md). Builds tokens, one canonical component per family, docs and checks from the app you have, and proves them on one real flow.
- [migrate-design-system](skills/migrate-design-system/SKILL.md). Moves every screen onto the system with parallel workers, each checked against its before screenshot. Start with audit mode, which writes only its own notes under `.design-system/` and commits nothing.
- [token-mapping](skills/token-mapping/SKILL.md). Maps hex codes and pixel values to your tokens by purpose, so an 8px radius never stands in for an 8px gap. It never edits.
- [component-docs](skills/component-docs/SKILL.md). Writes a component's docs from its code and two real uses in your product, with the rules right next to the examples.
- [ui-review](skills/ui-review/SKILL.md). Reviews a screen or flow, including the states a screenshot misses, and ranks what's actually broken.

Shared words are in [glossary.md](skills/build-design-system/references/glossary.md), and the default bans, widths and voice in [taste.md](skills/build-design-system/references/taste.md). Both ship inside `build-design-system`, which the other skills build on, so install it next to any skill you add on its own. Replace the taste file with your own.

evidence.heading: FieldCraft
evidence.text:
An open-source, clean-room CAE application in pure Rust: from a parametric SolidCraft part to a
verified finite element analysis, with tetrahedral and hexahedral meshing, its own implicit,
explicit, thermal and lattice Boltzmann solvers, and decks for Abaqus, Nastran and LS-DYNA. The
desktop app, the command line and AI agents (over MCP) drive the same commands.

**Status:** early but working end to end — open a part, mesh it, define the analysis, solve,
see the results — with a nonlinear implicit solver (large deformation, plasticity, rubber) now
in place. Hex meshing is the centre of gravity. Next: buckling and arc-length, contact, then
the wider material and multiphysics library. See [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).
**Want to help?** Pick an issue labelled
[good first issue](https://github.com/tangency-labs/fieldcraft/labels/good%20first%20issue) or
[help wanted](https://github.com/tangency-labs/fieldcraft/labels/help%20wanted) and read
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).



*Claude driving FieldCraft through its [MCP server](docs/mcp.md): one prompt, and it opens the part, meshes it, defines and solves the analysis, then checks the tip deflection against beam theory. Real session, waits shortened. [Full video](docs/media/claude-mcp.mp4).*



An AI agent drives FieldCraft over [MCP](docs/mcp.md), each stage captioned with the tool it
calls: it opens an I-beam, hex meshes it, defines the material, the clamp and a 1000 N tip load,
solves, and shows the von Mises stress and the deformed shape (tip deflection 0.176 mm; beam
theory with shear 0.177 mm).
[MP4](docs/media/ibeam-analysis.mp4) · regenerated by [tools/demo-video](tools/demo-video/README.md).

evidence.heading: Hex meshing a part that does not sweep
evidence.text:
A filleted L-bracket with a hole through each leg cannot be swept in one piece. Split into 30
cells in SolidCraft, FieldCraft meshes it all-hex as one conforming mesh — O-grids round the holes,
graded through the fillet — and its hex20 tip deflection matches a fine tet10 solution to 0.1 %.
The same part also meshes all-hex automatically with the octree mesher (`mesh.hex.octree`).

| Cells | Conforming hex mesh | Von Mises (clamp and load drawn) |
|---|---|---|
|  |  |  |

evidence.heading: What it does today
evidence.text:
- **Geometry in:** SolidCraft designs (`.solidcraft`) with persistent face, edge and body names,
  and face-tagged 3MF meshes; surface checks (weld, manifold, orientation, self-intersection).
- **Meshing:** constrained Delaunay tetrahedra (tet4, tet10) with exact predicates and a
  certified validity gate; Delaunay refinement, smoothing and sliver removal; structured hex by
  sweeping, revolving and mapping (hex8, hex20), and conforming multi-block hex across a part
  split into cells (`mesh.hex.blocks`); unstructured octree all-hex for any part
  (`mesh.hex.octree`); 2D quad and tri meshes; quality metrics per element and set.
- **Elements:** solids (tet4, tet10, wedge6, hex8 with incompatible modes, hex20 full and
  reduced, hybrid u–p for near-incompressible materials), plane stress, plane strain and
  axisymmetric, trusses, Timoshenko beams, MITC3/MITC4 shells, springs, dashpots and point masses.
- **Model:** sets bound to geometry names, so they survive remeshing; isotropic and orthotropic
  elasticity, J2 plasticity (isotropic and kinematic hardening, Johnson–Cook), Johnson–Cook
  damage, neo-Hookean, Mooney–Rivlin and Yeoh hyperelasticity, thermal properties; fixed, displacement,
  symmetry and temperature conditions; forces, moments, pressure, gravity, centrifugal and heat
  loads; reference points with kinematic and distributing couplings; undo, redo and a
  text-diffable `.fieldcraft` file.
- **Solvers:** linear static and frequency (supernodal Cholesky, block Lanczos); nonlinear static
  by Newton–Raphson with automatic increments — large deformation (total Lagrangian) on every
  solid element, follower pressure, finite- and small-strain plasticity sharing one return map
  with the explicit solver, rubber and thermal strain, with measured quadratic convergenc

evidence.heading: Examples
evidence.text: Ready-to-solve samples: open one from **File ▸ Samples** (or the start screen), or start the app with `fieldcraft --sample NAME`, and press **Solve**. Each opens and solves within half a minute and is checked against a closed form or a reference solution ([docs/examples.md](docs/examples.md)). Drop test (drop-test): an aluminium bracket dropped 2 m onto a tilted floor; explicit dynamics, the strike's stress waves Rubber seal (rubber-seal): a Mooney–Rivlin gasket ring squeezed 25 %; nonlinear static, large strain Heated bracket (heated-bracket): a clamped steel bracket heated at one end; steady heat and thermal stress Hex-meshed bracket (bracket-hex): the bracket split into 30 cells, meshed all-hex (hex20), von Mises Bicycle crank arm (crank-arm): an aluminium crank meshed structured all-hex (hex20) from a partitioned half and its mirror image, a rider's weight on the pedal; root bending within 0.3 % of M/Z No picture yet: the viewport does not draw flow results (M12).Flow past a bracket (flow-past): air past an L-bracket on the floor; lattice Boltzmann flow, the drag and the force on each face

github_projects.description: Local-first, open-source security gateway for AI coding agents. Enforce tool-call policies, detect secrets, and audit actions on-device.
github_projects.description_zh: 以本地优先的开源 AI 编码智能体安全网关。在设备上强制执行工具调用策略、检测密钥并审计操作。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Local-first, open-source security gateway for AI coding agents. Enforce tool-call policies, detect secrets, and audit actions on-device.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Security Badges
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
      
    
  



  Contributing ·
  Security


---

**SolonGate Agent Security** is SolonGate's open source, local first security
gateway for AI coding agents. It checks tool calls against your policies before
they run, with secret detection, rate limits and a local audit trail.

This repository is the Agent Security gateway. The rest of the portfolio is at
[solongate.com](https://solongate.com).

Everything stays on the machine. The policy is a file, the audit trail is a
file, and the guard makes no network calls. No account, no telemetry.

evidence.heading: Install and use
evidence.text:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/solongate/agent-security.git
cd agent-security
./scripts/install.sh
solongate
```

Then open a new terminal. Hooks load when a session starts, so an already open
one is not guarded yet.

evidence.heading: What it looks like when it fires
evidence.text:
A real Claude Code session: the agent reaches for a `.env`, the guard refuses it,
and the agent says so rather than quietly working around it.

evidence.heading: What it does
evidence.text:
| Layer | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Policy rules** | Allow or deny by path, command, filename or URL, scoped to READ, WRITE, EXECUTE or NETWORK. |
| **DLP** | 70 built in secret patterns plus your own, in four modes: `off`, `detect`, `redact`, `block`. |
| **Egress** | In block mode, refuses an upload whose file holds a secret, which pattern matching on the call alone cannot see. |
| **Rate limits** | A cap per minute, hour or day. |
| **The prompt** | A shim masks the outbound request body on Claude Code, which no tool call hook can reach. |
| **Tamper protection** | The guard's own state is unreachable from a tool call, and a policy in a repository cannot switch it off. |
| **Protected paths** | A path the OS itself refuses the agent, rather than a rule matched against the words in a tool call. |
| **Sandbox** | The agent's whole root is a new, minimal filesystem holding only the project; everything else is not refused, it is not there. |

evidence.heading: The CLI
evidence.text:
```
solongate              the TUI: policies, audit, settings
solongate policy       list, create and edit the policy
solongate dlp          secret detection
solongate ratelimit    the rate limit

solongate policy protect <path>   lock a path, and say what the lock is worth
solongate policy protect list     what is actually holding each path, read from disk

solongate sandbox list            the boxes this machine has, and their ids
solongate sandbox 001 claude      start the agent inside box 001
solongate sandbox --explain 001   everything that is in that box

solongate run -- claude           start an agent with protected paths out of reach

solongate audit        browse the audit trail
solongate watch        live tail tool calls
solongate trace        what the guard saw in this directory
solongate doctor       health check
solongate repair       restore the guard, hooks and settings
solongate update       pull the newest version and reinstall
solongate range        how far an update is allowed to move
solongate range short  every commit on the branch
solongate range long   tagged releases only, reliable (the default)
```

evidence.heading: Contributing
evidence.text:
Go 1.26.

There is one implementation of the guard, in Go. The one JavaScript file left
in the tree, `packages/hooks/opencode-plugin.mjs`, is a thin protocol shim
with no policy logic of its own: it spawns the Go binary and translates
OpenCode's plugin API to SolonGate's hook protocol, nothing more.

Two things check the decision path, and neither is a test suite. Ten
end-to-end cases drive the real guard binary through protected paths,
require-sandbox, agent scoping, and the `.last-deny` flag, asserting the exit
code the guard must produce; twenty-five more drive it through every layer
that refuses something. That means DLP in all four modes and on file content,
the rate limit, tamper protection, the four policy constraint kinds, whitelist
mode.
Alongside them, Go's own unit tests cover the decisions a pure function can
answer. What is left is what you ran it against by hand, and that is most of
it. [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) is the rest.

How it's put together: [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the actors and the
decision path a tool call takes, and [docs/INTERFACES.md](docs/INTERFACES.md) for
every external interface (CLI, hook, policy file, audit log).

Reporting a vulnerability: [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md), privately, never a public
issue. [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) applies everywhere.
