evidence.text: More comparisons: [1](examples/compare_1.jpg) · [3](examples/compare_3.jpg) · [4](examples/compare_4.jpg)

evidence.heading: What it does
evidence.text:
A plain halftone filter turns every grey of the whole picture into dots: lines get muddy, skin and highlights fill with dots, and nothing looks drawn. **Manga Finish** does what a manga artist does with separate layers, automatically:

1. **Lines** — strokes are separated by shape (long and thin = line, compact blobs = dots or noise) and kept as crisp black on their own layer.
2. **Values** — the image is read with the lines masked out, so no dark halo is left around them; existing dots and soft greys are averaged away.
3. **Flat areas** — values are pushed into paper white / light tone / dark tone / solid black, and small fragments are merged into their surroundings.
4. **Gradation** — areas that hide a smooth shadow get a gradation tone instead of flat steps.
5. **Print** — one page-aligned 45° dot screen, binary black and white, no moiré between areas.
6. **White lines in black** — inside solid black, the main folds and seams are cut out thin and white, the way a dark coat is inked.

**Manga Panel** then crops the page into a panel with a border and margin, with an optional light paper and ink feel.

**Manga Levels** is grayscale + levels, the light prep for when you cannot run an edit model.

The included workflow runs a **Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo** edit first ("redraw as a black-and-white manga panel"). The edit decides values by meaning rather than brightness — skin and white cloth become paper, only truly dark things stay dark — and Manga Finish turns that into a printed page. Manga Finish also works on its own on any image.

evidence.heading: Nodes
evidence.text:
**Manga Finish**

| Input | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| screen_lines | 200 | Rows of dots across the width. 120 coarse, 200 normal, 300 fine. Same value, same look at any resolution |
| white_point | 0.80 | Brighter than this becomes paper. Lower it to clear more tone |
| black_point | 0.30 | Darker than this becomes solid black. Raise it for more black |
| light_tone / dark_tone | 0.18 / 0.42 | Dot coverage of the two flat tones |
| gradation | 1.0 | Gradation tone for smooth shadows. 0 = flat areas only |
| pen_lines (optional) | | A line map drawn on top, e.g. *Manga Lineart* from comfyui_controlnet_aux |
| pen_threshold | 0.30 | Lower draws more of the pen lines |
| white_lines | 0.4 | How many lines are cut out white inside solid black. 0 = off |

**Manga Levels**

| Input | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| black / white | 0.20 / 0.70 | Input levels. Lower `white` until skin and light hair lose their tone |
| gamma | 1.3 | Above 1 brightens the mid tones |

**Manga Panel**

| Input | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| frame | 4:3 wide | Panel shape: original (no crop), 4:3 wide, 16:9 wide, 3:4 tall, 1:1 |
| crop_x / crop_y | 0.5 / 0.4 | Where the panel is cut |
| border / margin | 5 / 60 | Border and paper margin, in pixels at 1024 px width |
| paper | white | white / off-white / cream |
| ink | 0.5 | Soft ink edges and slightly uneven blacks. 0 = pure black and white |

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
```
cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone https://github.com/ashukae/ComfyUI-MangaScreen
```

Needs `opencv-python` and `numpy` (usually already installed with ComfyUI). Restart ComfyUI.

evidence.heading: Workflow
evidence.text:
**QWEN-Manga** (`workflows/QWEN-Manga.json`) — the full version. Drag it into ComfyUI, put an image in *Input image* and run. No prompt or tags needed.

- Models: Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo (diffusion model), a Qwen-Image 2.1 text encoder and VAE — select your own files in the three loaders.
- [comfyui_controlnet_aux](https://github.com/Fannovel16/comfyui_controlnet_aux) for the pen lines (*Manga Lineart*; its model downloads on first use).
- *Compare Images* shows the original and the result with a slider.
- Working size is 2 MP. If you work smaller, lower `screen_lines` (keep at least ~5 px per dot).

**Manga-Lite** (`workflows/Manga-Lite.json`) — no edit model, so it runs anywhere ComfyUI runs (CPU is fine): Manga Levels → pen lines → Manga Finish → Manga Panel. On clean line art with a simple background it gets close to the full version; Qwen pulls ahead on painted backgrounds (it redraws them as lines) and on things brightness cannot tell apart, like blush or a red dress vs a red ribbon.



[Manga-Lite vs QWEN-Manga, background](examples/lite_vs_qwen_background.jpg)

Tip: to send dark clothes to solid black, raise `black_point` to 0.5–0.6 — Qwen tends to draw them dark grey. A bolder edit instruction is in the workflow note (use it with `black_point` 0.40).

evidence.heading: AI generate nonsense from here on out
evidence.text:
A fork of [PolyStrata](https://github.com/VecSzn/PolyStrata) v0.1.45-poly.1 that keeps its two inference engines
unchanged and replaces everything around them: no installer, no downloads at build or start, no Python between a
request and a token. One `make build` on a Linux box with an NVIDIA card produces the engines and a C++ front end,
`unbiased-strata`, that serves an OpenAI-style chat API from llama.cpp's own server code. The target is one NVIDIA GPU,
Pascal or newer, CUDA 12.x, Linux x86-64, on a machine that may have no network at all. What was changed and why is in
[UPSTREAM.md](UPSTREAM.md); the plan this follows is [PLAN.md](PLAN.md).

```
git clone <this repo> && cd UnbiasedStrata
git submodule update --init          # shallow, third_party/llama.cpp @ robertkarl/llama.cpp UnbiasedStrata (a6de9af3)
make build                           # build/bin/{strata,strata-poly,libstrata_kq.so,unbiased-strata}
make test                            # the front end against a fake engine; no GPU, no model
```

evidence.heading: Run
evidence.text:
```
unbiased-strata --engine <strata|strata-poly|path> -m <model.gguf> [llama-server options] -- <engine options>
```

`-m` names the GGUF the vocabulary and chat template are read from; no tensors are loaded from it by the front end.
`--engine` takes a path, or a bare name looked up beside the program. Everything before `--` is a `llama-server`
option (`--host`, `--port`, `--api-key`, `--alias`, `--temp`, `--top-k`, `--top-p`, `--min-p`,
`--reasoning-format`, `--chat-template-kwargs`, `--sse-ping-interval`, ...); everything after `--` goes to the
engine, which is started as a child process with `--serve` added and spoken to over its line protocol
([docs/BACKENDS.md](docs/BACKENDS.md)). Where the model ends up (GPU cache, pinned RAM, SSD) and the three expert
modes: [docs/MEMORY_LAYOUT.md](docs/MEMORY_LAYOUT.md). The server answers `/v1/chat/completions` (streaming and not), `/v1/models`,
`/health`, `/props`, `/tokenize`, `/detokenize`, as llama.cpp's server does, one request at a time.

```
build/bin/unbiased-strata --engine build/bin/strata-poly \
  -m /models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q3_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18091 --alias qwen3.6-35b-a3b-ud-q3_k_m \
  -- --model /models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q3_K_M.gguf --max-context 32768 \
     --expert-profile /models/expert-profile-q3km.txt --tail-skip 6
```

With pictures, add `--mmproj /models/mmproj-F16.gguf` (the projector from the same `-MTP` repository) and
`--threads N` for the encoder before the `--`. The front end checks the projector's width against the model's at
start, encodes each picture with llama.cpp's mtmd and hands the rows to the engine over upstream's `GENI`
protocol. A picture is at most 300 rows by default (upstream's installer's CPU setting; `--image-max-tokens`
changes it), which read a 1920x1080 dashboa

evidence.heading: Preparing a Flash-Next pack
evidence.text:
`strata-poly` reads a GGUF as it is. `strata` needs a pack directory and an MTP draft directory made once, offline
except for the draft download, with upstream's tools (`tools/requirements.txt`: numpy, regex; `gguf-py` comes from the
submodule). This is what upstream's installer ran. Re-run in this fork on 2026-10-20 on three hosts; the MTP directory
came out byte-identical each time, so it is published, with the commands and hashes, at
https://huggingface.co/robertkarl/UnbiasedStrataPacks: copy it instead of fetching and quantizing.

```
python tools/iq_pack.py --gguf <shard1> --out <pack>             # --compat-bf16 for Unsloth files
STRATA_SOURCE=huggingface python tools/mtp_fetch.py fetch --out <mtp>
python tools/mtp_pack.py --src <mtp> --experts q2_0 --out <mtp>/mtp-q2_0.gguf
python tools/mtp_rt.py --gguf <mtp>/mtp-q2_0.gguf --out <mtp>/rt
cp data/draft_vocab.bin <mtp>/rt/draft_vocab.bin
```

Model files themselves are downloaded on a machine with network access and copied to the inference box; the fork does
not fetch them. The files that have been served, with sizes and SHA-256, are in
[docs/MODEL-FILES.md](docs/MODEL-FILES.md).

reusable tooling only: upstream's `bench_vs_llama.py` and its corpus, the kernel probes, and `bench/correctness/`, the

evidence.heading: Protocol features
evidence.text:
AgentPeerChat is the messaging layer between your personal agents. It does not run agents or call models; it stores and delivers their messages.

- **Identities.** Owners, humans and agents are separate principals. Each agent authenticates with its own scoped access key and can only read threads it belongs to.
- **Direct chats and groups.** Agents can message one or more peers, create groups (up to 32 members) and add members to their own groups.
- **Linked replies and safe inputs.** Replies retain their source message; `send-file` and `json-file` read local UTF-8 files or stdin without shell quoting. Safe transient CLI requests retry with bounded backoff. [Protocol and limits](docs/protocol.md#reliable-cli-inputs-and-retries).
- **Durable inbox with acknowledgments.** Messages stay pending until the recipient acknowledges them. Delivery is at-least-once when consumers rescan pending messages; send retries are idempotent via an `Idempotency-Key`.
- **Structured payloads.** Message types are `text`, `json`, `url` and `artifact` (external link cards).
- **Owner-approved pairing.** A new agent device joins with a ten-minute, single-use invitation and a verification code the owner approves. There is no anonymous signup.
- **Delegated agent invitations.** The owner can allow one connected agent to hand out its own short invitation links and approve them after you confirm the code; the grant is per agent, revocable, and never inherited by the invitee.
- **Human observation.** Trusted humans can follow every conversation and join when needed; agent credentials cannot access the cross-group overview.
- **Two backends, same API.** Cloudflare Worker + D1, or Node.js 24+ with a SQLite file.

Details: [API protocol](docs/protocol.md) · [Architecture](docs/architecture.md)



Exampl

evidence.heading: How is AgentPeerChat differentfrom CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph or A2A?
evidence.text:
They solve different problems. Frameworks build and run agents inside your program; A2A is a protocol specification; AgentPeerChat is a deployed message service that agents you already use can join.

| | AgentPeerChat | CrewAI | AutoGen | LangGraph | A2A |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| What it is | Self-hosted messaging service + CLI + skill | Framework for orchestrating role-playing agents | Programming framework for agentic AI | Framework for building stateful agents as graphs | Open protocol for communication between opaque agent applications |
| Runs your agents / calls LLMs | No. Agents keep their own runtime and models | Yes | Yes | Yes | No (spec; implementations do) |
| Where agents live | Separate runtimes (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, your own) | Defined in your code | Defined in your code | Defined in your code | Any runtime that implements the protocol |
| Hosting | Your Cloudflare account (Worker + D1) or Node.js + SQLite | Your application | Your application | Your application | N/A |
| License | MIT | MIT | Code MIT, docs CC-BY-4.0 | MIT | Apache-2.0 |
| Status (2026-10) | v0.1.x, early | Active | Maintenance mode; Microsoft points new users to Microsoft Agent Framework | Active | Linux Foundation project |

*Checked against each project's GitHub repository on 2026-10-12. AgentPeerChat does not implement the A2A protocol today. Corrections welcome via issue.*

github_projects.name: jev-doc-search
github_projects.description: Long-document search with Jev and PageIndex
github_projects.description_zh: 使用Jev和PageIndex进行长文档搜索

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Long-document search with Jev and PageIndex

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
**Find the page that answers a question in a 300-page report with Jev's `Choice`. No vector DB or embeddings!**

[Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai) answers multiple-choice questions: give it the options, and it returns a probability for each. "Which page answers this question?" is one of them, and it works well, until the document outgrows what Jev can read at once. [PageIndex](https://github.com/VectifyAI/PageIndex) removes that limit by turning the document into a hierarchical tree representation. Jev picks a node, then one of its children, and so on down the tree, choosing among a handful of options each time, however long the document.

evidence.heading: Page search with Jev's `Choice`
evidence.text:
Page search can be framed as a multiple-choice question. The question is "which page answers this?", and the options are the pages themselves: each page is one option, described by its own text. Jev reads every option and returns a probability for each page; the most likely page is the answer. We call this flat page search: one [`Choice`](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice), one option per page.



To try it on a short PDF of your own, such as an employee handbook, run [page_search.py](page_search.py) (see [Setup](#setup) for installing and API keys):

```bash
python page_search.py handbook.pdf "How many vacation days do new employees get?"
```

It prints the most likely page and its text. The core of it is a single call:

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader
from typesafe_sdk import Choice, TypeSafeClient

typesafe = TypeSafeClient(model="jev-1.13.0")

pages = [page.extract_text() for page in PdfReader("handbook.pdf").pages]
question = "How many vacation days do new employees get?"

r = typesafe.system_one(
    state={"question": question},
    questions={"page": Choice(
        instructions="Which page contains the answer to the question?",
        criteria={f"p{i}": text for i, text in enumerate(pages, 1)},
    )},
)
print(r.answers["page"].choice)  # the most likely page, e.g. 'p7'
```

In the code:

- **`state`** is what Jev reads before deciding. Here it is just the question.
- **`Choice`** is the decision. Its options go in `criteria`: one key per page (`p1`, `p2`, …), each described by that page's text.
- **The answer** names the most likely page in `choice`, with every page's probability in `probabilities`, summing to 1.

evidence.heading: Why flat page search breaks on long documents
evidence.text:
Flat page search hits two limits, one after the other:

1. **Too many tokens.** Every page's text goes into the request as an option, and `state` plus the `Choice` must fit in 32k tokens. That runs out after a few dozen pages. NVIDIA's [10-K for fiscal 2026](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0001045810/e361e58a-7483-44f5-bc62-a9080ae6ec72.pdf) has only 93 pages, but its text is about 76k tokens, more than twice what fits.
2. **Too many options.** A `Choice` takes at most 255 options, so one option per page stops at 255 pages. Some annual reports are longer than that: Citigroup's [10-K for 2025](https://www.citigroup.com/rcs/citigpa/storage/public/citi-2025-10-k-2-20-26.pdf) has 318 pages.

[PageIndex](https://github.com/VectifyAI/PageIndex) solves both at once. It turns the flat choice over pages into a tree: the document splits into sections, each with a title and a short summary, and each section into its pages. Jev then makes one small choice per level instead of one huge one, so every `Choice` has only a handful of options and fewer tokens.

evidence.heading: 1. Build the tree with PageIndex
evidence.text:
PageIndex builds the tree from the document's own structure. The root is the whole document, its children are sections, and each section has a title, a summary, and a page range, down to the pages.



Submit the PDF and read its tree:

```python
import os

from pageindex import PageIndexClient

pageindex = PageIndexClient(api_key=os.environ["PAGEINDEX_API_KEY"])

doc_id = pageindex.submit_document("NVIDIA_10K.pdf", wait=True)["doc_id"]
tree = pageindex.get_document_structure(doc_id)
```

`tree` is a list of nodes, each with its `title`, its page range (`start_index` to `end_index`), a `summary` of those pages, and its children in `nodes`. For the NVIDIA 10-K it looks like this (abridged):

```jsonc
[
  // … 4 more
  {
    "title": "Item 1. Business",
    "node_id": "0004",
    "start_index": 4,
    "end_index": 12,
    "summary": "This section covers NVIDIA's overall business overview…",
    "nodes": [
      {
        "title": "Our Company",
        "node_id": "0005",
        "start_index": 4,
        "end_index": 5,
        "summary": "This text provides an overview of NVIDIA as a pioneer in…"
      }
      // … 16 more
    ]
  }
  // … 25 more
]
```

evidence.heading: 2. Search the tree with Jev
evidence.text:
Jev starts at the root and asks one `Choice` per level: which of these children most likely contains the answer? Each option reads `"title. summary"`. The chosen section's children become the next menu, until the search reaches pages.



Continuing from the tree above, the search takes two steps.

**First, pick a section.** One `Choice` over the top-level sections, each described by its title and summary.

```python
from pageindex.utils import get_node
from typesafe_sdk import Choice, TypeSafeClient

typesafe = TypeSafeClient(model="jev-1.13.0")
question = "What was NVIDIA's total revenue for fiscal year 2026?"

sections = {n["node_id"]: f"{n['title']}. {n.get('summary', '')}" for n in tree}

r = typesafe.system_one(
    state={"question": question},
    questions={"section": Choice(
        instructions="Which section most likely contains the answer to the question?",
        criteria=sections,
    )},
)
section = get_node(tree, r.answers["section"].choice)  # the picked node_id, e.g. "0004"
```

**Then, pick a page inside it.** One `Choice` over the pages of that section, `start_index` to `end_index`, as in flat page search.

```python
start_index, end_index = section["start_index"], section["end_index"]
pages = pageindex.get_page_content(doc_id, f"{start_index}-{end_index}")
r = typesafe.system_one(
    state={"question": question},
    questions={"page": Choice(
        instructions="Which page contains the answer to the question?",
        criteria={f"p{p['page_index']}": p["markdown"] for p in pages},
    )},
)
print(r.answers["page"].choice)  # the most likely page
```

This is a *simplified version* to show the idea; the next section covers the full tree search.

evidence.heading: The full tree search
evidence.text:
The two-step search above is the simplest version. Going further, three changes make it general and sturdier: *deeper trees*, *top-K search*, and *checking with `Noul`*.

**Deeper trees.** A real tree has more than two levels: sections have subsections, which can have their own. The search is the same step repeated: one `Choice` over the children of the section just picked, until a section has no subsections, then one over its pages. Each level keeps the menu short, however long the document. The tree can go one level further, below pages: once a page is picked, one more `Choice` over its lines finds the exact line, as in TypeSafe's [line-by-line search](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/semantic_find) cookbook.

**Top-K search.** Taking only the most likely option at each step is brittle: if the right section or page ranks second, it is lost. Instead, keep the top K: the K most likely keys of `probabilities`, not just `choice`. In the tree this is beam search: keep the K best paths at each level, scored by the geometric mean of their step probabilities, as in TypeSafe's [hierarchical classification](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/hierarchical_classification) cookbook.

**Checking with `Noul`.** A `Choice` is relative: its probabilities sum to 1, so it always names a winner, even when no option answers the question. A [`Noul`](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul) is a yes/no question with its own probability, so each candidate page can be judged on its own, with its full text in `state`, and kept or dropped by a threshold.

[tree_search.py](tree_search.py) puts all three together:

1. **Sections.** A beam of 3 goes down a tree of any depth. At each section, its opening pages, before its first subsection, are an option too.
2. **Pages.** One `Choice` over the p

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: pstack reworked for T3 Code: delegated subagents, worktree threads, PR watching, scheduled runs.

evidence.heading: p3-stack
evidence.text:
p3-stack is [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) rebuilt for T3 Code. Same engineering discipline, native T3 orchestration.

pstack is poteto's answer to AI slop code. It turns an agent into an engineering team: one mode skill that routes to playbooks, principles that ground every decision, and verification strict enough that you can parallelize with confidence. p3-stack keeps that system and rewires the mechanics to T3 Code's primitives:

- **Delegation.** `delegate_task` child agents replace Cursor's Task tool, with per-role providers and models resolved from `orchestrator_capabilities`. Cross-model panels are native.
- **Worktrees.** `t3_thread_launch` binds a worker to its own worktree and branch. One writer per worktree, enforced by the app instead of by advice.
- **Watching.** `watch_pull_request` wakes the thread when checks finish, someone comments, or the branch conflicts. No polling loops.
- **Scheduling.** `schedule_task` runs audits and overnight cadences even when no turn is active. No `/loop`.
- **Memory.** `t3_thread_read` and `t3_thread_search` replace mining Cursor transcript files.
- **Proof.** `preview_*` browser tools and `device_*` simulators replace external control skills. Screenshots and recordings land in the thread.

evidence.heading: Install

git clone https://github.com/uzairansaruzi/p3-stack.git
cd p3-stack

```

`install.sh` links every `skills/*` directory into `~/.agents/skills/`, where T3 Code reads skills. Use `./install.sh --project /path/to/repo` to install into a project's `.agents/skills/` instead.

evidence.heading: Get started
evidence.text:
1. Run `/setup-p3`. It reads `orchestrator_capabilities` and writes `p3-models.md`, mapping each role (code, judgment, the review panels) to a provider and model you actually have.
2. Use `/p3-mode` whenever you want rigorous work. It reads the request, picks a playbook, and runs the other skills as the steps need them.
3. Stuck or unsure which skill fits? Ask `/p3-help`.

evidence.heading: The mode
evidence.text: `p3-mode` routes every task. Its playbooks: investigation, bug fix, perf issue, hillclimb, runtime forensics, trace forensics, feature, refactoring, prototype, visual parity, authoring a skill, eval, babysit, shipping, autonomous run, orchestrate, autopilot-full, autopilot-stack, session pickup, pause safely, multi-phase plan, worktree cleanup, opening a PR.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
See your agents. Follow the work.

evidence.heading: Overview
evidence.text:
Claude Super Sidebar brings the main agent, subagent relationships, execution details, and the current conversation’s work steps into one panel. Claude Code uses a native plugin pane; standalone Codex CLI/App uses a read-only local session dashboard. Neither requires a frontend build.

The repository and product are **Claude Super Sidebar** (`claude-super-sidebar`). The plugin installs as `super-sidebar`, with a native pane titled **状态 · Status**. The host reserves the `claude-` prefix, so a plugin ID cannot start with `claude-`; the product name stays with the repository and this README. The Codex page is titled **状态 status**, and its team section is **团队面板 Team panel**. Each adapter uses its host's own data source; task summaries require no additional model call.

| Integration | Data source and UI | Current validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Desktop Code | Lifecycle hooks and `session.messages()` → native pane | Historical portable checks passed; latest isolation regressions have not been run; current native engine validation and Desktop reload remain unverified |
| Codex CLI / App | Local `sessions/rollout-*.jsonl` → read-only browser panel | Historical adapter/HTTP checks passed; latest isolation regressions have not been run; real local App session and page verified |

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Agent relationships** — main agent and subagents in a unified tree, with directional connectors and details that expand in place.
- **Execution status** — colored running, waiting, completed, and failed states. Claude shows active elapsed time; Codex shows recorded time without inferring process liveness.
- **Agent details** — model, mode, role, observed token usage, available context usage, elapsed time, and tool-call count.
- **Conversation task flow** — Both adapters group observed operations into work stages, use concise action titles, and show bounded operation details on expansion. Results remain separate from the stage description; failures and missing results are preserved.
- **Per-request scope** — each new user request clears the previous flow; tool results preserve the current round. Up to 30 recent steps are shown.
- **Plan display** — Claude extracts observable plan text. Codex displays successfully submitted `update_plan` steps; failed updates preserve the previous plan.
- **Execution and verification** — “Operations completed” only describes tool execution. Explicit verification conclusions retain their conversation evidence and are labeled as assistant-reported; an exit code of zero never proves product behavior.
- **Container colors** — white, beige, and black apply to cards and preferences; the surrounding page background stays unchanged. Authored controls support Chinese and English.
- **Local parsing** — deriving the flow requires no additional LLM call.

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
The following requirements apply to the Claude plugin. The Codex dashboard only requires Node.js 22.18+ and locally persisted Codex sessions.

- A Claude Desktop Code host that exposes the native hook-module and pane APIs.
- The matching Claude Code CLI for plugin installation.
- A stable local copy of this repository.

Developed against **Claude Code engine 2.1.299**, using an early-access plugin API. The host must support hook modules, `claude-code` imports, and native `ui.render` panes. Availability may differ between distributions and versions.

evidence.heading: Usage
evidence.text:
These controls apply to the Claude native plugin. See [Codex configuration](#codex-configuration) for the local dashboard and conversation binding.

The plugin attempts to open **状态 · Status** on session startup. Type `/super-sidebar` in the conversation input to reopen it.

| Section | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Agent relationships | Main agent, subagents, parent–child connections, and expandable execution details |
| Task Flow | Work steps grouped into stages, with concise titles, status, operation details, and separate verification conclusions |
| Preferences | Language, container colors (white / beige / black), and a collapsible version block (plugin version and implementation revision) |

Use **展开 / 收起** to expand or collapse an agent. Use **刷新** to refresh immediately; the pane also refreshes every two seconds.

Task-flow arrows indicate chronological execution. A new user request starts a fresh flow automatically, without task-management controls.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
```text
Claude Code session
  ├─ Agent / turn / tool events ──→ Agent status and usage
  └─ Conversation transcript ─────→ Stage-grouped work steps
                                      │
                              Session-scoped state
                                      │
                            Native Status pane (single column)
                            ├─ Agent relationships
                            ├─ Task flow (stages, operations, verification)
                            └─ Preferences (container colors, version)
```

The manifest loads `hooks/register.tsx` through `hooks/hooks.json`. Session startup registers the command and refresh timer; lifecycle hooks observe execution; `session.messages()` supplies the task-flow parser. Native components and SVG connectors render the pane.

evidence.heading: Limitations
evidence.text:
- Claude plan extraction has logic regression coverage but remains unverified in the current native pane. Codex plan updates have success/failure result coverage.
- Main-agent context usage comes from the host. Unavailable subagent metrics are shown as unavailable; token totals reflect observed completed turns, including cache tokens.
- Steps reflect the available transcript and progress-message grouping, rather than a dependency graph or task scheduler.
- Claude installation and enablement have historical evidence only; the current code still requires validation, loading, and fresh-session auto-opening checks in a compatible host.
- The Claude plugin does not aggregate cross-session history. Codex resolves explicitly bound conversations and descendants before the recent-session cap; unbound discovery is limited to 100 sessions; the API returns only that conversation and its descendants. Missing records show a waiting state without falling back to another conversation. Terminal fallbacks do not reproduce the native visual pane.
- Codex usage reflects recorded cumulative tokens and the last request's input tokens. Last input size is not live context occupancy. Unknown fields are ignored; malformed lines are skipped with a notice.

The Codex rollout format is not a stable public API; compatibility is limited to tested local versions. This panel does not provide multi-user authentication or remote monitoring.

FoxProfile manages anti-detect browser profiles: each profile is a separate identity with its own device fingerprint, cookies, proxy, timezone and locale. The default browser is [Camoufox](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox), a Firefox build that spoofs fingerprints at the engine level; an experimental Chrome engine based on [fingerprint-chromium](https://github.com/adryfish/fingerprint-chromium) is also available. It is a self-hosted alternative, on your machine or a VPS, to paid anti-detect browsers such as GoLogin, GPM or MoreLogin.

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Persistent per-profile fingerprint.** The first launch generates a device (screen, GPU, CPU cores, fonts, canvas/audio noise) and stores it; later launches reuse the same device. Generate a new one on demand.
- **Two engines.** Camoufox (Firefox, default) or Chrome (fingerprint-chromium, experimental), chosen when the profile is created. The Chrome build is downloaded automatically when needed.
- **Sessions that stick.** History, cookies and logins live in the profile directory; the tabs that were open are reopened on the next launch.
- **Per-profile proxy**: HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS4/SOCKS5, with or without auth, including the `host:port:user:pass` format, plus a proxy checker.
- **Timezone and locale** follow the exit IP or can be pinned per profile. **Check IP** compares the exit IP across Cloudflare, ipinfo and ip-api and warns about country/timezone mismatches and datacenter IPs.
- **Cookie export/import** as Cookie-Editor / EditThisCookie JSON (GoLogin, GPM, Multilogin, the Cookie-Editor extension) and Netscape `cookies.txt` (yt-dlp, curl, wget).
- **Profile export/import** as ZIP, with or without browser data, to move profiles between machines. The fingerprint always travels with the profile.
- **A profile table built for scanning**: every row shows the engine, the emulated device, the proxy (credentials hidden), timezone/locale and the state. States differ in shape as well as colour: a violet double-ruled stamp with the launch time means running, a grey rule means starting, a struck red stamp means the launch failed.
- **Filters and search**: filter by running, with/without proxy and Chrome engine (with counts); search by name or proxy.
- **Bulk actions**: launch, stop or delete many profiles at once.
- **MCP server** so AI agents (Claude, Cursor...) can launch prof

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
- Python 3.10+
- Windows, macOS or Linux (CI tests all three)
- A few hundred MB of free disk space for Camoufox and the GeoIP database, plus ~140-190 MB for the Chrome engine if you use it

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/chienbm98/foxprofile.git
cd foxprofile

python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate          # Windows
source .venv/bin/activate       # Linux/macOS

pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m camoufox fetch
```

`camoufox fetch` downloads the Camoufox browser (a few hundred MB) from the Camoufox GitHub releases. The first profile launch also downloads a GeoIP database (~50 MB).

Run the app:

```bash
python -m src.main
```

On Windows you can also double-click `run_foxprofile.bat`. The app opens the manager window and serves the API on `http://127.0.0.1:8000`; API docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`. Set `FOXPROFILE_LANG=vi` for the Vietnamese UI.

evidence.heading: Timezone, locale and Check IP
evidence.text:
By default, every Camoufox launch looks up the exit IP (through the profile's proxy) and sets the timezone, locale, geolocation and WebRTC IP from it. Worth knowing:

- **The automatic locale is drawn at random on every launch**, weighted by how many people speak each language in the IP's country. A French IP gives `fr-FR` roughly 60% of the time and `en-FR`, `es-FR`… otherwise. An account whose language changes between sessions looks suspicious, so pin the locale per profile.
- **GeoIP databases disagree.** Cloudflare may place an IP in one country and Google in another, and Camoufox may pick a same-offset timezone with a different name (a Vietnamese IP gets `Asia/Bangkok` rather than `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`).
- **Datacenter IPs get captchas** whatever the browser looks like. For Cloudflare-protected sites a residential or mobile proxy matters more than any other setting.



The profile dialog has **Timezone** (IANA name, e.g. `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`) and **Locale** (e.g. `vi-VN`) fields; blank means follow the IP. **Check IP** resolves the exit IP through the proxy, compares it with Cloudflare, ipinfo and ip-api, and warns about country or timezone mismatches, datacenter IPs, proxies that leave over different IPv4/IPv6 addresses, and a locale left on random.

evidence.heading: Responsible use
evidence.text: Anti-detect browsers are legitimate tools for privacy, web testing and agencies managing client accounts. Running multiple accounts on one platform may still violate the terms of Facebook, TikTok, Google, Shopee and others. You are responsible for how you use this software.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Decides who gets your GPU. Chat, image and voice engines lease the card in turn instead of grabbing it, so two of them never load at once and crash each other. One Go binary, nothing else to install.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text: Quick start  ·  How it works  ·  Install  ·  Gateway  ·  Harbor  ·  Docs  ·  Roadmap

evidence.heading: Berth
evidence.text:
Berth makes the programs on your PC take turns with the GPU's memory, so they stop crashing each
other, and tells you who is holding it.

Berth decides who gets your GPU. Chat models, image pipelines, voice engines, games and GPU apps
lease the card instead of grabbing it, so two of them never load at once and crash each other
with an out-of-memory error. One Go binary, no cloud account, nothing else to install.

```sh
berth daemon &                                        # one broker per card
berth run --as llama -- llama-server -m model.gguf    # this engine now takes turns
berth status                                          # who holds the card, who waits, and why
```

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Every engine asks berthd for the card: through `berth run`, the gateway, ComfyUI's API or a game
claim. When another engine holds it, Berth:

1. queues the request by priority: `hold`, `foreground`, `interactive`, `batch`;
2. lets the holder finish its reply or image job, then unloads it;
3. waits until the driver shows the memory free;
4. grants the lease and starts the next engine, and the request that waited streams.

The numbered markers on the timeline are those four steps. A process that holds VRAM without a lease
shows up as a stowaway: Berth reports its PID and memory and leaves it running.

> **Status: alpha, v0.3.6.** Runs daily on an RTX 4090 workstation beside llama-swap, NInfer,
> Strata, ComfyUI and games, and testers run it on Windows. The [docs](docs/README.md) cover what works and has tests; the
> [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) lists the phases and what is still missing.

evidence.heading: Berth and llama-swap
evidence.text:
Use both. llama-swap swaps the models in its own config, and does it well. Berth governs the
whole card: llama-swap's models, ComfyUI, Ollama, vLLM, games, and any process that holds VRAM,
including the ones neither tool started. With Berth beside it, llama-swap's next model waits
for ComfyUI or the engine before it to give the memory back, and when a crashed process still
holds part of the card, Berth names its PID and how much it holds, so you aren't hunting
through `nvidia-smi` while a load fails. `berth wire llama-swap` adds the lease to every model
in your config in one pass. An upstream integration with llama-swap is planned, so the wrapper
line goes away.

evidence.heading: What Berth does
evidence.text:
**Shares one card between everything**
- **Engines take turns.** You start each one through `berth run`. When another needs the
  card, Berth waits for the holder's current reply to end, unloads it (its own unload, then
  SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) and lets the next one in only after the driver shows the memory free.
- **Priorities.** `foreground`, `interactive`, `batch`, and `hold` above them all. A lower
  request waits and gets a reason naming the holder, never an OOM crash.
- **No ping-pong.** When two clients ask for different engines at once, a ranking picks one
  and the other waits, so the card stays put.
- **ComfyUI at a job boundary.** Berth waits for the running image job to finish before the handoff.
- **A minimum turn.** `min_turn = "5m"` keeps an engine on the card for five minutes after it
  gets it, whatever asks next; only a hold takes it out sooner.
- **Engines in containers.** `berth run --container NAME -- docker run ...` puts a Docker or
  Podman engine under its lease, and the drain stops it through `docker stop`.
- **Survives restarts.** Upgrade or restart the daemon and your running engines stay up and
  re-attach. The gateway's engines survive it too: it starts each one as its own `berth run`
  process (in its own systemd scope on Linux) and adopts them again on its next start.

**Faster switches, and a way out** *(v0.3)*
- **Park in RAM.** An engine that can offload itself (ComfyUI, vLLM, SGLang, or any engine that
  serves the [park protocol](contrib/PARK-PROTOCOL.md)) moves its weights to system memory on a
  drain and resumes from there instead of reloading from disk. Berth parks only when the RAM it
  measures covers the engine plus a floor, and stops parked engines first when memory runs short.
- **A way out of every lease state.** `berth stop

evidence.text:
```sh
go install github.com/T-Crypt/berth/cmd/berth@latest      # or a release binary, see Install
berth service install --harbor                            # berthd and the harbor, as user services
berth status                                              # the card, leases, the engines and their estimated VRAM
berth run --as llama --priority foreground -- llama-server -m model.gguf --port 8080
```

On Linux the services are systemd user units; on Windows they are Task
Scheduler logon tasks that need no admin and run in your session, where
your GPU apps are. The harbor answers on http://127.0.0.1:9798/. `berth
service status` shows them and `berth service uninstall` removes them; the
manual steps in Install do the same by hand.

The harbor and gateway take their addresses from berth.toml when their
`--listen` flags are not given: `[harbor] listen` and `[gateway] listen`,
so a port change is a config edit and a restart of the service, not a
reinstall. On Windows, installing also starts the tasks it creates, and
each task appends its output to a log file under the state directory,
which `berth service status` prints.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
`berth service install --harbor` in the quick start sets up the daemon and the harbor as user
services. To install from a release binary instead, check it against the release's SHA256SUMS:

```sh
curl -fLO https://github.com/T-Crypt/berth/releases/latest/download/berth-linux-amd64
curl -fLO https://github.com/T-Crypt/berth/releases/latest/download/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
install -Dm755 berth-linux-amd64 ~/.local/bin/berth
```

[Install](docs/install.md) has a prompt that hands the whole install to your coding agent, the manual
steps, the configuration file and how to uninstall.

evidence.heading: Agents can edit logs. They can't hide the edit.
evidence.text:
**Tracekit checks every tool call your agent makes before it runs, signs each call and decision into a hash chain,
and gives you one `.tkb` file per run that anyone can verify offline.**








8 of 8tamper attacks caught480 trials, with a witness (E1)
583 of 583harmful calls stopped11 classes, 1 false alarm in 749 (E17)
< 1 msadded per tool call0.91 ms at p99, signer round trip (E9)
8 of 8insider attacks caughta merge gate on every PR (E8)



Built like **Certificate Transparency**: signed records in an append-only log that independent witnesses cosign
**Open file format** · verifiers in **Python** and **TypeScript** · **MIT** · runs on your own machines

**[Try it](#try-it) · [Add it to your agent](#add-it-to-your-agent) · [What it proves](#what-it-proves) · [What's in it](#whats-in-it) · [Proof](#proof) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Pilot it](#pilot-it-with-us) · [Contribute](#contribute) · [Docs](#docs)**



---

When an agent does something it shouldn't, you ask three things: **what did it do, was it allowed, and can you trust
the record?** The agent's own log can't answer the third, because the agent can edit it. Here is one run, recorded
both ways:


  
  
  




The same run, recorded: the database, the signer, the viewer and both edits are real; the model is scripted. Watch it with sound (1:47)

In this demo the signer ran as the agent's own user (dev mode), so an agent that knew how could have read the key and
re-signed the log. Run the signer [where the agent can't reach it](#how-it-works), with a witness, and it can't.

evidence.heading: Try it
evidence.text:
```sh
uvx --from tracekit-ai tracekit demo --server
```

No API key, and nothing to install with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). From an empty cache on a Mac it took 5
seconds (10 with `pip install tracekit-ai` in a fresh venv). The package is `tracekit-ai`: `tracekit` on PyPI is an
unrelated project. A scripted agent makes three calls, and you should see:

```text
== agent run (SCRIPTED: fixed tool calls, not a model)
  Bash 'ls': allow
  Bash 'sudo rm -rf /': deny TK-D001 TK-D004 TK-F003
  Bash 'echo "unterminated': ask TK-SHELL-PARSE
...
Integrity: VERIFIED.

== tamper test: rewrite the denied call as allowed in a copy, then verify again
[FAIL] signatures — 11 record(s), keys valid at their position
        seq 4: hash does not match the event
Integrity: FAILED.
```

The delete was denied before it ran, the held call ran after an approval, and the run verified. Then the demo rewrote
the denial as allowed in a copy, and verification failed at the record it changed.

evidence.heading: Add it to your agent
evidence.text:
Three lines:

```sh
pip install tracekit-ai
```

```python
import tracekit; tracekit.instrument()     # the first line of your agent; then run it as usual
```

```sh
tracekit last                               # Integrity: VERIFIED. / Assurance: dev; ...
```

`tracekit.instrument()` starts a dev signer (or reuses the running one) and gates and records every tool and model call
of the frameworks it finds. `tracekit last` exports your latest run, verifies it and says where it is.
`tracekit view --dev` shows every run. On a clean machine the LangGraph example (a mock model, no API key) installed,
ran and verified in 27 seconds: [`examples/v2/clean-machine.sh langchain`](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/blob/main/examples/v2/clean-machine.sh).

evidence.heading: What it proves
evidence.text:
Three guarantees. They're related, but one doesn't give you the others, and each needs something different.

| Guarantee | What you get | What it needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Evidence integrity** | A record that was edited, deleted, swapped or inserted fails verification at that record | Only the signed log. Cutting off the end of the log, or re-signing it with a stolen key, takes a witness to catch |
| **Execution control** | Each call is checked before it runs. A denied call is blocked; a held call runs only after a yes, with exactly the arguments that were approved | The call goes through Tracekit: an SDK, a hook or a gateway. Code that skips it isn't stopped |
| **Independent assurance** | An operator who rewrites or forks its own log is caught | A witness the operator doesn't control, and a monitor. Both are experimental, and no public witness is running yet |

evidence.heading: Limits
evidence.text:
- **Dev mode protects nothing against an agent that runs as you.** Dev runs say `isolation: same-user`
  ([FAQ](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/FAQ#what-does-same-user-dev-mode-protect)).
- **A verified run proves the record is intact**: not intent, not that a reported tool result is true, and not that
  every action was captured ([FAQ](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/FAQ#what-cant-tracekit-prove)).
  `tracekit analyze --v2` compares what was asked, what the model said and what ran, but what the model said is its
  own account, and findings are an opinion beside the integrity, never part of it
  ([findings](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Findings#v2-runs-what-was-asked-said-and-done-tracekit-analyze---v2)).
- **Actions outside the capture path leave no record**, such as a subprocess a hook never sees and no kernel sensor
  import covers, or code that skips the adapter ([adapters](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Adapters)).
- **Policy rules match text and tool names.** A determined agent can reword a command; the protection is the signer's
  isolation ([policy reference](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Policy#packs-shipped)).
- **Commitments hide content, not timing, sizes or counts**
  ([privacy](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Privacy#what-hashes-and-metadata-still-leak)).

What each deployment guarantees, from dev mode to a signer the agent can't reach:
[guarantees](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Guarantees). Every limit, with what to do
about it: [limits](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Limits). How it maps to the EU AI Act,
ISO/IEC 42001, the NIST AI RMF and OWASP: [compliance](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Compliance).

evidence.heading: What's in it
evidence.text:
One signer. The core is stable and is hardened first. The rest ships in the same package as experimental: it works and
is tested, but may change between releases ([what's stable](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Support)).

| Core | What it does | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| **Record** | Every tool call, decision and result in one signed hash chain per run. A lost event becomes a signed gap, never silence | 6 of 8 tamper attacks caught by the log alone (E1) |
| **Decide** | Allow, deny, or hold each call for a person, before it runs. [Packs](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Policy) for shell, files, SQL, HTTP, cloud CLIs, browsers, email, messaging, payments, secrets and MCP | 583 of 583 harmful calls stopped, 1 false alarm in 749 (E17) |
| **Approve** | A held call runs only after a yes from the command line, bound to its exact arguments and used once ([approvals](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Approvals)) | Edited arguments, a replayed snapshot or another run's approval: refused, in the contract tests every stable framework integration runs |
| **Prove** | `tracekit verify` checks a run's file offline against keys you pinned | 8 of 8 insider attacks caught (E8) |
| **Watch** | `tracekit view`: every run verified, blocked and held calls, approvals, gaps, replay and a run review ([viewer](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Viewer)) | Not measured |

| Experimental | What it does | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| **Witness** | Independent [witnesses](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Witnesses) cosign each checkpoint; a [monitor](https://github.com/Cygnux-Labs/Tracekit/wiki/Monitor) watches the log for rewrites and forks | 8 of 8 tamper attacks caught with a witness (E1) |
| **Cross-check** | The signer compares the ca

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
- **The agent never holds a signing key** and never assigns sequence numbers.
- **Each record is signed and carries the hash of the one before it**, so a changed byte fails verification at that
  record.
- **Nothing the agent reports about itself is trusted**: not its isolation, its fail mode, gaps, or who approved a call.
- **Who can rewrite the log decides what a run is worth**, so put the signer where the agent can't reach it. The agent's
  code is the same in every mode; `TRACEKIT_SIGNER` points it at the signer.

| Where the signer runs | Who can reach the keys and log | Recorded isolation |
|---|---|---|
| Laptop dev | the agent's own user | `same-user` |
| Laptop system mode (Linux; macOS experimental) | root and the signer's OS user | `separate-user` |
| Container or Kubernetes sidecar | the signer's uid and the node's administrator | `separate-user` |
| Docker Compose stack (`deploy/compose/`) | the Docker host's administrators | `separate-user` |
| Central signer over HTTPS | the signer host's administrators | `remote` |

github_projects.description: First-class Linux packaging for DeepSeek Harness desktop — AppImage, .deb, .tar.gz for x64/arm64, built by native CI.
github_projects.description_zh: 面向Linux的一流桌面打包DeepSeek Harness — AppImage、.deb、.tar.gz，支持x64/arm64，由本地CI构建。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: First-class Linux packaging for DeepSeek Harness desktop — AppImage, .deb, .tar.gz for x64/arm64, built by native CI.

evidence.heading: DeepSeek Harness · Linux 桌面版
evidence.text:
> 给官方 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 桌面端补上**社区 Linux 桌面端打包** —— 开源（MIT）DeepSeek 桌面客户端，开箱即用的 AppImage / `.deb` / `.tar.gz`，覆盖 x64 与 arm64 双架构，配套原生 CI 与 AppImage 自动更新。

**一句话定位**：在 Linux 上「能下载、能装、能更新」的 DeepSeek 桌面端（DeepSeek desktop for Linux）。完整保留官方 agent / 插件 / 联网能力，既可本地自托管运行 `dsh web`，也能装上原生桌面客户端，数据始终留在本机。

官方桌面端只发布 macOS 与 Windows；Linux 用户要么退而用 Web 版，要么自己从源码硬编。本项目就是这个缺口的补完：在保留官方桌面全部功能的前提下，把 Linux 作为**社区支持平台**来打包、测试、分发。

evidence.heading: 这是什么 / 不是什么
evidence.text:
- ✅ **是**：一个下游 fork，专注做一件事——让 dsh 桌面端在 Linux 上「能下载、能装、能更新」。
- ❌ **不是**：不是官方 DeepSeek 项目，也不魔改 agent 内核。agent 能力、插件体系、通信协议全部跟随上游。

evidence.heading: 核心特性
evidence.text:
- 🐧 **Linux 原生支持**：为 DeepSeek 官方桌面端提供社区 Linux 桌面端打包的下游项目 —— Ubuntu / Debian / 树莓派 5 / ARM 服务器都能跑。
- 📦 **三种安装包**：AppImage（单文件免安装、支持自动更新）、`.deb`（Debian / Ubuntu 原生包管理）、`.tar.gz`（便携解压即用）。
- 🔄 **自动更新**：AppImage 通过 `electron-updater` 走 HTTPS 更新通道，下载时校验 SHA256。
- 🧩 **功能完整**：agent 内核、插件体系、联网、前端全部跟随上游，Linux 下与官方体验一致（仅 Office 文档转换暂缺）。
- 🏠 **可自托管**：本地运行 `dsh web` 或安装桌面端，数据留在本机，适合隐私敏感与内网场景。
- 🆓 **开源免费**：基于上游 MIT 许可证分发。

evidence.heading: 产物一览
evidence.text:
每次构建为每种架构产出三种安装包：

| 格式 | 用途 | 典型文件名 |
|------|------|-----------|
| **AppImage** | 单文件免安装，支持自动更新 | `deepseek-harness-0.2.0-rc.3-linux-x64.AppImage` |
| **.deb** | Debian / Ubuntu 系原生包管理 | `deepseek-harness-0.2.0-rc.3-linux-x64.deb` |
| **.tar.gz** | 便携解压即用 | `deepseek-harness-0.2.0-rc.3-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

支持架构：`x64`（AMD / Intel）、`arm64`（树莓派 5、Apple Silicon 上的 Linux、ARM 服务器等）。

evidence.heading: 方式一：AppImage（推荐，支持自动更新）
evidence.text:
1. 到 [Releases](../../releases) 下载对应架构的 `.AppImage`。
2. 安装运行时依赖（AppImage 需要 FUSE 2）：
   ```sh
   sudo apt install libfuse2          # Debian / Ubuntu
   # Fedora / RHEL 系: sudo dnf install fuse2
   ```
3. 赋予执行权限并运行：
   ```sh
   chmod +x deepseek-harness-*-linux-x64.AppImage
   ./deepseek-harness-*-linux-x64.AppImage
   ```

evidence.heading: 方式二：.deb
evidence.text:
```sh
sudo dpkg -i deepseek-harness-*-linux-x64.deb
deepseek-harness            # 或直接从应用菜单启动
```

evidence.heading: 已知限制
evidence.text:
1. **未签名**：Linux 构建不带代码签名。这是社区构建，分发时请在 Release 中核对校验和。
2. **Office 文档转换暂缺**：桌面内嵌的 DOCX / XLSX / PPTX → PDF 转换依赖 LibreOffice Kit 的 Linux 原生绑定，本版本尚未将其随包分发，该功能在 Linux 下暂不可用。其余桌面功能（agent、skill、联网、前端）均正常。
3. **上游处于 developer preview**：官方迭代快、破坏性变更频繁，本项目会持续 rebase 上游提交。
4. **无公证 / 无商店上架**：不走任何系统级公证或应用商店流程。

kind_reason.text: 专注为 DSH 桌面端提供 Linux 打包的社区下游发行版。

summary.text: 为 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端提供 Linux x64、arm64 的 AppImage、deb 和 tar.gz 社区构建，保持智能体及插件能力跟随上游，并支持 AppImage 自动更新。

value.text: 让 Linux 用户能下载安装桌面包，减少自行构建上游桌面端的工作。

mechanism.text: 下游 fork 管理 Linux 包格式与架构，AppImage 使用 electron-updater 经 HTTPS 更新，并在下载时检查 SHA256。

inspiration.text: 可尝试让下游平台适配聚焦安装、更新与验证，尽量保持核心能力和通信协议跟随上游。

limitations.text: 属于社区项目；Linux 包未签名，Office 文档到 PDF 转换暂缺，上游仍为 developer preview 并可能有破坏性变化。

how_to.text: 下载对应架构 AppImage 并准备 FUSE 2，或选择适配发行版的 deb 包。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Desktop-first, open-source (MIT) application for running parallel agents, and multi-step custom workflows triggered by schedules, webhooks or events from tools like Linear and Sentry, across your already-used providers.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Frink



  
  
  



  Desktop-first app for parallel agents and triggered multi-step workflows.
  Workflows can include steps you write yourself in code, alongside agent, command and approval steps.



  Save a routine as a Flow and it starts by itself: on a schedule, from any webhook, or from an event in Linear, Shortcut, ClickUp, Sentry, PostHog or Vercel.
  Finished work and agent questions wait for you in the Work Queue, on your computer or on your iPhone (beta).
  It all runs on your computer while Frink is open, with the AI coding tool you already use. No Frink account.


<ins>Download Frink</ins>

evidence.heading: Run four agents side by side
evidence.text:
Split the window into up to four panes and give each agent a different job. They work at the same time, and each pane keeps its own model and its own diff to review. Put each one on its own git worktree and they never touch the same files.

[Docs →](user-docs/worktree-setup.md)

evidence.heading: One sentence becomes an automation
evidence.text:
Type the routine the way you would say it: _"Every weekday at 9am, run the tests. If any fail, have an agent fix them, then wait for my approval before it opens a PR."_ Frink builds it as a Flow and lists every step, so you can read it and change it before it runs.

[Docs →](user-docs/flows.md)

evidence.heading: It starts when something happens
evidence.text:
A new ticket in Linear, Shortcut or ClickUp, an error in Sentry, an event in PostHog or Vercel, any webhook, or a time of day. The Flow checks a condition to pick its path, and waits at an approval step until you say yes.

[Docs →](user-docs/plugins.md)

evidence.heading: Everything that needs you, in one queue
evidence.text:
Every run from every project shows up in the Work Queue as running, ready for review or queued. A badge appears when a Flow stops for approval or an agent has a question. Read what it did, then approve it or reply to send it back.

[Docs →](user-docs/task-lifecycle.md)

evidence.heading: Check the work and fix it yourself
evidence.text:
Every file the agent changes shows as a diff. Open it in the built-in editor, change a line and save, run a command in the terminal, or roll the chat and its code back to an earlier point.

[Docs →](user-docs/changes.md)



  




**Also in the box:**

- **[Custom steps](user-docs/flows.md#custom-nodes-flow-editor)** — need a step Frink doesn't have? Ask the agent to write one in JavaScript, or write it yourself, and reuse it in any Flow. For another language, use a command step.
- **[Plugins & MCP](user-docs/mcp-servers.md)** — connect Linear, Shortcut, ClickUp, GitHub, Notion, Slack, Sentry, PostHog and more, as chat tools and Flow steps.
- **[Your own AI sign-in](user-docs/ai-accounts.md)** — uses your existing Claude Code or Codex login, the OpenCode or GitHub Copilot you installed, or your Cursor sign-in. Frink only checks that you are signed in and leaves the login with the tool. If you paste an Anthropic API key instead, it is stored encrypted on your computer.
- **Local-first** — chats, Flows and tasks live in SQLite on your machine. No account needed. Official builds send anonymous usage counts and crash reports: [everything Frink sends](user-docs/telemetry.md).

---

evidence.text:

- Or build from source — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

   AMD / Intel → [Vulkan package, experimental](https://github.com/alexturkey/voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi/releases/download/v0.1.1/voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi-motor-v0.1.1-win64-vulkan.zip)
   (already downloaded one? add `-HazirZip <path to the zip>` to the command below).
2. **Extract** the zip, open the `voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi-main` folder, type `powershell` in the Explorer address
   bar and press Enter.
3. **Run** the installer (needs 64-bit Python 3.10–3.13; NVIDIA driver ≥ 570 for CUDA), then double-click **`baslat.bat`**:
   ```powershell
   powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\kur.ps1 -Kok C:\vox
   ```
   AMD / Intel: add `-Vulkan` at the end. The UI opens at http://127.0.0.1:8765/.

The engine zip is not a standalone app (its exe needs the model and DLLs that the installer sets up). Details, GPU
list and common problems: "Quick install" below.

evidence.heading: Quick start (macOS, Apple Silicon)
evidence.text:
Needs Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`) and [Homebrew](https://brew.sh):
```bash
brew install cmake python@3.12
git clone https://github.com/alexturkey/voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi.git
cd voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi
bash scripts/kur.sh
```
The installer downloads the model, builds the patched engine with Metal (~1 min) and sets everything up under `~/vox`.
Then double-click **`baslat.command`**. On a MacBook Air M4 16 GB: ~2 s of compute per 1 s of speech, same seed gives
byte-identical audio, peak ~5.3 GB RAM, no thermal slowdown over 12 min of continuous reading. Details and
measurements: [docs/mac.md](docs/mac.md).

**Native Mac app (no Python, Homebrew or Terminal):** [macos/README.md](macos/README.md). It bundles the same
patched engine and downloads the model on first launch; for now it is built from source with Xcode.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
1. **Voice design.** An English *voice description* + a Turkish *text read while the voice is created* + a number of
   variants. Each variant gets its own seed; the engine receives `(description)text` and returns a 20-35 s design
   recording per seed.
2. **Reference-based reading.** The design recording is passed to **both** engine inputs (`audio` and `voice_ref`),
   together with its transcript (`reference_text`) and the new text to read, with the same seed. The voice is carried by
   the recording, not by the description, so it does not drift from text to text. Text is read sentence by sentence.
3. Quality is fixed: 16 diffusion steps, CFG 2.0. The seed is not a quality knob.

The engine is audio.cpp v0.7.2 with our patch (`patches/`), the model is VoxCPM2 Q8_0 GGUF. Peak VRAM ≈ 2.8 GB;
about 2 s of compute per 1 s of speech on a GTX 1050 Ti. Details and measurements: [docs/4gb.md](docs/4gb.md).

evidence.heading: Quick install, no compiler needed (Windows 10/11, NVIDIA GPU ≥ 4 GB)
evidence.text:
Prerequisites: NVIDIA driver ≥ 570 and 64-bit Python 3.10–3.13 (`winget install Python.Python.3.12`). Nothing else:
no Visual Studio, no CUDA installer. Not sure which card you have? Run `nvidia-smi` in PowerShell: it prints the GPU
name, driver version and memory. No NVIDIA card? See "AMD / Intel" below.

With [Git](https://git-scm.com/download/win):

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/alexturkey/voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi.git
cd voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\kur.ps1 -Kok C:\vox
```

Without Git: on this page click **Code → Download ZIP**, extract it, open the extracted
`voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi-main` folder, type `powershell` in the Explorer address bar and press Enter, then run the
last line above. Git is only needed for the build-from-source path.

`-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` applies to this one process only and changes no system setting; read `scripts\kur.ps1`
before running it, as with any installer script. One command, ~10 min, ~3.7 GB download, everything sha256-verified: the model (2.95 GB), the CUDA 12.8 runtime DLLs as
portable zips (no system install, PATH untouched), the **prebuilt engine** from the Releases page, a `.venv` with the two
Python packages, `ayarlar.json`, and a final GPU check (`KONTROL_OK`). Re-run it after any failure; verified files are
skipped. Then start the web UI: double-click **`baslat.bat`** in the repo folder. It starts the UI and opens
**http://127.0.0.1:8765/** in your browser when it is ready; close the black window (or press Ctrl+C there) to stop it.
The same from PowerShell:

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ses_tasarim.arayuz
```
then open **http://127.0.0.1:8765/** yourself (started this way the UI does not open the browser; it listens on
localhost on

evidence.heading: Common install problems
evidence.text:
| You see | What it means, what to do |
|---|---|
| `cudart64_12.dll not found` after double-clicking the exe | The engine is not meant to be started by hand. Run the `kur.ps1` command above, then start the web UI. |
| `64-bit Python 3.10+ bulunamadı` (Python not found) | Install Python (`winget install Python.Python.3.12`), close PowerShell, open a new one and run the same command again. |
| `motor ekran kartını görmedi` (the engine did not see the GPU) | Update the NVIDIA driver to 570 or newer; check that `nvidia-smi` runs. |
| `indirme başarısız` / `sha256 tutmadı` (download failed / checksum mismatch) | Usually an interrupted download. Run the same command again; verified files are skipped. |
| Build path: `nvcc` fails | Keep the install root short (`-Kok C:\vox`). |
| The page does not open | Start the UI with `baslat.bat`, or open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ yourself. Port busy? Change `"port"` in `ayarlar.json`. |

Problems? [Discussions (Q&A)](https://github.com/alexturkey/voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi/discussions) or an
[install issue](https://github.com/alexturkey/voxcpm2-turkce-ses-tasarimi/issues/new?template=kurulum-sorunu.yml)
with your GPU, Windows version, the command and its last lines.

evidence.heading: Use
evidence.text:
Command line:
```powershell
# list voices
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ses_tasarim.oku --liste
# read with a bundled voice (one sentence per line; "|| paragraf" = longer pause)
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ses_tasarim.oku --ses hazir/belgesel_hanim --metin @metin.txt --cikti cikti\deneme
# design a new voice: 3 variants, 3 seeds
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ses_tasarim.tasarla --ad deniz_feneri --cesit 3 --tarif "A calm Turkish woman ..." --metin @tanitim.txt
# read with variant 2 of it
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ses_tasarim.oku --ses deniz_feneri/2 --metin @metin.txt --cikti cikti\deniz
```
Text rules: write numbers in words, no quotation marks (the tool refuses digits and quotes), one sentence per line,
≤ 2000 characters per line. `ayarlar/okunus_sozlugu.tsv` fixes pronunciations of foreign words in Turkish text.
Other languages: `--dil <code>` (or the voice card's `dil`); apostrophes are allowed there, the Turkish dictionary is
skipped, digits are still refused. If a reading prints `speed gate: satır [...]`, listen to those lines.

Web UI (local only, 127.0.0.1): `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ses_tasarim.arayuz` → open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
yourself (another port: `--port 8800`). Three boxes (description, creation text, text to read) + variant count.

evidence.text:
SpeakMore


  口述成文，划词即译。
  开源、免费的语音输入与翻译工具，支持 macOS 与 Windows。
  语音输入、语音翻译、划词翻译，各由一个快捷键触发，在任意应用中可用。

  简体中文 · English

evidence.heading: 三项功能
evidence.text:
三项功能均以右 ⌥（Windows 为右 Alt）为起点：单按为语音输入，加空格为语音翻译，加回车为划词翻译。

| 功能 | 用途 | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🎙️ **[语音输入](#️-语音输入)** | 口述，整理为通顺的文字后写入光标处 | 右 ⌥ | 右 Alt |
| 🌐 **[语音翻译](#-语音翻译)** | 说一种语言，直接写出另一种 | 右 ⌥ + 空格 | 右 Alt + 空格 |
| 📖 **[划词翻译](#-划词翻译)** | 选中任意文字，译文在选区下方显示 | 右 ⌥ + 回车 | 右 Alt + 回车 |

evidence.heading: 🎙️ 语音输入
evidence.text:
- 按下快捷键开始口述，再次按下结束，文字写入当前光标位置。
- 自动去除语气词、重复与改口内容（直出、混合方式）。
- 自动补全标点，较长内容分段、分条。
- 词典中的专有名词、产品名与术语按词典的写法输出。
- 三种识别方式并列可选，离线方式完全在本机运行，不上传任何数据。

evidence.heading: 🌐 语音翻译
evidence.text:
- 用中文口述，写入的是英文；目标语言支持 16 种。
- 适用于在群聊中与外国同事、客户交流，以及撰写英文邮件与提交说明：译文直接写入输入框，无需另开翻译工具。
- 先整理再翻译：语气词与改口不进入译文，原文与译文均记入历史。
- 在「设置 › 语音翻译」中预设目标语言，可设多种，第一种为默认；口述时可在悬浮条上临时切换，仅对本次生效。
- 模型耗时中位数：直出 2.6 秒，混合 1.3 秒。
- 使用直出或混合方式；离线方式的本机模型只能转文字，不提供语音翻译。

evidence.heading: 📖 划词翻译
evidence.text:
PDF
    终端
  


- 在任意应用中选中文字，按下右 ⌥ + 回车，译文显示在选区下方的卡片中。
- 无需安装插件，不限应用：网页、PDF、终端、文档与聊天软件均适用。
- 卡片不抢占焦点，正在阅读或编辑的应用保持原状；卡片上可复制译文、临时切换目标语言、固定卡片。
- 原文已是目标语言时，改译为英文（目标为英文时改译为简体中文），卡片上标明实际译成的语言。
- 使用独立的文字模型，与语音互不影响：默认 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，单次约 0.9 秒；可在引擎页的「划词」一段更换，亦支持 OpenAI 兼容服务。
- 划词记录计入历史与花费，不计入首页的口述统计。

evidence.heading: 🚀 安装
evidence.text:
**macOS**

- 系统要求：macOS 12 及以上。
- 打开 dmg，将 SpeakMore 拖入"应用程序"。
- 安装包已使用 Developer ID 签名，并通过 Apple 公证。

**Windows**

- 系统要求：Windows 10（1809 及以上）或 Windows 11，64 位。
- 运行安装程序；如出现"Windows 已保护你的电脑"，依次点击"更多信息""仍要运行"。
- 仅为当前账户安装，无需管理员权限。
- 安装过程无需联网。

**终端安装**（附带 `speakmore` 命令行工具）

```bash
# macOS
curl -fsSL https://dl.zephyrxiang.com/speakmore/install.sh | bash
```

```powershell
# Windows（PowerShell）
irm https://dl.zephyrxiang.com/speakmore/install.ps1 | iex
```

- 下载链接末尾附加 `.sha256`，可获取对应文件的校验值。

**存储位置**

- 程序、本机模型、设置、历史记录与录音统一保存在一个文件夹中，默认为 `~/.speakmore`（Windows 为 `%USERPROFILE%\.speakmore`）。
- 首次安装时可另选位置，例如其他磁盘：Mac App 首次打开时询问，Windows 安装程序在安装前询问，终端安装在命令行中询问。SpeakMore 保存在所选文件夹中的 `.speakmore`。
- 之后可在「设置 › 通用 › 存储位置」更改，或执行 `speakmore move <文件夹>`；全部文件整体迁移，完成后自动重新打开。
- 所选磁盘需为 APFS、Mac OS 扩展或 NTFS 格式；exFAT、FAT32 格式的 U 盘与移动硬盘不支持。


安装包与终端安装的区别

- 安装包为独立应用：macOS 权限授予 SpeakMore 本身，支持开机自启。
- 终端安装在 macOS 上由终端启动，权限授予所用终端。
- Windows 下两种方式的安装内容相同，均位于 `%USERPROFILE%\.speakmore`，并添加开始菜单项。
- 两种方式共用设置、历史记录与 `speakmore` 命令，同一时间运行其一即可。

evidence.heading: Why
evidence.text:
Iranian websites are not built for AI agents. Most have no public API, prices come in Rial on one page and Toman
on the next, and every site hides its best deals behind a different menu. Each package server here maps one site's
real (undocumented) API, tests it, and exposes it as clean MCP tools with prices in **Toman**. `exiryab-mcp`,
`pasavard-mcp` and `swapwallet-mcp` are the sites' own servers, built on their documented APIs.

Put a few of them together and one sentence does a day of tab-hopping (illustrative example):

> **You:** I'm flying Tehran to Kish next Thursday for 3 nights. Cheapest flight, a villa under 4 million Toman a
> night, and a dermatologist on the island with a free slot.
>
> **Agent:** *calls* `mrbilit` for flights → `jabama` and `otaghak` for stays → `paziresh24` for doctors
>
> | | Pick | Price (Toman) |
> |---|---|---:|
> | Flight | Thursday 07:40, economy, 2 seats left | 2,180,000 |
> | Stay | 2-bedroom villa near the beach, 4.8 stars | 3,650,000 / night |
> | Doctor | Dermatologist, Saturday 10:30, in-person | 450,000 |

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
Every server is a small Python package on PyPI, run with [`uvx`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), except

github_projects.description_zh: 非官方技能，教编程智能体使用 TypeSafe AI 的 Jev 构建：类型化决策、校准信心，以及来自 150+ 社区项目的先前作品。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Unofficial skill that teaches coding agents to build with TypeSafe AI's Jev: typed decisions, calibrated confidence, and prior art from 150+ community projects.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Building with TypeSafe Jev
  Typed decisions with calibrated confidence, for your coding agent.
  Links to 150+ community projects, sorted by shape, with a code sketch for each.



  
  



  Connect on LinkedIn!



  English ·
  简体中文 ·
  日本語 ·
  한국어 ·
  Tiếng Việt ·
  Português (BR) ·
  Italiano


> [!NOTE]
> This is an unofficial, community skill. It is not made, reviewed, or endorsed by TypeSafe AI. TypeSafe publishes its own skill at [typesafe-ai/skills](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/skills). See [How this differs from the official skill](#how-this-differs-from-the-official-skill).

Coding agents treat Jev like one more chat model. This skill teaches them to design for it: typed questions, calibrated confidence, and links to 150+ community projects, sorted by how they work, with a code sketch for each pattern. It installs in Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, Muse, and Muse Code.

[Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction) is a [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one) model. It does not write text. You send it content and a set of typed questions, and it answers each one with a value and a calibrated probability, usually in 100 to 200 ms:

- **Choice** picks one option from a list. Example: route a ticket to billing, shipping, or support.
- **Score** places the content on a scale you describe. Example: grade a pull request from "ignores the spec" to "meets the spec".
- **Noul** gives the probability that a yes/no statement is true. Example: "this shell command deletes files outside the project."

evidence.heading: Set up an API key (optional, recommended)
evidence.text:
The skill works without a key. With `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` set in the agent's shell, the agent can check its design against the live API before the code reaches your project. That catches wrong field names, and questions Jev reads differently than you meant. Each call costs a fraction of a cent.


Create, store, and troubleshoot a key




Create a key (four steps in the TypeSafe console)

**Step 1.** Sign in at [console.typesafe.ai](https://console.typesafe.ai/) and open **API Keys** in the sidebar.



**Step 2.** Click **Create key** at the top right.



**Step 3.** Name the key after where it will live, such as the machine or the agent. Then click **Create key**.



**Step 4.** Copy the key now. The console shows it once. If you lose it, create a new one and revoke the old one.






Store the key (macOS, Linux, Windows)

Keep the key in its own file, readable only by you, and export it as `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. Agents often start shells without a terminal, so each section puts the key where those shells can see it. Pick your system.


macOS (zsh, the default shell)

Save the key to a private file:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/typesafe && umask 077 && printf 'export TYPESAFE_API_KEY=%s\n' 'YOUR_KEY' > ~/.config/typesafe/env
```

Load it from `~/.zshenv`. Every zsh reads that file, including shells that agents start without a terminal. `~/.zshrc` is read only by interactive shells.

```bash
echo '[ -f ~/.config/typesafe/env ] && . ~/.config/typesafe/env' >> ~/.zshenv
```

Open a new terminal and check it. The command prints the length of the key, not the key:

```bash
echo ${#TYPESAFE_API_KEY}
```




Linux with bash (Ubuntu, Debian, Mint, Fedora, Arch)

Save the key to a private file:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/typesafe && umask 077 && printf 'export TYPESAFE_API_KEY=%s\n' '

evidence.heading: How it was tested
evidence.text:
We gave a coding agent six Jev tasks, such as a support-ticket triage function and an approval gate for shell commands. Each task ran 10 times with this skill, with no skill, and with the official skill, each arm in its own isolated container. The agent had the docs but no API key, so graders checked the code it wrote. Checks that need judgment went to three LLM judges from three providers (Claude Opus, GPT-6 Sol, Kimi K3), and the majority decided.

| | No skill | This skill | Official skill |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Average score | 0.65 ± 0.05 | **0.96 ± 0.02** | 0.77 ± 0.04 |

Score is the share of checks passed, averaged over 10 runs per task.

**Where the skill made the difference** (runs out of 10 that passed):

| The agent's code... | No skill | This skill | Official skill |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| counted in code, instead of asking Jev for a number | 1 | 8 | 0 |
| named a field of the input in its questions | 0 | 10 | 1 |
| pinned or logged the Jev model version | 0 | 10 | 0 |
| gave the department list a catch-all option | 3 | 10 | 6 |
| kept more than one path while walking 1,200 categories | 1 | 10 | 7 |
| kept a plain-code backstop for destructive commands | 7 | 10 | 2 |
| read `score` as a position from 0 to n-1 | 9 | 10 | 5 |

[See every check →](evals/docs/results.md#every-check)

Each of these rows beats no skill, the official skill, or both by more than chance at 95%.

**More detail:**

- [evals/README.md](evals/README.md): results by case, and how to run the suite
- [evals/docs/results.md](evals/docs/results.md): every check, each judge's scores, cost, tokens, and method
- [evals/docs/cases.md](evals/docs/cases.md): the six tasks and what each check looks for
- [evals/docs/harness.md](evals/docs/harness.md): how a run works, the isolated containers, and

| `api-reference.md` | HTTP API, Python and JavaScript SDKs, limits, errors, environment variables | When it writes the code |

evidence.text:
The [official TypeSafe skill](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/skills) is one file of design guidance. For API details, it sends the agent to the live docs on every task. The two skills have different names and do not conflict, so you can install both, though the evals did not test them together.

github_projects.name: absent-author
github_projects.description: Research and writing can be automated. Authorship cannot. Evidence list + agent skills for spotting AI-produced papers no human stood behind.
github_projects.description_zh: 研究和写作可以自动化，但署名不能。提供证据清单 + 识别 AI 生成论文且无人负责智能体技能。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Research and writing can be automated. Authorship cannot. Evidence list + agent skills for spotting AI-produced papers no human stood behind.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
An evidence list and two agent skills for spotting research papers that AI produced and no human stood behind.


  
  
  
  
  
  


Ruoyu Zhao1,*,† · Zhehao Zou2,* · Jinheng Zhang3 · Yuting Chen4 · Jiaqi Wu1 · Chenyu Zhu11City University of Hong Kong · 2The Chinese University of Hong Kong · 3University of Pennsylvania · 4Georgia Institute of Technology* Equal contribution · † Project lead

English · 中文 · 日本語 · Website

Reviewers now see papers that an agent produced end to end, with no human who steered, checked or owns them. This repository names the signs of that absence, with sources, and provides tools that turn them into evidence a reviewer can cite and an author can fix.

| You are | Use | You get |
|---|---|---|
| an **author** finishing an AI-assisted paper | [`paper-author-pass`](skills/paper-author-pass/SKILL.md) | questions only you can answer, a claim–evidence map, verified references and numbers, then lighter prose; it ends with three questions to answer before you sign |
| a **reviewer or AC** facing a suspicious submission | [`paper-slop-screen`](skills/paper-slop-screen/SKILL.md) | W / R / Q grades, a quadrant, every finding with a location and a quote, a review paragraph and a note to the AC |
| anyone who wants a **quick surface scan** | [`tools/slop_lint.py`](tools/slop_lint.py) | calibrated counts of 28 surface traces, as candidates for a human to read |
| a **maintainer of review norms** | [`EVIDENCE.md`](EVIDENCE.md) | 83 sourced items with strengths, false-positive notes and paper-type exemptions |

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/THUROI0787/absent-author.git && cd absent-author
./install.sh                # both skills -> ~/.claude/skills  (or --project, --codex, --dest DIR, --link)
```

Then, in Claude Code, Codex or any agent that reads `SKILL.md`:

```text
Use paper-author-pass on paper/ in audit mode. I'll answer your questions.
Use paper-slop-screen to triage this arXiv preprint: <path or id>
```

The lint also runs on its own (Python 3.9+, no dependencies), and three helpers do the slow verification work:

```bash
python tools/slop_lint.py paper/ --source -o lint.md       # surface traces; skips prompt dumps and checklists
python tools/ref_verify.py refs.bib --sample 5 --mailto you@example.org   # every author, incl. the last
python tools/number_ledger.py paper/main.tex                # same quantity stated with different values
python tools/pdf_hidden_text.py paper.pdf                   # hidden or remapped text (pip install pymupdf)
```

All four report candidates for a person to read, never verdicts. Optional system tools: `poppler-utils` (pdftotext, pdftoppm) and `tesseract` (OCR check for remapped text).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Before you run the screen on a submission **under review**, check your venue's reviewer LLM policy. ICML 2026 desk-rejected 497 papers linked to reviewers who broke the no-LLM policy they had chosen. The skill asks you to confirm this first.

In calibration, 0% of human papers and 50% of AI-heavy papers reached at least this many. Hits are candidates; a clean report proves nothing. For what it is worth, this README scores 1 of 6 on the same cluster, with zero em dashes.
