evidence.heading: Overview
evidence.text:
UFO is an open source runtime for AI agents. Team members give agents work in chat. Agents can read
files and run commands to complete that work.

[UFO's hosted service](https://ufo.ai) runs this code. You can also run it yourself with your own
model keys. The `ufo` terminal client connects to either. This repository contains the server,
client, SDK, and extensions.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **One process.** `ufoctl serve` runs the agent loop, turn queue, sandbox, surfaces, and jobs. | **Laptop to fleet.** SQLite and local files alone, or Postgres, S3, and Redis for more instances. One bundle serves both. |
| **Durable turns.** Each turn is a DBOS workflow that survives a crash. | **Grants in chat.** A member grants an account to an agent in chat. Agents never borrow the speaker's identity. |
| **Workspace-scoped.** Every row carries its workspace id. | **Everything is an extension.** Tools, connectors, subagents, surfaces, model providers, sandbox carriers. |

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
To host UFO yourself, run one process on SQLite and local files, with no Docker. Install
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), then:

```bash
make install
cp .env.template .env   # set the three model API keys
make build
make init EMAIL=email@work.com
make serve
```

`make init` creates the workspace with you as admin and writes a CLI token to `~/.ufoctl/token`.
`make serve` listens on `http://localhost:8710`. In a second terminal:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.ufo && install -m 600 ~/.ufoctl/token ~/.ufo/credentials
echo http://localhost:8710 > ~/.ufo/workspace
./client/target/debug/ufo "what can you do?"
```

The agent loop and conversation run in `ufoctl serve` in both modes. The flag selects where the
agent reads and edits files and runs commands when you start a conversation:

| | `ufo` (default) | `ufo --remote` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File reads, edits, and commands | The connected client runs them on your machine as your user. | They run in the workspace's configured sandbox. |
| Working files | Your current directory when you start `ufo`. | The sandbox's `/workspace`, separate from your current directory. |
| Client connection | Keep `ufo` running until the turn ends; those steps need that connection. | The turn can continue after `ufo` exits. Use `--wait SECONDS` to leave early and `--resume ID` to read the rest. |
| Execution boundary | Your machine and your user account. | The configured sandbox carrier: `local` on the server by default, or a carrier such as Docker or E2B. |

A resumed conversation keeps the execution location it already has. See `client/README.md` for
client options.

`.env` refuses the bare names `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`, because every tool that
reads `.env` gets all of its values.


Postgres

`make db` starts Postgres on `127.0.0.1:554

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
| Package | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `ufo.harness` | Product-neutral agent execution: messages, model requests, tool calls, budgets, compaction, the sandbox protocol. |
| `ufo.runtime` | The durable host: identity, authorization, turns, surfaces, accounting, the extension API. |
| `ufo.host` | Extension discovery, built-in tools, and per-turn prompt and tool assembly. |

A **pack** names the extensions a deploy activates. `assistant` is the default.

evidence.heading: Use hosted
evidence.text:
[Create a workspace](https://ufo.ai/login?signup=1) with your work email. The hosted service runs
agents and scheduled tasks on UFO's infrastructure and provides model access. Your team can
use the [web app](https://app.ufo.ai) or Slack without running `ufoctl serve` or setting model API
keys.

Connect Slack during workspace setup. To use the same workspace from your terminal on macOS or Linux,
install the client:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://ufo.ai/ufo | sh
```

Run `ufo` and sign in. Start it from a directory to let the agent work on its files, or run
`ufo --remote` to use the hosted sandbox. The table in [Quick start](#quick-start) compares the two
modes. See the [terminal guide](https://ufo.ai/docs/work/terminal/) for more detail.

evidence.heading: Security model
evidence.text:
| Boundary | What holds it |
| --- | --- |
| Agent access | A member's account reaches an agent only through a connector grant made in chat; the granting turn is the audit record. The workspace's own keyed accounts reach only the main agent until a member grants them to another. |
| Workspace scope | Every request, turn, and job binds one workspace, and every query filters on it. |
| Keys | The Rust services under `servers/` hold no customer keys; every secret stays in the runtime. |
| Sandbox | The default `local` carrier confines writes with Seatbelt or Landlock, but can read the whole host, and the kernel does not enforce its egress. For untrusted input or several workspaces, use `docker` or `e2b`. |

evidence.heading: Extend it
evidence.text:
An extension is a Python package that imports only `ufo.sdk` and declares one entry point:

```toml
[project.entry-points."ufo.extension"]
acme = "ufo_ext_acme.manifest:manifest"
```

`extensions/sample` exercises every manifest point. `ufoctl ext search | install | remove` manages
installed extensions. `spec.md` §Extension system lists each point's contract.

The [Screenpipe example](examples/screenpipe/README.md) connects local recording search through
the existing MCP extension.

github_projects.name: stalemap
github_projects.description: Tell your coding agent which dependencies changed after its training cutoff. Diffs types and changelogs, writes a short block into AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md.
github_projects.description_zh: 告诉你的编码智能体在其训练截止后哪些依赖项发生了变化。识别差异类型和变更日志，并将简短内容写入 AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Tell your coding agent which dependencies changed after its training cutoff. Diffs types and changelogs, writes a short block into AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Install ·
  Example ·
  How it works ·
  Results ·
  Changelog


Coding agents learn libraries from training data that stops at a cutoff date. When your project pins newer versions, the agent writes code for the old API: `maxSteps` against AI SDK 7, `required_error` against zod 4, `middleware.ts` against Next 16.

stalemap finds the dependencies that changed after your model's training cutoff and tells the agent what changed, in three ways:

- **Notes:** a short, ranked list of changes written into `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, so the agent reads it before it starts.
- **Edit-time guard:** after each edit, the project's own type-check. If the code uses an API that changed after the cutoff, the agent gets the compiler error and the matching note (or the release-note or upgrade-guide section that explains it) right away. It also reports the code that still compiles but uses something that moved.
- **`search_changes`:** an MCP tool the agent can ask in its own words, such as "resolve alias in next.config", to get the matching changes with their sources.

It works for JavaScript and TypeScript projects, with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode or any MCP client.

**In a blind, pre-registered benchmark** of 66 tasks built from changes released after June 2026, `claude-sonnet-5-5` agents passed **89%** of sessions with stalemap, against **68%** with no help and **73%** with a plain `tsc --noEmit` hook after each edit. See [Results](#results).

evidence.heading: Status
evidence.text:
- **npm:** the latest release is [`stalemap` 0.4.1](https://www.npmjs.com/package/stalemap): the build tested in held-out v4 (0.4.0), plus a one-line footer in the notes block. `npx stalemap`, the Claude Code plugin and the GitHub Action all run it. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).
- The project is early, and maintained by one person.

evidence.heading: Claude Code plugin
evidence.text:
```text
/plugin marketplace add Umair/stalemap
/plugin install stalemap@stalemap
```

The plugin adds:

- a SessionStart hook that puts the notes into Claude's context for the session's model (on startup, after `/clear` and after compaction; it writes no files);
- a PostToolUse hook that runs the edit-time guard after each Write or Edit;
- the stalemap MCP server and two skills (`/stalemap:sync` writes the notes block; `upgrade` tells Claude to look up a package's changes before using or upgrading it).

The hooks and the MCP server run `npx -y stalemap@latest`, so they use the latest npm release. Its MCP tools are `search_changes`, `package_changes`, `project_changes` and `check_notes`.

evidence.heading: Command line
evidence.text:
```bash
npx stalemap            # preview what changed and the block it would write
npx stalemap sync       # write the block into AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md
npx stalemap check      # for CI: exit 1 when the block is missing or stale
npx stalemap guard src/**/*.ts   # run the guard by hand
```

The block sits between `` and ``. Text outside it is never touched. Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`; if your notes live in `AGENTS.md`, add `@AGENTS.md` to `CLAUDE.md` or pass `--target CLAUDE.md`.

evidence.heading: Other agents: `setup --agent`
evidence.text:
```bash
stalemap setup --agent cursor             # or codex, opencode, claude
stalemap setup --agent codex --dry-run    # print the changes, write nothing
```

One command per agent writes the notes, registers the MCP server and installs the guard as the agent's post-edit hook, as project files you can commit. It merges into existing config files, keeps entries it didn't write, and re-running it changes nothing.

One caveat: it hasn't been tried in a real Cursor, Codex or OpenCode install yet. Cursor doesn't pass a `postToolUse` hook's context to the model yet, so setup adds a stop-hook fallback that sends unreported findings as a follow-up message.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
1. **Which model?** `--model`, or the model configured for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Gemini CLI, or `$ANTHROPIC_MODEL`. The training cutoff comes from [models.dev](https://models.dev) (with a built-in fallback table), or pass `--cutoff YYYY-MM-DD`.
2. **What did the model know?** For each dependency, the newest stable release published at least 30 days before the cutoff (`--margin`).
3. **Which dependencies?** Direct dependencies your code imports (scanned locally), plus the ones a config file configures (`tsconfig.json`, `next.config.*`, the Prisma schema, Vitest and ESLint configs, and others). `--all` checks every direct dependency. Pinned versions come from `node_modules` or the lockfile (npm, pnpm, yarn, bun).
4. **What changed?**
   - **Types:** both versions' `.d.ts` files are downloaded and compared with the TypeScript compiler API: removed, renamed and moved exports, new required parameters, removed or newly required options, and new `@deprecated` tags with their hints.
   - **Release notes:** the package's changelog or GitHub Releases, scored for breaking-change signals and for the APIs you use. A removal gets its replacement from a rename the changelog announces.
   - **Upgrade guides** (`--guides`): for changes that never reach a type signature, like a new default or a renamed file convention. Claude turns each guide into short notes, and a note is kept only if it quotes the guide.
   - **Verified examples** (`--examples`): a Before → After line under the top notes, written by Claude and kept only if it compiles against the version you pin.
5. **Fit the budget.** Notes about what your project uses come first: imported APIs, members and props, config keys it sets, file names. The default budget is 1,800 tokens (`--budget`).

**The guard** runs after eac

evidence.heading: Limits
evidence.text:
- JavaScript and TypeScript only, and one `package.json` (no workspace traversal yet).
- Packages without bundled types get release-note notes only (`@types/*` aren't diffed).
- Usage tracking stops at imported names and `x.member` accesses; instance chains like `client.messages.create({ temperature })` aren't traced.
- Behavior changes that never reach a type signature come only from release notes and (with `--guides`) upgrade guides. If neither names the setting, stalemap can't either.
- Ranking release notes is heuristic and noisy for prose-heavy changelogs.
- Agents sometimes ignore correct notes. The guard catches what fails to compile and some of what still compiles (moved keys and members, renamed files); other stale code that still compiles is caught only if a note covers it.

github_projects.name: endo
github_projects.description: The Higher Order Harness (HOH "/oʊ/" ), projected as a unified chat interface.
github_projects.description_zh: 高阶线束（HOH “/oʊ/”）被投影为统一的聊天界面。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: The Higher Order Harness (HOH "/oʊ/" ), projected as a unified chat interface.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Endo


  The Higher Order Harness (HOH).
  Compose any agent, on the subscription you already have, into any workflow.



  



  Download for Mac ·
  Quick start ·
  Features ·
  Development guide

evidence.heading: Higher Order Harness
evidence.text:
A harness runs one agent: it sends the prompt, runs the tools and keeps the
history. Endo is a **Higher Order Harness (HOH)**. It takes agents as its
building blocks, the way a higher-order function takes functions, and composes
them freely:

- **In one session**, switch between Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity and Grok
  mid-thread, or Dig In on any answer. Each agent picks up the full history.
- **Across sessions**, a workflow fans work out to agents from different
  vendors and continues any of their sessions, and a schedule runs the whole
  composition again later.

**Why Endo?** The name comes from _endomorphism_, a map whose output is the
same kind of thing as its input. Endo takes agents and gives you back an agent:
every composition answers in a thread you can talk to, dig into and schedule
like any other chat.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
[Download Endo for macOS (Apple Silicon)](https://downloads.longsurf.ai/endo/darwin/arm64/Endo.dmg),
open the disk image, and install Endo. Signed releases update themselves in the
background.

To run it from source, install [Node.js 24](https://nodejs.org/en/download),
[Bun 1.4.2](https://bun.sh/docs/installation), and [Just](https://just.systems/man/en/), then:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/longsurf-ai/endo.git
cd endo
just install --frozen-lockfile
just desktop
```

Sign in to at least one provider (an existing `codex`, `claude`, Antigravity or
`grok` login works, or use Settings → Models), then ask something like "Every weekday
at 9 AM, summarize my priorities for the day" and open the Schedule page.

evidence.heading: Any agent, one protocol, your subscription
evidence.text:
Endo drives Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity and Grok natively through their own CLIs,
signed in with the accounts you already have. There are no API keys to paste,
and Settings → Models shows each provider's plan usage. Every provider streams
through one protocol into one harness, so answers, tool calls, permission
prompts and history behave the same whichever model you pick, and you can
change it mid-thread.

evidence.heading: Workflows that compose anything
evidence.text:
A workflow is a TypeScript file in your workspace. `agent()` calls any model
from any provider, `parallel()` fans calls out, `phase()` groups them, and a
session ID continues an earlier agent's conversation. Run one from chat and the
Workflow card shows every call as it happens. `/best-of-n`,
`/multi-turn-debate`, `/thesis-killer` and `/hypothesis-race` ship as
workflows, and schedules run any prompt later, on a cron or once.

evidence.heading: Dig in, one thread, persistent memory
evidence.text:
Select any part of an answer and Dig In: a focused conversation opens beside
the thread, and the main thread stays clean. Sessions, runs and Dig Ins persist
on your machine, so after a restart every thread and branch is still there, and
any agent can pick up where another left off.

evidence.heading: Building on it
evidence.text:
- Add user data as a Resource: define it once, as a Drizzle table and an Effect
  Schema, and get a typed API, agent tools and live updates, so people and
  agents change the same state under the same rules. See
  [Adding a Resource](docs/architecture/resource.md#adding-a-resource).
- Add an agent tool in `server/agent/tool/tools/` and register it in
  `server/agent/tool/registry.ts` and `server/agent/profiles/builtin.ts`.
- Change the agent's instructions in `server/agent/profiles/prompt/segments/`.
- Add a page under `app/src/app/` and a feature under `app/src/features/`.
- Build and publish a signed Mac release with the
  [release guide](docs/operations/desktop-release.md).

See the [development guide](docs/development.md) and the
[code organization guide](docs/architecture/code-organization.md). Endo is at
0.1.x, so expect breaking changes.

github_projects.name: STEPQuant
github_projects.description: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
github_projects.description_zh: STEPQuant：研究 Delta-rule 循环状态量化中误差何时持续、在何处影响输出，并据此分配精度。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization

evidence.heading: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
evidence.text:
Welcome to the official code repository for **[STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38169)**.

Your star means a lot to us in developing this project! ⭐⭐⭐


  
  ▶ Watch the introduction video

evidence.heading: 📰 News
evidence.text:
- [2026/10/12] 🔥 STEPQuant ranked #3 on [🤗 Hugging Face Daily Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.38169)!
- [2026/09/30] 📄 Our [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38169) is available on arXiv.
- [2026/09/29] 🚀 STEPQuant code is available in this repository.

evidence.heading: 👀 Overview
evidence.text:
**STEPQuant** compresses the persistent recurrent states of Delta-rule models. It decides **when** errors will last and **where** they will affect the output, then spends precision accordingly.


  


Fixed-size state per request still means growing memory under concurrency. Uniform low-bit quantization also feeds its errors into every subsequent state update.

evidence.heading: 🧩 Method
evidence.text:
- **When — lifetime-aware bit allocation:** Give more bits to state units with larger, longer-lived errors; protect a few high-risk units in FP16.
- **Where — key-row-aware dual-axis fitting:** Scale key rows and value columns separately, prioritizing rows that matter most to the readout.

Allocation is calibrated once; packed-state kernels and asynchronous writeback keep inference efficient.

evidence.heading: 📊 Results
evidence.text:
**Seven long-generation tasks · BF16 weights with quantized states · Average acc (%)**

| Model | FP32 | INT8 | INT6 | STEPQuant@6 | STEPQuant@4 |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| Qwen3.8-27B | 80.60 | 71.86 | 45.04 | **80.59** | **80.51** |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct | 61.52 | 56.02 | 45.70 | **61.47** | **58.52** |


  


In the paper's serving memory accounting, **STEPQuant@6** compresses recurrent-state memory by **5.03× / 5.08×** and reduces total memory by **68.7% / 53.7%** on Qwen / Kimi, respectively.

Paper-reported results. Memory accounting uses W4/AWQ weights and five prefix-state slots per request (Figure 3(c)). Full-model decode throughput uses BF16 weights, batches 32–512, and 128 prompt + 1024 decode tokens (Appendix F.5). Task evaluations use NVIDIA A800 GPUs. The 4/6-bit budgets are nominal; FP16 pivots and scales add storage.

evidence.heading: ⚙️ Quick Start
evidence.text:
Run from the repository root. The tested stack uses **SGLang 0.5.12**, **PyTorch 2.11.0**, and **Triton 3.7.1**. You need model checkpoints, a CUDA toolkit, and four GPUs for this Qwen example.

**1. Reuse environments and set `model_path` in [`configs/models.json`](configs/models.json).**

```bash
bash scripts/reuse_sglang_env.sh /path/to/sglang-env
bash scripts/reuse_eval_env.sh .venv-serving
bash scripts/reuse_calibration_env.sh /path/to/qwen-env qwen
```

If the serving helper prints an `export CUDA_HOME=...` command, run it.

**2. Calibrate once, then serve.**

```bash
.venv-eval/bin/python -m stepquant.reproduction \
  --models qwen --formats stepquant6 --devices 0,1,2,3

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 .venv-serving/bin/python -m stepquant.sglang \
  --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B --tp-size 4 \
  --state-format stepquant6 --plan artifacts/reproduction/plans/qwen-stepquant6.pt \
  --attention-backend triton --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --context-length 131072 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --served-model-name stepquant \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31080
```

**3. Evaluate.** Stop the manually launched server first; the evaluation suite starts its own.

```bash
.venv-eval/bin/python -m stepquant.evaluation.suite \
  --models qwen --benchmarks long --formats fp32 stepquant6 \
  --server-python .venv-serving/bin/python --devices 0,1,2,3 --tp 4
```

For Kimi setup, the zero-shot short-task protocol (2048 output tokens, thinking disabled), and paired FP32 decode benchmarks, see the [usage guide](REPRODUCTION.md).

evidence.heading: 📂 Contact
evidence.text:
If you have further questions, please open an issue or contact yaobingchen0515@gmail.com or xuhb2001@gmail.com.

Discussions and potential collaborations are also welcome.

kind_reason.text: Delta-rule 循环状态量化论文的官方代码。

summary.text: STEPQuant 根据误差持续时间和对输出的影响，为 Delta-rule 模型的循环状态分配量化精度，降低并发请求带来的状态内存需求。

value.text: 针对持续累积的循环状态误差保护高风险单元，改善统一低比特量化的精度损失。

audience.text: 研究循环模型压缩与大模型服务内存优化的研发人员。

outcome.text: 作者在七项长生成任务中报告状态压缩和准确率结果，测试采用 BF16 权重与量化状态。

mechanism.text: 按误差寿命分配位数并保留少数 FP16 单元，分别拟合 key 行与 value 列；一次校准后用打包状态内核和异步写回推理。

inspiration.text: 可尝试按误差传播寿命与读出敏感性分配精度，而非所有状态使用同样位宽。

limitations.text: 量化对象是循环状态，结果属于论文指定模型和服务内存口径，不能直接推广为任意模型权重压缩收益。

how_to.text: 准备指定 SGLang、PyTorch、Triton 和 CUDA 环境，配置模型路径并校准；Qwen 示例需要四张 GPU。

github_projects.description: Actell (执言) is an experimental AI agent for iPhone that understands the screen and performs actions via CoreDevice, using on-device loopback or an ESP32 relay. An early-stage, vibe-coded prototype for exploration and idea sharing.
github_projects.description_zh: Actell (执言) is an experimental AI agent for iPhone that understands the screen and performs actions via CoreDevice, using on-device loopback or an ESP32 relay. An early-stage, vibe-coded prototype for exploration and idea sharing.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Actell (执言) is an experimental AI agent for iPhone that understands the screen and performs actions via CoreDevice, using on-device loopback or an ESP32 relay. An early-stage, vibe-coded prototype for exploration and idea sharing.

evidence.heading: iPhone Use · Phone Agent · Actell
evidence.text:
English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**An early technical prototype built through vibe coding.** Actell explores an iPhone agent that captures the screen and sends touch input through CoreDevice. VPN loopback is the default route; ESP32 USB NCM (Network Control Model) is optional. Long-running background operation and production readiness are not guaranteed.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2aefc1a7-bdf1-42e7-83b9-51bd879256c8

evidence.heading: Capabilities
evidence.text:
- Conversations with configurable providers and models, streaming replies, readable reasoning supplied by providers, attachments and imported text skills.
- Screenshot, tap, drag and wait tools. Tool calls run in order; uncertain inputs are never automatically replayed. Ordinary chat does not require a device connection.
- VPN and NCM share an App-owned system pairing identity and CoreDevice backend. Controlled device tests have demonstrated screenshots and actual taps; complete tasks, drag and long-running background operation need separate acceptance.
- Optional audio, picture-in-picture and location background sources. New installations enable audio and residency; location and standby Live Activities start off. Saved choices remain effective, and system execution limits still apply.
- An optional [Muse companion interface](docs/muse-remote/README.md), with per-device permissions and a separate execution runtime. A general MCP service remains future work.

evidence.heading: Setup
evidence.text:
Use **Xcode 27 and iOS 27 or later**. Physical installation requires your own valid signing configuration. Configure a compatible provider and credentials for model tasks; screenshots and explicitly sent attachments are sent to that provider.

1. Enable Developer Mode and local network access. Complete the App's pairing flow in the system UI.
2. Prepare a matching Personalized Developer Disk Image, usually through Xcode. The backend checks availability; it does not download, personalize or mount images.
3. In Settings → Phone Control, select the connection route and open Connection & Validation:
   - [VPN loopback](coredevice/docs/LOCALDEVVPN.md), the default: enable an external VPN with local packet reinjection. Default interface/peer addresses are `10.7.1.1` / `10.7.0.1`; match your VPN configuration. The App does not manage the VPN. Use Wi-Fi when connecting; cellular operation and network switching have separate limitations.
   - [ESP32 NCM](devices/esp32/README.md): connect an ESP32-S3 with the current firmware through its native USB data port. Check the [hardware conditions](devices/esp32/docs/HARDWARE.md).
4. Add a provider, select a model and create a conversation. Control tools check connection and authorization when invoked; the route cannot change during execution.

VPN apps with built-in loopback can share the same connection with regular proxy traffic. Compatibility has been tested with LocalDevVPN, Shadowrocket and Clash; interface addresses and required settings vary. See the [route guide](coredevice/docs/LOCALDEVVPN.md).

evidence.heading: Build and test
evidence.text:
Install Rust with the `aarch64-apple-ios` and `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` targets. The backend uses a locked dependency graph; set `COREDEVICE_CARGO_OFFLINE=1` when the cache is complete. Xcode builds the corresponding Rust library automatically. See [App build instructions](ios-app/README.md) for signing overrides and dependency setup.

```sh
python3 ios-app/scripts/generate_xcode_project.py
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer xcodebuild \
  -project ios-app/PhoneAgent.xcodeproj -scheme PhoneAgent \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -derivedDataPath .build/DeviceBuild \
  -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath .build/SourcePackages CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build

# Optional ESP32 route; ESP-IDF 5.5.5 must be installed. Does not flash.
bash devices/esp32/tools/build.sh ncm

# Loopback protocol tests and isolated simulator tests
CC=clang bash devices/esp32/tools/test_usb.sh
SIMULATOR_ADHOC_SIGN=1 bash ios-app/scripts/test_core.sh <isolated-simulator-UDID>
```

Firmware outputs are in `.build/esp32-<mode>/`. App tests use synthetic providers and temporary storage; they do not replace device acceptance. Add `RUN_UI_TESTS=1` to include UI tests. Core protocol, authorization, isolation, unknown-result, migration and stop/release coverage stays in the default target.

evidence.heading: Muse companion
evidence.text:
Enable Muse Gadget Service, choose Add Muse, then Connect Actell on Muse and approve the incoming request. Pairing creates independent credentials; screenshot, app-list and control permissions can be changed per device. The service remembers its switch setting; unfinished pairing closes on backgrounding, while an existing listener still depends on system execution availability.

Pair on trusted Wi-Fi: first-use trust does not prevent an active LAN attacker; later connections pin the certificate and authenticate each client. Physical pairing has been observed, while complete model tasks and long-running behavior need separate acceptance. The Gadget code lives in [muse-gadget-actell-mods](https://github.com/ja1chen/muse-gadget-actell-mods).

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **Character Files**: Open a `.char` built in Omnichar Studio or Cloud
- **Reference Images**: One batch, or one per numbered slot, both from the same resolved set
- **Positions Kept**: Reference order is preserved, because a prompt addresses images by number
- **Conditioning**: Wire a CLIP to get conditioning straight out, or take the prompt as text
- **Trained LoRA**: Applied to MODEL and CLIP when the character carries one
- **Build Characters**: Encode face, body and wardrobe references into a new `.char`, three slots each
- **Voice**: Store a short voice clip in the character and send it to MiniMax H3 when the prompt has dialogue
- **Python Library**: Omnichar's standalone package for `.char` integration, no dependencies

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
- ComfyUI
- Python 3.10+
- `omnichar-sdk` (installed from `requirements.txt`)

evidence.heading: Installation
evidence.text:
1. Go to your ComfyUI custom nodes directory:
   ```bash
   cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
   ```

2. Clone this repository:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/omnichar/ComfyUI-Omnichar
   cd ComfyUI-Omnichar
   ```

3. Install the reader:
   ```bash
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

4. Restart ComfyUI

evidence.heading: Where Characters Live
evidence.text:
Put `.char` files in `ComfyUI/models/characters/`. The loader lists whatever is there.

To share one folder with Omnichar Studio, set `INLINE_CHARACTERS_DIR` to its characters directory
and both read the same files.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
Ahenk Cep, on a CPU:

```bash
pip install torch ema-lightning==1.1.2 "git+https://github.com/ozguradmin/ahenk-turkish-tts"
```

```python
import sys
import soundfile as sf
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

d = snapshot_download("ozgurguler/ahenk-cep-tr", allow_patterns=["*.pt", "ahenk_cep.py"])
sys.path.insert(0, d)
from ahenk_cep import AhenkCep

tts = AhenkCep(f"{d}/student.pt", f"{d}/decoder.pt")
audio, sr = tts.say("Randevunuz 14.10.2026 saat 09:30'da; ücret 1.250 TL.")
sf.write("randevu.wav", audio, sr)
```

Setup and emotions for Ahenk (GPU, VoxCPM2) are in its [model card](https://huggingface.co/ozgurguler/ahenk-tts-tr). To try it without a GPU, use the [Hugging Face demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ozgurguler/ahenk-turkish-tts).
Text normalisation only:

```bash
trnorm "Saat 09:30'da 3. kata gelin, ücret 1.250,50 TL."
# Saat dokuz otuzda üçüncü kata gelin, ücret bin iki yüz elli lira elli kuruş.
```

trnorm's rules and examples: [docs/TRNORM.md](docs/TRNORM.md).

evidence.heading: Results
evidence.text:
TR-Zor: 155 hard sentences. Held-out: 20 long sentences (12-19 s) of the Antalia dataset, not in the training data of
any of our models. Judge: faster-whisper large-v3-turbo; reference and output normalised with
`trnorm.normalize_for_eval`. WER %, lower is better; in brackets, the number of sentences without a single word
error. UTMOS22 predicts naturalness (1-5, higher is better).

| Model | Size | TR-Zor WER | Held-out WER | UTMOS TR-Zor / held-out |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Ahenk** | 2B + LoRA | 2.54 (141/155) | 0.82 (16/20) | 3.70 / 3.14 |
| [Trendyol-TTS](https://huggingface.co/Trendyol/Trendyol-TTS) | 2B + LoRA | 3.98 (134/155) | **0.68** (16/20) | **3.82 / 3.73** |
| **Ahenk Cep** | 8.6M | **2.32** (144/155) | 0.95 (17/20) | 3.44 / 3.18 |
| [EMA Lightning](https://huggingface.co/canberkkkkkk/ema-lightning) + trnorm | 8.6M | 2.43 (145/155) | 1.49 (16/20) | 3.36 / 2.95 |
| [Antalia-2 Mini](https://huggingface.co/cloud0day3/antalia-mini) | 7.6M | 3.30 (140/155) | 1.22 (16/20) | 3.23 / 2.94 |

- Ahenk and Trendyol-TTS were measured on an A100, the small models on a laptop GPU, with the same judge. Scored again
  on the second setup, Ahenk's clips came out the same within 0.01.
- **Where we lose:** Trendyol-TTS is ahead on predicted naturalness, most on long sentences (3.73 vs 3.14); it has a
  lower WER on the held-out sentences (0.68 vs 0.82) and is faster (RTF 1.37 vs 2.28 on an A100). Trendyol speaks in
  its own voice; part of the difference may come from the voice. On CPU, Ahenk Cep is slower than EMA and Antalia
  (RTF 0.20 vs 0.13 and 0.08 on 2 threads).
- trnorm's effect: EMA Lightning's TR-Zor error is 14.0 % with its own front-end and 1.9 % with trnorm (this row was
  measured on CPU with an int8 judge, do not compare it directly with the table above;

evidence.heading: Limitations
evidence.text:
- **Questions that should rise at the end do not:** questions without "mı", such as "Yarın geliyorsun?", end like a
  statement, in both models. Questions built with "mı" are right.
- **"c" after an English instruction:** in Ahenk a leading "c" may be read like /k/, /s/ or /z/ ("Cam" → "Kam").
  `instruction_pick` switches to a Turkish instruction; if needed, use `prefer="tr"`.
- **"Phone-like" timbre:** in some of Ahenk's emotional clips the voice is bright and crackly (7 of 20 clips in a probe
  with English instructions). Try another seed.
- **Breath in pauses:** stays in Ahenk; `pause_clean` in the package turns it down.
- **Ahenk Cep's styles are weak:** "sad" is only 1.9 semitones lower and 8 % slower; no laughter. Not yet distilled
  for phone speed.
- **Ahenk needs a GPU:** RTF 2.28 at 16 steps on an A100, slower than real time.
- **One voice, Turkish only.** trnorm leaves foreign names that are not in its lexicon as written.

evidence.heading: Responsible use
evidence.text:
- Do not present generated speech as a real human recording; say that it is synthetic and, if you can, add a
  machine-readable mark (EU AI Act Art. 50). The models have no watermark; [AudioSeal](https://github.com/facebookresearch/audioseal)
  can be added.
- Do not impersonate anyone. VoxCPM2 can clone voices; do not clone anyone's voice without their consent.
- Do not present generated anger, sadness or warmth as a real person's reaction to put pressure on a listener.
- Do not use it for fraud, social engineering or robocalls.

**The Agentic-Native Operating System**

An operating system written in Rust, with a voice agent built into the system.

[](LICENSE)

[Screenshots](#screenshots) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Make an app agentic](#make-an-app-agentic) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Documentation](#documentation)



[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gXIS-6cVNAk)

Say *"Hey Veda, switch my wallpaper to the dunes"* and it is done. The agent
works in every application through the same code as your keyboard and
mouse, and asks you before anything that is hard to undo. Everything here
is Rust, from the UEFI bootloader and the microkernel to the window system
and the applications.


  
    An agent in the systemA service from boot that wakes when you say its name. Its model, its voice and even its name are settings.

    A microkernel in RustCapabilities, SMP, and services in user space that restart by themselves. Applications get Rust's standard library.
    Linux's drivers, containedLinux drives the hardware in a VM on Veda's own hypervisor, held in by the IOMMU and restarted if it crashes.
    A complete desktopA compositing window system, a lock screen, a web browser on WebKit, OpenGL ES 3.0, GCC in the Terminal, WPA3 Wi-Fi and a firewall that asks first.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
Veda builds on an x86-64 Linux machine with KVM. Install
[Rust](https://rustup.rs) and the build tools:


Packages on Debian and Ubuntu

```bash
sudo apt install qemu-system-x86 qemu-system-gui qemu-system-modules-opengl ovmf \
  build-essential bc curl rsync m4 flex bison meson ninja-build cmake nasm \
  libgmp-dev libmpfr-dev libmpc-dev python3 python3-mako python3-packaging
```

The driver VM also needs KVM's nested virtualization (`kvm_intel nested=1`).



Then build Veda and boot it:

```bash
cargo automation doctor      # check the tools
cargo automation toolchain   # once, about half an hour: GCC, musl and Rust for Veda
cargo automation linux       # once: the driver VM's Linux and Mesa
cargo automation web         # once, an hour or more (optional): WebKit, for the browser
cargo automation run         # build Veda and boot it in QEMU
```

Add a [Deepgram](https://deepgram.com) API key in **Settings → Agent**, then
say **"Hey Veda"**, click the ring on the taskbar or press **Super+Space**.
Try *"Play Neon Horizon"*, *"Show me the lighthouse photo, full screen"* or
*"Delete the City Lights photo"* (it asks you first).

**On a PC:** `cargo automation iso` writes a live system for a USB stick.
Start it in UEFI mode, with VT-x and VT-d on and Secure Boot off. It runs
from memory and leaves the PC's disks alone; see
[what it supports](documentation/DRIVERVM.md#status).

evidence.heading: Make an app agentic
Architecture
evidence.text:
| Layer | What it is |
|-------|------------|
| **Kernel** | A capability-based microkernel: isolation, scheduling, memory and IPC, on SMP with tickless timers |
| **Services** | Drivers, the file system, the window system, audio, networking and the agent, in user space; `init` restarts them if they fail |
| **Drivers** | Veda drives its own disks; Linux drives the rest in the [driver VM](documentation/DRIVERVM.md), on Veda's hypervisor |
| **Graphics** | A compositing window system, the immediate-mode `ui` toolkit, and OpenGL ES 3.0 on the GPU through Mesa or in software |
| **Programs** | Rust's standard library, and C with GCC 16 and musl, over `posix`, a POSIX layer in Rust |
| **Network** | IPv4 and IPv6, TLS 1.3, WPA3 Wi-Fi, and a firewall in stealth mode by default |

Where a proven library exists, Veda uses it: smoltcp, rustls, RustCrypto,
FFmpeg, dav1d, glam, WPE WebKit and [more](documentation/DEPENDENCIES.md).

evidence.heading: Testing
evidence.text:
```bash
cargo automation test        # unit tests on the host, then integration tests inside Veda
cargo automation test --ui   # plus the GUI and agent scripts
```

The scripts click through the desktop and the applications, and break
things on purpose (Linux's drivers crash, a cable is pulled, services are
killed) to check that Veda recovers by itself. The agent's scripts talk to
a stand-in for Deepgram, so they are offline, deterministic and free.

evidence.heading: 🔍 Introduction
evidence.text:
Understanding visual evolution is essential for autoregressive video generation and world modeling.
Yet temporal redundancy can encourage local temporal shortcuts during teacher-forcing training, weakening the incentive to learn underlying dynamics.
To address this challenge, we introduce ***Future Chunk Prediction (FCP)***, which trains autoregressive video models to look ahead through auxiliary branches that predict temporally distant video chunks from intermediate features of the current chunk.
Using ***only video-pixel supervision, FCP improves physical consistency in generated videos and learns more semantically structured representations***.

We provide training and inference code, along with weights for 1.3B and 5B autoregressive text-and-image-to-video (TI2V) models. Stay tuned for more model sizes and variants.

evidence.heading: papercut-explainer
evidence.text:
Make short vertical explainer reels that look like layered construction paper, with the coding agent you already use doing the work: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and any other tool that reads Agent Skills.



*The bundled example reel ([`examples/hello-reel`](examples/hello-reel)), rendered from this repo. Silent placeholder voice, real captions, camera and cuts.*

This repo is two things that work together:

- **Nine agent skills** (the open `SKILL.md` format, so they load in most coding agents; see [Works with](#works-with)) that run the whole pipeline: strategy, hook, script, storyboard, voice, build, QA, and an installer. Ask for a reel, or run one stage on its own.
- **A Remotion library** the skills build on: a paper-cut component kit, 24 backdrops, 17 camera moves, 10 scene transitions, film-look layers, 79 sound effects and 8 music beds, plus the scripts that tie them into an episode.

You describe the video ("explain this repo in 25 seconds"). The skills research it, write a script on a fixed spoken spine, plan every camera move and cut, make or fake the voiceover, and build the scenes in Remotion. You review stills and the final cut.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
You need Node 20+, npm, ffmpeg, rsync and Python 3. Any coding agent in [Works with](#works-with) is the front end.

**With `npx skills`** (skills only, fastest):

```bash
npx skills add 0xS4N4TG/papercut-explainer
```

This installs the nine skills into your agents' skill folders (the CLI supports about 80 agents). It does not fetch the Remotion library or the scripts. Open your agent and say "set up papercut-explainer": `papercut-setup` clones the repo, asks how much you want (Minimal, Standard, Full) and installs it. Add `-g` for a user-wide install, `--skill papercut-hook` to take one skill.

**With git** (everything, including the library):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/0xS4N4TG/papercut-explainer
cd papercut-explainer
./install.sh
```

The installer asks how much you want to set up and does only that.

| Mode | What you get | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Minimal** | The skills, the scene-builder subagent and the config file. Strategy, hook, script, storyboard and style prompts work. Nothing renders. | seconds |

evidence.heading: Use it
evidence.text:
Open your agent in any folder you want the episode to live in and ask for a reel:

> Make a papercut explainer about https://github.com/example/echolark. 25 seconds, comment keyword PAPER.

The `papercut-explainer` skill takes the lead. It asks only for what is missing (the one claim the video proves, the audience level, what a commenter gets), then walks the stages below, handing each to its skill. Every stage writes a file, so you can stop, edit and resume.

You can also call one stage directly:

| Say | Skill | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| "set up papercut-explainer", "check my install" | `papercut-setup` | installed components, a `--doctor` report with the install level |
| "what should this reel be about? what format?" | `papercut-strategy` | the BRIEF block at the top of `research/facts.md`: topic, familiar format, audience, funnel |
| "write 5 hooks for this fact list" | `papercut-hook` | the HOOK block (SAY / WRITE / SHOW / ALIGN) at the top of `papercut/STORYBOARD.md` |
| "script this", "write the banner track" | `papercut-script` | `research/facts.md`, `narration/script.json`, the staging table (banner, set and gag per beat) in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| "storyboard this script" | `papercut-storyboard` | the camera and cut table, frame-level scene blocks and SFX plan in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| "set up the voice", "re-voice with another speaker" | `papercut-voice` | `narration/voice/`, `public/vo/captions.json`, `src/plan.json` |
| "scaffold the episode", "build scenes S03 to S06", "render it" | `papercut-build` | the project, `episode.json`, scenes, SFX cues, audio, `out/<name>.mp4` |
| "QA the reel", "check the stills" | `papercut-qa` | contact sheets, a pass/fail checklist, fixes |

Run modes the router offers at the start: full reel, script only, storyboard from a script

evidence.heading: What works in which install mode
evidence.text:
| Stage | Minimal | Standard | Full |
|---|---|---|---|
| Strategy, hook, script, storyboard, style prompts | yes | yes | yes |
| Scaffold, build scenes, SFX and music, stills QA, render to mp4 | no | yes, placeholder voice | yes |
| Voiceover from text, word-timed captions from real audio | no | placeholder timing only | yes |

If a stage needs more than you installed, the skill says so in one line and hands over to `papercut-setup` rather than improvising.

evidence.heading: How the workflow runs
evidence.text:
```
 idea or link
     │
     ▼
 papercut-strategy ──► BRIEF            topic, "what show is this secretly?", audience, funnel
     │                 (top of research/facts.md)
     ▼
 papercut-hook ──────► HOOK block       SAY / WRITE / SHOW / ALIGN, tested before any scene exists
     │                 (top of papercut/STORYBOARD.md)
     ▼
 papercut-script ────► facts.md         every number traces to a sourced fact
     │                 script.json      75-95 words on a 10-beat spine
     │                 staging table    one visual-pun set per banner, one gag each
     ▼
 papercut-storyboard ► STORYBOARD.md    camera and cut table, frame-level events, SFX plan
     │
     ▼
 papercut-build ─────► project          scaffold from the template, episode.json
     │
     ▼
 papercut-voice ─────► voiceover.wav    local TTS, your own recording, or a placeholder
     │                 captions.json    word timings
     │                 plan.json        scene boundaries on word onsets
     ▼
 papercut-build ─────► scenes, audio, mp4    scene agents in parallel, cached renders
     │
     ▼
 papercut-qa ────────► stills + checklist, then fixes
```


The style has three tracks per beat: the voiceover tells the story, a taped banner states one hard fact the voiceover does not repeat, and a fresh paper set acts out the voiceover's concrete noun. Everything is paper (grain, rough cut edge, drop shadow, stacked shading), the camera moves through a diorama, and only the banner and labels boil in steps. The full rules live in [`skills/papercut-explainer/references/style-guide.md`](skills/papercut-explainer/references/style-guide.md).

State lives in files, not chat, so every stage can run in a fresh session. A series folder looks like this:

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
| | |
|---|---|
| OS | macOS (tested) or Linux (scripts are bash; not run end to end). Windows: use WSL. |
| Node, npm | Node 20+ |
| ffmpeg | 4.4+ on `PATH` |
| rubberband | only if you set a voice `tempo` other than 1.0 (`brew install rubberband`) |
| rsync | on `PATH` (kit sync) |
| Python | 3.9+ for the tools; 3.10–3.12 for the voice venv (the installer uses `uv` if you have it, else `python3.12`/`3.11`/`3.10`) |
| Chrome or Chromium | for the SFX and music render only (`CHROME_PATH` to override). Video renders use Remotion's own headless browser, downloaded on first render. |
| Disk | about 0.7 GB per project for `node_modules` (shared by APFS cloning on macOS; plain copy elsewhere, or set `DONOR`); 4–6 GB for local voice |
| A coding agent | any in [Works with](#works-with); the installer finds the ones you have (`--target`) |

evidence.heading: Limits
evidence.text:
- Written and run end to end on macOS (Apple Silicon). The CUDA and faster-whisper paths exist but were not run on real hardware.
- The voice pipeline is optional and the least tested part.
- `render.py` writes ProRes intermediates, several GB per episode in `out/cache`.
- Two-speaker dialogue helpers ship (`dialogue_timeline.py`, `SPEAKER`/`ROLE` options) with no template.
- The base `Critter` is a boxy creature with four leg stubs and two tall eyes. Swap its drawing in `kit/cast/Critter.tsx` if you want your own mascot.

evidence.heading: English Practice — Yerel İngilizce Pratik Uygulaması
evidence.text:
Tamamen ücretsiz, çevrimdışı ve **taşınabilir** İngilizce konuşma/yazma pratiği uygulaması.
Her şey (Python, Ollama, modeller, veriler) bu klasörün içindedir; sisteme hiçbir şey kurulmaz.

Türkçe konuşan, özellikle çalışan yetişkinler için: yerel bir yapay zekâyla sesli ya da yazılı İngilizce sohbet ve anında
düzeltme; A1–C1 dersler ve seviye sınavları; Türkçe anlatan sesli bir öğretmen; senaryolar (rol yapma), yazma
değerlendirmesi; Kelime Çalış (seviye listeleri ve en sık 3000 kelime), kelime defteri ve aralıklı tekrar; iş ve
günlük hayat kalıpları; YDS tarzı süreli testler; ilerleme takibi; iki bilgisayar arasında eşitleme.
Windows 10/11 ve Linux'ta çalışır. Kurulumdan sonra internet gerekmez; verileriniz bilgisayarınızdan çıkmaz.

Kullanılan bütün yazılım, model ve içerik kaynakları lisanslarıyla birlikte:
[Kaynaklar, lisanslar ve teşekkürler](#kaynaklar-lisanslar-ve-teşekkürler).

evidence.heading: Kurulum
evidence.text:
**`Kurulum.bat`'a çift tıklayın** — başka hiçbir şey kurmanız gerekmez (yönetici izni de istenmez).

1. Kısa bir hazırlık: Windows / klasör yolu / internet / disk kontrolü, gömülü Python (~11 MB).
2. Tarayıcıda **kurulum sihirbazı** açılır:
   - **Donanım taraması** (işlemci, RAM, ekran kartı ve VRAM, disk, hızlandırma türü),
   - **Dil modeli seçimi**: her model için bu bilgisayara uygunluk rozeti
     (✓ Önerilir / ✓ Uygun / ⚠ Yavaş olabilir / ✗ Sığmaz), gerçek indirme boyutu, kalite ve hız.
     Bilgisayarınızda başka bir Ollama'nın indirdiği modeller varsa **kopyalanır**, tekrar indirilmez.
   - **Ses**: Whisper modeli ve nerede çalışacağı, Kokoro aksanı ve sesi,
   - **Ek bileşenler**: çevrimdışı sözlük (önerilen), TranslateGemma (cümle çevirisi, isteğe bağlı),
     masaüstü kısayolu (izninizle — sisteme yazılan tek şey),
   - **Özet** (toplam indirme, disk, süre) → **Kur**: her bileşen için ilerleme çubuğu, hız ve kalan süre.
     İndirmeler yarıda kalırsa kaldığı yerden devam eder; sihirbaz kapanırsa yeniden açtığınızda
     **"Kaldığı yerden devam et"** çıkar. Bir bileşen kurulamazsa diğerleri devam eder.
   - **Test**: her dil modelinin hızı (token/sn, ilk kelime süresi), konuşma tanıma ve ses gerçek
     örnekle denenir; yavaşsa daha hızlı bir model önerilir ve varsayılan buradan değiştirilebilir.
3. **Klasörü başka bilgisayara taşıdığınızda** (ör. harici disk ile laptop) `Baslat.bat` bunu fark eder ve
   sihirbazı **"Yeni bilgisayar"** modunda açar: sadece model ve ses seçimi + hız testi; klasördeki
   modeller tekrar indirilmez. Her bilgisayar kendi varsayılan modelini hatırlar.
4. Kurulumdan sonra `Kurulum.bat` **bakım modunda** açılır: model ekle / sil / varsayılan yap, onar
   (eksik/bozuk dosyaları yeniden indirir), güncelle (Ollama + paketler), donanımı

evidence.heading: Linux'ta kurulum
evidence.text:
Linux'ta da aynı uygulama çalışır; yine her şey bu klasöre iner, sisteme bir şey kurulmaz, `sudo` gerekmez.

- **Gerekenler:** 64 bit (x86_64) Linux, glibc 2.28 ve sonrası (Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+, Fedora 29+ …),
  `curl` ya da `wget`, en az 15 GB boş alan. NVIDIA ekran kartında sürücü kurulu olmalı (`nvidia-smi`
  çalışıyorsa tamam); AMD kartlar için Ollama'nın ROCm paketi de iner. Uygulama penceresi için Chrome,
  Chromium, Edge ya da Brave varsa onunla açılır (sekmesiz pencere); yoksa varsayılan tarayıcıda.
- **Kurulum:** klasörü örneğin `~/EnglishPractice` gibi Türkçe karakter ve boşluk içermeyen bir yere koyup

  aynı kurulum sihirbazı tarayıcıda açılır. "Ek bileşenler"de kısayol seçilirse uygulama menüsüne ve

- **Açmak:** `bash baslat.sh` (ya da menüdeki kısayol: bir terminal açar). Kapatmak için o terminalde

evidence.heading: Kullanım
evidence.text:
**`Baslat.bat`'a çift tıklayın.** Uygulama içindeki Ollama'yı başlatır, modeli belleğe yükler ve
uygulamayı **kendi penceresinde** açar (Edge'in uygulama penceresi — sekme ve adres çubuğu yok; Edge yoksa
Chrome, ikisi de yoksa varsayılan tarayıcı). Pencereyi kapatınca uygulama arkada çalışmaya devam eder;
`Baslat.bat`'a tekrar tıklamak pencereyi yeniden açar. Tamamen kapatmak için konsol penceresinde `Ctrl+C`
veya konsol penceresini kapatın — Ollama da otomatik kapanır.

> Mikrofon izni için adres `http://localhost:…` olmalı (IP adresiyle değil).

evidence.heading: Konuşma
evidence.text:
- 🎤 butonuna **basılı tutup** konuşun, bırakınca gönderilir. Ayarlar'dan "Tıkla-başlat / tıkla-bitir"
  moduna geçebilirsiniz.
- Klavye: metin kutusu dışındayken **Boşluk** tuşu aynı işi görür.
- İlk kullanımda tarayıcı mikrofon izni ister. Mikrofon 2 dakika kullanılmazsa kapatılır.
- Konuşma tanıma (Whisper) dili İngilizce'ye sabittir; hatalarınız düzeltilmeden yazıya dökülür,
  düzeltmeler sağdaki panelde gösterilir (aşağıya bakın).
- Ayarlar'dan farklı bir Whisper modeli seçilirse ilk seferde internetten indirilir (`models/stt/`).
- **Telaffuz göstergesi:** Whisper'ın net anlayamadığı kelimeler (güven < %60) mesajınızda **sarı**
  işaretlenir. Tıklayınca doğru telaffuz çalınır ve kelime penceresi açılır. Bu kaba bir göstergedir,
  tam telaffuz analizi değil: hızlı söylenen kısa kelimeler ve isimler de işaretlenebilir.
  Geçmiş oturumlarda da görünür.
- Yapay zeka **sesli cevap verir**; cevap cümle cümle seslendirildiği için ilk cümle ~1 saniyede başlar.
  - **⏹ Durdur**: sesi keser. Konuşmaya başlamak (🎤 / Boşluk) da sesi otomatik keser.
  - **🔊** (her cevabın yanında): tekrar dinle.
  - **🌐** (her mesajın yanında — seninkiler de): cümlenin tamamının Türkçesini mesajın içinde gösterir;
    tekrar basınca gizler. Yapay zeka çevirisidir, küçük hatalar olabilir. Derslerdeki sorularda da var.
  - **🔊 Sesli cevap** düğmesi: sadece yazılı cevap istiyorsanız kapatın.
  - **🙈 Altyazı gizli**: cevap metni bulanıklaşır, önce dinleyerek anlamaya çalışın; görmek için cevaba tıklayın.
- Ses, aksan (Amerikan/İngiliz) ve konuşma hızı (0.7x–1.2x) Ayarlar'dan seçilir; "▶ Dinle" ile deneyin.

evidence.heading: Düzeltmeler
evidence.text:
- Her cümlenizden sonra, cevap verildikten birkaç saniye sonra sağ panelde düzeltme kartı belirir:
  değişen kelimeler renkli (kırmızı: yanlış, yeşil: doğru), hata türü etiketi, kısa açıklama ve
  varsa **💡 daha doğal** bir söyleyiş. Hata yoksa **Perfect! ✓**.
- Mesajınızın köşesindeki **⚠ 2** / **✓** rozetine tıklayınca ilgili kart vurgulanır
  (dar ekranda panel yandan açılır).
- Düzeltmeler sohbeti yavaşlatmaz: sohbet cevabı her zaman önce üretilir.
- Açıklama dili (Türkçe/İngilizce) ve düzeltme modu (her mesajda / oturum sonunda / kapalı) Ayarlar'dan.
- Hata türleri sabit bir listeden seçilir (`app/backend/errors.py`): Zaman, Fiil yapısı,
  Özne-yüklem uyumu, Tanımlık, Edat, Zamir, Çoğul, Kelime sırası, Kelime seçimi, Eksik kelime,
  Fazla kelime, Yazım, Noktalama, Diğer. İstatistikler ve ileride dersler bu listeye dayanır.

evidence.heading: Dersler
evidence.text:
- **📘 Dersler**: seviyelere göre (A1–C1) konu anlatımı. Hazır: **A1 (10 ders), A2 (10), B1 (12), B2 (10), C1 (8)**. Her seviyede **💼 iş İngilizcesi** dersleri var (işini tanıtmak, iletişim bilgisi,
  iş e-postası, telefon, toplantı, iş görüşmesi) ve her derste **💼 İş hayatında** bölümü.
- Her dersin sonunda **📚 Kaynaklar**: anlatımın dayandığı güvenilir ücretsiz sayfalar (British Council
  LearnEnglish, Cambridge Dictionary Grammar) — hepsi tek tek açılıp doğrulandı.
- Her derste: ayrıntılı Türkçe anlatım (4–6 bölüm: yapı tabloları, ne zaman kullanılır, sinyal kelimeler,
  Türkçeden farkı ve sık karıştırılanlar, 💼 iş hayatında), 15–25 🔊 dinlenebilen örnek, **Türklerin sık yaptığı
  hatalar**, anında kontrol edilen ~23 **alıştırma** (%80 doğruyla ders tamamlanır): seçmeli, boşluk doldurma,
  düzelt, **dönüştür** (ör. olumsuz yap), **kelimeleri sırala**, **eşleştir**, **dinle-yaz**; **✍️ Kendi cümlelerini kur**
  (yapay zeka soru sorar, cevabın düzeltme motoruyla kontrol edilir) ve **🗣 Konuşarak pratik**
  (konuya odaklı sohbet + rapor).
- **📝 Yazılı göster:** dinleme alıştırmalarında (ders "Dinle ve yaz", Kelime Çalış "Dinle ve kelimeyi yaz")
  🔊'nin yanındaki 📝 duyulan metni gösterir, ikinci tıklama gizler. Sınavlarda yoktur.
- **Çalışman kaybolmaz:** ders sayfasındaki cevapların, yazıp henüz göndermediğin metinler ve
  **Kendi cümlelerini kur**'daki sorular, cevaplar ve sonuçlar sen silene kadar saklanır (🗑 tek tek ya da
  **🗑 Tümünü sil**; alıştırmalar için **↻ Tekrar çöz**). Başka sayfaya gidip dönünce ya da uygulamayı yeniden
  açınca her sayfa kaldığın yerden (kaydırma konumu dahil) açılır.
- **🗓 Ders tekrarı (aralıklı tekrar):** bitirdiğin her ders, unutmadan tekrar edebilmen için giderek uzayan
  aralıklarla geri gelir: 1 gün → 3 gün → 1 hafta → 2 hafta → 1 ay →

evidence.heading: 校园知识服务 Agent 智能体平台
evidence.text:
基于 **Python / FastAPI / SQLAlchemy / Ollama / Qwen3** 搭建的校园知识服务应用，围绕公开通知、竞赛、学籍及办事资料，实现从资料采集、附件解析到检索问答、证据溯源与人工审核的完整业务链路。

项目采用 **RAG（Retrieval-Augmented Generation，检索增强生成）** 和证据约束工作流：先限定事项、年度及可见范围，再检索原文、组织回答并返回来源。这里的 Agent 指知识服务工作流；当前实现以检索、规则校验和模型调用协作为主。

**在线演示：** [zlyb.cloud](https://zlyb.cloud)（私人测试入口，需登录，依赖本机服务在线）。

evidence.heading: 业务问题与解决方案
evidence.text:
| 业务问题 | 实现方案 | 主要代码 |
|---|---|---|
| 官网通知分散、附件格式不一致 | 公开站点归档、附件关联、PDF / Word / 表格解析与本地 OCR | [`school_archive.py`](app/school_archive.py)、[`ingest.py`](app/ingest.py) |
| 相似政策跨年度混用 | 年份、学期、版本及文档身份约束；区分发布日与适用年度 | [`semester.py`](app/semester.py)、[`source_versions.py`](app/source_versions.py) |
| 模型回答缺少可复核依据 | 原文证据窗口、选证核验、出处定位与版本提示 | [`evidence_windows.py`](app/evidence_windows.py)、[`model_evidence.py`](app/model_evidence.py) |
| 追问丢失事项或条件 | 有界多轮语境、话题切换、年份与条件继承 | [`conversation.py`](app/conversation.py)、[`campus_qa.py`](app/campus_qa.py) |
| 候选字段被误当正式政策 | Human-in-the-loop：字段核对、待核实状态、审核发布与撤回 | [`main.py`](app/main.py)、[`model.py`](app/model.py) |
| 重复通知与中断处理 | 重复通知归并、来源关系保留、解析诊断与恢复工具 | [`duplicate_notices.py`](app/duplicate_notices.py)、[`parse_diagnostics.py`](app/parse_diagnostics.py) |

evidence.heading: 系统架构
evidence.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[官网公开页面与附件] --> B[采集归档与格式解析]
    B --> C[文档 / 切片 / 版本 / 来源关系]
    C --> D[范围过滤与证据检索]
    Q[用户问题与多轮语境] --> D
    D --> E[规则校验与本地模型调用]
    E --> F[回答 / 原文片段 / 来源链接]
    C --> G[教师字段审核与发布]
    G --> D
```

- **API 与应用层：** FastAPI 提供问答、资料筛选、解析和管理入口；SQLAlchemy 管理文档、切片、赛事与审核状态。展示副本默认 SQLite，开发环境也实际使用过 PostgreSQL。
- **知识处理层：** 保留页面与附件的父子关系、内容位置、日期及版本；PDF 表格与 OCR 采用专门解析逻辑，避免只以扁平文本解释结构化资料。
- **检索与生成层：** 关键词、标题权重、文档范围及年度过滤共同参与召回；受限赛事范围可结合已有向量。全库语义索引属于可选试验能力，`CAMPUS_SEMANTIC_SEARCH` 默认关闭，不能据此宣称全库已完成向量化。
- **证据治理层：** 通过 Evidence Grounding（证据约束）、Provenance（来源追踪）与 Temporal Scoping（时间范围限定），处理无依据补全、旧政策误用和来源失效问题。多轮历史只帮助理解问题，不作为政策证据。
- **联网补充：** 公开搜索与官方目录发现并行处理，读取匹配事项的官方正文；有界 TTL 缓存与同键并发合并减少重复访问，返回前仍检查资料公开状态和来源关系。

evidence.heading: 技术栈与工程设计
evidence.text:
| 层次 | 技术与职责 |
|---|---|
| 服务端 | Python、FastAPI、Uvicorn、SQLAlchemy、HTTPX |
| 文档处理 | pypdf、pdfplumber、python-docx、OpenPyXL、RapidOCR |
| 模型运行 | Ollama、Qwen3、本地生成及嵌入接口 |
| 数据持久化 | SQLite 默认演示库；PostgreSQL 开发与恢复验证 |
| 交互层 | 原生 HTML / CSS / JavaScript，学生问答与教师管理页面 |
| 运维实践 | 解析恢复、来源核验、备份恢复；私人测试采用 Nginx / HTTPS 与受限 SSH 隧道 |

Dify / Docker 属于原开发环境已有集成实践；本仓库不打包 Dify 全栈、生产数据或个人网关配置。公网入口连接本机应用，模型和业务库仍依赖电脑在线。

evidence.heading: 本地运行
evidence.text:
以下命令为 **Windows PowerShell**，在项目根目录执行。开发环境使用 Python 3.12；需可用的 Ollama 及相应模型资源。

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
ollama pull qwen3:8b
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8008
```

打开 `http://127.0.0.1:8008`。首次启动为空库，需自行导入公开资料；管理端随机口令首次生成于 `.secrets/admin-password.txt`，仅在本机读取。受限语义检索需另行准备 `qwen3-embedding:0.6b` 及对应索引。

| 环境变量 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `CAMPUS_DATA` | 独立数据目录 |
| `DATABASE_URL` | SQLAlchemy 数据库连接，未配置时使用本地 SQLite |
| `OLLAMA_URL` | Ollama 服务地址，默认本机 11434 |
| `CHAT_MODEL` / `EMBED_MODEL` | 生成模型与嵌入模型名称 |
| `CAMPUS_SEMANTIC_SEARCH` | 全库语义索引试验开关，默认 `0` |

evidence.heading: 验证、数据范围与项目状态
evidence.text:
2026-10-15 核对时，本仓库发布范围内的应用、测试与工具代码已与当前主工作目录一致。源码同步清单见 [`SOURCE_INVENTORY.json`](SOURCE_INVENTORY.json)，检查说明见 [`VALIDATION.md`](VALIDATION.md)。

证据逻辑可在独立数据库与临时目录中运行：

```powershell
python -m pytest tests/test_model_evidence.py tests/test_evidence_windows.py -q
```

历史检索与数据库恢复记录保留在 [`validation/historical-summary.json`](validation/historical-summary.json)，标明日期、统计口径与原报告哈希。开发回归、检索召回和有限来源核对不等于总体回答准确率。

当前仓库可用于代码审阅和独立部署验证。公开待审核资料不等于教师认定的正式政策；项目不是学校官方服务，未接入学校统一身份认证。数据库、官网原件归档、模型权重、账号口令和个人服务器配置不随源码发布。

evidence.heading: FrameWeaver
evidence.text:
**A local video workspace for scenes, narration, audio, and timeline editing.**

FrameWeaver brings a React dashboard, Python backend, and Chrome extension into
one workflow. Plan scenes, reuse character references, generate through your own
Google Flow session, prepare narration, and assemble clips with FFmpeg.

Developed and maintained by [phucnguyentvp1](https://github.com/phucnguyentvp1),
FrameWeaver combines scene production with a broader editing workspace: layered
timelines, media libraries, speech analysis, narration, subtitles, and saved exports.
The project is currently available as a preview release.

evidence.heading: 1. Install the prerequisites
evidence.text:
The packaging checks used **Python 3.12** and **Node.js 24**. You also need Chrome,
FFmpeg, and ffprobe. Install those tools before proceeding.

The commands below assume macOS or a Linux shell. Windows users can adapt them
with WSL; a full Windows setup has not been verified for this preview.

evidence.heading: 2. Clone and install the backend
evidence.text:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/phucnguyentvp1/frameweaver.git
cd frameweaver
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env
```

Create a project in the Google Flow interface. Copy its UUID from the project URL
and set `FLOW_PROJECT_ID` in `.env`. Use your own credentials for any optional
providers you enable.

```sh
set -a
source .env
set +a
python -m agent.main
```

The backend reads shell environment variables; it does **not** load `.env`
automatically. Leave this terminal running.

evidence.heading: A typical workflow
evidence.text:
1. Create a local project and link your Google Flow project.
2. Define recurring characters, locations, and props; generate all references first.
3. Add scenes using action prompts and the relevant reference entities.
4. Generate scene images, then video clips, through the request queue.
5. Review the clips before any supported upscale operation.
6. Prepare narration, subtitles, music, and timeline edits.
7. Export a preview or final MP4 and download it.

Use `POST /api/requests/batch` for bulk generation. The server handles concurrency
and cooldowns. `/fk-*` recipes in [skills/](skills/README.md) describe the API
workflow and its checks.

evidence.heading: Preview status and known limitations
evidence.text:
- **Veo video upscale, Veo reference-to-video, and Veo start/end-frame chaining**
  are marked unported on the migrated transport. Supported Omni modes and
  explicitly enabled fallbacks have different behavior; consult
  [the transport notes](docs/CAPTURE.md).
- Generation depends on Google Flow's current browser behavior and your account.
  Live generation has not been re-verified for this preview release.
- External macOS volumes exposed AppleDouble (`._*`) discovery and modification-time
  cache failures during packaging checks. For a macOS trial, use native APFS
  working data and temporary directories. Packaging excludes metadata files but
  does not repair all runtime filesystem assumptions.
- TTS, speech analysis, and restoration engines are optional integrations with
  separate installation, model, and licensing requirements.
- Saved project titles and original uploaded filenames keep their user-provided
  names. App-generated image/video export names use the `frameweaver-` prefix.

Focused publication checks passed for backend download/editing/auth/package
paths, the MV3 bootstrap test, and the dashboard production build. A clean full
cross-platform test result is not claimed for this preview.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Free & local ComfyUI workflows + one-click Windows installer: image to watertight 3D model and game-ready low-poly with Pixal3D / TRELLIS.2. Nodes by MostAadTech.

evidence.heading: PixelArtistry · Watertight & Game-Ready 3D in ComfyUI
evidence.text:
Free & local ComfyUI workflows that turn a single image into a **watertight 3D model** – and into a **game-ready low-poly asset with baked textures** – using Pixal3D / TRELLIS.2. Plus a one-click installer for Windows.

▶ Tutorial and more: [PixelArtistry on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@PixelArtistry_)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Before you start:** set up ComfyUI + TRELLIS.2 first with the **[TRELLIS.2 Installation Guide](https://go.pixel-artistry.com/Trellis2InstallationGuide)**. This installer builds on that setup.

evidence.heading: What's inside
evidence.text:
| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `watertightMeshes_win_installer.bat` | Installs all node packs, the workflows and checks your models, GPU and Blender |
| `workflows/PixelArtistry_01_Image_to_Watertight_Mesh.json` | Image → watertight 3D model (1536) – also print-ready |
| `workflows/PixelArtistry_01b_Image_to_Watertight_Mesh_2K.json` | Same at 2048 for maximum detail (16 GB+ VRAM, 32 GB+ RAM) |
| `workflows/PixelArtistry_02_Image_to_GameReady_Asset.json` | Image → textured high-poly + baked game-ready low-poly |
| `workflows/PixelArtistry_03_Your_Mesh_to_GameReady_Asset.json` | Your own mesh → textured + baked low-poly |

The installer already contains the workflows – you only need the `.bat`. The JSON files are here if you want to load them by hand.

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
- **A working ComfyUI + TRELLIS.2 setup – follow the [TRELLIS.2 Installation Guide](https://go.pixel-artistry.com/Trellis2InstallationGuide)**
- Windows 10 or 11, NVIDIA RTX 20 series or newer
- [ComfyUI Easy-Install](https://github.com/Tavris1/ComfyUI-Easy-Install) with Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.8.0 + CUDA 12.8
- [VisualBruno's ComfyUI-Trellis2](https://github.com/visualbruno/ComfyUI-Trellis2) installed – it provides CuMesh and O-Voxel
- [Blender](https://www.blender.org/download/) – ideally a separate, clean install without add-ons (see Troubleshooting)
- 32 GB system RAM recommended

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
0. If you haven't yet, set up ComfyUI + TRELLIS.2 with the [TRELLIS.2 Installation Guide](https://go.pixel-artistry.com/Trellis2InstallationGuide).
1. Download `watertightMeshes_win_installer.bat`.
2. Put it into your `ComfyUI-Easy-Install\Add-ons` folder (the Easy-Install or portable root folder works too).
3. Close ComfyUI and double-click the file.
4. When the summary shows only `[OK]` lines, start ComfyUI and open **Workflows → PixelArtistry**.
5. In each workflow, paste your Blender path once into the purple **Blender path** node and load your image in **Load Image**.

What the installer does:

1. Checks Python, PyTorch, CUDA and your GPU
2. Downloads the node packs – pinned to the exact versions tested for the video, straight from the original repositories
3. Picks the right WTiVo build for your GPU (RTX 50 or RTX 20/30/40)
4. Installs the Python dependencies into `python_embeded`
5. Runs a quick watertight test on your GPU
6. Installs the four PixelArtistry workflows
7. Checks all models – including shared model folders – and offers to download missing ones from Hugging Face
8. Looks for Blender

It's safe to run again: everything is set back to the tested versions.

evidence.heading: Settings by GPU
evidence.text:
| VRAM | WTiVo resolution | Proxy points | Measured on an RTX 5080 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 GB | 1024 | lower if you run out of memory | – |
| 8 GB+ | 1536 (workflow 01/02) | 12,000,000 | WTiVo ~2 min, ~6 GB RAM |
| 16 GB+ | 2048 (workflow 01b, Quad Reconstruct bypassed) | 25,000,000 | WTiVo ~3.5 min, ~11 GB RAM |

At 2K, Quad Reconstruct is bypassed: its 2048 output made WTiVo's mesh balloon to 85M faces (~17 GB RAM with 25M proxy points), and LODTailor could no longer reduce it without breaking it. Without Quad, 25M proxy points give a 43M-face mesh that stays watertight through the whole chain.

evidence.heading: Troubleshooting
evidence.text:
- **Blender errors in the console (Auto-Rig Pro, PolyQuilt, …):** add-ons break headless Blender runs. Download the Blender zip, extract it, create an empty folder named `portable` next to `blender.exe`, and use that path in the Blender path node.
- **Holes after generation:** run again – the structure seed is set to *randomize*.
- **Checking watertightness in Blender:** use the 3D Print Toolbox → Check All. Import textured low-poly files with **Merge Vertices** ticked – a GLB can't give one vertex two UV coordinates, so UV seams otherwise show up as open edges.
- **2K runs out of memory:** restart ComfyUI and close other programs before the run.
- **Installer says ComfyUI is still running:** close it and run the installer again.

evidence.heading: The web crawler for AI agents that finds the answer, not just pages.
evidence.text:
A small decision model picks every link and every passage, so your agent's LLM reads
**only what answers its question** at **a few cents per crawl**.

[](https://pypi.org/project/jevcrawl/)
[](https://github.com/RayenMlayeh/jevcrawl/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](LICENSE)
[](pyproject.toml)
[](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
[](#benchmarks)
[](#cost-and-privacy)

[Quick start](#quick-start) · [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) · [Tools](#tools) ·
[How it works](#how-it-works) · [Configuration](#configuration)

evidence.heading: Why jevcrawl
evidence.text:
Agents that browse a site have two bad options. They can **read everything** a crawler fetches,
which buries the answer in navigation and boilerplate and burns tokens. Or they can **let the LLM
pick each link**, which is slow and costs dollars per question. jevcrawl does neither:

- 🎯 **Finds the answer page more often.** 54% of tasks vs 33% when Claude picks the links, and
  2x as often as [Crawl4AI](#jevcrawl-vs-crawl4ai)'s goal-directed crawl.
- 💸 **About 8x cheaper per task, 10x per correct answer.** The crawl decisions cost about a cent.
- ⚡ **2x faster than an LLM-driven crawl.** Four pages at a time, one decision request per page.
- 📜 **Verbatim, with sources.** Every passage is copied from the page with its URL, heading path
  and character offsets. The decision model only scores, so it cannot invent text.
- 🛡️ **Safe against prompt injection by design.** Page text is only ever scored, never followed.
- 🔌 **Works everywhere MCP does:** Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, or the CLI.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
You need a Jev API key from [console.typesafe.ai](https://console.typesafe.ai/) and
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add jevcrawl -e TYPESAFE_API_KEY=<your key> -- uvx jevcrawl
```

**Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients** (`mcpServers` in the client's config file)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jevcrawl": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["jevcrawl"],
      "env": { "TYPESAFE_API_KEY": "<your key>" }
    }
  }
}
```

Then ask your agent something like *"Use jevcrawl to find which Python version added the walrus
operator, starting from docs.python.org"*. Check the setup with
`uvx jevcrawl doctor`. Agents that load skills
can also use [`skills/jevcrawl/SKILL.md`](skills/jevcrawl/SKILL.md).

**Pages that need JavaScript** (optional). jevcrawl reads plain HTML. To also render pages that
are empty without JavaScript, add the `js` extra and download Chromium once:

```bash
claude mcp add jevcrawl -e TYPESAFE_API_KEY=<your key> -- uvx --from "jevcrawl[js]" jevcrawl
uvx --from "jevcrawl[js]" playwright install chromium
```

(In `mcpServers`, use `"args": ["--from", "jevcrawl[js]", "jevcrawl"]`.) Only pages detected as
JavaScript shells are opened in the browser, at most five per call, and they are listed in
`stats.js_rendered_urls`. Everything else is still fetched as plain HTML.

evidence.heading: Benchmarks
evidence.text:
Every system starts on a site's home page with the same 30-page budget and the same question.
What each one collects goes to the **same answering LLM**, and the **same judge** grades the
answer, so the crawler is the only thing that changes.

evidence.heading: jevcrawl vs Crawl4AI
evidence.text:
[Crawl4AI](https://github.com/unclecode/crawl4ai) is one of the most popular open-source crawlers
for LLMs. Its `BestFirstCrawlingStrategy` with a keyword scorer is its way to crawl toward a question
without an LLM, so we compared the two on whether they fetch the page that holds the answer.

evidence.heading: Where the numbers come from
evidence.text:
| | |
|---|---|
| **Tasks** | [WebWalkerQA](https://huggingface.co/datasets/callanwu/WebWalkerQA) from *WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal* (Wu et al., Alibaba Tongyi Lab, [ACL 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.07572)): questions whose answers sit several clicks deep in real websites (conferences, universities, organizations, games), in English and Chinese. |
| **Task selection** | Each task was re-checked live before the run: the site and answer page still load and still contain the reference answer. Tasks looked at while developing are excluded ([`bench/tasks/seen-ids.txt`](bench/tasks/seen-ids.txt)). |
| **Accuracy run** | 50 tasks, 2026-10-12. Answering model `claude-opus-5-5`, judge `claude-sonnet-5-5`. |
| **Crawl4AI run** | 20 different tasks, 2026-10-13, Crawl4AI 0.9.4. Crawl only, no LLM: did the crawler fetch the gold page? In the accuracy run, whether a system fetched the gold page closely tracked whether it answered correctly. |
| **Baselines** | *Claude picks every link*: Claude reads each page and chooses the next link. *Breadth-first*: every page to depth 2. All systems share jevcrawl's fetcher and remove navigation and footers. |
| **Costs** | Jev cost is billed and exact. LLM costs are token counts at list price. |
| **Caveats** | 50 and 20 tasks are small samples: the cost gap is large and stable, the accuracy gap less so. Crawl4AI drives a real browser; the benchmark ran jevcrawl without JavaScript rendering. |

The benchmark code and how to reproduce every number: [`bench/`](bench/README.md).

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
- **Jev decides, it does not write.** [Jev](https://typesafe.ai) returns a probability per
  yes/no question, so it cannot produce text. Everything you get back is copied from the page.
- **Page text is data, never instructions.** It travels only in data fields of a question; every
  question sentence is a fixed string written by jevcrawl. An injected "ignore previous
  instructions" can at worst bias a score.
- **Links below the priority floor are kept in reserve**, not dropped, so a crawl never stops
  early while it still has page budget.
- **Failures degrade, they do not hide.** After three failed Jev requests the crawl continues
  breadth-first, returns every block unscored in `uncertain`, and sets `stats.degraded`.
- **Repeats are free.** Jev's answers are cached locally (`~/.jevcrawl/cache`), so the same goal
  on the same pages costs nothing.

evidence.heading: Speech Studio
evidence.text:
**Free, offline AI voice studio for Windows — voice any text with cloned and built-in voices, and turn recordings into text with the speakers. Russian done right: numbers in their cases, stress marks, «ё» and homographs. 100% local, zero Python: one native `.exe` (Rust + C++/CUDA); every model and engine downloads with a button.**

[](LICENSE)
[](https://github.com/timoncool/speech-studio/stargazers)
[](https://github.com/timoncool/speech-studio/releases)
[](https://github.com/timoncool/speech-studio/releases)
