evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview-official","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview-official", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
```

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```
```bash
  -d '{"model":"gpt-image-2-official","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gpt-image-2-official", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

> **from $0.0125 per image** — one OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `https://api.apimart.ai/v1`, no monthly plan required. *(observed 2026-10-12)*

**[Get an API key](https://go.apimart.ai/k-5f6273)** · **[Live pricing](https://go.apimart.ai/k-1b73b7)** · **[Model page](https://go.apimart.ai/k-bafcf1)** · [⚡ 60-second quickstart](#quickstart)

**Why teams call Nano Banana (`gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview`) through APIMart**

- **One key, entire catalog.** The same `https://api.apimart.ai/v1` base URL and `Authorization` header reach Nano Banana (`gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview`) and 300+ other image, video and language models — switch the `model` field, not your client.
- **$1 minimum, pay as you go.** No subscription and no prepaid plan to size up front: top up from $1 and spend it on calls.
- **The charge comes back in the response.** Every completed task reports the amount billed (`cost` / `credits_cost`); a task marked `failed` is refunded.
- **Async by design.** Submit, take the `task_id`, poll `GET /v1/tasks/{id}` — batching and retries are ordinary queue work, not a bespoke integration.



Nano Banana is Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash Image route on APIMart: fast text-to-image and reference-image editing through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

evidence.text:
| Route | `model` value | Billing | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Endpoint: `POST https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations` (OpenAI-compatible), then poll `GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}`.

evidence.text:
| Output | List price | Effective price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | $0.0375 | $0.02 |
| 4K | $0.05 | $0.03 |

The token-billed official route bills per million tokens instead: `text_input` $1.60, `cached_text_input` free, `image_input` $1.60, `cached_image_input` free, `text_output` $9.60, `image_output` $96.00.

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

Runnable versions: [`examples/`](examples). The task lifecycle is `pending → processing → completed | failed`.

evidence.heading: Quickstart

```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={

}).json()

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
```

**[Get an API key](https://go.apimart.ai/k-5ea64a)** · **[Live pricing](https://go.apimart.ai/k-788d36)** · **[Model page](https://go.apimart.ai/k-57338a)** · [⚡ 60-second quickstart](#quickstart)

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"grok-imagine-2.0-ext","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "grok-imagine-2.0-ext", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

Runnable versions: [`examples/`](examples). The task lifecycle is `pending → processing → completed | failed`.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: 基于麦当劳 MCP 的点单决策求解器：在预算、热量、钠约束下求解满足感最高的组合

evidence.heading: 今天麦什么
evidence.text:
[](https://github.com/ftxcgwf/mcd-solver/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

**给我预算、热量上限和一个心情，我给你麦当劳的最优解。**

基于麦当劳 MCP 能力的点单决策求解器。不是菜单查询，不是领券脚本——它把「怎么点」建模成一个带约束的优化问题：预算、热量、钠、蛋白质是约束，目标函数是**满足感**，而不是「最便宜」。

> **WorkBuddy 原生项目**：本项目从方向选型、MCP 接入、求解器实现到参赛文档，全程在 WorkBuddy 智能体中完成，并可通过 `SKILL.md` 被 WorkBuddy 直接加载调用。`workbuddy.md` 即 WorkBuddy 专项奖励凭证（作品进入前 100 名额外 +3000 积分）。

> **为什么不是又一个「算最便宜」的工具？** 榜单前十里已有多个省钱 / 卡路里 / 预算类方案。本项目的差异点在于把 **控钠（盐）** 与 **口感层次 / 温度反差（满足感）** 也建模进目标函数——目前公开作品里**独一份**这么做。
>
> 同一预算、同一门店，三种取向解出的钠含量差异明显（单位 mg）：
>
> | | 省钱派 | 嘴馋派 | 均衡派 |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 钠 | **768** | **1245** | **768** |
>
> 最便宜的和最贵的钠一样，夹在中间的反而高 62%——多花钱不等于吃得更健康。一个反直觉事实：板烧鸡腿堡钠 1041mg，比巨无霸的 961mg 还高。

---

evidence.heading: 先说一个可能颠覆你认知的数据
evidence.text:
你可能以为鸡腿堡比牛肉堡健康。但麦当劳官方营养数据是这样的：

| 餐品 | 热量 | 钠 |
|---|---|---|
| 板烧鸡腿堡 | 392 kcal | **1041 mg** |
| 巨无霸 | 513 kcal | 961 mg |

**板烧鸡腿堡比巨无霸还咸。**

中国居民膳食指南建议每日钠摄入不超过 2000mg。一份板烧鸡腿堡就吃掉了一半还多。而几乎所有控卡工具都只看热量，不看钠——这是本项目强调控钠的原因，`--max-sodium` 是一等公民参数。

---

evidence.heading: 它长什么样
evidence.text:
```
约束：预算 45 元　热量 ≤ 1200 kcal　（价格经 MCP 官方结算价校准）

【省钱派】满足感 -1.79   合计 ¥35.0　516kcal　钠  768mg
  主食 麦香鸡         1个    ¥17.0   370kcal  钠  731mg  [—]
  小食 玉米杯         小     ¥13.0    53kcal  钠    1mg  [清爽·温热]
  甜品 圆筒冰淇淋      1个    ¥5.0     94kcal  钠   36mg  [冰爽·奶香·甜]

【嘴馋派】满足感 37.41   合计 ¥41.0　632kcal　钠 1245mg
  主食 麦辣鸡腿汉堡     1个    ¥23.0   485kcal  钠 1208mg  [嚼劲·酥脆·多汁·咸香·嫩滑]
  小食 玉米杯         小     ¥13.0    53kcal  钠    1mg  [清爽·温热]
  甜品 圆筒冰淇淋      1个    ¥5.0     94kcal  钠   36mg  [冰爽·奶香·甜]

【均衡派】满足感 16.27   合计 ¥44.5　664kcal　钠  768mg
  主食 麦香鸡         1个    ¥17.0   370kcal  钠  731mg  [—]
  小食 玉米杯         小     ¥13.0    53kcal  钠    1mg  [清爽·温热]
  饮料 可口可乐        中     ¥9.5    147kcal  钠    0mg  [冰爽]
  甜品 圆筒冰淇淋      1个    ¥5.0     94kcal  钠   36mg  [冰爽·奶香·甜]
```

同一个约束、同一家门店，三种取向解出来的结果值得多看一眼：

| | 花费 | 热量 | **钠** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 省钱派 | ¥35.0 | 516kcal | **768mg** |
| 嘴馋派 | ¥41.0 | 632kcal | **1245mg** |
| 均衡派 | ¥44.5 | 664kcal | **768mg** |

**最便宜的和最贵的，钠含量一模一样；夹在中间的那个反而高出 62%。**

多花钱并不等于吃得更健康。省钱派和均衡派都绕开了那个 1208mg 的汉堡，钠就都压到了 769mg；嘴馋派为了口感层次选了它，钠直接跳一倍，尽管花的钱还在中间。这种事盯着菜单看是看不出来的，得把每一件的钠累加起来、放进同一个约束里比过才知道。

（各人设权重不同，且经济性惩罚项会让分数变负，满足感分数**不可横向比较**，只在同人设内比较。）

evidence.heading: 官方复核：让「我算的」变成「官方认的」
evidence.text:
求解器是本地累加的，这一单到底要付多少只有麦当劳自己知道。加 `--quote` 就把方案交回 MCP `calculate-price` 复核：

```
  【均衡派】
  官方复核 · 麦当劳常州万象城餐厅（1990558）
  官方复核（calculate-price）
    原价      ¥44.5
    应付      ¥44.5
    与求解器估算 ¥44.5 相比：一致
    明细：
      麦香鸡              x1  ¥17.0
      小杯玉米杯            x1  ¥13.0
      可乐               x1  ¥9.5
      圆筒冰淇淋            x1  ¥5.0
    取餐方式：堂食(eat-in)、外带(take-in-store)
```

复核不只是回显数字，它会真的拿这套商品去该门店验一次能否结算：遇到售罄自动剔除并重新报价，遇到门店打烊自动切到同城还在营业的门店。这次结果是「一致」——价格层事先被同一套 `calculate-price` 校准过，两边自然对齐。

> **一个容易看反的地方**：`--quote` 复核**不带券**，而求解器用的是**券后价**。
> 所以方案里有可用券的商品时，复核金额会**高于**求解器估算（例如冰美式求解器按券后
> ¥9.9、复核按原价 ¥11.9）。这不是求解器算少了，恰恰相反——它已经算到了用券之后的最低价，
> 而复核是按不含券报的。要让官方连同券一起确认，加 `--coupons`，它会逐张带着 `couponId`
> 试算并挑出最划算的那张。

---

evidence.heading: 为什么目标函数不是「最便宜」
evidence.text:
人点麦当劳时的真实心理是：**这顿吃完我不能后悔**。后悔通常来自四种情况：

- 花了钱但没吃到想吃的（口味单调）
- 吃完发现这顿咸得离谱（钠超标）
- 结构不完整，吃了跟没吃一样（没主食、没喝的）
- 明明有更划算的组合，自己没发现

所以满足感被拆成六项：

```
S = 固有满足度        # 单品口感愉悦分，来自口味先验，按边际递减累加
  + 口感层次奖励      # 酥脆/多汁/冰爽/奶香…覆盖维度越多越爽，边际递减
  + 温度反差奖励      # 热汉堡配冰可乐 > 全是热食
  + 结构完整奖励      # 主食/小食/饮料/甜品齐备度；没主食不成一顿饭
  - 同类堆叠惩罚      # 三个汉堡不叫一顿饭
  - 健康软惩罚        # 钠与脂肪，渐进扣分
  + 性价比愉悦        # 省得越多越开心（需价格）
```

其中**口感层次**和**温度反差**来自经验，不来自数据库——MCP 能给你热量和钠，但它永远不会告诉你「一份餐里同时有酥脆、多汁、冰爽三种口感时，满足感远高于三样都是软塌塌的」。这部分先验在 `solver/taste.py`，可用 `data/taste_override.json` 手工精修。

有三个反直觉但必要的修正，不加就会给出蠢方案：

- **固有满足度按边际递减累加**（第 n 件的愉悦 × 0.8ⁿ）。不衰减的话，五件小食的分数之和永远压过三件正餐，模型就会输出「脆薯饼 + 苹果片 + 薯条」这种凑数组合。
- **撑不起正餐的「主食」直接降级**。官网把脆薯饼（146kcal）、脆香油条（202kcal）挂在早餐分类下，而早餐算主食——于是它们会和汉堡抢主食名额，还经常因为便宜而胜出。只在评分里扣分不够，求解器照旧拿它们凑数，所以低于 300kcal 的一律降为小食。
- **钠要渐进惩罚，不能只罚超限**。一餐吃掉每日推荐（2000mg）的 78% 已经很咸了，但「只罚超 2000mg」的写法会给它满分——结果是均衡派选出钠 1555mg 的组合，和嘴馋派一模一样，控钠人设形同虚设。现在从占每日推荐一半起就开始罚，超限后斜率翻倍。

---

evidence.heading: 快速开始
evidence.text:
零第三方依赖，Python 3.9+，**不需要 MCP Token 就能跑**。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ftxcgwf/mcd-solver.git
cd mcd-solver

# 一行到底（会自动建营养快照并跑三个示例）
python scripts/quickstart.py
```

手工执行同样简单：

```bash
# 1. 建营养快照（约 2 分钟，抓自麦当劳官网公开营养计算器，无需 Token）
python scripts/fetch_nutrition_web.py

# 2. 直接问
python cli.py --max-kcal 750 --max-sodium 1800 --persona all
```

想让预算约束生效，需要真实价格——价格官网不提供，只能来自 MCP：

```bash
# 到 https://open.mcd.cn/mcp 登录激活，申请 MCP Token
export MCD_MCP_TOKEN=你的Token
python scripts/fetch_menu.py            # 抓在售菜单与价格 -> data/menu.json
python scripts/verify_prices.py         # 校准官方结算价 -> data/prices_verified.json
python scripts/coupons.py --calibrate   # 折算券后价 -> data/prices_coupon.json
python cli.py --budget 45 --max-kcal 1200 --persona all
```

券数据是可选的：没有券时求解照常，只是少一层价格优惠。

evidence.heading: 边界与免责
evidence.text:
- 营养数据来自麦当劳官方公开营养计算器（更新于 2025-04），实际出品可能因原料批次、产地、工艺存在差异，以官方公布与门店实际为准
- 价格随地区、时段、活动浮动，以门店实际为准
- 服务范围为麦当劳中国大陆，不含港澳台
- **同一商品的冷热 / 口味变体可能拿不到可下单的编码**。MCP 菜单的粒度粗于官网营养数据：菜单只有「美式」「新地」「牛奶」一条记录，官网却按口味冷热分列（「冰美式/热美式」「朱古力新地/草莓新地」）。冷热这种差异能靠结算明细名（「麦咖啡™冰美式中杯」）判定；口味这种两边都对不上的，只有唯一一个代表项能挂上编码并参与带价格的求解，其余变体仍保留营养数据，会出现在不需要下单、只看营养的场景里。
- **泛称商品的规格无从判定**。有的编码连结算明细都只返回泛称：「可乐」不带杯型、「新地」不带口味。此时只能退回「热量居中」这条保守启发式，取中间档；而官网各杯型的营养差异很大（可乐小/中/大 = 107/147/224 kcal），若实际不同可能偏 ±50%。这类项目在 `crosscheck_nutrition.py` 里会被明确标为「无从核对」，不冒充已验证。
- **不是每样在售商品都有营养数据**。官方营养计算器更新于 2025-04，而菜单是实时拉取的，因此当季新品（龙焰鸡腿堡、枫糖厚松饼系列、当季口味的麦旋风等）虽有价格与编码，却配不上营养值，进不了求解——这是数据源本身的滞后，不是匹配失败。已重跑 `fetch_nutrition_web.py` 确认官网确实没更新（两次抓取结果完全一致，仍标 2025-04）。
- `--place` 会创建真实订单（仍需你在麦当劳 APP 完成支付）。默认只试算，下单须手动输入金额确认
- 本项目只做**决策辅助**，不构成医疗或营养建议；有特殊健康需求请遵医嘱
- 本项目为个人开源作品，与麦当劳官方无隶属关系。使用麦当劳 MCP 服务须遵守其《使用条款》与《MCP 服务规则》

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview-official","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview-official", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

evidence.heading: Key Features
evidence.text: Multi-Engine Conversion Pipeline Intelligently dispatches between Microsoft MarkItDown (fast everyday documents), Docling (deep layout analysis and TableFormer reconstruction), Markit (InkDoc's own broad-format extractors, inspired by Shift Labs' Markit, for formats like EPUB, YAML and Jupyter Notebooks) and GLM-OCR (a downloadable OCR model for scans, photos, math and tables). Auto picks the engine per file, and every PDF is checked for missing text so a silently incomplete conversion gets a warning and a one-click fix. Single Source of Truth Interface The native desktop executable (Edge WebView2 on Windows, WebKit on macOS/Linux) and the local web workbench (http://127.0.0.1:13118/InkDoc) run the exact same user interface without code divergence. On large screens, Settings → General → Layout width (Standard, Wide or Full) gives tables, code and images more room, and A− / A+ set the preview's text size. LaTeX formulas from Docling and GLM-OCR are drawn as real math (bundled KaTeX, works offline; switch it off in Settings → Add-ons). Zero-Friction Auto-Save Documents convert asynchronously and are automatically saved to ~/Downloads, or to a folder you pick in Settings, the moment they finish, with collision-safe numbered suffixes (e.g., report (1).md). No manual export required. If the chosen folder is missing or read-only, the file goes to Downloads and InkDoc tells you. Embedded Local REST API FastAPI backend with streaming multipart uploads, URL conversion, interactive OpenAPI Swagger documentation (/docs), and a headless server mode for programmatic pipelines and CI/CD.

evidence.heading: Data, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and AI Engineering, the long way round
evidence.text:
*by Gonzalo L. Romero (DeepRat)*


  


---

Every week somebody on the internet promises to turn you into an "AI Engineer" in six weeks. You watch the videos, you copy the notebook, you call `model.fit()`, you get 97% accuracy on a dataset that has been solved since before you were born, and you put "AI" on your CV. Then you get your first real job, somebody hands you a table with 400 million rows, a label that is wrong 8% of the time, a latency budget of 50 ms and a security team that wants to know why your chatbot just emailed the customer database to a stranger. And the six-week course has nothing to say about any of that.

This course is my answer to that problem. It is long. It is not easy. It has math in it, and the math is there because you need it, not because I want to look smart. It has a lot of code, and every piece of code in the labs is executed by CI before it lands here, because I don't trust code I haven't run, and neither should you.

I'm a systems engineer (technically still a student, the paperwork is slower than the learning), a certified AI engineer, and I've been writing software for more than fifteen years: AI systems that had to work outside of a demo, data platforms that had to be secure because the data was worth stealing, and a fair amount of penetration testing, which is a polite way of saying I get paid to find out how other people's systems break. That last part shows up all over this course. When I teach you RAG, I will also teach you how to attack it. When I teach you data pipelines, I will show you where the credentials leak. An engineer who doesn't know how their system fails is not an engineer yet. They are an optimist.

evidence.heading: What "completing this course" is supposed to mean
evidence.text:
When you finish, you should be able to walk into a job as a **Data Engineer**, **Data Scientist**, **Machine Learning Engineer**, **Deep Learning Engineer** or **AI Engineer** and do the work. That means more than knowing what the words mean:

- You can take a messy business question and turn it into a well-posed learning problem, or tell people honestly that it isn't one.
- You can build the data platform under it: ingestion, storage, modeling, orchestration, streaming, quality checks, access control.
- You can derive, implement from scratch and then use in production the classical ML toolbox, and you know why gradient boosting still wins on tabular data.
- You can build and train deep networks in PyTorch, including a transformer and a small GPT, and you understand what is happening on the GPU while it trains.
- You can pretrain, fine-tune, align, quantize and serve language models, and you can build RAG systems and agents on top of them that survive contact with real users and real attackers.
- You can put all of the above into production with tracking, testing, CI/CD, monitoring, rollbacks, cost control, and a threat model.
- You know the responsibilities that come with it: fairness, privacy, regulation, and not shipping garbage because a deadline said so.

The full, boring, explicit version of that promise lives in [COMPETENCIES.md](COMPETENCIES.md). It maps every skill that the five roles require to the exact lesson that teaches it and the lab or capstone that proves you have it. If a skill is not on that map, I either consider it out of scope (and say so) or I missed it, in which case open an issue and tell me.

evidence.heading: How it's organized
evidence.text:

evidence.heading: How long this takes
evidence.text:
Honestly? If you start with decent programming skills and high school math, about **1,800 hours**, and that's my estimate for someone who actually does the labs. At 15 hours a week that's a bit over two years. At full time, about eleven months. Roughly the workload of a serious master's degree, minus the tuition and the group projects where one person does everything. Anybody who tells you it can be done in a weekend is selling something, usually a weekend course.

You can go faster through parts you already know. Every module starts with a short self-check. If you can do the self-check without looking anything up, skip the module and go do its lab. If the lab is easy, you really can skip it. If the lab is not easy, you were lying to the self-check. Happens to everyone :)

evidence.heading: Prerequisites
evidence.text:
- You can program in *some* language and you're not scared of a terminal. Python specifically is taught in Part I, but I won't teach you what a loop is.
- High school algebra. Everything above that (linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics) is taught from the ground up in Part I, fast but properly.
- A computer with 16 GB of RAM is comfortable. 8 GB works for almost everything. A GPU is nice but not required until Part IV, and even there every lab has a CPU-sized version. Free Colab or Kaggle GPUs cover the rest.

evidence.heading: Running the labs
evidence.text:
Clone the repository (GitHub's green **Code** button gives you the URL) or download it, then, from its folder:

```bash
uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate      # or python -m venv .venv
uv pip install -r requirements.txt        # or pip install -r requirements.txt
python tools/run_labs.py --part 1         # run every lab in Part I
python part-1-foundations/02-linear-algebra/labs/lab_02_3_least_squares.py
```

Labs are plain Python files split into cells with `# %%` markers. VS Code, PyCharm and Jupyter (via `jupytext`) all understand that format and will let you run them cell by cell. I don't keep notebooks as the source of truth because notebooks are where reproducibility goes to die: hidden state, out-of-order execution, diffs that nobody can review. If you prefer notebooks, `jupytext --to notebook lab.py` gives you one in a second. Just don't commit it back.

Every lab ends with assertions. If an assertion fails, the lab is telling you that you broke something. Read the message.

The numbers quoted in the lessons come from running the labs on a four-core CPU. Yours will differ in the last digit or two, because floating point on a different CPU, thread count or library version rounds differently, and several labs train small models. The assertions check the conclusions (this method beats that one, this error rate falls below that one), not the digits. If an assertion fails on your machine and you didn't touch the code, that's a bug in the lab, and I want to hear about it.

Labs from Part IV onward that train on this course's own text, or search it, read a frozen copy of Parts 0 to V (`part-5-language-models/_shared/course_snapshot.json.gz`), not the live lessons, so that a typo fix in a lesson doesn't retrain the shared models and change every number that depends on

evidence.heading: Nano Banana 2 (official) API (`gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview-official`)
evidence.text:
> token-billed: `text_input` $0.4/M, `image_input` $0.4/M, `text_output` $2.4/M, `image_output` $48/M — one OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `https://api.apimart.ai/v1`, no monthly plan required. *(observed 2026-10-12)*

**[Get an API key](https://go.apimart.ai/k-f5222d)** · **[Live pricing](https://go.apimart.ai/k-8a55e7)** · **[Model page](https://go.apimart.ai/k-7e338e)** · [⚡ 60-second quickstart](#quickstart)

**Why teams call Nano Banana 2 (official) (`gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview-official`) through APIMart**

- **One key, entire catalog.** The same `https://api.apimart.ai/v1` base URL and `Authorization` header reach Nano Banana 2 (official) (`gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview-official`) and 300+ other image, video and language models — switch the `model` field, not your client.
- **$1 minimum, pay as you go.** No subscription and no prepaid plan to size up front: top up from $1 and spend it on calls.
- **The charge comes back in the response.** Every completed task reports the amount billed (`cost` / `credits_cost`); a task marked `failed` is refunded.
- **Async by design.** Submit, take the `task_id`, poll `GET /v1/tasks/{id}` — batching and retries are ordinary queue work, not a bespoke integration.



The token-billed official route for Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) on APIMart.

evidence.heading: Model id and routes
evidence.text:
| Route | `model` value | Billing | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Per-image | `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview-official` | per delivered image, by resolution | see the [model page](https://go.apimart.ai/k-7e338e) for the exact tiers |

Endpoint: `POST https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations` (OpenAI-compatible), then poll `GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}`.

evidence.text:
| Output | List price | Effective price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | $0.0375 | $0.02 |
| 4K | $0.05 | $0.03 |

The token-billed official route bills per million tokens instead: `text_input` $1.60, `cached_text_input` free, `image_input` $1.60, `cached_image_input` free, `text_output` $9.60, `image_output` $96.00.


Prices are a snapshot; the [pricing page](https://go.apimart.ai/k-8a55e7) and [`data/model.json`](data/model.json) are refreshed by CI, and a completed task reports the exact amount in its `cost` field.

evidence.heading: Request parameters
evidence.text:
| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | string | required | the model id shown in the route table above |
| `prompt` | string | required | what to generate, or what to change when editing |
| `size` | string | `auto` / `1:1` | aspect ratio, or `auto` where the route supports it |
| `resolution` | string | `1K` | output resolution tier — cost scales with it |
| `n` | integer | `1` | number of images per task, where the route allows more than one |

The table lists the fields accepted by the APIMart OpenAI-compatible image endpoint. Check the [model page](https://go.apimart.ai/k-7e338e) for anything this model adds on top.

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview-official","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview-official", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

Runnable versions: [`examples/`](examples). The task lifecycle is `pending → processing → completed | failed`.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Iris-3B Metal


Direct RGB pixel-space diffusion on Apple Silicon.
An independent MPS and Metal inference engine, with a native macOS app, CLI, Python API and local HTTP API.









A real macOS app capture with an image generated by Iris-3B.

evidence.heading: Why pixel space
evidence.text:
[Iris-3B](https://github.com/speridlabs/iris-3b) is Speridlabs' 3B-parameter
pixel-space diffusion transformer. Its text-to-image path denoises RGB pixel
values directly and predicts their flow in pixel space; it uses no lossy VAE
latent representation or VAE encode/decode stage. This avoids the VAE
representation used by VAE-based latent diffusion, but it does not make
inference automatically faster or every image better. The pixel-space
transformer has substantial compute costs of its own.

| Upstream Iris-3B | Iris-3B Metal |
| --- | --- |
| Original model architecture, training code, weights, and depth and restoration fine-tunes by Speridlabs. | Independent Apple Silicon inference work: PyTorch MPS, custom Metal kernels, precision and memory optimizations, and streamed Qwen text encoding. Includes a macOS app, CLI, Python API and local HTTP API. |

The upstream depth and restoration fine-tunes reuse the Iris architecture for relative-depth estimation and image restoration. The model, original training and weights are upstream work; this repository does not claim them as its invention. The engine runs the official weights without fine-tuning or distillation.

evidence.heading: At a glance
evidence.text:
In the independent v0.6.0 audit on a base M5 MacBook Pro with 24 GiB,
official Turbo (4 steps, 1024 × 1024) took **9.81 s versus 12.52 s** for
repeated prompts: **21.6% lower median pipeline latency**, six requests per
version. Changed-prompt medians were **14.05 s versus 18.30 s**, four requests
per version. Both comparisons used the real text encoder.

Fixed-input checks matched intermediate tensors, pre-clamp samples, pixels
and metadata; they do not prove equivalence for every input. No Original
speedup or peak-memory improvement was established. See
[conditions, ranges and limits](#v060-independent-audit).
The [v0.5.0 measurements](#v050-final-measurements) below are a separate
session, not a direct baseline for these numbers. Macs with 16 GB remain untested.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
**Requirements:** Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later, and Python 3.11 or later.
First use downloads only the selected text-to-image checkpoint: Original
(12.0 GB) or official Turbo (6.0 GB BF16), plus the shared 8.9 GB
Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder from Hugging Face. Depth and restoration
weights (about 12 GB each) download only when first used. Model weights are not
included in the repository or release.

For the native app and engine, see [Install the macOS release](docs/macos-updates.md).
That route does not require Git or Xcode. The v0.6.1 release files are
an arm64 app ZIP and a matching Python wheel. The app uses a separately
installed engine and does not include Python or model weights.

To install only the CLI or Python package from source, use the development
instructions in [Development](#development). Installing the engine does not
download model weights; the first inference does.

**Explore:** [Usage](#usage) · [macOS app](#macos-app) · [Performance details](#performance-details) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Image quality](#image-quality) · [Development](#development) · [License and credits](#license-and-credits)

evidence.heading: What it supports
evidence.text:
- Original text-to-image at about one megapixel, with aspect ratios from 4:1 to 1:4
  (the model was trained on 21 sizes from 2048 × 512 to 512 × 2048). The
  upstream sampler is DPM-Solver++ (2nd order); steps, guidance, seed, size
  and negative prompt can be set.
- **Official Iris-3B Turbo:** the full-parameter distilled checkpoint, four fixed
  deterministic flow-Euler steps with sigmas `1, 0.938, 0.833, 0.625`. Guidance
  is baked into the weights; steps, CFG and negative prompts cannot be adjusted.
  This is a separate model with different image characteristics from Original.
  Turbo retains the official BF16 forward on MPS; see the
  [v0.6.0 pipeline measurements](#v060-independent-audit).
- Relative depth estimation and 4× image restoration/upscaling with the official upstream fine-tunes.
- A native SwiftUI macOS app, `iris-metal` CLI, `IrisPipeline` Python API, and localhost HTTP API.
- Local inference on Apple Silicon. Prompts and images are processed on the Mac; first use downloads model files from Hugging Face. The app's release checker contacts GitHub when enabled.

Iris-3B does not edit images from instructions, inpaint, or use earlier prompts or images. Each text-to-image request starts independently.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
Upstream Iris-3B uses a 24-block transformer over 16 × 16 pixel patches (8 dual-stream blocks, then 16 single-stream blocks; grouped-query attention, gated attention and sandwich RMSNorm), followed by four pixel-transformer blocks that predict pixels within patches, conditioned on twelve hidden layers of Qwen3-VL-4B. A 1024 × 1024 image at 100 steps is about 4.6 PFLOP. For Original, `src/iris_metal` evaluates the upstream weights with an independent forward pass:

- **Matrix multiplies and attention use PyTorch MPS kernels.** At the trunk's shapes they run at 13.7–15.5 TFLOPS in FP16 or BF16 on the M5, 84–95% of a compute-only Metal 4 `matmul2d` kernel measured on the same GPU. Custom GEMMs, epilogue fusion and wider packed projections were measured and rejected because they showed no gain beyond thermal drift. Attention uses PyTorch's fused, memory-efficient SDPA.
- **Custom Metal kernels fuse work around the matrix multiplies:** query/key RMSNorm, RoPE and head layout; input normalization and adaLN modulation; sandwich post-norm, gating and residual add on an FP32 residual stream; and the per-pixel half of each pixel block.
- **Original's precision is chosen per part.** The trunk's linear layers and attention take FP16 inputs, which have three more mantissa bits than BF16. Late single-stream QK-norm gains reach 27 and amplify query/key rounding. Norms, adaLN modulation and the residual stream stay FP32. The pixel stage and text adapter use BF16; the pixel stream reaches about 1.4 × 10⁴. The largest measured FP16 trunk value was 2520, and every result is checked for overflow.
- **Qwen text encoding is streamed.** One decoder layer is loaded at a time from checkpoint files for real prompt tokens, keeping the encoder process footprint near 1.5 GiB instead of loading the

evidence.heading: Limitations
evidence.text:
- The inference engine requires an Apple Silicon GPU; it has no CPU or CUDA path. The retained upstream training code supports CUDA. Performance and quality measurements are from one Mac.
- Ten- and twenty-step previews change fine detail. One hundred steps takes about 7.6 minutes per 1024 × 1024 image in the warm benchmark.
- Keep text-to-image sizes near one megapixel. At 512 × 512, the model can show its 16-pixel patch grid, as can upstream FP32; 2048 × 512 and 512 × 2048 were smoke-tested only.
- Python batches larger than one image are supported but untested at 1024 × 1024 on 24 GB. The app and server process one image at a time.
- Model errors are inherited: on a held-out prompt of hands on a piano, upstream FP32 also drew extra hands.
- The app requires macOS 15 or later. Release runtime testing covered an M5 Mac with 24 GB of memory. macOS 15 and 16 GB Macs were not tested.
- The engine does not call a remote inference or moderation service. Local execution does not guarantee what the underlying model can generate.

```bash
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

Runnable versions: [`examples/`](examples). The task lifecycle is `pending → processing → completed | failed`.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: I gave Claude Code 120 pages of my handwritten college notes. It gave me back my handwriting as a real font, in 66 minutes for $13.68.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
Harshpreet Hand


  I gave Claude Code 120 pages of my handwritten college notes.
  It gave me back my handwriting, as a real font.
  One prompt · 1 h 06 min · $13.68 in API calls



  Type in it → ·
  Download ·
  Use it in one line ·
  How it was made ·
  Make your own



  
  
  
  




Every letter comes from the notes: it was found in the page photos, then redrawn
along the pen's path with one steady ballpoint nib. Each letter has 2–3 real
variants from different pages that rotate as you type, so doubled letters never
look stamped.


Or install it on your computer for Figma, Keynote, Word and the rest: grab
`HarshpreetHand-Regular.ttf` and `-Bold.ttf` from the
[latest release](https://github.com/harshpreet931/harshpreet-hand/releases/latest).

evidence.heading: What's in `dist/`
evidence.text:
| File | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `HarshpreetHand-Regular.woff2` / `-Bold.woff2` | Web (use these) |
| `HarshpreetHand-Regular.woff` / `-Bold.woff` | Web fallback for very old browsers |
| `HarshpreetHand-Regular.ttf` / `-Bold.ttf` | Install on your computer (Figma, Keynote, …) |
| `harshpreet-hand.css` | `@font-face` rules + a ready `data-theme="handwritten"` theme |
| `specimen.html` | Specimen and type tester ([live version](https://harshpreet931.github.io/harshpreet-hand/)) |
| `notes-sample.jpg` | Crop of the original notes, used by the specimen |

evidence.heading: Features
evidence.text:
- **`calt` (on by default):** every letter and most figures have 2–3 real variants from different
  pages. The font rotates through them as you type, so `hello` → h, e², l³, l¹, o² and
  doubled letters never look stamped. Each variant also sits slightly higher or
  lower than the others, like real handwriting.
- **`ss01`:** a plain r without the little loop at its foot.
- **`kern`:** kerning computed from the letter outlines (e.g. `To`, `Ty`, `r.`).
- **Coverage:** A–Z, a–z, 0–9, ASCII punctuation, curly quotes, dashes, `… • · ° × ÷`,
  arrows `→ ← ↑ ↓` (taken from the arrows in the notes' margins), and Western European accents.

evidence.heading: How it was made
evidence.text:
The source is [`CN_CompleteNotes_FullSyllabus.pdf`](CN_CompleteNotes_FullSyllabus.pdf):
120 phone photos of my *Computer Networks* notes, covering the full syllabus. (If
you're studying CN, they're yours to read too.)

| Step | Script (`pipeline/`) | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `render_pages.py` | Renders the PDF pages to images |
| 2 | `ink.py`, `segment.py`, `segment_all.py` | Separates the blue ink from the paper, ruled lines, red margin and back-page bleed-through, then splits pages into words and letter groups |
| 3 | `labels/*.txt` | Transcriptions of 704 words by word id (`12: packets`, `{0:W}` to assign one group directly, `\?` for a literal ?) |
| 4 | `harvest.py` | Matches transcriptions to letter groups. Where letters touch, a dynamic-programming alignment recovers the single letters. Output: 2,479 samples normalized to baseline and x-height |
| 5 | `select_samples.py` | Ranks each letter's samples by typicality and photo sharpness |
| 6 | `candidates.py`, `strokes.py` | Skeleton → pen centerline graph → smoothing (strokes joined through crossings) |
| 7 | `design/picks.json`, `design.py`, `construct.py` | The chosen variants, height normalization, and letters built from parts of the hand (G, J, X, most punctuation, accents, ← ↑ ↓) |
| 8 | `build_font.py` | Round-nib rendering → potrace → TrueType, metrics, `calt`/`ss01`/`kern`, WOFF/WOFF2 |
| – | `verify.py`, `preview.py`, `grid.py`, `make_specimen.py` | Checks (HarfBuzz + FreeType) and the specimen page |

evidence.heading: Limitations
evidence.text:
- A few capitals (V, W, Z) had only one clean sample in the notes, so they have one variant.
- G, J, X and most punctuation were built from other parts of the hand rather than traced directly.
- No hinting: it renders well at normal web sizes on modern browsers, but it isn't tuned for tiny text on old Windows ClearType.

kind_reason.text: AI辅助从个人笔记制作的字体及可复用制作流水线。

summary.text: Harshpreet Hand 展示将120页手写笔记转成可安装字体的实践，提供网页与桌面字体、试字页面，以及提取蓝墨、分割字形的制作脚本。

value.text: 每字多种变体通过OpenType轮换，让重复字母更接近手写变化；源笔记与流水线也可供研究个人字体生成。

mechanism.text: PDF渲染后分离纸张、格线与蓝墨，再切分词及字母组，沿笔画路径重绘；calt轮换真实变体并微调高度，字距根据轮廓计算。

limitations.text: 66分钟与13.68美元为作者个案；部分大写仅一个变体，G/J/X及多数标点由其他笔画组合，未做hinting，旧系统小字号表现有限。

how_to.text: 网页加载提供的CSS，桌面应用安装Regular或Bold TTF；要制作自己的字体可参考pipeline与源PDF。

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
OmniAiLab AI 影视导演


  影视级全流程 AI 导演 Skill，也是一个会引导你做判断的创作系统
  写实与动画两类媒介并行支持　｜　30 秒短片 → 上百场次长片　｜　从剧本解析到成片交付



  
  
  
  
  



  简体中文　｜　English


> © OmniAiLab ｜ 开发者：Mochiball ｜ 平台：[omniailabx.com](https://www.omniailabx.com/)

**影视级全流程 AI 导演 Skill，也是一个会引导你做判断的创作系统。** 它不只执行流程——**开工第一件事是问清你要做什么片子**（剧情片／短剧／动画片／纪录片／宣传片／片头／MV／游戏 PV／UI 动效，各有各的路子），再让你指定导演、摄影机、布光与美学，或交由它判断；然后按影视工业标准从剧本解析一路做到成片。**写实与动画两类媒介并行支持**，体量从 30 秒短片到上百场次长片。

| 项目 | 值 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| Skill 调用名（唯一标识） | `omniailab-ai-director` | 全小写连字符写法；支持 skill 的工具直接用它调起，不支持的工具用自然语言描述也能触发（本 skill 允许隐式调用） |
| 显示名 | OmniAiLab AI 影视导演 | 仓库页面与文档里显示的名字，不是调用名 |
| 版本 | v2.4.0 | 与开源仓库、操作手册三处始终一致，每次更新同步推送 |
| 出品 / 开发者 | OmniAiLab ／ Mochiball | — |
| 许可 | MIT（见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)） | 可自由使用、修改与二次分发 |
| 配套操作手册 | [飞书文档](https://zcn03zgas1zl.feishu.cn/wiki/P2fhwADXvil24UkNkDCcw1x2nbA) ／ [Notion](https://tomatopark.notion.site/3eaa28d2e378800d8b8bee090c32c34d) | 如何调用、三步启动、逐阶段操作细则、子技能调度速查、模型口径、避坑总表、常见问题、交付物清单 |
| 开源仓库（公开） | [github.com/tomatoparkdao/omniailab-ai-director](https://github.com/tomatoparkdao/omniailab-ai-director) | 克隆即装最新版（`git clone` 到 skill 目录）；更新只需 `git pull`；发现问题欢迎在仓库提 issue |
| 官方社区 | [Discord](https://discord.gg/vdgTEpXMh3) ／ [WhatsApp](https://chat.whatsapp.com/DIiCmMcCTP94GmihRe4Nn1) | 提问求助、反馈 bug、提功能建议、分享作品、交流工作流 |

调用名是**全小写连字符**写法（`omniailab-ai-director`），不是「OmniAiLab AI 影视导演」这个显示名。支持 skill 的工具直接用调用名最稳；不支持原生 skill 的工具，用自然语言描述任务也能触发（本 skill 允许隐式调用）。

---

evidence.heading: 一句话
evidence.text:
把一份定稿剧本交给它，它会按影视工业标准从剧本解析一路带你做到成片；你在每个阶段末尾只需回答"确认"或"要改哪里"。

- **适用 · 媒介不限** —— 真人写实的影视级管线，与纯动画／2D 卡通／3D 游戏引擎渲染风格／三维＋手绘混合，都在范围内。
- **适用 · 体量不限** —— 30 秒短片、短剧单集、品牌宣传片、MV 叙事片段，到几十场甚至上百场、数十分钟至两小时以上的长片（**长片不再要求拆成多集**）。
- **默认媒介** —— 真人实拍影视级写实质感（不指定时按此执行）。动画／混合媒介项目由 P1 先做「媒介判定」并写进「全片风格锁定」，此后以该声明为全片唯一媒介口径：造型、笔触、运动与光线按**动画与混合媒介层**执行——运动遵守**动画原理**（挤压拉伸／预备动作／跟随重叠／弧形轨迹／夸张），物理正确让位于运动表现力。

---

evidence.heading: 能力一览
evidence.text:
**它不是"一个跑流程的模板"，而是一套会提问、会提案、会把形容词翻译成参数的创作系统。**

| 层面 | 具体有什么 |
|---|---|
| **① 入口会引导，不等你懂** | 开工先判定**作品形态**：剧情片／短剧／动画片／纪录片／宣传片／片头／MV／游戏 PV／UI 动效／达人视频／教育——每种形态走不同的线。你说不清时**只问三个问题**收敛（放哪放、里面的人是真实的还是演出来的、核心要交付什么），三问定不下来**不硬猜**，给"最短可交付"的建议让你拍板。 |
| **② 创作决策可点菜，也可托付** | **20 位导演预设**（单选或混搭：一位主导演决定全片基准，另可借 1–2 位指定维度）· **五维机位坐标**（6 机型格式 × 11 镜头性格 × 6 焦段 × 3 景深 × 20 运动）· **33 套布光 × 5 种色温变体** · **7 套成片级美学配方**（A01–A07）· **D／P／C／R／S 画风词汇**。全部可以由你点，也可以交给它判断——你说不清时，它按作品类型先给 2–3 个候选和理由。 |
| **③ 专业在机制，不在形容词** | **导演式推理**：选一位导演＝加载他处理空间／机位／光影／时间／潜文本的底层机制；每位都写明**「反例」**——与最容易混的相邻导演的**机制差异**（例如库布里克用广角把人压进建筑、芬奇用长焦把人切成样本，**两者的背景要求正好相反**）。**调度反查表**：按**作品类型 16 类／场景 22 类／人物 16 类／剧情节点 18 个**直接给机位与布光方案。**提示词 16 段固定块序 ＋ 十一条铁律**（"否定即召唤""几何绑画框不绑物件""把难的东西放进静帧"）。**资产体系**：成对资产、统一命名、状态管理、声音锁定。 |
| **④ 有真实项目背书** | **6 个商业级实战案例**（写实短片／长片／动画，含成品提示词块与「问题 → 解法」清单）· **49 张方法配图**（关键词反查索引，最难讲清的部分直接给图）· **7 条真实成片样例**（逐字原文 ＋ 拆解）· **14 个宣传片方向细则**（品牌广告／片头／动态视觉／游戏 PV／UI 动效／MV／达人视频／教育／视频拆解／音色克隆等）。拿不准怎么写，直接照抄成品块。 |
| **⑤ 全链路到成片** | P0 项目接收 → P0A 十项剧本解析与全片情绪曲线 → P1 摄影色彩与声音创作基准 → P2 角色与关键道具母板 → P3 场景资产与环境色卡 → P4 分镜设计与首帧 → P5 视频提示词与画布参数 → P6 在 **OmniAiLab 无限画布**中生成、剪辑、导出成片。**每阶段末尾一次确认门**，你只需回答"确认"或"第 X 处要改"。 |
| **⑥ 宣传片类会先帮你选通道** | 同一支宣传片／产品片／发布视频／功能演示，有两条路：**生成通道**（画面由模型生成，在 OmniAiLab 画布选 **MiniMax H3**）与**代码渲染通道**（真实页面截图 ＋ 代码逐帧渲染，画面 100% 可控，还能回交可编辑工程）。两条**并列且可接力**。它**先给判断、再给选项**：按**五个判据**（画面主角是真人实景还是界面数据／要不要分毫不差／有没有可截图的真实界面／要不要逐帧可控／时长与投放）报出倾向，并**说清代价**；**定形态时只报倾向、不展开**，**素材核完后、进分镜前正式确认并锁定**。场景覆盖**按画面主角分四类**（人为主体／物为主体／屏为主体／混合），含企业形象／TVC／公益／城市／招聘／产品广告／软件发布／功能演示／数据可视化／电视包装／大屏循环，并给出**混合接力分工**（会动的真人实物走生成、屏幕上的一切走代码渲染）。代码渲染侧自带 **157 张动效镜头配方卡**、七份规则文档、可跑工程模板与 **154 份音效素材**；**不适用的片子会明确说不，并给你替代路线**。 |
| **⑦ 判断有出处，不靠形容词** | **电影艺术知识层**：由电影艺术领域著作系统梳理成的**判断与来源层**——**15 个能力域**（读本到讲戏／剧本与叙事／选角与讲戏／视听语言／场面调度／分镜／剪辑／声音／光线／美术造型／类型／制片／方法与心法／

evidence.heading: 一、装到哪：按你用的工具
evidence.text:
把**整个 `omniailab-ai-director` 文件夹**（含 `SKILL.md`、`VERSION`、`openai.yaml`、`references/`、`examples/`）放进下面对应的目录，重开一个新会话即可生效。

| 工具 | 放哪里 | 怎么调起 |
|---|---|---|
| **Codex**（推荐主用） | 没有原生 skill 目录：把文件夹放进项目，例如 `<你的项目>/skills/omniailab-ai-director/`，再在项目根目录的 `AGENTS.md` 里加一行：`影视制作任务：先读 skills/omniailab-ai-director/SKILL.md，并按其流程执行。` | 说"按 SKILL.md 开始做片子"。它读 `AGENTS.md` 后会加载这个 skill。 |
| **Claude / Claude Code** | 个人级：`~/.claude/skills/omniailab-ai-director/`项目级：`<你的项目>/.claude/skills/omniailab-ai-director/` | 输入 **`/omniailab-ai-director`**；或直接描述任务（如"照这份剧本走完整影视流程"），它会按描述命中并加载。 |
| **WorkBuddy** | 用户级（全局可用）：`~/.workbuddy/skills/omniailab-ai-director/`项目级（只在该项目可用）：`<你的项目>/.workbuddy/skills/omniailab-ai-director/` | 新开会话后它出现在技能列表里；直接说 **`$omniailab-ai-director 开始`**。 |
| **OmniAiLab**（omniailabx） | [官网下载](https://www.omniailabx.com/plugin#desktop-download)（Windows 本地版 0.8.27，含安装版与免安装便携版；版本以官网为准），或[网盘备用](https://pan.baidu.com/s/12Wtj8pAKmXOGgWN-M07v7A?pwd=2gff)（提取码 `2gff`）；安装后把整个文件夹放进它的 **技能目录**（客户端内可查看技能目录位置） | 新开会话后它出现在技能列表里；直接说 **`$omniailab-ai-director 开始`**。 |

> **必须整个文件夹一起复制，不能只拷 SKILL.md。** 四个子技能（ACTING / EMOTION / LIRA / CINEDANCE）、全部专项层（COMBAT 打斗 / BLOCKING 站位 / AESTHETICS 美学 / PROMPT-DOCTRINE 提示词教义 / ASSET-SYSTEM 资产体系 / SCENE-ENGINE 剧本引擎 / OPTICS 光学 / FEATURE-PRODUCTION 长片工程 / MUSIC-SCENE 音乐场景 / ANIMATION 动画 / DOCUMENTARY 纪实 / PROMO 宣传片线 / ONBOARDING 入门引导 / MOTION-STUDIO 动效工作室）、视觉语言库、7 套现成提示词、纪实模板、**宣传片 14 个方向的完整细则**、**7 条宣传片成品样例**、**机位与布光索引**与 **49 张案例配图**，全都放在 `references/` 与 `examples/` 里；少拷一个目录，运行时就会断链。

**克隆安装（推荐）**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tomatoparkdao/omniailab-ai-director.git \
  ~/.workbuddy/skills/omniailab-ai-director
```

仓库是**公开仓库**，始终与最新版 skill 同步；以后更新只需在该目录执行 `git pull`。发现问题也可以在仓库里提 issue。

evidence.heading: 二、剧本从哪来（三选一）
evidence.text:
1. **你直接上传定稿剧本** —— 它读取后直接进入 P0。
2. **什么都不给，直接说"开始"** —— 它会先问一句"手上是已有剧本，还是只有一句创意？"，**不会自动载入内置剧本**；只有你明确说"跑默认项目"时，才用内置样例剧本《17楼》（30 秒悬疑短片）。
3. **只给一句话创意或标题**（例如"做一个太空惊悚短片"）—— 它先自动写出一版定稿剧本给你确认，确认后才进 P0。剧本时长控制在 30 秒 – 5 分钟。

evidence.heading: 三、启动指令
evidence.text:
```text
$omniailab-ai-director 开始
```

直接说"开始"即可，它**不会**反问"请问你的剧本是什么"，而是直接问"你手上有剧本，还是只有一句创意？"。

**默认不会自动跑内置剧本**；只有当你说下面这类话时，才使用内置样例剧本（30 秒悬疑短片《17楼》）：

```text
跑默认项目
做《17楼》
```

evidence.heading: 四、启动前必须想清楚的两件事
evidence.text:
- **剧情必须是定稿。** 它只处理已定稿剧情，不改戏、不加角色、不加台词、不改结局。中途大改剧情（尤其涉及角色或场景增删）会让前面已生成的资产全部作废。
- **交付规格先定好。** 默认 1080p / 16:9 / 24fps / MP4。要做竖屏或方屏（手机端、产品包装图等），请在 P1 就提出来——P1 之后改规格同样会导致资产返工。

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image-ext", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()

while True:

    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

evidence.heading: 仓库简介

evidence.heading: Hermes Deck
evidence.text:
Hermes Deck is a desktop app for [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent). It lets you chat with
your Hermes agents, see what they are doing right now (thinking, tools, sub-agents), steer or stop them, and keep an
eye on usage and subscription limits, all from one window on your Windows or macOS computer. It connects to the
Hermes instance you already run, over SSH, WSL or locally, through a small Hermes plugin. An optional relay on the
Hermes host adds a live view of every agent, host-wide usage, and letting agents use a browser or one window on your
computer, both off until you allow them. Telegram is optional.


  
    Needs you: approvals and questions from every agent in one inbox
    Bot Chat: every profile has its own chat and personality
  
  
    Telegram mode: your account, your bots, your group topics
    Desktop control: watch an agent work in one window, take control any time
  
  
    Agent browsers: the agent's own browser tab, live on your device
    Themes: dark, light and OLED themes, wallpapers, reading preferences

evidence.heading: Option A: give it to your Hermes
evidence.text:
Hermes Deck ships a setup skill that your own Hermes agent can follow on its host. Give your agent this prompt:

> Install Hermes Deck on this host from https://github.com/Hermes-Deck/hermes-deck. Use its
> skills/hermes-deck-setup skill. Ask me before changing any profile or starting services.

The skill checks your Hermes installation, shows the plugin installer's plan before applying it, optionally sets up
the relay, and prints the values to enter in the app. It asks before every change and never restarts a busy
gateway. Your agent can read it from a clone, or you can install it into Hermes first:

```bash
hermes skills install Hermes-Deck/hermes-deck/skills/hermes-deck-setup
```

To check a host at any time, run the read-only doctor from a clone with Hermes' Python:
`<hermes-python> scripts/doctor.py` (`--json` for agents, `--home <hermes-home>`, `--relay http://<relay-host>:9330`).
Details and the manual equivalent: [docs/install-with-hermes.md](docs/install-with-hermes.md).

Then install the desktop app (step 2 below) and complete its first-start setup (step 3).

evidence.heading: Option B: manual
evidence.text:
**1. Install the plugin on the Hermes host.** From a clone of this repository, with Hermes' own Python (the
interpreter of your Hermes installation):

```bash
cd hermes-plugin/hermes-deck
<hermes-python> install.py --dry-run   # shows the plan, changes nothing
<hermes-python> install.py
```

The installer backs up each changed `config.yaml`, enables `hermes-deck` in the selected profiles (`--profile NAME`,
default: all) and writes the direct-connection entry point to `<Hermes home>/hermes-deck/stream.py` (normally
`~/.hermes/hermes-deck/stream.py`). Restart each affected gateway only when its foreground and background work has
finished; a restart also ends background sub-agents. Options: [plugin README](hermes-plugin/hermes-deck/README.md).

**2. Install the desktop app.** Download from [Releases](https://github.com/Hermes-Deck/hermes-deck/releases/latest):

| System | File |
|---|---|
| Windows x64 | `Hermes-Deck-<version>-Setup.exe` (recommended) or `Hermes-Deck-<version>-win-x64.zip` |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `Hermes-Deck-<version>-mac-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS Intel | `Hermes-Deck-<version>-mac-x64.dmg` |

Builds are not code-signed (macOS builds are ad-hoc signed, not notarized). Check the download against the release's
`SHA256SUMS.txt` first:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\Hermes-Deck-<version>-Setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
```

```bash
shasum -a 256 Hermes-Deck-<version>-mac-arm64.dmg
```

On Windows, Setup installs per user without admin rights and adds Start menu and Desktop shortcuts (Windows
notifications need the Start menu shortcut). On macOS, drag the app to Applications. SmartScreen or Gatekeeper asks
once; approve only a download you verified.

**3. First-start setup.** The app walks you through:

1. **Chat modes**: Telegram, Sessions, Bots or a combination, and

evidence.heading: Updating
evidence.text:
- **Desktop app:** **Settings → General → Updates**. On Windows, Deck downloads the new installer, checks it against
  `SHA256SUMS.txt` and installs it. On macOS, install the new DMG from the release page.
- **Relay and plugin:** update them on the Hermes host to the same version as the app. The app tells you when they
  are behind and shows the command. See [docs/updating.md](docs/updating.md).

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
- Hermes Agent at or above the version in [`compat.json`](compat.json) (`minHermes`), on Linux, macOS or WSL.
- Python 3.10+ with PyYAML for the plugin installer (Hermes' own Python has it).
- Node.js 22.13+ for the relay.
- Windows x64 or macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) for the desktop app.
- For Telegram mode only: your own API keys from [my.telegram.org](https://my.telegram.org/apps).
- For agent desktops only: Docker (Docker Desktop, Docker Engine or colima) on the computer that hosts them.

App, relay and plugin share one version; run the same version of each. Full matrix and the version/protocol rules:
[docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md).

```python
import os, time, requests

HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
```

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"flux-kontext-pro","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "flux-kontext-pro", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

Runnable versions: [`examples/`](examples). The task lifecycle is `pending → processing → completed | failed`.

evidence.heading: Get started
evidence.text:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/Okohedeki/scroll-studio && cd scroll-studio
pip install -e .
studio doctor                         # what this machine can build
studio build examples/cellwright-bio  # live 3D: needs nothing but Python
studio preview cellwright-bio         # http://localhost:5173
studio ui                             # the Studio app: http://localhost:5180
```

| What you build | What it needs |
|---|---|

evidence.heading: Build with Claude
evidence.text:
Open the repo in Claude Code and ask for a site. The `scroll-studio` MCP server (`.mcp.json`) gives Claude every
engine tool, and the `scroll-site` skill gives it the workflow. Or paste this into any coding agent:

```text
Install Scroll Studio on this machine and build one of its examples, following
https://github.com/Okohedeki/scroll-studio/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md
```


Make your own site

```bash
studio new my-site                 # a starter site.yaml
studio directions my-site          # six art directions; --pick one
studio storyboard my-site --edit   # sketches, stills and an animatic before any video render
studio build my-site               # cached stage by stage: change one thing, rebuild one thing
studio inspect my-site             # pops, softness, halos and drift in every film
studio publish my-site --out site  # one static folder for GitHub Pages or any host
```

The whole workflow is in the [guide](docs/guide.md).

evidence.text:
An autonomous, always-on agent on your phone.
It has its own browser, keeps a wiki memory of everything it learns about you, and hands the heavy jobs to your own machines.
You bring the model. Paste an API key, or sign in with the ChatGPT or Claude plan you already pay for.

The best thing since Hermes.

[Get the APK](https://github.com/Past-da-king/agent/releases/latest) | [Watch it work](https://past-da-king.github.io/agent/) | [Build it from source](#build-from-source)

Free and open source, MIT. No account, no subscription, no server of ours.

evidence.heading: What it looks like
evidence.text: Home, chat, memory, routines. The two demo recordings are on the [project page](https://past-da-king.github.io/agent/).

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
It is not on the Play Store. You sideload the APK.

1. Open [Releases](https://github.com/Past-da-king/agent/releases/latest) and download `Agent-0.11.14.apk` on your phone.
2. Tap the file and allow the install when Android asks. That is the whole sideload.
3. Open Agent, give it a name, pick how it looks, then pick how to power it. See [Setup](#setup).
4. On a Samsung, Xiaomi or OnePlus phone, set the app's battery to **Unrestricted** under Settings, or Android will kill the browser and the routines while they work.

You need Android 10 or newer on an arm64 phone, which is every phone sold in the last few years. The APK is about 360 MB because the Node runtime, Codex and Claude Code ship inside it, so leave room for that and for its data.

evidence.heading: What it can actually do
evidence.text:
**It goes and looks.** The agent drives its own built-in browser. It cannot control your existing Chrome tabs, so you sign in to your sites inside it. That browser runs in a foreground service, so it keeps working while you are in another app or the screen is off. When a site throws a captcha or a sign-in at it, it hands the page to you and carries on when you are done. Profiles keep Personal and Work apart, and helper agents can split a big job up.

**It remembers you.** Everything it learns gets a page in a wiki on the phone, linked to the pages around it. Read it, change it, pin it or delete it. Nothing is kept that you cannot see.

**It runs on a clock.** A routine can fire at a set time, on a new email, or the moment an app you chose sends a notification. It can watch a price for weeks and only speak up when it actually moves.

**It uses the accounts you have.** Apps connect through [Composio](https://composio.dev) with your own key: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Slack and a few hundred more. It asks to connect one only when a job needs it, and the sign-in opens inside the app. You can hold several accounts per app, like two Outlooks or four Gmails.

**It hands heavy work to a real computer.** Any server or PC you can SSH into becomes a machine it can use. Run a command, start a long job that keeps going in the background, move files both ways. Looking around just runs. Anything that changes the machine shows you the exact command first.

**It answers in voice, and reads your files.** Voice notes in and out, live calls if you add a Gemini key, photos and documents in chat, including scanned PDFs read on the device.

**It tidies up overnight.** At 02:00, and only while charging and online, it sorts its memory, writes notes from the day and builds your morning screen.

**I

evidence.heading: What it is not
evidence.text:
- Not a product. No account, no subscription, nobody to pay.
- Not on the Play Store, so nobody at Google has looked at it. Read the source, or build it yourself, if that matters to you.
- Not finished. It has mostly been tested on one Samsung phone, and live voice calls are the newest part.
- Not faultless. It is an agent with a browser and access to whatever you connect, so it will get things wrong. Read what you approve.
- Not for everyone yet. It expects you to be comfortable sideloading an APK and pasting a key.

evidence.heading: Permissions and privacy
evidence.text:
Nothing is read until you allow it. Location, files, notifications and the rest are asked for at the moment a job needs them, and the app runs with all of them denied. The one most people want is notifications, and even then you pick the apps it may read, one at a time, and take it back whenever you like.

- Keys are stored on the phone in `EncryptedSharedPreferences`, locked by the Android Keystore.
- Memory, tasks, routines and chat live in a Room database on the phone.
- Traffic leaves the phone only to the model you picked, the sites the agent browses, Composio if you added a key, your voice provider if you added one, and the machines you added.
- Machine secrets stay encrypted on the phone and the agent only ever sees a machine's name. A machine is pinned the first time you connect, and refused if its identity changes later.

evidence.heading: How it works, in short
evidence.text:
- Kotlin and Jetpack Compose (Material 3 Expressive), Room, WorkManager.
- On the API key path, a provider-neutral agent loop in Kotlin that speaks both chat formats.
- On the subscription path, Node 24 (Termux's Android build) ships inside the APK as `lib*.so` files, because Android only lets an app execute files from its native library folder, and the Agent SDK runs on it. Codex and Claude Code ship the same way as their arm64 musl builds; Claude Code gets the musl loader as `libldmusl.so`, and a local proxy resolves DNS for both. The app's own tools are served to them over a local MCP server on `127.0.0.1` with a per-install token.
- The browser is an Android WebView hosted in a foreground service.

evidence.heading: Community Applications
evidence.text:
- [Code Déjà Vu](https://github.com/shashankbudem/code-dejavu) - Local cross-repository function search and similarity warnings through a non-blocking Git pre-commit hook; supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Rust functions of at least five lines, skips tests, and requires Python 3.10+ plus a model download.
- [Daemon](https://github.com/iamartyaa/daemon) - macOS 14+ Apple silicon app for capturing selected text, screenshots, files, and voice notes with a hotkey and recalling them by meaning; uses local llama.cpp, with unnotarized releases.
- [drive-lens](https://github.com/xcspl/drive-lens) - Search shared Google Drive photos, video previews, and PDFs with local EmbeddingGemma2 vectors and a Windows/macOS/Linux desktop app; requires an anyone-with-the-link folder and a separate vision LLM for descriptions, with previews sent to the provider when hosted.
- [GemSearch](https://github.com/IndigoJay/GemSearch) - Local photo and screenshot search for Linux with text, image, or combined image-and-text queries, a CLI, and a browser UI; defaults to NVIDIA CUDA with a CPU option, and needs an initial model download before offline use.
- [Local Search](https://github.com/btroussel/SemanticSearchMCP) - macOS local file search with MCP access for coding assistants; the app is not notarized, and snippets sent to cloud assistants leave the device.
- [MediaIndex](https://github.com/harsheetamorey/mediaindex) - macOS 13+ Apple silicon app for local image, audio, and video search with EmbeddingGemma2, plus object counting and photo editing via separate models; unsigned app, with extra model downloads for editing.
- [Mitsuke](https://github.com/kanaworksai-hue/mitsuke) - Local image and video-shot search on Apple silicon via MLX, using text, example images, or both; supports RAW

evidence.heading: Fine-tuning and Decision Models
evidence.text:
- [EG2 Typed Decision](https://huggingface.co/mrm8488/embeddinggemma-2-ft-typed-decision) - EmbeddingGemma2 text encoder with a roughly 0.5M-parameter head for `choice`, `noul` (Boolean), and `score` decisions with probabilities; includes weights, inference code, and further fine-tuning examples.
- [Typed Decisions](https://huggingface.co/datasets/LocalLLaMA/typed-decisions) - Training and evaluation data used by the model above, covering agent checks, support tickets, invoices, and security incidents; metrics measure agreement with teacher labels.
- [Typed Decision GGUF](https://huggingface.co/cstr/embeddinggemma-2-ft-typed-decision-GGUF) - Complete fine-tuned encoder and decision head in FP32/Q8 GGUF; requires CrispEmbed rather than stock llama.cpp, with only small-scale numerical parity checks reported.
- [Typed Decision Core ML](https://github.com/mikolaj92/embeddinggemma-typed-decisions-coreml) - Adaptation of the same fine-tuned model for macOS 15+ Apple silicon, without retraining; locally converted Core ML encoder uses CPU/Neural Engine with the original FP32 decision head on CPU, fixed token buckets, and overlength rejection.

The model author selected hyperparameters while inspecting the test split; its fine-tuned results are not directly comparable with the dataset's zero-shot leaderboard.

Core ML adaptation checked **2026-10-14** against its documentation and implementation; author-reported parity checks do not establish task accuracy or exclusive Neural Engine execution.

- [Multimodal Typed Decision](https://huggingface.co/Danny-Dasilva/embeddinggemma-2-multimodal-typed-decision) - EmbeddingGemma2 fine-tune for text, image, and video choice, Boolean, and ordinal decisions, with optional object-box localisation; requires the bundled runtime and is primaril

evidence.heading: Decision Application Examples
evidence.text: - [EmbeddingGemma2 Jeff](https://github.com/karimtn/embeddingGemma2-jeff) - Node.js examples for support intent classification, spam detection, and triage using Transformers.js and ONNX embeddings; matches labeled examples by cosine similarity without fine-tuning or a trained decision head.

evidence.heading: Guides and examples
evidence.text:
- [Text embeddings with Sentence Transformers](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/embeddinggemma/inference-embeddinggemma-with-sentence-transformers) - Official text retrieval walkthrough.
- [Multimodal embeddings with Sentence Transformers](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/embeddinggemma/multimodal-embeddinggemma-with-sentence-transformers) - Media and mixed-input examples.
- [Official multimodal fine-tuning guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/embeddinggemma/fine-tuning-multimodal-embeddinggemma-with-sentence-transformers) - Text-to-image retrieval training with cross-modal triplets and Sentence Transformers, including before/after evaluation; requires a BF16-capable GPU.
- [Transformers model documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/embedding_gemma2) - Lower-level model and processor APIs.
- [Minimal multimodal search](https://github.com/ranjankndev/embeddinggemma2-search) - A small Python example for local text, image, audio, and video retrieval using NumPy vectors, without a database or UI.
- [Gemma-Lens](https://github.com/johnrobinsn/gemma-lens) - Text, microphone, and image-query demo over COCO images and ESC-50 audio using direct cosine search, with a [step-by-step article](https://www.storminthecastle.com/posts/gemma_lens/); runs on CPU or CUDA, and ESC-50 audio is non-commercial.
- [UI Search](https://github.com/sai-prakash/ui-screenshot-search) - Browser text/screenshot search across sample components, IBM Carbon, and GitHub Primer, with a reusable Storybook indexer; screenshot retrieval accuracy remains unmeasured.

The Sentence Transformers tutorials require **6.1.0+**.

evidence.heading: What's New in 0.50.0
evidence.text:
- 🧠 **Dynamic Adaptive Concurrency & Timeout Engine (`pagesift::adaptive`)**:
  - **Bottleneck-Constrained Model ($\min$ Principal)**: Concurrency is strictly bounded by the intersection of CPU capacity, physical memory safety (2MB/conn), and OS file descriptors (`ulimit -n`):
    $$\text{Concurrency} = \min\big(C_{cpu},\; M_{mem},\; FD_{safe}\big)$$
  - **Auto-Configuring Hardware Profiles**: Micro (1C1GB), Small (2C2GB~4C4GB), Mid Desktop (8C16GB / i7-10700), High Server (32C128GB / AMD EPYC), and Extreme Supernode (64C+ 128GB+ FD>=65k).
  - **Dual Operational Modes**: `--tuning-mode adaptive` (saturates hardware safely) vs. `--tuning-mode conservative` (caps CPU < 20% for background workstation tasks).
  - **RTT-Aware Safe Timeout**: Calibrated 3.5s connect timeout and 10.0s total timeout, preventing drops of high-latency international websites.
- 🌐 **Dual-Protocol Firecrawl v1 & v2 Architecture**: Drop-in compatibility with official Firecrawl Python and Node.js SDKs covering `/v1/scrape`, `/v1/crawl`, `/v1/batch/scrape`, `/v1/map` and all `/v2/*` endpoints.
- ⚡ **Jina Reader Protocol Adapter**: Instant URL scraping via `GET /r/{*url}` or `POST /r`, with Server-Sent Events (`Accept: text/event-stream`) streaming for real-time LLM agent feeds.
- 🛡️ **128 GB Server & Chaos Defense**: Flat 188.4 MB memory across 100,000 live websites and zero memory leaks under 50,000 chaos URLs while Spider crashed from 11.7 GB OOM.
- 🦀 **100% Pure Safe Rust & Modular Architecture**: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` preserved across all core crates. All modified and created `.rs` source files strictly `<= 500 lines`.

evidence.heading: Architectural Highlights
evidence.text:
- **Segmented Bounded Frontier:** Memory does not scale with crawl depth. Even with 100,000 URLs, backpressure and bounded queues prevent out-of-memory disasters.
- **Dynamic Hardware Adaptive Tuning:** Detects system resources and calculates the safe theoretical saturation point without crashing or exhausting sockets.
- **Selective Rendering Pipeline:** Automatically detects static vs dynamic pages; executes headless Chrome *only* when dynamic JavaScript hydration provides net content gains.
- **SSRF & Sandbox Defense:** Strict private IP filtering, DNS-rebinding guards, and perpetual browser sandboxing ensure zero local network exposure.
- **Ethical Politeness:** Per-host token buckets, automatic robots.txt compliance, and RFC-compliant User-Agent identification.

**Why teams call FLUX 2 Max (`flux-2-max`) through APIMart**

- **One key, entire catalog.** The same `https://api.apimart.ai/v1` base URL and `Authorization` header reach FLUX 2 Max (`flux-2-max`) and 300+ other image, video and language models — switch the `model` field, not your client.
- **$1 minimum, pay as you go.** No subscription and no prepaid plan to size up front: top up from $1 and spend it on calls.
- **The charge comes back in the response.** Every completed task reports the amount billed (`cost` / `credits_cost`); a task marked `failed` is refunded.
- **Async by design.** Submit, take the `task_id`, poll `GET /v1/tasks/{id}` — batching and retries are ordinary queue work, not a bespoke integration.



FLUX 2 Max is the top FLUX 2 tier, priced per megapixel of output.

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"flux-2-max","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "flux-2-max", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```
