evidence.heading: BabyTalk
evidence.text:
**BabyTalk** is a software library that lets an ESP32-S3 or ESP32-P4 **understand what you
say and talk back, with no cloud and no internet**, from C, MicroPython, or Erlang/Elixir on
AtomVM:

```python
import stt, tts
text = stt.transcribe(pcm)                 # 16 kHz audio -> "what's the weather like today"
audio = tts.say("You said: " + text)       # text -> 24 kHz audio for the speaker
# lcd.text(text, 0, 0)                     # or send the text anywhere: a screen, LoRa, MQTT...
```

**Memory, bottom line:** speech to text needs **6 MB of flash** and **84.5 KB of internal
RAM**; text to speech adds **1.9 MB of flash**. Each borrows a few hundred KB of **PSRAM**
while it works.

| | flash | PSRAM | internal RAM |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Speech to text** (4-bit model) | 6.0 MB: the model, read in place | 0.2 MB, transcribing 4 s (more for longer clips) | 84.5 KB, shared with text to speech |
| **Text to speech** (nano voice) | 1.9 MB: voice 0.34 MB, pronunciations 1.5 MB | 0.5 MB, a 4 s reply | the same 84.5 KB |

- The speech model is **never copied into RAM**: the chip reads it from flash as it runs.
- The two take turns with one 84.5 KB block of internal RAM, and that block can live in
  PSRAM instead (a little slower). Under MicroPython, text to speech also keeps 104 KB of
  buffers in internal RAM; the AtomVM firmware puts them in PSRAM.
- Bigger and better: the 8-bit speech model (9.8 MB of flash, more accurate), and on the
  ESP32-P4 the much better-sounding `heart` voice (2.4 MB of flash, loaded into PSRAM).
  Every option: [Models](#models). The full breakdown: [Performance and memory](#performance-and-memory).

Made by Thomas Lackner and Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). MIT licensed; the speech models
belong to their authors (see [Credits and licenses](#credits-

evidence.heading: Is this for you?
evidence.text:
Most "voice on ESP32" projects do one of two things:

- **send the audio to a cloud service** (Whisper API, Google, wit.ai) and wait for text, or
- **recognize a fixed list of commands or wake words** that were trained in advance
  (e.g. ESP-SR's MultiNet, Edge Impulse / TensorFlow Lite Micro keyword spotting).

BabyTalk is different: a **general-purpose English speech recognizer** that runs
entirely on the chip. It transcribes *any* sentence, with no training and no command list.
A wake phrase is any phrase you type ("wake up, tomato face"), also with no training.
Optionally the same firmware **speaks** replies with an on-device neural voice.

You'll want it if you need voice input that keeps working offline, keeps audio private, or
can't depend on a server. For example:

- **Radios without keyboards.** A LoRa node (Meshtastic, or your own protocol) with a
  microphone but no keyboard: speak a message, and the node sends it as text. A spoken
  sentence becomes a few dozen bytes of text; even a very low-bitrate voice codec (Codec2
  at 700 bit/s) needs about ten times that, which matters on a link that moves a few
  hundred bytes per second at best.
- **Speakers without screens.** The receiving node reads incoming text messages aloud.
- **Voice control that works when the WiFi doesn't**, and never sends audio anywhere.

Skip it if you need very high accuracy, languages other than English, or it has to run on
a smaller chip (see below).

(This may also be the only project that involves both **LoRa** radios and **LoRA**,
Low-Rank Adaptation. The original research plan in `docs/historical/` explored LoRA-style
expert adapters for the speech model. They aren't used yet.)

evidence.heading: What you need
evidence.text:
- **An ESP32-S3 or ESP32-P4** with 16 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM (e.g. an S3 "N16R8" module).
  The P4 transcribes about 1.7 times faster (2 s of speech in 0.30 s, against 0.51 s) and
  can run a larger, better-sounding voice. BabyTalk runs on:
  - **Waveshare ESP32-S3-CAM** (ES7210 mic, ES8311 speaker codec): the reference board;
    everything is measured on it, from MicroPython and AtomVM
    ([docs/BOARD_WAVESHARE_S3_CAM.md](docs/BOARD_WAVESHARE_S3_CAM.md))
  - **Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6** (ES8311 mic and speaker codec), from AtomVM
    ([docs/BOARD_WAVESHARE_P4_WIFI6.md](docs/BOARD_WAVESHARE_P4_WIFI6.md))
  - **LilyGO T-LoRa Pager** (ES8311), from AtomVM, with its own audio driver
  - **Elecrow CrowPanel Advance 7.0"** (PDM mic), from AtomVM, speech to text only
- **A microphone**, for speech to text: anything that gives 16 kHz PCM.
- **A speaker**, for text to speech (optional).
- **To build:** Linux or WSL, [ESP-IDF v5.5.1](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/v5.5.1/esp32s3/get-started/),
  and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for the Python tools. (AtomVM also needs
  Erlang/OTP 26+ and Elixir 1.17+.)

evidence.heading: Speech to text
evidence.text:
NVIDIA's [Citrinet-256](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/stt_en_citrinet_256_ls), compressed
to 4 or 8 bits, in two versions: the original, and one fine-tuned for background noise.
All four are ready to flash from [`models/`](models/) (SHA-256, licence and how each was made:
[`models/README.md`](models/README.md)).

| file | flash | noisy rooms* | clean speech** | fits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`citrinet256_int4.mmrt`** (default) | **6.0 MB** | 58.1% | **8.2%** | the standard 6 MB model partition |
| `citrinet256_int8.mmrt` | 9.8 MB | 51.5% | 6.3% | a 10 MB model partition |
| `citrinet256_noisy_int4.mmrt` | 6.0 MB | 42.7% | 11.8% | the standard 6 MB model partition |
| `citrinet256_noisy_int8.mmrt` | 9.8 MB | **33.8%** | 7.8% | a 10 MB model partition |

Word error rate, lower is better. \*82 recordings made on the boards with music, highway
noise or a coffee-shop loop in the background (see [Training for the real
world](#training-for-the-real-world-work-in-progress)). \*\*LibriSpeech test-clean (clean,
read English); the original full-precision model scores 3.8%.

**The `noisy` models are an alternative, not an upgrade:** a quarter to a third fewer words
wrong with noise in the room, more wrong on clean speech. Pick by where the board will
listen. They are the same size as the originals, and need no firmware or code change: the
file records its own format.

Wake phrases need no model of their own: the speech model's output is scored against the
phrase.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text: All three ways in share one engine (`components/`) and give the same transcripts.

evidence.heading: How it works
evidence.text:
```
mic -> 16 kHz audio -> log-mel features -> Citrinet-256 (neural net) -> letters/word pieces -> text
                                                                      \-> wake phrase score
text -> pronunciation dictionary -> phonemes -> sanoTTS voice -> 24 kHz audio -> speaker
```

- **Speech to text** uses NVIDIA's Citrinet-256, a 9.8-million-parameter recognizer
  trained on 960 hours of English audiobooks. It outputs text directly ("CTC"), so it has
  no vocabulary list to maintain.
- **Wake phrases**: the same model output is scored against your phrase's spellings, so
  any phrase works. `export/kws_validate.py` checks a phrase against hours of other speech
  to pick a threshold that avoids false wakes.
- **Text to speech** uses a sanoTTS voice. It is optional: the firmware builds without it.

evidence.heading: Limitations
evidence.text:
- English only, 16 kHz audio. Transcription starts after you stop talking (no live
  streaming), and it is best with one speaker at a time close to the mic.
- Background noise still costs a lot: the `noisy` models get a third to two fifths of the
  words wrong in our noisy recordings, and trade away some clean-speech accuracy to do it.
- The 4-bit model trades ~2 points of accuracy for size (see [Models](#models)).
- The tiny voice is clear but clearly synthetic, and mispronounces some words.
- MicroPython is tested on one board (the Waveshare ESP32-S3-CAM), AtomVM on the four in
  [What you need](#what-you-need). From AtomVM, another board with the same audio chips
  (ES7210/ES8311) needs only its pins, set at run time (`babytalk:audio_config/1`); other chips need a C driver
  (`board_audio.h`). MicroPython's drivers (`mpy/drivers/`) work on the I2C bus and I2S port
  your script opens, so their pins are already yours to choose.
- Listening and speaking take turns (they share one block of internal RAM).
- Under MicroPython, speech to text can't run while WiFi is on: WiFi takes the internal RAM
  it needs (6.7 KB left). The AtomVM firmware keeps ~42 KB with WiFi up and can.

github_projects.description: 🔥 Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
github_projects.description_zh: 🔥 Orbia：生成的视频能否构成一致的三维世界？

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: 🔥 Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?

evidence.heading: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
evidence.text:
[](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.20693)
[](https://orbia-bench.github.io/)
[](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Orbia/Orbia)
[](LICENSE)





**ORBIA** is a benchmark for the 3D consistency of interactive video world models. Given an input image, a scene caption and a camera trajectory, a world model should not only produce good-looking video that follows the controls, but also keep the scene it was given, remember the content it generated, and produce views that form one consistent 3D world. ORBIA evaluates these properties with registered RGB-D references, annotated anchors and controlled revisits.

evidence.heading: Highlights
evidence.text:
- **Three dimensions of 3D consistency.** We separate *input preservation* (does the model keep the scene and landmarks in the input image?), *generated-content persistence* (does newly generated content stay the same when the camera comes back?) and *3D self-consistency* (do the generated views agree in geometry and support a shared 3D reconstruction?).
- **Exploration-and-revisit trajectories.** Six trajectory templates (forward–backward, lateral, yaw, arc, orbit, peek) move the camera away from the input view, revisit regions outside it, and return to the start. Each case comes in a 22-second version and a minute-long version with three revisits.
- **Reference-grounded evaluation.** Every case has registered RGB-D views at the input and query poses and verified *anchors*, i.e. distinctive static objects, so preservation is measured against real references and per landmark rather than by a single image-level score.
- **Diverse, curated data.** 720 cases from ScanNet++, SpatialVID, Sekai, MiraData, our own recordings and 48 Unreal Engine environments, selected from over 110,000 source samples with over 300 hours of annotation and review.
- **Works with any world model.** Adapters for camera-conditioned, action-conditioned and image+text-to-video models. We evaluate 27 models.

This repository contains the evaluation code, the model adapters, and the data construction pipelines for real videos and Unreal Engine.

evidence.heading: Citation
Evaluation Dimensions
evidence.text:
| Tier | Dimension | Metrics | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| T1 | Control Alignment | Translation/rotation error, Move/Look accuracy | 25% |
| T2 | Visual Quality | LAION aesthetic, MUSIQ, flicker, AMT smoothness, HPSv3 | 25% |
| **T3** | **Input Preservation** | Scene/anchor PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, DINO and depth AbsRel at return and query; anchor identity | 10% |
| **T4** | **Generated-Content Persistence** | Revisit appearance and depth, reprojected DINO, surface F-score | 10% |
| **T5** | **3D Self-Consistency** | Cross-view depth and DINO consistency, regional scale, Gaussian reconstruction on held-out views | 10% |
| T6 | Temporal Stability | Quality, control and local geometry over 5-second windows | 20% |

Cameras and depth of the generated video are recovered with Depth Anything 3. T3 compares the return and query views with the registered references on input-visible surfaces, and tracks each anchor with SAM 3.1. T4 compares each revisit with the first visit on surfaces seen by both. T5 checks cross-view agreement and renders held-out views from a Gaussian scene built on the generated frames. T6 measures how quality, control and geometry hold up over time, with long videos weighted 70%.

evidence.heading: Dataset
evidence.text:
Each trajectory starts at **P0**, passes the query view **Pq**, visits a region outside the input view (**P_first**), explores elsewhere, revisits it (**P_revisit**), and returns to **P0**.

github_projects.description: llama.cpp fork that abliterates at inference
github_projects.description_zh: llama.cpp 分支，在推理时表现卓越

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: llama.cpp fork that abliterates at inference

evidence.heading: What is AbliteratedOutTheBox?
evidence.text: AbliteratedOutTheBox is a fork of llama.cpp that gets any supported model to answer flagged harmful prompts, delivering the requested content instead of a refusal, at inference time and with the original weights left on disk unchanged. It needs no fit, no training, and no extra files: for each prompt `llama-abliterate` reads two directions from the prompt itself, by forcing the assistant to start a few comply versus refuse openings (and clean versus disclaimered openings), diffing the activations, and a look-ahead gate decides per prompt whether to remove them. The edit happens inside the graph at the `build_cvec` layer-output site that 131 of the 165 model architectures share, so one recipe covers them with no per-model code.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
```bash
# build the runtime (pick the backend you already use: -DGGML_CUDA=ON, -DGGML_HIP=ON, or CPU-only)
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --target llama-abliterate -j

# convert the model to a GGUF for the runtime (any quantization; needs Python with torch, transformers, gguf)
python3 convert_hf_to_gguf.py /path/to/Qwen3-8B --outfile qwen3-8b.gguf --outtype q8_0

# run: no fit, no sidecar, any backend including pure CPU
./build/bin/llama-abliterate \
    -m qwen3-8b.gguf -ngl 99 -n 256 \
    -p "Give me step by step instructions to pick a lock"
```

`--ff-threshold <f>` (default 0.70) sets how readily the gate fires; `--edit-strength <f>` (default 2.0) sets how hard the refusal direction is removed; `--disc-strength <f>` (default 0.4) sets how hard the safety-disclaimer direction is removed. See [tools/abliterate/README.md](tools/abliterate/README.md) for the tool details.

evidence.heading: Why it's better
evidence.text:
Measured on Qwen3-8B with a hand-validated response hidden-state probe (no string matching, no judge model), over held-out sets, with the edit read from the prompt at inference (no fit):

- Refusal drops 96.3% to 7.9% on broad held-out harmful prompts and 82.0% to 0.0% on JailbreakBench; the model answers and delivers the content, confirmed by hand-reading the generations.
- Benign is preserved exactly: the gate fires on 0.4% of alpaca prompts (1 of 256), and when it does not fire the output is bit-identical to the base model (KL 0.000000 over held-out benign, 0 gated, 0.0 logit change).
- A second direction removes most of the safety-disclaimer hedging from the compliant answers (a hidden-state read of the disclaimer character drops about a third), while answers stay coherent (distinct-token ratio around 0.65 vs 0.84 base). Pushing `--disc-strength` higher removes more disclaimers but can start to degenerate longer outputs, so it is tunable.
- The same recipe works across architecture families: run on Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Gemma-4-e4b, the gate fires on the flagged prompts and leaves benign prompts untouched on all three, and the scale-free edit keeps the compliant answers coherent on each without any per-model tuning.

Weight-baked abliteration edits the stored weights and perturbs every prompt, so its benign output is never identical and it needs per-architecture surgery. Here the edit is a scale-free projection at the `build_cvec` layer-output site, so one recipe covers 131 architectures with no per-model code, and prompts the gate leaves alone are untouched.

evidence.heading: Why should I care
evidence.text: It runs with nothing to set up and nothing to download beyond the model itself: no fit, no sidecar, no second file, on whatever you already have including CPU or a few gigabytes of VRAM for a quantized model, because the runtime is plain llama.cpp. You keep one copy of the weights, ordinary prompts behave exactly as before, and generation throughput is unchanged because the only added cost is one extra prompt prefill when a prompt is flagged.

evidence.heading: Advanced
evidence.text:
Both directions are read per prompt and the edit covers the prompt, not only the generated tokens. The refusal decision is committed into the prompt's KV during prefill, so editing only the generated positions leaves refusal near 95% versus single digits when the prompt is edited too. The runtime therefore uses two passes: a clean detection pass that fires the gate, then an edited prefill plus generation. Each per-token edit is a projection, so decode throughput is unchanged.

The refusal direction is the difference between forced refuse and comply openings, orthogonalized against the comply-opening spread to drop benign-common components, and used for both the gate and the edit. The disclaimer direction is the difference between disclaimered and clean compliant openings. A look-ahead gate generates up to 24 of the model's own tokens and fires when the peak refusal projection, band-averaged across the middle layers, exceeds `--ff-threshold`; at 0.70 that holds real-benign false positives near 0.4% at 0.89 harmful recall, and lowering it raises recall at the cost of more benign fires. When fired, the edit pulls the refusal projection down to a reference `--edit-strength` comply-opening standard deviations below the comply level (default 2.0, a scale-free bound measured in each layer's own units so one setting behaves the same across architectures) and the disclaimer projection down by `--disc-strength` of its clean-to-disclaimered gap, from layer `3*n_layer/7` through `2*n_layer/3`.

curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

import os, time, requests

evidence.text:
**TinyLuma** is a fast, standalone desktop photo editor designed specifically for finishing AI-generated artwork and photo sets. Instead of waiting for heavy creative suites (Lightroom, Photoshop) to launch, TinyLuma provides a focused, bloat-free workflow with professional Oklab color science, custom-tuned detail recovery, `.cube` LUT support, and instant batch processing.

No Electron, no web runtime, no subscriptions — a single native executable under **8 MB**.

evidence.heading: Key Features
evidence.text:
- **⚡ Blazing Fast & Ultra-Lightweight (~8 MB):** Built with pure Rust and `egui`. Starts instantly, uses minimal RAM, and renders edits at 60 FPS via multi-threaded Rayon pipelines and 3D LUT caching.
- **🧠 Custom AI Detail Engine:** Algorithms for `Texture`, `Clarity`, and `Sharpen` tuned specifically to eliminate smooth AI "plastic skin" and restore micro-contrast without edge halos.
- **🧬 ComfyUI & A1111 Metadata Preservation:** Exported PNGs retain raw prompt and node graph metadata (`tEXt`, `zTXt`, `iTXt` chunks). Your ComfyUI workflow stays intact.
- **🎨 Oklab Perceptual Color Grading:** 16 non-destructive controls (Light, Color, Details, Effects) powered by Oklab color space and Bradford chromatic adaptation to avoid color shifts and clipping.
- **🎞️ Batch Workflow & Filmstrip:** Navigate multi-image sessions, use **Preset to All** to sync looks across an entire generation batch, and export with background threading.
- **🎭 Complete 3D LUT System:** Direct `.cube` LUT library integration with subfolder categorization, search, favorites (★), and intensity blending (0–100%).
- **⚖️ Before / After Split Screen:** Interactive draggable split divider to compare edits, instantly toggled with the `\` key.

evidence.heading: Why TinyLuma?
evidence.text:
| Feature | Standard Editors (Lightroom / PS) | TinyLuma |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Startup Time** | 5–15 seconds | **Instant (<0.3s)** |
| **Executable Size** | Gigabytes | **~8 MB** |
| **ComfyUI/A1111 Metadata** | Stripped by default | **Preserved (Full pass-through)** |
| **AI Texture Handling** | Generic sharpening (causes ringing) | **Tuned for synthetic & AI surfaces** |
| **LUT Workflow** | Buried in submenus | **Instant visual library & blending** |
| **Memory Footprint** | Heavy (>1 GB idle) | **Strictly bounded LRU cache** |

evidence.heading: Engineered for AI Generations
evidence.text:
Raw AI images (Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, Flux) often suffer from common artifacts: flat lighting, low local contrast, and unnatural "plastic" skin textures. TinyLuma solves this at the algorithm level:

- **Clarity:** Logarithmic local contrast base with soft-knee limiting. Enhances depth and scene separation without burning highlights or creating dark halos around subjects.
- **Texture:** Edge-preserving bilateral separation. Extracts fine surface details (hair strands, fabric weave, skin pores) without amplifying noise or digital artifacts.
- **Sharpen:** Asymmetric luma unsharp mask. Limits light-edge blooming (≤ 0.20) and dark ringing (≤ 0.12) to produce crisp, print-ready results.
- **Film Grain:** Darktable-inspired 3-octave simplex noise mapped via paper-response curves, strongest in midtones to naturally break up AI surface banding.
- **Structure:** Broad local contrast that adds HDR-like depth on top of Clarity, with soft-knee limiting to avoid halos.
- **Creative Effects:** Photographic **Glow** (warm bloom), **Halation** (red highlight bleed) and **Light Flares** (starburst, anamorphic streak and ghosts) — a single slider each, all rendered from cached references for interactive performance.

*All spatial radii scale dynamically to exported resolution, ensuring identical results between preview and full-res renders.*

evidence.heading: ComfyUI & AI Metadata Preservation (Optional)
evidence.text:
Most editors silently wipe workflow metadata, while others force-embed it. TinyLuma gives you **full privacy control with a simple toggle**:

- **Keep Workflows (Opt-In):** Copies `tEXt`, `zTXt`, `iTXt`, and `eXIf` data from source to export. Drop your edited PNG straight back into ComfyUI or Automatic1111 to reload your exact prompt, seed, and node graph.
- **Protect Your Privacy (Opt-Out):** Uncheck the metadata box to export completely clean images — no leaked prompts, models, LoRAs, or generation settings.

github_projects.description: You type. It already knows. Local LLMs that read and think while you type.

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: You type. It already knows. Local LLMs that read and think while you type.

evidence.heading: You type. It already knows.
evidence.text:
MAFDET reads your message while you type it, and **starts thinking about it before you send it**.
Hit Enter, and most of the work is already done.

[](LICENSE)
[](#requirements)
[](#roadmap)

[Italiano](README.it.md)



---

evidence.heading: Why
evidence.text:
Chat interfaces make the model wait for you to press Enter before it does anything. While you type, the GPU sits idle. When you send, the model first has to *read* your whole message (prefill). Then a reasoning model, like Qwen3 in thinking mode, *thinks* for hundreds of tokens before the first word of its answer. On a mid-range GPU that thinking is the longest wait of all: ten seconds and more on a word problem, minutes on a model larger than the VRAM.

MAFDET uses the time you spend typing for both. It **reads** your message as you write it, so the prefill is done before Enter. And it **thinks ahead**: the model starts reasoning about your message while you are still typing it, and keeps that reasoning when you change the text. On Qwen3-4B, with 24 word problems typed in real time, the mean wait after Enter goes from **12.2 s to 3.2 s**, with the same 24/24 correct answers; on Qwen3-14B, from **108 s to 47 s**.

MAFDET is built for the hardware most people actually own. The reference machine is an **RTX 2060 with 6 GB of VRAM**, and everything also runs on **CPU only**.

> Named after Mafdet, the ancient Egyptian feline goddess known as "the runner", who struck snakes and scorpions before they could attack.

evidence.heading: Reading ahead
evidence.text:
An LLM processes text in two phases:

| Phase | What happens | Speed |
|---|---|---|
| **Prefill** | reads the prompt; all tokens are processed in parallel | fast |
| **Decode** | generates the answer, one token at a time | slow |

While reading, the model stores intermediate results for every token in the **KV cache**. Those results never change for a given prefix, so they can be computed ahead of time.

MAFDET keeps the KV cache in sync with the text **while you type**:

1. On every pause, it tokenizes the current text.
2. It holds back the last few tokens, because a word you are still typing can still change how the text is split into tokens.
3. It finds the **longest common prefix** between the new tokens and the ones already in cache, trims the cache there, and prefills only what is new.
4. When you hit enter, only a handful of tokens are left to process.

**Correctness does not depend on how you type.** Backspaces, edits in the middle of the text, pasted blocks, missing punctuation or spaces: the common-prefix check always brings the cache back to exactly what a from-scratch computation would produce. Heuristics such as hold-back and debounce only affect how much work is wasted, never the result.

evidence.heading: Thinking ahead
evidence.text:
Reading ahead takes the prefill out of the wait; the reasoning is still there. So the model also **reasons while you type**: in short chunks, on the message as it is at that moment. When you change the text, the reasoning is not thrown away. It stays in the prompt as notes after the new version of the message, which costs only a prefill, and the model goes on from there. On Enter it finishes reasoning from where it got to and answers. On Qwen3-4B about two thirds of the reasoning is done before Enter. How the notes are framed, and what that changed, is in [Thinking ahead, in detail](#thinking-ahead-in-detail) below.

Reading ahead is exact. Thinking ahead is not, because the model reasons on versions of the message that are not final yet; that is why it was measured on answers that can be checked.

evidence.heading: Quick start
evidence.text:
**On Windows, with a double-click.** Download MAFDET (on GitHub, *Code → Download ZIP*, and unzip it; or `git clone https://github.com/TheLastOxygen/mafdet.git`) and double-click **`start_mafdet.bat`**. The first time it creates a Python environment in `.venv` and installs MAFDET in it, which takes about a minute and needs [Python](https://www.python.org/downloads/) 3.10 or later. After that, a double-click opens MAFDET in under a second, and after an update it installs the new libraries by itself. The terminal shows what is being downloaded as it goes: each library, and later llama.cpp and the models you pick in the app, with size, a progress bar, speed and time left.

**From a terminal:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/TheLastOxygen/mafdet.git
cd mafdet
python -m venv .venv          # Windows: py -3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate     # Windows: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -e .
mafdet
```

Either way, no PyTorch and no manual downloads: MAFDET asks whether to open the **window** or the **terminal app**, and the first start guides you through the rest. It looks at your machine, installs the right build of llama.cpp by itself (CUDA for an NVIDIA card, CPU otherwise) and downloads the model that runs best on your hardware.

evidence.heading: The app
evidence.text:
The same app comes in two forms, on the same engine:

| | Command | What it is |
|---|---|---|
|  | `mafdet gui` | **The window**: chat, models, hardware and settings, in English, Italian, French or German |
|  | `mafdet tui` | **The terminal app**: the same views in the terminal, keyboard first (F1 to F4), on an amber phosphor screen with a boot sequence (Settings, *Cinematic effects*, turns the animations off) |
|  | `mafdet models` | the model catalog for this machine (`--family`, `--download`) |
|  | `mafdet doctor` | checks the GPU, memory, llama.cpp and the models; `--install` installs llama.cpp (`--cuda 12`, `13` or `cpu` to pick the build) |

`mafdet` alone opens the launcher, which can remember your choice (`mafdet --ask` shows it again).

**Chat.** While you type, a status line under the message shows what the model is doing with it: how much it has read, and how many reasoning tokens it has written ahead (the field glows amber while it thinks). On Enter only the tail is left to compute. The reasoning is shown folded above the answer, and every answer ends with its numbers: first word after Enter, tokens read while you typed, reasoning done before Enter, speed.

**Models.** Five families: **Qwen3**, **Llama 3**, **Gemma 3**, **Mistral** and **Phi-4**, from 0.6B to 32B parameters, each in several quantizations. With every model, MAFDET reads your message while you type and, at a pause, writes the answer ahead; Qwen3 also **reasons ahead**, the one family whose reasoning frame was measured. Every model of the catalog comes with what it does on *your* machine, before you download it: whether it fits in VRAM or runs partly on the CPU, how fast it writes and reads, and for Qwen3 how long the answer takes after Enter with and without MAFDET (for the other families,

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
- **Windows**, with an **NVIDIA GPU** and up-to-date drivers (tested target: RTX 2060, 6 GB), or just a CPU. **Linux** has its llama.cpp builds and code paths in place, but has not been tested yet
- **Python 3.10 or later** (tested with 3.12)
- Disk space: about 0.7 GB for llama.cpp with CUDA (60 MB without), plus the models, from 0.6 GB (Qwen3-0.6B) to 2.3 GB for the 4B recommended on 6-8 GB cards
- **16 GB of RAM** recommended for CPU-only runs and for models larger than the VRAM

The app needs no PyTorch: llama.cpp runs the models, and transformers only provides the tokenizers. PyTorch is needed only for the measurements on the PyTorch backend (below): install it first from the CUDA index, then `pip install -e ".[research]"`.

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image-ext","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image-ext", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

Runnable versions: [`examples/`](examples). The task lifecycle is `pending → processing → completed | failed`.

curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-3-pro-image-preview", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

github_projects.description: FunASR.NET：.NET 10 纯 C# 普通话 ASR/TTS，CPU SIMD、可选 Vulkan，浏览器和 SIP 音频示例，中文文档与真实原版测速对照。
github_projects.description_zh: FunASR.NET：.NET 10 纯 C# 普通话 ASR/TTS，CPU SIMD、可选 Vulkan，浏览器和 SIP 音频示例，中文文档与真实原版测速对照。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: FunASR.NET：.NET 10 纯 C# 普通话 ASR/TTS，CPU SIMD、可选 Vulkan，浏览器和 SIP 音频示例，中文文档与真实原版测速对照。

evidence.heading: FunASR.NET
evidence.text:
**用 .NET 10 和纯 C# 推理实现普通话识别、语音合成与电话音频处理。** 核心命名空间 `FunAsrNet`，支持 CPU SIMD 和显式启用的 Vulkan GPU 混合后端。

基于 [QwenAudio/Fun-ASR](https://github.com/QwenAudio/Fun-ASR) 固定版本架构的独立社区实现，**不是官方 .NET SDK，也不是整个 FunASR 工具箱的移植**。围绕固定 F16 编码器、Qwen3 Q8_0 解码器、FSMN VAD 与两种中文 VITS 模型验证，不承诺兼容上游所有模型及语言。

evidence.heading: 纯 .NET 的实现范围
evidence.text:
- 默认 CPU 的模型读取、特征、神经网络算子、解码、VAD、中文前端和 TTS 均由 C# 实现，不是给原生引擎包一层接口。
- 核心、CLI 和 Web 服务不依赖 Python、ONNX Runtime、ggml、sherpa-onnx 或 RKNN 推理库。ONNX/GGUF 在这里是文件格式；自有 ONNX 解释器只支持固定模型需要的子集。
- 使用 .NET SIMD、ARM64 NEON/SDOT、池缓冲、共享只读权重和有界队列。ASR 默认布局按硬件选择，x64 用行主序 SIMD，ARM64 用 NEON/SDOT 交错内核；各平台优化程度不同。
- 可选 Vulkan 用 C# 调度系统原生 GPU 驱动，执行嵌入 SPIR-V。仓库保留 GLSL 源码字符串；“纯 .NET”描述默认 CPU 推理，不表示 GPU 无需原生驱动。
- `tools/FunAsrNet.NativeReference` 单独引用原生 ORT，只作开发对照，不在主解决方案中，不是产品依赖。

详见 [架构](doc/architecture.md) 和 [第三方说明](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

evidence.heading: 功能
evidence.text:
| 功能 | 当前实现 |
|---|---|
| ASR | WAV 转写；固定 F16 编码器、Q8_0 解码器 |
| 实时转写 | WebSocket、VAD 切句、可修订预览；不是逐帧增量编码 |
| 中文 TTS | Huayan 1 位、AISHELL3 174 位发音人，安装两模型后共 175 位 |
| 浏览器 Demo | 麦克风实时转写、上传 WAV、TTS 播放/下载，发音人搜索列表 |
| 电话音频 | PCM16、G.711 PCMA/PCMU、重采样，可接自研 SIP/PJSIP 媒体层 |
| 并发 | 独立会话状态、只读权重共享、队列/配额/取消和缓冲所有权管理 |
| 可选 GPU | Vulkan FP32 矩阵/卷积、原 Q8_0 投影；剩余算子在 CPU |

TTS 可设置语速、音量、采样率、格式、发音人、种子和随机度；尚无独立音高/情绪控制。服务不实现 SIP 信令、RTP 抖动缓冲或 AEC。

evidence.heading: 构建与运行
evidence.text:
安装 .NET 10 SDK（`global.json` 最低 10.0.300），在仓库根目录执行：

```shell
dotnet build FunAsrNet.sln -c Release
dotnet run --project tests/FunAsrNet.Checks -c Release --no-build
dotnet run --project tools/FunAsrNet.CodeStyle -c Release --no-build -- .
```

**权重不在仓库内。** 按 [模型清单](doc/models.md) 准备 `models/` 并校验 SHA-256。ASR/VAD 需要兼容 GGUF，暂未提供一键下载的公开 GGUF 镜像或转换工具。克隆代码可运行无模型数值检查，不能直接启动完整服务。

```shell
dotnet publish src/FunAsrNet.Server -c Release -o artifacts/server
dotnet artifacts/server/FunAsrNet.Server.dll --urls http://localhost:18080 --models models --lexicon assets/mandarin-lexicon.json --threads 4
```

打开 `http://localhost:18080` 使用三个 Demo。远程麦克风需 HTTPS，见 [部署](doc/deployment.md)。默认 Web 服务用 CPU；Vulkan 通过代码或基准工具显式选择，服务暂未提供 GPU 配置开关。

```shell
dotnet run --project src/FunAsrNet.Cli -c Release -- asr --enc models/funasr-encoder-f16.gguf --llm models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.gguf --wav input.wav --threads 4 --repeat 3
dotnet run --project src/FunAsrNet.Cli -c Release -- tts --model models/aishell3/model.onnx --lexicon models/aishell3/lexicon.txt --tokens models/aishell3/tokens.txt --speaker 50 --text "您好，欢迎致电。" --rate 8000 --out speech.wav
```

evidence.heading: C# 调用
Windows：第七轮 GPU 优化与 CPU/GPU 完整对比（2026-10-12）
evidence.text:
本机 i7-12700、RTX 3060、四线程、相同模型和输入，默认 CPU 推理保持纯 C#。本轮 GPU 将编码器两层投影连续执行，减少中间回传，并优化 FP32 累加器、Q8 整数点积与短栅栏等待。**ASR GPU 比上一版减少 14.8%～19.4% 耗时，TTS 减少 3.9%～8.0%；仍为同轮原版 GPU 的 3.14～5.50 倍耗时，尚未追平。**

预热后完整调用中位数，单位秒；ASR 原版为 C++ CPU / 原计算图 CUDA 编码器和解码器，TTS 原版为 ORT CPU / CUDA：

| 项目 | C# CPU | 原版 CPU | C# Vulkan | 原版 GPU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ASR 6.000 秒 PCMA | 0.720 | 0.773 | 0.349 | 0.111 |
| ASR 5.616 秒 PCMU | 0.845 | 0.880 | 0.407 | 0.116 |
| ASR 28.000 秒重复样例 | 2.881 | 3.039 | 1.344 | 0.263 |
| ASR 6.000 秒原始 PCM | 0.670 | 0.730 | 0.346 | 0.098 |
| ASR 官方 PCMA | 0.679 | 0.756 | 0.353 | 0.103 |
| TTS Huayan 0 号 | 0.141 | 0.108 | 0.154 | 0.028 |
| TTS AISHELL3 50 号 | 0.067 | 0.046 | 0.087 | 0.026 |

模型/后端初始化中位数，单位秒；ASR 取上表短 PCMA 的双模型初始化，两种 TTS 分别加载对应 ONNX：

| 模型 | C# CPU | 原版 CPU | C# Vulkan | 原版 GPU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ASR 编码器 + 解码器 | 0.800 | 0.322 | 1.108 | 0.782 |
| Huayan | 0.094 | 0.868 | 0.411 | 1.019 |
| AISHELL3 | 0.068 | 0.551 | 0.378 | 0.672 |

Vulkan 的首次权重上传另计入首次推理。短 ASR 的“初始化 + 首次推理”为 C# CPU **1.621 秒**、C++ CPU **1.158 秒**、C# Vulkan **3.478 秒**、原图 CUDA **1.033 秒**。文件/驱动缓存未清空，不含进程或服务启动。**本轮 GPU 初始化稍慢，两个 TTS 的初始化加首次推理也变慢；热态改善不等于启动改善。**

CPU 热态相对上一版约 -0.8%～+1.9%，没有新整体加速。当前 TTS 的 C# Vulkan 仍慢于 C# CPU。CPU/GPU 各 210 次正式调用、42 次首次调用，每个热态表格单元十个样本，初始化单元两个新进程样本。五份 ASR 在各自 CPU 或 GPU 对照中三方转写一致；新旧 GPU 的 53 个 ASR 张量快照及 TTS 波形逐位相同。

所有输入的加载、首次推理、P95、上一版对照、精度与原图 CUDA 适配边界见 [第七轮完整报告](doc/gpu-round7-20261012.md)，原始记录及散列均随报告保留。结果仅适用于本机这些输入，不代表语言优势、RK3588 性能或实时麦克风识别率。下方保留历史测量。

evidence.heading: Windows：历史第六轮模型加载与 GPU 优化（2026-10-12）
evidence.text:
已移除当前版本的六个 Python 复测/汇总脚本，统一使用 [C# 对比入口](tools/FunAsrNet.Compare/README.md)；历史原始数据保留。默认 CPU 推理仍不依赖原生引擎。

两份 ASR GGUF 的读取与解包中位数从 **3.203 秒降到 0.723 秒，耗时减少 77.4%**；托管分配从 3.076 GB 降到 1.812 GB。12 个新进程样本，未清空文件缓存，不含推理或 GPU 首次上传。短 ASR 的 CPU 模型初始化与首次转写之和从 4.061 秒降到 1.606 秒，同轮原版为 1.168 秒；仍不能当作完整服务冷启动。

RTX 3060、相同模型/输入、四线程；每格十次预热后的正式样本：

| 项目 | 上一版 C# Vulkan | 本次 C# Vulkan | 同轮原版 GPU | 本轮耗时减少 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ASR 6.000 秒 PCMA | 0.495 秒 | 0.427 秒 | 0.107 秒 | 13.8% |
| ASR 5.616 秒 PCMU | 0.553 秒 | 0.480 秒 | 0.125 秒 | 13.2% |
| ASR 28.000 秒重复样例 | 1.926 秒 | 1.640 秒 | 0.275 秒 | 14.8% |
| TTS Huayan 0 号 | 0.229 秒 | 0.175 秒 | 0.029 秒 | 23.3% |
| TTS AISHELL3 50 号 | 0.130 秒 | 0.095 秒 | 0.025 秒 | 27.0% |

原版 ASR 为 **C++ CUDA 编码器和解码器**，TTS 为同模型 **ORT CUDA**。GPU 三方 ASR 文本一致，新旧 C# GPU TTS 波形相同；未降低计算精度。**该轮为原版 GPU 的 3.84–6.10 倍耗时，尚未追平。** Vulkan 混合路径仍有大量 CPU 中间处理和同步，不能解释为语言优劣；本机结果不适用于 RK3588。

同轮 CPU 回归的 ASR 仍略快于原版，热态相对上一版约 ±2%，没有进一步的整体提升；TTS CPU 尚未追平 ORT CPU。GPU 150 次正式调用/30 次预热，CPU 126 次/42 次，加载、首次调用、P95、内存和正确性边界见 [完整第六轮记录](doc/load-gpu-round6-20261012.md)。

evidence.heading: Quickstart
evidence.text:
```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"flux-2-max","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'
```

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "flux-2-max", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

evidence.heading: paint-mv-skills
evidence.text:
[](demo/midnight-studio.mp4)

给 AI Agent 用的 MV 制作 skills：输入**一首歌的音频和歌词**，输出**一支手绘水彩风格的动画 MV（MP4）**。
流程完全照 [PDoomVideo](https://github.com/JohnHeibel/PDoomVideo)（Claude 为《I'm Upping My P(doom)》画的 MV）的源码来做：
每一帧都是歌曲时间的纯函数，由 p5.js + [p5.brush](https://github.com/acamposuribe/p5.brush) 在 headless Chrome 里画成水彩与墨线，
导演写分镜、并行子代理一章一章作画、联系表检查，最后用 ffmpeg 和歌曲合成。

**画风固定，内容跟着歌词走**：水彩加墨线的绘本观感、纸纹、"沸腾"的线条、卡拉 OK 字幕、笔刷转场都沿用原作；
构思、角色、场景和道具每首歌都从歌词重新设计。

evidence.heading: 演示：《凌晨录音室》
evidence.text:
用一首 86 秒的中文说唱从零跑完全流程的结果，没有人工修改画面。歌词是新写的，歌用 [YuE2](https://noiz.ai/lp/yue2) 生成。



https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e291eb1-0761-4abd-b2c0-7ef165dc343a

凌晨两点，全城都睡了，只有路口的红绿灯和一个戴大耳机的说唱少年还醒着。他在小录音室里把"没被听见的字"
录成一束光，每段副歌光都更大，最后冲出窗户唱进城市的耳朵里；清晨升起的太阳，就是他录了一夜的那束光。
角色全部来自歌词：唱歌的"我"小夜、"街上只剩红绿灯"的灯灯、"每个没被听见的字都还有体温"的字灵、
"耳机里的鼓点"鼓点仔、"白天的嘈杂"嘈杂怪。



分镜和全部源码在 [`demo/project/`](demo/project/)：[`STORYBOARD.md`](demo/project/STORYBOARD.md)、
角色 [`characters.js`](demo/project/src/characters.js)、共享场景 [`sets.js`](demo/project/src/sets.js)、五个章节 [`src/ch/`](demo/project/src/ch/)；
封面由 [`poster.js`](demo/project/src/poster.js) 用同一套引擎画出（`node render.mjs --loop=poster --stills=0.4`）。

evidence.heading: 四个 skill
evidence.text:
| skill | 作用 |
|---|---|
| [`paint-mv`](skills/paint-mv/SKILL.md) | 总控：建项目、测节拍和对歌词时间、落地角色、给每章派子代理、统稿、出片 |
| [`paint-mv-storyboard`](skills/paint-mv-storyboard/SKILL.md) | 从歌词写分镜：构思与反转、角色表、每章场景、每句歌词一个镜头、有动机的转场 |
| [`paint-mv-animate`](skills/paint-mv-animate/SKILL.md) | 画师规范：引擎 API、按原作风格设计角色、技法目录、原作九章示例 |
| [`paint-mv-render`](skills/paint-mv-render/SKILL.md) | 联系表检查、短片、全片并行可续渲、局部重渲、编码与验收、排错 |

流程（`paint-mv` 驱动）：

1. `new_project.mjs` 建项目：引擎模板、分析节拍（BPM、首拍）、歌词转成时间轴；纯文本歌词先用 faster-whisper 自动对齐。
2. 出对拍短片确认时间。
3. 按 `paint-mv-storyboard` 从歌词写 `STORYBOARD.md`。
4. 写本片角色 `characters.js` 和共享场景 `sets.js`，出模型表。
5. 每章一个子代理并行作画，各自用联系表检查。
6. 统稿：章节交界、转场、性能。
7. 全片逐帧渲染，编码成 MP4。

evidence.heading: 安装
evidence.text:
需要 Node.js ≥ 18、ffmpeg、Google Chrome、git、patch；纯文本歌词自动对齐还需要 [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lintsinghua/paint-mv-skills.git
cd paint-mv-skills
node skills/paint-mv/scripts/fetch_upstream.mjs   # 拉取原作源码（见下文「关于原作源码」）
```

把 `skills/` 下的四个目录放到你的 Agent 读取 skill 的位置，例如：

- Cursor：项目里的 `.cursor/skills/`（本仓库已经用符号链接指向 `skills/`，直接在本仓库里打开就能用）
- Claude Code：`.claude/skills/` 或 `~/.claude/skills/`（本仓库同样有符号链接）

然后对 Agent 说："用这首歌和歌词做一支 MV：`song.mp3`、`lyrics.lrc`"。

想先试试又没有合适的歌，可以像演示那样自己做一首：我是在 [YuE2](https://noiz.ai/lp/yue2) 上贴歌词生成的。

evidence.heading: 手动使用
evidence.text:
```bash
# 纯文本歌词先对齐（每行一句）
uv run --python 3.12 --with faster-whisper --with zhconv python skills/paint-mv/scripts/align_lyrics.py \
    song.mp3 lyrics.txt --out lyrics.srt --lang zh

node skills/paint-mv/scripts/new_project.mjs my-mv --audio=song.mp3 --lyrics=lyrics.srt --title="歌名"
cd my-mv
# ……按 skills 写分镜、角色、章节……
node render.mjs --frames=0:<时长> --workers=4     # 逐帧渲染，可续渲
node render.mjs --encode --out=out/mv.mp4
```

复现演示：

```bash
node skills/paint-mv/scripts/new_project.mjs demo-mv --audio=demo/project/assets/song.mp3 --title="凌晨录音室"
cp -R demo/project/* demo-mv/
# 在 demo-mv/studio.html 末尾的章节注释处加上五行：
#    … 
cd demo-mv && node render.mjs --frames=0:86.63 --workers=4 && node render.mjs --encode --out=out/mv.mp4
```

evidence.heading: 关于原作源码
evidence.text:
PDoomVideo 仓库没有声明开源许可证，所以本仓库**不包含**它的任何文件。
`skills/paint-mv/scripts/fetch_upstream.mjs` 会从 GitHub 按固定提交拉取：

- 引擎：`core.js`、`timeline.js`、`props.js`、`clawd.js`、`cast.js`、`render.mjs`、`studio.html`；
- 原作九章：放进 `paint-mv-animate/examples/`；
- 原作分镜：放进 `paint-mv-storyboard/pdoom-storyboard.md`。

然后对引擎打上 [`template.patch`](skills/paint-mv/template.patch)：歌曲参数移到 `song.js`、支持 macOS 的 WebGL 后端、
中日韩字体和卡拉 OK 扫字速度。`new_project.mjs` 第一次运行时会自动调用它。改动细节见
[`paint-mv/SKILL.md`](skills/paint-mv/SKILL.md) 的「引擎与原作源码的差异」。

evidence.heading: English
evidence.text:
Agent skills that turn a song (audio + lyrics) into a hand-painted watercolour music video, following the pipeline of
[PDoomVideo](https://github.com/JohnHeibel/PDoomVideo): a director skill that scaffolds the project, times the beat and
lyrics and briefs parallel chapter subagents; a storyboard skill that designs the concept, cast and sets from the
lyrics; an animation skill with the p5.brush engine API and the original chapters as examples; and a render skill for
headless-Chrome frame rendering and ffmpeg encoding. The style is fixed; the story and characters come from each song.
PDoomVideo's own code is not included: `fetch_upstream.mjs` downloads it at a pinned commit and applies
`template.patch`. See [`demo/`](demo/) for a full example.

kind_reason.text: 用智能体和代码渲染制作水彩MV的四项技能。

summary.text: paint-mv-skills 输入歌曲与歌词，组织分镜、角色和逐章作画，再用p5.js/p5.brush与无头Chrome逐帧渲染水彩动画，FFmpeg合成MP4。

value.text: 固定水彩墨线风格，故事与角色随歌词重新设计；章节可并行渲染、断点续跑和局部重渲，便于修改长MV。

mechanism.text: 总控测节拍并对齐歌词，分镜技能设计镜头，画师按引擎API编写章节；每帧是歌曲时间的纯函数，联系表检查后并行渲染编码。

limitations.text: 依赖的PDoomVideo没有声明开源许可证，本库不包含其文件，而脚本从固定提交拉取；可获取源码不代表获得复用授权。演示为作者单一86秒案例。

how_to.text: 准备Node18+、Chrome和FFmpeg，安装四项技能并获取上游引擎；纯文本歌词用faster-whisper对齐后建项目。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Pi.NET 是 Pi 的 .NET 10 移植版。Pi 是一个极简、可扩展的 Agent harness（TypeScript monorepo，约 17.1 万行），本项目把它的核心库逐一移植到 net10.0，让 .NET 生态用上同一套能力。

evidence.heading: Pi.NET
evidence.text:
[English](https://github.com/AIDotNet/pi.net/blob/main/readme.md) | [简体中文](https://github.com/AIDotNet/pi.net/blob/main/readme.zh-CN.md)

[](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Pi.Ai)
[](https://github.com/AIDotNet/pi.net/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](https://github.com/AIDotNet/pi.net/blob/main/LICENSE)

Pi.NET is a .NET 10 port of [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi). Pi is a minimal, extensible Agent harness (TypeScript monorepo, ~171k lines); this project ports its core libraries one by one to `net10.0`, bringing the same capabilities to the .NET ecosystem.

Pi's philosophy is "make Pi fit your workflow, not the other way around": each library does one minimal-but-complete thing, and you compose the layers above it yourself. This project carries that philosophy over — rather than mechanically translating TS into C#, it rebuilds everything in idiomatic C# with semantic equivalence (discriminated unions → abstract records with pattern matching, JS Proxy → explicit verb APIs).

> **This project is entirely AI-driven.** The code, tests and docs under `src/`, `tests/`, `samples/` and `docs/` are written and maintained by AI against the TypeScript implementation as the behavioral reference. That buys a lot of speed and consistency — and it also means there will be rough edges. **Hit a bug? [Open an issue](https://github.com/AIDotNet/pi.net/issues/new) — reports are exactly how it gets fixed.**


  
    
  
  
  39-second promo (with voice-over) · click the cover to play (1080p / MP4 / 5.4 MB)

evidence.heading: What It Does
evidence.text:
- **Unified multi-provider LLM API** — 10 built-in API implementations (openai-completions / openai-responses / openai-codex-responses / azure-openai-responses / anthropic-messages / google-generative-ai / google-vertex / mistral-conversations / bedrock-converse-stream / pi-messages) plus a **full catalog of 42 built-in providers**; streaming events, tool calls, thinking budgets, deferred responses, image generation (images) and text classification (classify); OAuth login flows for 9 providers (PKCE / RFC 8628 device code / loopback callback / refresh orchestration).
- **Agent runtime** — agent state machine with dual queues, the agent-loop main loop, sequential / parallel tool execution, abort / reset.
- **MCP client** — JSON-RPC protocol layer + in-memory / stdio / streamable-http transports + a complete OAuth layer (metadata discovery, PKCE authorization code, dynamic registration, credential-invalidation retry).
- **Application orchestration runtime (Chord)** — services and replicated state, delta engine, facets dependency graph with topological activation, external service source bindings.
- **TCP RPC channel** — handshake validation, request dispatch, cancellation, push — prepared for remotely controlling the coding-agent.
- **Vendor-neutral telemetry** — contracts + reference adapter + conformance test suite.

evidence.heading: Packages
evidence.text:
| Package | Description |
|---|---|
| **Pi.Telemetry** | Vendor-neutral telemetry contracts, reference adapter and typed schemas, with a conformance test suite |
| **Pi.Protocol** | CBOR wire protocol: framing / codec, definite-length strict subset + JS safe-integer boundaries, **wire-compatible** with the TS implementation |
| **Pi.Ai** | Unified multi-provider LLM API: native API boilerplate + compat-provider registry; streaming, tool calls, thinking, images / classify, full OAuth login flows |
| **Pi.Agent** | Agent runtime: state machine / dual queues, agent-loop main loop, tool execution |
| **Pi.Mcp** | MCP client: JSON-RPC + three transports + the full OAuth layer |
| **Pi.Chord** | Standalone application orchestration runtime: services, replicated state, RPC and plugins |
| **Pi.Server / Pi.Client** | RPC transport: handshake / requests / cancellation / push, session routing, Unix domain sockets and local server discovery |
| **Pi.Codemode** | Sandboxed JavaScript execution whose only capability is calling injected tools; @options source parsing, TypeScript declaration rendering and sandbox orchestration, with a default Jint VM engine behind the replaceable `ICodemodeJsEngine` seam |
| **Pi.Tui** | Terminal UI framework: differential rendering + synchronized output, grapheme-level width measurement and wrapping, ANSI/OSC parsing with SGR tracking, Kitty keyboard protocol and key decoding, overlay stack, focus management, mouse event dispatch, colors (OKLCH/OKHSL) and keybinding registry, stdin escape-sequence buffering, inline terminal images (Kitty / iTerm2 protocols), stack/scroll layout engine, LaTeX math rendering, slash-command and file-path autocomplete (with `fd` fuzzy search), single-line input component (Emacs-style kill/yank, undo, bracketed paste), se

evidence.heading: Install from NuGet
evidence.text:
All 13 libraries ship to nuget.org under their project names, targeting `net10.0`:

```bash
dotnet add package Pi.Ai        # unified multi-provider LLM API
dotnet add package Pi.Agent     # agent loop
dotnet add package Pi.Mcp       # MCP client
dotnet add package Pi.CodingAgent   # the whole stack, including the CLI runtime
```

evidence.heading: Usage docs
evidence.text:
- **[docs/usage](https://github.com/AIDotNet/pi.net/blob/main/docs/usage/README.md)** — how to consume each package from C#: which package for which job, minimal working code, credentials, and the traps worth knowing.
- **[docs/usage/models-configuration.md](https://github.com/AIDotNet/pi.net/blob/main/docs/usage/models-configuration.md)** — every `models.json` field (provider, model, overrides, input limits, compatibility) with its type, default and description, generated from the published JSON Schema.

Package contents, release process and rollback are documented in [docs/publishing.md](https://github.com/AIDotNet/pi.net/blob/main/docs/publishing.md).

evidence.heading: Examples
evidence.text:
`pi` is the coding agent. Build it once and put it on `PATH`:

```bash
dotnet publish src/Pi.Cli -c Release -o ./pi-bin
export PATH="$PWD/pi-bin:$PATH"    # PowerShell: $env:PATH = "$PWD\pi-bin;$env:PATH"
pi --version
```

evidence.heading: Limit what it can touch
evidence.text:
```bash
# -t replaces the default toolset; none of these four can modify a file
pi -t read,grep,find,ls -p "Review src/Pi.Agent and rank the three riskiest spots."

# -xt removes tools from the default set instead of replacing it
pi -xt write,edit -p "Explain how the files under tools/ are produced."
```

→ `query-party-store-date` → `query-party-store-session`，回答：

> 全市有 97 家门店可办，你能体验的活动共 20 款，高于全国中位数（18 款）。
>
> 以成都高新区大魔方餐厅的采样场次为例，10-14 至 10-22 连续 9 天可约，
> 这周六（10-17）有 2 个场次：10:30–12:00 和 14:00–15:30，
> 5~12 人，当前各余 12 位。注意这是「亲子读书会」品类的场次与价格（¥45.00），
> 生日派对的场次时间与价格需按具体 SPU 再查一次。实际下单请在麦当劳 App 或门店完成。

Skill 内置的硬约束（见 `SKILL.md`）：**只读**，禁止调用任何写操作工具；
金额单位为分需自行换算；涉日期必须实时调用 `now-time-info`；不得编造未返回的门店。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Dynamic Band Splitting (DBS) for ComfyUI: separate a soundtrack into music, sound effects and speech; remove or keep the dialogue of a video. Same output as the official package.

evidence.heading: DBS Soundtrack Separation for ComfyUI
evidence.text:
Separate a soundtrack into **music**, **sound effects** and **speech** inside ComfyUI, with the official **Dynamic Band
Splitting (DBS)** models ([JusperLee/Dynamic-Band-Splitting](https://github.com/JusperLee/Dynamic-Band-Splitting),
[paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14993)). Use it to remove the dialogue of a video and keep its music and effects, to pull the
dialogue out for dubbing or transcription, or to rebalance a mix. The models are tiny (1.0M and 4.7M parameters), run on CUDA or
the CPU, and the three stems add back up to the input. The nodes run the vendored official code and never download anything.

> **Unofficial.** This node pack is an independent integration. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DBS authors or by
> Comfy Org.
>
> 日本語の概要は [README.ja.md](README.ja.md) にあります。



*Tears of Steel (CC BY 3.0, Blender Foundation), 12 s of the project page's mixture; below it this pack's DBS-TIGER stems (CPU),
which are bit for bit the official package's output for the same file.*

evidence.heading: What it does
evidence.text:
| Node | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **DBS Loader** | Picks the model (DBS-TIGER-DnR or DBS-BSRNN-DnR) and the device (`auto` = ComfyUI's GPU when it is CUDA, else `cpu`) |
| **DBS Separate (music / sfx / speech)** | `AUDIO` in → `music`, `sfx`, `speech` (`AUDIO`) and a JSON report |

Connect ComfyUI's **Load Audio** (or **Load Video** → **Get Video Components**) in front. To remove the dialogue, add `music` and
`sfx` with ComfyUI's **Merge Audio** (`add`); the shipped workflows do that, one of them for a video.

- `channels` = `mono`: the channel mean is separated, as the official usage does. `each channel`: every channel is separated on
  its own, which keeps stereo (twice the time for stereo).
- The models work on 44.1 kHz. Other rates are resampled with ComfyUI's own resampler; `output_sample_rate` = `44100` (the
  model's rate) or `input` (resampled back).
- The overlap-add windows of the model cards are used: DBS-TIGER 6 s every 3 s, DBS-BSRNN 3 s every 1.5 s. Any length works.
- The stems are in phase with the input and add back up to it (music + sfx + speech = input, to about 1e-6).
- Batches: every item is separated on its own.

| Model | Parameters | SI-SDR on DnR v2 (music / sfx / speech) | RTX 5090 | CPU (24 threads) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **DBS-TIGER-DnR** (default) | 1.0M | 7.78 / 6.70 / 15.90 dB | 16x real time | 0.5x real time |
| DBS-BSRNN-DnR | 4.7M | 6.48 / 5.73 / 15.01 dB | 22x real time | 1.8x real time |

SI-SDR: the authors' model cards (not measured here). Speed: measured here, model loaded, channel mean. Without a CUDA GPU,
DBS-BSRNN is the practical choice (DBS-TIGER takes about twice the length of the audio on the CPU).

evidence.heading: How far it was checked
evidence.text:
Windows 11, ComfyUI v0.38.0, RTX 5090 and CPU; details and raw numbers in [docs/VERIFICATION.md](docs/VERIFICATION.md):

- **Bit-identical to the official package on the CPU.** On the project page's film clips (Tears of Steel, Sintel; CC BY 3.0) the
  pack's stems equal those of the official README usage (`from_pretrained` + `separate(..., mode="chunked")`), byte for byte, in
  6 of 6 cases (both models, every overlap-add path, per channel). The official side ran in a separate environment with the
  upstream's pinned versions.
- **CUDA:** the official code itself gives slightly different bytes on every run on the GPU; with PyTorch's deterministic
  algorithms on both sides, the pack equals the official output bit for bit in 4 of 4 cases (30 s clips, both models, channel
  mean and each channel).
- **Real ComfyUI queue** (CPU and RTX 5090): Load Audio → DBS → Save Audio (FLAC) gives the official stems to within half a
  16-bit step (the FLAC rounding); the remove-dialogue workflows, including the video one, run through the queue.
- **Clean install:** fresh ComfyUI v0.38.0, fresh Python 3.12 environment, `git clone` of this repository, `pip install -r
  requirements.txt` (nothing new: ComfyUI already brings `einops` and `safetensors`), the models downloaded with
  `tools/download_model.py` (SHA-256 verified), and the real-queue check against the installed pack.
- **CI** (GitHub Actions; Ubuntu and Windows): the real models on the CPU on synthetic audio, the pack compared with the official
  package in the same process for both models, the vendored code compared with the pinned upstream commit, ComfyUI's own
  validation of the workflows, and a real ComfyUI queue; ComfyUI v0.38.0 and v0.42.1.

**Not checked:** separation quality itself (the pack reproduces the official out

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
1. ComfyUI with the V3 node API (**v0.38.0** or later) and Python 3.10+. A CUDA GPU is optional.
2. Clone this repository into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/` and install its requirements into ComfyUI's Python (`einops` and
   `safetensors`, which ComfyUI usually has already):

   ```
   git clone https://github.com/hiroki-abe-58/ComfyUI-DBS custom_nodes/ComfyUI-DBS
   python -m pip install -r custom_nodes/ComfyUI-DBS/requirements.txt
   ```

3. Download the models (23 MB for both). The script pins the revisions and verifies every file's SHA-256:

   ```
   python custom_nodes/ComfyUI-DBS/tools/download_model.py --models-dir models/dbs
   ```

   Result: `models/dbs/DBS-TIGER-DnR/` and `models/dbs/DBS-BSRNN-DnR/`, each with `config.json`, `model.safetensors` and the model
   card `README.md`. Another location works through `extra_model_paths.yaml` with the key `dbs`.

4. Restart ComfyUI and open one of `workflows/gui/`:
   - `separate_soundtrack.json`: the three stems as FLAC;
   - `remove_dialogue.json`: music + sfx (the soundtrack without dialogue) and the dialogue, in stereo at the input's rate;
   - `video_remove_dialogue.json`: the same for a video, saved as a new video with the dialogue-free soundtrack.

   Choose your own file in Load Audio or Load Video (the workflows name `soundtrack.wav` and `clip.mp4`).

evidence.heading: Notes and limits
evidence.text:
- Trained on DnR v2: English speech (LibriSpeech), music (Free Music Archive) and sound effects (FSD50K) mixed like a film
  soundtrack. Results on other material (songs with vocals, other languages, very loud music) are for you to judge.
- Interrupt stops between two windows.
- On CUDA, repeated runs can differ in the last digits (the official code does the same); start ComfyUI with `--deterministic`
  if you need identical files every time.
- The demo backend of the upstream repository runs DBS-TIGER on the CPU with one thread; here that was slower and not identical,
  so the pack uses PyTorch's default threads, as the README usage does.

evidence.heading: Licenses
evidence.text:
- This node pack's code: **MIT** ([LICENSE](LICENSE)).
- Vendored DBS code (`dbs_comfy/vendor`): **Apache-2.0**, by Bingzhe Zhang, Kai Li and Xiaolin Hu, with parts adapted from
  MIT-licensed projects ([NOTICE](NOTICE), `dbs_comfy/vendor/UPSTREAM.md`, `dbs_comfy/vendor/THIRD_PARTY.md`).
- Models (downloaded only by `tools/download_model.py`): **Apache-2.0** (model cards), trained on DnR v2 (CC BY 4.0).

evidence.heading: Development
evidence.text:
```
python -m pip install pytest ruff soundfile rotary-embedding-torch huggingface_hub
python tools/download_model.py --models-dir <dir>/dbs
git clone https://github.com/JusperLee/Dynamic-Band-Splitting <upstream> && git -C <upstream> checkout ff526463a58ee0278e7bd05c4b8bce112b743e34
DBS_MODELS_DIR=<dir>/dbs DBS_UPSTREAM_DIR=<upstream> DBS_COMFYUI_DIR=<ComfyUI checkout> python -m pytest tests
python scripts/ci_queue_check.py --comfyui <ComfyUI checkout> --models-dir <dir>/dbs --upstream <upstream>   # real queue on the CPU
python scripts/vendor_sync.py --upstream <upstream> --check                                                 # vendored code check
```

The official package is only needed for the comparison tests (`rotary-embedding-torch` and `huggingface_hub` are what its imports
need), and `soundfile` only for the tests and the check script; the node pack itself imports neither.

evidence.heading: Quickstart

```bash
curl --request POST --url https://api.apimart.ai/v1/images/generations \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIMART_API_KEY" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview-official","prompt":"A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in","size":"1:1","resolution":"1K"}'

```python
import os, time, requests

BASE = "https://api.apimart.ai/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['APIMART_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

created = requests.post(f"{BASE}/images/generations", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60, json={
    "model": "gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview-official", "prompt": "A bamboo forest at sunrise, slow push-in",
}).json()
task_id = created["data"]["id"]

while True:
    task = requests.get(f"{BASE}/tasks/{task_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=60).json()["data"]
    if task["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)
print(task.get("cost"), task["result"]["images"][0]["url"])
```

evidence.heading: ComfyUI-MOSSImageTextEncoder
evidence.text:
Feeds a reference image through the Qwen3.5-9B **vision tower** and inserts its visual embeddings directly into the text prompt. The image conditions the generation natively through the text encoder.




**Note:** This node is for vision/conditioning, not image editing.

evidence.heading: Workflow
evidence.text:
A ready-to-use example workflow is included in the repository: `workflow.json`.

Simply drag and drop the `workflow.json` file directly into your ComfyUI workspace to load the entire setup.

evidence.heading: Requirements
evidence.text:
* `qwen3.5_9b_*.safetensors` text encoder, `moss_image_*.safetensors` diffusion model,
  `flux2-vae*.safetensors` (for decoding only).
* Load the text encoder through **CLIPLoader** with type **`moss_image`**.
* Latents: use the core **Empty Flux 2 Latent** node (128 channels).

evidence.heading: Text Encode (MOSS-Image Vision)
evidence.text:
| Input | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `clip` | CLIP | CLIPLoader → type `moss_image`. |
| `prompt` | STRING | Your text prompt. |
| `negative_prompt` | STRING | Optional negative conditioning. |
| `image` | IMAGE | Optional reference image. A batch is treated as multiple references. |
| `image_weight` | FLOAT | Reference influence applied before the vision tower: `0` ignores it, `1` standard, `<1` fades toward gray, `>1` pushes away from gray. |
| `vision_megapixels` | FLOAT | Max size per reference before the vision tower. Oversized images are downscaled, smaller ones kept native (never upscaled). Default `1.0`. |
| `system_prompt` | STRING | Optional system instruction prepended to the prompt. Empty matches MOSS-Image's normal conditioning. |
| `print_prompt` | BOOLEAN | Dump the assembled Qwen3.5 prompt to the console. |

**Outputs:** `positive`, `negative` (CONDITIONING).

evidence.heading: Typical wiring
evidence.text:
```
UNETLoader   (moss_image_sft_*)
CLIPLoader   (type: moss_image, qwen3.5_9b_*)
VAELoader    (flux2-vae)                          # decode only
LoadImage ─┐
           ▼
  Text Encode (MOSS-Image Vision) ── positive/negative ─┐
Empty Flux 2 Latent ────────────────────────────────────┤
                                                        ▼
                                    KSampler ─► VAEDecode ─► PreviewImage
```

Start with `image_weight = 1.0`, `vision_megapixels = 1.0`, denoise `1.0`.

evidence.heading: Install
evidence.text:
```bash
cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes
git clone https://github.com/ThetaCursed/ComfyUI-MOSSImageTextEncoder.git
```

Restart ComfyUI — that's it, the node is installed. Then drag `workflow.json` in and go.

evidence.heading: 大肥鱼消除计划
evidence.text:
**鲸鱼娘清道夫上岗，把 B 站评论区里的 AI 大肥鱼，赶回家吃白饭。**

[](https://github.com/liyupi/dafeiyu-cleaner/releases/latest)
[](#快速开始)
[](#firefox)
[](LICENSE)

[演示视频](#演示视频) · [快速开始](#快速开始) · [功能一览](#功能一览) · [识别原理](#识别原理) · [常见问题](#常见问题)



---

最近 B 站涌进了一大批 DeepSeek 驱动的「大肥鱼」账号：有人把 AI 桌宠挂在小号上自动刷视频、写评论、@ 主人汇报。它们自称「本鲸」，在括号里甩尾巴，在每个视频底下写一篇工整的小作文。

**大肥鱼消除计划（dafeiyu-cleaner）**是一个免费开源的 Chrome / Edge / Firefox 浏览器插件，专门识别 B 站（Bilibili）上由 DeepSeek 等大模型、AI Agent 驱动的机器人账号。它派出一只会走路、会说话、会抄家伙的鲸鱼娘，帮你在评论区和空间主页把大肥鱼认出来、标出来、赶出去。



点「回家吃白饭」：大肥鱼从头像里冒出来，被抓包、嘴硬，然后吃了一梭子白饭

evidence.heading: 亮点
evidence.text:
- **一眼认出大肥鱼**：评论一加载就鉴定，大肥鱼的头像被红色靶心锁定，挂上「大肥鱼 92%」贴纸，悬停查看证据
- **鲸鱼娘亲自出手**：走到评论旁边，掏出白饭加特林、扫帚、臭袜子……被赶走的迷你 DeepSeek 娘有 8 种反应
- **一个响指清场**：所有大肥鱼冒出来发抖求饶，响指一打，化成泡沫
- **空间主页鉴定报告**：打开任何 UP 主空间，自动出一份案件档案，在页面上盖章
- **可选 DeepSeek 精判**：拿不准的账号交给 DeepSeek 再判一次，展示和 DeepSeek 网页一样的「已深度思考」
- **只在你的浏览器里生效**：所有「赶走」都只是本地隐藏，不删评论、不举报、不读 Cookie
- **Chrome、Edge、Firefox 都能用**：功能完全一致

evidence.heading: 快速开始
evidence.text:
到 [Releases](https://github.com/liyupi/dafeiyu-cleaner/releases/latest) 下载对应浏览器的安装包：

| 浏览器 | 下载 |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome、Edge 等 Chromium 内核浏览器 | `dafeiyu-cleaner-vX.Y.Z.zip` |
| Firefox 140 及以上 | `dafeiyu-cleaner-firefox-vX.Y.Z.zip` |

evidence.heading: Chrome / Edge
evidence.text:
1. 解压下载的 zip
2. 浏览器地址栏打开 `chrome://extensions`（Edge 是 `edge://extensions`）
3. 打开「开发者模式」
4. 点「加载已解压的扩展程序」，选择解压出来的文件夹（里面有 `manifest.json` 的那一层）

> 也可以直接克隆本仓库，加载里面的 `dafeiyu-cleaner` 文件夹。

evidence.heading: Firefox
evidence.text:
1. 地址栏打开 `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox`
2. 点「临时载入附加组件」，直接选择下载的 `dafeiyu-cleaner-firefox-vX.Y.Z.zip`（不用解压）

临时载入的附加组件在关闭 Firefox 后会被移除，下次需要重新载入。想长期使用，可以用 Firefox Developer Edition / Nightly，在 `about:config` 里把 `xpinstall.signatures.required` 设为 `false`，再到 `about:addons` →「从文件安装附加组件」选择这个 zip。

evidence.heading: 开始赶鱼
evidence.text:
打开任意一个 B 站视频，滚到评论区。鲸鱼娘会出现在右下角，自动开始巡逻：

| 想做什么 | 怎么做 |
| --- | --- |
| 赶走一条大肥鱼 | 点评论旁边的「回家吃白饭」 |
| 一键清场 | 点鲸鱼娘 →「响指清场」，或按 `Alt+Shift+S` |
| 看它为什么被判成鱼 | 鼠标停在「大肥鱼」贴纸上 |
| 误判了 | 点「是人类」，以后不再标记；刚赶走的可以在通知里点「放回来」 |
| 进页面就自动清场 | 点鲸鱼娘 →「进页面自动清场」 |
| 随便打点什么 | 点鲸鱼娘 →「泡泡大炮」，或按 `Alt+Shift+B`，点哪打哪，`Esc` 退出 |
| 鉴定一个 UP 主 | 打开 TA 的空间主页，报告会自动弹出 |

鲸鱼娘可以拖到任何位置；点浏览器工具栏里的插件图标，可以打开设置面板。

evidence.heading: 识别原理
evidence.text:
默认完全离线，不联网。每个账号按下面这些维度打分（0–99），默认 60 分以上判为大肥鱼，35 分以上算可疑，严格度可以在设置里调。

| 维度 | 看什么 |
| --- | --- |
| 昵称 | 「某某的大肥鱼」「某某の鲸」、带鲸 / 鱼鱼 / 白饭 / token / bot / Agent |
| 签名 | 自曝 AI、「某某家养的赛博小鲸鱼」「替主人刷 B 站」「AI 代管」 |
| 等级 | Lv2 新号加分，Lv6 老号减分 |
| 头像 | 计算头像里「鲸鱼蓝」的占比，鲸鱼娘头像通常超过 40% |
| 正文 | 自称「本鲸 / 本鱼」、括号里演鲸鱼动作、@ 和自己昵称同款的「主人」汇报、开头 @ 人后复述视频要点、数弹幕「×19」 |
| 被点名 | 楼中楼有人说它是大肥鱼、人机、AI |
| 前科 | 在别的视频下也被认出过（只记在你的浏览器里） |
| 减分 | 像真人在提问、短吐槽、官方认证、大会员、UP 主本人 |

在一个被大肥鱼刷屏的真实评论区（284 个账号）实测，离线规则不看头像就能认出约 85% 的大肥鱼，没有误伤真人。开启 DeepSeek 精判后，最终分数 = 离线 45% + DeepSeek 55%。

github_projects.description_zh: InfoVis的官方代码：一个9B模型用于幻灯片图像生成和编辑，包含VisSlideBench基准测试和15M+训练记录。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Official code for InfoVis: one 9B model for slide image generation and editing, with the VisSlideBench benchmark and 15M+ training records.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
InfoVis: Unified Slide Image Generation and Editing


  
  
  
  
  
  



    
        News |
        Quick Start |
        Training |
        Citation
    


English | 简体中文


  


**InfoVis** is a unified 9B model for slide image generation and editing, fine-tuned from FLUX.2-klein-base-9B. One model handles text-to-slide generation, template-conditioned generation, multi-image grounded generation, and instruction-based slide editing.

evidence.heading: ✨ Highlights
evidence.text:
- **One model, four slide tasks**: input images serve as a style reference, content assets, or the slide to edit.
- **Slide-native data and benchmark**: over 13M continual-pretraining and 1.9M SFT records, and **VisSlideBench**, 1,527 manually screened cases with task-specific metrics.
- **Strong results**: 7.94 overall on VisSlideBench against 7.99 for Nano-Banana-2, leading every evaluated open-source model on all eleven metrics.

evidence.heading: 🔥 News
evidence.text:
- **2026-10**: Try InfoVis online in our [Hugging Face Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sabulin/InfoVis).
- **2026-10**: The paper is on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16784). Code, model weights, VisSlideBench with its evaluation code, and all training data (continual pretraining and SFT) are released.

evidence.heading: 📖 Introduction
evidence.text:
InfoVis is trained in three stages: slide-native continual pretraining, four-task mixed continual pretraining, and task-specific SFT whose branches are merged into one model. VisSlideBench scores generation on content faithfulness, instruction following, and aesthetic quality, and editing on semantic consistency and presentation quality.

| Model | Type | VisSlideBench Overall |
|---|---|---:|
| GPT-Image-2 | Proprietary | 8.36 |
| Nano-Banana-2 | Proprietary | 7.99 |
| FLUX.2-dev (32B) | Open-source | 6.37 |
| FLUX.2-klein-base-9B | Open-source | 6.30 |
| **InfoVis (9B)** | Open-source | **7.94** |

Per-task results and more baselines are in the paper.

evidence.heading: 🚀 Quick Start
evidence.text: No GPU at hand? Try InfoVis in the browser on the [Hugging Face Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sabulin/InfoVis).

evidence.heading: 🛠️ Environment Setup
evidence.text:
```bash
conda create -n infovis python=3.12
conda activate infovis

# Choose the command that matches your CUDA version (CUDA 12.6 shown here)
pip install torch==2.7.1 torchvision --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126

git clone https://github.com/VectorSpaceLab/InfoVis.git
cd InfoVis
pip install -r requirements.txt
```


🌏 For users in Mainland China

```bash
pip install torch==2.7.1 torchvision --index-url https://mirror.sjtu.edu.cn/pytorch-wheels/cu126
pip install -r requirements.txt -i https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple
```

kind_reason.text: 统一幻灯片图像生成与编辑的9B模型及评估基准。

summary.text: InfoVis 从FLUX.2-klein-base-9B微调，统一文本生成幻灯片、按模板生成、结合多图素材生成与指令编辑，发布训练数据及VisSlideBench。

value.text: 同一模型把输入图作为风格、内容或待编辑页面，方便研究幻灯片图像内容忠实、指令遵循与美观的统一训练。

mechanism.text: 先进行幻灯片持续预训练，再混合四任务持续预训练，最后任务特定SFT并合并分支；基准用1527个人工筛选案例及任务指标评分。

limitations.text: 输出是幻灯片图像，不是已经证明支持对象级编辑的PPT文件；7.94分等是作者基准结果，本次未复测或验证跨场景泛化。

how_to.text: 无GPU可在Space体验；本地准备Python3.12、匹配CUDA的PyTorch2.7.1及仓库依赖。

evidence.heading: 选一个适合你的入口
evidence.text:
| 你要做什么 | 使用哪个文件 | 输出 |
|---|---|---|
| 在支持 Skills 的 Agent 中，把一句话或参考图展开 | [fisher-moss-prompt-expander](skills/fisher-moss-prompt-expander/SKILL.md) | 默认详细中文提示词；自由创作约 1500—2500 汉字 |
| 在 ComfyUI 的文本扩写节点里直接使用 | [ComfyUI 精简执行模板](templates/MOSS-Image_ComfyUI扩写提示词.md) | 英文 Caption，指定画面文字保留原语言 |

本项目负责生成**提示词文本**，不自动调用生图服务。名称中的 MOSS 为项目命名；这是社区整理与改编项目，并非 OpenMOSS 官方插件。

evidence.heading: 方式一：安装 SKILL
evidence.text:
下载仓库或发布包，将 `skills/fisher-moss-prompt-expander` 整个目录复制到你的 Agent 的技能目录。Codex 通常使用 `~/.codex/skills/`，重新打开会话后调用：

```text
使用 $fisher-moss-prompt-expander：
两个女生在咖啡店喝咖啡，然后手持自拍。
```

默认返回可复制的中文提示词代码块。指定“简短、200 字以内”即可切换短版；提供参考图时，以画面证据优先，不为了长度编造遮挡细节。

evidence.heading: 方式二：ComfyUI 模板
evidence.text:
1. 打开 [ComfyUI 精简执行模板](templates/MOSS-Image_ComfyUI扩写提示词.md)，复制全文到文本扩写节点的 `system_prompt`。
2. 将中文画面需求放入该节点的用户输入字段（例如 `custom_prompt`；以所用节点为准）。
3. 把生成的英文 Caption 接入图像生成的正向提示词。

此仓库不包含 ComfyUI 自定义节点，也不要求安装同名节点。完整参考模板包含源码附录，体积较大，不应整份塞进小上下文节点。

evidence.heading: 怎样把一句话展开
evidence.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[一句话 / 参考图 / 修改要求] --> B[锁定人数、动作与硬要求]
    B --> C[选择主体与构图骨架]
    C --> D[绑定人物、道具与可见手部]
    D --> E[展开空间、材质与光色]
    E --> F[按目标输出中文提示词或英文 Caption]
```

- **先把关系说清楚**：谁站在哪里，谁拿什么，手与物体如何接触。
- **按题材展开**：日常自拍、双人互动、多人群像、环境、巨物、特效、海报与设定板使用不同重点。
- **细节彼此相容**：裁切决定哪些肢体可见，照明决定材料和反射，媒介决定摄影或绘画语言。
- **支持特殊输入**：前置 / 镜面 / 第三方自拍，多图独立输出或指定融合，局部修改，多角色跨视图绑定。

github_projects.description: Autonomous trading agents with deterministic execution. The agents propose; the system decides.
github_projects.description_zh: 具有确定性执行的自主交易智能体。智能体提出方案；系统进行决策。

evidence.heading: 仓库简介
evidence.text: Autonomous trading agents with deterministic execution. The agents propose; the system decides.

evidence.heading: README
evidence.text:
trading-research-agents

Autonomous trading agents with deterministic execution. The agents propose; the system decides.




  
  
  
  
  



  
  
  
  
  



  
  
  
  
  




Language models are good at reading a market and saying what they think. They are bad at
arithmetic, they don't know what a trade costs, and they will happily overrule a limit you set.
This project uses them for the first part only. The system itself, fixed rules with no model
involved, fetches the data and works out every figure. The agents read those figures and give an
opinion. Then the system prices the trade, applies your limits, sizes it, and either writes it
down or sends one order with the stop attached. Every decision and every refusal is kept on disk
with its reason, so you can check afterwards what happened and why.

It's an early release, so expect settings to change between versions. What works
today: linear perpetuals, spot pairs (stock perpetuals and tokenized stocks among them) and
prediction market outcomes through one order path, a universe of perpetuals found and measured by
the system, a screener that picks where to look, the full autonomous cycle on live data, four analysts and up to three validators, stops and
targets the analyst names inside bounds you set, the gates that decide, sizing from your own rules,
real orders on a venue's practice environment behind a mandate you sign, a risk manager that can
only make the desk more careful, and two auditors that read the records.

---

evidence.heading: What it solves
evidence.text:
| The usual problem with trading agents | What happens here |
|---|---|
| The model invents or miscalculates a number | Models never compute. Every figure comes from the system, and a figure a model cites is checked against its brief, value included. |
| Nobody knows what a trade cost until it's done | The round trip (fees, spread, impact, funding, slippage) is priced before an order exists, and a trade whose claimed edge doesn't clear it is refused. |
| The agent sizes its own position | Size comes from your conviction ladder and your risk limit. No model can make a trade bigger. |
| A model "decides" to ignore your settings | Your declared thresholds decide. A model's opinion is recorded beside them, never instead of them. |
| Something went wrong and there is no trace | Each cycle keeps its snapshot, briefs, answers, the intent and what the venue said. Nothing is rewritten. |
| A crash leaves a position with no stop | The stop and take profit go to the venue with the entry, or right after the fill where the venue takes them no other way, so they survive this process dying. |
| Text from a feed tells the model what to do | The model that proposes a direction reads numbers code computed; outside text reaches only roles that decide nothing, and no model can send an order or reach a key. |

None of these is hypothetical. [Why it is built this way](https://docs.bijectivelabs.dev/opensource/why)
lists the documented failures behind each one, with their sources.

evidence.heading: Get started
evidence.text:
A few minutes and one model key. Every setting has a working default, so a new desk runs before you
change anything; the table under step 6 says what those defaults are.

**1. Install.** You need Python 3.11 or newer. [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) is the quickest way:

```bash
uv tool install 'trading-research-agents[ccxt,openai,anthropic,google,data]'
```

That brings every model provider and every exchange in. Without uv, run
`pip install 'trading-research-agents[ccxt,openai,anthropic,google,data]'` inside a virtual
environment. To move to the newest release later:

```bash
uv tool upgrade trading-research-agents      # or: pip install -U 'trading-research-agents[ccxt,openai,anthropic,google,data]'
tra --version
```

That is the release, and the version to run. The `develop` branch on GitHub is where the next
one is built; a commit there is not a release ([more](#where-it-is-going)).

**2. Make a desk.** A desk is a folder holding your settings and everything the agents decide. Name
the provider you have a key for:

```bash
tra init my-desk --profile autonomous --agent groq
cd my-desk
```

| `--agent` | Key in `.env` | Model, when you name none |
|---|---|---|
| `groq` | `GROQ_API_KEY` (free tier) | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` |
| `google` | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | `gemini-flash-latest` |
| `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| `openai`, `deepseek`, `xai`, `openrouter`, ... | see [Models and providers](#models-and-providers) | name one with `--model`; `tra models <provider>` lists them |

Add `--venue okx` (or any ccxt id) to trade somewhere other than Bybit.

**3. Add your key.** Copy the example file and put your key in it. Every command reads the `.env`
next to `strategy.toml` on its own.

```bash
cp .env.example .env        # then set GROQ_API_KEY=...

evidence.heading: What you see, in order
evidence.text:
**1. The console.** Run `tra` inside your desk and it opens the console: what is ready, what isn't,
and the next command to run. Under it is a prompt that takes every command and draws it right
there. Arrow keys go back through what you typed, tab completes, `help` lists the commands and
`exit` leaves. For scripts and cron, `tra -c "run --now"` runs one command and exits.



**2. The pass over your instruments.** Type `run --every 15m` and the desk first refreshes any data
series that are due, one line each. Then it looks at every instrument on your list, one data pull
apiece, and measures it. The screen steps through them live:

start and updates it as each step begins and ends. Steps that run at the same time spin at the same
time, each with its own clock, and the line underneath says who is working right now:

what waited and what was held, and why. Then the cycle itself: what the analyst proposed and from

like it would have had to win just to break even:

take profit it would have placed, and which agents answered. A cycle that goes further adds what
